**INTERNATIONAL ERP SYSTEM**

Multilingual Product Requirements, Architecture\
and Implementation Specification

**Reference technology baseline: ASP.NET Core / .NET 11 • PostgreSQL • Next.js App Router**

Date-qualified technical snapshot: 22 November 2026\
Document assembled: 23 November 2026\
Prepared by Manus AI

**Document scope**

A cross-domain baseline for a configurable, internationally deployable ERP covering finance, procurement, sales, inventory, manufacturing and quality, people/payroll, projects and assets, platform services, localization, security, integration, delivery, and implementation. The main catalog contains one uniquely identified, testable requirement per specification card. It is designed as a product baseline, not as a claim of universal legal or regulatory compliance.

**1,120 individually identified requirements across 16 domains**

The system supports tenant-configured language, formatting locale, time zone, currency, jurisdiction, legal entity, and industry policy boundaries. Specific countries, statutory profiles, hosting choices, SLOs, and language launch sets remain decisions for the product owner.

## Design priorities

- Keep country, tax, payroll, privacy, and industry rules configurable and evidence-backed.
- Enforce tenant and legal-entity authorization across APIs, jobs, exports, caches, and reports.
- Keep each module accountable for its authoritative business facts and publish versioned contracts.
- Support translated user interfaces, locale-sensitive formatting, Unicode, and right-to-left layouts.
- Preserve immutable approval, posting, inventory, payroll, and integration evidence.
- Make acceptance criteria testable, auditable, and traceable to a stable requirement identifier.

# How to use this specification

Read the integration and assumptions note first, then each domain design chapter. The individual requirement cards are the normative build-and-test catalog: each has a stable identifier, shall-statement, rationale, acceptance criteria, edge case, control and localization implications, and verification approach. Product teams should map each card to an owner, implementation issue, test evidence, and release status without changing its identifier.

A date-qualified framework or database baseline is not a permanent guarantee. Reconfirm vendor support, patches, provider compatibility, and tooling at implementation approval and production release. Legal, tax, payroll, privacy, retention, and industry rules are explicitly configurable and require accountable jurisdiction-specific review.

# Integrated architecture and decision baseline

**Purpose.** This note integrates the 16 completed workstream chapters into a coherent product and technical baseline. It is an integration layer, not a replacement for the detailed chapter requirements. The Manufacturing, Planning, and Quality chapter contains 70 requirements and is included in the assembled specification.

## 1. Explicit product assumptions

**1.** The product is a configurable, multi-entity ERP intended to support finance, procurement, sales, inventory/logistics, manufacturing/quality, people/payroll, projects/service/fixed assets, and shared platform capabilities. Customer-specific legal semantics are profiles or reviewed extensions, not universal defaults.

**2.** ASP.NET Core is the authoritative business/API tier; PostgreSQL is the transactional system of record; Next.js is a lightweight, locale-aware presentation tier and does not access PostgreSQL directly.

**3.** Default deployment architecture is a modular monolith with explicit bounded contexts and contracts. Services or database-per-tenant placements may be selected where justified, but are not presumed.

**4.** Cross-module work is asynchronous where appropriate. Commands and events are versioned, tenant/entity scoped, traceable, idempotent, retryable, and reconcilable. Durable outbox/inbox processing is the default for externalized side effects.

**5.** Financial and other posted/issued facts are not silently overwritten. Corrections use linked reversals, adjustments, or compensating events with provenance. Monetary computations use exact decimal arithmetic and explicit currency/rounding policy.

**6.** Identity-provider authentication is distinct from tenant membership and authorization. The server enforces authorization, with PostgreSQL row-level security (RLS) as defense in depth rather than the only boundary.

**7.** Tenant, legal entity, jurisdiction, accounting basis, tax profile, locale, time zone, currency, language, and data-residency policy are distinct concepts. Each is explicit in applicable requests, records, or policy context.

**8.** The .NET baseline is the latest stable supported release asserted by the chapter authors for the reference date **2026-11-22: .NET 11 / ASP.NET Core 11**. Reconfirm support and servicing patch at implementation approval and production release. .NET 10 LTS remains an explicit alternative when support-track duration is preferred.

**9.** PostgreSQL is selected, and PostgreSQL 19 was verified and selected by several chapters for the reference date; other chapters intentionally did not pin a major. Treat PostgreSQL 19 as a **candidate baseline**, not an irrevocable fleet-wide mandate: confirm support, provider availability, extensions, backup/replication, and application-driver compatibility at implementation approval.

**10.** Next.js App Router is selected, with Server Components by default and narrowly scoped Client Components. The precise Next.js and Node.js versions are not established in the supplied results and must be pinned after compatibility/support checks.

**11.** WCAG 2.2 AA is the product accessibility target for application-owned workflows, subject to jurisdiction-specific obligations and testing.

**12.** Requirements presume effective-dated configuration, controlled policy releases, tenant-safe audit evidence, and explicit migration/reconciliation paths.

## 2. Out of scope and non-assumptions

- This note does not choose a country, tax regime, accounting basis, statutory filing schema, payroll rule set, industry qualification, retention schedule, or legal interpretation.
- It does not assert universal legal compliance, certification, a particular procurement regime, worker classification, tax treatment, or privacy-law applicability.
- It does not select a hosting provider, cloud, region, tenancy topology, database-per-tenant strategy, or data-residency location.
- It does not set product scale, availability/performance SLOs, RPO/RTO, support hours, or a universal retention period; those require service and customer profiles.
- It does not prescribe a specific Next.js release, PostgreSQL provider, Npgsql/EF Core version, or claim OpenAPI 3.2.1 is supported by the chosen tooling without qualification.
- It does not prescribe an MES vendor or claim that the configurable manufacturing/quality baseline satisfies every industry-specific qualification or regulation.
- This integration note does not replace the detailed domain chapters, requirement cards, or project-specific validation.

## 3. Coherent reference architecture

### 3.1 Logical shape

Browser / accessible localized UI

│ HTTPS; locale-aware Next.js App Router (thin presentation/BFF)

▼

ASP.NET Core on supported .NET (authoritative APIs, policies, workflows)

├── Modular domain contexts and versioned internal contracts

├── PostgreSQL system of record (constraints, transactions, RLS defense-in-depth)

├── Transactional outbox ──► durable broker/adapters ──► external systems

├── Durable inbox/deduplication ◄── callbacks/events; reconciliation queues

└── Audit/evidence, telemetry, documents, identity and policy adapters

Keep bounded contexts logically separated even in the default modular monolith. A domain owns its write model and invariants; other domains use APIs/events or governed read models, never direct table mutation. Read models may be eventually consistent and must disclose freshness where operational decisions depend on it. PostgreSQL remains authoritative for transactional ERP state; analytics projections must not become implicit write authorities.

### 3.2 Versioning and release baseline

- **Backend:** ASP.NET Core/.NET 11 is the date-stamped reference baseline from the chapter authors. Verify the then-current Microsoft lifecycle and patch before build freeze, deployment, and ongoing release; explicitly choose .NET 10 LTS instead if the approved support policy values LTS over the asserted latest stable STS.
- **Database:** PostgreSQL 19 is a candidate date-stamped supported-major baseline in chapters 04, 07, 08, 11, 15, and 16. Chapters 01–03, 05, 09–10, 12–14 did not consistently assert that pin. Resolve through an implementation compatibility gate; pin supported minor/provider release, extensions, Npgsql/EF Core compatibility, and tested upgrade/rollback or forward-recovery approach.
- **Frontend:** Next.js App Router is the common choice, but the stable version and Node runtime remain release-gated. Keep it thin: no database credentials or authoritative business-rule enforcement in the browser/BFF.
- **API descriptions:** OpenAPI 3.2.1 is a proposed integration chapter baseline, contingent on generator, validator, gateway, and client tooling support. If qualification fails, record the supported contract version rather than implying compatibility.

## 4. Cross-cutting coherence principles

### 4.1 Tenancy, entity scope, and authorization

- Carry an authenticated principal, tenant, legal entity where applicable, and correlation context from request ingress through jobs, events, callbacks, exports, and audit records. Do not infer tenant scope from locale, URL alone, or untrusted payload fields.
- Separate identity-provider authentication from tenant membership, role/permission assignment, and resource authorization. Enforce authorization server-side at each operation; use explicit permission codes and least privilege.
- Apply tenant filters in application/data access and use PostgreSQL RLS as a second control where the selected topology supports it. Test with actual runtime roles, pooled-connection transaction-local context, owner/BYPASSRLS paths, background jobs, support tooling, and failure/default-deny behavior.
- Treat shared-schema discriminator, schema-per-tenant, and database/cluster-per-tenant as topology choices with equivalent isolation and operational evidence. Do not mix assumptions from one topology into another without tests.
- Tenant scope must survive cache keys, search indexes, analytics, document links, notifications, telemetry, support access, and restore/migration procedures.

### 4.2 Identity, audit, and evidence

- Use centralized identity and authorization integration, but keep ERP business roles, legal-entity membership, approvals, and segregation-of-duties policy in the application domain.
- Record actor/service identity, tenant/entity, permission/approval context, action, timestamp, correlation and causation identifiers, before/after or immutable business reference as appropriate, and policy/schema/version provenance.
- Preserve append-only evidence for high-consequence state transitions and external interactions. Redact or minimize sensitive data in logs and telemetry; audit records must not become an uncontrolled copy of secrets or personal data.
- Require approval and auditable provenance for configuration/rule-pack changes that affect posting, tax, payroll, access, localization, or statutory documents.

### 4.3 Localization and canonical data

- Separate UI language, formatting locale, time zone, calendar, numbering system, currency, script direction, legal jurisdiction, and legal entity. Use BCP 47 language tags and locale data; accept locale only after validation and tenant policy checks.
- Preserve canonical values and original user-supplied text independently of localized display. Use explicit currency codes and precision/rounding rules, UTC instants plus explicit business time-zone semantics, and locale-neutral stable identifiers.
- Localize rendering and documents with catalog/template version provenance. Keep machine codes and APIs stable and locale-neutral unless a contract explicitly carries language-tagged content. Support right-to-left and bidirectional text safely; accessibility target is WCAG 2.2 AA.
- Locale context may be explicit in a request/event when needed for a human-facing artifact; it must never replace authorization or jurisdiction/entity context. Database collation is a separately governed technical choice, not the user's display locale.

### 4.4 Data lifecycle, integrity, and finance controls

- Use relational constraints for core identities and invariants; govern JSONB as an extension/integration envelope rather than an untyped substitute for domain schema.
- Use exact decimal arithmetic for money and quantities where required; define precision, rounding, unit-of-measure, exchange-rate source/date, and conversion provenance in domain policy. Avoid floating point for authoritative financial amounts.
- Posted journals, issued invoices, approved payroll results, and posted stock/asset events are immutable facts. Corrections must link to the original and preserve approval, accounting period, reason, and external acknowledgments as applicable.
- Separate physical on-hand, reservation, custody, ownership, and finance valuation; Inventory owns stock movements and Finance owns general-ledger posting and period control. Similarly, operational domains own their source facts while Finance owns accounting representations.
- Define retention, legal hold, deletion/anonymization, archival, backup/restore, and data residency by approved jurisdiction/tenant policy. A deletion path must not erase records whose retention or evidentiary duties are unresolved.
- Schema migrations and business-data migrations are distinct. Use expand/contract or an approved alternative, compatibility checks, rehearsal, reconciliation, and forward recovery; do not assume a database major upgrade is an ERP data migration.

### 4.5 Integration reliability and security

- Use versioned API/event schemas, stable IDs, tenant/entity scope, correlation/causation IDs, idempotency keys, explicit timestamps and decimal encodings, and documented error/acknowledgment semantics.
- Persist outbound intent atomically with the business transaction through a transactional outbox; consume through a durable inbox or equivalent deduplication. Define bounded retries, backoff, poison-message handling, replay authorization, ordering requirements, and reconciliation.
- Distinguish command acceptance from business completion and settlement. Unknown provider outcome is not success: preserve accepted/rejected/returned/unknown states and reconcile before marking a payment, filing, or external action complete.
- Keep external networks/providers behind authenticated, replaceable adapters. Preserve original provider status and payload reference alongside normalized domain state. Minimize sensitive fields in events and apply access controls to replay/export.
- Use documented API error semantics, rate limits, contract tests, compatibility/deprecation policy, health checks, and security review. Next.js is not a trusted integration processor.

## 5. Module boundaries and key contracts

| Context | Owns authoritative facts | Main contracts and non-ownership rules |

|---|---|---|

| Finance, accounting, tax | Ledgers, journals, periods, AP/AR open items, payment allocation, accounting/tax calculation provenance and posting state | Consumes source-domain versioned events from procurement, sales/billing, inventory, projects/assets and payroll. Owns ledger posting and finance-side payment execution; source modules do not write ledger tables. Tax/e-reporting providers are versioned jurisdiction adapters. |

| Procurement and suppliers | Sourcing, requisitions, purchase orders, supplier/order/commitment context, receipt/acceptance/return context | Finance owns invoice posting, budget ledger and payment execution. Inventory owns physical receipt/stock posting; procurement supplies expected receipt, provenance and approved landed-cost context. Integrates identity/org, budget/AP, quality, contract/document networks and analytics. |

| Sales, CRM, order and billing | Customer/order/line commercial lifecycle and sales-facing status | Inventory owns stock/reservations and shipment outcomes; configured tax services determine traceable tax calculations; Finance/AR owns ledger handoff, open items, payment allocation and authoritative credit exposure. Provider submission and e-invoice states are idempotent and auditable. |

| Inventory, warehouse and logistics | Physical stock events/projections, reservation/availability, custody and operational fulfillment | Consumes procurement expected receipts and approved landed costs; accepts sales/manufacturing demand and returns allocation/shortage/fulfillment outcomes; consumes quality disposition; publishes valuation events to Finance, which alone posts GL. Carrier adapters preserve native and normalized statuses. |

| Manufacturing, planning and quality | Production orders, BOMs/recipes, routes/operations, planning, scheduling, shop-floor execution, quality records, disposition, genealogy, and operational cost handoffs | Inventory owns physical stock movements/reservations; Manufacturing issues scoped material/WIP/scrap commands and reconciles movement references. Procurement owns suppliers and commitments; Finance owns costing policy, journals, periods, and ledger posting. Quality disposition authority is permissioned and separable from routine receiving/picking/reporting. Industry-specific legal and qualification profiles remain configurable. |

| People, workforce and payroll | Worker lifecycle, time/leave approvals, payroll calculations/results and jurisdictional rule-pack provenance | Approved, attributable, idempotent time/leave inputs feed payroll; corrections route through retroactive/off-cycle adjustment. Finance receives balanced traceable journals by entity/currency/cost dimensions and returns posting/rejection reference. ATS, identity, benefits, banks and statutory authorities use versioned contracts. |

| Projects, service, fixed assets | Project/service/asset operational lifecycle and domain-specific costing/service records | Contracts with GL, billing/AR, procurement/AP, inventory, HR/resources, customer/contracts, rates, tax, documents, identity and notifications. Accounting, tax, service, retention and industry rules remain configured; Finance owns ledger posting. |

| Platform, master data, workflow, reporting | Shared identifiers, tenant/entity and master-data governance, workflow primitives, reporting/read-model patterns, configuration provenance | Supplies stable references, permission codes, workflow/API/event compatibility and governed projections. Domain contexts retain authority over their own master/transaction facts; reports declare freshness and scope. |

| Identity, security, privacy | Authentication integration, tenant membership/authorization policy integration, security/audit controls | Identity provider proves identity; ERP authorizes tenant/resource/action. RLS is additional isolation, not authorization by itself. Applies consistently to APIs, jobs, exports, caches, search, documents and support access. |

| Localization | Locale catalog/release and rendering policy | Cross-cutting context, not a business-data owner. Domains declare localized fields and rendering policy; Finance owns statutory monetary precision and outputs; documents retain template/catalog release provenance. |

| Integration and delivery | API/event envelopes, outbox/inbox, adapters, compatibility, release evidence, telemetry and operational controls | No business domain bypasses source ownership. Integrations carry stable identifiers, version, tenant/entity and correlation context; delivery gates include test evidence and immutable artifact provenance. |

### Event/API envelope minimum

For events and asynchronous commands, define: eventId/stable message ID, type, schemaVersion, source, occurredAt (canonical timestamp), tenant and legal-entity scope when applicable, subject/source key, correlation and causation IDs, idempotency key where command semantics require one, actor/service attribution, payload classification, and trace context. Payload fields use canonical codes/units/decimals and explicit locale only when content is localized. Consumers must document duplicate handling, ordering assumptions, schema compatibility, authorization, retry/replay and reconciliation. APIs expose equivalent scope and correlation metadata, stable error contracts, optimistic concurrency where needed, and explicit acceptance versus completion semantics.

## 6. Prioritized conflicts and reconciliation actions

**P0 — Resolve before architecture/build freeze**

**1. PostgreSQL major pin versus no pin.** Some workstreams verified PostgreSQL 19; others deliberately left the major open. Adopt PostgreSQL 19 only after support/provider/extension/Npgsql-EF compatibility and operational qualification. Otherwise choose the supported qualified major and update all chapter baselines consistently. Never leave deployment teams to infer a version from the word “current.”

**2. Tenancy topology.** Workstreams describe shared-schema RLS, discriminator tenancy, and dedicated database/cluster options. Product must choose supported topologies and a normative threat model, then prove isolation for runtime roles, pools, jobs, restore, support, caches/search and analytics. RLS does not replace application authorization.

**3. Manufacturing scope and contract qualification.** The manufacturing chapter is complete with 70 requirements. Before implementation commitment, confirm the targeted industry/MES depth and reconcile material issue/return, WIP, quality disposition, genealogy, subcontracting, and costing contracts with inventory, procurement, people/assets, and finance.

**4. Legal and data policy profiles.** Country, tax, accounting, payroll, privacy/retention and e-document profiles are intentionally unspecified. Do not enable jurisdiction-dependent posting, filing, payroll or retention behavior until approved profile and accountable interpretation are available.

**P1 — Resolve before integration and production qualification**

**5. .NET STS versus LTS.** The common reference is .NET 11 STS as of 2026-11-22; .NET 10 LTS is the documented alternative. Product owner must choose support-track policy and servicing cadence; reconfirm lifecycle at release because the reference date is not a permanent fact.

**6. Next.js/Node and API-spec compatibility.** No exact Next.js/Node release is established; OpenAPI 3.2.1 was proposed with a tooling caveat. Pin tested stable frontend/runtime and contract-toolchain versions together; publish the compatibility matrix.

**7. Manufacturing/quality ownership granularity.** Other chapters imply Quality as a capability/context; establish whether it is a distinct bounded context, embedded in Manufacturing, or shared quality service, and define disposition authority and segregation from receipt/picking.

**8. Canonical master-data stewardship.** Define ownership and lifecycle for tenant, legal entity, party/customer/supplier, item, unit of measure, currency/rates, account, cost dimension, warehouse, language/catalog, and external identifiers. Prevent multiple domains from becoming competing writers.

**P2 — Resolve during service and rollout design**

**9. Scale and service objectives.** Define availability, latency, throughput, batch windows, data volumes, RPO/RTO, support and observability objectives before capacity design; avoid universal targets unsupported by customer context.

**10. Event consistency and replay policy.** Specify ordering keys and freshness budgets only for workflows that need them; establish retention, replay approvals, dead-letter recovery, backfill and reconciliation ownership.

**11. Document and audit lifecycle.** Decide document repository, content classification, immutable evidence requirements, legal hold, deletion/anonymization and export controls by profile.

**12. Rollout feature and migration governance.** Agree configuration promotion, extension approval, tenant-by-tenant enablement, rollback/forward-recovery and data migration acceptance evidence.

## 7. Three-wave rollout sequence

### Wave 1 — Foundation and controlled pilot

- Ratify user-specific choices and release baselines: jurisdiction/entity model, industry, tenancy and hosting, .NET support track, qualified PostgreSQL major/provider, Next.js/Node, identity integration, data residency and service objectives.
- Establish platform foundations: tenant/entity context, server-side authorization, tested RLS or equivalent isolation, identity lifecycle, audit/evidence, configuration versioning, locale-neutral IDs, localization/accessibility foundation, API/event envelope, transactional outbox/inbox, telemetry and secure document handling.
- Implement representative master data and migration tooling; exercise end-to-end tenant isolation, immutable audit trails, backup/restore, schema deployment and reconciliation in non-production.
- Pilot a bounded set of low-risk end-to-end flows selected by the product owner (for example, procure-to-receive and order-to-fulfill with finance posting controlled behind approvals). Do not enable unconfigured statutory or payroll behavior. Require operational runbooks and evidence before expanding.

### Wave 2 — Core transactional domains and cross-module close

- Expand finance/accounting controls, AP/AR, procurement, sales/billing, inventory/warehouse/logistics, projects/service/assets, and people/time/payroll only for approved jurisdictions and profiles.
- Complete source ownership, versioned APIs/events, idempotency, retries, provider-unknown reconciliation, period controls, balanced journals, stock/valuation separation, approved payroll handoff, and cross-domain contract tests.
- Implement approved manufacturing scope by reconciling planning, production, quality, traceability, subcontracting and inventory authority, and by testing cross-module contracts against the selected industry profile.
- Run representative volume, security, localization/RTL, accessibility, migration, recovery, close/payroll, and external-adapter failure exercises. Pilot with selected legal entities and gate by evidence and accountable sign-off.

### Wave 3 — Scale, localization breadth, and optimization

- Add jurisdictions, languages/scripts, industry profiles, tenant placements and external networks incrementally through versioned, reviewed configuration/adapters; preserve localized-document and rule-pack provenance.
- Scale read models, analytics, integrations, partitioning/replication or dedicated tenant placements only against measured SLOs and data-residency decisions; ensure analytical/export paths retain tenant scope.
- Rehearse upgrades (including PostgreSQL major upgrades separately from business-data migration), disaster recovery, high-volume event replay, support access, legal holds, and decommissioning.
- Use production evidence to tune capacity and workflows; maintain compatibility/deprecation policy, regression packs, tenant-by-tenant rollout controls and post-release reconciliation.

| ID | Decision required | Why it is unresolved / required owner input | Needed by |

|---|---|---|---|

| D-01 | Countries, legal entities, tax regimes, accounting basis, statutory invoice/filing schemas, legal numbering and currency rules | Chapters intentionally avoid universal legal assumptions; determines finance/tax configuration and acceptance evidence. | Before domain design freeze |

| D-02 | Industry and regulated/quality scope, including manufacturing depth | The manufacturing chapter provides a configurable baseline; target industry drives workflows, traceability, quality evidence, MES depth and extensions. | Before scope and estimates |

| D-03 | Hosting model/provider, cloud/on-premise constraints, managed database and deployment environment | Not selected; affects supported database versions, networking, secrets, operations and release topology. | Before architecture/build freeze |

| D-04 | Tenancy model: shared discriminator/schema with RLS, schema-per-tenant, database-per-tenant, cluster-per-tenant, or supported combination | Workstreams offer alternatives rather than a single choice; isolation and operational tests differ materially. | Before data model and threat-model approval |

| D-05 | Payroll jurisdictions, worker populations, providers, pay calendars and statutory filing responsibilities | Payroll rates, thresholds, classifications, benefits and filings are configurable and not universally defined. | Before payroll implementation |

| D-06 | Data residency, cross-border processing, backup/DR locations, retention/legal-hold and deletion rules | These depend on jurisdiction, customer obligations and hosting choice; no universal values supplied. | Before hosting and data lifecycle design |

| D-07 | Supported product languages, formatting locales, calendars, numbering systems, scripts, right-to-left requirements and translation ownership | Workstreams define architecture principles but not the product's actual locale catalog or launch languages. | Before UX/content freeze |

| D-08 | Scale profile and SLOs: active users/tenants, peak rates, batch windows, data growth, latency/availability, RPO/RTO and support hours | Chapters explicitly leave operational targets to service/customer profiles. | Before sizing and SRE sign-off |

| D-09 | .NET support track: .NET 11 STS or .NET 10 LTS alternative; patch cadence and upgrade policy | Authors agree on .NET 11 for the stated date but identify .NET 10 LTS as an alternative; future lifecycle must be reconfirmed. | Before implementation approval |

| D-10 | Qualified PostgreSQL major/minor/provider, extension allowlist, Npgsql/EF Core versions, and upgrade strategy | PostgreSQL 19 is a candidate verified baseline in several chapters, not a universal pin across all results. | Before database qualification |

| D-11 | Next.js/Node exact versions, hosting mode, frontend/BFF boundary, and OpenAPI tooling compatibility | No exact frontend pin; OpenAPI 3.2.1 is contingent on implementation tool support. | Before build freeze |

| D-12 | System-of-record ownership/stewards for shared master data and the boundary between Quality and Manufacturing | Needed to prevent duplicate writers and settle disposition/release authority. | Before contract freeze |

| D-13 | External systems/providers: IdP, bank/payment, tax authority, e-invoice/network, carrier, ATS, benefits, document store, notification, analytics | Adapters are specified but provider choices and contract profiles are not. | Before integration testing |

# Finance, Accounting, Tax, and Controls

# Finance, Accounting, Tax, and Controls

**Chapter ID:** ERP-FINANCE-01 **Status:** Product specification baseline **Requirement count:** 70 **Platform as-of date:** 2026-11-22

## Domain design

### Scope and configuration boundary

This chapter specifies the finance domain for a commercial, multi-tenant ERP serving mid-market and enterprise organizations. It covers the general ledger, accounting configuration, journals, AP/AR accounting, tax determination and reporting interfaces, fixed assets, cash and bank reconciliation, consolidation, budgeting, period close, financial reporting, audit evidence, and finance security controls. It defines the accounting core and contracts to adjacent modules; it does not define procurement, sales, payroll, inventory valuation, treasury trading, or industry-specific recognition rules in full. Those modules own their operational source events and integrate through documented finance contracts.

Jurisdiction, accounting framework, entity, tax registrations, invoice rules, filing schema, retention periods, and industry policy are explicit configuration dimensions. The product must not encode one jurisdiction’s tax rate, tax point, exemption, filing cadence, chart, or legal sequence as universal. IFRS IAS 21 describes functional currency and translation questions; IAS 1 sets financial-statement presentation requirements for IFRS reporting, while local GAAP and statutory reports require separately selected, versioned profiles. \[5] \[6] Tax digital reporting spans different systems and schemas, including national SAF-T adaptations and near-real-time e-invoice exchanges, so authority adapters and schema versions are jurisdictional extensions. \[7]

### Actors

Finance configuration administrator maintains charts, calendars, currencies, dimensions, policy mappings, tax profiles, and workflow rules. Journal preparers, AP processors, AR/cash-application staff, asset accountants, and consolidation accountants prepare domain transactions. Independent approvers authorize journals, payments, tax overrides, close exceptions, and reports. Payment-release operators transmit approved batches through provider interfaces. Tax specialists maintain filing mappings and authority adapters. Auditors have scoped read/export access, while tenant administrators manage identity and assignments without implied rights to post or release money. Background services use named, narrowly scoped identities.

### Core entities and state

The accounting core consists of tenant, legal entity, ledger, accounting basis, chart version, account, dimension, fiscal calendar, period, currency, exchange-rate record, journal header/line, posting batch, source-system key, approval, and audit event. Subledger entities include supplier/customer, invoice, credit note, payment/receipt, tax determination, tax evidence, asset, bank statement, reconciliation, budget, commitment, and allocation. Group accounting adds consolidation unit, entity mapping, intercompany match, translation run, and elimination journal. Each externally sourced event keeps a stable source key and lineage; posted facts and issued tax documents are immutable, with corrections represented as linked events.

Amounts use exact decimal storage and explicitly defined precision/scale; PostgreSQL documents numeric as exact and recommends it for monetary values, unlike inexact floating-point types. \[3] Currency identifiers use ISO 4217 codes, but currency code metadata is not an accounting-policy substitute. \[10] Accounting date, transaction timestamp, tax point, and display locale remain distinct. Functional and presentation currency roles are separate, and each translation records rate type, source, effective date, policy version, and approval. \[5]

### Primary workflows

Configure and approve entity accounting structure; prepare and validate journals; approve and post under period locks; import subledger batches idempotently; reconcile subledger control accounts; process supplier invoices through coding, match, tax, approval, and payment proposal; release payments through independent approval and provider status confirmation; issue customer invoices and corrections; apply receipts; calculate and reconcile tax; import bank statements and match cash; calculate asset depreciation; perform period close; and produce versioned statutory and management reports. Consolidation uses separately mapped entity books and group-only eliminations. Each critical action yields a stable correlation ID and evidence link.

### Permission boundaries and control model

Authorization is server-side and scoped by tenant, legal entity, ledger, action, and sensitive field. Preparation, approval, posting, payment release, tax rule publication, supplier bank-data maintenance, close sign-off, and audit export are separable permissions. Conflict rules are configurable, but configured conflicts must be checked at action time, including delegated and temporary roles. PostgreSQL row-level security may add defense in depth; its default is no row access when enabled without a policy, while table owners and BYPASSRLS roles can bypass policies unless controls are carefully designed. \[2] NIST SP 800-53 is a customizable control catalog, not a jurisdiction-specific legal mandate; its access-control and audit/accountability families inform this design. \[11]

Audit logs are append-only to ordinary application roles, capture actor/service identity, UTC time, target, action, correlation ID, approval and before/after values where appropriate, and exclude credentials. Database transactions protect atomic journal posting; PostgreSQL Serializable isolation can raise serialization failures and callers must retry whole transactions as appropriate. \[4] External release and tax submission operations use idempotency keys, correlation IDs, and explicit pending/accepted/rejected/unknown states.

### Platform baseline and major decisions

**Backend:** ASP.NET Core on **.NET 11.0** is the latest stable supported release shown in Microsoft’s official support policy as of 2026-11-22: .NET 11 was released on 2026-11-10, is active STS, and its listed end of support is 2028-11-14; .NET 10 is also active LTS. Pin the deployed SDK/runtime and keep the selected release on current patches. \[1] The build and release owner must reconfirm the latest supported .NET release on implementation approval and each annual upgrade; do not use preview or unsupported releases as production baseline.

**Database:** PostgreSQL is the relational system of record. Pin an officially supported GA major version in deployment policy; the cited current documentation can roll forward and is not, by itself, a version pin. Reconfirm the latest supported PostgreSQL major at implementation approval. Use explicit decimal precision, unique constraints, transactional outbox/idempotency controls, and tenant-aware access design.

**Frontend:** lightweight Next.js App Router frontend, with locale-aware routes/dictionaries or equivalent translation layer. Next.js documents locale routing and dictionaries; WCAG 2.2 provides technology-neutral, testable accessibility criteria. \[8] \[9] This chapter does not freeze a future Next.js version: select and pin a supported stable release at build approval and reconfirm then.

Major decisions are: core ledger is framework-neutral but every ledger selects an accounting basis; configuration packages own jurisdiction/industry rules; one transaction stores source currency and functional values and reporting translates via retained rate lineage; immutable posted/issued facts are corrected by new linked records; a core service boundary separates operational source modules from ledger posting; and no provider submission is represented as final settlement until an authoritative outcome is received.

### Dependencies and cross-module contracts

Procurement supplies approved orders, receipts, supplier identity and invoice references; billing/order management supplies billable events, customers, invoice lines and correction events; inventory and project systems supply valued source events under their own policies; HR/payroll may supply summarized postings but not personal payroll detail unless authorized; banking/payment providers supply statements and payment statuses; identity management supplies authenticated users, groups, and MFA context; tax authorities or accredited networks supply schemas, validation and correlation statuses; document storage supplies immutable evidence references and content hashes.

The finance posting API accepts tenant/entity/ledger, source namespace and key, accounting date, basis, currency, balanced lines, dimensions, document references, tax components, and idempotency token. It returns journal ID, validation state, posting state, and correlation ID. The caller cannot set privileged status fields. Financial reads use entity/ledger-scoped query contracts. Reversals, receipts, refunds, invoice corrections, tax returns, payment statuses, and close evidence return linked identifiers rather than rewriting source records. All contracts define canonical decimal/date serialization, schema versions, idempotent retries, error codes, and locale-neutral machine identifiers.

### Risks and implementation constraints

Material risks include incorrect effective dating, decimal rounding differences, stale or unsourced FX rates, jurisdiction misclassification, tax-schema drift, duplicate retries, hidden cross-tenant access paths, owner/BYPASSRLS database roles, period-close races, and loss of report reproducibility after mapping changes. Mitigate with effective-dated configuration, golden tax/accounting fixtures owned by local experts, validation of authority schemas, retriable atomic posting, least-privilege runtime roles, segregation-of-duties tests, and immutable evidence snapshots. The product specification does not constitute legal or accounting advice; each deployment must have the responsible local accounting/tax professional approve its policy package and tests.

## Finance, Accounting, Tax, and Controls — requirement cards

**REQUIREMENT 0001 OF 1120  |  FINANCE, ACCOUNTING, TAX, AND CONTROLS**

## ERP-FINANCE-001 — Versioned chart of accounts

**Normative requirement:** The system shall maintain a versioned chart of accounts for each legal entity and accounting basis, with stable account identifiers, parent-child hierarchy, effective dates, and status.

**Rationale:** Versioning preserves historical reporting meaning when account structures change.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Given an effective-dated account revision, a posting dated before its start resolves to the prior revision and a posting within its range resolves to the new revision.

**AC 2.** Reject activation when an account has a missing parent, a circular hierarchy, or an overlapping active interval for the same entity and basis.

**Exception / edge case:** A leaf account with existing posted entries cannot be deleted; it may be end-dated and replaced through an approved mapping.

**Security and audit implications:** Only finance configuration administrators may create or activate revisions; retain before/after values, actor, timestamp, and approval for each change.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Account codes remain locale-neutral identifiers; descriptions support per-locale translations and retain the entered legal/local language.

**Verification method:** Automated configuration tests plus database constraint and audit-log inspection.

**REQUIREMENT 0002 OF 1120  |  FINANCE, ACCOUNTING, TAX, AND CONTROLS**

## ERP-FINANCE-002 — Posting eligibility and account type

**Normative requirement:** The system shall define account type, normal balance, direct-posting eligibility, and reconciliation control status for each account and enforce these attributes during journal validation.

**Rationale:** Consistent account properties prevent invalid direct postings and enable dependable reports.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Reject a journal line to a summary-only account and accept the same line to an enabled posting leaf.

**AC 2.** Reject an account whose configured normal-balance or account type is missing when activated for posting.

**Exception / edge case:** An account may be switched from direct-posting to summary-only only after existing open drafts are resolved; posted history remains queryable.

**Security and audit implications:** Privilege changes to posting status are logged; journal validation rechecks account status at commit, not only at draft creation.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** The display label and account classification captions may be localized without changing stable account type codes.

**Verification method:** Unit tests for validation matrix and integration tests against posting API.

**REQUIREMENT 0003 OF 1120  |  FINANCE, ACCOUNTING, TAX, AND CONTROLS**

## ERP-FINANCE-003 — Dimension sets and mandatory dimensions

**Normative requirement:** The system shall support configurable accounting dimensions and effective-dated dimension rules by entity, account, and transaction source, validating permitted values before posting.

**Rationale:** Dimensions support segment, department, project, fund, and other configurable analysis without multiplying accounts.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A configured required dimension omitted from a journal causes a line-level validation error naming the dimension.

**AC 2.** Reject a dimension value outside its effective interval or outside the entity's permitted value set.

**Exception / edge case:** A historical transaction may reference an inactive dimension when its accounting date falls within that dimension's effective interval.

**Security and audit implications:** Dimension administration and rule overrides are separately permissioned and audit logged; users cannot elevate scope by altering submitted identifiers.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Dimension names, values, and errors are translatable; codes and stored keys are stable, and display values respect user locale.

**Verification method:** Rule-engine unit tests and API integration tests using valid, missing, expired, and unauthorized values.

**REQUIREMENT 0004 OF 1120  |  FINANCE, ACCOUNTING, TAX, AND CONTROLS**

## ERP-FINANCE-004 — Fiscal calendars and periods

**Normative requirement:** The system shall support entity-specific fiscal calendars with configurable period lengths, year boundaries, adjustment periods, and accounting dates independent of UTC timestamps.

**Rationale:** Fiscal calendars vary by entity and must not be inferred from the user's display locale.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** For a configured 4-4-5 calendar, the service maps test accounting dates to the configured fiscal year, period, and adjustment period.

**AC 2.** Reject a calendar activation if dates overlap or leave an unintended gap in the configured coverage interval.

**Exception / edge case:** A 53-week year or non-monthly period is allowed only when explicitly configured and validated.

**Security and audit implications:** Calendar edits after posted transactions require a controlled revision and produce an audit event; timestamps are recorded in UTC alongside accounting dates.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Period labels and date presentations are localized; the persisted accounting date uses an unambiguous date type and explicit entity calendar.

**Verification method:** Calendar property-based tests across boundary dates and database/API integration tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0005 OF 1120  |  FINANCE, ACCOUNTING, TAX, AND CONTROLS**

## ERP-FINANCE-005 — Period status and close lock

**Normative requirement:** The system shall implement period statuses for open, soft-close, closed, and reopened states, and enforce them on all financial posting paths based on entity, ledger, and accounting date.

**Rationale:** A centralized lock avoids bypass through imports, APIs, or subledgers.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Posting dated in a closed period is rejected consistently through UI, API, import, and scheduled jobs.

**AC 2.** A user with reopen permission can reopen a period only with a reason, approval where configured, and recorded audit event.

**Exception / edge case:** A controlled late adjustment may be entered in a designated adjustment period without reopening the normal operating period.

**Security and audit implications:** Reopening is restricted to named finance roles and requires step-up authentication where configured; every attempt and result is logged.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Localized dates and explanations must not change the accounting-date decision; period names may be translated.

**Verification method:** Authorization and integration tests exercise every ingestion route and period-state transition.

**REQUIREMENT 0006 OF 1120  |  FINANCE, ACCOUNTING, TAX, AND CONTROLS**

## ERP-FINANCE-006 — Currency master and precision

**Normative requirement:** The system shall maintain currency identifiers using ISO 4217 alpha codes and versioned minor-unit metadata, while permitting explicit precision overrides only for configured measurement contexts.

**Rationale:** Three-letter codes reduce ambiguity, but currencies and minor-unit conventions can change and do not dictate every accounting precision.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Reject an unknown or inactive currency code on a newly created transaction; resolve the currency code and metadata for the transaction date.

**AC 2.** A configured zero-, two-, or three-decimal settlement test formats and validates amounts at the configured scale without binary floating-point drift.

**Exception / edge case:** A historic transaction remains renderable after a currency is withdrawn or its metadata changes, using its stored code and precision snapshot.

**Security and audit implications:** Changes to currency activation or precision are restricted and versioned; amounts are stored using exact decimal types rather than floating point.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Currency code is language-neutral; symbols, grouping, decimal separators, and digit shaping follow locale while showing an unambiguous code in financial reports.

**Verification method:** Boundary tests for precision, currency effective dates, API serialization, and persisted-value exactness.

**REQUIREMENT 0007 OF 1120  |  FINANCE, ACCOUNTING, TAX, AND CONTROLS**

## ERP-FINANCE-007 — Functional and presentation currencies

**Normative requirement:** The system shall store transaction, functional, and presentation currencies as distinct attributes and support entity-level accounting-policy configuration for currency translation.

**Rationale:** IAS 21 distinguishes functional currency from presentation currency; permitted policy details depend on the reporting framework and facts of the entity.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A multi-currency transaction stores transaction and functional-currency values independently and a report can be produced in a configured presentation currency.

**AC 2.** Changing an entity's functional currency does not rewrite posted history; the system requires an effective-dated transition and retains the approved basis.

**Exception / edge case:** A reporting entity may present in more than one currency when enabled by its reporting configuration.

**Security and audit implications:** Currency transition approvals and source rates are immutable audit evidence; restrict ability to select reporting basis or alter translation parameters.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Reports show currency code and locale-formatted values; translation labels identify transaction, functional, and presentation amounts distinctly.

**Verification method:** Integration tests using sample ledgers under two configured accounting policies and inspection of retained rate lineage.

**REQUIREMENT 0008 OF 1120  |  FINANCE, ACCOUNTING, TAX, AND CONTROLS**

## ERP-FINANCE-008 — Exchange-rate types and provenance

**Normative requirement:** The system shall store dated exchange rates by source, rate type, currency pair, effective timestamp, and approval status, and require a configured rate type for each conversion use.

**Rationale:** Different transactions and reporting policies may require different rates; traceability is necessary to reproduce converted values.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A conversion request resolves exactly one approved rate under the configured pair, date, and rate type, or returns a blocking missing-rate error.

**AC 2.** Store source identifier, retrieved-at timestamp, rate date, pair, precision, and approval actor with every rate record.

**Exception / edge case:** If a rate is unavailable for a holiday or restricted market, the configured fallback may be used only when a finance policy explicitly authorizes and records it.

**Security and audit implications:** Only authorized roles may approve or amend rates; preserve prior values and user/source attribution, and never expose provider credentials in audit data.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Rate values retain full stored precision; formatted rates and errors follow locale while currency pair notation is explicit.

**Verification method:** API tests with exact match, duplicate rate, missing rate, fallback, and unauthorized approval cases.

**REQUIREMENT 0009 OF 1120  |  FINANCE, ACCOUNTING, TAX, AND CONTROLS**

## ERP-FINANCE-009 — Balanced journal validation

**Normative requirement:** The system shall require each journal entry to balance in its ledger currency and, where configured, each transaction currency or balancing segment before commit.

**Rationale:** Balanced entries enforce the accounting equation at the atomic posting boundary.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A journal whose debit and credit totals differ by one smallest configured posting unit is rejected with the difference shown.

**AC 2.** A balanced journal with multiple currencies passes only when the configured ledger-currency conversion and balancing rules are satisfied.

**Exception / edge case:** A rounding residual may post only to a designated configured rounding account within a configured tolerance; otherwise posting fails.

**Security and audit implications:** The balancing check executes server-side in the same transaction as posting; callers cannot bypass it through bulk or integration routes.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Amounts and displayed differences use configured currency scale and locale formatting without changing the numeric comparison.

**Verification method:** API and concurrency tests against the journal posting transaction, including one-unit imbalance and rounding threshold.

**REQUIREMENT 0010 OF 1120  |  FINANCE, ACCOUNTING, TAX, AND CONTROLS**

## ERP-FINANCE-010 — Exact journal amount storage

**Normative requirement:** The system shall store journal amounts and computed monetary totals using exact decimal arithmetic with an explicitly configured precision and scale per amount role.

**Rationale:** PostgreSQL numeric supports exact decimal values; binary floating-point is unsuitable for authoritative financial amounts.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Round-trip a high-precision amount through entry, persistence, retrieval, and report with exact equality at declared scale.

**AC 2.** Reject an amount exceeding configured precision or reject/round excess scale only according to the transaction's explicit rounding rule.

**Exception / edge case:** Intermediate calculations retain full configured precision and round only at defined posting or settlement boundaries.

**Security and audit implications:** Database constraints and service validation reject NaN/infinity and invalid scale; audit calculations retain input values and applied rounding rule.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Number parsing accepts the user's locale-specific decimal/group separators unambiguously; API canonical amounts use locale-independent decimal representation.

**Verification method:** Database integration tests compare exact decimal values and test overflow and excess-scale inputs.

**REQUIREMENT 0011 OF 1120  |  FINANCE, ACCOUNTING, TAX, AND CONTROLS**

## ERP-FINANCE-011 — Journal source identity and idempotency

**Normative requirement:** The system shall assign each journal a unique entity-ledger identifier and enforce idempotency for externally submitted source keys within a configured source namespace.

**Rationale:** Retries from integrations must not create duplicate financial postings.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Submitting the same source key and identical payload twice returns the original posting reference and creates one journal.

**AC 2.** Submitting the same source key with a different payload returns a conflict and creates no second journal.

**Exception / edge case:** A source system reusing identifiers across namespaces is accepted only when it supplies a distinct configured namespace.

**Security and audit implications:** Idempotency records are tenant-scoped and tamper-evident; response details disclose no other tenant's source key or document data.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** External identifiers are preserved without locale transformations; user-visible conflict messages are translated.

**Verification method:** Automated retry and concurrent duplicate-submission tests across tenant boundaries.

**REQUIREMENT 0012 OF 1120  |  FINANCE, ACCOUNTING, TAX, AND CONTROLS**

## ERP-FINANCE-012 — Recurring journal templates

**Normative requirement:** The system shall support approved recurring-journal templates with schedule, date rules, line definitions, and generation previews that create drafts rather than bypassing posting controls.

**Rationale:** Repeatable accruals and allocations need controlled generation and review.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A monthly template generates exactly one draft per eligible period and records the template revision used.

**AC 2.** A generated draft fails validation and remains unposted when an account or required dimension becomes invalid.

**Exception / edge case:** If a scheduled date falls in a closed period, the draft is held for reassignment or exception handling according to policy; it is not silently shifted.

**Security and audit implications:** Only authorized preparers and approvers can edit/activate templates; generated journals link to the template version and scheduler identity.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Schedule descriptions, dates, and generated narrative use locale-aware formatting; numeric values remain exact.

**Verification method:** Time-controlled scheduler tests covering duplicate run, calendar boundary, invalid account, and closed-period scenarios.

**REQUIREMENT 0013 OF 1120  |  FINANCE, ACCOUNTING, TAX, AND CONTROLS**

## ERP-FINANCE-013 — Journal workflow and approval

**Normative requirement:** The system shall route journals through configurable preparation, validation, and approval states using amount, source, entity, and risk rules before posting.

**Rationale:** Approval thresholds and controls vary by organization and should be data-configurable.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A journal above a configured threshold cannot be posted by its preparer when approval is required.

**AC 2.** The system records approver, decision, timestamp, comments, and the exact journal revision approved.

**Exception / edge case:** A journal edit after approval invalidates the approval and returns the journal to the required review state.

**Security and audit implications:** Approval role and amount threshold changes are protected; enforce preparer/approver separation when configured and log rejected attempts.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Workflow status and approver messages are localized; stored comments retain original language and timestamp.

**Verification method:** Workflow integration tests for thresholds, edit-after-approval, delegation, and unauthorized posting.

**REQUIREMENT 0014 OF 1120  |  FINANCE, ACCOUNTING, TAX, AND CONTROLS**

## ERP-FINANCE-014 — Posted journal immutability

**Normative requirement:** The system shall prevent alteration or deletion of posted journal headers and lines and preserve the original posted content as append-only accounting evidence.

**Rationale:** Immutable posted records preserve a reliable audit trail and reproducibility.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Update and delete attempts against a posted entry through every public API return a conflict/authorization failure and leave the record unchanged.

**AC 2.** A privileged correction creates a separately identified compensating entry linked to the original, leaving original values unchanged.

**Exception / edge case:** A lawful privacy or retention action may restrict access to associated personal data but must not rewrite the accounting facts or audit references without approved legal design.

**Security and audit implications:** Application and database roles separate posting from maintenance; administrative database access is audited and cannot silently alter the ledger.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Historical descriptions and text remain stored in their entered language; displays may add translations but never overwrite originals.

**Verification method:** Negative API/database authorization tests plus tamper-evidence and correction-link inspection.

**REQUIREMENT 0015 OF 1120  |  FINANCE, ACCOUNTING, TAX, AND CONTROLS**

## ERP-FINANCE-015 — Correction by reversal and replacement

**Normative requirement:** The system shall correct a posted journal only through a linked reversal or adjustment journal with reason, date, reference, and independent approval where policy requires.

**Rationale:** Correction by new entries preserves the original event and creates a reconstructable history.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Reversal creation copies opposite signed values and references original entry and lines; original remains unchanged.

**AC 2.** The system blocks reversal in a closed period unless the user selects an authorized open/adjustment period and records the reason.

**Exception / edge case:** A partial reversal requires explicit line-level quantities or amounts and may not exceed the remaining unreversed balance.

**Security and audit implications:** Only permitted finance roles can request and approve corrections; link audit records in both directions.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Reasons are translatable for UI prompts while retaining the submitted original-language text.

**Verification method:** Integration tests for full/partial reversal, concurrent reversals, closed period, and audit links.

**REQUIREMENT 0016 OF 1120  |  FINANCE, ACCOUNTING, TAX, AND CONTROLS**

## ERP-FINANCE-016 — Document numbering sequences

**Normative requirement:** The system shall issue document numbers from entity- and document-type-specific sequences with concurrency safety and configurable gap-handling policy.

**Rationale:** Number formats and legal sequence requirements differ by document type and jurisdiction.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Concurrent requests receive distinct numbers from the correct entity/type sequence.

**AC 2.** A voided number remains recorded with status and reason, and is not silently reassigned when the configured policy prohibits reuse.

**Exception / edge case:** A jurisdictional continuous sequence or gapless rule is enabled only through local configuration and an approved legal policy; technical rollback behavior is disclosed to administrators.

**Security and audit implications:** Sequence configuration is privileged and versioned; issuance and void events are auditable and tenant scoped.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Prefixes, scripts, and date segments are presentation/configuration components; stored sequence ordering is locale-independent.

**Verification method:** Concurrency and rollback tests plus sequence audit-history inspection.

**REQUIREMENT 0017 OF 1120  |  FINANCE, ACCOUNTING, TAX, AND CONTROLS**

## ERP-FINANCE-017 — Accounting policy and basis assignments

**Normative requirement:** The system shall associate each ledger with an explicit accounting basis and versioned policy set, including entity-specific mapping and transition dates.

**Rationale:** IFRS, local GAAP, tax books, and management reporting differ; a shared product must not imply one universal basis.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A posted ledger identifies the policy version effective for its accounting date.

**AC 2.** A policy update affects future transactions only unless an approved restatement workflow creates separately traceable adjustments.

**Exception / edge case:** A group may maintain parallel ledgers under different bases, but one posting cannot silently switch its basis after approval.

**Security and audit implications:** Policy publishing requires authorized finance approval and stores a change diff; reports reveal the basis used.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Basis name and policy disclosures may be localized; the machine-readable basis identifier remains stable.

**Verification method:** Configuration and reporting tests with parallel basis ledgers and dated policy revisions.

**REQUIREMENT 0018 OF 1120  |  FINANCE, ACCOUNTING, TAX, AND CONTROLS**

## ERP-FINANCE-018 — Subledger-to-general-ledger reconciliation

**Normative requirement:** The system shall provide a controlled interface that posts subledger control totals to the general ledger with source references, batch identifiers, and reconciliation status.

**Rationale:** AP, AR, and assets must reconcile to the general ledger at a known posting boundary.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** For a completed subledger batch, the control account debit/credit totals equal the associated GL journal totals by ledger and currency.

**AC 2.** A mismatch prevents the batch from being marked reconciled and produces a line-level exception report.

**Exception / edge case:** A legitimate timing difference remains separately identified as pending and cannot be mislabeled as a completed reconciliation.

**Security and audit implications:** Batch import and reconciliation permissions are distinct; store source event IDs and immutable batch lineage.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Reconciliation reports use ledger currency codes and locale formatting, with canonical IDs unaffected by translated captions.

**Verification method:** End-to-end subledger posting and reconciliation tests with mismatch and duplicate batch cases.

**REQUIREMENT 0019 OF 1120  |  FINANCE, ACCOUNTING, TAX, AND CONTROLS**

## ERP-FINANCE-019 — Supplier tax identity and master validation

**Normative requirement:** The system shall maintain supplier legal name, jurisdiction, tax identifiers, withholding classifications, and validity evidence as effective-dated, jurisdiction-specific attributes.

**Rationale:** Tax identity requirements depend on local law and counterparty status.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A supplier configured as tax-registered cannot be activated for tax-controlled transactions while required jurisdiction fields are missing or fail configured validation.

**AC 2.** A valid-from/to tax registration change is resolved according to the invoice tax point date.

**Exception / edge case:** The platform shall not assume a single global tax-ID syntax or infer registration status when no authority validation is configured.

**Security and audit implications:** Access to bank/tax identifiers is restricted and field-change audit events capture old/new values and evidence reference without logging secrets.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Legal names support Unicode and original script; addresses and identifier validations are jurisdiction-specific and messages are localized.

**Verification method:** Country-profile validation tests with valid, invalid, expired, and unverified supplier records.

**REQUIREMENT 0020 OF 1120  |  FINANCE, ACCOUNTING, TAX, AND CONTROLS**

## ERP-FINANCE-020 — Supplier invoice capture and matching

**Normative requirement:** The system shall capture supplier invoice identity, dates, currency, lines, tax components, and optional purchase-order/receipt references, then expose configurable two-/three-way match outcomes.

**Rationale:** Invoice matching and mandatory fields vary with procurement policy and industry.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A matched invoice whose configured quantity, price, and receipt tolerances are met is eligible for approval.

**AC 2.** An invoice outside a configured tolerance receives a named hold reason and cannot proceed as a clean match.

**Exception / edge case:** A non-PO invoice may proceed only when the entity's workflow policy permits it and the required coding and approval are completed.

**Security and audit implications:** Invoice attachment access follows finance document permissions; file hash and source metadata are retained; prevent cross-tenant retrieval.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Supplier-provided descriptions and legal names are retained as entered; dates, decimals, and address fields parse using declared locale/format.

**Verification method:** Workflow tests for PO/receipt matches, tolerance boundary, missing receipt, and non-PO policy.

**REQUIREMENT 0021 OF 1120  |  FINANCE, ACCOUNTING, TAX, AND CONTROLS**

## ERP-FINANCE-021 — Supplier invoice tax determination

**Normative requirement:** The system shall determine supplier invoice tax only from a selected jurisdictional tax profile, transaction facts, effective-dated rules, and configured accounting treatment.

**Rationale:** Taxability and recovery are determined by applicable law, not by a globally fixed product default.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** For an invoice with a configured valid tax code and effective rate, stored tax components reconcile to configured computation and rule version.

**AC 2.** When jurisdiction, place-of-supply, tax point, or required counterparty facts are unresolved, the invoice is blocked or flagged per approved policy rather than assigned an assumed rate.

**Exception / edge case:** Reverse-charge, self-assessment, and import tax scenarios are enabled only through relevant local tax configurations.

**Security and audit implications:** Only tax administrators can publish rules; the determination record captures input facts, rule version, calculation, and override actor.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Tax labels, legal wording, invoice dates, and amounts are localized; canonical rates and code values are stable.

**Verification method:** Rule-engine tests against approved jurisdiction fixtures and trace inspection for a resolved/blocked case.

**REQUIREMENT 0022 OF 1120  |  FINANCE, ACCOUNTING, TAX, AND CONTROLS**

## ERP-FINANCE-022 — Duplicate supplier invoice control

**Normative requirement:** The system shall detect possible duplicate supplier invoices using configurable supplier, document number, date, amount, and currency keys and apply policy-defined blocks or review holds.

**Rationale:** Duplicate controls reduce duplicate disbursement while allowing legitimate recurring or corrected documents.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A repeated supplier/document-number/currency combination is surfaced before approval with a link to the prior invoice.

**AC 2.** A documented authorized override records reason and approver and does not delete the duplicate warning.

**Exception / edge case:** Same supplier number reused in distinct legal entities or fiscal contexts follows configurable uniqueness scope and must not be automatically rejected across unrelated entities.

**Security and audit implications:** Search and similarity responses are restricted to authorized AP users and include no data from another tenant.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Normalization may trim/normalize for candidate detection but the original supplier reference is retained and displayed correctly in its script.

**Verification method:** Duplicate-detection tests across exact/near matches, entity scope, and override audit trail.

**REQUIREMENT 0023 OF 1120  |  FINANCE, ACCOUNTING, TAX, AND CONTROLS**

## ERP-FINANCE-023 — Payment proposal generation

**Normative requirement:** The system shall generate payment proposals from approved, due, undisputed payables using payment terms, cash availability, currency, and configured payment-method eligibility.

**Rationale:** Separating proposal from execution enables review and cash-control decisions.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A proposal includes each selected invoice exactly once and exposes due date, discount, currency, hold, and exclusion reason.

**AC 2.** Changing a supplier bank account or invoice hold after proposal creation invalidates or revalidates the proposal before approval.

**Exception / edge case:** Partial payments, netting, and discounts are selected only when enabled by entity policy and the proposal shows the computation.

**Security and audit implications:** Proposal creators cannot silently change verified beneficiary data; proposed batches are access controlled and sensitive bank fields are masked.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Payment dates and amounts are locale-rendered; bank instructions use the receiving rail's required encoding rather than UI locale assumptions.

**Verification method:** Payment selection tests with due-date, holds, currency, stale master data, and partial-payment policy.

**REQUIREMENT 0024 OF 1120  |  FINANCE, ACCOUNTING, TAX, AND CONTROLS**

## ERP-FINANCE-024 — Payment maker-checker approval

**Normative requirement:** The system shall require independent approval of payment batches according to configurable value, currency, entity, and risk thresholds before release to an external payment channel.

**Rationale:** Independent approval limits unauthorized or erroneous disbursement.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A batch above a configured limit is not releasable until an eligible approver who is not the preparer approves it.

**AC 2.** Any change to beneficiary, amount, currency, or batch membership after approval resets the required approval state.

**Exception / edge case:** An emergency override requires a separately configured authorized role, documented reason, and post-event review; it is not an unlogged bypass.

**Security and audit implications:** Enforce separation of duties and least privilege; audit approval decisions and prevent approver identity spoofing.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Approver workflow content is translated, while amounts include currency code and exact canonical payment values.

**Verification method:** Authorization matrix tests for same-user attempts, threshold boundaries, post-approval mutations, and override.

**REQUIREMENT 0025 OF 1120  |  FINANCE, ACCOUNTING, TAX, AND CONTROLS**

## ERP-FINANCE-025 — Payment execution status interface

**Normative requirement:** The system shall integrate payment release through an authorized provider interface and track submitted, accepted, rejected, settled, and returned outcomes with idempotent external references.

**Rationale:** Payment execution is asynchronous and may fail after ERP approval; ledger status must reflect verified provider results.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A retried release request with the same idempotency key creates one provider instruction and returns the same reference.

**AC 2.** A rejected or returned payment does not mark the payable settled and creates a reconciliation exception with provider reason.

**Exception / edge case:** An unknown provider outcome remains pending investigation and cannot be auto-classified as paid.

**Security and audit implications:** External credentials are held outside application data and logs; release capability is narrowly scoped, independently authorized, and fully audited.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Provider codes are mapped to stable internal states with localized descriptions; preserve the provider's original response for support/audit.

**Verification method:** Sandbox provider contract tests for success, timeout, duplicate retry, rejection, return, and unknown status.

**REQUIREMENT 0026 OF 1120  |  FINANCE, ACCOUNTING, TAX, AND CONTROLS**

## ERP-FINANCE-026 — Supplier credit and debit adjustments

**Normative requirement:** The system shall record supplier credit/debit adjustments as separately approved documents linked to affected invoices and tax components, then post their accounting impact through configured rules.

**Rationale:** Credit adjustments require traceable application and potentially distinct tax treatment.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A credit note applied to an invoice reduces open balance by the applied amount and retains its own source document identifier.

**AC 2.** An adjustment with tax treatment inconsistent with its configured jurisdictional rule cannot be posted without authorized exception approval.

**Exception / edge case:** A credit exceeding the remaining invoice balance is left unapplied or handled by an explicit refund/netting workflow, never silently discarded.

**Security and audit implications:** Document edits and allocations are audited; only authorized roles may override tax or apply a credit across entities.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Supplier document text and references retain source language; reports localize amounts and preserve tax-code identifiers.

**Verification method:** AP integration tests for partial/excess credit, allocation, tax mismatch, and posting lineage.

**REQUIREMENT 0027 OF 1120  |  FINANCE, ACCOUNTING, TAX, AND CONTROLS**

## ERP-FINANCE-027 — Customer invoice issuance

**Normative requirement:** The system shall create customer invoices from approved billing facts with entity, customer, lines, currency, tax point, payment terms, and jurisdiction-specific tax determination before issuance.

**Rationale:** Invoice content and tax documents depend on jurisdiction, customer status, and industry rules.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** An issued invoice stores the approved calculation inputs, tax-rule version, document number, and immutable issued snapshot.

**AC 2.** Issuance is blocked when mandatory configured customer, address, tax, or jurisdiction data is absent.

**Exception / edge case:** An invoice's accounting date and tax point date may differ only when the local configuration explicitly supports that distinction.

**Security and audit implications:** Invoice issuance is permissioned; snapshot, numbering event, tax determination and actor are linked in the audit trail.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Support UTF-8 legal names and address forms; generate document language and number/date/amount formats from entity and customer policy, not browser language alone.

**Verification method:** Invoice tests for complete/incomplete facts, immutable issuance, number uniqueness, and locale variants.

**REQUIREMENT 0028 OF 1120  |  FINANCE, ACCOUNTING, TAX, AND CONTROLS**

## ERP-FINANCE-028 — Customer credit notes and cancellations

**Normative requirement:** The system shall issue corrections to an issued customer invoice as linked credit/debit notes or legally configured cancellation documents without altering the issued source document.

**Rationale:** Issued invoices need a legally traceable correction history.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A credit note references its source invoice and its signed tax/accounting impact is visible in both document histories.

**AC 2.** The system blocks direct edit/delete of an issued invoice and requires configured correction-document reason and numbering.

**Exception / edge case:** A cancellation method is jurisdiction-specific and unavailable unless its policy and document schema are configured for that entity.

**Security and audit implications:** Issuance, approval, and cancellation permissions are separate where policy requires; maintain tamper-evident references.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** The correction document may use a legally required language and must preserve original invoice text/amounts while localizing interface prompts.

**Verification method:** Integration tests for credit, cancellation, wrong-source rejection, and original snapshot immutability.

**REQUIREMENT 0029 OF 1120  |  FINANCE, ACCOUNTING, TAX, AND CONTROLS**

## ERP-FINANCE-029 — Customer receipt allocation
