**Normative requirement:** The system shall record receipts with bank/cash source, amount, date, currency, payer reference, and allocate them to one or more customer receivables with auditable residual balance.

**Rationale:** Allocation supports partial and multi-invoice settlement without losing receipt provenance.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Allocating a receipt updates applied and unapplied amounts so that applied plus unapplied equals the received amount exactly.

**AC 2.** An allocation to an already closed, reversed, or wrong-customer invoice is rejected unless an authorized reallocation flow is used.

**Exception / edge case:** A receipt in a different currency requires a configured conversion and stores both receipt and settlement values plus exchange difference.

**Security and audit implications:** Only authorized cash application staff can reallocate; capture old/new targets and reason; sensitive remittance data is protected.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Payer names and remittance references preserve Unicode; date and amount input follows explicit locale with canonical API values.

**Verification method:** Property and integration tests for partial/multiple allocations, currency, reversal, and sum invariant.

**REQUIREMENT 0030 OF 1120  |  FINANCE, ACCOUNTING, TAX, AND CONTROLS**

## ERP-FINANCE-030 — Unapplied cash and on-account receipts

**Normative requirement:** The system shall retain unidentified or excess customer receipts in an on-account state with a responsible owner, aging, and supported later allocation or refund workflow.

**Rationale:** Unapplied receipts must not be concealed or incorrectly treated as revenue.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A receipt with no invoice allocation appears in the unapplied-cash worklist and is excluded from settled AR totals.

**AC 2.** Applying or refunding an unapplied receipt changes its state and retains a link to the original receipt and approval.

**Exception / edge case:** A payer overpayment remains on account unless refund/netting is explicitly selected under policy.

**Security and audit implications:** Refund initiation requires payment-control permissions and independent approval; account balances are tenant/entity scoped.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Worklist reasons and contact templates are localized; original remittance text is preserved unmodified.

**Verification method:** AR workflow tests for unallocated, partial, excess, allocation, refund, and aging visibility.

**REQUIREMENT 0031 OF 1120  |  FINANCE, ACCOUNTING, TAX, AND CONTROLS**

## ERP-FINANCE-031 — Receivables aging and dunning

**Normative requirement:** The system shall calculate receivables aging from configurable due-date or invoice-date buckets and generate dunning worklists using entity-approved collection rules.

**Rationale:** Aging bases and collection practices vary; reproducible bucket logic supports operations and reporting.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** For a fixed as-of date, a fixture of due dates lands in the configured aging buckets with exact open balance totals.

**AC 2.** A disputed, legally held, or payment-plan account is excluded from automatic dunning when its configured suppression applies.

**Exception / edge case:** Aging cutoff at local midnight uses the entity's configured business timezone, even if the operator is in a different locale.

**Security and audit implications:** Access to customer balances and correspondence is role-restricted; record rule version and outbound contact decision.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Age bucket labels, statement dates, and customer correspondence are localized; the chosen as-of date and currency are explicit.

**Verification method:** Deterministic as-of-date tests with timezone boundaries, credit balances, dispute holds, and multiple currencies.

**REQUIREMENT 0032 OF 1120  |  FINANCE, ACCOUNTING, TAX, AND CONTROLS**

## ERP-FINANCE-032 — Tax code and rate registry

**Normative requirement:** The system shall maintain jurisdiction-scoped tax codes with effective dates, taxable basis, rate components, recoverability, reporting category, and rule provenance.

**Rationale:** Tax rates and classification labels change; records must be selected using legally relevant dates.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** For a transaction date before and after a configured rate change, the engine selects the corresponding effective tax code revision.

**AC 2.** Reject publishing a tax code with overlapping conflicting effective ranges or missing required reporting mapping.

**Exception / edge case:** A zero or exempt rate is distinct from an unconfigured rate and requires a configured reason/category.

**Security and audit implications:** Only tax administrators publish rule revisions; all downstream documents store the selected revision and any override event.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Tax descriptions support jurisdiction-specific legal language and multiple scripts; stored codes are stable, and numeric rates avoid locale-dependent parsing.

**Verification method:** Rule registry tests for date boundaries, overlapping intervals, zero/exempt distinction, and revision lineage.

**REQUIREMENT 0033 OF 1120  |  FINANCE, ACCOUNTING, TAX, AND CONTROLS**

## ERP-FINANCE-033 — Jurisdiction and tax profile configuration

**Normative requirement:** The system shall require each tax-bearing transaction to resolve an explicitly configured tax jurisdiction and profile from relevant business facts, without a universal country-rate fallback.

**Rationale:** Place-of-supply, registration, tax point, and industry rules vary materially by jurisdiction.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A transaction with missing mandatory jurisdiction facts is blocked or routed to a configured exception queue.

**AC 2.** Two jurisdictions with conflicting applicable profiles return a review-required state rather than choosing silently.

**Exception / edge case:** Cross-border, digital-service, marketplace, and permanent-establishment cases require explicit local profile rules when relevant.

**Security and audit implications:** Tax profile edits require authorized role and approval; retain resolved jurisdiction facts and rule explanation for audit.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Jurisdiction names and prompts are localized; country subdivisions and identifiers follow the configuration data source and remain machine-stable.

**Verification method:** Scenario tests with domestic, cross-border, unresolved, and competing-jurisdiction facts.

**REQUIREMENT 0034 OF 1120  |  FINANCE, ACCOUNTING, TAX, AND CONTROLS**

## ERP-FINANCE-034 — Tax exemption and zero-rating evidence

**Normative requirement:** The system shall capture the exemption/zero-rating basis, jurisdictional reason code, supporting evidence reference, validity dates, and counterparty scope where required by configured policy.

**Rationale:** Exemption conditions and documentary evidence requirements differ by law and transaction category.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A tax-exempt transaction subject to evidence-required policy cannot be finalized until a valid evidence reference and reason are supplied.

**AC 2.** An expired or counterparty-mismatched certificate fails validation for a transaction on the test date.

**Exception / edge case:** Evidence-required rules may allow an approved provisional hold state when local policy permits, but must not silently claim a final exemption.

**Security and audit implications:** Evidence files are protected and retention/access is controlled; viewing or overriding evidence status is audited.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Evidence metadata may be in the source language and script; reason labels are localized, with the legal code preserved.

**Verification method:** Validation tests for valid, expired, missing, mismatched, and provisional evidence cases.

**REQUIREMENT 0035 OF 1120  |  FINANCE, ACCOUNTING, TAX, AND CONTROLS**

## ERP-FINANCE-035 — Tax calculation and rounding policy

**Normative requirement:** The system shall calculate each tax component using a configured jurisdictional rounding method, scale, calculation level, and allocation method, storing unrounded basis and final rounded values.

**Rationale:** Tax computation may round per line or document and small differences can affect filing totals.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A golden test fixture produces the expected line and document totals under each configured rounding method.

**AC 2.** A credit/reversal uses the configured sign and rounding treatment and reconciles to the original transaction's tax component.

**Exception / edge case:** Where tax authority totals differ from a line-summed amount, a configured adjustment/rounding line is used and remains separately visible.

**Security and audit implications:** Rounding policy changes are approved/versioned; store the algorithm, scale, basis, and rule version with calculation evidence.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Rounding uses exact decimals, never locale separators; user-visible explanations format according to locale and currency.

**Verification method:** Deterministic golden tests for half values, negative values, multi-line allocations, and credit-note reversal.

**REQUIREMENT 0036 OF 1120  |  FINANCE, ACCOUNTING, TAX, AND CONTROLS**

## ERP-FINANCE-036 — Tax return mapping and workpapers

**Normative requirement:** The system shall map posted tax components to versioned jurisdictional return boxes and generate reproducible workpapers with transaction-level drill-through.

**Rationale:** Tax return layouts are jurisdiction- and period-specific and should be version-controlled, not universal.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A sample period's mapped box totals equal the sum of eligible source tax components and display the mapping version.

**AC 2.** A changed mapping creates a new version and does not silently alter a previously finalized return snapshot.

**Exception / edge case:** A filing form change effective mid-year may require period- or filing-version-specific mappings and is explicitly selectable.

**Security and audit implications:** Return preparation, review, and finalization permissions are distinct; export and changes to mappings are audited.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Labels, filing instructions, and generated narratives support the jurisdiction's required language; calculation keys and amounts are locale-neutral.

**Verification method:** Reconciliation tests from source tax entries to boxes, including effective mapping and finalized snapshot.

**REQUIREMENT 0037 OF 1120  |  FINANCE, ACCOUNTING, TAX, AND CONTROLS**

## ERP-FINANCE-037 — Electronic invoice adapter

**Normative requirement:** The system shall expose jurisdiction-specific electronic-invoice adapters that validate the required schema, submit documents, persist authority responses, and update status without changing the accounting source document.

**Rationale:** Digital reporting models range from batch files to real-time APIs and vary across authorities.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A valid configured document serializes to the adapter's schema and receives an external correlation ID and response state.

**AC 2.** Schema rejection or authority rejection leaves the issued ERP invoice intact, records the failure, and places it in a retry/correction queue.

**Exception / edge case:** Where law requires real-time acceptance before legal issuance, that gating behavior must be explicit in the local adapter configuration rather than assumed globally.

**Security and audit implications:** Authority credentials are encrypted and segregated by entity/environment; submissions are idempotent and immutable request/response evidence is access-controlled.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Support jurisdiction-required language, character sets, decimals, timezone, and canonical document identifiers; store original authority message and localized summary.

**Verification method:** Contract tests against published authority test schemas/sandboxes and replay tests for timeout, duplicate, reject, and accepted response.

**REQUIREMENT 0038 OF 1120  |  FINANCE, ACCOUNTING, TAX, AND CONTROLS**

## ERP-FINANCE-038 — Structured tax audit export

**Normative requirement:** The system shall produce tax audit exports using the selected jurisdiction's currently approved schema and include schema version, period, source lineage, and export validation results.

**Rationale:** OECD describes SAF-T as a standardised structured accounting/tax data file, while national adoption and schema details vary.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** An export for a configured schema passes local schema validation and reports row counts and totals by required record type.

**AC 2.** An unsupported or superseded schema version blocks export or requires an authorized selection with a warning and logged rationale.

**Exception / edge case:** A regulator's national extension or filing-specific variant is modeled as a separate adapter/schema version, not presented as universal OECD law.

**Security and audit implications:** Bulk exports require explicit permission, are encrypted at rest/in transit, logged, and scoped to one authorized entity/period.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Export strings preserve legal source language and Unicode; numeric/date serialization is canonical and conforms to the selected schema, not the user's display locale.

**Verification method:** Golden-file and schema-validation tests against the authority/OECD version configured for the test jurisdiction.

**REQUIREMENT 0039 OF 1120  |  FINANCE, ACCOUNTING, TAX, AND CONTROLS**

## ERP-FINANCE-039 — Recoverable and nonrecoverable input tax

**Normative requirement:** The system shall record recoverability classification and deductible/non-deductible tax amounts separately according to an effective-dated jurisdiction and transaction policy.

**Rationale:** Input-tax recovery can depend on use, evidence, taxpayer status, and local limitation rules.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A configured partial recovery percentage splits a tax amount into recoverable and nonrecoverable components whose exact sum equals the source tax.

**AC 2.** A transaction lacking a required recovery classification is held from final tax reporting and exposes the missing decision.

**Exception / edge case:** Mixed-use allocations require a configured approved allocation basis and may be trued up through a linked adjustment.

**Security and audit implications:** Recovery overrides require tax authority and reason; preserve original tax amount and allocation basis in audit record.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Labels for deductible/non-deductible categories and legal reasoning can be localized; calculations remain based on exact stored values.

**Verification method:** Rule-engine tests for full, partial, zero, missing, and adjusted recovery cases.

**REQUIREMENT 0040 OF 1120  |  FINANCE, ACCOUNTING, TAX, AND CONTROLS**

## ERP-FINANCE-040 — Withholding tax computation

**Normative requirement:** The system shall support jurisdiction-specific withholding tax profiles on eligible payable or receivable events, with configurable bases, rates, thresholds, certificates, and remittance reporting.

**Rationale:** Withholding rates and timing differ by jurisdiction and payment type.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A valid effective profile computes the configured withholding amount and links the resulting liability to the source document/payment.

**AC 2.** A missing or expired required certificate or tax profile blocks or routes the transaction according to explicit configured policy.

**Exception / edge case:** Threshold aggregation across multiple transactions is performed only where the jurisdiction profile defines the aggregation scope and period.

**Security and audit implications:** Only tax roles configure withholding; payment release cannot alter withholding liability without a logged approved adjustment.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Certificates and remittance documents preserve required local script/language; amounts and tax IDs serialize to required authority format.

**Verification method:** Scenario tests for threshold boundaries, certificate state, multiple payment aggregation, and liability reconciliation.

**REQUIREMENT 0041 OF 1120  |  FINANCE, ACCOUNTING, TAX, AND CONTROLS**

## ERP-FINANCE-041 — Tax liability reconciliation

**Normative requirement:** The system shall reconcile tax return workpapers, tax control accounts, and tax payment/refund transactions for a selected entity and reporting period, surfacing variances by source and tax category.

**Rationale:** A filing total, ledger balance, and payment must be traceable without presuming they are identical at every cut-off.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** For a balanced fixture, the reconciliation shows zero unexplained difference across mapped tax categories.

**AC 2.** When a source tax line is missing or duplicated, the reconciliation flags its source identifier and amount without auto-adjusting posted data.

**Exception / edge case:** Timing, foreign exchange, and prior-period adjustments appear as separately classified reconciling items rather than concealed netting.

**Security and audit implications:** Reconciliation sign-off is permissioned and immutable after approval except through a reopened, logged workflow.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Tax labels and report formats are localized; the as-of date, currency, and jurisdiction are explicit on each output.

**Verification method:** Integration tests inject missing, duplicate, timing, FX, and adjustment variances and assert traceable results.

**REQUIREMENT 0042 OF 1120  |  FINANCE, ACCOUNTING, TAX, AND CONTROLS**

## ERP-FINANCE-042 — Tax rule publication and change impact

**Normative requirement:** The system shall version tax rules and require a publish workflow that identifies effective date, jurisdiction, source reference, preparer, approver, and impacted transactions before activation.

**Rationale:** Tax law and authority specifications change; changes need controlled rollout and historical reproducibility.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A draft rule is not applied to production transactions until approved and published with a future or immediate effective date.

**AC 2.** Publishing an effective rule produces an impact preview listing affected open documents and does not mutate finalized historical documents.

**Exception / edge case:** Urgent retrospective rule changes may be recorded for a correction workflow, but cannot rewrite posted/issued evidence automatically.

**Security and audit implications:** Rule author and approver separation is enforced where configured; source references and change history are retained.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Legal source title and text may be stored in original language with translated internal summary; effective dates render per locale.

**Verification method:** Workflow tests for draft/publish, overlap validation, impact preview, and retroactive correction handling.

**REQUIREMENT 0043 OF 1120  |  FINANCE, ACCOUNTING, TAX, AND CONTROLS**

## ERP-FINANCE-043 — Fixed-asset register and capitalization

**Normative requirement:** The system shall maintain fixed-asset records with acquisition evidence, cost components, in-service date, asset class, book/tax basis, location, and linked GL balances.

**Rationale:** Capitalization thresholds, asset classes, and tax basis are configurable accounting/jurisdiction policies.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** An asset created from an approved acquisition retains source invoice and cost-line lineage and appears in the relevant register.

**AC 2.** Reject capitalization when mandatory class, in-service date, or ledger basis configuration is missing.

**Exception / edge case:** A low-value item may be expensed or pooled only under configured policy; no universal monetary threshold is presumed.

**Security and audit implications:** Asset master changes, transfers, and basis additions are permissioned and audited; protect sensitive asset location where applicable.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Asset descriptions support localized text; dates, amounts, units, and translated class labels are locale-aware while codes remain stable.

**Verification method:** Asset lifecycle tests for acquisition, mandatory-field validation, GL link, and localized register output.

**REQUIREMENT 0044 OF 1120  |  FINANCE, ACCOUNTING, TAX, AND CONTROLS**

## ERP-FINANCE-044 — Depreciation method and run control

**Normative requirement:** The system shall calculate depreciation from versioned asset methods, useful-life parameters, residual values, conventions, calendars, and accounting bases, with preview and controlled posting.

**Rationale:** Methods, conventions, and useful lives depend on the reporting policy and asset class.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A test asset's periodic depreciation matches the configured method and schedule to the expected precision.

**AC 2.** A depreciation run preview reports proposed amounts and the final posting batch references its run ID and parameter version.

**Exception / edge case:** A change in useful life or method is effective-dated and follows configured prospective/retrospective policy; it does not overwrite prior posted runs.

**Security and audit implications:** Run preparation and posting are separated; run inputs, calculation output, approvals, and resulting GL journal are auditable.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Periods and amounts display in the entity locale; method codes remain stable and accounting basis is shown explicitly.

**Verification method:** Golden calculation tests for straight-line and enabled methods, conventions, final-period residual, and change-effective-date.

**REQUIREMENT 0045 OF 1120  |  FINANCE, ACCOUNTING, TAX, AND CONTROLS**

## ERP-FINANCE-045 — Asset transfer, impairment, and disposal

**Normative requirement:** The system shall process asset transfers, impairment/write-down, retirement, and disposal as approved dated events that calculate configured book/tax impacts and post linked journals.

**Rationale:** Asset events need lifecycle history and policy-specific accounting treatment.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Disposal proceeds, carrying amount, and gain/loss components reconcile to the generated journal for a configured scenario.

**AC 2.** A transfer changes custodian/location from its effective date while retaining prior assignments and balances.

**Exception / edge case:** A partially disposed component requires an explicit component/quantity basis; a fully disposed asset cannot receive future depreciation.

**Security and audit implications:** Disposal and impairment permissions are restricted; capture approvals, evidence references, and prior/current asset state.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Descriptions and evidence may be multilingual; amounts use currency-specific precision and transaction date uses entity fiscal calendar.

**Verification method:** Lifecycle integration tests for transfer, partial/full disposal, impairment, and depreciation-stop behavior.

**REQUIREMENT 0046 OF 1120  |  FINANCE, ACCOUNTING, TAX, AND CONTROLS**

## ERP-FINANCE-046 — Industry accounting extension boundary

**Normative requirement:** The system shall implement industry-specific finance behavior as versioned extensions or configuration packages that declare prerequisite facts, posting rules, reports, and jurisdictions, without changing the universal ledger contract.

**Rationale:** Revenue, fund, project, inventory, insurance, and other specialist accounting differ by industry and must not be implied as universal rules.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Installing an extension adds its declared entities/rules without changing balances or semantics of an existing core ledger fixture.

**AC 2.** An extension cannot publish a tax or recognition rule until its jurisdiction and accounting basis prerequisites are configured.

**Exception / edge case:** Unsupported industry treatments remain explicitly out of scope and are reported as a configuration gap, not silently approximated.

**Security and audit implications:** Extensions are signed/versioned, least-privileged, audited on activation, and cannot access another tenant's records.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Extension labels and required legal notices are translatable; extension identifiers and migration keys remain locale-neutral.

**Verification method:** Extension compatibility tests against core ledger contracts and prerequisite-validation tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0047 OF 1120  |  FINANCE, ACCOUNTING, TAX, AND CONTROLS**

## ERP-FINANCE-047 — Bank statement import and normalization

**Normative requirement:** The system shall import bank statements through configured formats or provider interfaces, retain the original file/reference and hash, normalize entries to a canonical model, and report rejected rows.

**Rationale:** Bank formats and payment rails vary; retaining source evidence improves reconciliation and troubleshooting.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A valid statement produces canonical lines with bank account, currency, booking/value dates, signed amount, and source reference.

**AC 2.** A malformed or duplicate file is rejected or marked duplicate without silently creating duplicate cash entries.

**Exception / edge case:** Different date formats and debit/credit conventions are resolved only from an explicit bank-format profile, not inferred from display locale.

**Security and audit implications:** Bank files are malware-scanned where supported, encrypted and access-controlled; source hashes and import actor/time are recorded.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** File parsing supports declared encoding and locale conventions while storing normalized dates/decimals and original source text.

**Verification method:** Adapter contract tests for valid, malformed, duplicate, encoding, and debit/credit sign cases.

**REQUIREMENT 0048 OF 1120  |  FINANCE, ACCOUNTING, TAX, AND CONTROLS**

## ERP-FINANCE-048 — Bank reconciliation matching

**Normative requirement:** The system shall match imported bank lines to ledger cash transactions using configurable exact and tolerance-based criteria and preserve a reviewable match decision.

**Rationale:** Automated matching reduces manual work while uncertain matches require human review.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** An exact unique amount/date/reference match is proposed and confirmed according to configured policy.

**AC 2.** Two candidate ledger transactions within tolerance produce an ambiguous status and are not silently auto-cleared.

**Exception / edge case:** Partial settlement, fees, and foreign-currency settlement may use configured composite rules, each exposing the matched components.

**Security and audit implications:** Confirmation and rule changes require scoped permissions; retain match inputs, confidence/reason, user decision, and unmatch events.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Amounts show currency and localized dates; matching compares canonical numbers, dates, and references independent of visual formatting.

**Verification method:** Reconciliation tests for exact, tolerance, ambiguous, partial, fee, and reversed matches.

**REQUIREMENT 0049 OF 1120  |  FINANCE, ACCOUNTING, TAX, AND CONTROLS**

## ERP-FINANCE-049 — Reconciliation adjustments and write-offs

**Normative requirement:** The system shall create bank reconciliation adjustments only as separate balanced journals with configured accounts, reason codes, approval limits, and link to the statement line.

**Rationale:** Fees, interest, and write-offs can be recognized without mutating imported bank evidence.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** An approved bank fee adjustment creates a balanced linked journal and clears only the selected statement difference.

**AC 2.** An adjustment above a configured limit requires a different approver from its preparer.

**Exception / edge case:** An unexplained difference cannot be written off through a generic catch-all unless the entity explicitly enables and monitors that account.

**Security and audit implications:** Adjustment and write-off permissions are segregated; record original variance, journal link, explanation, and approver.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Adjustment reason captions are localized; numeric calculation and original statement currency remain explicit.

**Verification method:** Workflow tests for balanced adjustment, threshold separation, generic-account restriction, and audit linkage.

**REQUIREMENT 0050 OF 1120  |  FINANCE, ACCOUNTING, TAX, AND CONTROLS**

## ERP-FINANCE-050 — Foreign-currency revaluation

**Normative requirement:** The system shall revalue eligible open monetary balances at an approved period-end rate under a selected accounting basis and post the revaluation as a linked, reversible journal.

**Rationale:** Period-end measurement depends on accounting policy, item classification, and rate source.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A fixture with open monetary items and approved closing rates produces expected revaluation by account and currency.

**AC 2.** Repeating the same run ID or period does not create duplicate revaluation journals.

**Exception / edge case:** Nonmonetary items or balances excluded by the selected policy are reported as excluded with reason and are not revalued.

**Security and audit implications:** Rate sources, eligibility rules, run parameters, preview, approval, and reversal are audited; period lock is enforced.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Reports show source currency, functional currency, rate type/date, and localized output without losing canonical values.

**Verification method:** Calculation tests across gain/loss, excluded item, missing rate, rerun idempotency, and reversal.

**REQUIREMENT 0051 OF 1120  |  FINANCE, ACCOUNTING, TAX, AND CONTROLS**

## ERP-FINANCE-051 — Realized exchange differences

**Normative requirement:** The system shall calculate realized exchange differences at settlement from the original recognized functional amount, settlement amount, and configured accounting rule, posting linked gain/loss entries.

**Rationale:** Realized exchange gain/loss must reconcile the carrying value to the settlement event.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Settling an open foreign-currency payable or receivable records the source amount, settlement rate, realized difference, and linked journal.

**AC 2.** A partial settlement allocates only its settled portion and preserves the residual open amount and basis.

**Exception / edge case:** A settlement without an approved rate or with a previously settled amount is blocked or routed for correction, not double-recognized.

**Security and audit implications:** Settlement and rate edits after approval are restricted and audited; ensure idempotent source event processing.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** User locale affects presentation only; source and functional currency codes and rate direction are shown explicitly.

**Verification method:** Exact-decimal tests for gain/loss direction, partial settlement, repeated event, and missing rate.

**REQUIREMENT 0052 OF 1120  |  FINANCE, ACCOUNTING, TAX, AND CONTROLS**

## ERP-FINANCE-052 — Consolidation entity mapping

**Normative requirement:** The system shall maintain effective-dated mappings from entity accounts and dimensions to a group chart, with currency and accounting-basis compatibility checks.

**Rationale:** Group reporting requires mapping distinct legal charts without flattening entity books.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A consolidation run identifies mapped and unmapped balances and refuses finalization when required accounts lack a mapping.

**AC 2.** A mapping revision affects only runs using its effective version and preserves the prior mapping snapshot.

**Exception / edge case:** An approved one-to-many or many-to-one mapping is permitted only with explicit allocation rules and testable total reconciliation.

**Security and audit implications:** Mapping publication and run approval are restricted; store entity, group, mapping version, and source snapshot references.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Entity labels and group captions are translated independently; mapping keys and currencies are explicit in outputs.

**Verification method:** Consolidation tests for unmapped accounts, mapping versions, allocation balance, and source drill-through.

**REQUIREMENT 0053 OF 1120  |  FINANCE, ACCOUNTING, TAX, AND CONTROLS**

## ERP-FINANCE-053 — Intercompany transaction and matching

**Normative requirement:** The system shall identify intercompany counterparties and document references on eligible transactions and provide reciprocal balance matching by entity pair, period, currency, and transaction class.

**Rationale:** Intercompany balances need consistent counterparty attribution before consolidation elimination.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Reciprocal intercompany entries with equal configured values match and appear as reconciled for the entity pair.

**AC 2.** A one-sided or amount-mismatched item remains an exception with source references and difference amount.

**Exception / edge case:** Differences caused by timing or FX are classified separately and do not auto-create balancing entries without approval.

**Security and audit implications:** Entity access scopes are enforced; matching data may be shared only with users authorized for both relevant entities.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Counterparty legal names and narratives preserve original language; amounts include currency and entity labels.

**Verification method:** Integration tests for exact, one-sided, mismatched, timing, and unauthorized cross-entity view.

**REQUIREMENT 0054 OF 1120  |  FINANCE, ACCOUNTING, TAX, AND CONTROLS**

## ERP-FINANCE-054 — Consolidation eliminations

**Normative requirement:** The system shall generate consolidation-only elimination journals from approved rules and matched source balances, preserving both entity books and linkable elimination evidence.

**Rationale:** Elimination entries belong to the consolidation layer and must not alter subsidiary ledgers.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A configured reciprocal balance rule creates an elimination journal that nets the group balance to the expected value.

**AC 2.** The subsidiary trial balances remain unchanged after the elimination run.

**Exception / edge case:** Unmatched intercompany items are excluded or flagged under the configured rule and cannot be silently forced to zero.

**Security and audit implications:** Only consolidation roles can approve elimination runs; preserve source balance snapshot, rule version, and reversal lineage.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Group display captions may be localized; entities, currency, and elimination basis remain distinguishable.

**Verification method:** Reconciliation tests compare pre/post group balances and confirm entity books are unchanged.

**REQUIREMENT 0055 OF 1120  |  FINANCE, ACCOUNTING, TAX, AND CONTROLS**

## ERP-FINANCE-055 — Translation reserve and consolidation FX

**Normative requirement:** The system shall translate foreign operations using approved rate types and policy-defined treatment by account category, and separately track translation differences where required by the accounting basis.

**Rationale:** IAS 21 translation and resulting presentation depend on functional currency, presentation currency, and applicable policy.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A configured translation run applies rate categories to mapped account balances and reports the rate per category.

**AC 2.** The calculated difference required to balance the translated trial balance is posted to a configured translation reserve account only under the selected policy.

**Exception / edge case:** Lack of exchangeability or unusual exchange-rate constraints requires a configured policy/exception workflow; system shall not invent an official rate.

**Security and audit implications:** Rate and policy snapshots are immutable for each run; restrict overrides and log who approved them.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Consolidated reports identify presentation currency and translation date; labels and rates are locale-formatted without ambiguity.

**Verification method:** Golden translation tests by account category, rate date, reserve calculation, missing/exception rate, and rerun.

**REQUIREMENT 0056 OF 1120  |  FINANCE, ACCOUNTING, TAX, AND CONTROLS**

## ERP-FINANCE-056 — Cash position and forecast

**Normative requirement:** The system shall produce a cash position and forecast from authorized bank balances, open receivables/payables, scheduled cash items, and configurable forecast assumptions with source and confidence labels.

**Rationale:** Forecast assumptions and included cash flows vary by organization and should be separated from posted actuals.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** For a fixed data snapshot and assumption version, the forecast returns reproducible cash by date and currency.

**AC 2.** Unposted or probabilistic amounts are clearly labeled and excluded from actual cash balance totals.

**Exception / edge case:** Missing bank balance or stale integration data is shown as missing/stale rather than silently carried forward as a current fact.

**Security and audit implications:** Access to bank positions and forecast assumptions is restricted; record source freshness, as-of timestamp, and export action.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Forecast dates and amounts use user's locale while the as-of timestamp, timezone, currency, and scenario are explicit.

**Verification method:** Snapshot-based tests for reproducibility, stale feeds, multiple currencies, and actual-versus-forecast separation.

**REQUIREMENT 0057 OF 1120  |  FINANCE, ACCOUNTING, TAX, AND CONTROLS**

## ERP-FINANCE-057 — Budget version and actual comparison

**Normative requirement:** The system shall store versioned budgets by entity, period, account, and configured dimensions, and compare them with posted actuals under an explicit currency and calendar basis.

**Rationale:** Budget structures and cycles differ; versioning prevents revised plans from overwriting approved baselines.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A budget submission records version, owner, status, and period coverage; actual-versus-budget output uses that selected version.

**AC 2.** A posted actual with an unmatched account or dimension is surfaced as unmapped rather than dropped from the comparison.

**Exception / edge case:** A reforecast may replace an operational view only as a new version and cannot modify the approved baseline.

**Security and audit implications:** Budget write and approval roles are separated; budget exports and changes are logged and tenant scoped.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Period names, comments, and number formats are localized; stored period/account/dimension identifiers remain stable.

**Verification method:** Lifecycle tests for draft, approval, version selection, unmapped actual, and currency conversion.

**REQUIREMENT 0058 OF 1120  |  FINANCE, ACCOUNTING, TAX, AND CONTROLS**

## ERP-FINANCE-058 — Commitment and encumbrance control

**Normative requirement:** The system shall track approved commitments and encumbrances from configured upstream documents and optionally reserve budget, releasing or consuming amounts through linked lifecycle events.

**Rationale:** Commitment controls depend on purchasing policy and cannot assume that every order creates a legal liability.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A configured approved order reserves its eligible amount once and its receipt/invoice consumes or releases the corresponding balance.

**AC 2.** A canceled document releases the reserve exactly once and retains cancellation lineage.

**Exception / edge case:** A commitment over budget is blocked or escalated only when the entity enables a budget-control rule; no universal budget stop is imposed.

**Security and audit implications:** Override rights are limited and audited; commitment balances cannot be edited directly outside controlled adjustment workflow.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Commitment descriptions and supplier terms may be localized; monetary comparisons use the approved budget currency basis.

**Verification method:** Cross-module tests for approve, amend, partial receipt, invoice, cancel, duplicate event, and budget threshold.

**REQUIREMENT 0059 OF 1120  |  FINANCE, ACCOUNTING, TAX, AND CONTROLS**

## ERP-FINANCE-059 — Cost allocation rules and drivers

**Normative requirement:** The system shall allocate configured source costs across target dimensions using effective-dated drivers, preserve pre/post amounts, and post balanced allocation journals after preview and approval.

**Rationale:** Allocation methodologies vary by business and must be inspectable and repeatable.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A test driver distribution sums to the source amount within configured precision and produces a balanced journal.

**AC 2.** A missing, zero-total, or invalid allocation driver blocks the run and provides a diagnostic.

**Exception / edge case:** A residual from rounding is assigned only using a configured residual policy and designated target; otherwise the run fails.

**Security and audit implications:** Rule changes and allocation runs require scoped permission; record source set, driver snapshot, rule version, and approval.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Driver values are localized only in display; formulas and dimension keys remain consistent across locales.

**Verification method:** Deterministic tests for weighted distribution, zero driver, residual, and balanced output.

**REQUIREMENT 0060 OF 1120  |  FINANCE, ACCOUNTING, TAX, AND CONTROLS**

## ERP-FINANCE-060 — Financial statement definition and presentation

**Normative requirement:** The system shall generate configurable balance sheet, income statement, cash flow, equity, and supporting reports from mapped ledger balances using an explicit framework, period, comparative basis, and presentation currency.

**Rationale:** Statement structure and minimum disclosure requirements follow the selected accounting framework and jurisdiction, not a single universal report template.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A report identifies ledger, framework, period, currency, mapping version, and comparative period in its output metadata.

**AC 2.** Configured report lines reconcile to included trial-balance accounts and expose unmapped-account warnings.

**Exception / edge case:** IFRS IAS 1-specific statements are enabled only when the entity selects IFRS and the applicable version; local statutory forms remain jurisdiction-configured.

**Security and audit implications:** Report definitions and mapping approvals are restricted; preserve the exact definition and data snapshot for issued output.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Captions, dates, decimals, and page direction localize; each amount shows its currency and report language/version.

**Verification method:** Report integration tests reconcile line totals to trial balance and validate framework/version metadata.

**REQUIREMENT 0061 OF 1120  |  FINANCE, ACCOUNTING, TAX, AND CONTROLS**

## ERP-FINANCE-061 — Report reproducibility and drill-through

**Normative requirement:** The system shall retain report parameters, source snapshot or reproducible ledger cutoff, mapping versions, and generation timestamp for each finalized financial report.

**Rationale:** A later chart, translation, or policy change must not make an issued report irreproducible.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Regenerating a report from retained cutoff and versions yields identical account totals and document references.

**AC 2.** A user can drill from a report total to authorized contributing ledger entries without exposing records outside their entity scope.

**Exception / edge case:** If source records are lawfully retained in a separate archive, the report records archive references and indicates unavailable live drill-through.

**Security and audit implications:** Report access and export are audited; drill-through rechecks row-level authorization rather than inheriting report access blindly.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** User locale controls presentation only; report language, numeric conventions, and source timestamps are saved as parameters.

**Verification method:** Re-run and access-control tests with versioned mappings and cross-entity drill-through attempts.

**REQUIREMENT 0062 OF 1120  |  FINANCE, ACCOUNTING, TAX, AND CONTROLS**

## ERP-FINANCE-062 — Period close checklist and ownership

**Normative requirement:** The system shall provide configurable close checklists by entity and period with task owner, predecessor, status, evidence, due date, and sign-off state.

**Rationale:** Close steps and evidence differ by organization but benefit from clear accountability.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A configured task cannot be marked complete without its required evidence or an authorized documented waiver.

**AC 2.** The close dashboard reports overdue, blocked, and completed tasks based on saved status and period.

**Exception / edge case:** A checklist item not applicable to a specific entity/period is marked not applicable with reason, not silently removed.

**Security and audit implications:** Task ownership, waivers, evidence access, and sign-off are permissioned; capture status changes and actors.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Task labels and checklists are translatable; deadlines use entity timezone and unambiguous dates.

**Verification method:** Workflow tests for dependencies, evidence requirement, waiver, overdue calculation, and localized display.

**REQUIREMENT 0063 OF 1120  |  FINANCE, ACCOUNTING, TAX, AND CONTROLS**

## ERP-FINANCE-063 — Period close gate and subledger cutoff

**Normative requirement:** The system shall prevent final period closure until configured subledger, reconciliation, approval, and tax tasks are complete or explicitly waived by an authorized role.

**Rationale:** A close gate coordinates finance modules while allowing controlled exceptions.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Attempt to close with an incomplete mandatory reconciliation is rejected and identifies the blocking task.

**AC 2.** An authorized waiver permits closure only with reason, user, timestamp, and the unresolved item retained in close evidence.

**Exception / edge case:** A late-arriving source event after closure is routed to the configured adjustment/reopen workflow; it is not silently backdated and posted.

**Security and audit implications:** Closure and waiver are high-risk permissions; require auditable approval and record the control status snapshot at close.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Period and checklist labels localize, but accounting cut-off uses entity calendar/timezone rather than operator locale.

**Verification method:** End-to-end close tests with unresolved, waived, late-event, reopened, and final states.

**REQUIREMENT 0064 OF 1120  |  FINANCE, ACCOUNTING, TAX, AND CONTROLS**

## ERP-FINANCE-064 — Financial audit event log

**Normative requirement:** The system shall record append-only audit events for financial master changes, approvals, postings, reversals, tax determinations, payment actions, and security-relevant access with actor, time, target, action, and correlation ID.

**Rationale:** Audit evidence is needed to reconstruct who changed what and when across finance workflows.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A test posting creates linked events for preparation, approval, and commit, each with actor and UTC timestamp.

**AC 2.** An authorized auditor can filter events by entity, document, actor, and time range; an ordinary user cannot alter or delete events.

**Exception / edge case:** Automated jobs use a distinct service identity and preserve initiating user/context when a human action triggered them.

**Security and audit implications:** Use tamper-resistant storage/permissions; avoid recording credentials or unnecessary sensitive payloads; access to audit logs is itself audited.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Event metadata stores stable identifiers and UTC instants; display timestamps in user locale with original time zone context.

**Verification method:** Audit event integration tests for coverage, access denial, immutability, and sensitive-field redaction.

**REQUIREMENT 0065 OF 1120  |  FINANCE, ACCOUNTING, TAX, AND CONTROLS**

## ERP-FINANCE-065 — Finance administration privilege boundaries

**Normative requirement:** The system shall separate configuration administration, transaction preparation, approval, posting, payment release, tax rule publication, and audit review into assignable least-privilege permissions.

**Rationale:** Role separation limits fraud and accidental changes while reflecting distinct finance responsibilities.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A role lacking payment release cannot invoke the release API even if it can prepare the batch.

**AC 2.** Permission changes take effect on the next authorized operation and are recorded with grantor, grantee, scope, and expiry if temporary.

**Exception / edge case:** Emergency support access is time-bounded, approved, and reviewed after use; permanent shared administrator identities are prohibited.

**Security and audit implications:** Enforce server-side authorization for every operation and sensitive field; log denied high-risk actions and privilege grants.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Role and permission names can be localized in UI while stable permission codes remain language-neutral.

**Verification method:** Automated role matrix tests on UI/API and inspection of privilege-grant audit events.

**REQUIREMENT 0066 OF 1120  |  FINANCE, ACCOUNTING, TAX, AND CONTROLS**

## ERP-FINANCE-066 — Tenant and entity data isolation

**Normative requirement:** The system shall scope every finance record, lookup, search, export, background job, and database access path to an authenticated tenant and authorized legal entity.

**Rationale:** Commercial multi-tenancy requires defense in depth; PostgreSQL row security is one available mechanism but must be configured correctly.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A tenant-scoped principal cannot read, update, or infer another tenant's journal, supplier, tax, or attachment through any endpoint or export.

**AC 2.** Database tenant policies are enabled and tested under the runtime role; ownership/BYPASSRLS roles are not used by ordinary application traffic.

**Exception / edge case:** A group user with explicit cross-entity access can read only assigned entities, while tenant-wide service work requires a separately scoped service principal.

**Security and audit implications:** Use deny-by-default authorization, parameterized queries, row-level policies where appropriate, and controlled privileged roles; log tenant context with security events.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Tenant and entity identifiers are opaque stable values; user language and locale preferences are isolated and cannot alter data scope.

**Verification method:** Adversarial API/database tests for cross-tenant reads/writes, missing context, RLS bypass, exports, and scheduled jobs.

**REQUIREMENT 0067 OF 1120  |  FINANCE, ACCOUNTING, TAX, AND CONTROLS**

## ERP-FINANCE-067 — Segregation-of-duties conflict rules

**Normative requirement:** The system shall support configurable incompatible-role and transaction-level conflict rules for preparation, approval, supplier-bank changes, journal posting, payment release, tax override, and close sign-off.

**Rationale:** One person controlling incompatible steps can defeat otherwise valid workflow approvals.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A configured preparer-approver conflict is blocked for the same user at action time and recorded.

**AC 2.** An approved exception to a conflict includes scope, expiry, compensating control, approver, and review date.

**Exception / edge case:** A small organization may configure a permitted exception but cannot disable the conflict engine without explicit administrator authorization and audit.

**Security and audit implications:** Conflict rules are evaluated server-side against current assignments; temporary delegated roles and service identities are included in evaluation.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Conflict warnings and role captions localize; user identity and role codes remain stable across translated interfaces.

**Verification method:** Role-matrix and workflow tests for normal, delegated, temporary, exception, and expired-exception cases.

**REQUIREMENT 0068 OF 1120  |  FINANCE, ACCOUNTING, TAX, AND CONTROLS**

## ERP-FINANCE-068 — Locale, language, and accessibility settings

**Normative requirement:** The system shall support per-user language and formatting locale, entity legal locale, and document language as separate settings, and expose finance workflows in keyboard-operable accessible UI.

**Rationale:** Next.js supports locale-aware routes/content; financial UI requires explicit separation of legal locale from personal display preference.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Changing user language changes UI messages/date/number display but does not change posted values, tax rule selection, entity accounting date, or stored source language.

**AC 2.** Finance forms expose programmatic labels, text error identification, and keyboard-operable controls in the configured supported locale.

**Exception / edge case:** Unsupported locale falls back to an announced configured default without corrupting route state or silently changing entity jurisdiction.

**Security and audit implications:** Locale selection is not an authorization control; ensure translated screens do not reveal fields the user's role cannot access, and audit export language settings.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Support Unicode, right-to-left layouts where selected, locale-specific digits and calendars for display, and WCAG 2.2 AA-oriented testing; preserve canonical IDs/numbers.

**Verification method:** Automated locale-switch tests plus keyboard, screen-reader semantics, and accessibility checks on critical posting flows.

**REQUIREMENT 0069 OF 1120  |  FINANCE, ACCOUNTING, TAX, AND CONTROLS**

## ERP-FINANCE-069 — Audit evidence export and retention

**Normative requirement:** The system shall export a scoped, integrity-verifiable finance evidence package containing selected records, audit events, source attachments references, schema/version metadata, and cryptographic hashes, subject to configured retention policy.

**Rationale:** Auditors and regulators may require controlled evidence packages; retention periods and export formats vary by law and contract.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** An export manifest identifies entity, period, selection criteria, file hashes, generation actor/time, and included schema versions.

**AC 2.** A verifier detects a modified exported file by comparing it with the manifest hash.

**Exception / edge case:** An export with expired or legally held data follows the configured retention/legal-hold workflow and reports omissions rather than silently omitting records.

**Security and audit implications:** Only authorized audit/export roles can generate a package; encrypt sensitive packages, log download, minimize data, and enforce tenant/entity scope.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Evidence includes original legal-language documents and locale metadata; manifest fields and report summaries may be localized while hashes cover exact bytes.

**Verification method:** Export/verification tests for completeness, scope denial, tamper detection, legal hold, and retention handling.

**REQUIREMENT 0070 OF 1120  |  FINANCE, ACCOUNTING, TAX, AND CONTROLS**

## ERP-FINANCE-070 — Opening-balance migration control

**Normative requirement:** The system shall load opening balances through a controlled migration batch that identifies source trial balance, accounting basis, currency, dimensions, cutoff date, mapping version, and reconciliation evidence.

**Rationale:** Opening balances establish ledger continuity and require explicit validation before live posting begins.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A migration batch cannot be finalized unless debit and credit totals balance by configured ledger currency and the source-to-target mapping has no unresolved required accounts.

**AC 2.** Finalization records source totals, target totals, conversion rules, batch ID, approver, and a reproducible reconciliation report.

**Exception / edge case:** A permitted immaterial rounding variance is posted only to a configured opening-balance adjustment account within an approved tolerance; otherwise the batch remains blocked.

**Security and audit implications:** Migration preparation and final approval are separated; restrict access to imported files and retain hashes, mappings, exceptions, and all batch state changes.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Source descriptions and identifiers retain their original language; dates, decimal values, and currency codes are parsed using explicit source-format metadata rather than the operator locale.

**Verification method:** Integration tests for balanced/unbalanced trial balance, missing mapping, precision variance, duplicate batch, approval separation, and reconciliation reproduction.

# Procurement, Sourcing, and Supplier Management

# 02 — Procurement, sourcing, and supplier management

## Scope and baseline

This chapter specifies the commercial ERP’s procure-to-contract and procure-to-order domain: supplier master and onboarding; requisitions; sourcing events and bid evaluation; awards; contracts and supplier obligations; purchase orders; receiving; supplier performance; and procurement integrations. It defines procurement-owned records and handoffs. It does not define a jurisdiction’s procurement statute, tax treatment, sanctions law, public-sector tender procedure, accounting recognition, payment execution, or industry qualification regime. Those rules are tenant-, entity-, country-, category-, and effective-date-configured extensions reviewed by the organization’s legal, tax, security, and industry owners. ISO 20400:2017 is guidance for integrating sustainability into procurement, not a universal scoring rule or legal mandate \[9].

The requested backend baseline is ASP.NET Core on .NET 11. Microsoft’s official policy, last updated November 10, 2026, identifies .NET 11 as a supported STS release through November 14, 2028 and .NET 10 as supported LTS through the same date \[1] \[2]. Because the requirement is the latest stable supported .NET on the stated as-of date, .NET 11 is selected; it is stable, not a preview. The shorter STS path means the implementation must plan regular major upgrades. If a longer-lived deployment cadence outweighs the latest-version constraint, .NET 10 LTS is an explicitly different baseline choice. Pin current patches and re-confirm Microsoft’s release/support table at project kickoff and every production release; do not assume a future support date beyond the official page. ASP.NET Core 11 release notes confirm the framework release line \[3].

Use PostgreSQL as the transactional relational store. The database major version and hosting lifecycle are deployment decisions; this chapter does not infer a required major version from “PostgreSQL.” Select a supported PostgreSQL major at implementation/release gate and test migrations, extensions, backup/restore, and provider compatibility. PostgreSQL row-level security can provide defense in depth, but its table-owner/BYPASSRLS behavior and referential-integrity side channels mean it cannot replace application authorization and test coverage \[4]. Use a lightweight Next.js App Router frontend. Next.js supports locale-prefixed or locale-domain routing and localized content patterns; locale selection, translations, and fallback behavior remain explicit product decisions \[5].

## Actors and permission boundaries

Actors include requester, cost-center owner, approver, category manager, buyer, sourcing event owner, evaluator, award approver, contract owner, supplier-risk reviewer, supplier master-data steward, receiver/quality inspector, procurement analyst, internal auditor, tenant administrator, integration operator, and external supplier administrator/user. One identity may hold multiple roles, but authorizations are evaluated against tenant, legal entity, purchasing unit, category, transaction state, and assigned event/supplier scope.

Tenant isolation is mandatory at every API, job, report, export, and attachment boundary. A tenant administrator can configure that tenant’s profiles but cannot access another tenant’s business data. Supplier portal access is scoped to verified supplier organizations and explicit external roles. A buyer cannot see sealed bid content before the configured opening event. Evaluators see assigned scope and own scores before consensus. Approval, evaluation, award, supplier bank-detail maintenance, and order release can use incompatible-role rules configured by the tenant. Administrative override is separate from normal authorization and requires reason, actor attribution, and audit. NIST SP 800-53 is a customizable security/privacy control catalog, not a universal compliance certification; access-control and audit design should be mapped to the tenant’s selected control baseline \[11].

## Core entities

The domain centers on Tenant, LegalEntity, PurchasingOrganization, BusinessUnit, CostObject, CategoryVersion, UnitOfMeasure, CatalogEntry, SupplierOrganization, SupplierLegalEntity, SupplierSite, SupplierContact, SupplierRelationship, Qualification, EvidenceDocument, QuestionnaireVersion/Response, RiskAssessment, Requisition/HeaderLine, ApprovalRuleVersion/Instance/Decision, SourcingEvent/Lot/Invitation/Question/Addendum/Submission/Evaluation/Award, Contract/ContractVersion/Obligation, PurchaseOrder/HeaderLine/ChangeOrder, Acknowledgement, ShipmentNotice, Receipt/Inspection/Return, PerformanceObservation/Scorecard, Attachment, ExternalIdentifier/Crosswalk, IntegrationEvent, and AuditRecord. Tenant-defined identifiers and domain keys are stable and locale-neutral. Labels are translatable; original supplier-authored text and document bytes are preserved.

Use explicit lifecycle states and append-only version/change records for approvals, bids, executed contract terms, orders, and receipts. Store money as decimal plus ISO currency code, time-bound rules with effective intervals, and dates/timestamps with clear time-zone semantics. Database constraints enforce row-level invariants; cross-row process invariants use transactional workflows and concurrency controls rather than assumptions hidden in application UI \[7]. PostgreSQL documents constraint caveats, including CHECK constraints not being suitable for cross-row invariants \[8].

## Main workflows

**1.** Supplier onboarding creates a tenant relationship, collects configurable questionnaires and evidence, verifies identity/payment data under dual control, applies qualification/risk reviews, and activates only the allowed supplier scopes.

**2.** Request-to-buy captures business purpose and lines, validates budget through the finance contract, resolves approval routes from versioned rules, records decisions, and maintains approved residual quantity/value.

**3.** Sourcing creates an event from approved needs, defines lots and event terms, gates eligible suppliers, invites and communicates, receives timestamped submissions, controls sealed access where configured, evaluates against frozen criteria, and records award or no-award.

**4.** Award-to-contract creates a linked draft agreement or external CLM reference. Contract obligations and renewal notices are monitored without automatic exercise unless enabled by policy.

**5.** Requisition/award-to-order converts approved scope into a versioned order. Changes to released commercial terms follow change approval, dispatch and acknowledgement, then receiving and inspection. Returns, supplier claims, and performance observations remain linked to original transactions.

**6.** Procurement publishes order/receipt/acceptance balances to accounts payable and domain events to other ERP modules. Finance owns invoice posting, accounting, budget ledger, and payment; procurement is not the payment rail. Peppol or another e-document profile is a configurable external exchange adapter, not a universal deployment requirement \[10].

## Design decisions and dependencies

The common model is multi-tenant, multi-entity, multi-currency, multi-language, and configuration-first. Shared supplier records across legal entities are allowed inside a tenant only under explicit ownership and visibility rules; cross-tenant supplier sharing is not implied. Global master codes coexist with tenant classification maps. Catalog and contract prices carry supplier, currency, validity, and provenance.

Workflow policies are versioned and pinned to each transaction at activation or submission. Transactional state changes use optimistic concurrency; financially or operationally significant counter updates use database constraints/transactions and bounded retry of serialization failures. APIs and events use stable event IDs, schema versions, correlation IDs, idempotency keys, and replay/reconciliation support. PostgreSQL RLS may be enabled in addition to server-side authorization, with forced RLS/role separation evaluated per deployment and privileged paths specifically tested \[4].

Dependencies include identity/SSO and MFA, enterprise organization and cost-object master data, finance budget service and currency rates, contract lifecycle management where external, document/virus scanning and object storage, mail/notification delivery, identity/e-signature provider when configured, accounts payable, inventory/warehouse and quality, analytics, and external e-procurement networks. Each dependency has a bounded adapter contract and explicit unavailable/unknown state. Procurement never interprets a timeout as approval, budget availability, supplier eligibility, receipt, or message delivery.

Localization is functional data design, not string translation alone. Store content independently of locale; retain original supplier names, narratives, and evidence; localize system strings and generated documents; use canonical typed values and locale-aware formatting; set active document language; support mixed-direction RTL data isolation. W3C recommends declaring the HTML language and marking language changes, and gives bidi markup guidance for dynamic mixed-direction text \[5] \[6]. Unicode CLDR supplies locale data for dates, numbers, currencies, units, plural rules, and related conventions; the implementation should use maintained locale libraries instead of hand-coded formatting rules \[8]. Locale is a presentation/communication preference, never an authorization key.

## Risks and controls

Key risks are cross-tenant leakage; overly broad supplier portal access; duplicate or misidentified suppliers; changed bids or terms after approval; threshold avoidance; collusion/conflict-of-interest; stale compliance evidence; supplier bank redirection fraud; duplicate order creation after retries; overspent blanket agreements; locale-induced amount/date ambiguity; missed contract notice dates; sensitive evidence exposure; and integration replay or event loss. Controls include scope checks on every boundary, tenant-aware uniqueness, approval separation, version pinning, sealed bid gates, immutable audit packages, idempotency and reconciliation, dual control of payment data, explicit unknown/stale states, controlled exception routes, and deterministic calculation tests.

No module should treat a screening match as a legal determination, an optional sustainability field as a universal mandatory score, a configured document profile as proof of regulatory compliance, or a workflow approval as an accounting posting. Industry- and jurisdiction-specific extensions require a named owner, version, effective date, scope, localization, legal review, and test pack. Public procurement rules, sanctions lists, tax fields, retention durations, e-signature validity, accessibility targets beyond the selected product baseline, and data residency are deployment decisions.

## Cross-module contracts

- **Identity and organization:** actor ID, tenant ID, entity/unit assignments, role scopes, status, locale, time zone, and delegation claims. Authorization is re-evaluated on every action.
- **Finance/AP:** budget check/reservation and release contract; accounting dimensions; supplier approved remit-to reference; PO/receipt/acceptance and return balances; currency/rate context. AP owns invoice matching/posting and payments.
- **Inventory/quality:** order line, ship-to, shipment notice, receipt quantity, inspection disposition, accepted quantity, return, and reversal event. Inventory owns stock valuation and movement accounting.
- **Contracts/legal:** award lineage, contracting entity, executed-version reference/hash, obligations, amendment and controlling-language metadata. External CLM remains system of record when selected.
- **Integration/network:** typed external IDs, partner identity, selected profile/version, stable event ID, correlation/idempotency key, source timestamps, and acknowledgement/replay state. External documents are preserved with normalized mappings.
- **Analytics/audit:** transaction IDs, version IDs, effective timestamps, source references, currencies, actor and rule version. Reports state metric definitions, scope, locale, time zone, and conversion basis.

## Chapter-local references

## Procurement, Sourcing, and Supplier Management — requirement cards

**REQUIREMENT 0071 OF 1120  |  PROCUREMENT, SOURCING, AND SUPPLIER MANAGEMENT**

## ERP-PROCUREMENT-001 — Tenant and legal-entity partitioning

**Normative requirement:** The system shall scope every procurement record and operation to an authenticated tenant and an explicitly authorized legal entity or purchasing organization.

**Rationale:** Prevents cross-customer disclosure and keeps purchasing authority aligned with organizational structure.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A user in tenant A cannot read, search, export, or reference a tenant B requisition, supplier, event, contract, or order by changing an identifier.

**AC 2.** A user assigned to entity X cannot create or approve transactions for entity Y unless a separately granted scope permits it.

**AC 3.** An unscoped service request is rejected and produces a security event rather than returning global records.

**Exception / edge case:** A shared supplier master may be intentionally visible to multiple legal entities within one tenant, but never across tenants unless an explicitly governed shared-service model is enabled.

**Security and audit implications:** Enforce server-side tenant/entity authorization on every API and background job; record denied access and scope changes. PostgreSQL RLS may add defense in depth but privileged owners and BYPASSRLS roles must be controlled \[4].

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Tenant display names and entity names are Unicode text; scope selection must not rely on translated names as identifiers.

**Verification method:** Automated API authorization tests plus database policy inspection and penetration test.

**REQUIREMENT 0072 OF 1120  |  PROCUREMENT, SOURCING, AND SUPPLIER MANAGEMENT**

## ERP-PROCUREMENT-002 — Procurement organization and purchasing units

**Normative requirement:** The system shall model tenant-specific procurement organizations, business units, plants, cost centers, and their effective-dated relationships.

**Rationale:** Supports delegated operating structures and changing organizational ownership without corrupting history.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** An administrator can create, deactivate, and date-bound a purchasing unit and assign it to a legal entity.

**AC 2.** A transaction retains the unit assignment that was effective when it was authorized.

**AC 3.** A unit with an effective end date cannot receive a new requisition after that date.

**Exception / edge case:** A reorganized unit with open commitments remains reportable through its historical code and mapped successor.

**Security and audit implications:** Restrict structure maintenance to scoped administrators and audit before/after relationships; do not authorize on display labels.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Names can have locale-specific translations while stable IDs and codes stay locale-neutral.

**Verification method:** Integration test across effective dates; audit-log assertion.

**REQUIREMENT 0073 OF 1120  |  PROCUREMENT, SOURCING, AND SUPPLIER MANAGEMENT**

## ERP-PROCUREMENT-003 — Category and commodity taxonomy

**Normative requirement:** The system shall support tenant-configurable, versioned category trees and category attributes without assuming a single global commodity code.

**Rationale:** Different industries and jurisdictions use different classification schemes and mappings.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A category can have a parent, status, effective dates, and optional external classification codes.

**AC 2.** A sourcing event or requisition line records the taxonomy version and category ID used at submission.

**AC 3.** A category cannot be its own ancestor or create a cycle.

**Exception / edge case:** A deprecated category remains readable on past records but cannot be selected for a newly submitted request.

**Security and audit implications:** Category administration is privileged and version changes are audited; external classification labels are treated as untrusted imported data.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Category labels and help text support per-locale translations; classification codes are not translated.

**Verification method:** Schema validation, cycle-detection tests, and versioned-record integration test.

**REQUIREMENT 0074 OF 1120  |  PROCUREMENT, SOURCING, AND SUPPLIER MANAGEMENT**

## ERP-PROCUREMENT-004 — Unit of measure and quantity precision

**Normative requirement:** The system shall store quantities with configured precision and a controlled unit-of-measure registry, including explicit conversion rules where authorized.

**Rationale:** Supplier quotes and orders must compare quantities consistently without silently changing unit semantics.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Each item line stores its entered unit and normalized base unit when a conversion exists.

**AC 2.** Conversions are applied only when a configured, dimension-compatible conversion is active for the transaction date.

**AC 3.** The system rejects a quantity that exceeds configured precision rather than silently rounding it.

**Exception / edge case:** A non-convertible unit may be accepted for a service line only when the category policy allows it and the unit is retained verbatim.

**Security and audit implications:** Audit changes to conversion factors; protect quantities and unit mappings from unauthorized alteration after award/order.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Unit labels localize, but stored codes are stable; decimal separators are locale-specific in UI only, never in stored numeric values.

**Verification method:** Boundary and property-based tests for conversion, precision, and dimensional mismatch.

**REQUIREMENT 0075 OF 1120  |  PROCUREMENT, SOURCING, AND SUPPLIER MANAGEMENT**

## ERP-PROCUREMENT-005 — Supplier identity and duplicate detection

**Normative requirement:** The system shall maintain a tenant-scoped supplier identity record with configurable identifiers and flag probable duplicates before a new active supplier is created.

**Rationale:** Duplicate supplier records cause split spend, duplicate payments, and inconsistent risk reviews.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** An administrator can configure identifier type, issuing jurisdiction, and normalized matching rule per tenant.

**AC 2.** On create, the system returns candidate duplicates with match reasons without merging records automatically.

**AC 3.** A duplicate-resolution decision records the selected survivor, affected records, actor, timestamp, and reason.

**Exception / edge case:** Identifiers may be absent, reused by a different issuing authority, or legally unavailable; these cases require manual review rather than a fabricated global identifier.

**Security and audit implications:** Restrict sensitive identity fields; log duplicate search and merge actions; merge must preserve references and audit history.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Retain original scripts and diacritics; normalize only in a separate comparison key using a documented rule.

**Verification method:** Tests for exact/near duplicate candidates, authority-specific identifiers, and non-destructive merge.

**REQUIREMENT 0076 OF 1120  |  PROCUREMENT, SOURCING, AND SUPPLIER MANAGEMENT**

## ERP-PROCUREMENT-006 — Supplier legal entities and locations

**Normative requirement:** The system shall represent a supplier organization, its legal entities, sites, contacts, and tenant-specific supplier relationship as distinct linked records.

**Rationale:** One supplier may operate through multiple contracting and ship-from entities with distinct qualifications.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A supplier relationship can reference one or more supplier legal entities and sites.

**AC 2.** An order and contract identify the specific supplier entity and remit-to/ship-from context where applicable.

**AC 3.** Deactivating one site does not deactivate sibling sites or erase historical relationships.

**Exception / edge case:** A sole trader or supplier with no separate legal-entity structure can be represented using a configurable minimal profile.

**Security and audit implications:** Gate edits to registered/legal identity fields; log who changed remittance and legal entity bindings.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Store address components as structured, jurisdiction-configurable fields and preserve the supplier’s script.

**Verification method:** Entity relationship and lifecycle integration tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0077 OF 1120  |  PROCUREMENT, SOURCING, AND SUPPLIER MANAGEMENT**

## ERP-PROCUREMENT-007 — Currency and exchange-rate context

**Normative requirement:** The system shall store each quoted and ordered amount with an ISO currency code and preserve separately any configured accounting conversion context.

**Rationale:** Cross-border buying needs unambiguous transaction currency and auditable conversion inputs.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Amounts are stored as decimal values paired with a currency code, never as formatted strings.
