**AC 2.** A converted reporting amount records rate, rate date, source, and target currency.

**AC 3.** The user sees a validation error when a currency is not enabled for the relevant purchasing entity.

**Exception / edge case:** No approved rate exists for the required date; the transaction remains unconverted and cannot claim a calculated base-currency amount.

**Security and audit implications:** Restrict rate-source/config changes and log overrides; never allow a locale change to alter stored currency or amount.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Currency and amounts are entered and displayed according to user locale, but stored as canonical decimals and ISO currency codes.

**Verification method:** Tests with multiple currencies, missing rates, rounding boundaries, and rate override audit.

**REQUIREMENT 0078 OF 1120  |  PROCUREMENT, SOURCING, AND SUPPLIER MANAGEMENT**

## ERP-PROCUREMENT-008 — Tax, withholding, and regulatory fields as configuration

**Normative requirement:** The system shall expose configurable tax and regulatory data fields and validation rules by tenant, jurisdiction, supplier type, and transaction class without hard-coding a universal legal rule.

**Rationale:** Tax registrations, withholding, and required documents vary by jurisdiction and change over time.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** An authorized administrator can version a jurisdiction-specific field set with effective dates.

**AC 2.** A transaction validates against the rule set selected for its legal entity and date.

**AC 3.** The system reports rule-set version and validation outcome on the transaction.

**Exception / edge case:** If no applicable rule set is configured, the system marks the transaction as requiring review rather than assuming tax exemption or compliance.

**Security and audit implications:** Configuration changes require privileged approval and immutable audit; access to tax identifiers is limited.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Labels and help are translated, but identifiers and tax values preserve exact input; localized numeric parsing is validated.

**Verification method:** Rule-version integration tests using synthetic country profiles; configuration review.

**REQUIREMENT 0079 OF 1120  |  PROCUREMENT, SOURCING, AND SUPPLIER MANAGEMENT**

## ERP-PROCUREMENT-009 — Addresses and supplier contacts

**Normative requirement:** The system shall capture supplier and delivery addresses using configurable structured fields while preserving an original formatted address and contact-language preference.

**Rationale:** Address formats, postal conventions, and contact conventions differ across countries.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A tenant can configure required address fields by country or use a free-form fallback.

**AC 2.** The system stores country code separately and does not require a province/state field universally.

**AC 3.** A contact can have preferred language, time zone, and channel consent/status fields.

**Exception / edge case:** A supplier’s country has no postal code or a nonstandard address; policy may make postal code optional and retain a free-form address.

**Security and audit implications:** Mask personal contact data by role; audit exports and edits to contact endpoints; enforce consent/contact restrictions configured by tenant.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Support non-Latin text and RTL addresses; display with bidirectional isolation and locale-aware punctuation.

**Verification method:** UI/API validation tests for multiple profiles including RTL and no-postcode case.

**REQUIREMENT 0080 OF 1120  |  PROCUREMENT, SOURCING, AND SUPPLIER MANAGEMENT**

## ERP-PROCUREMENT-010 — External identifiers and crosswalks

**Normative requirement:** The system shall store multiple typed external identifiers for suppliers, items, categories, and organizations with source-system provenance.

**Rationale:** Integrations need stable mappings without overloading a single internal key.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** An external identifier is unique within its configured source and object type, where the mapping policy requires uniqueness.

**AC 2.** An identifier update preserves the prior value and effective interval.

**AC 3.** An incoming record with an unmapped identifier is quarantined or routed for mapping instead of linked by fuzzy name alone.

**Exception / edge case:** A partner identifier is not globally unique; uniqueness is scoped to scheme, issuer, and trading partner.

**Security and audit implications:** Only integration administrators can alter crosswalks; log mappings and changes because they can redirect records.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Do not translate identifiers; preserve source labels and UTF-8 payload fields.

**Verification method:** Contract tests for matching, collision handling, and historical lookup.

**REQUIREMENT 0081 OF 1120  |  PROCUREMENT, SOURCING, AND SUPPLIER MANAGEMENT**

## ERP-PROCUREMENT-011 — Purchase requisition intake

**Normative requirement:** The system shall allow an authorized requester to create a procurement requisition with business purpose, requester, entity, delivery context, lines, and supporting files.

**Rationale:** A traceable, complete request is the controlled starting point for buy-side commitments.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A draft may be saved with incomplete fields but cannot be submitted until configured required fields are present.

**AC 2.** Submission assigns a stable request ID and captures submitter, time, and current record version.

**AC 3.** A submitted requisition cannot be edited in place without an amendment or return-to-requester transition.

**Exception / edge case:** A service or expense request has no physical delivery address; required delivery fields can be category-configurable.

**Security and audit implications:** Verify create permission by tenant/entity; quarantine uploads and audit submission, return, withdrawal, and resubmission.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Requester-entered narrative and attachments preserve the original language; prompts, errors, and statuses localize.

**Verification method:** Workflow API tests for draft/submit/edit transitions and attachment scan status.

**REQUIREMENT 0082 OF 1120  |  PROCUREMENT, SOURCING, AND SUPPLIER MANAGEMENT**

## ERP-PROCUREMENT-012 — Requisition line completeness and validation

**Normative requirement:** The system shall validate each requisition line against its category-specific minimum data contract before approval routing.

**Rationale:** Line-level validation prevents incomplete specifications reaching sourcing and receiving.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Configured fields can include description, quantity, unit, need-by date, category, and service period.

**AC 2.** Submitting a line missing a mandatory field returns field-specific errors and keeps it in draft.

**AC 3.** A service line with a configured period cannot have an end date earlier than its start date.

**Exception / edge case:** A one-time non-catalog purchase may omit a catalog SKU but must still carry a human-readable specification.

**Security and audit implications:** Do not expose restricted catalog prices to requesters; record validation rule version and user override.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Description may be authored in multiple languages; locale-specific date and number input parses to typed canonical values.

**Verification method:** Schema and UI tests for each line type and invalid boundary.

**REQUIREMENT 0083 OF 1120  |  PROCUREMENT, SOURCING, AND SUPPLIER MANAGEMENT**

## ERP-PROCUREMENT-013 — Budget check and commitment reservation

**Normative requirement:** The system shall call a configurable budget-control contract before authorizing a requisition or purchase order and record the response without substituting for the finance ledger.

**Rationale:** Budget availability and encumbrance are owned by finance configuration and must be visible at procurement decision points.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A configured budget service receives entity, account/cost object, currency, amount, and transaction ID.

**AC 2.** A hard-stop response blocks progression; a warning response proceeds only when policy permits and records acknowledgement.

**AC 3.** Retry of the same transaction ID does not create a second reservation.

**Exception / edge case:** Budget service unavailable or indeterminate; policy selects fail-closed, queue-for-retry, or controlled override and displays the state distinctly.

**Security and audit implications:** Budget override requires an authorized role, reason, actor, and audit trail; APIs authenticate service identities.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Amounts are sent as exact decimal plus currency; localized display does not alter payload.

**Verification method:** Contract test with mock budget adapter, idempotency replay, and outage behavior.

**REQUIREMENT 0084 OF 1120  |  PROCUREMENT, SOURCING, AND SUPPLIER MANAGEMENT**

## ERP-PROCUREMENT-014 — Approval matrix and route resolution

**Normative requirement:** The system shall resolve approval steps from versioned rules using configurable factors such as entity, category, amount band, risk flag, and cost object.

**Rationale:** Enterprise approval rules vary by policy and should be inspectable and testable.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Each approval instance stores the exact rule version and resolved approver set.

**AC 2.** The routing engine rejects a configuration that has an unresolvable required approver or an unintended zero-step route.

**AC 3.** A rule simulation returns route, matched conditions, and warnings before activation.

**Exception / edge case:** A user is no longer active when a step becomes due; system routes to a configured substitute or pauses for an administrator instead of silently approving.

**Security and audit implications:** Limit rule publishing to procurement-control administrators; log rule version, simulation, activation, and manual routing changes.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Approver identities are locale-independent; notification text and action labels are translated per recipient preference.

**Verification method:** Table-driven routing tests covering overlap, no match, inactive approver, and rule-version pinning.

**REQUIREMENT 0085 OF 1120  |  PROCUREMENT, SOURCING, AND SUPPLIER MANAGEMENT**

## ERP-PROCUREMENT-015 — Delegation and out-of-office substitution

**Normative requirement:** The system shall support time-bounded, scope-bounded approval delegation that never grants broader authority than the delegator possesses.

**Rationale:** Delegation protects workflow continuity while preserving separation of duties.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A delegation records delegator, delegate, start/end time, entity/category/amount scope, and reason.

**AC 2.** An out-of-scope action is denied even if the delegate has another active delegation.

**AC 3.** The audit record distinguishes the acting delegate from the accountable delegator.

**Exception / edge case:** Overlapping delegations are resolved by an explicit configured precedence or blocked for administrator review.

**Security and audit implications:** Delegation creation and use are audited; prevent self-delegation and disallow delegation to suspended users.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Dates/times render in user locale and time zone; persisted validity instants remain unambiguous.

**Verification method:** Authorization tests for boundary times, scope intersections, and audit attribution.

**REQUIREMENT 0086 OF 1120  |  PROCUREMENT, SOURCING, AND SUPPLIER MANAGEMENT**

## ERP-PROCUREMENT-016 — Approval separation of duties

**Normative requirement:** The system shall enforce configurable incompatible-role and self-approval rules across request, sourcing, award, supplier bank change, and order release stages.

**Rationale:** Separation of duties reduces fraud and error without imposing one universal organization chart.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** An actor who created a transaction is prevented from approving it when the configured self-approval rule applies.

**AC 2.** A role conflict between evaluator and award approver is detected before final approval.

**AC 3.** A permitted exception requires a separately authorized override and reason.

**Exception / edge case:** An organization with a small team may configure a documented exception matrix; the system must label and audit the exception rather than bypass controls.

**Security and audit implications:** Evaluate permissions using immutable user IDs and active role assignments; alert on privileged overrides.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Names in audit output follow recipient locale but actor IDs and timestamps remain stable.

**Verification method:** Role-combination matrix tests and denied/approved exception tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0087 OF 1120  |  PROCUREMENT, SOURCING, AND SUPPLIER MANAGEMENT**

## ERP-PROCUREMENT-017 — Approval decisions and rationale

**Normative requirement:** The system shall capture approve, reject, return, and request-information decisions with actor, timestamp, stage, version, and rationale where policy requires.

**Rationale:** A reconstructable decision history supports internal review and process transparency.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** An approval cannot complete without a decision and current record version.

**AC 2.** A return or reject decision captures a configured minimum reason length or coded reason.

**AC 3.** A decision history view shows prior state, decision, actor, and timestamps in sequence.

**Exception / edge case:** An approver can abstain or recuse if configured; the system reroutes without deleting the recusal record.

**Security and audit implications:** Decision history is append-only to ordinary users and exportable only under audit permission.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Rationale supports Unicode and preserves the authoring locale; coded reasons have localized labels.

**Verification method:** Workflow transition tests and audit-log immutability test.

**REQUIREMENT 0088 OF 1120  |  PROCUREMENT, SOURCING, AND SUPPLIER MANAGEMENT**

## ERP-PROCUREMENT-018 — Concurrent approval version control

**Normative requirement:** The system shall use optimistic concurrency and transaction-safe state transitions so that stale approval decisions cannot authorize a changed request.

**Rationale:** Avoids approvals being applied to values the approver never reviewed.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** The approval API requires the version token shown to the approver.

**AC 2.** If the underlying request changes before decision commit, the API returns a conflict and preserves the pending task.

**AC 3.** Only one concurrent terminal decision succeeds for the same approval step.

**Exception / edge case:** A database serialization or deadlock failure is retried only within a bounded policy and otherwise reported as retryable; PostgreSQL serializable transactions can abort and require retry \[7].

**Security and audit implications:** Log conflict and retry events without exposing record contents to unauthorized users; ensure idempotency key uniqueness.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Conflict notices and timestamps localize; comparison snapshots preserve original multilingual text.

**Verification method:** Concurrent integration test with two approvers and forced transaction conflict.

**REQUIREMENT 0089 OF 1120  |  PROCUREMENT, SOURCING, AND SUPPLIER MANAGEMENT**

## ERP-PROCUREMENT-019 — Urgent and sole-source justification

**Normative requirement:** The system shall support configurable urgent, sole-source, and waiver justifications with required reason codes, evidence, and compensating approval paths.

**Rationale:** Exceptions are legitimate in some policies but must be observable and reviewable.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Enabling a configured exception requires a reason code and narrative before submission.

**AC 2.** Policy can require one or more additional approvals or post-event review.

**AC 3.** Reports can filter transactions by exception type, requester, approver, and date.

**Exception / edge case:** Emergency operations during connectivity loss may permit a controlled offline record that must be reconciled and approved within the tenant-defined window.

**Security and audit implications:** Exception permissions are narrowly scoped; justification and linked evidence are retained in tamper-evident audit history.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Reason narratives support local scripts; policy-provided reason code labels are translated.

**Verification method:** Scenario tests for normal, emergency, waived, and post-review flows.

**REQUIREMENT 0090 OF 1120  |  PROCUREMENT, SOURCING, AND SUPPLIER MANAGEMENT**

## ERP-PROCUREMENT-020 — Conflict-of-interest declaration

**Normative requirement:** The system shall collect, version, and associate conflict-of-interest declarations with configured sourcing participants and decision-makers.

**Rationale:** A procurement governance control should disclose and manage conflicts without asserting one global legal declaration form.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Configured participants are prompted to declare before accessing confidential evaluation materials.

**AC 2.** A positive disclosure blocks assignment or routes to an authorized reviewer under policy.

**AC 3.** Each declaration stores form version, response, timestamp, and reviewer disposition.

**Exception / edge case:** A participant has no conflict or is unavailable; no response is not treated as a negative declaration.

**Security and audit implications:** Declarations are restricted as sensitive personnel data; access and disposition are audited.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Questionnaire text is versioned and translated; free-text explanation preserves original language.

**Verification method:** Role-flow tests, no-response case, and access-control test.

**REQUIREMENT 0091 OF 1120  |  PROCUREMENT, SOURCING, AND SUPPLIER MANAGEMENT**

## ERP-PROCUREMENT-021 — Anti-splitting and threshold analysis

**Normative requirement:** The system shall flag configured patterns of related requisitions that may have been split to avoid approval or sourcing thresholds, without automatically declaring misconduct.

**Rationale:** Threshold rules and anti-avoidance controls depend on organization policy and local rules.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A configurable detection rule groups requests by entity, requester, category, supplier, and rolling date window.

**AC 2.** A flagged group shows the matched threshold and underlying records to an authorized reviewer.

**AC 3.** The flag does not change transaction status unless a separately configured workflow rule applies.

**Exception / edge case:** Legitimate recurring purchases can trigger a false positive; a reviewer can disposition the alert with a reason.

**Security and audit implications:** Limit related-spend insight to authorized controls users; audit alert access and dispositions.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Threshold values and amounts are evaluated as canonical numeric/currency values and displayed in the reviewer locale.

**Verification method:** Synthetic dataset tests for threshold hit, non-hit, and false-positive disposition.

**REQUIREMENT 0092 OF 1120  |  PROCUREMENT, SOURCING, AND SUPPLIER MANAGEMENT**

## ERP-PROCUREMENT-022 — Sourcing event creation and lot structure

**Normative requirement:** The system shall allow authorized buyers to create a sourcing event from one or more approved needs, define lots, response format, schedule, and evaluation method.

**Rationale:** Competition can be structured at category, line, or lot level according to business and policy needs.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** An event records source requisition references, lot structure, event type, dates, and rule version.

**AC 2.** Each lot can be evaluated and awarded independently where configuration allows.

**AC 3.** Event activation validates that at least one supplier and one evaluation method are configured.

**Exception / edge case:** A market-sounding or request-for-information event has no award intent and cannot create an order directly.

**Security and audit implications:** Limit event editing after publication; audit scope changes and preserve source-line traceability.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Event title, descriptions, and supplier instructions can be translated by locale; schedule stores time zone/UTC context.

**Verification method:** End-to-end event creation and lot integrity tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0093 OF 1120  |  PROCUREMENT, SOURCING, AND SUPPLIER MANAGEMENT**

## ERP-PROCUREMENT-023 — Supplier eligibility gates

**Normative requirement:** The system shall evaluate suppliers against tenant-configured eligibility criteria before invitation, bid submission, and award.

**Rationale:** Eligibility can depend on category, geography, qualification, status, and jurisdictional configuration.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Criteria have effective dates, severity, and evidence source.

**AC 2.** A failed hard gate prevents the configured next action and displays a reason code.

**AC 3.** An authorized reviewer can grant a time-bounded exception only when the rule allows it.

**Exception / edge case:** Supplier status changes after bid submission but before award; the event re-evaluates eligibility at award and logs the change.

**Security and audit implications:** Do not expose other suppliers’ eligibility evidence; record rule version and any override.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Supplier-facing failure explanations are translatable and avoid revealing confidential screening logic where policy requires.

**Verification method:** Rule-engine tests for pass/fail/warning/expiry timing.

**REQUIREMENT 0094 OF 1120  |  PROCUREMENT, SOURCING, AND SUPPLIER MANAGEMENT**

## ERP-PROCUREMENT-024 — Invitation and supplier communication log

**Normative requirement:** The system shall issue supplier invitations through configured channels and associate every send, delivery result, and response with the sourcing event.

**Rationale:** A complete communication record helps demonstrate consistent event administration.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Invitation content is generated from the current published event version.

**AC 2.** A delivery failure creates a retryable status and is not represented as a successful delivery.

**AC 3.** Buyer-entered communication is visible in the event log with actor and timestamp.

**Exception / edge case:** A supplier contact opts out or endpoint bounces; the buyer must select an allowed alternate contact or channel.

**Security and audit implications:** Protect recipient lists and prohibit event staff from seeing unrelated supplier contacts; audit message access and sends.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Templates localize per recipient; sent artifact retains exact language and rendered content.

**Verification method:** Mail/API adapter contract tests and message-log assertions.

**REQUIREMENT 0095 OF 1120  |  PROCUREMENT, SOURCING, AND SUPPLIER MANAGEMENT**

## ERP-PROCUREMENT-025 — Confidential and sealed bid handling

**Normative requirement:** The system shall enforce event-configured confidentiality so that supplier submissions remain inaccessible to buyers and evaluators until the configured opening condition is met.

**Rationale:** Sealed processes need controlled access, though confidentiality rules differ across procurement regimes.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Before opening, non-administrator buyer roles cannot retrieve submitted response files or prices through UI, API, search, or export.

**AC 2.** Opening requires the authorized trigger and records participants, timestamp, event version, and file hashes.

**AC 3.** An unsubmitted draft is visible only to the submitting supplier account.

**Exception / edge case:** A technical exception permits authorized escrow recovery, but records two-person access and reason.

**Security and audit implications:** Encrypt data in transit and at rest per deployment policy; audit privileged access, decrypt/read operations, and key use.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Supplier text/files preserve original encodings; opening notifications localize but timestamps use an unambiguous instant.

**Verification method:** Role-based adversarial access test and opening-event audit test.

**REQUIREMENT 0096 OF 1120  |  PROCUREMENT, SOURCING, AND SUPPLIER MANAGEMENT**

## ERP-PROCUREMENT-026 — Event deadlines and time-zone semantics

**Normative requirement:** The system shall store sourcing event deadlines as explicit instants with the authoring time zone and display them in the user or supplier locale without changing the deadline.

**Rationale:** Participants need an unambiguous close time despite daylight-saving and cross-border differences.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Event activation requires date, time, and named time zone.

**AC 2.** A displayed deadline for two time zones resolves to the same UTC instant.

**AC 3.** The system rejects or flags ambiguous/nonexistent local times during daylight-saving transitions.

**Exception / edge case:** A time zone’s daylight-saving rule changes after event creation; the stored instant remains fixed and the rendered zone label updates transparently.

**Security and audit implications:** Restrict deadline changes after publication and audit old/new instant, actor, and notice to suppliers.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Localized date/time formats and numerals are presentation-only; deadline text includes zone or UTC offset.

**Verification method:** Time-zone boundary tests including DST gap, overlap, and locale change.

**REQUIREMENT 0097 OF 1120  |  PROCUREMENT, SOURCING, AND SUPPLIER MANAGEMENT**

## ERP-PROCUREMENT-027 — Questions, answers, and addenda

**Normative requirement:** The system shall manage supplier questions and buyer answers through a controlled event Q&A process, including publication scope and addenda versioning.

**Rationale:** Clarifications may affect all invitees or one supplier, depending on policy and sensitivity.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A question records supplier, time, topic, and confidentiality choice.

**AC 2.** A published answer can be marked event-wide or supplier-specific under a configured rule.

**AC 3.** An addendum increments event version and notifies all affected invitees.

**Exception / edge case:** A confidential question contains supplier proprietary material; only the authorized buyer can view the original, while a redacted general response may be published.

**Security and audit implications:** Audit draft and published versions; prevent unauthorized buyer from altering a published answer without a new version.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Question/answer text accepts Unicode; notices use recipient language when available.

**Verification method:** Workflow tests for private, public, redacted, and amended Q&A.

**REQUIREMENT 0098 OF 1120  |  PROCUREMENT, SOURCING, AND SUPPLIER MANAGEMENT**

## ERP-PROCUREMENT-028 — Bid submission and receipt evidence

**Normative requirement:** The system shall accept supplier responses with line/lot values, attachments, acknowledgements, and a server-generated receipt timestamp and receipt identifier.

**Rationale:** Suppliers need proof of what was submitted and when.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A successful submission returns a receipt ID, event version, timestamp, and content digest.

**AC 2.** A response cannot be submitted after its close instant unless event policy records an authorized extension.

**AC 3.** A retransmission with the same idempotency key does not create a second bid.

**Exception / edge case:** Large file or transient network failure; incomplete uploads remain unsubmitted and can be resumed only until the configured deadline.

**Security and audit implications:** Authenticate supplier users; scan uploads, enforce file limits, and prevent supplier cross-account access.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** File names and response content preserve international characters; receipt timestamp displays in sender locale with source zone.

**Verification method:** Black-box supplier portal tests for receipt, deadline, upload interruption, and replay.

**REQUIREMENT 0099 OF 1120  |  PROCUREMENT, SOURCING, AND SUPPLIER MANAGEMENT**

## ERP-PROCUREMENT-029 — Bid schema and arithmetic validation

**Normative requirement:** The system shall validate each supplier response against the event’s published response schema and calculate totals using explicit precision and rounding configuration.

**Rationale:** Deterministic validation makes offers comparable and surfaces mistakes before evaluation.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** The system reports required unanswered fields and line-level validation errors before final submission.

**AC 2.** Calculated totals reconcile from quantities, unit prices, discounts, and configured charges using the event’s rounding rule.

**AC 3.** Submitted response data is immutable after close except through an explicitly versioned clarification workflow.

**Exception / edge case:** An optional charge is not applicable; supplier can mark not applicable only if the published schema allows it.

**Security and audit implications:** Do not reveal competitor response data in validation messages; retain submitted payload and calculation version.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Currency/number formats adapt to locale on entry, while stored decimals and calculation rules remain exact.

**Verification method:** Golden calculation tests across decimal precision, rounding, and invalid fields.

**REQUIREMENT 0100 OF 1120  |  PROCUREMENT, SOURCING, AND SUPPLIER MANAGEMENT**

## ERP-PROCUREMENT-030 — Published evaluation criteria and weights

**Normative requirement:** The system shall freeze evaluation criteria, weights, gates, and scoring scales when a sourcing event is published and identify their version on each evaluation.

**Rationale:** Evaluation rules must be consistent with what suppliers were told and auditable after the event.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Published criteria weights sum to the configured required total or activation fails.

**AC 2.** Post-publication changes create an addendum/version and invalidate prior evaluations as policy dictates.

**AC 3.** Each evaluation record references the criteria version used.

**Exception / edge case:** A criterion is pass/fail and has no numeric weight; the schema permits typed criteria while validating configured totals.

**Security and audit implications:** Only sourcing-control roles can publish criteria changes; audit prior and new content and affected evaluators.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Criterion descriptions and scales can be translated while a stable criterion ID preserves meaning across languages.

**Verification method:** Configuration unit tests and post-publication mutation test.

**REQUIREMENT 0101 OF 1120  |  PROCUREMENT, SOURCING, AND SUPPLIER MANAGEMENT**

## ERP-PROCUREMENT-031 — Independent evaluator assignments

**Normative requirement:** The system shall assign evaluations to named evaluators and maintain independent scoring records until the configured consensus stage.

**Rationale:** Independent scoring reduces undue influence and reveals scoring variance.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Each evaluator can access only assigned events/lots and only their own draft scores before release.

**AC 2.** A score submission stores evaluator, criteria version, timestamp, and comments.

**AC 3.** Consensus cannot begin until all required evaluations are submitted or formally waived.

**Exception / edge case:** Evaluator recuses or becomes unavailable; an authorized reassignment records reason and preserves the prior draft state under restricted access.

**Security and audit implications:** Enforce least privilege and confidentiality; audit evaluation reads, score changes, recusals, and consensus access.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Comments preserve author language; score labels and evaluation UI localize.

**Verification method:** Permission matrix tests and parallel evaluator workflow test.

**REQUIREMENT 0102 OF 1120  |  PROCUREMENT, SOURCING, AND SUPPLIER MANAGEMENT**

## ERP-PROCUREMENT-032 — Score normalization and calculation trace

**Normative requirement:** The system shall compute comparative scores using the event’s frozen formula and expose an authorized calculation trace for each criterion and lot.

**Rationale:** Transparent calculations make ranking reproducible and allow review of weight/normalization logic.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** For fixed inputs, repeated score computation produces the same result and formula version.

**AC 2.** An authorized user can inspect raw value, normalized value, weight, rounding, and final score.

**AC 3.** The system flags missing or out-of-range score inputs rather than silently coercing them.

**Exception / edge case:** Qualitative criterion has no numeric score; it remains separately reasoned and is not assigned a fabricated numeric value.

**Security and audit implications:** Limit calculation trace to event-authorized roles; log overrides to automated score outputs.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Decimal formatting localizes but rank and numeric value are locale-neutral; textual rationale retains its language.

**Verification method:** Reference-vector unit tests for each formula type plus access test.

**REQUIREMENT 0103 OF 1120  |  PROCUREMENT, SOURCING, AND SUPPLIER MANAGEMENT**

## ERP-PROCUREMENT-033 — Award decision and approval

**Normative requirement:** The system shall produce an award recommendation from evaluation outcomes and require configured award authorization before establishing an awarded supplier/lot.

**Rationale:** Evaluation, recommendation, and award authority are separate control points.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** The award record references event, lot, winning supplier entity, evaluation result, and approval decision.

**AC 2.** Award approval fails if required due diligence or eligibility gates are unresolved.

**AC 3.** A rejected award returns the event to a configured state with reason and no order created.

**Exception / edge case:** No bid is acceptable; the event can close as no-award with recorded rationale and no supplier marked winner.

**Security and audit implications:** Separate evaluator, recommender, and authorizer privileges where policy requires; audit outcome, override, and notifications.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Award rationale and supplier communication templates are translated; record retains original decision text.

**Verification method:** End-to-end award approval and no-award tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0104 OF 1120  |  PROCUREMENT, SOURCING, AND SUPPLIER MANAGEMENT**

## ERP-PROCUREMENT-034 — Split awards and line allocation

**Normative requirement:** The system shall support configurable multi-supplier award allocations by lot or line while validating that awarded quantities/values do not exceed the sourcing scope.

**Rationale:** Some categories use multiple winners, alternates, or split awards.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** The award allocation total is within the event quantity/value ceiling unless a controlled amendment changes it.

**AC 2.** Each allocation records supplier, quantity/share, price basis, and effective period.

**AC 3.** An unallocated remainder is visible and requires explicit disposition.

**Exception / edge case:** An alternate supplier is ranked but not activated; the system stores alternate status without creating an orderable allocation.

**Security and audit implications:** Only authorized award users can amend allocation; log value/quantity changes and reasons.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Percent and decimal quantity input follow locale display while stored values are canonical.

**Verification method:** Allocation arithmetic boundary tests and award-to-order integration test.

**REQUIREMENT 0105 OF 1120  |  PROCUREMENT, SOURCING, AND SUPPLIER MANAGEMENT**

## ERP-PROCUREMENT-035 — Negotiation and best-and-final offer rounds

**Normative requirement:** The system shall support optional, versioned negotiation rounds that preserve original offers and apply consistent, event-wide rules to invited participants.

**Rationale:** Negotiation patterns differ and must not erase the initial competitive record.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A round has participant scope, open/close instants, instructions, and response schema.

**AC 2.** A new offer is stored as a new version linked to the prior response.

**AC 3.** The evaluator can distinguish original and later offers and identify which round is the basis of award.

**Exception / edge case:** Negotiation allowed for one participant only under a configured policy; the system records rationale and affected scope.

**Security and audit implications:** Restrict round access to participants; audit invitations, offer versions, and any extension.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Supplier instructions localize; original offers retain submitter’s language and locale metadata.

**Verification method:** Multi-round integration test and response version immutability test.

**REQUIREMENT 0106 OF 1120  |  PROCUREMENT, SOURCING, AND SUPPLIER MANAGEMENT**

## ERP-PROCUREMENT-036 — Contract creation from award

**Normative requirement:** The system shall create a draft contract or framework agreement from an approved award while retaining links to the event, awarded lots, supplier entity, and source terms.

**Rationale:** Contracting converts an award to an enforceable commercial record and preserves decision lineage.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Draft contract links to one approved award and identifies supplier contracting entity.

**AC 2.** Awarded scope, currency, price basis, and validity are carried forward or explicitly marked as changed.

**AC 3.** Contract activation requires configured legal/business review and effective dates.

**Exception / edge case:** The organization uses an external CLM; procurement stores an external contract reference and sync status without claiming contract execution.

**Security and audit implications:** Restrict draft terms and signed documents; audit creation, term changes, review, and activation.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Contract text supports multilingual versions with one configured controlling language if tenant policy requires.

**Verification method:** Award-to-contract mapping test and external CLM adapter test.

**REQUIREMENT 0107 OF 1120  |  PROCUREMENT, SOURCING, AND SUPPLIER MANAGEMENT**

## ERP-PROCUREMENT-037 — Contract terms and amendment history

**Normative requirement:** The system shall version commercial terms and amendments, including price schedules, scope, service levels, and supplier obligations, without overwriting executed versions.

**Rationale:** Commercial terms evolve but executed agreements must remain historically reconstructable.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** An executed version is immutable to ordinary editing and identified by version/hash.

**AC 2.** An amendment records changed clauses/lines, effective date, approval, and linked prior version.

**AC 3.** The system prevents overlapping active price schedules for the same contract item where configuration forbids overlap.

**Exception / edge case:** A retroactive amendment is allowed only under configured authority and must distinguish signing date from effective date.

**Security and audit implications:** Use least-privilege access to legal terms and audit every version, approval, and attachment access.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Clause text may be multilingual; distinguish translation status from legal controlling language.

**Verification method:** Version immutability tests and amendment effective-date overlap tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0108 OF 1120  |  PROCUREMENT, SOURCING, AND SUPPLIER MANAGEMENT**

## ERP-PROCUREMENT-038 — Contract obligations and milestones

**Normative requirement:** The system shall represent contract deliverables, service levels, insurance/certification obligations, and milestones with owner, due date, evidence, and status.

**Rationale:** Operational obligation tracking connects contractual commitments to performance monitoring.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** An obligation has a type, responsible internal owner, due date, source clause, and evidence requirement.

**AC 2.** Overdue open obligations appear in an authorized work queue.

**AC 3.** Evidence submission updates status only after configured review.

**Exception / edge case:** An obligation is not applicable to a particular lot or entity; it can be waived with reason and approver rather than deleted.

**Security and audit implications:** Obligation evidence access follows contract confidentiality; audit submission, review, waiver, and status change.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Due dates display in owner locale; evidence filenames/text accept Unicode.

**Verification method:** Workflow test for due, overdue, complete, and approved waiver.

**REQUIREMENT 0109 OF 1120  |  PROCUREMENT, SOURCING, AND SUPPLIER MANAGEMENT**

## ERP-PROCUREMENT-039 — Renewal and expiry management

**Normative requirement:** The system shall track contract dates, renewal options, notice periods, and configurable lead-time alerts without automatically exercising a renewal unless explicitly enabled.

**Rationale:** Renewal rights and deadlines are contract-specific and should not be inferred universally.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Contract configuration stores original expiry, option periods, notice deadline, and responsible owner.

**AC 2.** Alerts are sent at tenant-configured lead times and deduplicated for the same milestone/recipient.

**AC 3.** Renewal exercise records authorized decision, date, option number, and updated end date.

**Exception / edge case:** No renewal option exists; expiry alert still surfaces transition actions but cannot create an extension.

**Security and audit implications:** Restrict renewal exercise authority; audit alert delivery, acknowledgement, and renewal action.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Dates and notices are localized; persisted instants and contract time zone are explicit.

**Verification method:** Calendar boundary tests and notification idempotency tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0110 OF 1120  |  PROCUREMENT, SOURCING, AND SUPPLIER MANAGEMENT**

## ERP-PROCUREMENT-040 — Supplier onboarding questionnaire

**Normative requirement:** The system shall support configurable, versioned supplier onboarding questionnaires with conditional fields, document requests, and review states.

**Rationale:** Different supplier types and sectors require different data and evidence.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Questionnaire version is pinned to each supplier response.

**AC 2.** Conditional questions appear only when their configured predicate is true.

**AC 3.** A reviewer can return an incomplete submission with field-level comments.

**Exception / edge case:** Supplier cannot answer a required item; they may select a configured “not applicable” option with explanation if allowed.

**Security and audit implications:** Supplier portal users can view only their organization’s questionnaire; questionnaire changes and review decisions are audited.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Prompts can be translated and supplier responses retain original language; support Unicode free text.

**Verification method:** Questionnaire schema tests and cross-supplier isolation tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0111 OF 1120  |  PROCUREMENT, SOURCING, AND SUPPLIER MANAGEMENT**

## ERP-PROCUREMENT-041 — Supplier evidence and document control

**Normative requirement:** The system shall manage supplier evidence files with document type, issuer, issue/expiry dates, verification state, version, and provenance.

**Rationale:** Supplier credentials and attestations need controlled lifecycle and traceability.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Evidence upload captures document type and at least configured mandatory metadata.

**AC 2.** An expired document cannot satisfy a current qualification gate unless policy explicitly permits grace.

**AC 3.** Replacing a file preserves prior version and verification result.

**Exception / edge case:** A document has no expiry date; configuration allows a no-expiry type or requires manual review rather than inventing one.

**Security and audit implications:** Virus-scan uploads, encrypt sensitive evidence, use least privilege, and audit view/download/update.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Original filename and document text retain Unicode; metadata labels and expiry dates localize.

**Verification method:** Upload security test and date/version qualification tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0112 OF 1120  |  PROCUREMENT, SOURCING, AND SUPPLIER MANAGEMENT**

## ERP-PROCUREMENT-042 — Supplier risk profile and due diligence rules

**Normative requirement:** The system shall calculate a configurable supplier risk profile from declared inputs, evidence, and review outcomes while exposing data provenance and rule version.

**Rationale:** Risk models differ by organization, industry, and jurisdiction and must be explainable.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Each risk result records source facts, rule version, calculation time, and reviewer disposition.

**AC 2.** A changed input recomputes or marks the profile stale according to configured policy.

**AC 3.** A high-risk status can trigger configured review but does not silently exclude a supplier.

**Exception / edge case:** External risk data is unavailable or stale; the profile is marked unknown/stale instead of assigning low risk.

**Security and audit implications:** Limit sensitive risk evidence access; audit profile views, manual ratings, overrides, and model changes.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Risk labels localize; source-provided narrative is preserved in source language.

**Verification method:** Deterministic rule tests, stale-feed test, and override audit test.

**REQUIREMENT 0113 OF 1120  |  PROCUREMENT, SOURCING, AND SUPPLIER MANAGEMENT**

## ERP-PROCUREMENT-043 — Jurisdiction-specific screening adapter

**Normative requirement:** The system shall integrate configurable screening sources through a replaceable adapter and require tenant-approved matching thresholds and disposition workflow.

**Rationale:** Sanctions, exclusion, and other screening requirements are jurisdiction-specific and change over time.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Adapter response stores source, query timestamp, result status, and source reference.

**AC 2.** A possible match is queued for human disposition and is not treated as a confirmed match automatically.

**AC 3.** Unavailable source returns unknown and follows tenant-defined fail/hold behavior.

**Exception / edge case:** Common name creates ambiguous matches; reviewer can record false-positive rationale and preserve the source result.

**Security and audit implications:** Restrict screening data to approved roles; audit searches and disposition; never imply legal compliance from integration alone.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Names are compared with accent/script-aware configured strategies while original spellings remain intact.

**Verification method:** Mock-provider contract tests for clear, possible match, no data, and outage.

**REQUIREMENT 0114 OF 1120  |  PROCUREMENT, SOURCING, AND SUPPLIER MANAGEMENT**

## ERP-PROCUREMENT-044 — Qualification and certification validity

**Normative requirement:** The system shall track supplier qualifications and certificates by scope, jurisdiction, category, issuing authority, and validity interval.

**Rationale:** A credential valid for one service or location may not qualify a different scope.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Qualification matching checks configured scope and date interval at invitation and award.

**AC 2.** An expired credential raises a gate or warning according to tenant policy.

**AC 3.** A renewal evidence submission creates a new version without erasing past valid periods.

**Exception / edge case:** Credential validity is under dispute; reviewer can set pending status and prevent hard-gated action until resolved.

**Security and audit implications:** Only qualified reviewers can verify credentials; audit status, evidence, and exceptions.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Credential issuer and description accept native scripts; dates follow locale display with canonical stored intervals.

**Verification method:** Date/scope matrix tests and credential history inspection.

**REQUIREMENT 0115 OF 1120  |  PROCUREMENT, SOURCING, AND SUPPLIER MANAGEMENT**

## ERP-PROCUREMENT-045 — Supplier payment detail control

**Normative requirement:** The system shall treat supplier bank or payment instructions as sensitive, versioned data and separate their maintenance from payment release authority.

**Rationale:** Payment redirection is a high-impact fraud risk and may be owned by finance controls.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A payment-detail change creates a pending version and cannot overwrite the approved active version directly.

**AC 2.** Activation requires a configured independent verifier or dual approval.

**AC 3.** The downstream finance interface receives only the active approved version and its change reference.

**Exception / edge case:** Supplier has no bank account or uses a permitted alternative payment method; profile can record the alternative without fictitious bank fields.

**Security and audit implications:** Mask account values, require step-up verification where available, audit read/change/verification/export, and never include full details in notifications.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Names and bank-country input preserve scripts; account identifiers are not localized or reformatted destructively.

**Verification method:** Access-control test, approval workflow test, and outbound payload inspection.

**REQUIREMENT 0116 OF 1120  |  PROCUREMENT, SOURCING, AND SUPPLIER MANAGEMENT**

## ERP-PROCUREMENT-046 — Supplier portal identity and delegated users

**Normative requirement:** The system shall authenticate external supplier users and scope their actions to an approved supplier organization and explicit portal roles.

**Rationale:** Suppliers often have multiple contacts, and account compromise must not enable cross-supplier access.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A supplier user can view only the organizations explicitly linked to their account.

**AC 2.** A supplier administrator can invite or revoke users only within their own organization.

**AC 3.** A portal role cannot approve internal procurement actions or change internal award decisions.

**Exception / edge case:** A consultant represents multiple suppliers; each organization link requires explicit verified authorization and separate context selection.

**Security and audit implications:** Use external identity controls, least privilege, session protections, and audit login, linking, invitation, and revocation.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Portal content follows user language; account names and submissions support Unicode and RTL display.

**Verification method:** Multi-tenant penetration tests for account switching and portal API authorization.

**REQUIREMENT 0117 OF 1120  |  PROCUREMENT, SOURCING, AND SUPPLIER MANAGEMENT**

## ERP-PROCUREMENT-047 — Supplier status and suspension lifecycle

**Normative requirement:** The system shall support configurable supplier lifecycle states, including active, pending, suspended, blocked, and inactive, with reason, scope, and effective period.

**Rationale:** Supplier availability may be blocked for a specific entity, category, or period rather than globally.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A status transition requires an authorized actor and reason code.

**AC 2.** A blocked state prevents configured downstream actions such as invitation, award, or new order.

**AC 3.** Historical orders and performance records remain queryable after deactivation.

**Exception / edge case:** A supplier is suspended only for one category/entity; unrelated permissible buying scopes remain active.

**Security and audit implications:** Restrict status changes; audit actor, reason, scope, evidence, and notifications; avoid exporting confidential reasons.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** State names and reason labels localize; underlying state codes remain stable.

**Verification method:** State transition and scope evaluation tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0118 OF 1120  |  PROCUREMENT, SOURCING, AND SUPPLIER MANAGEMENT**

## ERP-PROCUREMENT-048 — Supplier diversity and sustainability attributes

**Normative requirement:** The system shall support optional tenant-configured supplier sustainability, diversity, and responsible-sourcing attributes with provenance and review dates.

**Rationale:** ISO 20400 provides guidance for integrating sustainability in procurement but does not prescribe one universal scoring model \[9].

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A tenant can enable attributes and define evidence, scale, or self-declared status per category.

**AC 2.** Each value identifies source, assessment date, reviewer, and evidence reference.

**AC 3.** A report can separate verified, self-declared, expired, and missing values.

**Exception / edge case:** A supplier declines to provide a voluntary field; the system records “not provided” without converting it to zero or noncompliant.

**Security and audit implications:** Restrict sensitive personal/community attributes; audit use in evaluation and prohibit hidden discriminatory criteria without governance.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Labels and questionnaires localize; supplier statements preserve source language and avoid culturally fixed categories.

**Verification method:** Attribute provenance and report classification tests; governance review.

**REQUIREMENT 0119 OF 1120  |  PROCUREMENT, SOURCING, AND SUPPLIER MANAGEMENT**

## ERP-PROCUREMENT-049 — Requisition-to-order conversion

**Normative requirement:** The system shall convert approved requisition lines to purchase-order lines while preserving source links and preventing unauthorized changes to approved scope.

**Rationale:** Maintains end-to-end traceability from need authorization to commercial commitment.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Every converted order line references requisition line, approved quantity/value, and approval instance.

**AC 2.** Conversion rejects quantities/value exceeding approved residual scope unless an amended approval exists.

**AC 3.** A partial conversion leaves a visible open balance on the source requisition.

**Exception / edge case:** A sourcing award changes commercial supplier or price; conversion uses the approved award values and flags any variance for approval.

**Security and audit implications:** Only buyers with conversion rights can create the order; audit source-to-order mappings and variance approvals.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Descriptions may remain bilingual; quantities/currencies are preserved as typed values rather than locale strings.

**Verification method:** Integration test for full/partial conversion, overrun, and award price variance.

**REQUIREMENT 0120 OF 1120  |  PROCUREMENT, SOURCING, AND SUPPLIER MANAGEMENT**

## ERP-PROCUREMENT-050 — Purchase-order numbering and idempotency

**Normative requirement:** The system shall assign a unique order identifier within the configured numbering scope and make order creation idempotent for a supplied request key.

**Rationale:** Prevents duplicate commitments during retries and supports legally/operationally configured numbering.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Concurrent creations cannot receive the same tenant/entity/series number.

**AC 2.** Repeating the same creation key returns the original order ID and does not create a second order.

**AC 3.** A canceled order number is not silently reused unless numbering policy explicitly permits it.

**Exception / edge case:** A numbering series is exhausted or unavailable; order creation fails without a partial header or line record.

**Security and audit implications:** Treat numbering-series administration as privileged; audit assignment, cancellation, and key collision.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Numbers are identifiers, not localized quantities; display formatting may group characters only if stored ID remains visible.

**Verification method:** Concurrency and retry test with unique constraint verification.

**REQUIREMENT 0121 OF 1120  |  PROCUREMENT, SOURCING, AND SUPPLIER MANAGEMENT**

## ERP-PROCUREMENT-051 — Order terms, delivery, and ship-to

**Normative requirement:** The system shall capture order-level and line-level delivery instructions, requested dates, incoterm-like commercial terms, and ship-to context as configurable fields.

**Rationale:** Delivery obligations depend on goods/services, jurisdiction, and contract terms.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** An order can inherit eligible values from the award or contract and records each source.

**AC 2.** Line delivery dates can differ from header date when enabled.

**AC 3.** Configured mandatory delivery fields are validated before release.

**Exception / edge case:** A service line has no ship-to address; line type makes physical delivery fields optional without dropping service location.

**Security and audit implications:** Restrict changes to payment/delivery terms after supplier transmission; audit amendments and user overrides.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Delivery notes support native scripts; dates and addresses render per recipient locale.

**Verification method:** Order validation tests by line type and source inheritance.

**REQUIREMENT 0122 OF 1120  |  PROCUREMENT, SOURCING, AND SUPPLIER MANAGEMENT**

## ERP-PROCUREMENT-052 — Purchase-order change control

**Normative requirement:** The system shall require a versioned change order and configured reapproval when a released order’s value, quantity, supplier, terms, or delivery scope changes materially.

**Rationale:** A released order is a binding commitment; silent mutation breaks approval and supplier alignment.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Material fields are defined by tenant-configurable change policy and detected by comparing versions.

**AC 2.** A change requiring approval is not transmitted until approval completes.

**AC 3.** The change record displays before/after values and linked rationale.

**Exception / edge case:** A non-material correction (for example, typo) may use a lower-control path only if tenant policy defines it and audit records the reason.

**Security and audit implications:** Restrict order change rights; audit old/new snapshots, approvals, and supplier notice.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Change summaries preserve multilingual original text and localize field labels only.

**Verification method:** State-machine tests for material and non-material changes; audit comparison.

**REQUIREMENT 0123 OF 1120  |  PROCUREMENT, SOURCING, AND SUPPLIER MANAGEMENT**

## ERP-PROCUREMENT-053 — Supplier order acknowledgement

**Normative requirement:** The system shall record supplier acknowledgements, rejections, and proposed deviations against an exact purchase-order version.

**Rationale:** A response must not be mistaken as acceptance of a later order revision.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Acknowledgement records supplier identity, received time, order version, and line-level status.

**AC 2.** A supplier-proposed change creates a buyer review task and does not mutate the order automatically.

**AC 3.** Only an acknowledgement for the currently effective version marks that version acknowledged.

**Exception / edge case:** A late acknowledgement references a superseded version; it is retained but flagged for reconciliation.

**Security and audit implications:** Authenticate source message where available; audit inbound payload and decision; restrict supplier-visible order scope.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Supplier comments preserve original language; dates and numbers parse using the sender profile or explicit schema, not browser locale.

**Verification method:** Adapter contract and out-of-order message tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0124 OF 1120  |  PROCUREMENT, SOURCING, AND SUPPLIER MANAGEMENT**

## ERP-PROCUREMENT-054 — Blanket orders and call-off releases

**Normative requirement:** The system shall support framework or blanket orders with value/quantity ceilings, validity dates, supplier scope, and child release orders when configured.

**Rationale:** Recurring purchasing often requires controlled releases under a master agreement.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A release cannot exceed remaining ceiling or validity unless a separately approved amendment exists.

**AC 2.** Each release references the parent agreement/order and debits remaining commitment atomically.

**AC 3.** An expired parent blocks new release creation while preserving existing releases.

**Exception / edge case:** Concurrent releases compete for the final remaining amount; only the transaction within the ceiling succeeds and others receive a conflict.

**Security and audit implications:** Restrict ceiling and validity changes; audit release creation and remaining-balance adjustments.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Amount display localizes but ceiling comparison uses canonical currency and precision.

**Verification method:** Concurrent balance test, expiry test, and parent-child reconciliation.

**REQUIREMENT 0125 OF 1120  |  PROCUREMENT, SOURCING, AND SUPPLIER MANAGEMENT**

## ERP-PROCUREMENT-055 — Order dispatch and delivery receipt evidence

**Normative requirement:** The system shall transmit released orders through configured delivery channels and store a delivery receipt or explicit failed/unknown status.

**Rationale:** Buyers need evidence that the supplier-facing version was dispatched.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Dispatch payload identifies order version and idempotency key.

**AC 2.** Failed transmission remains retryable without duplicate supplier orders.

**AC 3.** The order UI distinguishes sent, delivered/acknowledged, failed, and delivery unknown.

**Exception / edge case:** Email provider accepts the message but recipient bounces later; status is updated from available delivery events without claiming supplier acceptance.

**Security and audit implications:** Encrypt transport, protect supplier endpoint data, audit transmissions and retries, and prevent unauthorized re-send of obsolete versions.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Generated document follows recipient locale and preserves canonical monetary/date values.

**Verification method:** Mock transport tests for accepted, failed, duplicate retry, and delayed bounce.

**REQUIREMENT 0126 OF 1120  |  PROCUREMENT, SOURCING, AND SUPPLIER MANAGEMENT**

## ERP-PROCUREMENT-056 — Advance shipping notice interface

**Normative requirement:** The system shall ingest optional supplier advance-shipping notices and match notice lines to open order lines without treating notice as proof of receipt.

**Rationale:** Pre-arrival visibility improves receiving, especially for multi-site or batch deliveries.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** An inbound notice references supplier, order version, shipment ID, items, quantities, and expected arrival where available.

**AC 2.** Unmatched or over-quantity lines are quarantined for buyer review.

**AC 3.** A notice never increases received quantity until a receipt transaction is posted.

**Exception / edge case:** A shipment is split into multiple notices or one notice covers multiple orders; policy supports explicit multi-reference mapping.

**Security and audit implications:** Validate sender identity and message signature where available; audit payload, quarantine decision, and mapping.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Supplier product names and lot/batch values preserve original characters; dates parse from schema-defined timezone.

**Verification method:** Inbound contract tests for partial shipment, overage, duplicate, and unmatched order.

**REQUIREMENT 0127 OF 1120  |  PROCUREMENT, SOURCING, AND SUPPLIER MANAGEMENT**

## ERP-PROCUREMENT-057 — Goods and service receipt with tolerance

**Normative requirement:** The system shall record goods receipts and service confirmations by order line, quantity/value, location, date, and receiver, enforcing configured tolerances.

**Rationale:** Receipts provide the evidence used for commitment closeout and invoice matching.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Receipt quantity cannot exceed open quantity plus configured tolerance without an override.

**AC 2.** A service confirmation records the covered service period or milestone when configured.

**AC 3.** Every posted receipt references an order line and a receiving actor.

**Exception / edge case:** Over-delivery or early/late service is held for exception review; receipt is not silently rounded to order quantity.

**Security and audit implications:** Only authorized receivers can post or reverse receipts; audit quantities, dates, location, and reversal reason.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Quantity entry accepts locale decimals but stores exact values; service periods display in user locale.

**Verification method:** Boundary tests for exact, under, tolerance, over, and reversal.

**REQUIREMENT 0128 OF 1120  |  PROCUREMENT, SOURCING, AND SUPPLIER MANAGEMENT**

## ERP-PROCUREMENT-058 — Inspection, nonconformance, and acceptance

**Normative requirement:** The system shall support configurable inspection plans and nonconformance dispositions that separate physical receipt from quality acceptance.

**Rationale:** Received goods may be held, rejected, or accepted conditionally under industry-specific rules.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A configured inspection lot can be marked pending, accepted, partially accepted, or rejected.

**AC 2.** Rejected quantity is excluded from accepted quantity available to invoice match.

**AC 3.** Disposition records defect code, evidence, reviewer, and supplier notification state.

**Exception / edge case:** No inspection plan applies; receipt can be accepted directly under category policy with the policy reference logged.

**Security and audit implications:** Restrict quality evidence and dispositions; audit inspection decisions and any manual override.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Defect codes can have translated labels; supplier-provided descriptions retain original language.

**Verification method:** Inspection workflow tests for partial acceptance and direct acceptance.

**REQUIREMENT 0129 OF 1120  |  PROCUREMENT, SOURCING, AND SUPPLIER MANAGEMENT**

## ERP-PROCUREMENT-059 — Return, replacement, and supplier claim

**Normative requirement:** The system shall track authorized returns, replacement shipments, credits, and supplier claims as linked records rather than deleting or editing the original receipt.

**Rationale:** Returns and disputes must preserve original accepted/rejected quantities and commercial history.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A return references receipt and order lines, reason, quantity, and disposition.

**AC 2.** Replacement or credit record links to the return and does not inflate accepted quantity.

**AC 3.** Closing a claim requires an outcome code and financial/quantity reconciliation status.

**Exception / edge case:** Supplier disputes the return or requests replacement before physical return; workflow supports open claim state with no false closure.

**Security and audit implications:** Restrict financial adjustments to authorized roles; audit evidence, supplier correspondence, and resolution.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Claim text supports supplier language; currency and quantity are structured, localized only for display.

**Verification method:** Linked-record integration test and reconciliation invariant test.

**REQUIREMENT 0130 OF 1120  |  PROCUREMENT, SOURCING, AND SUPPLIER MANAGEMENT**

## ERP-PROCUREMENT-060 — Invoice-matching handoff

**Normative requirement:** The system shall expose ordered, received, accepted, and remaining quantities/values to accounts payable through a versioned interface, while leaving invoice posting to the finance module.

**Rationale:** Procurement supplies the purchase/receipt evidence needed for matching, but does not become the accounting ledger.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** AP can query or receive change events for order, receipt, return, and acceptance balances.

**AC 2.** Each balance response identifies currency, calculation time, and source record version.

**AC 3.** A procurement reversal emits a compensating event rather than deleting an earlier balance event.

**Exception / edge case:** AP is offline or consumes an event twice; replay uses stable event IDs and does not duplicate accounting commitments.

**Security and audit implications:** Authenticate AP service principal; minimize supplier banking data in procurement payload; audit export/consumer acknowledgements.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Payload numbers and dates use schema-standard formats; supplier text retains Unicode.

**Verification method:** Consumer-driven contract test, duplicate delivery test, and reversal reconciliation test.

**REQUIREMENT 0131 OF 1120  |  PROCUREMENT, SOURCING, AND SUPPLIER MANAGEMENT**

## ERP-PROCUREMENT-061 — Supplier performance observations

**Normative requirement:** The system shall record dated supplier performance observations linked to contract/order/receipt context and an identified source.

**Rationale:** Operational performance evidence informs reviews without substituting an unsupported hidden rating.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Observation captures metric, observed value, period, source, evidence, and reviewer status.

**AC 2.** An observation can be disputed and retains both original and amended values with actor history.

**AC 3.** Unverified observations are distinguishable from reviewed observations in reports.

**Exception / edge case:** A qualitative narrative has no numeric measure; it can be stored without forcing a score.

**Security and audit implications:** Restrict personnel-sensitive comments; audit authorship, edits, review, and supplier disclosure.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Narrative supports Unicode; metric units and decimals are typed and locale-rendered.

**Verification method:** CRUD, dispute, provenance, and report-filter tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0132 OF 1120  |  PROCUREMENT, SOURCING, AND SUPPLIER MANAGEMENT**

## ERP-PROCUREMENT-062 — Supplier scorecards and corrective action

**Normative requirement:** The system shall generate configurable scorecards from disclosed metrics and permit a supplier corrective-action workflow with response and closure evidence.

**Rationale:** Scorecards create a structured improvement channel rather than a one-way opaque grade.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Scorecard identifies metric definitions, period, data sources, and calculation version.

**AC 2.** A supplier can submit a response or corrective-action plan where portal configuration permits.

**AC 3.** Closure requires an internal reviewer outcome and timestamp.

**Exception / edge case:** Insufficient volume exists for a score; scorecard labels the metric not rated rather than imputing zero.

**Security and audit implications:** Control who can publish scorecards and disclose underlying evidence; audit score changes and corrective-action closure.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Supplier receives scorecard in selected locale when translation exists; metric definitions preserve exact versions.

**Verification method:** Calculation golden tests and supplier response lifecycle tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0133 OF 1120  |  PROCUREMENT, SOURCING, AND SUPPLIER MANAGEMENT**

## ERP-PROCUREMENT-063 — Spend and sourcing analytics

**Normative requirement:** The system shall provide authorized procurement analytics over requisitions, events, awards, orders, receipts, and supplier performance with documented measure definitions.

**Rationale:** Consistent measures support sourcing decisions and controlled reporting.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Each metric definition states numerator, denominator, included states, currency basis, and time basis.

**AC 2.** Analytics respect tenant/entity/category access scopes applied to source records.

**AC 3.** A report can be reconciled to a filtered transaction detail set for a test dataset.

**Exception / edge case:** Multi-currency totals lack an approved conversion rate; report separates unconverted amounts instead of silently combining them.

**Security and audit implications:** Analytics exports are permissioned and logged; aggregate data must not leak another tenant’s supplier or spend information.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Filters and labels localize; report data exports declare locale, currency, and time-zone context.

**Verification method:** Golden dataset reconciliation, authorization test, and multi-currency test.

**REQUIREMENT 0134 OF 1120  |  PROCUREMENT, SOURCING, AND SUPPLIER MANAGEMENT**

## ERP-PROCUREMENT-064 — Attachments, retention, and legal hold boundary

**Normative requirement:** The system shall apply configurable retention, deletion, archival, and legal-hold controls to procurement records and attachments according to tenant policy.

**Rationale:** Retention obligations vary by jurisdiction, industry, contract, and organization policy.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A retention rule can be scoped by record type, entity, jurisdiction profile, and effective period.

**AC 2.** A held record is excluded from automatic purge and displays hold status to authorized records managers.

**AC 3.** A purge job logs record counts and outcomes without retaining the deleted sensitive payload.

**Exception / edge case:** No retention profile is configured or a hold conflicts with deletion; system blocks destructive action and raises an administrator exception.

**Security and audit implications:** Apply least-privilege access, secure deletion/archive policy, and immutable audit of retention actions; legal hold is not inferred by the product.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Metadata remains searchable with translated labels; original artifact language and encoding are retained.

**Verification method:** Dry-run retention simulation, hold/purge integration test, and access review.

**REQUIREMENT 0135 OF 1120  |  PROCUREMENT, SOURCING, AND SUPPLIER MANAGEMENT**

## ERP-PROCUREMENT-065 — Procurement APIs and event contracts

**Normative requirement:** The system shall expose versioned, authenticated APIs and domain events for procurement lifecycle changes with stable identifiers, schema, and correlation IDs.

**Rationale:** ERP modules and external partners need explicit contracts instead of direct database coupling.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Every API/event carries tenant scope, entity reference, event ID, schema version, and correlation ID as applicable.

**AC 2.** Breaking contract changes use a new version or documented compatibility path.

**AC 3.** Consumers can retrieve event status or equivalent reconciliation data after transient delivery failure.

**Exception / edge case:** Unknown event version arrives; consumer quarantines it and emits an observable incompatibility alert rather than discarding silently.

**Security and audit implications:** Use service identities, scoped permissions, input validation, rate limits, and audit sensitive event delivery.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Payloads use Unicode and locale-neutral machine formats; localized display strings are not used as keys.

**Verification method:** Schema contract tests, authentication tests, and compatibility test.

**REQUIREMENT 0136 OF 1120  |  PROCUREMENT, SOURCING, AND SUPPLIER MANAGEMENT**

## ERP-PROCUREMENT-066 — Electronic procurement document profile

**Normative requirement:** The system shall map purchase orders and related procurement documents through configurable external document profiles, including optional Peppol BIS integration where tenant/country profile requires it.

**Rationale:** Peppol BIS standardizes exchange of common procurement documents including eOrders and eInvoices, but network use and profiles are optional and context-dependent \[10].

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A profile maps internal fields to a named external schema/version and records the profile ID on each transmission.

**AC 2.** Missing mandatory profile fields block transmission and produce field-level mapping errors.

**AC 3.** Inbound and outbound documents retain the original payload and normalized transaction link.

**Exception / edge case:** No applicable profile is configured or an external partner uses a different schema; dispatch remains unavailable pending profile selection rather than inventing a mapping.

**Security and audit implications:** Protect partner endpoint credentials and payloads; audit profile changes and transmissions; honor data minimization.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Preserve source-language descriptions and exact locale-independent numeric/date serialization defined by the selected profile.

**Verification method:** Profile conformance tests against published schema/examples and adapter contract test.

**REQUIREMENT 0137 OF 1120  |  PROCUREMENT, SOURCING, AND SUPPLIER MANAGEMENT**

## ERP-PROCUREMENT-067 — Integration retries, ordering, and reconciliation

**Normative requirement:** The system shall deliver outbound procurement events with retry, idempotency, dead-letter, and reconciliation capabilities that do not reorder state transitions silently.

**Rationale:** Distributed integrations fail transiently and must recover without duplicating or losing commitments.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A retry reuses the event ID and includes attempt metadata.

**AC 2.** Events for the same aggregate are delivered in sequence or carry an explicit aggregate version that allows consumers to detect gaps.

**AC 3.** A dead-letter item is visible to an authorized operator with replay and discard actions requiring a reason.

**Exception / edge case:** A late event arrives after a later version; consumer stores or rejects it according to documented version policy and raises a reconciliation signal.

**Security and audit implications:** Restrict replay/discard, mask payload secrets, and audit all operator interventions.
