**Shall:** The system shall validate bulk customer, lead, quote, and order imports before commit and report row-level outcomes with stable external IDs.

**Rationale:** Enterprise migration and integrations require controlled, repeatable loading.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**1.** Preview identifies valid, invalid, and duplicate rows without writing business records.

**2.** Replay of a committed file with same external IDs does not create duplicates.

**Exception / edge case:** Partial commit is allowed only when selected import mode explicitly permits valid-row application.

**Security and audit:** Authorize import scopes, scan attachments, and audit uploader, file hash, and results.

**Localization:** Importer accepts declared encoding and locale-specific source formats but normalizes data before persistence.

**Verification:** Import fixtures for replay, partial failure, encoding, and validation.

### ERP-SALES-067 — Versioned sales integration events

**Shall:** The system shall publish versioned sales lifecycle events with tenant/entity scope, immutable business ID, event ID, occurred time, and schema version.

**Rationale:** Decoupled modules need reliable change propagation without sharing database tables.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**1.** Consumers can deduplicate repeated event ID and reject unsupported schema version safely.

**2.** Events distinguish business occurrence time from publication time.

**Exception / edge case:** Out-of-order event delivery is reconciled using aggregate version and does not regress state.

**Security and audit:** Authenticate publishers, minimize payload PII, and retain correlation IDs for audit.

**Localization:** Events carry locale only when required for rendered content; codes and numeric data are locale-neutral.

**Verification:** Schema compatibility, duplicate, and out-of-order consumer tests.

### ERP-SALES-068 — Sales role and field permissions

**Shall:** The system shall enforce least-privilege permissions by tenant, legal entity, record scope, action, and sensitive field for CRM and commercial documents.

**Rationale:** Sales access spans personal data, pricing, credit, and financial documents with different confidentiality.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**1.** Unauthorized API attempts to view, edit, export, approve, or post protected records are denied.

**2.** Role changes take effect on subsequent requests and are represented in audit history.

**Exception / edge case:** Emergency access is time-bound, approved, and reviewed after use.

**Security and audit:** Use server-side authorization, deny-by-default policy, and tamper-resistant access/change logs.

**Localization:** Permission names can be translated in UI but canonical action IDs are stable.

**Verification:** Authorization matrix tests and privileged-access review.

### ERP-SALES-069 — Sales audit trail and retention

**Shall:** The system shall retain attributable before/after audit events for material customer, opportunity, quote, order, invoice, approval, and configuration changes under tenant retention policy.

**Rationale:** Commercial disputes and accounting review require reconstructable history.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**1.** Audit event includes actor/service, timestamp, entity ID, action, changed field names, and correlation ID.

**2.** Ordinary business users cannot alter or erase retained events.

**Exception / edge case:** Privacy erasure or statutory retention conflicts route through configured legal review and controlled anonymization, not ad hoc deletion.

**Security and audit:** Protect audit storage, restrict query/export, and monitor tampering or privileged reads.

**Localization:** Audit timestamps are stored in an unambiguous canonical form and displayed in viewer locale.

**Verification:** Mutation history tests, access-control tests, and retention-policy simulation.

### ERP-SALES-070 — Multilingual accessible sales interface

**Shall:** The system shall provide locale-selectable sales UI and documents, language/direction metadata for content, and accessible keyboard-operable controls aligned to the selected WCAG conformance target.

**Rationale:** Multilingual enterprise users require understandable content and usable workflows across scripts and assistive technologies.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**1.** Changing locale updates translated chrome and formatting without changing stored monetary values or status codes.

**2.** Automated accessibility checks and manual keyboard/screen-reader review cover lead, quote, order, and invoice critical paths.

**Exception / edge case:** A missing translation falls back to configured tenant language and marks the untranslated field for administrators.

**Security and audit:** Escape user-provided localized content, isolate bidirectional text, and retain authorization behavior across locales.

**Localization:** Support language tags, RTL layout, Unicode input, locale-aware dates/numbers, and document-language metadata; locale does not determine tax or legal policy.

**Verification:** Locale/RTL test matrix plus WCAG-targeted automated and manual accessibility evaluation.

## Sales, CRM, Order Management, and Billing — requirement cards

**REQUIREMENT 0141 OF 1120  |  SALES, CRM, ORDER MANAGEMENT, AND BILLING**

## ERP-SALES-001 — Tenant-scoped customer account

**Normative requirement:** The system shall assign each customer account to exactly one tenant and legal entity context, and enforce that scope in every read and write.

**Rationale:** Customer records are sensitive and may be legally owned by distinct entities.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Create account A in tenant T1; an authenticated T2 user cannot read, update, export, or reference A.

**AC 2.** Attempt cross-tenant account association through API and batch import; reject without mutation.

**Exception / edge case:** A specifically authorized shared-service operator may access multiple tenants only through an audited support grant.

**Security and audit implications:** Apply tenant authorization in service and database access paths; audit privileged cross-tenant access and denials.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Store language and regional preferences on accounts without using locale as a tenant boundary.

**Verification method:** Automated API/DB integration tests using two tenants plus authorization review.

**REQUIREMENT 0142 OF 1120  |  SALES, CRM, ORDER MANAGEMENT, AND BILLING**

## ERP-SALES-002 — Customer party and role model

**Normative requirement:** The system shall represent a customer as a party that can have separate organization, person, billing, shipping, and sold-to roles linked by explicit relationships.

**Rationale:** Enterprise account relationships cannot safely be flattened into a single name/address record.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** An organization can have multiple contacts and ship-to sites while retaining one billing account.

**AC 2.** Changing a contact relationship does not rewrite historic invoice recipient snapshots.

**Exception / edge case:** A sole trader may be both an organization-like account and its only contact.

**Security and audit implications:** Restrict personal contact fields by role and log changes to party links.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Names, honorifics, and address forms must support local scripts and configurable display order.

**Verification method:** Domain tests for relationship cardinality and historical snapshot regression.

**REQUIREMENT 0143 OF 1120  |  SALES, CRM, ORDER MANAGEMENT, AND BILLING**

## ERP-SALES-003 — Multichannel lead capture

**Normative requirement:** The system shall accept leads through UI, API, and configured imports with source, received timestamp, owner, and consent provenance where collected.

**Rationale:** Lead origin and intake history support follow-up and lawful processing.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Each accepted lead retains channel, source reference, and server-recorded receipt time.

**AC 2.** Malformed required identifiers are returned as row-level errors in imports without losing valid rows.

**Exception / edge case:** Anonymous inquiries may be stored without a named individual until identification is necessary.

**Security and audit implications:** Rate-limit public intake, sanitize content, and restrict access to personal data.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Accept Unicode names and locale-specific phone formats without assuming English or a fixed phone pattern.

**Verification method:** API contract tests and import fixtures covering Unicode and malformed rows.

**REQUIREMENT 0144 OF 1120  |  SALES, CRM, ORDER MANAGEMENT, AND BILLING**

## ERP-SALES-004 — Lead qualification lifecycle

**Normative requirement:** The system shall provide configurable lead statuses and required qualification fields, with governed conversion to an account, contact, and opportunity.

**Rationale:** Separating prospect qualification from committed pipeline improves data quality.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Tenant administrator configures statuses and transition-required fields.

**AC 2.** Conversion creates linked records once and records source lead ID; repeated conversion is rejected or returns the same result.

**Exception / edge case:** A lead may be disqualified or retained without conversion and later re-opened by an authorized role.

**Security and audit implications:** Limit status configuration and conversion rights; record actor, old/new status, and conversion links.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Status labels and validation messages are translatable while stored codes remain locale-neutral.

**Verification method:** State-transition tests and role-based API tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0145 OF 1120  |  SALES, CRM, ORDER MANAGEMENT, AND BILLING**

## ERP-SALES-005 — Potential duplicate detection

**Normative requirement:** The system shall identify likely duplicate parties using configurable normalized identifiers and present a reviewable match explanation before merge.

**Rationale:** Duplicate accounts fragment activities, credit exposure, and billing history.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Configure email, tax identifier, and phone matching independently; candidate list identifies matched attributes.

**AC 2.** A suspected match is never auto-merged solely from fuzzy similarity.

**Exception / edge case:** Shared corporate email or switchboard phone can legitimately appear on many contacts.

**Security and audit implications:** Protect search results from unauthorized party disclosure; audit candidate resolution and merges.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Normalization must preserve source values and account for Unicode normalization and locale-specific phone parsing.

**Verification method:** Deterministic matching tests with collision and multilingual-name cases.

**REQUIREMENT 0146 OF 1120  |  SALES, CRM, ORDER MANAGEMENT, AND BILLING**

## ERP-SALES-006 — Marketing and contact preferences

**Normative requirement:** The system shall record purpose-specific contact preferences, source, timestamp, and withdrawal history separately from operational service communications.

**Rationale:** Consent and communication rules vary by jurisdiction, channel, and purpose.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A recorded withdrawal suppresses subsequent configured marketing sends for that channel and purpose.

**AC 2.** Preference history is append-only and shows actor/source and effective time.

**Exception / edge case:** Applicable legal basis and mandatory retention or service messages may differ; tenant compliance configuration determines treatment.

**Security and audit implications:** Restrict preference changes and retain evidence without exposing unnecessary personal data.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Capture notice language/version and render preference controls in user-selected language.

**Verification method:** Event-driven suppression tests plus audit-history inspection.

**REQUIREMENT 0147 OF 1120  |  SALES, CRM, ORDER MANAGEMENT, AND BILLING**

## ERP-SALES-007 — CRM interaction timeline

**Normative requirement:** The system shall link calls, meetings, emails, notes, and tasks to authorized party, lead, or opportunity records with actor, occurred-at time, and source.

**Rationale:** A coherent timeline reduces duplicate outreach and preserves context.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Timeline orders events by occurred-at while distinguishing late entry from recorded-at.

**AC 2.** Deleting a party cannot silently delete an interaction required by configured retention rules.

**Exception / edge case:** Imported activity with unknown actor retains an explicit external-source identity rather than impersonating a user.

**Security and audit implications:** Apply record-level visibility to notes and attachments; audit edits and deletions.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Render timestamps in viewer timezone and translate activity types without translating original note content.

**Verification method:** API and UI tests with timezone, ownership, and deletion cases.

**REQUIREMENT 0148 OF 1120  |  SALES, CRM, ORDER MANAGEMENT, AND BILLING**

## ERP-SALES-008 — CRM case and escalation record

**Normative requirement:** The system shall support customer issues as cases with configurable category, priority, owner, status, response target, and linked account/order references.

**Rationale:** Sales CRM requires traceable issue ownership without conflating a case with an order or invoice.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Case transitions validate required resolution fields and preserve status history.

**AC 2.** Authorized users can filter overdue cases by configured target and owner.

**Exception / edge case:** A case can exist before customer identity is verified and later be linked without losing history.

**Security and audit implications:** Restrict sensitive case notes and attachments; record reassignment and escalation actions.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Support localized case categories and translated templates while preserving source text.

**Verification method:** Workflow tests and permission tests on case notes and links.

**REQUIREMENT 0149 OF 1120  |  SALES, CRM, ORDER MANAGEMENT, AND BILLING**

## ERP-SALES-009 — Effective-dated product sales catalog

**Normative requirement:** The system shall maintain sellable products and services with stable IDs, status, effective dates, and configurable sales attributes.

**Rationale:** Quotes and orders must retain the offering definition applicable at transaction time.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A product outside its effective interval cannot be newly quoted unless an explicit override is authorized.

**AC 2.** Changing a product description does not alter a previously accepted quote snapshot.

**Exception / edge case:** A discontinued product may remain selectable for an approved replacement or service renewal.

**Security and audit implications:** Limit catalog publication and audit effective-date changes.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Store translated descriptions by locale with fallback; identifiers and SKU remain language-independent.

**Verification method:** Catalog boundary-date tests and quote snapshot regression.

**REQUIREMENT 0150 OF 1120  |  SALES, CRM, ORDER MANAGEMENT, AND BILLING**

## ERP-SALES-010 — Product units and quantities

**Normative requirement:** The system shall model sales unit of measure, precision, and approved conversions per product, and reject ambiguous or unsupported quantities.

**Rationale:** Quantity interpretation must remain consistent across pricing, orders, and fulfillment.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Configured conversion transforms quantity using explicit numerator/denominator and preserves entered unit.

**AC 2.** Precision beyond the product's allowed scale is rejected or rounded only by an explicit policy.

**Exception / edge case:** Services may be sold in fractional hours while discrete goods prohibit fractional units.

**Security and audit implications:** Audit changes to conversion factors because they affect value and fulfillment.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Localize unit labels and decimal display; never parse stored quantities using display separators.

**Verification method:** Calculation tests with fractional, large, and conversion quantities.

**REQUIREMENT 0151 OF 1120  |  SALES, CRM, ORDER MANAGEMENT, AND BILLING**

## ERP-SALES-011 — Sales territories and ownership

**Normative requirement:** The system shall assign account, lead, and opportunity ownership using configurable territory rules and explicit manual override permissions.

**Rationale:** Territory assignment governs workload, pipeline, and access decisions.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Rule execution records matched rule/version and resulting owner or queue.

**AC 2.** Changing territory rules does not silently rewrite closed-period ownership.

**Exception / edge case:** Overlapping rules route to a configured priority or exception queue, not nondeterministic ownership.

**Security and audit implications:** Audit rules, reassignment, and override reasons; use ownership only as one access attribute.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Territory labels are translatable; geographic boundaries use configured authoritative codes rather than translated names.

**Verification method:** Rule-engine unit tests and access-control integration tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0152 OF 1120  |  SALES, CRM, ORDER MANAGEMENT, AND BILLING**

## ERP-SALES-012 — Account hierarchy and rollups

**Normative requirement:** The system shall support parent-child account relationships with cycle prevention and configurable roll-up views for pipeline and exposure.

**Rationale:** Corporate groups need consolidated visibility without losing legal-entity detail.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Attempted self-parenting and indirect cycles are rejected.

**AC 2.** Roll-up totals identify included entities and exclude records outside the viewer's authorization.

**Exception / edge case:** A customer may have matrix affiliations; only the designated hierarchy is used for standard roll-up, with secondary links explicit.

**Security and audit implications:** Audit hierarchy changes and prevent roll-ups from disclosing inaccessible subsidiary data.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Display hierarchy labels in user locale while retaining legal registered names as entered.

**Verification method:** Graph integrity tests and filtered aggregation tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0153 OF 1120  |  SALES, CRM, ORDER MANAGEMENT, AND BILLING**

## ERP-SALES-013 — Customer onboarding controls

**Normative requirement:** The system shall support configurable onboarding checks and approval gates before an account can transact on credit or receive invoices.

**Rationale:** Risk and regulatory onboarding requirements vary by industry and jurisdiction.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Tenant configures required checks and evidence types by account class.

**AC 2.** Order submission for an account missing an enabled mandatory check returns the unmet control IDs.

**Exception / edge case:** Cash-only or low-risk customer classes may have a configured reduced check set.

**Security and audit implications:** Restrict sensitive evidence, mask identifiers, and log reviewer decisions and overrides.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Onboarding check labels and notices are translatable; legal evidence formats are configured per region.

**Verification method:** Configuration-driven workflow tests with approved and incomplete account fixtures.

**REQUIREMENT 0154 OF 1120  |  SALES, CRM, ORDER MANAGEMENT, AND BILLING**

## ERP-SALES-014 — Controlled party merge

**Normative requirement:** The system shall provide an authorized, previewable merge of duplicate accounts or contacts that preserves a permanent redirect and transaction provenance.

**Rationale:** Data cleanup must not orphan orders, invoices, or audit trails.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Merge preview lists records and relationships to be reassigned before confirmation.

**AC 2.** After merge, prior identifiers resolve to the surviving party and historic documents retain original snapshots.

**Exception / edge case:** Parties with conflicting legal entities or posted balances require specialist resolution rather than direct merge.

**Security and audit implications:** Require elevated permission, reason, and immutable before/after merge audit event.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Choose surviving display names explicitly; do not auto-translate legal party names.

**Verification method:** Integration tests checking referential integrity and event history.

**REQUIREMENT 0155 OF 1120  |  SALES, CRM, ORDER MANAGEMENT, AND BILLING**

## ERP-SALES-015 — Opportunity value and close plan

**Normative requirement:** The system shall track opportunity amount, expected close date, stage, owner, currency, source, and linked customer with change history.

**Rationale:** Consistent opportunity facts enable pipeline governance and forecast analysis.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Required fields can vary by configured stage and opportunity type.

**AC 2.** Currency and amount changes preserve previous values, actor, and timestamp.

**Exception / edge case:** An early-stage opportunity may link to a prospect before account conversion.

**Security and audit implications:** Enforce record visibility and audit sensitive amount/owner changes.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Store ISO-like currency identifier and decimal amount; localize dates and display formatting only.

**Verification method:** Schema/API tests and history assertions across stage changes.

**REQUIREMENT 0156 OF 1120  |  SALES, CRM, ORDER MANAGEMENT, AND BILLING**

## ERP-SALES-016 — Opportunity stage transition rules

**Normative requirement:** The system shall implement configurable opportunity stage transitions with stage entry criteria and required exit fields.

**Rationale:** Governed transitions make pipeline state meaningful and reportable.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A prohibited transition is rejected with an actionable validation code.

**AC 2.** A closed-won transition requires configured contract/order linkage or an explicit exception route.

**Exception / edge case:** An authorized administrator may reopen a closed opportunity with a reason and retained prior closure event.

**Security and audit implications:** Restrict stage configuration and reopening; preserve actor and reason.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Translate stage labels and errors while keeping stable codes for integrations.

**Verification method:** State-machine tests for allowed, prohibited, and reopen paths.

**REQUIREMENT 0157 OF 1120  |  SALES, CRM, ORDER MANAGEMENT, AND BILLING**

## ERP-SALES-017 — Opportunity products and value

**Normative requirement:** The system shall permit opportunity line items with product, quantity, target price, and currency, and calculate a configurable opportunity total.

**Rationale:** Line-level estimates support solution planning and quote generation.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Configured total equals the sum of line estimates under the selected currency precision.

**AC 2.** Generating a quote copies selected opportunity lines without modifying the opportunity.

**Exception / edge case:** Non-product opportunities may use a manually estimated amount with an explicit estimate type.

**Security and audit implications:** Audit adjustments to amounts and prevent unauthorized product visibility.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Localize unit and currency display; retain numeric values independent of locale.

**Verification method:** Calculation and quote-conversion integration tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0158 OF 1120  |  SALES, CRM, ORDER MANAGEMENT, AND BILLING**

## ERP-SALES-018 — Pipeline forecast categories

**Normative requirement:** The system shall support configurable forecast categories and period rollups that distinguish user forecasts from system-calculated pipeline.

**Rationale:** Forecast judgments must be identifiable rather than confused with weighted pipeline.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A forecast report separately shows unweighted value, configured probability-weighted value, and submitted override.

**AC 2.** Submitted forecast records owner, period, submission time, and version.

**Exception / edge case:** An opportunity without a forecast category appears in an explicit unclassified bucket.

**Security and audit implications:** Limit forecast submission and audit overrides.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Period labels follow the entity fiscal calendar; number formatting follows viewer locale.

**Verification method:** Reproducible report fixtures and forecast submission audit test.

**REQUIREMENT 0159 OF 1120  |  SALES, CRM, ORDER MANAGEMENT, AND BILLING**

## ERP-SALES-019 — Opportunity competitors and risks

**Normative requirement:** The system shall record configurable competitors, decision criteria, risks, and next actions on opportunities as structured, reportable fields.

**Rationale:** Structured competitive context supports coaching and win-loss analysis.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Configured competitor and reason codes are selectable by authorized users.

**AC 2.** Closed-lost transition captures configured loss reason and optional competitor.

**Exception / edge case:** Competitor may be unknown or undisclosed; null remains distinguishable from 'none'.

**Security and audit implications:** Restrict commercially sensitive notes and audit changes to loss classification.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Translate controlled labels; preserve free-text descriptions in their authored language.

**Verification method:** UI/API validation and report aggregation tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0160 OF 1120  |  SALES, CRM, ORDER MANAGEMENT, AND BILLING**

## ERP-SALES-020 — Sales forecast snapshots

**Normative requirement:** The system shall preserve period-end forecast snapshots separately from live opportunity values and support reproducible comparison across snapshots.

**Rationale:** Forecast accuracy analysis requires historical, not retrospectively changed, inputs.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Snapshot contains included record IDs, values, categories, and generation timestamp.

**AC 2.** Editing an opportunity after snapshot creation does not change that snapshot's totals.

**Exception / edge case:** A failed snapshot job is marked incomplete and cannot be presented as a finalized period snapshot.

**Security and audit implications:** Restrict snapshot deletion and record execution identity.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Snapshot data is locale-neutral; reports render with selected locale and recorded fiscal calendar.

**Verification method:** Snapshot immutability test and deterministic recomputation.

**REQUIREMENT 0161 OF 1120  |  SALES, CRM, ORDER MANAGEMENT, AND BILLING**

## ERP-SALES-021 — Quote composition and validity

**Normative requirement:** The system shall create customer quotes with lines, terms, expiration, currency, delivery assumptions, and a versioned total calculation.

**Rationale:** Quotes establish the commercial offer presented for acceptance.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Expired quote cannot be accepted without authorized revalidation.

**AC 2.** Rendered quote reconciles exactly to stored lines, discounts, taxes if configured, and total.

**Exception / edge case:** A quote may have no expiry only when tenant policy explicitly allows it.

**Security and audit implications:** Restrict quote issuance and capture document generation and recipient events.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Quote language and number/date formatting are selected independently from operator locale.

**Verification method:** Document-to-record reconciliation and expiry tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0162 OF 1120  |  SALES, CRM, ORDER MANAGEMENT, AND BILLING**

## ERP-SALES-022 — Immutable quote revisions

**Normative requirement:** The system shall create a new revision for any material change to a sent or accepted quote and retain prior revision content and status.

**Rationale:** A customer must be able to distinguish the exact offer accepted.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Changing price or scope creates a new revision with distinct ID.

**AC 2.** Acceptance references one specific revision and cannot silently migrate to a later version.

**Exception / edge case:** Draft-only unsent quotes may be edited in place if no downstream reference exists.

**Security and audit implications:** Preserve prior rendered copies and audit revision author and reason.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Retain the language and locale used for each issued revision.

**Verification method:** Version lifecycle tests and archived-document comparison.

**REQUIREMENT 0163 OF 1120  |  SALES, CRM, ORDER MANAGEMENT, AND BILLING**

## ERP-SALES-023 — Quote approval routing

**Normative requirement:** The system shall route quotes through configurable approvals based on discount, margin, value, product, and customer risk before issuance.

**Rationale:** Commercial authority limits vary by organization and product.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A quote meeting configured threshold remains blocked until all required approvals are recorded.

**AC 2.** Any material edit after approval invalidates affected approvals and records the changed fields.

**Exception / edge case:** An emergency override requires a designated role, reason, and post-action audit trail.

**Security and audit implications:** Separate requester and approver when policy demands; protect approval records from modification.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Approval messages and reasons support translated UI; numeric thresholds are currency-aware.

**Verification method:** Rules-engine tests for thresholds, edits, delegation, and override.

**REQUIREMENT 0164 OF 1120  |  SALES, CRM, ORDER MANAGEMENT, AND BILLING**

## ERP-SALES-024 — Effective-dated price books

**Normative requirement:** The system shall resolve a customer quote price from an effective-dated price book using explicit product, currency, unit, and eligibility rules.

**Rationale:** Price determination must be repeatable and explainable.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Pricing response includes selected price-book ID, rule, effective interval, and base value.

**AC 2.** Overlapping active entries are rejected or resolved by an explicit configured precedence.

**Exception / edge case:** A missing catalog price yields a controlled exception or authorized manual price, never silent zero.

**Security and audit implications:** Restrict price book changes and retain change history.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Price books key by currency, not formatted symbol; date boundaries use entity timezone policy.

**Verification method:** Boundary and precedence test matrix.

**REQUIREMENT 0165 OF 1120  |  SALES, CRM, ORDER MANAGEMENT, AND BILLING**

## ERP-SALES-025 — Line and document discounts

**Normative requirement:** The system shall calculate percentage and fixed discounts at line or document level using explicit stacking order and rounding rules.

**Rationale:** Discount sequencing changes the net price and approval requirement.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** For configured stack order, test fixtures produce documented net line and document totals.

**AC 2.** Discounts cannot exceed configurable caps without approval.

**Exception / edge case:** A 100% promotional line may be permitted by rule; negative net price is rejected unless explicitly configured as a credit.

**Security and audit implications:** Restrict discount-policy edits and record approver, override, and applied discount details.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Percent and fixed amounts are parsed and displayed by locale, but calculations use canonical decimals and currency precision.

**Verification method:** Discount sequencing, cap, and rounding test matrix.

**REQUIREMENT 0166 OF 1120  |  SALES, CRM, ORDER MANAGEMENT, AND BILLING**

## ERP-SALES-026 — Contracted customer pricing

**Normative requirement:** The system shall support customer-specific contracted prices with effective periods, minimum quantities, and precedence over standard price books when configured.

**Rationale:** Enterprise agreements need price commitments distinct from public catalog prices.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Eligible account and quantity resolve to the applicable contract price with source reference.

**AC 2.** Expired contract pricing is excluded unless extension approval is recorded.

**Exception / edge case:** A contract price can be superseded by a more specific amendment with a later effective date.

**Security and audit implications:** Limit contract price visibility and audit amendments and overrides.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Contract descriptions may be multilingual; calculations use configured currency and unit precision.

**Verification method:** Precedence, quantity threshold, and effective-date tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0167 OF 1120  |  SALES, CRM, ORDER MANAGEMENT, AND BILLING**

## ERP-SALES-027 — Transaction and base currency handling

**Normative requirement:** The system shall preserve transaction currency, entered amount, and applicable exchange-rate source/date separately from entity base-currency reporting values.

**Rationale:** Multi-currency sales require a clear distinction between customer value and ledger translation.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Quote or order stores transaction currency and rate metadata used for any base conversion.

**AC 2.** Changing a later rate does not restate an already posted invoice.

**Exception / edge case:** If no rate exists for a required date, posting is blocked or uses an explicitly approved fallback policy.

**Security and audit implications:** Restrict rate override and retain rate provenance with each converted value.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Format transaction and base currencies by viewer locale; never infer currency from locale.

**Verification method:** Rate-date, missing-rate, and historical non-restatement tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0168 OF 1120  |  SALES, CRM, ORDER MANAGEMENT, AND BILLING**

## ERP-SALES-028 — Configurable tax determination boundary

**Normative requirement:** The system shall call a configured tax determination service or ruleset for jurisdiction, product tax category, and transaction context, and retain returned tax detail without hard-coding universal tax law.

**Rationale:** Taxability, place-of-supply, rates, and document rules vary by jurisdiction and date.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Tax calculation request records jurisdiction inputs, rule/version, effective time, and returned components.

**AC 2.** Unresolved tax jurisdiction blocks invoice posting when tenant policy marks tax required.

**Exception / edge case:** A tenant may explicitly configure tax-exempt or out-of-scope treatment with evidence and reason.

**Security and audit implications:** Authenticate tax-service calls, protect sensitive tax identifiers, and audit any manual determination override.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Jurisdiction codes and legal tax outcomes are configured by entity; translated labels do not alter tax rules.

**Verification method:** Tax adapter contract tests with jurisdiction, effective-date, and unresolved-input cases.

**REQUIREMENT 0169 OF 1120  |  SALES, CRM, ORDER MANAGEMENT, AND BILLING**

## ERP-SALES-029 — Delivery and trade-term capture

**Normative requirement:** The system shall record delivery address, requested date, carrier instructions, and optional configured trade-term code and named place on quote and order.

**Rationale:** Fulfillment responsibility and delivery assumptions affect commercial commitments.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Order captures a delivery-address snapshot even when linked account address later changes.

**AC 2.** Trade-term value is selected from tenant-enabled code set and requires place when configured.

**Exception / edge case:** Digital services may have no physical ship-to address and use a configured service location instead.

**Security and audit implications:** Mask personal delivery details in broad reports; audit changes after acceptance.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Address entry is country-specific and allows non-Latin scripts; term labels can be translated.

**Verification method:** Address snapshot and configured-field validation tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0170 OF 1120  |  SALES, CRM, ORDER MANAGEMENT, AND BILLING**

## ERP-SALES-030 — Quote acceptance evidence

**Normative requirement:** The system shall record acceptance evidence against an exact quote revision, including method, timestamp, accepting identity when known, and retained artifact reference.

**Rationale:** Order creation should be traceable to an agreed offer.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Accepted revision ID is immutable and visible on generated order.

**AC 2.** API acceptance with duplicate external event ID is idempotent.

**Exception / edge case:** Verbal acceptance may be recorded by an employee with approver role and explicit evidence type.

**Security and audit implications:** Protect evidence artifacts and log access and state changes.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Capture acceptance language and document locale; do not infer legal validity from locale.

**Verification method:** Acceptance workflow tests plus evidence access audit.

**REQUIREMENT 0171 OF 1120  |  SALES, CRM, ORDER MANAGEMENT, AND BILLING**

## ERP-SALES-031 — Sales order creation

**Normative requirement:** The system shall create a sales order from an accepted quote or authorized direct entry with customer, lines, terms, currency, and source links.

**Rationale:** The order is the operational commitment connecting sales to fulfillment and billing.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Converted order references source quote revision and copies accepted commercial terms.

**AC 2.** Direct order requires configured authority and records its origin.

**Exception / edge case:** A quote may convert to multiple orders only when split-conversion policy explicitly permits it.

**Security and audit implications:** Separate order entry, release, and approval rights where configured; audit source and edits.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Order document language can differ from user interface language.

**Verification method:** Quote conversion and direct-order role tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0172 OF 1120  |  SALES, CRM, ORDER MANAGEMENT, AND BILLING**

## ERP-SALES-032 — Idempotent order submission

**Normative requirement:** The system shall accept a client idempotency key for order creation and return the original order result for a repeated identical request.

**Rationale:** Network retries must not create duplicate customer orders.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Repeating a request with same tenant/key/body returns the same order identifier.

**AC 2.** Reusing a key with materially different body returns conflict and creates no second order.

**Exception / edge case:** Keys expire only after a documented retention period, and external business reference uniqueness remains separately configurable.

**Security and audit implications:** Scope keys to tenant and caller; avoid leaking an order to a different principal.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** No locale-specific formatting is accepted as a substitute for canonical numeric payloads.

**Verification method:** Concurrent duplicate-request API test.

**REQUIREMENT 0173 OF 1120  |  SALES, CRM, ORDER MANAGEMENT, AND BILLING**

## ERP-SALES-033 — Order validation and lifecycle

**Normative requirement:** The system shall validate order header and lines against configured status transitions, customer eligibility, price, and required fulfillment data before release.

**Rationale:** Invalid commitments create downstream billing and shipping errors.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Release returns field-addressable error codes for each failed validation.

**AC 2.** Released order records validation result version and release actor.

**Exception / edge case:** A configured non-stock service line may bypass warehouse checks but not customer and price checks.

**Security and audit implications:** Restrict release and bypass permissions; log validation exceptions.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Return stable error codes with locale-specific messages and correctly formatted field labels.

**Verification method:** Negative and positive release test matrix.

**REQUIREMENT 0174 OF 1120  |  SALES, CRM, ORDER MANAGEMENT, AND BILLING**

## ERP-SALES-034 — Post-release order amendments

**Normative requirement:** The system shall version material changes to a released order and require configured reapproval for price, quantity, date, or destination changes.

**Rationale:** Changes after commitment can affect fulfillment, tax, and customer agreement.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Material edit creates an amendment event and preserves prior values.

**AC 2.** Downstream fulfillment and billing receive the amendment only after required approval.

**Exception / edge case:** A spelling correction to a non-legal internal note need not create a commercial amendment.

**Security and audit implications:** Audit who changed each commercial field and why.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Retain localized customer-facing text per amendment revision.

**Verification method:** Amendment workflow and downstream event tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0175 OF 1120  |  SALES, CRM, ORDER MANAGEMENT, AND BILLING**

## ERP-SALES-035 — Order holds and release control

**Normative requirement:** The system shall support independent credit, compliance, pricing, and manual holds that prevent configured downstream actions until an authorized release.

**Rationale:** A single undifferentiated hold obscures why work is blocked and who can clear it.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** An order with any blocking hold cannot be released to the configured next stage.

**AC 2.** Hold record includes reason code, source, set time, and clear actor/time.

**Exception / edge case:** A nonblocking informational hold does not prevent fulfillment if configuration says so.

**Security and audit implications:** Restrict hold override by reason and role; monitor override frequency.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Translate hold codes and messages but preserve canonical code in interfaces.

**Verification method:** Multi-hold transition tests and audit event inspection.

**REQUIREMENT 0176 OF 1120  |  SALES, CRM, ORDER MANAGEMENT, AND BILLING**

## ERP-SALES-036 — Order line partial fulfillment

**Normative requirement:** The system shall permit fulfillment quantities to be tracked by order line and shipment so partial delivery does not close unfulfilled quantities.

**Rationale:** Many orders ship in installments or from multiple sites.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Two shipments against one line update fulfilled and remaining quantities independently.

**AC 2.** Invoice eligibility follows configured shipped, delivered, milestone, or order basis.

**Exception / edge case:** Over-fulfillment is rejected unless tolerance and approval are configured.

**Security and audit implications:** Authenticate fulfillment events and preserve shipment references.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Use product unit precision and localized delivery documents.

**Verification method:** Partial shipment and invoice-eligibility integration tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0177 OF 1120  |  SALES, CRM, ORDER MANAGEMENT, AND BILLING**

## ERP-SALES-037 — Backorder and shortage policy

**Normative requirement:** The system shall represent unfulfilled demand as backorder quantity and apply a configured allocation, substitution, or cancellation policy.

**Rationale:** Customers and planners need explicit handling of supply shortage.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A shortage leaves a measurable remaining quantity and expected date or unknown-date status.

**AC 2.** Substitution requires customer approval when configured and links substitute to original line.

**Exception / edge case:** Non-backorderable products automatically enter the configured exception or cancellation flow.

**Security and audit implications:** Audit quantity and promised-date overrides.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Backorder notices use customer's selected language and local date representation.

**Verification method:** Inventory shortage simulation and substitution consent test.

**REQUIREMENT 0178 OF 1120  |  SALES, CRM, ORDER MANAGEMENT, AND BILLING**

## ERP-SALES-038 — Inventory reservation contract

**Normative requirement:** The system shall request and consume inventory availability through an explicit inventory-module contract rather than maintaining a competing stock ledger.

**Rationale:** A single inventory authority prevents divergent available-to-promise values.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Reservation request includes tenant, order line, item, site, quantity, and requested date.

**AC 2.** Timeout or rejection leaves order reservation status pending/failed and creates no false confirmed allocation.

**Exception / edge case:** Non-inventory service items skip reservation by explicit item classification.

**Security and audit implications:** Authenticate service identity and correlate all reservation commands and replies.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Unit and item descriptions are localized at presentation only; payload identifiers are stable.

**Verification method:** Contract tests for success, timeout, duplicate, and rejection.

**REQUIREMENT 0179 OF 1120  |  SALES, CRM, ORDER MANAGEMENT, AND BILLING**

## ERP-SALES-039 — Order cancellation and closeout

**Normative requirement:** The system shall cancel unfulfilled order quantities through a reasoned workflow and release reservations without deleting posted commercial history.

**Rationale:** Cancellation must reconcile customer commitment and downstream resources.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Cancellation produces a dated event, reason, and remaining quantity outcome.

**AC 2.** Posted invoices remain and require a separate credit-note/refund process.

**Exception / edge case:** Partially fulfilled orders cancel only remaining eligible quantity unless full cancellation is separately approved.

**Security and audit implications:** Require role-based approval for cancellation after release and log linked resource releases.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Customer cancellation notice uses document locale and localized reason label.

**Verification method:** Partial/full cancellation tests with invoice and reservation references.

**REQUIREMENT 0180 OF 1120  |  SALES, CRM, ORDER MANAGEMENT, AND BILLING**

## ERP-SALES-040 — Recurring order schedule

**Normative requirement:** The system shall support recurring sales schedules with frequency, time zone, effective interval, billing trigger, and pause/cancel status.

**Rationale:** Subscriptions and repeat services require controlled recurring execution.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Schedule generates at most one occurrence per period and idempotency key.

**AC 2.** Paused schedule produces no new order or invoice while preserving prior occurrences.

**Exception / edge case:** Month-end dates absent in a target month follow an explicit roll-forward/last-day rule.

**Security and audit implications:** Audit schedule edits and restrict next-run overrides.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Frequency and dates are presented in account/entity timezone policy, including daylight-saving transitions.

**Verification method:** Calendar-boundary, DST, pause, and retry tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0181 OF 1120  |  SALES, CRM, ORDER MANAGEMENT, AND BILLING**

## ERP-SALES-041 — Configured bundles and options

**Normative requirement:** The system shall represent configurable product bundles with versioned component rules, required options, and derived order-line provenance.

**Rationale:** Industry extensions need product configuration without hard-coded product-specific code.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Invalid option combination is rejected by the active configuration version.

**AC 2.** Order snapshot lists selected options and derived components used at acceptance.

**Exception / edge case:** A retired configuration remains readable for historic orders but cannot be newly selected.

**Security and audit implications:** Restrict rule publication and audit overrides to invalid configurations.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Option labels and help text are localized while option codes remain stable.

**Verification method:** Configuration rule and historical snapshot tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0182 OF 1120  |  SALES, CRM, ORDER MANAGEMENT, AND BILLING**

## ERP-SALES-042 — Invoice source and eligibility

**Normative requirement:** The system shall generate billing candidates only from configured eligible sales events such as order, shipment, milestone, or subscription occurrence.

**Rationale:** Billing timing is contract- and industry-dependent and must be configurable.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Each invoice line retains source order/line and triggering event ID.

**AC 2.** The same source event cannot be billed twice unless an explicit split-billing rule applies.

**Exception / edge case:** A deposit invoice may precede fulfillment when contract and tenant policy permit it.

**Security and audit implications:** Audit billing source event and any manual candidate creation.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Invoice language inherits configured customer document language, not the operator locale.

**Verification method:** Source-to-invoice traceability and duplicate-event tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0183 OF 1120  |  SALES, CRM, ORDER MANAGEMENT, AND BILLING**

## ERP-SALES-043 — Draft invoice assembly

**Normative requirement:** The system shall assemble draft invoices from eligible billing events and allow authorized review of customer, lines, dates, amounts, tax results, and terms before posting.

**Rationale:** Review prevents incorrect documents from becoming accounting records.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Draft lines reconcile to source quantities and pricing snapshots.

**AC 2.** Changing a source order after draft creation flags the draft for refresh or review.

**Exception / edge case:** Automatically posted recurring invoices may bypass manual review only under an explicit tenant control.

**Security and audit implications:** Separate draft editor from poster where configured; log manual adjustments.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Preview supports selected document language and locale formatting.

**Verification method:** Draft reconciliation tests and posting authorization tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0184 OF 1120  |  SALES, CRM, ORDER MANAGEMENT, AND BILLING**

## ERP-SALES-044 — Configurable invoice numbering

**Normative requirement:** The system shall assign invoice identifiers using a configurable legal-entity series and numbering policy, with uniqueness and no silent reuse after posting.

**Rationale:** Numbering requirements differ by law, document type, and entity.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Posted invoices are unique within configured numbering scope.

**AC 2.** Voided numbers remain represented with status and reason if tenant rules require sequence continuity.

**Exception / edge case:** Drafts may use provisional identifiers where configured and do not consume a legal series until posting.

**Security and audit implications:** Restrict sequence configuration and audit gaps, voids, and resets.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Use configured numbering format without locale-dependent sorting or digit conversion in stored ID.

**Verification method:** Concurrent posting and numbering-policy tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0185 OF 1120  |  SALES, CRM, ORDER MANAGEMENT, AND BILLING**

## ERP-SALES-045 — Atomic invoice posting

**Normative requirement:** The system shall post an invoice as an atomic operation that persists finalized document data and emits one accounting handoff event or none.

**Rationale:** Billing documents and receivable postings must not diverge on partial failure.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Injected failure before commit leaves no posted invoice or handoff event.

**AC 2.** Retry after successful commit returns the same invoice and does not emit a duplicate posting event.

**Exception / edge case:** A downstream ledger outage leaves a durable pending handoff state without changing the posted invoice.

**Security and audit implications:** Poster identity and final values are immutable; restrict reversal to controlled process.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Persist exact rendered document version and locale with posted invoice.

**Verification method:** Transactional fault-injection and event idempotency tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0186 OF 1120  |  SALES, CRM, ORDER MANAGEMENT, AND BILLING**

## ERP-SALES-046 — Credit and debit adjustment documents

**Normative requirement:** The system shall issue credit or debit adjustment documents linked to original invoices, with reason, amount, and configured approval and tax recalculation.

**Rationale:** Corrections should preserve the original invoice rather than rewrite posted history.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Adjustment references original invoice and cannot exceed its eligible open amount except configured debit cases.

**AC 2.** Posted original invoice fields remain unchanged after adjustment.

**Exception / edge case:** Standalone credit may be allowed only under tenant policy and separate source reason.

**Security and audit implications:** Require reason and elevated approval thresholds; audit links and approvals.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Adjustment document follows jurisdiction-configured language and required labels.

**Verification method:** Credit/debit limit and original immutability tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0187 OF 1120  |  SALES, CRM, ORDER MANAGEMENT, AND BILLING**

## ERP-SALES-047 — Milestone and installment billing

**Normative requirement:** The system shall support configured billing schedules with milestone/installment amount, due trigger, status, and reconciliation to contract/order value.

**Rationale:** Project, service, and deposit billing do not always follow shipment quantities.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Schedule total is validated against contract value or a configured permitted variance.

**AC 2.** A completed milestone is billed no more than once unless an approved rebill event exists.

**Exception / edge case:** Milestone amount may be variable, but posting requires an authorized approved amount and evidence reference.

**Security and audit implications:** Limit milestone approval and record supporting evidence reference.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Milestone names can be translated; financial amounts remain canonical decimal values.

**Verification method:** Schedule reconciliation and duplicate milestone billing tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0188 OF 1120  |  SALES, CRM, ORDER MANAGEMENT, AND BILLING**

## ERP-SALES-048 — Tax line preservation

**Normative requirement:** The system shall preserve each tax determination component, taxable basis, rate, jurisdiction code, exemption treatment, and service/rule reference on the invoice.

**Rationale:** Tax audit and correction require the exact calculation context used at posting.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Invoice total equals net plus stored tax components under configured rounding policy.

**AC 2.** Replaying a tax response can reproduce stored components without consulting a changed current rate.

**Exception / edge case:** Tax engine unavailable blocks posting when tax is mandatory; a configured non-taxable route must be explicit.

**Security and audit implications:** Protect tax identifiers and log manual tax overrides.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Format tax labels per jurisdiction and document locale; retain jurisdiction codes untranslated.

**Verification method:** Tax calculation fixtures and persisted-component replay tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0189 OF 1120  |  SALES, CRM, ORDER MANAGEMENT, AND BILLING**

## ERP-SALES-049 — Currency rounding policy

**Normative requirement:** The system shall apply configured currency and document rounding rules consistently to line, tax, and invoice totals and expose any rounding adjustment.

**Rationale:** Rounding differences otherwise cause reconciliation failures across documents and ledger postings.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Defined boundary fixtures produce expected line and document totals for each enabled currency.

**AC 2.** Any aggregate rounding adjustment is stored as an explicit line/component, not hidden in an unexplained total.

**Exception / edge case:** A currency may have a nonstandard cash settlement precision distinct from accounting precision.

**Security and audit implications:** Changes to rounding configuration require approval and audit.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Display separators and symbols are locale-specific but do not affect arithmetic.

**Verification method:** Property-based decimal tests and cross-module total reconciliation.

**REQUIREMENT 0190 OF 1120  |  SALES, CRM, ORDER MANAGEMENT, AND BILLING**

## ERP-SALES-050 — Electronic invoice jurisdiction adapter

**Normative requirement:** The system shall expose a versioned adapter interface for jurisdiction-specific e-invoicing validation, signing, clearance, and status tracking without treating one country's format as universal.

**Rationale:** Mandatory schemas, clearance, signatures, and transport vary by jurisdiction and evolve over time.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Adapter identifies jurisdiction, schema/version, request correlation ID, and external status.

**AC 2.** Failed validation prevents transmission and returns structured error details.

**Exception / edge case:** Where e-invoicing is not enabled for the entity, standard invoice flow remains available subject to local policy.

**Security and audit implications:** Protect signing keys and credentials outside application logs; audit payload delivery and response.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Use jurisdictional schemas and language-specific mandated labels as adapter configuration.

**Verification method:** Adapter contract tests with sandbox responses and schema-version fixtures.

**REQUIREMENT 0191 OF 1120  |  SALES, CRM, ORDER MANAGEMENT, AND BILLING**

## ERP-SALES-051 — Invoice delivery tracking

**Normative requirement:** The system shall track invoice delivery attempts by channel, recipient, document revision, response, and time without equating delivery with payment or legal receipt.

**Rationale:** Operational delivery evidence is distinct from accounting state and legal service rules.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Resending creates a new delivery attempt linked to the same posted document revision.

**AC 2.** Bounce or rejection is visible and does not mark the invoice paid.

**Exception / edge case:** A manual delivery method may have unknown external receipt and must be labelled accordingly.

**Security and audit implications:** Restrict access to recipient details and delivery artifacts; log re-send actions.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Render attachment and email in the configured recipient language; preserve delivery status codes.

**Verification method:** Delivery event workflow and non-payment-state regression tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0192 OF 1120  |  SALES, CRM, ORDER MANAGEMENT, AND BILLING**

## ERP-SALES-052 — Receivables handoff contract

**Normative requirement:** The system shall publish posted invoice, credit, and debit documents to the finance/receivables module using stable IDs, due date, amounts, tax, and customer account references.

**Rationale:** Sales billing creates documents; receivables owns open-item accounting and settlement.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Handoff payload reconciles to the posted source document total and currency.

**AC 2.** Repeated event delivery is deduplicated by immutable document ID and event version.

**Exception / edge case:** A rejected account mapping is queued for correction and does not silently discard the document.

**Security and audit implications:** Use authenticated service identities and record payload correlation IDs without exposing unnecessary PII.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Contract codes are locale-neutral; document presentation language is carried as metadata.

**Verification method:** Schema contract, replay, and accounting reconciliation tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0193 OF 1120  |  SALES, CRM, ORDER MANAGEMENT, AND BILLING**

## ERP-SALES-053 — Payment terms and due-date policy

**Normative requirement:** The system shall calculate invoice due dates from configured payment terms, invoice date, calendar, and jurisdiction/entity policy, storing the rule used.

**Rationale:** Due dates depend on contract terms and local business calendars.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Net-days and configured month-end terms produce expected due dates across month and year boundaries.

**AC 2.** Changing a term definition does not recompute posted invoice due dates.

**Exception / edge case:** A contract-specific due date overrides default terms only when authorized and recorded.

**Security and audit implications:** Audit term changes and invoice-level overrides.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Show date in document locale and use the configured calendar/timezone for cutoffs.

**Verification method:** Calendar boundary and immutable posted-date tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0194 OF 1120  |  SALES, CRM, ORDER MANAGEMENT, AND BILLING**

## ERP-SALES-054 — Customer payment receipt reference

**Normative requirement:** The system shall capture customer payment references and remittance data as unapplied receipt candidates, with amount, currency, value date, and source channel.

**Rationale:** Payment receipt and invoice settlement belong to receivables but require sales billing context.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Receipt candidate preserves bank/provider reference and raw amount/currency.

**AC 2.** Unmatched receipt remains unapplied and does not close an invoice.

**Exception / edge case:** A payer may be unknown at receipt time and linked after review without losing original reference.

**Security and audit implications:** Mask bank/payment identifiers and restrict access to remittance files.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Parse locale-formatted remittance only at ingestion boundary and persist normalized amount.

**Verification method:** Import and unapplied-receipt tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0195 OF 1120  |  SALES, CRM, ORDER MANAGEMENT, AND BILLING**

## ERP-SALES-055 — Payment allocation integrity

**Normative requirement:** The system shall allocate receipts to eligible receivable documents through the finance module and reflect settlement status from that authoritative allocation.

**Rationale:** Billing must not maintain a competing cash application ledger.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Partial allocation leaves accurate residual open amount.

**AC 2.** Unallocation or reversal from finance updates displayed status with traceable event ID.

**Exception / edge case:** A receipt in a different currency follows configured FX settlement handling, not implicit face-value matching.

**Security and audit implications:** Only finance-authorized roles allocate cash; audit referenced event and status changes.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Display localized currency format while preserving transaction and settlement currencies.

**Verification method:** Finance contract tests for partial, full, reversed, and FX allocation.

**REQUIREMENT 0196 OF 1120  |  SALES, CRM, ORDER MANAGEMENT, AND BILLING**

## ERP-SALES-056 — Receivables reconciliation view

**Normative requirement:** The system shall provide an authorized view reconciling each posted sales invoice and adjustment to its finance document status and open balance as of a stated time.

**Rationale:** Collections teams need one explainable view without duplicating the ledger.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** View shows source document ID, finance reference, currency, open amount, and as-of timestamp.

**AC 2.** Missing or stale finance updates are marked unresolved rather than displayed as settled.

**Exception / edge case:** An offline finance service shows last-known status with a visible stale indicator.

**Security and audit implications:** Apply account-level access and log bulk exports.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Dates and amounts honor viewer locale; status codes map to translated labels.

**Verification method:** Reconciliation fixture tests and stale-event simulation.

**REQUIREMENT 0197 OF 1120  |  SALES, CRM, ORDER MANAGEMENT, AND BILLING**

## ERP-SALES-057 — Customer credit exposure control

**Normative requirement:** The system shall evaluate configurable credit exposure using finance-provided open receivables plus eligible open orders and apply threshold-based holds before order release.

**Rationale:** Credit limits should use authoritative open balances and visible order commitments.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Exposure calculation identifies included balance sources, currency conversion policy, and evaluation time.

**AC 2.** Order exceeding configured limit creates a credit hold and cannot release without authorized override.

**Exception / edge case:** A stale finance balance triggers configured fail-open or fail-closed policy and is visibly flagged.

**Security and audit implications:** Restrict credit-limit changes and overrides; audit evaluation inputs and decision.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Convert with configured rate policy; present exposure in account credit currency.

**Verification method:** Exposure calculation and stale-data policy tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0198 OF 1120  |  SALES, CRM, ORDER MANAGEMENT, AND BILLING**

## ERP-SALES-058 — Configurable collection reminders

**Normative requirement:** The system shall schedule configurable invoice reminders from finance-provided due and open status, with suppression rules and delivery history.

**Rationale:** Collection cadence and permissible communications vary by contract and jurisdiction.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** No reminder is generated for settled, disputed, or explicitly suppressed documents.

**AC 2.** Each reminder records template version, recipient, channel, and event time.

**Exception / edge case:** A partial payment updates the reminder amount from current authoritative balance before dispatch.

**Security and audit implications:** Restrict templates and export recipient data; audit manual suppression removal.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Use customer communication locale and local time windows.

**Verification method:** Scheduler simulation with settled, disputed, partial, and timezone cases.

**REQUIREMENT 0199 OF 1120  |  SALES, CRM, ORDER MANAGEMENT, AND BILLING**

## ERP-SALES-059 — Dispute and promise-to-pay tracking

**Normative requirement:** The system shall record invoice disputes and promise-to-pay commitments linked to receivable references, including owner, reason, due date, and outcome.

**Rationale:** Collections actions should explain why balances are delayed and support follow-up.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Dispute status can suppress configured reminders without changing posted invoice amount.

**AC 2.** Promise due date expiration creates an overdue follow-up task.

**Exception / edge case:** A partial dispute may apply to selected invoice lines while the remainder remains collectible.

**Security and audit implications:** Limit sensitive dispute attachments and audit status and amount-scope changes.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Reason codes translate; original customer statement remains in its authored language.

**Verification method:** Dispute/reminder and promise-due workflow tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0200 OF 1120  |  SALES, CRM, ORDER MANAGEMENT, AND BILLING**

## ERP-SALES-060 — Tax exemption evidence

**Normative requirement:** The system shall store customer tax-exemption classification, jurisdiction, valid interval, evidence reference, and verification status when enabled by tenant rules.

**Rationale:** Exemption eligibility and proof are jurisdiction-specific and may expire.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Expired or unverified evidence is excluded from tax request unless configured review exception is approved.

**AC 2.** Invoice retains exemption reference and decision status used at posting.

**Exception / edge case:** One certificate may cover only selected products or locations, which must be represented as scoped applicability.

**Security and audit implications:** Protect certificate documents and audit classification, scope, and verification changes.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Evidence metadata supports local identifiers and language; do not translate legal document content automatically.

**Verification method:** Validity, scope, and invoice-tax integration tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0201 OF 1120  |  SALES, CRM, ORDER MANAGEMENT, AND BILLING**

## ERP-SALES-061 — Return authorization workflow

**Normative requirement:** The system shall create return authorizations linked to original order lines with requested quantity, reason, condition, disposition, and approval status.

**Rationale:** Returns need traceable authorization distinct from refund and inventory receipt.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Authorized return quantity cannot exceed eligible sold quantity less prior returns unless override approved.

**AC 2.** Received quantity is recorded separately from authorized quantity.

**Exception / edge case:** Warranty replacement without physical return follows a configured no-return disposition.

**Security and audit implications:** Restrict return approval and preserve evidence for damaged or regulated items.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Reason labels and customer instructions localize; item IDs and reason codes remain stable.

**Verification method:** Return quantity and disposition integration tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0202 OF 1120  |  SALES, CRM, ORDER MANAGEMENT, AND BILLING**

## ERP-SALES-062 — Refund and credit separation

**Normative requirement:** The system shall distinguish commercial credit issuance from cash refund instruction and obtain refund status from the finance/payment provider contract.

**Rationale:** A credit note does not prove money was returned.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Posting a credit alone does not mark refund completed.

**AC 2.** Refund command links to approved credit/receipt and repeated request is idempotent.

**Exception / edge case:** Customer may choose credit-on-account instead of cash refund, with explicit disposition.

**Security and audit implications:** Require refund authority and record external payment reference without storing prohibited payment credentials.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Refund advice uses customer language and localized amounts; provider status remains canonical.

**Verification method:** Credit-only, refund, retry, and provider rejection tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0203 OF 1120  |  SALES, CRM, ORDER MANAGEMENT, AND BILLING**

## ERP-SALES-063 — Customer rebate accrual claim

**Normative requirement:** The system shall model configurable customer rebate agreements with eligibility basis, accrual period, claim evidence, and settlement reference.

**Rationale:** Volume incentives may depend on industry-specific rules and should be auditable separately from line discounts.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Rebate calculation identifies eligible transactions and agreement version.

**AC 2.** Claim settlement cannot exceed approved accrued amount absent documented adjustment.

**Exception / edge case:** Retroactive agreement changes require recalculation preview and approval before posting adjustment.

**Security and audit implications:** Restrict agreement edits and settlement approval; record calculation provenance.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Agreement terms may be multilingual; amounts and units follow configured contract basis.

**Verification method:** Eligibility, retroactive-change, and settlement reconciliation tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0204 OF 1120  |  SALES, CRM, ORDER MANAGEMENT, AND BILLING**

## ERP-SALES-064 — Sales commission plan boundary

**Normative requirement:** The system shall expose eligible sales events and attribution data to a configurable commission component without hard-coding universal compensation law or payroll rules.

**Rationale:** Commission plans, clawbacks, and labor rules vary widely by organization and jurisdiction.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Commission input identifies credited owner, source transaction, event date, and reversal linkage.

**AC 2.** Changing ownership after an eligible event does not silently rewrite finalized commission attribution.

**Exception / edge case:** A transaction reversal emits a linked reversal event subject to the commission plan's configured treatment.

**Security and audit implications:** Restrict compensation data and audit attribution overrides.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Support local currency and plan-language labels; payroll output is owned by payroll integration.

**Verification method:** Commission event contract and reversal tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0205 OF 1120  |  SALES, CRM, ORDER MANAGEMENT, AND BILLING**

## ERP-SALES-065 — Sales performance analytics

**Normative requirement:** The system shall provide role-filtered CRM, order, and billing metrics with documented definitions, source timestamps, and drill-through identifiers.

**Rationale:** Operational metrics are useful only when definitions and source freshness are transparent.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Report totals reconcile to included source records under the documented filter and status rules.

**AC 2.** Unauthorized drill-through returns no protected row details while aggregate policy is explicit.

**Exception / edge case:** Late-arriving events restate a metric only under visible refresh/version semantics.

**Security and audit implications:** Apply row-level filters to exports and log sensitive bulk queries.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Translate labels and format numeric outputs by locale without changing grouping keys.

**Verification method:** Golden dataset reconciliation and role-scoped export tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0206 OF 1120  |  SALES, CRM, ORDER MANAGEMENT, AND BILLING**

## ERP-SALES-066 — Bulk import validation and replay

**Normative requirement:** The system shall validate bulk customer, lead, quote, and order imports before commit and report row-level outcomes with stable external IDs.

**Rationale:** Enterprise migration and integrations require controlled, repeatable loading.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Preview identifies valid, invalid, and duplicate rows without writing business records.

**AC 2.** Replay of a committed file with same external IDs does not create duplicates.

**Exception / edge case:** Partial commit is allowed only when selected import mode explicitly permits valid-row application.

**Security and audit implications:** Authorize import scopes, scan attachments, and audit uploader, file hash, and results.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Importer accepts declared encoding and locale-specific source formats but normalizes data before persistence.

**Verification method:** Import fixtures for replay, partial failure, encoding, and validation.

**REQUIREMENT 0207 OF 1120  |  SALES, CRM, ORDER MANAGEMENT, AND BILLING**

## ERP-SALES-067 — Versioned sales integration events

**Normative requirement:** The system shall publish versioned sales lifecycle events with tenant/entity scope, immutable business ID, event ID, occurred time, and schema version.

**Rationale:** Decoupled modules need reliable change propagation without sharing database tables.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Consumers can deduplicate repeated event ID and reject unsupported schema version safely.

**AC 2.** Events distinguish business occurrence time from publication time.

**Exception / edge case:** Out-of-order event delivery is reconciled using aggregate version and does not regress state.

**Security and audit implications:** Authenticate publishers, minimize payload PII, and retain correlation IDs for audit.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Events carry locale only when required for rendered content; codes and numeric data are locale-neutral.

**Verification method:** Schema compatibility, duplicate, and out-of-order consumer tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0208 OF 1120  |  SALES, CRM, ORDER MANAGEMENT, AND BILLING**

## ERP-SALES-068 — Sales role and field permissions

**Normative requirement:** The system shall enforce least-privilege permissions by tenant, legal entity, record scope, action, and sensitive field for CRM and commercial documents.

**Rationale:** Sales access spans personal data, pricing, credit, and financial documents with different confidentiality.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Unauthorized API attempts to view, edit, export, approve, or post protected records are denied.

**AC 2.** Role changes take effect on subsequent requests and are represented in audit history.

**Exception / edge case:** Emergency access is time-bound, approved, and reviewed after use.

**Security and audit implications:** Use server-side authorization, deny-by-default policy, and tamper-resistant access/change logs.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Permission names can be translated in UI but canonical action IDs are stable.

**Verification method:** Authorization matrix tests and privileged-access review.

**REQUIREMENT 0209 OF 1120  |  SALES, CRM, ORDER MANAGEMENT, AND BILLING**

## ERP-SALES-069 — Sales audit trail and retention

**Normative requirement:** The system shall retain attributable before/after audit events for material customer, opportunity, quote, order, invoice, approval, and configuration changes under tenant retention policy.

**Rationale:** Commercial disputes and accounting review require reconstructable history.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Audit event includes actor/service, timestamp, entity ID, action, changed field names, and correlation ID.

**AC 2.** Ordinary business users cannot alter or erase retained events.

**Exception / edge case:** Privacy erasure or statutory retention conflicts route through configured legal review and controlled anonymization, not ad hoc deletion.
