**Security and audit implications:** Protect audit storage, restrict query/export, and monitor tampering or privileged reads.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Audit timestamps are stored in an unambiguous canonical form and displayed in viewer locale.

**Verification method:** Mutation history tests, access-control tests, and retention-policy simulation.

**REQUIREMENT 0210 OF 1120  |  SALES, CRM, ORDER MANAGEMENT, AND BILLING**

## ERP-SALES-070 — Multilingual accessible sales interface

**Normative requirement:** The system shall provide locale-selectable sales UI and documents, language/direction metadata for content, and accessible keyboard-operable controls aligned to the selected WCAG conformance target.

**Rationale:** Multilingual enterprise users require understandable content and usable workflows across scripts and assistive technologies.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Changing locale updates translated chrome and formatting without changing stored monetary values or status codes.

**AC 2.** Automated accessibility checks and manual keyboard/screen-reader review cover lead, quote, order, and invoice critical paths.

**Exception / edge case:** A missing translation falls back to configured tenant language and marks the untranslated field for administrators.

**Security and audit implications:** Escape user-provided localized content, isolate bidirectional text, and retain authorization behavior across locales.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Support language tags, RTL layout, Unicode input, locale-aware dates/numbers, and document-language metadata; locale does not determine tax or legal policy.

**Verification method:** Locale/RTL test matrix plus WCAG-targeted automated and manual accessibility evaluation.

# Inventory, Warehouse, and Logistics

# Chapter 04 — Inventory, Warehouse, and Logistics

## 1. Scope and domain boundary

This chapter specifies stock identity and balances, reservations, receipts, warehouse execution, traceability, quality controls, shipment planning, transport visibility, inventory valuation handoffs, and inventory reporting for a multi-tenant commercial ERP serving mid-market and enterprise organizations. Industry extensions are configurable and versioned. The chapter does not make this module the system of record for purchasing commitments, customer orders, production routings, quality laboratory systems, tax/customs determinations, carrier contracts, financial ledgers, or statutory records. Those remain owned by Procurement, Sales, Manufacturing, Quality, Finance, jurisdictional adapters, or external providers under explicit contracts.

No rule about ownership, negative stock, lot/serial capture, expiry, inspections, costing, customs, trade restrictions, carrier documentation, or retention is universal. Tenant and legal-entity configuration selects the policy and its effective period; industry/jurisdiction extensions identify applicability, authoritative source/version, and local owner. The core must hold unresolved mandatory data rather than infer law from a user’s language, IP location, or destination alone. Traceability interoperability can map to GS1 EPCIS when selected; EPCIS is a visibility-event standard, not a replacement for each tenant’s inventory ledger. GS1 identifies distinct trade items, locations, and logistics units using different keys such as GTIN, GLN, and SSCC. \[6] \[7]

## 2. Platform and architecture baseline

**Backend.** Use ASP.NET Core on .NET 11 as the verified latest stable supported major release as of 2026-11-22. Microsoft’s official policy last updated November 10, 2026 lists .NET 11 GA on November 10, 2026 as active STS, with support through November 14, 2028; the latest patch shown on that policy page is 11.0.0 as of its update. Do not treat that patch as a future deployment pin: reconfirm the servicing patch, supported operating systems, and support lifecycle at build/deploy time. \[1] ASP.NET Core provides the backend API surface; inventory APIs should return machine-stable error codes and explicit authentication/authorization outcomes. \[9]

**Database.** Use PostgreSQL with tenant-aware relational constraints and transactional posting. The official versioning page currently lists PostgreSQL 19.0 as supported, released November 19, 2026, and recommends staying current on the current minor release. Use PostgreSQL 19 as the verified major baseline for the requested reference date, but reconfirm upstream support, host availability, extensions, and migration compatibility before rollout. \[2] Apply foreign keys, uniqueness, and checks to stable row-level invariants. \[10] Use transaction isolation/locking suitable for allocation and movement concurrency; PostgreSQL documents that Read Committed can expose serialization anomalies for complex concurrent operations, so allocation needs explicit invariant protection, bounded retries, and conflict handling. \[11]

Enable row-level security (RLS) where appropriate as defense in depth, but retain application authorization. PostgreSQL documents default-deny when RLS is enabled without a matching policy and notes that table owners normally bypass policies; superusers and BYPASSRLS roles always bypass them. Restrict runtime roles, consider FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY, and test the real connection role. \[3]

**Frontend.** Use a lightweight Next.js App Router frontend for warehouse web and responsive handheld workflows, with authenticated calls to ASP.NET Core APIs. Next.js documents locale routing and dictionary-based translation as options, not as the sole localization architecture. Define and re-confirm the Next.js release baseline at implementation; the cited guide is versioned documentation and does not itself establish which stable release is latest on 2026-11-22. \[4] Target an explicit accessibility conformance level selected by the product owner; WCAG 2.2 defines testable success criteria and levels. \[5]

**Data and integration principles.** Keep internal IDs, codes, unit values, event times, quantities, and money independent of display locale. Store exact source identifiers and original external status values alongside normalized mappings. Use versioned APIs/events, idempotent commands, a transactional outbox, and reconciliation queues. Never permit module-to-module table writes. Cross-module quantity or cost changes occur only through an owned command/event contract.

## 3. Actors and permission boundaries

Typical actors include item/catalog administrators; inventory controllers; warehouse managers; receiving clerks; putaway/replenishment operators; pickers and packers; cycle counters; count approvers; quality inspectors and disposition approvers; shipping planners; dock operators; carrier/integration identities; finance controllers; procurement and sales service identities; tenant and legal-entity administrators; support operators; and auditors.

Permissions are independently assignable by tenant, legal entity, warehouse, location, item class, owner, action, and sensitive field. Receiving, posting, reservation, picking, adjustment, count approval, quality release, dispatch, costing setup, trade-profile configuration, integration management, and export are distinct permissions. Where policy requires maker-checker, the initiator cannot approve their own high-impact adjustment or release. A shared physical site does not imply shared legal ownership or cross-tenant access. Emergency support access is separate, time-bounded, reason-coded, and reviewed. NIST SP 800-53 is a customizable security and privacy control catalog; each organization must select controls appropriate to its risk and obligations. \[8]

## 4. Core entities and invariants

The principal entities are tenant; legal entity; item and variant; item control profile; unit and conversion; package definition; warehouse, zone, location, capacity rule, and calendar; owner/custodian; lot, serial, expiry record, and handling unit; inventory ledger entry and balance projection; reservation; receipt and receipt line; appointment and ASN; putaway/pick/replenishment/count task; inspection plan, inspection, evidence, and disposition; transformation/genealogy event; shipment, load, carrier tender, tracking event, transport unit, label, and proof; valuation layer/event; policy profile; integration mapping; and audit/outbox event.

The stock key is explicitly dimensioned by tenant, item, location, status, owner, lot/serial/handling-unit as applicable, and legal entity. Operational on-hand is distinct from reserved quantity, available-to-promise, in-transit stock, and financial valuation. Posted quantity changes are immutable ledger events. Balances are projections that can be reconstructed and reconciled. Reservations do not change physical on-hand. Transfers preserve total quantity unless a separately recorded conversion, loss, or adjustment explains the difference. Quality-held, expired, blocked, and otherwise ineligible quantities cannot become available through UI-only logic. Posted corrections use linked reversals or governed adjustments. PostgreSQL constraints and transactions enforce durable integrity at database boundaries. \[10] \[11]

## 5. Workflows

**Inbound-to-stock:** import an expected receipt or create an appointment; resolve ASN and identifiers; scan/count delivered quantities; record variance, evidence, and provenance; route sensitive or discrepant material to quarantine; inspect under the configured profile; post receipt; suggest and confirm putaway; and expose only eligible quantity to reservations. Partial receipts and unresolved discrepancies remain explicit.

**Demand-to-warehouse:** Sales or Manufacturing publishes an authorized demand/reservation request. Inventory evaluates eligible stock under allocation policy, emits allocation outcome, and generates release-approved warehouse tasks. Operators scan source location and item/lot/serial, pick partial or complete quantities, record short-pick exceptions, pack into handling units, stage, load, and confirm dispatch. Shipment creation, tender, dispatch, and carrier delivery are separate events.

**Count-to-correction:** create a cutoff-defined blind count; record one or more physical observations; reconcile against the specified book snapshot; route variance by threshold; approve or reject/recount; and post linked adjustment only after authorization. Counts do not directly rewrite a balance.

**Quality and traceability:** run versioned inspections; apply authorized disposition; maintain lot/serial and packaging genealogy through transformations and shipment; support forward/backward trace queries; and map selected business events to an EPCIS or other partner contract. Unknown identifiers, missing links, and unmapped codes are surfaced as incomplete or quarantined—not guessed. \[6]

**Outbound logistics:** consolidate only compatible demand; select a configured carrier/service adapter or manual path; generate labels and manifests; confirm actual handover; ingest carrier status events idempotently; and reconcile partial, refused, lost, or returned freight. Physical return receipt does not automatically issue a customer credit or finance posting.

**Valuation handoff:** the configured finance policy determines cost treatment and approved landed-cost allocations. Inventory publishes the versioned valuation event and mapping inputs to Finance; Finance remains owner of GL posting and period controls. Reconciliation reports disclose effective time, posting time, currency, scope, and exceptions.

## 6. Major design decisions

**1. Immutable events plus projections.** Ledger, genealogy, count observations, status transitions, and carrier events are append-only. Balance views are derived and rebuildable. This supports replay and audit without treating an event history as an excuse to retain unnecessary personal data.

**2. Eligibility is policy-driven.** “Available” is calculated from physical status, reservations, ownership, expiry, location rules, and tenant policy. Hardcoded industry assumptions are disallowed.

**3. Lot and serial are control profiles.** Item master configuration defines where each identifier is mandatory. Profile changes require migration when historical/open stock would become inconsistent.

**4. Location is not ownership.** Warehouse and bin identify custody; owner and legal entity determine separate attribution. Shared operators cannot merge balances across owners or tenants.

**5. API/event contracts separate modules.** Procurement supplies expected receipt and supplier evidence; Sales/Manufacturing supply demand; Quality supplies inspection dispositions; Finance receives valuation events; Shipping/carrier providers exchange transport events. Inventory never writes another module’s tables.

**6. Localization is presentation plus input policy.** UI language, user timezone, warehouse timezone, output-document language, unit rendering, and numeric/date parsing are separate settings. Stable identifiers, raw partner values, and canonical API numbers remain locale-neutral. Accessibility criteria are tested at the chosen WCAG 2.2 level. \[4] \[5]

**7. Versioned extensions own legal variation.** Jurisdiction and industry packages declare their scope and source/version. A missing or ambiguous determination blocks the dependent action and routes an exception instead of defaulting to a global rule.

## 7. Cross-module contracts and dependencies

- **Procurement → Inventory:** purchase/transfer order, supplier, expected receipt, ASN, price/currency, lot/source data, and receipt tolerance. Procurement remains authoritative for the commitment; Inventory owns counted physical receipt and stock posting.
- **Sales/Manufacturing → Inventory:** demand, reservation request, priority, customer-specific constraints, and cancellation/amendment. Inventory responds with reserved/short/backorder outcome and immutable fulfillment events.
- **Quality → Inventory:** inspection plan version, measurements, disposition, release limits, and evidence references. Quality authority is separated from receipt/pick roles where configured.
- **Inventory → Finance:** valuation movement, legal entity, valuation policy version, cost basis, effective/posting times, currency, account-class mapping, and reconciliation identifier. Finance confirms posting or returns a controlled error.
- **Inventory ↔ Logistics providers:** authenticated tender, label, shipment identifiers, tracking events, delivery proof, and carrier errors. Provider-specific data is stored alongside normalized events.
- **Identity/tenant platform:** tenant/entity/warehouse context, user roles, device identity, locale/timezone preference, and authorization decisions. No untrusted request field can select another tenant.
- **Document/storage service:** versioned label/doc templates and protected evidence attachments with digest, retention, and access policy.

All mutating cross-module commands need idempotency keys. A committed state change and its outbound event are durable together; delivery may be at-least-once, so consumers deduplicate stable event IDs. API payloads carry schema version and correlation ID. Unknown versions/codes are quarantined and observable.

## 8. Risks and mitigations

Concurrency defects can over-allocate or lose stock; require database-backed race tests, real transaction semantics, and operational conflict queues. Incorrect master-data conversion, barcode parsing, or date-zone handling can produce silent quantity/expiry errors; use canonical units, preserved source values, explicit policy versions, and boundary tests. Partial trace links weaken recall coverage; expose graph gaps and report trace completeness. Broad warehouse access can cause fraud or cross-tenant leakage; separate roles and scopes, protect exports, test RLS under the production runtime role, and audit exceptional access. Carrier/API outages can strand events; use durable outbox/inbox, retry-safe event identity, and visible dead-letter queues. Over-customizing legal or industry logic in the core can misstate obligations; place policy in versioned extensions and require a named business/compliance owner. Locale-sensitive input can corrupt quantities; declare accepted formats, reject ambiguity, and test non-Latin and RTL layouts. PostgreSQL and .NET patch/servicing states change; re-confirm supported patches and hosting compatibility at release gates. \[1] \[2] \[3]

## 9. Requirements

The following 70 requirements are normative. Acceptance criteria are executable outcomes. Exceptions identify controlled boundary behavior rather than implied universal rules.

### A. Inventory foundation and master data

### ERP-INVENTORY-001 — Product inventory identity

**Shall:** The system shall identify each stock-managed item by a tenant-scoped immutable item ID, a unique tenant item code, and an explicit inventory-control profile.

**Rationale:** Stable identity prevents translated descriptions or supplier aliases from changing stock keys and supports variant-specific handling.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Creating a duplicate item code within one tenant is rejected; the same code in another tenant is accepted.
- An item ID and posted movement references remain unchanged when the item code or description is edited.
- The profile exposes independent lot, serial, expiry, catch-weight, and inspection flags.

**Exception / edge case:** A retired code cannot be reused while historical movements reference it; a tenant may explicitly map a legacy alias instead.

**Security and audit:** Item-code changes, profile edits, and alias maintenance require permission and record before/after values, actor, and timestamp.

**Localization:** Item codes remain locale-neutral; descriptions support separately versioned translations and fallback to the tenant default.

**Verification:** API/schema tests for tenant-scoped uniqueness and immutable foreign keys; UI tests for translated descriptions.

### ERP-INVENTORY-002 — Item variants and dimensions

**Shall:** The system shall model stock-distinct variants as separate item identities linked to a parent product and stable variant attributes.

**Rationale:** A sellable/stockable size, grade, color, formulation, or configuration must not share a balance with another variant.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Two variants under one parent produce separate on-hand and reservation rows.
- Variant attribute codes are stable while labels can be translated.
- An order or receipt referencing a parent without a required variant is rejected.

**Exception / edge case:** A parent product may be non-stocked and informational; it cannot receive quantity unless configured as a stock item.

**Security and audit:** Only authorized catalog roles may create variants or retire them; all edits are audited with affected item IDs.

**Localization:** Variant display labels and attribute values are localized; machine attributes/codes remain invariant.

**Verification:** Integration test creates two variants, posts movements, and asserts independent balances.

### ERP-INVENTORY-003 — Unit-of-measure conversions

**Shall:** The system shall store a base inventory unit per item and apply only explicitly configured, dimensionally compatible, effective-dated conversions to transaction units.

**Rationale:** Unambiguous conversion preserves quantities and prevents locale-sensitive or implicit arithmetic.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Conversion requires numerator, denominator, source unit, target unit, and effective interval.
- A conversion outside its effective interval or across incompatible dimensions is rejected.
- The posted transaction stores the entered quantity, transaction unit, converted base quantity, and conversion version.

**Exception / edge case:** Variable-weight goods require an actual measured quantity per transaction; a fixed conversion is not silently used as actual weight.

**Security and audit:** Changes to conversions cannot rewrite posted quantities; configuration changes are approved and audited.

**Localization:** Unit symbols and decimal input are locale-aware at the UI; persisted quantities and unit codes are locale-neutral.

**Verification:** Property tests for round-trip conversions, interval boundaries, and non-integral precision.

### ERP-INVENTORY-004 — Packaging and handling hierarchy

**Shall:** The system shall allow item-specific packaging definitions that relate base units to pack, case, pallet, or other handling levels without conflating packaging identity with item identity.

**Rationale:** Warehouse and shipping operations need pack quantities and dimensions while maintaining inventory in a canonical base unit.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Configured package levels have positive integral or explicitly fractional quantities and an effective period.
- Pack conversion is applied to quantities only when the selected package version is valid.
- A scan of a recognized package code resolves to the item and package level.

**Exception / edge case:** A returnable handling asset may be tracked separately from disposable packaging and need not be included in stock quantity.

**Security and audit:** Package definition edits are restricted, versioned, and logged; scans cannot authorize an inventory adjustment by themselves.

**Localization:** Package names are translatable; package codes, dimensions, and quantities remain canonical.

**Verification:** API tests for package version selection and scanner-to-item resolution.

### ERP-INVENTORY-005 — Warehouse and bin hierarchy

**Shall:** The system shall model tenant-owned warehouses and nested operational locations with unique stable IDs, typed location roles, and an active/inactive state.

**Rationale:** Explicit sublocations support directed putaway, picking, staging, quarantine, and reconciliation.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- A bin code is unique within its warehouse and location path.
- A movement source and destination must belong to authorized active locations.
- An inactive location cannot accept a new movement except through a configured exception workflow.

**Exception / edge case:** A location may be logically virtual, such as in-transit or supplier-owned stock, and must be typed distinctly from a physical bin.

**Security and audit:** Warehouse scope is checked server-side; changes to hierarchy and location status are audited.

**Localization:** Location names and instructions are localized while scannable codes remain locale-neutral.

**Verification:** Database constraint tests plus API authorization tests for cross-warehouse movement.

### ERP-INVENTORY-006 — Location capacity and compatibility

**Shall:** The system shall support configurable location capacity and item compatibility rules evaluated during putaway, replenishment, and directed transfer.

**Rationale:** Capacity and compatibility checks reduce overfill and unsafe storage without assuming universal industry rules.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Capacity checks compare configured unit, volume, weight, or handling-unit occupancy to the projected load.
- A disallowed item-location combination is blocked with the violated rule identified.
- Authorized override records reason and approving identity.

**Exception / edge case:** Missing dimensions do not imply unlimited capacity when the location policy requires dimensional data; the task is held for resolution.

**Security and audit:** Sensitive compatibility rules are editable only by configured safety/warehouse administrators and overrides are fully audited.

**Localization:** Unit labels are localized; calculations use canonical units and tenant-defined unit conversions.

**Verification:** Boundary tests for capacity exactly met/exceeded and incompatible item classes.

### ERP-INVENTORY-007 — Inventory ownership and custody

**Shall:** The system shall represent legal/economic owner separately from physical custodian and shall attribute quantity balances and movements to both where configured.

**Rationale:** Consigned, customer-owned, subcontractor, and third-party logistics stock must not be treated as enterprise-owned by default.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Balance queries distinguish owner, custodian, tenant, site, and item.
- A custody transfer without an ownership change does not alter owner attribution.
- A configured owner-required item cannot post a movement with owner omitted.

**Exception / edge case:** Legacy or unidentified stock can be held in an explicitly designated suspense ownership bucket and excluded from available-to-promise.

**Security and audit:** Ownership changes require workflow authorization; cross-tenant owner data is never exposed merely because physical custody is shared.

**Localization:** Owner display names are localized only for presentation; owner IDs and legal entity associations remain stable.

**Verification:** Scenario tests for consignment receipts, custody transfers, and tenant isolation.

### ERP-INVENTORY-008 — Inventory status dimensions

**Shall:** The system shall track physical quantity separately from usability status, including configurable statuses such as available, reserved, quality hold, damaged, blocked, and in-transit.

**Rationale:** One scalar on-hand value cannot accurately express sellable, restricted, or moving stock.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Every quantity bucket has exactly one configured status and location/ownership dimensions.
- Available-to-promise excludes statuses configured as unavailable and includes only eligible reservations.
- Status transitions are event-recorded rather than silently overwritten.

**Exception / edge case:** An unrecognized status code arriving from an integration is quarantined from availability until mapped.

**Security and audit:** Status configuration is permissioned; blocked/held inventory cannot be released by a user lacking release authority.

**Localization:** Status labels and reason codes are translatable; stable codes drive logic and exports.

**Verification:** Balance projection tests across status transitions and unmapped codes.

### ERP-INVENTORY-009 — Legal entity stock attribution

**Shall:** The system shall attribute inventory transactions to a configured owning legal entity and operating entity, independently of tenant and warehouse, when multi-entity operation is enabled.

**Rationale:** The data model needs entity-level stock and accounting handoffs without embedding any jurisdiction’s statutory rules.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Each posted movement records tenant and owning entity; configured operations also record executing entity.
- A transfer between entities requires an explicit inter-entity movement pair or configured transfer contract.
- Entity access filters prevent unauthorized read and adjustment.

**Exception / edge case:** A warehouse shared by entities can contain separate entity-attributed balances; a single physical scan does not merge ownership.

**Security and audit:** Entity-level segregation and role checks apply to APIs, reports, and exports and are included in audit events.

**Localization:** Entity legal names and addresses are localized in outputs by document-language policy; entity IDs remain stable.

**Verification:** Multi-entity integration and negative authorization tests.

### ERP-INVENTORY-010 — Warehouse calendars and local time

**Shall:** The system shall associate each warehouse with a time zone and configurable operating calendar and shall store event instants in UTC with the applicable local zone retained for interpretation.

**Rationale:** Appointment windows, shift cutoffs, and elapsed-time reporting need unambiguous instant and local business context.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- An event instant serializes in UTC and renders in the warehouse’s configured zone.
- A nonexistent or ambiguous daylight-saving local time is rejected or requires explicit disambiguation.
- Calendar closures affect appointment/task scheduling but do not rewrite posted timestamps.

**Exception / edge case:** A carrier event lacking a reliable time zone is stored with source time and an explicit unknown/assumed-zone flag, never silently treated as UTC.

**Security and audit:** Time-zone and calendar changes are audited; event source and original timestamp are retained.

**Localization:** Date/time formats follow user locale while warehouse zone governs operational cutoffs.

**Verification:** Tests around daylight-saving transitions, locale rendering, and event round trips.

### B. Balances, reservations, and valuation

### ERP-INVENTORY-011 — Append-only quantity ledger

**Shall:** The system shall record every posted quantity change as an immutable, tenant-scoped inventory ledger entry and derive balances from those entries or a reconciled projection.

**Rationale:** The ledger provides a reconstructible stock history and prevents mutable balance-only state from erasing movement evidence.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Each ledger entry has unique ID, item, quantity, unit, location, status, owner, timestamp, source reference, and posting actor/system.
- A balance at a tested cutoff equals the sum of eligible ledger entries through that cutoff.
- A projection rebuild reproduces balances without modifying original ledger records.

**Exception / edge case:** Voided business activity is represented by a linked reversal entry, not deletion or editing of the original ledger row.

**Security and audit:** Ledger reads and exports are scoped; privileged corrections preserve actor, reason, source, and correlation ID.

**Localization:** Descriptions and reason text may be localized; ledger keys, units, timestamps, and numeric quantities are canonical.

**Verification:** Property-based ledger reconstruction test and immutability integration test.

### ERP-INVENTORY-012 — Reservation allocation

**Shall:** The system shall represent reservations as separately identifiable claims against eligible stock and shall expose reserved, unreserved, and available-to-promise quantities by the configured allocation dimensions.

**Rationale:** Reservations must be auditable and distinct from physical stock movement.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Creating a reservation reduces eligible available-to-promise without changing physical on-hand.
- Reservation quantity cannot exceed eligibility unless an authorized policy explicitly permits backorder.
- Release, consume, and reallocate operations reference the original reservation and preserve history.

**Exception / edge case:** A partial fulfillment consumes only the fulfilled portion and leaves the remainder active or explicitly backordered.

**Security and audit:** Only authorized order/fulfillment services can create or consume reservations; owner/entity and tenant scope are enforced.

**Localization:** User-facing allocation reasons/status labels are translated; quantities and dates follow locale preferences.

**Verification:** API tests assert on-hand invariant and reservation lifecycle across partial shipment.

### ERP-INVENTORY-013 — Concurrent allocation safety

**Shall:** The system shall serialize or otherwise protect concurrent allocations against a shared stock balance so that committed allocations cannot exceed policy-eligible quantity.

**Rationale:** Concurrency controls prevent over-allocation under simultaneous order, pick, or replenishment activity.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- With eligible quantity Q and concurrent requests totaling more than Q, the committed total does not exceed Q unless backorder policy allows it.
- A losing request receives a deterministic conflict/shortage result and no partial orphan reservation.
- Retrying a transient serialization conflict re-evaluates eligibility before commit.

**Exception / edge case:** If a request spans multiple items and one item fails, the system follows a documented all-or-partial allocation policy and reports the exact outcome.

**Security and audit:** Concurrency retry logs include correlation ID but exclude secrets; authorization is rechecked on retry.

**Localization:** Locale does not affect comparison or numeric reservation invariants; conflict messages are localized.

**Verification:** Parallel load test against real PostgreSQL transaction semantics with deterministic assertions.

### ERP-INVENTORY-014 — Atomic inventory movement

**Shall:** The system shall post a transfer or transformation as a single atomic transaction that debits all source buckets and credits all destination buckets or commits none.

**Rationale:** Atomicity prevents phantom loss or duplication across bins, owners, and status buckets.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- A successful transfer produces equal total debit and credit in the transaction unit or a documented conversion/variance entry.
- Injected failure after source write rolls back every related balance and ledger row.
- Each movement links source and destination lines under one movement ID.

**Exception / edge case:** For inter-warehouse transport, departure and arrival are separate committed events represented through an in-transit location, not one long database transaction.

**Security and audit:** Movement creation and posting are separately permissioned; audit includes each line and the initiating identity.

**Localization:** Canonical units and precision are used regardless of display locale; printed movement docs use selected language.

**Verification:** Fault-injection transaction tests and ledger conservation tests.

### ERP-INVENTORY-015 — Reversal and correction handling

**Shall:** The system shall correct a posted inventory transaction only through a linked compensating transaction or an explicitly governed adjustment that preserves the original transaction.

**Rationale:** Immutable correction histories support audit and reliable reconciliation.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Posted entries are not editable or deletable through public APIs or user interfaces.
- A reversal references its original entry and carries a reason and authorization.
- A full reversal cannot exceed the unreversed original quantity; partial reversals report the remaining reversible amount.

**Exception / edge case:** A correction after a period is closed can be dated by posting time and business-effective time separately under tenant policy.

**Security and audit:** Only correction roles may initiate; high-impact adjustments require a second approver when configured.

**Localization:** Localized reasons are stored with stable reason codes; timestamps retain UTC and display by user zone.

**Verification:** Negative tests for update/delete, reversal bounds, and approval enforcement.

### ERP-INVENTORY-016 — Cost layer and valuation records

**Shall:** The system shall preserve cost-bearing receipt and issue records with explicit currency, cost amount, valuation method version, and quantity basis, separate from operational availability.

**Rationale:** Valuation requires reproducible cost evidence and must not be inferred from localized display or current supplier price.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Each valued receipt captures source cost, currency, and cost-policy version.
- Issue valuation identifies the layer or method allocation used and can be recomputed from retained records.
- Operational quantity changes with no financial valuation effect are explicitly typed and not silently costed at zero.

**Exception / edge case:** Items configured as non-valued or statistical stock remain quantity tracked but are clearly excluded from financial inventory valuation.

**Security and audit:** Cost-detail access is segregated from warehouse roles where appropriate; valuation changes and overrides are audited.

**Localization:** Currency codes and rounding policies are explicit; presentation formatting follows locale without changing stored amounts.

**Verification:** Reconciliation test from cost layers to valuation projection and security role tests.

### ERP-INVENTORY-017 — Configurable costing policy

**Shall:** The system shall support tenant/legal-entity-level effective-dated valuation methods selected from approved implementation options and shall prevent silent method mixing within a valuation scope.

**Rationale:** Accounting policy varies by reporting entity and sector; the core product must expose a configurable boundary, not assert one method universally.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Each valuation scope has one active method and effective interval at a time.
- Posting under an expired/unconfigured method is blocked or sent to controlled exception handling.
- The method and input snapshot are persisted on each cost-affecting event.

**Exception / edge case:** Changing method with existing layers requires a governed conversion/revaluation procedure; a configuration toggle alone cannot rewrite history.

**Security and audit:** Only finance/configuration roles can set policy; approval and before/after values are retained.

**Localization:** Policy labels may be translated; method codes and calculation precision remain invariant.

**Verification:** Method configuration state-machine tests and sample-valued movement reconciliation.

### ERP-INVENTORY-018 — Landed-cost allocation interface

**Shall:** The system shall accept approved landed-cost allocations from procurement or finance against identified receipts or shipments and preserve allocation basis and source document references.

**Rationale:** Freight, duties, insurance, and handling may affect inventory value under entity policy; allocation ownership belongs to configured costing rules.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Allocation records identify cost type, currency, source document, receipt/handling units, basis, and allocated amount.
- Allocated totals reconcile to the approved cost pool subject to explicit rounding residual handling.
- A posted cost allocation creates a linked valuation event and does not alter physical quantity.

**Exception / edge case:** A cost pool arriving after the stock has been consumed is sent to the configured variance/adjustment path rather than applied to nonexistent on-hand stock.

**Security and audit:** Only approved upstream cost events are accepted; imported amounts and approvals are auditable.

**Localization:** Currency conversion source/date and amount precision are retained; rendered documents can be localized.

**Verification:** Contract tests with procurement/finance fixtures and rounding reconciliation cases.

### ERP-INVENTORY-019 — Inventory-to-finance reconciliation

**Shall:** The system shall publish versioned inventory valuation movements to the finance/ledger module and expose reconciliation totals by legal entity, account mapping, period, and currency.

**Rationale:** Inventory owns physical and valuation subledger events while the general ledger remains a separate financial system of record.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- A posted event has a unique finance handoff ID and deterministic debit/credit payload under configured mapping.
- Retrying delivery does not create duplicate finance postings.
- Period totals reconcile to the inventory valuation projection with recorded timing or mapping exceptions.

**Exception / edge case:** An unmapped valuation class is held from posting and surfaced as an actionable exception; it is never routed to a default account.

**Security and audit:** Financial handoff payloads are access-controlled, signed/authenticated per integration policy, and retained for audit.

**Localization:** Account descriptions may be localized; account IDs, currency, and amounts use canonical values.

**Verification:** End-to-end reconciliation test with duplicate delivery, mapping gap, and period close fixture.

### ERP-INVENTORY-020 — Negative stock policy

**Shall:** The system shall enforce a configured negative-stock policy per item, warehouse, or legal entity at the posting boundary and shall distinguish shortage from technical concurrency failure.

**Rationale:** Some industries permit controlled negative balances, while others require hard blocking; the choice is an explicit policy.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Under a blocking policy, a transaction that would reduce eligible quantity below zero is rejected atomically.
- Under a permitted-negative policy, the resulting deficit is visible by item/location/status and produces a policy-tagged event.
- Changing policy cannot retroactively erase deficits.

**Exception / edge case:** A delayed external receipt may be applied to a previously accepted deficit without changing the historical issue event.

**Security and audit:** Only designated administrators may set exceptions; every negative-quantity event and override is audited.

**Localization:** Error descriptions localized; arithmetic always uses canonical units and precise decimal representation.

**Verification:** Boundary and concurrent movement tests for block and configured exception paths.

### C. Inbound, receiving, and putaway

### ERP-INVENTORY-021 — Inbound appointment and expected receipt

**Shall:** The system shall register expected inbound deliveries with source order/ASN references, warehouse, time window, item quantities, handling requirements, and lifecycle status.

**Rationale:** A scheduled receipt provides operational context before goods physically enter stock.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- An expected delivery can be created from an authorized source or manual role and has a unique tenant reference.
- Appointment capacity checks prevent booking beyond configured dock limits unless approved override is used.
- Expected quantities do not increase on-hand or available stock.

**Exception / edge case:** A walk-in arrival without appointment is recorded as unscheduled and routed through the warehouse exception queue.

**Security and audit:** Supplier and appointment data are tenant-scoped; changes to slot or expected quantity are audited.

**Localization:** Appointment display uses site time zone and locale; supplier reference codes are not translated.

**Verification:** API/UI tests for scheduling capacity and zero-stock effect.

### ERP-INVENTORY-022 — ASN and receipt discrepancy

**Shall:** The system shall compare an advance shipping notice or expected receipt with counted physical receipt and capture discrepancies by item, unit, lot/serial where required, and reason.

**Rationale:** Explicit variance records enable supplier follow-up and accurate stock posting.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Receipt lines store expected, received, rejected, and accepted quantities separately.
- Variance requires a configured reason code and optional evidence attachment.
- A discrepancy cannot be hidden by overwriting expected quantity during receipt.

**Exception / edge case:** Unannounced line items are quarantined or accepted only under a configurable over-receipt policy and authorized reason.

**Security and audit:** Receipt variance thresholds and overrides are permissioned; supplier-facing exports exclude internal comments unless selected.

**Localization:** Variance reason labels are localized; the exact received quantities and supplier references are retained.

**Verification:** Test matching receipt, shortage, overage, and damaged scenarios; audit assertion.

### ERP-INVENTORY-023 — Scan-based receiving identification

**Shall:** The system shall resolve scanned item, handling-unit, lot, serial, and location identifiers against tenant-configured identifier rules before a receipt is posted.

**Rationale:** Scanning reduces key-entry errors and can interoperate with standard identifiers such as trade-item GTIN and logistic-unit SSCC without requiring them universally. \[7]

**Acceptance criteria:**

- A valid registered identifier resolves to exactly one permitted entity in the active tenant context.
- An unknown or ambiguous barcode cannot post quantity and is displayed as an exception.
- The receipt event preserves raw scan value, symbology/parser result, and resolved internal IDs.

**Exception / edge case:** A partner’s external identifier may be mapped by a scoped alias; conflicting aliases block resolution until reconciled.

**Security and audit:** Scan ingestion is treated as untrusted input; tenant scope and permission are enforced before lookup or mutation.

**Localization:** Scanner input may use locale-independent identifier syntax; localized help and error details are available.

**Verification:** Scanner/API contract tests with valid, malformed, unknown, and cross-tenant codes.

### ERP-INVENTORY-024 — Partial receipt posting

**Shall:** The system shall permit authorized receipt lines to be posted in partial quantities while retaining the remaining expected quantity and linking every posted portion to the same source delivery.

**Rationale:** Split deliveries and mixed acceptance decisions are normal operational cases.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Two partial posts plus any accepted remainder reconcile to the received total without duplicating stock.
- Each posted portion has its own immutable timestamp, operator, and inventory movement ID.
- Closing a receipt with a remainder requires an explicit cancel, backorder, or unresolved status.

**Exception / edge case:** A second scan of the same package cannot post duplicate quantity unless a user explicitly enters a separate package/receipt quantity.

**Security and audit:** Partial receipt changes and closures are auditable; warehouse users cannot change upstream order commitments.

**Localization:** Receipt summaries render in the operator’s locale but retain base and entered quantities.

**Verification:** Workflow tests for repeated partial post, remaining balance, and duplicate scan.

### ERP-INVENTORY-025 — Directed putaway suggestion

**Shall:** The system shall propose putaway destinations using configured capacity, compatibility, zone, and handling rules and require a committed destination before stock becomes pick-available.

**Rationale:** A received stock status should not imply correct storage or immediate pickability.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Suggestion returns only active eligible bins and includes rule-based reason/rank.
- Posting a putaway validates capacity and eligibility again at commit.
- Accepted putaway creates a movement from receiving/staging to the destination.

**Exception / edge case:** If no eligible bin exists, the receipt remains in a controlled staging/exception location and is not silently marked put away.

**Security and audit:** Manual destination override requires permission and a reason; suggestions cannot bypass incompatible-bin restrictions.

**Localization:** Location names are localized; stable codes and capacity values are not; zone schedules use warehouse time.

**Verification:** Rule-engine tests for ranked candidates, full bin race, and no-candidate behavior.

### ERP-INVENTORY-026 — Quarantine on receipt

**Shall:** The system shall route configured items or discrepant receipt quantities into a non-available quarantine status pending an explicit disposition.

**Rationale:** Quality review must be separate from physical receipt confirmation.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Quarantined quantity appears in on-hand but is excluded from available-to-promise and picking.
- Release requires an authorized quality disposition linked to the receipt/lot.
- A rejected quantity can be scrapped, returned, or held without being silently released.

**Exception / edge case:** Emergency conditional release is allowed only through a separately enabled, approved exception path with scope and expiry.

**Security and audit:** Quality-release permission is segregated from receiving confirmation; every disposition and evidence reference is auditable.

**Localization:** Disposition codes and operator instructions are localized; code values remain stable.

**Verification:** Authorization and availability tests for receive/hold/release/reject lifecycle.

### ERP-INVENTORY-027 — Customer and supplier return receipt

**Shall:** The system shall record returned material against a return authorization or controlled exception reference and keep received, inspected, restocked, repaired, and scrapped quantities distinct.

**Rationale:** Returned goods may not be saleable or owned until identified and inspected.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Return receipt references origin order/shipment or states an approved unmatched-return reason.
- Returned quantities enter a designated return/inspection status and location.
- Only an authorized disposition creates a transfer to sellable stock.

**Exception / edge case:** A mismatched serial, expired lot, or unknown original shipment remains unresolved and cannot inherit eligibility from another return line.

**Security and audit:** Return authorization and stock disposition permissions are separate; personal customer data is minimized in warehouse views.

**Localization:** Return instructions and disposition labels are localized; original identifiers remain verbatim.

**Verification:** Test authorized, unmatched, serial-mismatch, and restock workflows.

### ERP-INVENTORY-028 — Supplier lot and source provenance

**Shall:** The system shall capture source supplier, supplier lot reference, internal lot reference, receipt date, and linked order/receipt for lot-controlled inbound stock.

**Rationale:** Traceability must connect incoming goods to supplier provenance without assuming supplier lot formats are globally unique.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Supplier lot uniqueness is scoped by supplier and tenant policy, not assumed globally.
- Lot-controlled receipt cannot post without mandatory provenance fields.
- Internal and supplier lot references remain separately searchable.

**Exception / edge case:** A supplier reuses a lot code for distinct products; item and supplier context disambiguate it or the receipt is held.

**Security and audit:** Provenance access follows supplier and site permissions; edits after posting create a history event.

**Localization:** Supplier/item names are localized on screens; exact supplier-provided lot string is preserved as received.

**Verification:** Database/API tests for contextual lot uniqueness and immutable provenance history.

### ERP-INVENTORY-029 — Barcode and label validation

**Shall:** The system shall validate generated or received barcode payloads against the selected symbology, identifier scheme, and configured check-digit or application-identifier rules before issuing warehouse labels.

**Rationale:** Wrongly encoded labels can cause misidentification and downstream custody errors.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Each label template declares symbology, payload fields, and version.
- Known test vectors encode/decode to the same canonical identifier and quantity/date fields.
- Invalid check digit or unsupported field combination blocks print or capture with diagnostic.

**Exception / edge case:** A tenant-specific proprietary label format must be explicitly registered and versioned rather than silently parsed as a standard.

**Security and audit:** Label templates are change-controlled; print actions log template version, printer identity, and business source.

**Localization:** Human-readable label text is localized; encoded payloads follow the applicable identifier format and remain unchanged.

**Verification:** Golden-vector tests with barcode encoder/decoder and print-template inspection.

### ERP-INVENTORY-030 — Receipt evidence attachments

**Shall:** The system shall link receipt evidence such as packing slips, photographs, temperature readings, and exception notes to a specific receipt event with metadata and access controls.

**Rationale:** Evidence enables resolution of disputes and quality issues with correct provenance.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Evidence metadata includes receipt ID, uploader/source, timestamp, media type, and integrity digest.
- Deleting a receipt does not orphan evidence; retention follows configured tenant policy.
- Unsupported or oversized uploads are rejected before persistence.

**Exception / edge case:** If a device is offline, evidence is queued with capture time and upload time separately and marked unverified until synchronized.

**Security and audit:** Uploads are scanned/validated, access is least-privilege, downloads are audited, and evidence links are not public by default.

**Localization:** Evidence captions may be localized, while original image/measurement data and timestamps remain preserved.

**Verification:** Upload security tests, integrity check, and offline synchronization test.

### D. Warehouse execution

### ERP-INVENTORY-031 — Wave release and task generation

**Shall:** The system shall create warehouse work from approved demand through explicit release rules and generate uniquely identified pick tasks tied to order lines and allocation records.

**Rationale:** Separate release from order capture allows workload, stock, and customer commitments to be checked before execution.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- A released wave records criteria, source order set, warehouse, and release identity/time.
- Each pick task links item, quantity, source bin, destination/staging, and reservation.
- Repeated release of the same wave cannot create duplicate tasks without explicit replan version.

**Exception / edge case:** A released order with a stock or credit hold is excluded or surfaced as a blocked line according to configured policy.

**Security and audit:** Wave release authority is separate from order entry; release and replanning are audited.

**Localization:** Task instructions and customer-facing priorities are localized; item and bin codes remain machine-readable.

**Verification:** Workflow/API tests for hold filtering, duplicate release, and task linkage.

### ERP-INVENTORY-032 — Pick strategy and source selection

**Shall:** The system shall select eligible pick sources according to a configurable strategy such as location sequence, expiry priority, lot restriction, or handling-unit preference and expose the applied rule.

**Rationale:** Picking should be reproducible and should respect quality and traceability controls.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Candidate sources exclude blocked, quarantined, expired, or otherwise ineligible stock.
- Selection output records the rule version and the selected source bucket.
- A user override records selected alternative and reason.

**Exception / edge case:** If configured FEFO conflicts with a customer-locked lot or serial, the stricter applicable constraint controls and shortage is raised if unsatisfied.

**Security and audit:** Overrides require warehouse permission; the service reevaluates status and reservation at pick commit.

**Localization:** Sequence labels and reason prompts are localized; expiry comparisons use dates as configured by policy.

**Verification:** Decision-rule tests with competing lots, status blockers, and override authorization.

### ERP-INVENTORY-033 — Short pick and split pick

**Shall:** The system shall allow a pick task to complete as one or more partial picks and record short quantity with a controlled reason and disposition of the remaining task quantity.

**Rationale:** Real locations may contain less stock than their book quantity; the system must represent the variance and retain unfulfilled demand.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Picked quantity cannot exceed task remaining quantity without an explicit over-pick allowance.
- A short pick records actual picked, missing, and remaining quantities plus reason.
- Unpicked demand is retained, canceled, or reallocated only through a documented task transition.

**Exception / edge case:** A scan of a wrong item or lot cannot be accepted as a shortage completion; it is a mismatch exception.

**Security and audit:** A picker may record but not approve a material inventory adjustment unless separately authorized.

**Localization:** Instructions, reasons, and decimal quantities are localized; item identifiers are not translated.

**Verification:** UI/API tests for partial, full, mismatch, and reallocation cases.

### ERP-INVENTORY-034 — Pack and handling-unit aggregation

**Shall:** The system shall support packing picked items into identified handling units and maintain explicit parent-child aggregation membership with quantities and timestamps.

**Rationale:** Pack structure supports shipment confirmation and traceability of cases, pallets, and parcels.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- A handling unit has a unique identifier within its issuing scope and cannot be an ancestor of itself.
- Pack/unpack operations update membership atomically and retain the previous membership event.
- Packed contents reconcile to picked quantities by item and serialized unit.

**Exception / edge case:** A mixed-item pallet is permitted only when the order, transport, and location rules allow it; otherwise the operation is blocked.

**Security and audit:** Only packing roles can alter pack structure after validation; repacking is logged and shipment state is checked.

**Localization:** Handling-unit labels can be rendered in selected language; encoded IDs and quantity data remain canonical.

**Verification:** Graph invariant tests and pack/unpack trace reconstruction.

### ERP-INVENTORY-035 — Staging and dock loading

**Shall:** The system shall track packed handling units through staging lanes and loading events, validating shipment/order association and recording the loading resource and time.

**Rationale:** A pick-complete status alone does not prove that cargo reached the correct outbound trailer or dock.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- A handling unit can be staged/loaded against only one active outbound load at a time.
- Load confirmation lists the expected versus actual handling units and records each difference.
- Loaded stock transitions to the configured shipped/in-transit status only on a valid dispatch confirmation.

**Exception / edge case:** A trailer change after loading requires an unload/reload event chain and cannot silently overwrite the original load reference.

**Security and audit:** Dock roles may confirm physical loading but cannot change customer order quantities or carrier contracts.

**Localization:** Dock names and operator prompts are localized; load IDs, scan keys, and timestamps remain stable.

**Verification:** Integration tests for load association, mismatch handling, and trailer reassignment.

### ERP-INVENTORY-036 — Replenishment from reserve to pick face

**Shall:** The system shall generate replenishment tasks when pick-face quantity crosses configured thresholds and source eligible reserve stock without altering total site quantity.

**Rationale:** Replenishment separates bulk storage from picking locations and avoids treating internal movement as new receipt.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- A trigger uses explicit minimum, target, unit, item, and location scope.
- Replenishment movement debits and credits the same ownership/status total.
- Concurrent replenishment tasks cannot exceed pick-face capacity or duplicate the same requirement beyond configured tolerance.

**Exception / edge case:** No eligible reserve stock creates an exception task; the system does not create inventory to satisfy the target.

**Security and audit:** Rule edits and manual replenishment overrides are permissioned and audited.

**Localization:** Thresholds use canonical unit values; displayed quantities use locale formatting and translated task instructions.

**Verification:** Threshold, capacity, and duplicate-task race-condition tests.

### ERP-INVENTORY-037 — Offline-capable handheld command sync

**Shall:** The system shall support warehouse clients that temporarily lose connectivity by queuing signed or authenticated commands with stable client-generated IDs and resolving duplicates during synchronization.

**Rationale:** Warehouse scanning areas can have intermittent networks, and repeated uploads must not duplicate movements.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- A replayed command ID produces the original outcome rather than another posting.
- Commands include actor/device, capture time, expected state/version, and command payload.
- Stale commands are rejected or routed for explicit conflict resolution without silent overwrites.

**Exception / edge case:** Two offline devices may scan the same serial; only the first valid commit succeeds and the other receives a conflict for disposition.

**Security and audit:** Device identity and user authorization are validated at sync; queued commands are protected at rest and failed attempts are audited.

**Localization:** Offline UI strings are bundled for supported languages; identifiers and timestamps include original capture-zone metadata.

**Verification:** Network-disconnect/replay tests including duplicate serial and stale-state conflicts.

### ERP-INVENTORY-038 — Task prioritization and workload view

**Shall:** The system shall rank warehouse tasks using tenant-configurable urgency, due time, zone, handling requirements, and service-level flags while preserving the underlying business priority inputs.

**Rationale:** Operational queues need transparent sequencing rather than hidden or untestable ranking.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- For a fixed rule version and input fixture, task ranking is deterministic.
- Each task exposes contributing rank factors and any manual priority override.
- Changing a rank rule affects only eligible open tasks and records its effective time/version.

**Exception / edge case:** Equal-ranked tasks use a deterministic tiebreaker such as created timestamp then task ID.

**Security and audit:** Users may see only authorized warehouses and task details; manual priority changes are logged with reason.

**Localization:** Priority labels and timestamps are localized; sort keys remain locale-independent and stable.

**Verification:** Rule unit tests and role-scoped task queue tests.

### ERP-INVENTORY-039 — Blind cycle count

**Shall:** The system shall support scheduled and ad hoc counts that can conceal expected quantity from counters and capture physical counts separately from book quantity.

**Rationale:** Blind count reduces confirmation bias and separates observation from adjustment authority.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- A blind counter cannot view expected quantity before submission when blind mode is enabled.
- Count task identifies scope, cutoff/version, counter, and status.
- Rescans or recounts create separate count observations rather than overwrite the first observation.

**Exception / edge case:** Counts spanning active movement require a frozen snapshot, movement cutoff, or explicit reconciliation policy to avoid comparing different stock states.

**Security and audit:** Counter and approver roles are separated when configured; concealment applies to APIs and exports, not only the screen.

**Localization:** Instructions and units are localized; numeric entry uses locale decimal parsing with clear validation.

**Verification:** UI, API, and export tests verifying expected quantity is inaccessible to blind counters.

### ERP-INVENTORY-040 — Count variance approval and adjustment

**Shall:** The system shall compare submitted counts with a defined book snapshot and require policy-based approval before posting any count variance as an inventory adjustment.

**Rationale:** Physical count observations are evidence, not authority to alter stock automatically.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Variance calculation identifies book version/cutoff, counted amount, and delta.
- Configured thresholds route variance to required approval levels or block self-approval.
- Approved adjustment posts a linked ledger event; rejected variance remains available for recount.

**Exception / edge case:** A second recount that matches book quantity closes the investigation without posting a net adjustment, while retaining both observations.

**Security and audit:** High-value variance thresholds and approver separation are configurable; all approvals/rejections and reasons are audited.

**Localization:** Variance display follows locale formatting; calculation uses precise canonical unit and defined rounding.

**Verification:** Workflow tests for below/above thresholds, self-approval block, recount, and ledger posting.

### E. Lot, serial, quality, and traceability

### ERP-INVENTORY-041 — Lot and serial control profile

**Shall:** The system shall enforce the item’s configured batch/lot, serial, or quantity-only control profile consistently across receipt, transfer, pick, shipment, return, and adjustment operations.

**Rationale:** Traceability cannot be optional at one lifecycle stage after being required at another.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Required lot or serial fields are validated at every transaction boundary.
- Changing an item profile is blocked while incompatible open stock or documents exist unless an approved migration is performed.
- The profile version is stored with each applicable movement.

**Exception / edge case:** An item with no historic lot data cannot be retroactively represented as lot-tracked without an explicit unknown-lot migration record.

**Security and audit:** Profile configuration is restricted and audited; API paths cannot bypass client-side validation.

**Localization:** Translated control labels do not change stable profile codes or data validation.

**Verification:** Lifecycle matrix tests for each control profile and attempted profile changes.

### ERP-INVENTORY-042 — Serial number uniqueness and lifecycle

**Shall:** The system shall ensure each serialized unit is uniquely identified within the configured identifier namespace and maintain its status/location lifecycle without allowing simultaneous duplicate active custody.

**Rationale:** Serial-level control is necessary for individual item accountability and warranty/recall lookup.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- A serialized ID cannot be received twice as two active units within its uniqueness scope.
- Transfer, ship, return, and scrap events maintain a single coherent serial history.
- Serial lookup returns tenant-authorized current state and prior event chain.

**Exception / edge case:** A serial identifier may be reused only if the configured external scheme permits it and prior lifecycle is closed; uniqueness scope is explicit.

**Security and audit:** Serial lookups are access-controlled, export events audited, and high-risk status changes require reason.

**Localization:** Serial strings are preserved exactly and searched without locale-dependent case or digit conversion unless scheme specifies normalization.

**Verification:** Concurrency tests for duplicate receipt plus serial lifecycle reconstruction tests.

### ERP-INVENTORY-043 — Expiry-aware allocation

**Shall:** The system shall support item/lot expiry dates and configurable allocation rules that prevent allocation of expired stock and can prioritize earlier-expiring eligible stock.

**Rationale:** Expiry-sensitive distribution needs reliable date-aware allocation while shelf-life rules differ by industry and customer.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Expired lots are excluded according to the tenant’s expiry-zone/date policy.
- FEFO selection orders eligible lots by expiry and applies deterministic tiebreakers.
- Minimum remaining shelf-life checks can be configured per customer/order/item and are evaluated at pick or reservation.

**Exception / edge case:** A lot without expiry may be eligible only where policy permits; it is never assigned an invented expiry date.

**Security and audit:** Overrides of expired or minimum-life restrictions are separately authorized and logged.

**Localization:** Expiry display respects warehouse/user zone and locale date format; comparison uses stored date semantics, not formatted text.

**Verification:** Boundary tests at expiry cutoff, local midnight, FEFO ordering, and customer shelf-life constraint.

### ERP-INVENTORY-044 — Traceability genealogy and transformations

**Shall:** The system shall record parent-child lot/serial/handling-unit relationships for configured assembly, repack, split, merge, relabel, or transformation events with input and output quantities.

**Rationale:** Transformation provenance supports forward and backward tracing beyond simple location movement.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- A transformation event lists all consumed inputs and produced outputs under one event ID.
- Input/output quantities reconcile under configured yield, scrap, and unit-conversion rules.
- Queries traverse upstream and downstream relationships with cycle detection.

**Exception / edge case:** A many-to-many transformation with unknown yield is held for recorded variance rather than forcing a false one-to-one mapping.

**Security and audit:** Transformation posting is restricted to authorized roles; source data and correction links are retained.

**Localization:** Transformation descriptions and reason codes are localized; identifiers and quantitative conversions remain canonical.

**Verification:** Graph traversal tests for split/merge/cycle, yield variance, and correction handling.

### ERP-INVENTORY-045 — Recall and trace query

**Shall:** The system shall provide authorized forward and backward trace queries from item, lot, serial, receipt, shipment, or handling unit to all linked inventory and logistics events within defined scope.

**Rationale:** A recall investigation requires a complete, explainable set of affected on-hand, shipped, and transferred stock.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- A query returns relevant current and historical locations/owners and source/sink events with pagination and time bounds.
- Results identify incomplete or unmapped external references rather than implying full trace coverage.
- The same query against unchanged event data produces the same result set and event identifiers.

**Exception / edge case:** If a link is missing, the output marks the trace as partial and identifies the traversal boundary or data gap.

**Security and audit:** Recall access is least-privilege and export is logged; sensitive partner/customer fields are minimized.

**Localization:** Search labels and results are localized while exact lot/serial IDs and timestamps remain verbatim.

**Verification:** Seeded-graph end-to-end tests, partial-trace fixture, and export audit check.

### ERP-INVENTORY-046 — Quality inspection plan execution

**Shall:** The system shall support configurable inspection plans that define trigger, sample basis, measurements, acceptance limits, required evidence, and disposition authority for selected items or lots.

**Rationale:** Inspection depth and criteria differ by product, customer, and regulatory regime and must remain configurable.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- An inspection task records plan version, sampled quantity/unit, measured values, result, inspector, and timestamp.
- A failed required measurement prevents automatic release.
- An inspection plan cannot be edited in place for an already-started inspection; a new version is created.

**Exception / edge case:** An incomplete measurement set remains pending and cannot be treated as pass by absence of failures.

**Security and audit:** Inspection plan editing and disposition rights are separate; result changes retain old value, actor, reason, and evidence.

**Localization:** Measurement labels, instructions, and report language are localized; unit codes and stored values are canonical.

**Verification:** Plan lifecycle tests for pass/fail/incomplete and immutable version association.

### ERP-INVENTORY-047 — Quality disposition and release

**Shall:** The system shall restrict transitions among quality hold, accepted, rework, rejected, and scrapped states to configured disposition rules and authorized roles.

**Rationale:** Inspection outcomes require explicit operational treatment before quantity becomes usable or leaves custody.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Only permitted transitions from the current quality state can commit.
- Release to available stock verifies all required inspection and documentation prerequisites.
- Rework creates a linked work reference and does not erase the original failing evidence.

**Exception / edge case:** A conditional release can carry quantity, destination, customer/order, and expiration limits and must not be generalized to the whole lot.

**Security and audit:** Disposition requires reason; conditional or high-risk releases can require two-person approval and are audited.

**Localization:** State and reason labels are translated; state codes control availability and integrations.

**Verification:** State-machine authorization tests for normal, forbidden, conditional, and rejected transitions.

### ERP-INVENTORY-048 — Shelf-life and date semantics

**Shall:** The system shall store manufacture, best-before, expiry, and retest dates as distinct typed fields with an item/industry configuration specifying which field drives operational eligibility.

**Rationale:** Distinct dates have different meanings and must not be conflated into a universal expiration law.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Date fields are separately stored and retained with source and precision (date versus timestamp).
- Eligibility rules identify the controlling date field and boundary convention.
- A date-only value is not converted into a timestamp using an implicit timezone.

**Exception / edge case:** If source documents disagree, the receipt is held for resolution or follows a documented precedence rule; values are not auto-merged.

**Security and audit:** Date overrides and provenance edits require reasoned authorization and are audited.

**Localization:** Localized date entry/display is separate from canonical ISO data; ambiguous date strings are rejected or disambiguated.

**Verification:** Schema/API tests plus locale and boundary-date tests.

### ERP-INVENTORY-049 — Industry and jurisdiction control profiles

**Shall:** The system shall implement regulated or industry-specific inventory controls as named, versioned configuration profiles or separately deployable extensions, never as undocumented global assumptions.

**Rationale:** Food, healthcare, chemicals, aerospace, and other sectors can impose different controls; legal applicability must be reviewed for each deployment.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Every enabled profile identifies its version, scope, effective date, and source owner.
- A profile’s mandatory fields and transitions are validated in automated acceptance tests.
- Changing jurisdiction/entity assignment does not retroactively relabel completed events.

**Exception / edge case:** An unconfigured jurisdiction or industry extension yields a deployment/configuration warning and cannot be inferred from user locale alone.

**Security and audit:** Profile changes require configuration privilege and approval; compliance evidence access is controlled and audited.

**Localization:** UI help and controlled vocabularies are localized; compliance values and source/version identifiers remain stable.

**Verification:** Configuration matrix test over base and extension profiles; review by domain/compliance owner.

### ERP-INVENTORY-050 — Trace event interoperability

**Shall:** The system shall expose configurable mapping of inventory and logistics events to an interoperable trace-event contract, preserving event identity, time, what/where/why context, and provenance.

**Rationale:** A canonical trace event facilitates partner visibility; GS1 EPCIS describes interoperable visibility-event exchange without requiring every tenant to adopt it. \[6]

**Acceptance criteria:**

- A configured adapter can emit or ingest required event fields with stable business IDs and event time.
- Events include source/destination/location, object or quantity, business step/reason, and actor/source as applicable.
- Unknown code values are retained or quarantined according to adapter policy and never silently remapped.

**Exception / edge case:** External recipients may lack a compatible vocabulary; mapping or a versioned proprietary extension is explicit and documented.

**Security and audit:** Partner data sharing is opt-in, scoped by contract/tenant configuration, authenticated, and access logged.

**Localization:** Payload natural-language text may be localized; event codes, IDs, and machine fields follow the versioned contract.

**Verification:** Contract tests against EPCIS 2.0 test vectors or chosen adapter schema; unknown-code test.

### F. Outbound logistics and transport

### ERP-INVENTORY-051 — Shipment planning and carrier tender

**Shall:** The system shall build an outbound shipment from eligible order lines and handling units, recording ship-from, ship-to, service requirement, planned date, carrier/tender status, and source document references.

**Rationale:** A shipment is a transport execution object, distinct from order commitment and inventory pick tasks.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Shipment creation validates customer/order scope, warehouse, and eligible packed quantity.
- Tender request has an idempotent correlation ID and stores carrier response/reference.
- Shipment status distinguishes planned, tendered, accepted, dispatched, and canceled.

**Exception / edge case:** Carrier rejection returns the shipment to a retry/replan state without duplicating picked stock or cancelling the customer order.

**Security and audit:** Tender authorization and carrier account credentials are server-side and separately protected from warehouse roles.

**Localization:** Addresses and service labels are localized for print/read; country/region codes and exact recipient strings are preserved.

**Verification:** End-to-end test with carrier mock acceptance, rejection, and duplicate tender retry.

### ERP-INVENTORY-052 — Carrier rates and label adapter

**Shall:** The system shall integrate optional carrier rate and label services through replaceable adapters that normalize service, charge, package, tracking identifier, and label artifact responses.

**Rationale:** Carrier APIs change and vary by territory; they should not be embedded in core inventory rules.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Adapter responses map to a versioned canonical contract and preserve provider IDs.
- A returned label is linked to shipment/package and has media type, creation time, and adapter version.
- Provider timeout or malformed response leaves stock state unchanged and creates a retryable exception.

**Exception / edge case:** A tenant with no carrier account can use manual service and tracking entry with a separate authorization policy.

**Security and audit:** Secrets are stored outside business records, redacted from logs, and rotated per tenant/provider configuration.

**Localization:** Labels may be generated in carrier-required locale and paper format; canonical data and returned image/PDF bytes are preserved.

**Verification:** Mock-provider contract tests, secret scanning, and malformed response test.

### ERP-INVENTORY-053 — Shipment consolidation

**Shall:** The system shall permit compatible orders to be consolidated into a shipment while preserving per-order, per-line, and per-handling-unit attribution and allocation of shipment costs where configured.

**Rationale:** Consolidation can lower transport cost but must not merge customer ownership, quantities, or shipment proof.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Consolidated shipment lists each source order and quantity allocation.
- Incompatible destinations, handling profiles, or service constraints are rejected or split.
- Unconsolidation preserves original picks and records resulting shipment relationship changes.

**Exception / edge case:** One order may split across multiple shipments; totals reconcile to the order’s eligible fulfilled quantity.

**Security and audit:** Only permitted order/warehouse scopes can be combined; consolidation, split, and cost allocation are audited.
