**Normative requirement:** The system shall record parent-child lot/serial/handling-unit relationships for configured assembly, repack, split, merge, relabel, or transformation events with input and output quantities.

**Rationale:** Transformation provenance supports forward and backward tracing beyond simple location movement.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A transformation event lists all consumed inputs and produced outputs under one event ID.

**AC 2.** Input/output quantities reconcile under configured yield, scrap, and unit-conversion rules.

**AC 3.** Queries traverse upstream and downstream relationships with cycle detection.

**Exception / edge case:** A many-to-many transformation with unknown yield is held for recorded variance rather than forcing a false one-to-one mapping.

**Security and audit implications:** Transformation posting is restricted to authorized roles; source data and correction links are retained.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Transformation descriptions and reason codes are localized; identifiers and quantitative conversions remain canonical.

**Verification method:** Graph traversal tests for split/merge/cycle, yield variance, and correction handling.

**REQUIREMENT 0255 OF 1120  |  INVENTORY, WAREHOUSE, AND LOGISTICS**

## ERP-INVENTORY-045 — Recall and trace query

**Normative requirement:** The system shall provide authorized forward and backward trace queries from item, lot, serial, receipt, shipment, or handling unit to all linked inventory and logistics events within defined scope.

**Rationale:** A recall investigation requires a complete, explainable set of affected on-hand, shipped, and transferred stock.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A query returns relevant current and historical locations/owners and source/sink events with pagination and time bounds.

**AC 2.** Results identify incomplete or unmapped external references rather than implying full trace coverage.

**AC 3.** The same query against unchanged event data produces the same result set and event identifiers.

**Exception / edge case:** If a link is missing, the output marks the trace as partial and identifies the traversal boundary or data gap.

**Security and audit implications:** Recall access is least-privilege and export is logged; sensitive partner/customer fields are minimized.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Search labels and results are localized while exact lot/serial IDs and timestamps remain verbatim.

**Verification method:** Seeded-graph end-to-end tests, partial-trace fixture, and export audit check.

**REQUIREMENT 0256 OF 1120  |  INVENTORY, WAREHOUSE, AND LOGISTICS**

## ERP-INVENTORY-046 — Quality inspection plan execution

**Normative requirement:** The system shall support configurable inspection plans that define trigger, sample basis, measurements, acceptance limits, required evidence, and disposition authority for selected items or lots.

**Rationale:** Inspection depth and criteria differ by product, customer, and regulatory regime and must remain configurable.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** An inspection task records plan version, sampled quantity/unit, measured values, result, inspector, and timestamp.

**AC 2.** A failed required measurement prevents automatic release.

**AC 3.** An inspection plan cannot be edited in place for an already-started inspection; a new version is created.

**Exception / edge case:** An incomplete measurement set remains pending and cannot be treated as pass by absence of failures.

**Security and audit implications:** Inspection plan editing and disposition rights are separate; result changes retain old value, actor, reason, and evidence.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Measurement labels, instructions, and report language are localized; unit codes and stored values are canonical.

**Verification method:** Plan lifecycle tests for pass/fail/incomplete and immutable version association.

**REQUIREMENT 0257 OF 1120  |  INVENTORY, WAREHOUSE, AND LOGISTICS**

## ERP-INVENTORY-047 — Quality disposition and release

**Normative requirement:** The system shall restrict transitions among quality hold, accepted, rework, rejected, and scrapped states to configured disposition rules and authorized roles.

**Rationale:** Inspection outcomes require explicit operational treatment before quantity becomes usable or leaves custody.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Only permitted transitions from the current quality state can commit.

**AC 2.** Release to available stock verifies all required inspection and documentation prerequisites.

**AC 3.** Rework creates a linked work reference and does not erase the original failing evidence.

**Exception / edge case:** A conditional release can carry quantity, destination, customer/order, and expiration limits and must not be generalized to the whole lot.

**Security and audit implications:** Disposition requires reason; conditional or high-risk releases can require two-person approval and are audited.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** State and reason labels are translated; state codes control availability and integrations.

**Verification method:** State-machine authorization tests for normal, forbidden, conditional, and rejected transitions.

**REQUIREMENT 0258 OF 1120  |  INVENTORY, WAREHOUSE, AND LOGISTICS**

## ERP-INVENTORY-048 — Shelf-life and date semantics

**Normative requirement:** The system shall store manufacture, best-before, expiry, and retest dates as distinct typed fields with an item/industry configuration specifying which field drives operational eligibility.

**Rationale:** Distinct dates have different meanings and must not be conflated into a universal expiration law.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Date fields are separately stored and retained with source and precision (date versus timestamp).

**AC 2.** Eligibility rules identify the controlling date field and boundary convention.

**AC 3.** A date-only value is not converted into a timestamp using an implicit timezone.

**Exception / edge case:** If source documents disagree, the receipt is held for resolution or follows a documented precedence rule; values are not auto-merged.

**Security and audit implications:** Date overrides and provenance edits require reasoned authorization and are audited.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Localized date entry/display is separate from canonical ISO data; ambiguous date strings are rejected or disambiguated.

**Verification method:** Schema/API tests plus locale and boundary-date tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0259 OF 1120  |  INVENTORY, WAREHOUSE, AND LOGISTICS**

## ERP-INVENTORY-049 — Industry and jurisdiction control profiles

**Normative requirement:** The system shall implement regulated or industry-specific inventory controls as named, versioned configuration profiles or separately deployable extensions, never as undocumented global assumptions.

**Rationale:** Food, healthcare, chemicals, aerospace, and other sectors can impose different controls; legal applicability must be reviewed for each deployment.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Every enabled profile identifies its version, scope, effective date, and source owner.

**AC 2.** A profile’s mandatory fields and transitions are validated in automated acceptance tests.

**AC 3.** Changing jurisdiction/entity assignment does not retroactively relabel completed events.

**Exception / edge case:** An unconfigured jurisdiction or industry extension yields a deployment/configuration warning and cannot be inferred from user locale alone.

**Security and audit implications:** Profile changes require configuration privilege and approval; compliance evidence access is controlled and audited.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** UI help and controlled vocabularies are localized; compliance values and source/version identifiers remain stable.

**Verification method:** Configuration matrix test over base and extension profiles; review by domain/compliance owner.

**REQUIREMENT 0260 OF 1120  |  INVENTORY, WAREHOUSE, AND LOGISTICS**

## ERP-INVENTORY-050 — Trace event interoperability

**Normative requirement:** The system shall expose configurable mapping of inventory and logistics events to an interoperable trace-event contract, preserving event identity, time, what/where/why context, and provenance.

**Rationale:** A canonical trace event facilitates partner visibility; GS1 EPCIS describes interoperable visibility-event exchange without requiring every tenant to adopt it. \[6]

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A configured adapter can emit or ingest required event fields with stable business IDs and event time.

**AC 2.** Events include source/destination/location, object or quantity, business step/reason, and actor/source as applicable.

**AC 3.** Unknown code values are retained or quarantined according to adapter policy and never silently remapped.

**Exception / edge case:** External recipients may lack a compatible vocabulary; mapping or a versioned proprietary extension is explicit and documented.

**Security and audit implications:** Partner data sharing is opt-in, scoped by contract/tenant configuration, authenticated, and access logged.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Payload natural-language text may be localized; event codes, IDs, and machine fields follow the versioned contract.

**Verification method:** Contract tests against EPCIS 2.0 test vectors or chosen adapter schema; unknown-code test.

**REQUIREMENT 0261 OF 1120  |  INVENTORY, WAREHOUSE, AND LOGISTICS**

## ERP-INVENTORY-051 — Shipment planning and carrier tender

**Normative requirement:** The system shall build an outbound shipment from eligible order lines and handling units, recording ship-from, ship-to, service requirement, planned date, carrier/tender status, and source document references.

**Rationale:** A shipment is a transport execution object, distinct from order commitment and inventory pick tasks.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Shipment creation validates customer/order scope, warehouse, and eligible packed quantity.

**AC 2.** Tender request has an idempotent correlation ID and stores carrier response/reference.

**AC 3.** Shipment status distinguishes planned, tendered, accepted, dispatched, and canceled.

**Exception / edge case:** Carrier rejection returns the shipment to a retry/replan state without duplicating picked stock or cancelling the customer order.

**Security and audit implications:** Tender authorization and carrier account credentials are server-side and separately protected from warehouse roles.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Addresses and service labels are localized for print/read; country/region codes and exact recipient strings are preserved.

**Verification method:** End-to-end test with carrier mock acceptance, rejection, and duplicate tender retry.

**REQUIREMENT 0262 OF 1120  |  INVENTORY, WAREHOUSE, AND LOGISTICS**

## ERP-INVENTORY-052 — Carrier rates and label adapter

**Normative requirement:** The system shall integrate optional carrier rate and label services through replaceable adapters that normalize service, charge, package, tracking identifier, and label artifact responses.

**Rationale:** Carrier APIs change and vary by territory; they should not be embedded in core inventory rules.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Adapter responses map to a versioned canonical contract and preserve provider IDs.

**AC 2.** A returned label is linked to shipment/package and has media type, creation time, and adapter version.

**AC 3.** Provider timeout or malformed response leaves stock state unchanged and creates a retryable exception.

**Exception / edge case:** A tenant with no carrier account can use manual service and tracking entry with a separate authorization policy.

**Security and audit implications:** Secrets are stored outside business records, redacted from logs, and rotated per tenant/provider configuration.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Labels may be generated in carrier-required locale and paper format; canonical data and returned image/PDF bytes are preserved.

**Verification method:** Mock-provider contract tests, secret scanning, and malformed response test.

**REQUIREMENT 0263 OF 1120  |  INVENTORY, WAREHOUSE, AND LOGISTICS**

## ERP-INVENTORY-053 — Shipment consolidation

**Normative requirement:** The system shall permit compatible orders to be consolidated into a shipment while preserving per-order, per-line, and per-handling-unit attribution and allocation of shipment costs where configured.

**Rationale:** Consolidation can lower transport cost but must not merge customer ownership, quantities, or shipment proof.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Consolidated shipment lists each source order and quantity allocation.

**AC 2.** Incompatible destinations, handling profiles, or service constraints are rejected or split.

**AC 3.** Unconsolidation preserves original picks and records resulting shipment relationship changes.

**Exception / edge case:** One order may split across multiple shipments; totals reconcile to the order’s eligible fulfilled quantity.

**Security and audit implications:** Only permitted order/warehouse scopes can be combined; consolidation, split, and cost allocation are audited.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Destination and service display strings follow locale; address comparison uses configured normalized identifiers, not translated labels.

**Verification method:** Tests for compatible/incompatible consolidation, split, and per-order reconciliation.

**REQUIREMENT 0264 OF 1120  |  INVENTORY, WAREHOUSE, AND LOGISTICS**

## ERP-INVENTORY-054 — Dispatch confirmation and proof of handover

**Normative requirement:** The system shall record dispatch as a timestamped handover event with shipment, handling units, carrier/driver identity as available, dispatch location, and proof reference.

**Rationale:** Inventory transitions to in-transit or shipped status only on a defined physical dispatch event, not merely label creation.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Dispatch is blocked if required packed units are missing or an active hold remains.

**AC 2.** Successful dispatch transitions only the confirmed quantities and records actor and event time.

**AC 3.** Proof attachment or an explicit no-proof reason is linked to the dispatch record.

**Exception / edge case:** A carrier collects fewer units than staged; only the handed-over units dispatch and the rest remain staged with discrepancy status.

**Security and audit implications:** Dispatch confirmation is restricted to authorized dock roles; proof downloads and corrections are audited.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Dispatch documents render in configured language and time zone; external proof content is preserved in its original form.

**Verification method:** Workflow tests for full/partial handover, hold, missing proof, and stock transition.

**REQUIREMENT 0265 OF 1120  |  INVENTORY, WAREHOUSE, AND LOGISTICS**

## ERP-INVENTORY-055 — Freight status lifecycle

**Normative requirement:** The system shall maintain shipment status as an event-derived lifecycle with provider/source, event time, received time, and normalized status while preserving original carrier status text/code.

**Rationale:** External shipment visibility should be traceable and should not overwrite the authoritative internal dispatch record.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Carrier events are stored immutably with both event and ingestion timestamps.

**AC 2.** Out-of-order events do not move a shipment backward without an explicit correction/reconciliation rule.

**AC 3.** Normalized status mapping is versioned and can represent unknown status.

**Exception / edge case:** A delivered scan arriving before an earlier in-transit scan remains in the timeline; current state follows the configured ordering policy.

**Security and audit implications:** Webhook signatures and tenant/carrier association are validated; raw payload access is restricted and audited.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Carrier-provided strings remain verbatim; normalized status labels and timeline timestamps are localized.

**Verification method:** Contract tests with out-of-order, duplicate, invalid-signature, and unknown carrier events.

**REQUIREMENT 0266 OF 1120  |  INVENTORY, WAREHOUSE, AND LOGISTICS**

## ERP-INVENTORY-056 — Trade and cross-border data boundary

**Normative requirement:** The system shall capture configurable shipment customs/trade fields and document references through jurisdiction-specific extensions without treating any field set, tariff, export restriction, or trade term as universal law.

**Rationale:** Cross-border obligations vary by commodity, destination, origin, and time; the core needs an explicit policy/provider boundary.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A shipment requiring a configured extension cannot be finalized without its configured mandatory fields.

**AC 2.** Extension versions and determination source/time are retained on the shipment.

**AC 3.** Core shipment creation remains available for domestic/no-extension flows.

**Exception / edge case:** When a classification or jurisdiction determination is missing, the workflow reports unresolved data and does not invent a default classification.

**Security and audit implications:** Restricted trade data is access-controlled; decisions, source evidence, and overrides are auditable.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Official names, units, dates, and document language follow tenant/entity policy; codes and declarations retain source precision.

**Verification method:** Extension acceptance tests maintained with legal/compliance owner; domestic baseline regression tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0267 OF 1120  |  INVENTORY, WAREHOUSE, AND LOGISTICS**

## ERP-INVENTORY-057 — Carrier tracking event ingestion

**Normative requirement:** The system shall ingest carrier tracking events through authenticated webhooks or polling adapters, deduplicate by provider event identity, and link accepted events to the correct tenant shipment.

**Rationale:** Freight visibility depends on reliable event reception and duplicate-safe integration behavior.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Repeated identical provider event ID creates one business event and increments delivery telemetry only.

**AC 2.** An event whose tracking number maps ambiguously to shipments is quarantined for resolution.

**AC 3.** Failed signature/authentication does not change shipment state.

**Exception / edge case:** A carrier reuses event IDs across accounts; deduplication includes provider account and tenant namespace.

**Security and audit implications:** Inbound endpoints validate signatures, timestamps/replay window, and tenant mapping; rejected payloads are retained only under configured security retention.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Raw event text is preserved; normalized labels and times follow the user’s language and shipment zone.

**Verification method:** Webhook integration tests for replay, duplicate ID scope, ambiguous tracking, and signature failure.

**REQUIREMENT 0268 OF 1120  |  INVENTORY, WAREHOUSE, AND LOGISTICS**

## ERP-INVENTORY-058 — Transport unit and container relationships

**Normative requirement:** The system shall model shipment handling units and their optional aggregation into trailers, containers, or other transport units with explicit load/unload events.

**Rationale:** Multi-leg and containerized logistics require custody structure beyond an order-to-package link.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A transport-unit manifest enumerates member handling units at a recorded time.

**AC 2.** Load/unload operations validate current membership and location and preserve prior membership events.

**AC 3.** A handling unit cannot be simultaneously assigned to conflicting active transport units.

**Exception / edge case:** A sealed container opened for inspection creates seal-break and reseal events if the configured workflow requires them.

**Security and audit implications:** Transport manifest visibility follows partner/tenant permissions; seal and custody events are tamper-evident and audited.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Container codes and security seal values remain verbatim; human instructions are localized.

**Verification method:** Relationship integrity and conflict tests across concurrent loading operations.

**REQUIREMENT 0269 OF 1120  |  INVENTORY, WAREHOUSE, AND LOGISTICS**

## ERP-INVENTORY-059 — Reverse logistics authorization

**Normative requirement:** The system shall coordinate a return shipment against an approved return authorization and link carrier tracking, returned handling units, and subsequent receiving disposition without automatically crediting finance.

**Rationale:** Transport return, physical receipt, and financial credit are separate contracts and require separate confirmations.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Return shipment references return authorization and original shipment where available.

**AC 2.** Tracking events update return transport only and do not change stock until receipt is posted.

**AC 3.** Return completion exposes an event/reference to the owning returns and finance modules.

**Exception / edge case:** Unsolicited return freight is recorded as an exception shipment and cannot be matched to an unrelated order by fuzzy name alone.

**Security and audit implications:** Return shipments and customer references are access-scoped; exception resolution and data sharing are audited.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Return instructions, labels, and customer-facing updates support selected language; original identifiers remain intact.

**Verification method:** Cross-module tests proving no inventory or finance mutation before corresponding receipt/credit events.

**REQUIREMENT 0270 OF 1120  |  INVENTORY, WAREHOUSE, AND LOGISTICS**

## ERP-INVENTORY-060 — Shipping documents and measurement presentation

**Normative requirement:** The system shall generate shipment documents from immutable shipment data using versioned templates that select document language, units, address rendering, and numeric/date formats independently of stored canonical values.

**Rationale:** Warehouse documents must be operationally legible across locales without changing the underlying shipment facts.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Template records identify version and chosen locale/unit policy.

**AC 2.** Re-rendering with another locale changes presentation but not shipment IDs, quantities, weights, or timestamps in payload data.

**AC 3.** A missing translation falls back to the configured default and is visible to the document administrator.

**Exception / edge case:** A carrier requires a mandated field or label language; the carrier adapter’s requirement overrides the user display language only for that output artifact.

**Security and audit implications:** Generation and download are audited; output access excludes fields not needed by the recipient.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Support right-to-left layout, translated labels, locale-aware numbers/dates, and preserved identifier strings.

**Verification method:** Golden-document tests for at least two locales, decimal separators, RTL layout, and canonical-value equality.

**REQUIREMENT 0271 OF 1120  |  INVENTORY, WAREHOUSE, AND LOGISTICS**

## ERP-INVENTORY-061 — Tenant isolation for all inventory data

**Normative requirement:** The system shall enforce tenant scope on every inventory, warehouse, logistics, attachment, search, report, and integration operation at the service boundary and in database policy where available.

**Rationale:** Shared commercial SaaS must prevent cross-tenant data access through both application flaws and direct query paths.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Cross-tenant read, write, lookup, and export attempts return no protected data and do not mutate state.

**AC 2.** Every tenant-owned row has non-null tenant identity and tenant-consistent foreign-key relationships.

**AC 3.** Runtime database role tests demonstrate no owner or BYPASSRLS bypass is used by ordinary application paths.

**Exception / edge case:** A formally authorized platform support operation uses a separate, time-bound, reason-coded support context and is never implicit tenant switching.

**Security and audit implications:** Tenant scoping is authorization-critical; RLS is defense in depth and owner/superuser exceptions are tested. \[3]

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Tenant translations and locale settings are isolated; no translation cache may return another tenant’s private term overrides.

**Verification method:** Automated multi-tenant penetration tests plus database schema/role and RLS tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0272 OF 1120  |  INVENTORY, WAREHOUSE, AND LOGISTICS**

## ERP-INVENTORY-062 — Action and data permission boundaries

**Normative requirement:** The system shall authorize inventory actions by tenant, entity, warehouse, object scope, and action, with separable privileges for receive, move, reserve, pick, adjust, release quality, dispatch, configure, and export.

**Rationale:** Role separation reduces unauthorized adjustment and self-approval risk; NIST’s control catalog is adaptable rather than a universal mandate. \[8]

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Unauthenticated callers cannot invoke protected action APIs; unauthorized authenticated users receive denial without mutation.

**AC 2.** Configured maker-checker rules prevent the initiating actor from approving their own high-impact adjustment.

**AC 3.** Permission changes take effect on server requests and are auditable.

**Exception / edge case:** Emergency access is time-bounded and requires a reason plus post-event review when enabled by tenant policy.

**Security and audit implications:** Enforce least privilege server-side and audit grant, revoke, denial, approval, and override events.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Role labels and denial messages are translated; permission identifiers remain stable.

**Verification method:** Role matrix tests including API bypass attempts, self-approval, and expired emergency grant.

**REQUIREMENT 0273 OF 1120  |  INVENTORY, WAREHOUSE, AND LOGISTICS**

## ERP-INVENTORY-063 — Audit event integrity and provenance

**Normative requirement:** The system shall append audit events for material master, quantity, valuation, status, approval, configuration, and integration changes with actor/source, timestamp, correlation, target, and before/after or payload digest as appropriate.

**Rationale:** A traceable change history supports incident investigation and business reconciliation.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Audit event is created atomically with the governed business commit or via a durable transactional outbox.

**AC 2.** Ordinary application roles cannot alter or delete historical audit events.

**AC 3.** Audit search is filterable by target, actor, operation, and time and is tenant-scoped.

**Exception / edge case:** A privacy or retention policy requires redaction/deletion of selected personal data; the event preserves a permitted non-identifying digest and redaction record under approved policy.

**Security and audit implications:** Audit records are protected from ordinary operators; viewing/exporting audit trails is itself logged.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Human-readable reason may be localized but canonical operation code, actor ID, and timestamps remain stable.

**Verification method:** Tamper/role tests, event atomicity test, and audit search/export authorization tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0274 OF 1120  |  INVENTORY, WAREHOUSE, AND LOGISTICS**

## ERP-INVENTORY-064 — Idempotent inventory command APIs

**Normative requirement:** The system shall require an idempotency key or stable source event ID for externally retried commands that create receipts, movements, reservations, picks, dispatches, adjustments, or count postings.

**Rationale:** Network retries must not duplicate physical quantity changes.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Same key and same request returns the original committed result.

**AC 2.** Same key with a different request body is rejected as conflict.

**AC 3.** Idempotency records are tenant-scoped and retained for a configured period at least as long as the maximum retry horizon.

**Exception / edge case:** If the first request is still processing, concurrent duplicates receive a consistent pending/result response rather than both committing.

**Security and audit implications:** Keys are unguessable or appropriately scoped; responses do not leak results to other tenants, and replay attempts are logged.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Error payloads are localized while stable error codes and request IDs remain invariant.

**Verification method:** API concurrency tests, same-key/different-payload tests, and retry after timeout test.

**REQUIREMENT 0275 OF 1120  |  INVENTORY, WAREHOUSE, AND LOGISTICS**

## ERP-INVENTORY-065 — Versioned events and transactional outbox

**Normative requirement:** The system shall publish committed inventory/logistics events through a durable outbox with schema version, tenant, aggregate ID, sequence, event time, and correlation ID.

**Rationale:** Cross-module or partner integrations must not observe an uncommitted movement or lose a committed event on process failure.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Business transaction and outbox insert commit or roll back together.

**AC 2.** Dispatcher retries delivery and marks each destination outcome without duplicating business event identity.

**AC 3.** Consumers can detect unsupported schema version and quarantine it.

**Exception / edge case:** Out-of-order delivery is handled by aggregate sequence or consumer reconciliation rather than assuming network order.

**Security and audit implications:** Outbox payload access and delivery credentials are restricted; secret fields are excluded and delivery outcome is audited.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Machine contract codes remain locale-neutral; optional descriptive fields include declared language tags.

**Verification method:** Crash/fault-injection tests between commit and publish; consumer duplicate/version tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0276 OF 1120  |  INVENTORY, WAREHOUSE, AND LOGISTICS**

## ERP-INVENTORY-066 — Bulk import/export safeguards

**Normative requirement:** The system shall validate bulk inventory imports and exports against tenant scope, schema version, reference integrity, row limits, and explicit posting mode before any irreversible bulk posting.

**Rationale:** Bulk operations can create large-scale balance errors and broad data exposure if validation or authorization is weak.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Dry-run returns row-level valid/error counts and does not change stock.

**AC 2.** Commit requires explicit authorized confirmation tied to the validated file digest/version.

**AC 3.** Export includes only authorized rows/fields and records filters, actor, and output reference.

**Exception / edge case:** A file changes after dry-run; its digest mismatch invalidates the prior validation and requires a new dry-run.

**Security and audit implications:** Uploads are malware-checked, sensitive exports are permissioned and audited, and error reports avoid disclosing unrelated tenant data.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Templates expose locale-neutral machine formats plus localized human labels; decimal/date parsing requires declared locale or canonical format.

**Verification method:** End-to-end dry-run/commit tests, digest tamper test, and export authorization test.

**REQUIREMENT 0277 OF 1120  |  INVENTORY, WAREHOUSE, AND LOGISTICS**

## ERP-INVENTORY-067 — As-of inventory reporting

**Normative requirement:** The system shall provide quantity and valuation reports that specify effective-time cutoff, posting-time cutoff where available, status/ownership/location filters, unit/currency, and source projection version.

**Rationale:** Historical reports need explicit temporal meaning and scope to be reproducible.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A report response includes filters, as-of instant, generated time, unit/currency, and data version.

**AC 2.** Re-running an unchanged report against unchanged ledger data yields identical totals.

**AC 3.** Aggregated totals reconcile to underlying authorized detail for the same filters.

**Exception / edge case:** Late-arriving events are either excluded from prior generated snapshot or reported as restatement/delta under explicit policy.

**Security and audit implications:** Report rows obey row-level permissions; exports are audited and large downloads are time-limited.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Dates, decimals, and currency display follow locale while the report retains canonical machine data and time-zone context.

**Verification method:** Fixture-based reconciliation tests with late events and multiple status/owner filters.

**REQUIREMENT 0278 OF 1120  |  INVENTORY, WAREHOUSE, AND LOGISTICS**

## ERP-INVENTORY-068 — Operational alerts and expiry queues

**Normative requirement:** The system shall create configurable alerts for low stock, blocked putaway, overdue task, impending expiry, failed integration, and unresolved discrepancy with severity, owner, age, and actionable reference.

**Rationale:** Operational exceptions should be visible before they become missed shipments, loss, or compliance gaps.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Each alert rule has scope, threshold, effective version, and routing target.

**AC 2.** Repeated source conditions update or deduplicate an open alert according to configured key.

**AC 3.** Closing an alert requires resolution code or linked completed action.

**Exception / edge case:** A false-positive threshold change closes no existing alert automatically unless an explicit bulk disposition is approved.

**Security and audit implications:** Alert subscriptions respect warehouse/entity access; external notifications omit sensitive details by default and are logged.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Messages and time-to-due values are localized; alert keys and severities remain canonical.

**Verification method:** Rule tests for trigger/deduplication/escalation/close and cross-role visibility.

**REQUIREMENT 0279 OF 1120  |  INVENTORY, WAREHOUSE, AND LOGISTICS**

## ERP-INVENTORY-069 — Multilingual UI and user formatting

**Normative requirement:** The system shall allow each user to select a supported interface locale independently of tenant defaults while rendering stable inventory codes, translated labels, and locale-appropriate numbers, dates, and units.

**Rationale:** A multilingual ERP must separate business identity from presentation and must not confuse decimal/date input formats.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Changing locale changes labels and formatting but not stored quantity, IDs, or API payload values.

**AC 2.** Every user-editable date/decimal field declares accepted format and rejects ambiguous unsupported input.

**AC 3.** Translation fallback follows configured user-to-tenant fallback and identifies missing resource keys in non-production diagnostics.

**Exception / edge case:** A shared terminal with no user locale uses warehouse default without changing the signed-in user’s persisted preference.

**Security and audit implications:** Locale preference is user profile data; tenant translation overrides are scoped and admin-edited changes are audited.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Support Unicode input/search and bidirectional text while preserving exact scanned identifiers and legal names.

**Verification method:** Automated locale tests for English plus a non-Latin locale and RTL smoke checks; API payload invariant tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0280 OF 1120  |  INVENTORY, WAREHOUSE, AND LOGISTICS**

## ERP-INVENTORY-070 — Accessible warehouse workflows

**Normative requirement:** The system shall provide accessible keyboard, screen-reader, focus, status-message, contrast, and target-size behavior for core inventory actions and handheld-compatible views, with a defined WCAG 2.2 conformance target selected by the product owner.

**Rationale:** Warehouse software is used under varied physical conditions and must offer testable accessible interaction; WCAG defines testable success criteria and conformance levels. \[5]

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Automated accessibility checks detect no critical violations on receiving, picking, counting, and shipment pages.

**AC 2.** All core actions are operable by keyboard and expose programmatic labels and result/status messages.

**AC 3.** An approved manual assistive-technology test plan records criterion-level results against the selected conformance level.

**Exception / edge case:** A specialized scanner or device interaction that cannot meet a criterion supplies an equivalent accessible workflow and is documented as an exception.

**Security and audit implications:** Accessible alternatives cannot bypass authorization or expose hidden expected quantities/records.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** All accessible names and announcements are translated; focus order and bidirectional layout are tested in supported locales.

**Verification method:** Automated axe/WCAG tooling plus manual keyboard and screen-reader acceptance tests.

# Manufacturing, Planning, and Quality

# Chapter 05 — Manufacturing, Planning, and Quality

**Status:** normative implementation-ready domain specification. **Reference date:** 2026-11-22. This chapter defines a configurable manufacturing and quality capability for mid-market and enterprise deployments. It does not assert universal manufacturing practice, tax/accounting treatment, legal obligation, certification, industry rule, or quality standard. Applicability is selected through customer-owned, versioned profiles and reviewed extensions.

## 1. Scope and boundaries

This bounded domain owns production-order intent and lifecycle, approved manufacturing structures and routings, planning runs and recommendations, execution records, manufacturing WIP projections, operation-level quality workflows, nonconformance/CAPA records, production genealogy, and operational inputs sent to costing. Quality may be deployed as a distinct logical context or as a closely coupled capability, but disposition authority and contracts must remain explicit. It does not own inventory balances or stock movements, purchasing commitments, supplier master data, worker master/time payroll, fixed-asset maintenance records, general-ledger posting, or shared identity and localization services.

No default dictates make-versus-buy, lot/serial capture, inspection sampling, acceptance limits, scrap accounting, overproduction, retention, approval threshold, or local compliance. Customers configure these controls by item, site, process, supplier, entity, and effective interval; gaps in required policy are surfaced and block dependent actions rather than being guessed. GS1 traceability guidance is a voluntary interoperability reference for recording transformations and sharing event/data concepts; it is not imposed as a certification or law. \[4]

## 2. Platform baseline and architecture

Use ASP.NET Core on .NET 11 as the verified reference baseline for 2026-11-22. Microsoft lists .NET 11 as active STS, released 2026-11-10, with end of support 2028-11-14; supported deployments must stay current on released patches. .NET 10 LTS is an alternative when the approved support-track policy prioritizes LTS. Reconfirm runtime, patch, OS, and hosting support before build freeze and production release. \[1]

PostgreSQL is selected as the transactional system of record. PostgreSQL major 19 was listed as supported, released 2026-11-19, for the reference date, but remains a candidate pending provider, extension, driver, backup/replication, and upgrade qualification. PostgreSQL major releases are supported for five years and the project recommends the current minor; pin the qualified major/minor at release. \[2]

Use a lightweight Next.js App Router frontend as a presentation layer for planner and shop-floor workflows. The App Router is documented as filesystem routing using React Server Components, Suspense, and Server Functions; the exact Next.js and Node versions remain release-gated. The frontend must not own authoritative business rules or bypass ASP.NET Core authorization. \[3] \[5]

Keep manufacturing, inventory, procurement, finance, people, assets, and platform as logical bounded contexts even in a modular monolith. Use versioned APIs/events and authorized commands rather than direct cross-module table writes. Changes that need external side effects use transactional outbox/inbox, stable IDs, idempotency, bounded retries, and reconciliation. Store canonical IDs, units, quantities, times, and codes independently from translated labels.

## 3. Actors and segregation

Actors include product/item and process engineers; BOM/recipe and routing stewards; production planners and schedulers; order releasers; shop-floor operators and supervisors; machine/IoT service identities; inventory controllers; subcontract coordinators; quality plan authors, inspectors, nonconformance investigators, CAPA owners, and disposition approvers; maintenance planners; cost accountants; integration operators; tenant/site administrators; and auditors. These roles are independently scoped by tenant, legal entity, site, work center, item, operation, and action.

Authentication does not grant authority. Server-side resource authorization applies to reads, commands, exports, background jobs, and event replay. Configuration authoring, approval, order release, production reporting, quality disposition, scrap approval, subcontract reconciliation, costing setup, close, and audit access are separable permissions. Maker-checker or role incompatibility policies are tenant-configurable for high-impact decisions; emergency access is time-bounded, reason-coded, and reviewed.

## 4. Core entities and invariants

Core entities include Tenant, LegalEntity, Site/Plant, Item reference, Unit and Conversion Revision, Manufacturing Policy Profile, BOM/Recipe and Revision, Engineering Change, Routing and Revision, Operation, Work Center/Resource, Calendar and Capability, Demand Peg, Production Order/Line, Plan Run and Snapshot, Planned Supply Recommendation, Schedule Scenario, Execution Packet, Operation Event, Material Issue Reference, Labor Entry, Machine Event, Downtime Event, WIP Projection, Subcontract Operation/Custody Reference, Quality Plan/Revision, Inspection and Result, Quality Hold/Disposition, Nonconformance, CAPA, Genealogy Transformation, Scrap/Rework Record, Cost Handoff, Audit Event, and Outbox Message.

Business identifiers are immutable and separate from human-readable numbers and translated labels. Approved BOM/recipe, route, quality-plan, policy, and schedule versions are immutable; transactions record the versions they used. Posted or accepted execution, inventory, quality, genealogy, and costing facts are not silently overwritten. Corrections link to originals and emit compensating events. WIP and planning displays are projections with source watermarks, not substitute ledgers.

## 5. Main workflows

Engineering authors a BOM/recipe, route, quality plan, and effective-dated change; the applicable stewards validate, assess open-order impact, approve, and publish a revision. Planning snapshots demand, eligible supply, calendars, resource availability, and approved structures; MRP generates pegged requirements, action messages, and typed supply recommendations. A finite-capacity schedule books feasible resource intervals; an infinite-capacity plan remains clearly non-executable.

An authorized user releases an order only after applicable configuration and policy checks pass. Operators receive a versioned execution packet, report operation events, request inventory-owned issues/returns, capture labor and machine facts, and record output, scrap, WIP transfer, and exceptions. Manufacturing retains accepted movement IDs and reconciles late or unknown outcomes before retry. Subcontract steps link procurement supplier commitments and inventory-owned custody to supplier receipt and quality disposition.

Quality plans govern configured inspections. Failed or unevaluable results can place scoped stock/WIP on hold; authorized quality disposition controls release, return, rework, scrap, or another configured outcome. Nonconformance investigation and CAPA follow configured review and effectiveness checks. Genealogy links source lots/serials to output through transformation events. On order close, manufacturing reconciles quantities and publishes versioned operational cost inputs; Finance alone applies costing policy and posts the ledger.

## 6. Integration contracts

- **Inventory:** Manufacturing sends demand, reservation, issue, return, WIP transfer, scrap/disposal, and lot/serial requests; Inventory alone accepts and posts stock movements, custody, holds affecting stock availability, and balance changes. Manufacturing consumes accepted movement references and reconciles unknown outcomes. See \[Chapter 04 — Inventory](04-inventory.md).
- **Procurement:** Procurement owns purchase/service commitments and supplier master. Manufacturing supplies planned purchase/subcontract recommendations and order-operation context; Procurement returns commitment, dispatch, and supplier receipt references. A subcontract operation does not itself establish supplier payment or ownership. See \[Chapter 02 — Procurement](02-procurement.md).
- **Finance:** Manufacturing publishes attributable cost inputs and actuals with currency, entity, dimensions, source-event references, profile version, and effective time. Finance owns cost policy, period controls, journal creation, and general-ledger posting; acknowledgements or rejections return by idempotent handoff ID. See \[Chapter 01 — Finance](01-finance.md).
- **People/workforce:** Worker IDs, employment status, and payroll authority are externally owned. Approved manufacturing time entries may be submitted through a governed labor/time contract; production reporting is not itself payroll approval. See \[Chapter 06 — People](06-people.md).
- **Assets/maintenance:** Asset maintenance remains owned by the asset/maintenance context. Manufacturing consumes resource availability/outage events and exposes schedule-impact requests with idempotent source IDs. See \[Chapter 07 — Assets](07-assets.md).
- **Platform and integrations:** Platform supplies tenant/entity membership, authorization, stable master references, workflow, locale/time-zone context, and audit services. All APIs/events include tenant scope, schema version, event/message ID, correlation/causation IDs, actor/service identity, canonical timestamps, explicit units, and idempotency semantics where required. Unknown codes or schema versions are quarantined and observable, not guessed.

## 7. Risks and policy boundaries

Key risks include double issue on retries, over-allocation under concurrency, stale MRP inputs, infeasible schedules presented as executable, incorrect engineering effectivity, missing genealogy links, unapproved substitutions, uncontained quality holds, unauthorized self-approval, locale-corrupted numeric input, late subcontract evidence, cost handoff drift, and cross-tenant exposure through exports or replay. Controls include database-enforced invariants, immutable revision/snapshot IDs, source watermarks, explicit schedule mode, idempotent contracts, linked corrections, quality/role segregation, reconciliation queues, adversarial access tests, and audit review.

No jurisdiction- or industry-specific FDA, eCFR, ISO, or other regulatory requirement is asserted here. Where a customer requires such controls, it must identify the applicable authoritative source, version, scope, interpretation owner, and validation evidence in a governed profile or extension. GS1 is cited only as an optional interoperability vocabulary for traceability events and identifiers. \[4]

## 8. Requirements

The following 70 requirements are normative and distinct. Acceptance criteria are intended to be objectively testable. The machine-readable counterpart is 05-manufacturing.json.

### A. Manufacturing foundation and master data

### ERP-MFG-001 — Manufacturing context and tenant scope

**Shall:** The manufacturing context shall scope every manufacturing record to its owning tenant and, where relevant, legal entity, site, plant, and production area.

**Rationale:** Explicit scope prevents cross-company planning and makes ownership and integration boundaries testable.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Every production order, plan run, quality record, and costing handoff resolves to one tenant and its configured site/entity scope.
- A user lacking site scope receives a denied response when querying or mutating that site.
- The same business code may be reused only where its configured uniqueness scope permits.

**Edge case:** A shared physical site used by multiple entities retains separate ownership and authorization scope.

**Security and audit:** Server-side resource authorization is mandatory; tenant and site predicates are included in audit and integration envelopes.

**Localization:** Names and descriptions may be translated; tenant, entity, site, item, and order IDs remain locale-neutral.

**Verification:** API authorization tests, tenant-isolation tests, and persistence constraint tests.

### ERP-MFG-002 — Manufacturing master-data references

**Shall:** The system shall reference centrally owned items, units of measure, sites, warehouses, work centers, calendars, and workers by stable platform identifiers without becoming their competing master.

**Rationale:** Common identifiers enable coherent inventory, procurement, people, and operations contracts.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Each reference stores the source-system ID and validated lifecycle state.
- Retirement of a referenced object blocks new use but preserves historical order and event references.
- Unit conversions used by a production transaction are recorded with the conversion revision.

**Edge case:** A source master is unavailable or retired during import; the record is quarantined rather than mapped by description.

**Security and audit:** Import and mapping administration are separately permissioned and all mappings are auditable.

**Localization:** Human-readable labels are localized from the owning master; IDs and codes are not translated.

**Verification:** Contract tests against platform, inventory, procurement, and workforce reference fixtures.

### ERP-MFG-003 — Manufacturing policy profiles

**Shall:** The system shall resolve planning, execution, quality, traceability, and posting behavior from explicitly versioned tenant/site/item policy profiles rather than hidden global defaults.

**Rationale:** Profiles allow configurable software without asserting universal operating or regulatory rules.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Each active profile has owner, scope, version, effective interval, and change history.
- An operation resolves and persists the profile version it used.
- Missing mandatory profile data blocks the dependent transaction with a stable error code.

**Edge case:** Profile versions overlap or leave a gap at a transaction effective time; validation rejects publication.

**Security and audit:** Only designated configuration stewards can publish profiles; maker-checker is configurable and recorded.

**Localization:** Profile labels, guidance, and error text are translated; machine codes and policy values are canonical.

**Verification:** Profile lifecycle and effective-date unit tests plus authorization/audit review.

### ERP-MFG-004 — Manufacturing identifier and numbering policy

**Shall:** The system shall assign stable internal IDs to manufacturing objects and apply configurable human-readable numbering schemes by tenant, entity, site, object type, and effective date.

**Rationale:** Numbering needs vary and must not become a hidden legal or cross-entity assumption.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- The generated ID is immutable when display number or description changes.
- Configured uniqueness scope is concurrency-safe under parallel creation.
- A disabled or exhausted sequence fails without silently reusing an issued number.

**Edge case:** Offline devices create provisional references; reconciliation preserves their local reference and links one authoritative server ID.

**Security and audit:** Sequence configuration and manual overrides require scoped permission; issued numbers and actor are audited.

**Localization:** Human-readable prefixes may vary by locale/profile, but IDs and event keys do not.

**Verification:** Concurrent sequence stress test and audit inspection.

### ERP-MFG-005 — Manufacturing quantity and unit precision

**Shall:** The system shall store production quantities using item-compatible units and explicit decimal precision, conversion revision, and rounding policy for each transaction.

**Rationale:** Canonical quantity handling avoids locale parsing errors and uncontrolled yield or consumption variance.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- API payloads accept invariant decimal representations and explicit unit codes.
- A transaction outside configured precision or conversion validity is rejected or handled by an explicitly configured rounding rule.
- Entered and normalized quantities remain available for audit.

**Edge case:** Variable-measure output differs from nominal conversion; actual measurement is retained and not replaced by a fixed factor.

**Security and audit:** Only authorized stewards change UOM/precision policy; posted event quantities are immutable.

**Localization:** Numeric entry follows the user locale in UI while canonical API values remain locale-neutral.

**Verification:** Boundary tests for precision, conversions, rounding, and non-Western numeric input.

### ERP-MFG-006 — Manufacturing audit and event envelope

**Shall:** The system shall record auditable state transitions and publish manufacturing events through a versioned, idempotent outbox contract carrying tenant/entity scope, event ID, correlation ID, actor/service, and effective and recorded timestamps.

**Rationale:** Durable provenance and retry-safe contracts are required for cross-module manufacturing workflows.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- A committed state change and its outbox event persist atomically.
- Replaying the same event ID does not duplicate the consumer-side effect.
- Event schema version and correlation ID are present in every published event.

**Edge case:** An external consumer is unavailable after local commit; the manufacturing transaction remains committed and delivery is retried/reconciled.

**Security and audit:** Event replay, payload export, and dead-letter resolution require explicit permission and are audited.

**Localization:** Event codes are stable and locale-neutral; localized text is not used as an integration key.

**Verification:** Outbox/inbox integration test with duplicate delivery and downstream outage.

### B. Production orders

### ERP-MFG-007 — Production order lifecycle

**Shall:** The system shall manage production orders through configured states including draft, planned, released, in-process, completed, closed, and cancelled, with guarded transitions.

**Rationale:** Explicit lifecycle states prevent planning records from being mistaken for authorized shop-floor work.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Transition table identifies eligible commands and required fields per state.
- Invalid transitions return a stable reason code and leave the order unchanged.
- Every successful transition records actor, time, source version, and reason where required.

**Edge case:** An order is cancelled after execution postings exist; cancellation requires a controlled close/reversal path rather than deletion.

**Security and audit:** Create, release, cancel, complete, and close permissions are separable; self-approval rules can be configured.

**Localization:** State codes remain locale-neutral; labels and transition explanations are localized.

**Verification:** State-machine unit and API authorization tests.

### ERP-MFG-008 — Production order demand and quantity

**Shall:** The system shall store an order’s demanded quantity, planned quantity, released quantity, completed quantity, and remaining quantity as distinct values with explicit units.

**Rationale:** Separate quantities support partial runs, yield reporting, and demand reconciliation.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Order quantity ledger exposes the five values and their units.
- Completed quantity cannot exceed permitted overproduction tolerance without an authorized override.
- Order quantity amendments after release create a versioned change record.

**Edge case:** Demand is withdrawn while a batch is partly complete; remaining quantity is flagged for disposition and demand re-pegging.

**Security and audit:** Quantity overrides are permissioned and record original/new values and reason.

**Localization:** Quantities render using user locale and unit labels while stored values retain invariant precision.

**Verification:** API and UI tests for partial completion, overrun, and post-release change.

### ERP-MFG-009 — Production order source and pegging

**Shall:** The system shall retain one or more demand-source references and pegging quantities for each order or order line when the order is demand-driven.

**Rationale:** Pegging preserves the relationship between independent demand and planned or executed supply.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Demand source type, stable source ID, line ID, required date, and pegged quantity are queryable.
- Aggregated pegging quantities reconcile to the linked order quantity within the configured unit conversion.
- Unpegged make-to-stock orders are explicitly marked as such.

**Edge case:** A single production order fulfills multiple demands; each split is independently traceable and amendable.

**Security and audit:** Users may view only authorized source demand; event payloads do not expose unrelated customer data.

**Localization:** Customer-facing descriptions are localized only at presentation; stable source references remain unchanged.

**Verification:** Integration test linking, splitting, and unpegging demand.

### ERP-MFG-010 — Order release readiness gate

**Shall:** The system shall validate configured release prerequisites before production order release, including effective BOM/recipe, route, material availability policy, quality prerequisites, and required approvals.

**Rationale:** Release validation prevents execution against incomplete or superseded instructions.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Validation returns a machine-readable list of failed prerequisites.
- A passing order stores the exact BOM, route, and policy revisions used at release.
- A configured approval must be satisfied before the release command succeeds.

**Edge case:** A prerequisite changes between validation and release; optimistic concurrency or revalidation prevents a stale release.

**Security and audit:** Release approver identity and evidence are immutable and distinct from configuration edits.

**Localization:** Prerequisite messages are localized while codes and referenced revisions are stable.

**Verification:** Race-condition test for validation/release plus approval workflow tests.

### ERP-MFG-011 — Production order split and merge

**Shall:** The system shall support controlled splitting and merging of eligible production orders while preserving source demand, quantities, configuration revisions, and genealogy references.

**Rationale:** Splitting supports capacity and batch constraints without losing the parent demand trail.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Split quantities sum to the source remaining quantity or a recorded variance.
- A merge is rejected when orders have incompatible item, site, effective BOM/route, ownership, or quality controls.
- Parent-child links remain queryable after closure.

**Edge case:** An order already has material or labor postings; only unexecuted quantity may be split unless a configured correction flow is invoked.

**Security and audit:** Splitting, merging, and quantity adjustments require dedicated rights and audit records.

**Localization:** Localized labels do not alter stable parent-child keys.

**Verification:** Property-based quantity conservation and incompatible-merge tests.

### ERP-MFG-012 — Production order document snapshot

**Shall:** The system shall provide an immutable, versioned execution packet for each released order containing applicable product, BOM/recipe, route, instructions, and control-plan references.

**Rationale:** Operators need consistent instructions even when future revisions are published.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Execution packet is bound to a release revision and can be retrieved for every released order.
- Subsequent master-data edits do not alter the released packet.
- A controlled superseding packet records prior and new versions and approval.

**Edge case:** An instruction attachment becomes unavailable; order release is blocked or a protected immutable copy is retained per tenant policy.

**Security and audit:** Document retrieval follows order and attachment scope; downloads are logged where configured.

**Localization:** Instruction versions can include approved language editions with a designated controlling revision.

**Verification:** Snapshot immutability and authorization tests.

### ERP-MFG-013 — Production order close and residual handling

**Shall:** The system shall close an order only after configured completion checks reconcile output, consumption, scrap, WIP, subcontract receipts, and unresolved quality holds.

**Rationale:** Closeout establishes a complete operational record and a clear point for downstream costing.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Close validation lists each unreconciled quantity or hold.
- Successful close freezes further routine reporting and emits a versioned close event.
- Authorized reopen creates a linked audit event and does not erase the prior close.

**Edge case:** Late external labor or supplier confirmation arrives after close; it is routed to an approved adjustment or reopen path.

**Security and audit:** Close/reopen permissions are separate from routine execution; close evidence is retained.

**Localization:** Close status is locale-neutral and report labels are translated.

**Verification:** Close-gate integration tests for each outstanding quantity/status.

### C. BOMs, recipes, and engineering change

### ERP-MFG-014 — BOM and recipe revision control

**Shall:** The system shall manage bills of material and process recipes as immutable approved revisions with explicit status, owner, effective interval, and input/output item references.

**Rationale:** Revision control makes production instructions reproducible over time.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- An approved revision cannot be overwritten; changes create a successor revision.
- Effective selection returns exactly one applicable revision or a validation error.
- Released orders persist the selected revision ID.

**Edge case:** A date falls into overlapping or missing revision intervals; activation is rejected or selection is blocked.

**Security and audit:** Author, reviewer, and approver roles are separable; publication records before/after and approvals.

**Localization:** Names/instructions may be translated per revision; recipe codes and item IDs are canonical.

**Verification:** Revision lifecycle and interval-overlap tests.

### ERP-MFG-015 — BOM component requirements

**Shall:** The system shall model BOM/recipe lines with component item, planned quantity, unit, operation association where applicable, issue policy, and effective revision.

**Rationale:** Typed component lines support material planning and execution without ambiguous free-text consumption.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Each active line resolves to an item and compatible unit conversion.
- Requirement calculation records basis quantity, component quantity, and selected conversion revision.
- Optional, variable, and fixed-quantity line behavior is explicitly identified.

**Edge case:** A component is discontinued after an order release; existing orders retain the released revision and new planning raises an exception.

**Security and audit:** Only approved engineering/configuration roles may publish line revisions.

**Localization:** Instructions localize while item and unit codes remain stable.

**Verification:** BOM calculation tests for variable/fixed/optional lines.

### ERP-MFG-016 — Alternate and substitute materials

**Shall:** The system shall allow explicitly approved alternate or substitute components with item eligibility, priority, quantity conversion, approval scope, and effective dates.

**Rationale:** Governed substitution handles supply disruption without silently changing product definition.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- An unapproved substitute is rejected at reservation/issue.
- Substitution records requested component, actual component, approval reference, and quantity conversion.
- Effective/expired alternatives are excluded from new execution.

**Edge case:** An emergency substitution is needed while approver connectivity is unavailable; configured emergency authorization captures later review without hiding the deviation.

**Security and audit:** Substitution approval and material issue may require separate roles; exceptions are audited.

**Localization:** Alternate names are localized, but approval codes and item identities are not.

**Verification:** Positive/negative authorization tests and effective-date boundary tests.

### ERP-MFG-017 — By-products, co-products, and yield

**Shall:** The system shall represent configured co-products, by-products, and expected yield/loss factors separately from primary output and actual production results.

**Rationale:** Explicit output modeling supports multi-output processes and measurable yield reconciliation.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Order output lines distinguish primary, co-product, by-product, and expected loss.
- Actual quantity and unit are captured for each reportable output.
- Configured yield variance thresholds raise a review status without changing quantities automatically.

**Edge case:** Actual output is zero or greater than input due to a process conversion; transaction requires a configured explanation or measurement model.

**Security and audit:** Yield policy changes are approved, versioned, and cannot rewrite posted actuals.

**Localization:** Yield explanations are localized; quantities and type codes stay canonical.

**Verification:** Calculation tests for multi-output and yield variance.

### ERP-MFG-018 — Phantom and non-stock components

**Shall:** The system shall support explicitly typed phantom or non-stock BOM lines and expand phantom subassemblies according to a versioned planning/execution policy.

**Rationale:** This supports kit planning without confusing structure-only items with inventory-backed components.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Explosion output identifies each expanded source line and effective revision.
- A non-stock line does not create an inventory reservation or issue.
- Cycles in a BOM graph are rejected with the offending path.

**Edge case:** A phantom child has a separately planned operation or is not valid on the selected site; explosion reports the unsupported line.

**Security and audit:** Only authorized engineering users alter structure and expansion policies.

**Localization:** Display labels localize, but expansion order and component IDs do not depend on locale.

**Verification:** Graph-cycle and reservation-generation tests.

### ERP-MFG-019 — Operation-linked material consumption

**Shall:** The system shall associate component consumption with a production order operation or an explicitly designated order-level issue point.

**Rationale:** Operation linkage supports staged material availability and consumption traceability.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Every posted material issue has an operation/order link or an explicit order-level marker.
- Materials assigned to a later operation are not presented as required at an earlier point unless policy says so.
- The issue record retains planned and actual quantities.

**Edge case:** Component is consumed at a different operation than planned; actual event is accepted only through a variance reason path.

**Security and audit:** Issue and variance permissions are scoped to site and operation; issue reversals retain original linkage.

**Localization:** Operator UI localizes work instructions and unit formatting without translating canonical operation IDs.

**Verification:** Shop-floor tests for planned and deviated operation issues.

### ERP-MFG-020 — Effective-dated manufacturing engineering change

**Shall:** The system shall manage engineering changes to BOMs, recipes, routes, and control plans through approved changes with effectivity by date, serial/lot range, or explicit order boundary.

**Rationale:** Controlled effectivity avoids applying new instructions to already committed or in-process work without authorization.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- A change record contains affected objects, reason, approval, effective rule, and predecessor revision.
- Selection tests resolve the applicable revision at specified date/serial/order boundaries.
- Open-order impact is listed before publication.

**Edge case:** Calendar-time and serial-range effectivity conflict; the system flags ambiguous selection instead of choosing silently.

**Security and audit:** Engineering change approval is separated from authoring where configured; impact report access is scoped.

**Localization:** Change description and operator notice are localized; effectivity keys are canonical.

**Verification:** Boundary matrix tests over open/released orders and overlapping effectivity.

### ERP-MFG-021 — Manufacturing change impact assessment

**Shall:** The system shall calculate and retain the impact set of an engineering change across planned and released orders, material reservations, supplier commitments, inspections, and costing setup.

**Rationale:** Change owners need an actionable, reproducible view of affected execution and dependent commitments.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Impact output lists object ID, prior/new revision, state, and required action.
- Re-running against unchanged source versions yields the same set and version hash.
- Publication records acknowledgement or disposition of every configured mandatory impact category.

**Edge case:** A downstream system is temporarily unavailable; impact is marked incomplete and publication follows configurable block/approval policy.

**Security and audit:** Impact export is permissioned and audit logged; supplier/customer-sensitive fields are minimized.

**Localization:** Impact notices are localized; object identifiers and version hashes remain invariant.

**Verification:** Changed-source replay and incomplete-impact policy tests.

### ERP-MFG-022 — BOM/recipe effectivity and order snapshot

**Shall:** The system shall resolve and persist effective BOM/recipe revisions at planning and again at order release, recording any authorized difference between those points.

**Rationale:** This makes planned supply explainable and executed consumption reproducible.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- MRP output records the revision and effective date used.
- Order release records its selected revision separately from planning revision.
- Revision change between plan and release produces a visible delta list.

**Edge case:** An order crosses an effective boundary during execution; its original revision remains unless an approved changeover is recorded.

**Security and audit:** Override of the selected revision requires permission and reason; audit stores both revision identifiers.

**Localization:** Localized revision labels do not affect revision matching.

**Verification:** Plan-to-release effective-date transition tests.

### ERP-MFG-023 — Recipe parameter and batch scaling

**Shall:** The system shall define recipe-specific process parameters and scaling formulas with typed units, valid ranges, scaling basis, and revision provenance, separately from component quantity lines.

**Rationale:** Process targets may scale or vary independently from material quantities and must be executable and auditable.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Each parameter declares data type, unit or category, allowed range, scaling basis, and effective recipe revision.
- Batch scaling records input batch size, formula revision, and calculated parameter values.
- Out-of-range values prevent release or require an explicitly configured approval path.

**Edge case:** A parameter is manually overridden for a particular batch; both calculated and actual values remain available with a reason.

**Security and audit:** Recipe parameter authoring and batch override approval are permissioned separately; revisions and actual-value changes are audited.

**Localization:** Parameter labels and instructions support translation; machine keys, units, and values remain canonical.

**Verification:** Formula determinism, range validation, and approved-override tests.

### D. Routing, capacity, and scheduling

### ERP-MFG-024 — Routing revision and operation sequence

**Shall:** The system shall define an approved, versioned routing of ordered operations with operation IDs, precedence rules, expected durations, and required resource capabilities.

**Rationale:** Explicit operation sequence supports scheduling and execution control.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- A routing contains unique operation IDs and a valid precedence graph.
- Cycles and references to inactive capabilities are rejected at approval.
- Released orders retain the routing revision and operation sequence.

**Edge case:** An operation may run in parallel with another; an explicit dependency graph represents this rather than relying on display order.

**Security and audit:** Routing approval and shop-floor edit rights are distinct and recorded.

**Localization:** Operation instructions may be translated; operation IDs and precedence remain invariant.

**Verification:** Routing graph validation and execution packet test.

### ERP-MFG-025 — Work center and resource capability

**Shall:** The system shall model work centers and finite-capacity resources with capability tags, site scope, availability state, and effective-dated calendars.

**Rationale:** Scheduling requires explicit resource eligibility and availability inputs.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- An operation is assignable only to a resource with the required capabilities and active scope.
- Unavailable resources are excluded for intervals marked unavailable.
- Capability and calendar revisions used by a schedule are persisted.

**Edge case:** A resource is shared across sites or has an emergency outage; scope and outage window are explicit rather than inferred.

**Security and audit:** Resource availability changes require authorized roles and retain actor, interval, and reason.

**Localization:** Resource names localize; capability codes and timestamps remain canonical.

**Verification:** Eligibility and outage-interval test suite.

### ERP-MFG-026 — Operation time model

**Shall:** The system shall store setup, run, queue, move, wait, and teardown duration assumptions as typed operation parameters with units and scaling basis.

**Rationale:** Typed time assumptions enable consistent load estimation without conflating elapsed and labor time.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Each enabled duration identifies unit, fixed/per-lot/per-unit basis, and revision.
- Duration calculation outputs its inputs and computed value.
- Zero or negative values are rejected except for explicitly permitted zero-duration operations.

**Edge case:** Batch size exceeds a configured maximum; the operation is split into capacity-feasible segments or flagged for review.

**Security and audit:** Only planners or engineering stewards with permission may change standards; changes are audited.

**Localization:** Time display uses selected locale and site time zone; stored durations are unit-coded.

**Verification:** Duration formula and boundary-value tests.

### ERP-MFG-027 — Finite-capacity scheduling mode

**Shall:** The system shall support a finite-capacity schedule mode that places operations only in eligible resource intervals within configured capacity and calendars.

**Rationale:** Finite scheduling provides a feasible sequence under selected resource constraints.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- A schedule run records planning horizon, resource calendar revision, and scheduling algorithm/configuration version.
- No scheduled operation exceeds available resource capacity or overlaps an exclusive resource booking.
- Unscheduled operations include a reason code.

**Edge case:** No feasible interval exists within the horizon; the operation remains unscheduled and is not silently placed beyond capacity.

**Security and audit:** Schedule publication and manual overrides have separate permissions and audit trails.

**Localization:** Schedule dates render in site time zone; canonical instants and time-zone ID are preserved.

**Verification:** Constraint solver tests with oversubscribed resources and daylight-saving transitions.

### ERP-MFG-028 — Infinite-capacity planning mode

**Shall:** The system shall support an explicitly labeled infinite-capacity planning mode that calculates dates without asserting resource feasibility.

**Rationale:** Rough-cut planning can be useful for demand scenarios but must not be mistaken for an executable schedule.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Every output and export identifies capacity mode as infinite.
- Capacity overload indicators show demand load versus configured capacity.
- Release gate rejects an infinite-capacity plan when tenant policy requires finite scheduling.

**Edge case:** A user opens a rough-cut plan from a dispatch screen; the UI displays a persistent non-executable status.

**Security and audit:** Only planning roles can publish the infinite-capacity scenario; it cannot authorize shop-floor release by itself.

**Localization:** Labels and explanatory text are localized; identifiers, codes, canonical quantities, and timestamps remain locale-neutral.

**Verification:** Capacity-mode labeling and release policy tests.

### ERP-MFG-029 — Schedule scenario, freeze, and reschedule

**Shall:** The system shall support named schedule scenarios and a configurable frozen interval, preserving prior published schedules when a new scenario is calculated.

**Rationale:** Scenario comparison and frozen work prevent exploratory rescheduling from mutating active commitments.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Scenario records source plan, assumptions, and computed result version.
- Publishing a new schedule requires an explicit compare-and-promote action.
- Frozen operations remain unchanged unless a permitted override records reason and approver.

**Edge case:** Unexpected outage invalidates frozen work; an authorized exception can override only affected operations and records a recovery plan.
