**Security and audit:** Override and promote rights are separately assigned; all changes are diffable and audited.

**Localization:** Labels and explanatory text are localized; identifiers, codes, canonical quantities, and timestamps remain locale-neutral.

**Verification:** Scenario isolation, freeze-window, and promotion tests.

### ERP-MFG-030 — Finite schedule resource conflicts

**Shall:** The system shall detect resource and labor-calendar conflicts before publishing a finite schedule and shall report all conflicting order-operation pairs.

**Rationale:** Conflict visibility makes schedule publication operationally reviewable.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Conflict report identifies resource, interval, both operations, and constraint type.
- A schedule with hard conflicts cannot publish unless an explicit configured override is approved.
- Soft preference violations are distinguished from hard constraints.

**Edge case:** An operation uses a shared alternate resource; the conflict check evaluates its actual assigned resource and capability.

**Security and audit:** Conflict overrides require a reason and approver where configured; report access follows site scope.

**Localization:** Labels and explanatory text are localized; identifiers, codes, canonical quantities, and timestamps remain locale-neutral.

**Verification:** Conflict injection and override tests.

### ERP-MFG-031 — Dispatch list and schedule adherence

**Shall:** The system shall provide a versioned dispatch list ordered by the active schedule and show status, prerequisites, queue priority, and schedule deviation for each operation.

**Rationale:** Operators need a clear, current execution queue and planners need adherence feedback.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Dispatch list identifies active schedule version and refresh timestamp.
- Items with blocked material or quality prerequisites are visibly non-dispatchable.
- Late/early status derives from configured tolerance and site time zone.

**Edge case:** An offline workstation has a stale dispatch snapshot; it must display snapshot time and reject prohibited stale actions.

**Security and audit:** Work center users see only authorized operations; dispatch exports are audited.

**Localization:** Labels and explanatory text are localized; identifiers, codes, canonical quantities, and timestamps remain locale-neutral.

**Verification:** Role-based dispatch UI test with stale data and blocker cases.

### ERP-MFG-032 — Capacity load and utilization view

**Shall:** The system shall calculate planned resource load and configured capacity by time bucket and expose the utilization assumptions used.

**Rationale:** Planners need explainable load views rather than opaque utilization percentages.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Load reports disclose bucket size, shift/calendar version, duration basis, and excluded work.
- Load equals the sum of included scheduled/planned durations within stated rounding tolerance.
- Filters preserve tenant and site scope.

**Edge case:** Unassigned or unscheduled operations are shown separately and not counted as zero-load completed work.

**Security and audit:** Reports enforce row-level site permissions and log sensitive exports.

**Localization:** Labels and explanatory text are localized; identifiers, codes, canonical quantities, and timestamps remain locale-neutral.

**Verification:** Reconciliation calculation test against known operation samples.

### E. Material requirements planning

### ERP-MFG-033 — MRP run inputs and immutable run record

**Shall:** The system shall create an immutable material requirements planning run record capturing demand snapshot, supply snapshot, BOM/recipe revisions, planning parameters, and horizon.

**Rationale:** Reproducible inputs allow planners to explain action messages and compare runs.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Run stores cutoff timestamps and source snapshot identifiers.
- Rerunning with the same snapshots and parameters yields identical planned requirement values within declared deterministic precision.
- A run in progress or failed state is distinguishable from completed output.

**Edge case:** Upstream data changes during extraction; snapshot boundaries prevent mixing versions or mark the run inconsistent.

**Security and audit:** Only authorized planners can create, inspect, publish, or export runs; run data remains tenant-scoped.

**Localization:** Labels and explanatory text are localized; identifiers, codes, canonical quantities, and timestamps remain locale-neutral.

**Verification:** Plan replay determinism tests and snapshot consistency tests.

### ERP-MFG-034 — MRP demand netting

**Shall:** The system shall net eligible demand against eligible on-hand, reservations, scheduled receipts, and approved supply according to a versioned policy with explicit statuses and dates.

**Rationale:** Netting must be explainable and must not treat held or unrelated inventory as available.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Each netting line shows gross demand, eligible supply categories, exclusions, and net requirement.
- Quality-held, blocked, expired, or wrong-owner stock is excluded according to profile.
- Supply quantities are not double counted across categories.

**Edge case:** A receipt or reservation changes while a plan is running; the run retains its snapshot and reports staleness relative to current data.

**Security and audit:** Netting configuration changes require approval; plan output cannot directly mutate stock.

**Localization:** Display uses locale-aware units/dates while canonical source values remain intact.

**Verification:** Golden dataset netting tests including exclusions and duplicate-supply guards.

### ERP-MFG-035 — MRP multi-level explosion

**Shall:** The system shall explode multi-level BOM/recipe requirements by selected revision, quantity, yield policy, and effective date, retaining the parent-demand path for each dependent requirement.

**Rationale:** Path-level explosion supports planned purchase and production decisions across levels.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Every dependent requirement has a traversable parent path to independent demand.
- Yield and unit conversions used at each level are stored.
- Circular BOM structures fail the run with a path-specific diagnostic.

**Edge case:** A component is both a top-level demand item and a lower-level component; independent demand and dependent requirement remain separately identifiable.

**Security and audit:** Plan output and path visibility obey item/site scope restrictions.

**Localization:** Labels and explanatory text are localized; identifiers, codes, canonical quantities, and timestamps remain locale-neutral.

**Verification:** Engine test for multi-level, shared-component, cycle, and conversion cases.

### ERP-MFG-036 — MRP lead time and calendar dates

**Shall:** The system shall calculate planned start and due dates using configured item/site lead times, operation calendars, supplier or internal supply calendars, and an explicit date convention.

**Rationale:** Planning dates must disclose assumptions and respect business calendars.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Calculated dates identify each lead-time/calendar source and version.
- Nonworking periods are handled according to selected calendar rules.
- Missing required lead-time data creates an exception rather than a zero-day assumption.

**Edge case:** A due date falls on a time-zone daylight-saving boundary or nonworking day; stored instants and selected business-date convention remain unambiguous.

**Security and audit:** Calendar maintenance is permissioned and versioned.

**Localization:** Labels and explanatory text are localized; identifiers, codes, canonical quantities, and timestamps remain locale-neutral.

**Verification:** Calendar/date boundary tests across time zones and DST transitions.

### ERP-MFG-037 — MRP planned supply recommendations

**Shall:** The system shall generate typed planned production, purchase, transfer, and reschedule recommendations without creating firm orders until an authorized conversion command is accepted.

**Rationale:** Recommendations separate planning proposals from procurement or manufacturing commitments.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Each recommendation has source plan/run, item, quantity, date, site, supply type, and action status.
- Converting a recommendation creates one linked order and is idempotent on retry.
- Rejected or deferred recommendations remain visible with reason.

**Edge case:** An item is make/buy configurable by site; ambiguous sourcing produces a planner exception instead of arbitrary selection.

**Security and audit:** Conversion permissions are distinct from planner review; every action is attributed.

**Localization:** Labels and explanatory text are localized; identifiers, codes, canonical quantities, and timestamps remain locale-neutral.

**Verification:** Conversion API tests for idempotency and source linkage.

### ERP-MFG-038 — MRP action messages and exceptions

**Shall:** The system shall create actionable messages for shortages, excesses, delays, cancellations, reschedules, and invalid planning data, with priority and recommended disposition.

**Rationale:** Planners require clear exceptions instead of having to infer problems from aggregate output.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Each message references affected plan line and source facts.
- Message status supports open, acknowledged, resolved, and dismissed with reason.
- Resolution records user, timestamp, and linked corrective action when one exists.

**Edge case:** A shortage is caused by a held lot; the action message links the specific eligibility reason without exposing unauthorized supplier details.

**Security and audit:** Message acknowledgement and dismissal are audited; scope follows site and item permissions.

**Localization:** Labels and explanatory text are localized; identifiers, codes, canonical quantities, and timestamps remain locale-neutral.

**Verification:** Exception lifecycle and permission tests.

### ERP-MFG-039 — MRP planning fences and order modifiers

**Shall:** The system shall apply configurable planning time fences, order modifiers, minimum/maximum quantities, multiples, and rounding rules per item/site profile.

**Rationale:** Planning parameters vary by operation and are made explicit rather than hardcoded.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Run output identifies each applied modifier and resulting quantity.
- Values outside configured ranges are rejected during profile publication.
- A disabled modifier has no effect on the calculated planned quantity.

**Edge case:** A modifier produces supply beyond remaining demand; excess is surfaced with reason and never silently discarded.

**Security and audit:** Parameter changes are reviewed, versioned, and audited.

**Localization:** Labels and explanatory text are localized; identifiers, codes, canonical quantities, and timestamps remain locale-neutral.

**Verification:** Boundary/property tests across minimums, multiples, fences, and maxima.

### ERP-MFG-040 — MRP plan publication and stale-source control

**Shall:** The system shall require planners to review source freshness and material exceptions before publishing a plan for downstream conversion.

**Rationale:** A calculated run can become stale and must not silently drive supply commitments.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Publication records reviewer, snapshot IDs, and exception disposition.
- If configured critical sources have changed beyond tolerance, publication is blocked or requires explicit override.
- Published plan events are idempotent and carry the run ID.

**Edge case:** One source adapter is unreachable; the run is marked incomplete and publication follows a configured block/approval rule.

**Security and audit:** Publish, override, and downstream conversion are separately permissioned and audited.

**Localization:** Labels and explanatory text are localized; identifiers, codes, canonical quantities, and timestamps remain locale-neutral.

**Verification:** Changed-source and upstream-outage publication tests.

### F. Shop-floor execution, labor, machine data, and WIP

### ERP-MFG-041 — Shop-floor operation start and completion

**Shall:** The system shall record operation start, pause, resume, partial completion, and completion against a released order with operator, resource, timestamps, and quantity where applicable.

**Rationale:** Execution events create an attributable operational record and support partial processing.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Start requires a released, dispatchable operation.
- Completion cannot exceed remaining quantity beyond configured tolerance.
- Pause/resume produces separate events and preserves elapsed and reported time.

**Edge case:** Network loss occurs after a scan; client retry with same idempotency key produces one operation event.

**Security and audit:** Operators may report only assigned or authorized resources; supervisor corrections are distinct and audited.

**Localization:** Labels and explanatory text are localized; identifiers, codes, canonical quantities, and timestamps remain locale-neutral.

**Verification:** API/UI state tests including duplicate submissions and partial completions.

### ERP-MFG-042 — Shop-floor material issue and return

**Shall:** The system shall request material issue and return through inventory-owned commands and record the accepted inventory movement reference against the manufacturing order/operation.

**Rationale:** Inventory owns physical stock movements; Manufacturing owns consumption context.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Issue command contains item, quantity, unit, order, operation, and requested lot/serial where controlled.
- Manufacturing status updates only after receiving an accepted movement reference.
- Return quantity links to the originating issue and cannot exceed its remaining returnable amount unless policy allows an adjustment.

**Edge case:** Inventory returns unknown/timeout outcome; Manufacturing retains pending status and reconciles before resubmitting a new movement.

**Security and audit:** Issue/return roles are scoped; cost or quantity override requires elevated permission.

**Localization:** Labels and explanatory text are localized; identifiers, codes, canonical quantities, and timestamps remain locale-neutral.

**Verification:** Contract tests for accepted/rejected/unknown responses and duplicate callbacks.

### ERP-MFG-043 — Backflush consumption

**Shall:** The system shall support backflush consumption only when enabled by the item/site/order profile, calculate it from reported output and approved BOM revision, and submit the result to Inventory for posting.

**Rationale:** Backflush can reduce transaction effort but requires controlled calculation and explicit inventory posting.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Backflush output shows calculated components, basis quantity, yield/rounding rule, and revision before commit.
- Posted issue events link to completion event and order operation.
- Actual or configured exceptions exceeding tolerance create a review hold.

**Edge case:** A required lot-controlled material lacks a valid lot allocation; completion does not bypass lot capture.

**Security and audit:** Backflush enablement and tolerance changes require approval; override values are audited.

**Localization:** Labels and explanatory text are localized; identifiers, codes, canonical quantities, and timestamps remain locale-neutral.

**Verification:** Calculation tests for partial output, rounding, missing lot, and retry.

### ERP-MFG-044 — Labor time reporting

**Shall:** The system shall capture labor time entries linked to worker, order, operation, resource where relevant, start/end or duration, time category, and approval state.

**Rationale:** Attributable labor facts support operational analysis and a governed finance/payroll handoff.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Overlapping entries for one worker are flagged under configured overlap policy.
- Submitted duration is recalculated or validated against timestamps and declared time zone.
- Approved entries are immutable except through a linked correction.

**Edge case:** An overnight shift crosses local midnight or DST change; elapsed duration and business-date attribution are both defined and tested.

**Security and audit:** Workers report own time; supervisors approve exceptions; payroll/finance exports are separately permissioned.

**Localization:** Labels and explanatory text are localized; identifiers, codes, canonical quantities, and timestamps remain locale-neutral.

**Verification:** Labor API tests for overlap, DST, correction, and approval.

### ERP-MFG-045 — Machine and production counter reporting

**Shall:** The system shall capture machine states and production counters from authorized manual or integrated sources, retaining raw value, normalized value, source identity, and event time.

**Rationale:** Raw-source preservation enables reconciliation between shop-floor equipment and ERP projections.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Duplicate source event IDs are ignored idempotently.
- Counter reset or rollover is flagged and does not create negative production without configured handling.
- Normalized output links to order/resource and the mapping revision.

**Edge case:** Equipment timestamp is outside allowed clock skew; event is quarantined or accepted with an explicit quality flag.

**Security and audit:** Device credentials are scoped to permitted resources; configuration and manual override are audited.

**Localization:** Labels and explanatory text are localized; identifiers, codes, canonical quantities, and timestamps remain locale-neutral.

**Verification:** Adapter contract test for duplicates, reset, clock skew, and bad mapping.

### ERP-MFG-046 — Downtime and production loss reason

**Shall:** The system shall record downtime, delay, or lost-production intervals with resource, affected order/operation if known, category code, cause, and attribution source.

**Rationale:** Structured loss events support schedule adherence and capacity feedback without presuming a universal taxonomy.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Configured reason codes are validated against effective profile.
- Overlapping intervals for the same exclusive resource are flagged.
- A correction links to the original event and preserves both records.

**Edge case:** Cause is unknown at time of reporting; provisional status and later classification are supported.

**Security and audit:** Reason-code administration and retrospective edits require permission and are audited.

**Localization:** Labels and explanatory text are localized; identifiers, codes, canonical quantities, and timestamps remain locale-neutral.

**Verification:** Interval-overlap, provisional-cause, and correction tests.

### ERP-MFG-047 — WIP quantity and status projection

**Shall:** The system shall maintain a rebuildable WIP projection by order, operation, item, quantity, unit, status, and relevant lot/serial references using accepted execution and inventory events.

**Rationale:** WIP visibility supports operational control while preserving source ownership of movements.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Projection reconciles to accepted output, issue, transfer, scrap, and completion events for a test fixture.
- Every displayed WIP balance includes an as-of watermark and source event versions.
- Projection rebuild produces the same result from an identical event set.

**Edge case:** A source event is delayed or reordered; the view discloses lag and does not overwrite a newer event with stale state.

**Security and audit:** WIP query is tenant/site scoped; trace-level details require appropriate permission.

**Localization:** Labels and explanatory text are localized; identifiers, codes, canonical quantities, and timestamps remain locale-neutral.

**Verification:** Event replay reconciliation and delayed/out-of-order delivery tests.

### ERP-MFG-048 — WIP transfer between operations

**Shall:** The system shall record controlled WIP transfer, queue, and custody changes between operations with source and destination operation, quantity, time, and status.

**Rationale:** Explicit transfer events make work location and in-process quantity visible.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Transferred quantity does not exceed the transferable open quantity.
- Source/destination operations comply with routing precedence or an approved deviation.
- The transfer event appears in order genealogy and WIP projection.

**Edge case:** WIP is split across multiple downstream operations; each transfer conserves quantity or records a reason-coded loss.

**Security and audit:** Transfer and routing-deviation rights are separately permissioned.

**Localization:** Labels and explanatory text are localized; identifiers, codes, canonical quantities, and timestamps remain locale-neutral.

**Verification:** Quantity conservation and route-deviation integration tests.

### ERP-MFG-049 — Production reporting correction

**Shall:** The system shall correct posted production, labor, downtime, and consumption reports through linked reversal or adjustment records rather than silent overwrite.

**Rationale:** Immutable corrections preserve auditability and downstream reconciliation.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Correction references original event and reason.
- Affected WIP, inventory, quality, and costing projections receive compensating events.
- Correction audit records initiator and approver where maker-checker is enabled.

**Edge case:** Correction is requested after financial period close; the configured finance period policy determines whether adjustment is deferred or escalated.

**Security and audit:** Correction and approval permissions are separated; sensitive correction exports are audited.

**Localization:** Labels and explanatory text are localized; identifiers, codes, canonical quantities, and timestamps remain locale-neutral.

**Verification:** End-to-end correction and replay tests.

### G. Subcontracting and maintenance interfaces

### ERP-MFG-050 — Subcontract operation definition

**Shall:** The system shall identify subcontracted routing operations with supplier reference, service item, expected duration, send/return milestones, and applicable quality checks.

**Rationale:** External processing needs explicit routing and supplier context without transferring procurement ownership.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Subcontract operation references a valid procurement supplier and service configuration.
- Route identifies expected dispatch and return events.
- Supplier/service data used is versioned or snapshotted at order release.

**Edge case:** Supplier is blocked or contract data is expired; the operation cannot be newly released without an authorized exception.

**Security and audit:** Supplier changes and subcontract release require appropriate procurement/manufacturing permissions.

**Localization:** Labels and explanatory text are localized; identifiers, codes, canonical quantities, and timestamps remain locale-neutral.

**Verification:** Supplier contract reference and manufacturing/procurement API integration tests.

### ERP-MFG-051 — Subcontract material custody and reconciliation

**Shall:** The system shall track materials or WIP sent to and returned from a subcontractor by order, item, quantity, lot/serial, and custody status using Inventory-owned transfer/consignment events.

**Rationale:** Custody must remain distinct from on-hand ownership and manufacturing completion.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Outbound and return transactions reference accepted inventory movement IDs.
- Open subcontract quantity reconciles sent quantity to returned, consumed, scrapped, or outstanding amounts.
- Partial returns are supported without closing the remaining balance.

**Edge case:** Supplier reports loss or additional consumption; discrepancy remains open until authorized disposition.

**Security and audit:** External portal/service identity is supplier-scoped; custody adjustments require review and are audited.

**Localization:** Labels and explanatory text are localized; identifiers, codes, canonical quantities, and timestamps remain locale-neutral.

**Verification:** Contract/reconciliation tests for partial, discrepant, and duplicate messages.

### ERP-MFG-052 — Subcontract receipt, quality, and completion

**Shall:** The system shall accept subcontract completion only after receipt status and configured quality disposition are available, then reconcile returned quantity to the open order operation.

**Rationale:** External processing cannot bypass inspection or custody reconciliation controls.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- A receipt event can be partial and retains supplier evidence reference.
- Quality-required output remains held until disposition is accepted.
- Operation completion quantity cannot exceed accepted returned quantity.

**Edge case:** Return arrives without the expected order reference; it is quarantined for resolution rather than auto-matched by item alone.

**Security and audit:** Receipt, quality disposition, and operation completion permissions remain distinguishable.

**Localization:** Labels and explanatory text are localized; identifiers, codes, canonical quantities, and timestamps remain locale-neutral.

**Verification:** Integrated receipt-quality-operation workflow test.

### ERP-MFG-053 — Maintenance availability interface

**Shall:** The system shall consume versioned maintenance availability events for manufacturing resources and expose planned maintenance requests or downtime referrals through a defined interface without owning asset maintenance records.

**Rationale:** Capacity planning depends on current equipment availability while maintenance remains the asset-system authority.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Imported event contains resource ID, status, interval, source event ID, and source revision.
- Duplicate or out-of-order maintenance messages do not duplicate or regress availability.
- Unmapped asset/resource links produce an integration exception.

**Edge case:** An emergency breakdown is reported locally before the maintenance system confirms it; temporary unavailability is time-bounded and reconciled.

**Security and audit:** Only approved service identities may alter resource availability; audit keeps source and normalization values.

**Localization:** Labels and explanatory text are localized; identifiers, codes, canonical quantities, and timestamps remain locale-neutral.

**Verification:** Interface contract tests for duplicate, stale, and unmapped events.

### ERP-MFG-054 — Maintenance-to-schedule coordination

**Shall:** The system shall show the effect of maintenance windows on finite schedules and require planner review when a newly received outage intersects released or frozen operations.

**Rationale:** Coordination minimizes hidden schedule violations and makes disruption response traceable.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- The impact list identifies affected operations, resources, and intervals.
- An accepted outage either reschedules work or creates a documented planner exception.
- Resolved maintenance status does not erase prior schedule impact evidence.

**Edge case:** Maintenance events conflict with planned work but the resource is not exclusively reserved; applicable capacity rule determines conflict severity.

**Security and audit:** Planner overrides and maintenance interface changes are permissioned and logged.

**Localization:** Labels and explanatory text are localized; identifiers, codes, canonical quantities, and timestamps remain locale-neutral.

**Verification:** Schedule impact test with open, frozen, and released operations.

### H. Quality plans, inspections, nonconformance, and CAPA

### ERP-MFG-055 — Quality plan version and scope

**Shall:** The system shall manage quality plans as approved, versioned definitions scoped by configured item, supplier, process, site, and effective interval.

**Rationale:** Versioned plans identify the checks applicable to a particular receiving or production context.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Each active plan has owner, revision, scope, effective interval, and approval state.
- Inspection creation stores the exact plan revision.
- Overlapping or missing mandatory plan coverage is detected before activation.

**Edge case:** A plan is not applicable to a site or operation; the system reports a coverage gap instead of selecting a nearest match.

**Security and audit:** Plan author, approver, inspector, and disposition authority can be separated.

**Localization:** Plan content supports language-specific instructions while check IDs and units remain stable.

**Verification:** Applicability matrix and approval-separation tests.

### ERP-MFG-056 — Inspection characteristics and methods

**Shall:** The system shall define inspection characteristics with type, unit, method/instruction reference, acceptance rule, evidence requirement, and result precision as configured.

**Rationale:** Typed checks allow repeatable data capture while acceptance rules remain tenant-owned policy.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Characteristic type validates numeric, categorical, Boolean, or attachment result shape.
- Acceptance evaluation records rule version and raw result.
- Missing required characteristic prevents inspection completion.

**Edge case:** An acceptance limit is missing or not effective at inspection time; result is marked unevaluable and disposition is blocked where configured.

**Security and audit:** Limit changes require approval and cannot recalculate prior signed results silently.

**Localization:** Labels and explanatory text are localized; identifiers, codes, canonical quantities, and timestamps remain locale-neutral.

**Verification:** Input validation and rule-evaluation tests at boundaries.

### ERP-MFG-057 — Inspection sampling configuration

**Shall:** The system shall support configurable inspection sampling plans with sample size or selection logic, population basis, and revision provenance, without embedding a universal sampling standard.

**Rationale:** Sampling requirements differ by customer, industry, and jurisdiction and must remain explicit policy.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- A sample selection records population size, selected identifiers, plan revision, and selection timestamp.
- The engine rejects a plan whose parameters cannot produce a valid sample for the population.
- A configured full-inspection plan selects every unit or records each required result.

**Edge case:** Population changes after selection; the system invalidates or re-evaluates the sample according to configured policy.

**Security and audit:** Sampling-plan authoring and result approval are controlled and audited.

**Localization:** Labels and explanatory text are localized; identifiers, codes, canonical quantities, and timestamps remain locale-neutral.

**Verification:** Sample boundary tests at zero, one, and threshold population sizes.

### ERP-MFG-058 — Inspection result capture and signature

**Shall:** The system shall record inspection result, unit, method, evidence reference, inspector identity, event time, and completion state for each required characteristic.

**Rationale:** Complete context supports review and downstream disposition.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- A result cannot be finalized without all required context and checks.
- Finalized results are immutable; correction creates a linked amended result.
- Evidence attachment has access classification and integrity metadata.

**Edge case:** Inspection is recorded offline and later synchronized; original capture time and server receipt time are retained separately.

**Security and audit:** Inspectors can record results only within assigned scope; approval/signature evidence is attributable and protected.

**Localization:** Labels and explanatory text are localized; identifiers, codes, canonical quantities, and timestamps remain locale-neutral.

**Verification:** API tests for completeness, offline sync, and immutable amendments.

### ERP-MFG-059 — Quality hold and disposition authority

**Shall:** The system shall place affected inventory or WIP on a quality hold and accept release, rework, return, scrap, or other configured disposition only from an authorized quality decision.

**Rationale:** Physical availability and manufacturing progress must respect the current quality decision.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- A hold is linked to inspection or nonconformance and applies to identified quantity/lot/serial scope.
- Inventory availability reflects the accepted hold/disposition response.
- Only permitted states allow subsequent movement or production use.

**Edge case:** Quality service response is unknown; affected stock remains held until reconciliation confirms disposition.

**Security and audit:** Quality disposition is separate from routine receipt, picking, and production-report permissions; decisions are audited.

**Localization:** Labels and explanatory text are localized; identifiers, codes, canonical quantities, and timestamps remain locale-neutral.

**Verification:** End-to-end hold enforcement tests across inventory and shop-floor operations.

### ERP-MFG-060 — Nonconformance record

**Shall:** The system shall create a nonconformance record linked to affected item, lot/serial, order, operation, supplier, inspection, and containment action as applicable.

**Rationale:** A structured record connects defect evidence to impacted work and material.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Nonconformance ID is unique and references at least one affected object and source event.
- Severity, defect code, status, and disposition follow effective tenant configuration.
- Affected quantity is reconciled to held, accepted, reworked, returned, or scrapped quantities.

**Edge case:** Defect source is not yet known; record supports provisional cause and later controlled classification.

**Security and audit:** Creation, investigation, and closure roles are separately configurable; sensitive evidence is access-controlled.

**Localization:** Defect taxonomies and narrative fields support translation without changing code identity.

**Verification:** Lifecycle tests for unknown cause and quantity reconciliation.

### ERP-MFG-061 — Nonconformance containment and review

**Shall:** The system shall track containment scope, owner, due date, affected locations/orders, review decisions, and effectiveness evidence for each nonconformance.

**Rationale:** Containment prevents affected product from being treated as conforming while investigation proceeds.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Containment action has status, responsible role, scope, and evidence.
- Closure is blocked while mandatory containment remains open.
- Review decision records approver, timestamp, and references to affected stock/WIP actions.

**Edge case:** Affected scope expands after initial containment; the system adds linked scope without erasing previous actions.

**Security and audit:** Only authorized reviewers may release containment; all scope changes are audited.

**Localization:** Labels and explanatory text are localized; identifiers, codes, canonical quantities, and timestamps remain locale-neutral.

**Verification:** Workflow test for expanding scope, overdue action, and blocked closure.

### ERP-MFG-062 — Corrective and preventive action workflow

**Shall:** The system shall support configurable CAPA cases linking root-cause analysis, corrective/preventive actions, owners, due dates, evidence, verification, and effectiveness checks.

**Rationale:** CAPA workflows need measurable closure gates but no universal regulatory terminology or mandated timing is assumed.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- A CAPA cannot close until configured actions and effectiveness criteria are satisfied.
- Each action records owner, due date, status, and completion evidence.
- The case links to originating nonconformance(s) and subsequent verification outcome.

**Edge case:** Effectiveness check fails; case reopens or creates a linked follow-up according to configured workflow.

**Security and audit:** Action completion and case closure approvals can require different roles; changes remain auditable.

**Localization:** Labels and explanatory text are localized; identifiers, codes, canonical quantities, and timestamps remain locale-neutral.

**Verification:** Workflow acceptance tests for pass, fail, overdue, and reopen paths.

### ERP-MFG-063 — Quality dashboards and evidence retrieval

**Shall:** The system shall provide scoped quality queries for open inspections, holds, nonconformances, CAPA status, and disposition aging using declared freshness and source ownership.

**Rationale:** Operational visibility supports follow-up without turning reports into authoritative write paths.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Each dashboard declares refresh/as-of time and source modules.
- Filters preserve tenant/entity/site scope.
- Evidence download rechecks current authorization and records export where configured.

**Edge case:** A projection is stale or unavailable; the interface indicates freshness and links to authoritative records.

**Security and audit:** Quality exports are separately permissioned, tenant-filtered, and audited.

**Localization:** Labels and explanatory text are localized; identifiers, codes, canonical quantities, and timestamps remain locale-neutral.

**Verification:** Role-scope and stale-projection/export reauthorization tests.

### I. Genealogy, scrap, rework, costing, and close controls

### ERP-MFG-064 — Lot and serial genealogy capture

**Shall:** The system shall link consumed input lots/serials to produced output lots/serials through immutable transformation events associated with order, operation, time, and quantity.

**Rationale:** Transformation links enable forward and backward traceability across production events. \[4]

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Each transformation records input/output identifiers and quantities with units.
- A trace query from an input returns all linked outputs and from an output returns all linked inputs.
- Missing or inconsistent links are reported as trace gaps, not inferred.

**Edge case:** A production output combines multiple source lots or splits one source lot across multiple outputs; links preserve all many-to-many allocations.

**Security and audit:** Trace searches are scope-limited; external trace exports are permissioned and logged.

**Localization:** Localized labels do not alter lot/serial IDs; trace reports can render language-specific captions.

**Verification:** Forward/backward graph tests including split, merge, and missing-link cases.

### ERP-MFG-065 — Traceability profile and identity capture

**Shall:** The system shall apply configurable lot, serial, or other trace-identity capture rules at configured production, issue, transformation, and output events.

**Rationale:** Capture points vary by product and customer; explicit profiles prevent undocumented universal assumptions.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Each required capture event validates identifier format according to the configured profile.
- A controlled item cannot complete the event with missing mandatory identity.
- The event stores raw scanned identifier and normalized key when normalization is configured.

**Edge case:** Identifier is unreadable or duplicated; the operator receives a controlled exception and no substitute ID is silently assigned.

**Security and audit:** Profile changes require approved migration/impact analysis; access to trace searches is scoped.

**Localization:** Identifier input supports Unicode/scanner handling where configured while stable IDs remain exact.

**Verification:** Profile and barcode parsing tests including duplicate and malformed input.

### ERP-MFG-066 — Genealogy query and trace completeness

**Shall:** The system shall provide forward and backward genealogy queries with traversal depth, quantity reconciliation, event timestamp, source revision, and completeness indicators.

**Rationale:** Users must distinguish a complete trace from a partial path before relying on it operationally.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Query output identifies all traversed events and unresolved edges.
- Completeness status changes to incomplete when required links or source acknowledgements are absent.
- Large query results are bounded and support authorized continuation or export.

**Edge case:** Cycles or duplicate events appear in imported genealogy; query terminates safely and highlights data quality defects.

**Security and audit:** Sensitive customer/supplier endpoints are minimized by role; trace export is audited.

**Localization:** Query labels and units localize; event keys remain stable.

**Verification:** Graph tests for cycles, incomplete paths, pagination, and access control.

### ERP-MFG-067 — Scrap and yield-loss reporting

**Shall:** The system shall record scrap quantity, item, lot/serial when applicable, order/operation, reason code, disposition, and whether inventory or WIP movement is required.

**Rationale:** Scrap is a distinct operational outcome and must reconcile with quality, inventory, and costing.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Scrap report records planned versus actual quantity and configured reason code.
- If physical quantity changes, the system sends an Inventory-owned adjustment/disposal command and waits for its reference.
- Scrap quantity is included in order completion reconciliation.

**Edge case:** Scrap is discovered after order closure; a linked adjustment path preserves the original order result.

**Security and audit:** Scrap approval thresholds and disposition permissions are configurable; adjustments are audit-linked.

**Localization:** Reason labels localize while codes and canonical quantities remain stable.

**Verification:** Integration tests across scrap approval, inventory acknowledgement, and closeout.

### ERP-MFG-068 — Rework order and return-to-process

**Shall:** The system shall create a linked rework order or rework operation referencing the originating order, defect/nonconformance, affected quantity, route, and required quality reinspection.

**Rationale:** Rework must preserve original genealogy and defect context while creating an executable corrective path.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Rework quantity cannot exceed identified affected quantity without approved adjustment.
- Rework output links to original lot/serial genealogy and the source nonconformance.
- Rework completion invokes the configured reinspection gate before release.

**Edge case:** Rework changes product identity or revision; new output identity is linked to the original through a transformation event.

**Security and audit:** Rework approval and final quality release may require distinct roles; actions are audited.

**Localization:** Rework instructions and defect notes may be localized; source trace IDs are not translated.

**Verification:** End-to-end rework quantity, identity, and inspection tests.

### ERP-MFG-069 — Manufacturing cost handoff

**Shall:** The system shall publish versioned production cost inputs and actuals to Finance, including order, legal entity, item, quantity, material/labor/machine/subcontract/scrap components where configured, cost dimensions, currency, effective time, and source references.

**Rationale:** Manufacturing supplies operational cost facts while Finance owns valuation policy, accounting, and ledger posting.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Handoff totals reconcile to included source events within declared currency precision.
- Payload identifies costing basis and mapping/profile version.
- Finance acknowledgement or rejection is linked to the handoff ID; retry is idempotent.

**Edge case:** Cost event arrives after finance period closure or mapping is missing; it remains in a visible exception queue and is not silently dropped.

**Security and audit:** Cost export and mapping changes require permission; sensitive worker-level detail is minimized.

**Localization:** Currency and numbers are canonical; translated descriptions are supplemental only.

**Verification:** Finance contract tests for balanced totals, rejected mapping, duplicate delivery, and late period.

### ERP-MFG-070 — Manufacturing close reconciliation and exception controls

**Shall:** The system shall provide an order-level reconciliation of planned, issued, returned, consumed, completed, scrapped, reworked, subcontracted, held, WIP, and cost-handoff quantities/statuses before configurable close or period reporting.

**Rationale:** Reconciliation exposes differences across independently owned modules before they become unexplained operational or financial results.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- For a controlled fixture, each category reconciles to its source event set and displays any variance.
- Every unresolved variance has owner, age, source reference, and disposition status.
- Close policy blocks or records an approved override for each configured critical exception.

**Edge case:** Inventory or finance is unavailable during close; the system records pending acknowledgement and avoids claiming reconciliation succeeded.

**Security and audit:** Exception override, reconciliation export, and close approval are permissioned and audited.

**Localization:** Reconciliation reports localized labels and explicit units/currency while preserving canonical IDs.

**Verification:** Cross-domain end-to-end test with missing, late, and corrected source events.

## Manufacturing, Planning, and Quality — requirement cards

**REQUIREMENT 0281 OF 1120  |  MANUFACTURING, PLANNING, AND QUALITY**

## ERP-MFG-001 — Manufacturing context and tenant scope

**Normative requirement:** The manufacturing context shall scope every manufacturing record to its owning tenant and, where relevant, legal entity, site, plant, and production area.

**Rationale:** Explicit scope prevents cross-company planning and makes ownership and integration boundaries testable.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Every production order, plan run, quality record, and costing handoff resolves to one tenant and its configured site/entity scope.

**AC 2.** A user lacking site scope receives a denied response when querying or mutating that site.

**AC 3.** The same business code may be reused only where its configured uniqueness scope permits.

**Exception / edge case:** A shared physical site used by multiple entities retains separate ownership and authorization scope.

**Security and audit implications:** Server-side resource authorization is mandatory; tenant and site predicates are included in audit and integration envelopes.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Names and descriptions may be translated; tenant, entity, site, item, and order IDs remain locale-neutral.

**Verification method:** API authorization tests, tenant-isolation tests, and persistence constraint tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0282 OF 1120  |  MANUFACTURING, PLANNING, AND QUALITY**

## ERP-MFG-002 — Manufacturing master-data references

**Normative requirement:** The system shall reference centrally owned items, units of measure, sites, warehouses, work centers, calendars, and workers by stable platform identifiers without becoming their competing master.

**Rationale:** Common identifiers enable coherent inventory, procurement, people, and operations contracts.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Each reference stores the source-system ID and validated lifecycle state.

**AC 2.** Retirement of a referenced object blocks new use but preserves historical order and event references.

**AC 3.** Unit conversions used by a production transaction are recorded with the conversion revision.

**Exception / edge case:** A source master is unavailable or retired during import; the record is quarantined rather than mapped by description.

**Security and audit implications:** Import and mapping administration are separately permissioned and all mappings are auditable.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Human-readable labels are localized from the owning master; IDs and codes are not translated.

**Verification method:** Contract tests against platform, inventory, procurement, and workforce reference fixtures.

**Source references:**

ERP-INVENTORY-001

**REQUIREMENT 0283 OF 1120  |  MANUFACTURING, PLANNING, AND QUALITY**

## ERP-MFG-003 — Manufacturing policy profiles

**Normative requirement:** The system shall resolve planning, execution, quality, traceability, and posting behavior from explicitly versioned tenant/site/item policy profiles rather than hidden global defaults.

**Rationale:** Profiles allow configurable software without asserting universal operating or regulatory rules.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Each active profile has owner, scope, version, effective interval, and change history.

**AC 2.** An operation resolves and persists the profile version it used.

**AC 3.** Missing mandatory profile data blocks the dependent transaction with a stable error code.

**Exception / edge case:** Profile versions overlap or leave a gap at a transaction effective time; validation rejects publication.

**Security and audit implications:** Only designated configuration stewards can publish profiles; maker-checker is configurable and recorded.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Profile labels, guidance, and error text are translated; machine codes and policy values are canonical.

**Verification method:** Profile lifecycle and effective-date unit tests plus authorization/audit review.

**REQUIREMENT 0284 OF 1120  |  MANUFACTURING, PLANNING, AND QUALITY**

## ERP-MFG-004 — Manufacturing identifier and numbering policy

**Normative requirement:** The system shall assign stable internal IDs to manufacturing objects and apply configurable human-readable numbering schemes by tenant, entity, site, object type, and effective date.

**Rationale:** Numbering needs vary and must not become a hidden legal or cross-entity assumption.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** The generated ID is immutable when display number or description changes.

**AC 2.** Configured uniqueness scope is concurrency-safe under parallel creation.

**AC 3.** A disabled or exhausted sequence fails without silently reusing an issued number.

**Exception / edge case:** Offline devices create provisional references; reconciliation preserves their local reference and links one authoritative server ID.

**Security and audit implications:** Sequence configuration and manual overrides require scoped permission; issued numbers and actor are audited.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Human-readable prefixes may vary by locale/profile, but IDs and event keys do not.

**Verification method:** Concurrent sequence stress test and audit inspection.

**REQUIREMENT 0285 OF 1120  |  MANUFACTURING, PLANNING, AND QUALITY**

## ERP-MFG-005 — Manufacturing quantity and unit precision

**Normative requirement:** The system shall store production quantities using item-compatible units and explicit decimal precision, conversion revision, and rounding policy for each transaction.

**Rationale:** Canonical quantity handling avoids locale parsing errors and uncontrolled yield or consumption variance.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** API payloads accept invariant decimal representations and explicit unit codes.

**AC 2.** A transaction outside configured precision or conversion validity is rejected or handled by an explicitly configured rounding rule.

**AC 3.** Entered and normalized quantities remain available for audit.

**Exception / edge case:** Variable-measure output differs from nominal conversion; actual measurement is retained and not replaced by a fixed factor.

**Security and audit implications:** Only authorized stewards change UOM/precision policy; posted event quantities are immutable.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Numeric entry follows the user locale in UI while canonical API values remain locale-neutral.

**Verification method:** Boundary tests for precision, conversions, rounding, and non-Western numeric input.

**REQUIREMENT 0286 OF 1120  |  MANUFACTURING, PLANNING, AND QUALITY**

## ERP-MFG-006 — Manufacturing audit and event envelope

**Normative requirement:** The system shall record auditable state transitions and publish manufacturing events through a versioned, idempotent outbox contract carrying tenant/entity scope, event ID, correlation ID, actor/service, and effective and recorded timestamps.

**Rationale:** Durable provenance and retry-safe contracts are required for cross-module manufacturing workflows.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A committed state change and its outbox event persist atomically.

**AC 2.** Replaying the same event ID does not duplicate the consumer-side effect.

**AC 3.** Event schema version and correlation ID are present in every published event.

**Exception / edge case:** An external consumer is unavailable after local commit; the manufacturing transaction remains committed and delivery is retried/reconciled.

**Security and audit implications:** Event replay, payload export, and dead-letter resolution require explicit permission and are audited.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Event codes are stable and locale-neutral; localized text is not used as an integration key.

**Verification method:** Outbox/inbox integration test with duplicate delivery and downstream outage.

**REQUIREMENT 0287 OF 1120  |  MANUFACTURING, PLANNING, AND QUALITY**

## ERP-MFG-007 — Production order lifecycle

**Normative requirement:** The system shall manage production orders through configured states including draft, planned, released, in-process, completed, closed, and cancelled, with guarded transitions.

**Rationale:** Explicit lifecycle states prevent planning records from being mistaken for authorized shop-floor work.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Transition table identifies eligible commands and required fields per state.

**AC 2.** Invalid transitions return a stable reason code and leave the order unchanged.

**AC 3.** Every successful transition records actor, time, source version, and reason where required.

**Exception / edge case:** An order is cancelled after execution postings exist; cancellation requires a controlled close/reversal path rather than deletion.

**Security and audit implications:** Create, release, cancel, complete, and close permissions are separable; self-approval rules can be configured.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** State codes remain locale-neutral; labels and transition explanations are localized.

**Verification method:** State-machine unit and API authorization tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0288 OF 1120  |  MANUFACTURING, PLANNING, AND QUALITY**

## ERP-MFG-008 — Production order demand and quantity

**Normative requirement:** The system shall store an order’s demanded quantity, planned quantity, released quantity, completed quantity, and remaining quantity as distinct values with explicit units.

**Rationale:** Separate quantities support partial runs, yield reporting, and demand reconciliation.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Order quantity ledger exposes the five values and their units.

**AC 2.** Completed quantity cannot exceed permitted overproduction tolerance without an authorized override.

**AC 3.** Order quantity amendments after release create a versioned change record.

**Exception / edge case:** Demand is withdrawn while a batch is partly complete; remaining quantity is flagged for disposition and demand re-pegging.

**Security and audit implications:** Quantity overrides are permissioned and record original/new values and reason.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Quantities render using user locale and unit labels while stored values retain invariant precision.

**Verification method:** API and UI tests for partial completion, overrun, and post-release change.

**REQUIREMENT 0289 OF 1120  |  MANUFACTURING, PLANNING, AND QUALITY**

## ERP-MFG-009 — Production order source and pegging

**Normative requirement:** The system shall retain one or more demand-source references and pegging quantities for each order or order line when the order is demand-driven.

**Rationale:** Pegging preserves the relationship between independent demand and planned or executed supply.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Demand source type, stable source ID, line ID, required date, and pegged quantity are queryable.

**AC 2.** Aggregated pegging quantities reconcile to the linked order quantity within the configured unit conversion.

**AC 3.** Unpegged make-to-stock orders are explicitly marked as such.

**Exception / edge case:** A single production order fulfills multiple demands; each split is independently traceable and amendable.

**Security and audit implications:** Users may view only authorized source demand; event payloads do not expose unrelated customer data.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Customer-facing descriptions are localized only at presentation; stable source references remain unchanged.

**Verification method:** Integration test linking, splitting, and unpegging demand.

**REQUIREMENT 0290 OF 1120  |  MANUFACTURING, PLANNING, AND QUALITY**

## ERP-MFG-010 — Order release readiness gate

**Normative requirement:** The system shall validate configured release prerequisites before production order release, including effective BOM/recipe, route, material availability policy, quality prerequisites, and required approvals.

**Rationale:** Release validation prevents execution against incomplete or superseded instructions.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Validation returns a machine-readable list of failed prerequisites.

**AC 2.** A passing order stores the exact BOM, route, and policy revisions used at release.

**AC 3.** A configured approval must be satisfied before the release command succeeds.

**Exception / edge case:** A prerequisite changes between validation and release; optimistic concurrency or revalidation prevents a stale release.

**Security and audit implications:** Release approver identity and evidence are immutable and distinct from configuration edits.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Prerequisite messages are localized while codes and referenced revisions are stable.

**Verification method:** Race-condition test for validation/release plus approval workflow tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0291 OF 1120  |  MANUFACTURING, PLANNING, AND QUALITY**

## ERP-MFG-011 — Production order split and merge

**Normative requirement:** The system shall support controlled splitting and merging of eligible production orders while preserving source demand, quantities, configuration revisions, and genealogy references.

**Rationale:** Splitting supports capacity and batch constraints without losing the parent demand trail.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Split quantities sum to the source remaining quantity or a recorded variance.

**AC 2.** A merge is rejected when orders have incompatible item, site, effective BOM/route, ownership, or quality controls.

**AC 3.** Parent-child links remain queryable after closure.

**Exception / edge case:** An order already has material or labor postings; only unexecuted quantity may be split unless a configured correction flow is invoked.

**Security and audit implications:** Splitting, merging, and quantity adjustments require dedicated rights and audit records.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Localized labels do not alter stable parent-child keys.

**Verification method:** Property-based quantity conservation and incompatible-merge tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0292 OF 1120  |  MANUFACTURING, PLANNING, AND QUALITY**

## ERP-MFG-012 — Production order document snapshot

**Normative requirement:** The system shall provide an immutable, versioned execution packet for each released order containing applicable product, BOM/recipe, route, instructions, and control-plan references.

**Rationale:** Operators need consistent instructions even when future revisions are published.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Execution packet is bound to a release revision and can be retrieved for every released order.

**AC 2.** Subsequent master-data edits do not alter the released packet.

**AC 3.** A controlled superseding packet records prior and new versions and approval.

**Exception / edge case:** An instruction attachment becomes unavailable; order release is blocked or a protected immutable copy is retained per tenant policy.

**Security and audit implications:** Document retrieval follows order and attachment scope; downloads are logged where configured.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Instruction versions can include approved language editions with a designated controlling revision.

**Verification method:** Snapshot immutability and authorization tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0293 OF 1120  |  MANUFACTURING, PLANNING, AND QUALITY**

## ERP-MFG-013 — Production order close and residual handling

**Normative requirement:** The system shall close an order only after configured completion checks reconcile output, consumption, scrap, WIP, subcontract receipts, and unresolved quality holds.

**Rationale:** Closeout establishes a complete operational record and a clear point for downstream costing.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Close validation lists each unreconciled quantity or hold.

**AC 2.** Successful close freezes further routine reporting and emits a versioned close event.

**AC 3.** Authorized reopen creates a linked audit event and does not erase the prior close.

**Exception / edge case:** Late external labor or supplier confirmation arrives after close; it is routed to an approved adjustment or reopen path.

**Security and audit implications:** Close/reopen permissions are separate from routine execution; close evidence is retained.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Close status is locale-neutral and report labels are translated.

**Verification method:** Close-gate integration tests for each outstanding quantity/status.

**REQUIREMENT 0294 OF 1120  |  MANUFACTURING, PLANNING, AND QUALITY**

## ERP-MFG-014 — BOM and recipe revision control

**Normative requirement:** The system shall manage bills of material and process recipes as immutable approved revisions with explicit status, owner, effective interval, and input/output item references.

**Rationale:** Revision control makes production instructions reproducible over time.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** An approved revision cannot be overwritten; changes create a successor revision.

**AC 2.** Effective selection returns exactly one applicable revision or a validation error.

**AC 3.** Released orders persist the selected revision ID.

**Exception / edge case:** A date falls into overlapping or missing revision intervals; activation is rejected or selection is blocked.

**Security and audit implications:** Author, reviewer, and approver roles are separable; publication records before/after and approvals.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Names/instructions may be translated per revision; recipe codes and item IDs are canonical.

**Verification method:** Revision lifecycle and interval-overlap tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0295 OF 1120  |  MANUFACTURING, PLANNING, AND QUALITY**

## ERP-MFG-015 — BOM component requirements

**Normative requirement:** The system shall model BOM/recipe lines with component item, planned quantity, unit, operation association where applicable, issue policy, and effective revision.

**Rationale:** Typed component lines support material planning and execution without ambiguous free-text consumption.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Each active line resolves to an item and compatible unit conversion.

**AC 2.** Requirement calculation records basis quantity, component quantity, and selected conversion revision.

**AC 3.** Optional, variable, and fixed-quantity line behavior is explicitly identified.

**Exception / edge case:** A component is discontinued after an order release; existing orders retain the released revision and new planning raises an exception.

**Security and audit implications:** Only approved engineering/configuration roles may publish line revisions.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Instructions localize while item and unit codes remain stable.

**Verification method:** BOM calculation tests for variable/fixed/optional lines.

**REQUIREMENT 0296 OF 1120  |  MANUFACTURING, PLANNING, AND QUALITY**

## ERP-MFG-016 — Alternate and substitute materials

**Normative requirement:** The system shall allow explicitly approved alternate or substitute components with item eligibility, priority, quantity conversion, approval scope, and effective dates.

**Rationale:** Governed substitution handles supply disruption without silently changing product definition.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** An unapproved substitute is rejected at reservation/issue.

**AC 2.** Substitution records requested component, actual component, approval reference, and quantity conversion.

**AC 3.** Effective/expired alternatives are excluded from new execution.

**Exception / edge case:** An emergency substitution is needed while approver connectivity is unavailable; configured emergency authorization captures later review without hiding the deviation.

**Security and audit implications:** Substitution approval and material issue may require separate roles; exceptions are audited.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Alternate names are localized, but approval codes and item identities are not.

**Verification method:** Positive/negative authorization tests and effective-date boundary tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0297 OF 1120  |  MANUFACTURING, PLANNING, AND QUALITY**

## ERP-MFG-017 — By-products, co-products, and yield

**Normative requirement:** The system shall represent configured co-products, by-products, and expected yield/loss factors separately from primary output and actual production results.

**Rationale:** Explicit output modeling supports multi-output processes and measurable yield reconciliation.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Order output lines distinguish primary, co-product, by-product, and expected loss.

**AC 2.** Actual quantity and unit are captured for each reportable output.

**AC 3.** Configured yield variance thresholds raise a review status without changing quantities automatically.

**Exception / edge case:** Actual output is zero or greater than input due to a process conversion; transaction requires a configured explanation or measurement model.

**Security and audit implications:** Yield policy changes are approved, versioned, and cannot rewrite posted actuals.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Yield explanations are localized; quantities and type codes stay canonical.

**Verification method:** Calculation tests for multi-output and yield variance.

**REQUIREMENT 0298 OF 1120  |  MANUFACTURING, PLANNING, AND QUALITY**

## ERP-MFG-018 — Phantom and non-stock components

**Normative requirement:** The system shall support explicitly typed phantom or non-stock BOM lines and expand phantom subassemblies according to a versioned planning/execution policy.

**Rationale:** This supports kit planning without confusing structure-only items with inventory-backed components.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Explosion output identifies each expanded source line and effective revision.

**AC 2.** A non-stock line does not create an inventory reservation or issue.

**AC 3.** Cycles in a BOM graph are rejected with the offending path.

**Exception / edge case:** A phantom child has a separately planned operation or is not valid on the selected site; explosion reports the unsupported line.

**Security and audit implications:** Only authorized engineering users alter structure and expansion policies.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Display labels localize, but expansion order and component IDs do not depend on locale.

**Verification method:** Graph-cycle and reservation-generation tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0299 OF 1120  |  MANUFACTURING, PLANNING, AND QUALITY**

## ERP-MFG-019 — Operation-linked material consumption

**Normative requirement:** The system shall associate component consumption with a production order operation or an explicitly designated order-level issue point.

**Rationale:** Operation linkage supports staged material availability and consumption traceability.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Every posted material issue has an operation/order link or an explicit order-level marker.

**AC 2.** Materials assigned to a later operation are not presented as required at an earlier point unless policy says so.

**AC 3.** The issue record retains planned and actual quantities.

**Exception / edge case:** Component is consumed at a different operation than planned; actual event is accepted only through a variance reason path.

**Security and audit implications:** Issue and variance permissions are scoped to site and operation; issue reversals retain original linkage.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Operator UI localizes work instructions and unit formatting without translating canonical operation IDs.

**Verification method:** Shop-floor tests for planned and deviated operation issues.

**REQUIREMENT 0300 OF 1120  |  MANUFACTURING, PLANNING, AND QUALITY**

## ERP-MFG-020 — Effective-dated manufacturing engineering change

**Normative requirement:** The system shall manage engineering changes to BOMs, recipes, routes, and control plans through approved changes with effectivity by date, serial/lot range, or explicit order boundary.

**Rationale:** Controlled effectivity avoids applying new instructions to already committed or in-process work without authorization.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A change record contains affected objects, reason, approval, effective rule, and predecessor revision.

**AC 2.** Selection tests resolve the applicable revision at specified date/serial/order boundaries.

**AC 3.** Open-order impact is listed before publication.

**Exception / edge case:** Calendar-time and serial-range effectivity conflict; the system flags ambiguous selection instead of choosing silently.

**Security and audit implications:** Engineering change approval is separated from authoring where configured; impact report access is scoped.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Change description and operator notice are localized; effectivity keys are canonical.

**Verification method:** Boundary matrix tests over open/released orders and overlapping effectivity.

**REQUIREMENT 0301 OF 1120  |  MANUFACTURING, PLANNING, AND QUALITY**

## ERP-MFG-021 — Manufacturing change impact assessment

**Normative requirement:** The system shall calculate and retain the impact set of an engineering change across planned and released orders, material reservations, supplier commitments, inspections, and costing setup.

**Rationale:** Change owners need an actionable, reproducible view of affected execution and dependent commitments.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Impact output lists object ID, prior/new revision, state, and required action.

**AC 2.** Re-running against unchanged source versions yields the same set and version hash.

**AC 3.** Publication records acknowledgement or disposition of every configured mandatory impact category.

**Exception / edge case:** A downstream system is temporarily unavailable; impact is marked incomplete and publication follows configurable block/approval policy.

**Security and audit implications:** Impact export is permissioned and audit logged; supplier/customer-sensitive fields are minimized.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Impact notices are localized; object identifiers and version hashes remain invariant.

**Verification method:** Changed-source replay and incomplete-impact policy tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0302 OF 1120  |  MANUFACTURING, PLANNING, AND QUALITY**

## ERP-MFG-022 — BOM/recipe effectivity and order snapshot

**Normative requirement:** The system shall resolve and persist effective BOM/recipe revisions at planning and again at order release, recording any authorized difference between those points.

**Rationale:** This makes planned supply explainable and executed consumption reproducible.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** MRP output records the revision and effective date used.

**AC 2.** Order release records its selected revision separately from planning revision.

**AC 3.** Revision change between plan and release produces a visible delta list.

**Exception / edge case:** An order crosses an effective boundary during execution; its original revision remains unless an approved changeover is recorded.

**Security and audit implications:** Override of the selected revision requires permission and reason; audit stores both revision identifiers.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Localized revision labels do not affect revision matching.

**Verification method:** Plan-to-release effective-date transition tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0303 OF 1120  |  MANUFACTURING, PLANNING, AND QUALITY**

## ERP-MFG-023 — Recipe parameter and batch scaling

**Normative requirement:** The system shall define recipe-specific process parameters and scaling formulas with typed units, valid ranges, scaling basis, and revision provenance, separately from component quantity lines.

**Rationale:** Process targets may scale or vary independently from material quantities and must be executable and auditable.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Each parameter declares data type, unit or category, allowed range, scaling basis, and effective recipe revision.

**AC 2.** Batch scaling records input batch size, formula revision, and calculated parameter values.

**AC 3.** Out-of-range values prevent release or require an explicitly configured approval path.

**Exception / edge case:** A parameter is manually overridden for a particular batch; both calculated and actual values remain available with a reason.

**Security and audit implications:** Recipe parameter authoring and batch override approval are permissioned separately; revisions and actual-value changes are audited.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Parameter labels and instructions support translation; machine keys, units, and values remain canonical.

**Verification method:** Formula determinism, range validation, and approved-override tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0304 OF 1120  |  MANUFACTURING, PLANNING, AND QUALITY**

## ERP-MFG-024 — Routing revision and operation sequence

**Normative requirement:** The system shall define an approved, versioned routing of ordered operations with operation IDs, precedence rules, expected durations, and required resource capabilities.

**Rationale:** Explicit operation sequence supports scheduling and execution control.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A routing contains unique operation IDs and a valid precedence graph.

**AC 2.** Cycles and references to inactive capabilities are rejected at approval.

**AC 3.** Released orders retain the routing revision and operation sequence.

**Exception / edge case:** An operation may run in parallel with another; an explicit dependency graph represents this rather than relying on display order.

**Security and audit implications:** Routing approval and shop-floor edit rights are distinct and recorded.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Operation instructions may be translated; operation IDs and precedence remain invariant.

**Verification method:** Routing graph validation and execution packet test.

**REQUIREMENT 0305 OF 1120  |  MANUFACTURING, PLANNING, AND QUALITY**

## ERP-MFG-025 — Work center and resource capability

**Normative requirement:** The system shall model work centers and finite-capacity resources with capability tags, site scope, availability state, and effective-dated calendars.

**Rationale:** Scheduling requires explicit resource eligibility and availability inputs.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** An operation is assignable only to a resource with the required capabilities and active scope.

**AC 2.** Unavailable resources are excluded for intervals marked unavailable.

**AC 3.** Capability and calendar revisions used by a schedule are persisted.

**Exception / edge case:** A resource is shared across sites or has an emergency outage; scope and outage window are explicit rather than inferred.

**Security and audit implications:** Resource availability changes require authorized roles and retain actor, interval, and reason.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Resource names localize; capability codes and timestamps remain canonical.

**Verification method:** Eligibility and outage-interval test suite.

**REQUIREMENT 0306 OF 1120  |  MANUFACTURING, PLANNING, AND QUALITY**

## ERP-MFG-026 — Operation time model

**Normative requirement:** The system shall store setup, run, queue, move, wait, and teardown duration assumptions as typed operation parameters with units and scaling basis.

**Rationale:** Typed time assumptions enable consistent load estimation without conflating elapsed and labor time.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Each enabled duration identifies unit, fixed/per-lot/per-unit basis, and revision.

**AC 2.** Duration calculation outputs its inputs and computed value.

**AC 3.** Zero or negative values are rejected except for explicitly permitted zero-duration operations.

**Exception / edge case:** Batch size exceeds a configured maximum; the operation is split into capacity-feasible segments or flagged for review.

**Security and audit implications:** Only planners or engineering stewards with permission may change standards; changes are audited.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Time display uses selected locale and site time zone; stored durations are unit-coded.

**Verification method:** Duration formula and boundary-value tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0307 OF 1120  |  MANUFACTURING, PLANNING, AND QUALITY**

## ERP-MFG-027 — Finite-capacity scheduling mode

**Normative requirement:** The system shall support a finite-capacity schedule mode that places operations only in eligible resource intervals within configured capacity and calendars.

**Rationale:** Finite scheduling provides a feasible sequence under selected resource constraints.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A schedule run records planning horizon, resource calendar revision, and scheduling algorithm/configuration version.

**AC 2.** No scheduled operation exceeds available resource capacity or overlaps an exclusive resource booking.

**AC 3.** Unscheduled operations include a reason code.

**Exception / edge case:** No feasible interval exists within the horizon; the operation remains unscheduled and is not silently placed beyond capacity.

**Security and audit implications:** Schedule publication and manual overrides have separate permissions and audit trails.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Schedule dates render in site time zone; canonical instants and time-zone ID are preserved.

**Verification method:** Constraint solver tests with oversubscribed resources and daylight-saving transitions.

**REQUIREMENT 0308 OF 1120  |  MANUFACTURING, PLANNING, AND QUALITY**

## ERP-MFG-028 — Infinite-capacity planning mode

**Normative requirement:** The system shall support an explicitly labeled infinite-capacity planning mode that calculates dates without asserting resource feasibility.

**Rationale:** Rough-cut planning can be useful for demand scenarios but must not be mistaken for an executable schedule.

**Acceptance criteria:**
