**AC 1.** Every output and export identifies capacity mode as infinite.

**AC 2.** Capacity overload indicators show demand load versus configured capacity.

**AC 3.** Release gate rejects an infinite-capacity plan when tenant policy requires finite scheduling.

**Exception / edge case:** A user opens a rough-cut plan from a dispatch screen; the UI displays a persistent non-executable status.

**Security and audit implications:** Only planning roles can publish the infinite-capacity scenario; it cannot authorize shop-floor release by itself.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Labels and explanatory text are localized; identifiers, codes, canonical quantities, and timestamps remain locale-neutral.

**Verification method:** Capacity-mode labeling and release policy tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0309 OF 1120  |  MANUFACTURING, PLANNING, AND QUALITY**

## ERP-MFG-029 — Schedule scenario, freeze, and reschedule

**Normative requirement:** The system shall support named schedule scenarios and a configurable frozen interval, preserving prior published schedules when a new scenario is calculated.

**Rationale:** Scenario comparison and frozen work prevent exploratory rescheduling from mutating active commitments.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Scenario records source plan, assumptions, and computed result version.

**AC 2.** Publishing a new schedule requires an explicit compare-and-promote action.

**AC 3.** Frozen operations remain unchanged unless a permitted override records reason and approver.

**Exception / edge case:** Unexpected outage invalidates frozen work; an authorized exception can override only affected operations and records a recovery plan.

**Security and audit implications:** Override and promote rights are separately assigned; all changes are diffable and audited.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Labels and explanatory text are localized; identifiers, codes, canonical quantities, and timestamps remain locale-neutral.

**Verification method:** Scenario isolation, freeze-window, and promotion tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0310 OF 1120  |  MANUFACTURING, PLANNING, AND QUALITY**

## ERP-MFG-030 — Finite schedule resource conflicts

**Normative requirement:** The system shall detect resource and labor-calendar conflicts before publishing a finite schedule and shall report all conflicting order-operation pairs.

**Rationale:** Conflict visibility makes schedule publication operationally reviewable.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Conflict report identifies resource, interval, both operations, and constraint type.

**AC 2.** A schedule with hard conflicts cannot publish unless an explicit configured override is approved.

**AC 3.** Soft preference violations are distinguished from hard constraints.

**Exception / edge case:** An operation uses a shared alternate resource; the conflict check evaluates its actual assigned resource and capability.

**Security and audit implications:** Conflict overrides require a reason and approver where configured; report access follows site scope.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Labels and explanatory text are localized; identifiers, codes, canonical quantities, and timestamps remain locale-neutral.

**Verification method:** Conflict injection and override tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0311 OF 1120  |  MANUFACTURING, PLANNING, AND QUALITY**

## ERP-MFG-031 — Dispatch list and schedule adherence

**Normative requirement:** The system shall provide a versioned dispatch list ordered by the active schedule and show status, prerequisites, queue priority, and schedule deviation for each operation.

**Rationale:** Operators need a clear, current execution queue and planners need adherence feedback.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Dispatch list identifies active schedule version and refresh timestamp.

**AC 2.** Items with blocked material or quality prerequisites are visibly non-dispatchable.

**AC 3.** Late/early status derives from configured tolerance and site time zone.

**Exception / edge case:** An offline workstation has a stale dispatch snapshot; it must display snapshot time and reject prohibited stale actions.

**Security and audit implications:** Work center users see only authorized operations; dispatch exports are audited.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Labels and explanatory text are localized; identifiers, codes, canonical quantities, and timestamps remain locale-neutral.

**Verification method:** Role-based dispatch UI test with stale data and blocker cases.

**REQUIREMENT 0312 OF 1120  |  MANUFACTURING, PLANNING, AND QUALITY**

## ERP-MFG-032 — Capacity load and utilization view

**Normative requirement:** The system shall calculate planned resource load and configured capacity by time bucket and expose the utilization assumptions used.

**Rationale:** Planners need explainable load views rather than opaque utilization percentages.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Load reports disclose bucket size, shift/calendar version, duration basis, and excluded work.

**AC 2.** Load equals the sum of included scheduled/planned durations within stated rounding tolerance.

**AC 3.** Filters preserve tenant and site scope.

**Exception / edge case:** Unassigned or unscheduled operations are shown separately and not counted as zero-load completed work.

**Security and audit implications:** Reports enforce row-level site permissions and log sensitive exports.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Labels and explanatory text are localized; identifiers, codes, canonical quantities, and timestamps remain locale-neutral.

**Verification method:** Reconciliation calculation test against known operation samples.

**REQUIREMENT 0313 OF 1120  |  MANUFACTURING, PLANNING, AND QUALITY**

## ERP-MFG-033 — MRP run inputs and immutable run record

**Normative requirement:** The system shall create an immutable material requirements planning run record capturing demand snapshot, supply snapshot, BOM/recipe revisions, planning parameters, and horizon.

**Rationale:** Reproducible inputs allow planners to explain action messages and compare runs.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Run stores cutoff timestamps and source snapshot identifiers.

**AC 2.** Rerunning with the same snapshots and parameters yields identical planned requirement values within declared deterministic precision.

**AC 3.** A run in progress or failed state is distinguishable from completed output.

**Exception / edge case:** Upstream data changes during extraction; snapshot boundaries prevent mixing versions or mark the run inconsistent.

**Security and audit implications:** Only authorized planners can create, inspect, publish, or export runs; run data remains tenant-scoped.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Labels and explanatory text are localized; identifiers, codes, canonical quantities, and timestamps remain locale-neutral.

**Verification method:** Plan replay determinism tests and snapshot consistency tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0314 OF 1120  |  MANUFACTURING, PLANNING, AND QUALITY**

## ERP-MFG-034 — MRP demand netting

**Normative requirement:** The system shall net eligible demand against eligible on-hand, reservations, scheduled receipts, and approved supply according to a versioned policy with explicit statuses and dates.

**Rationale:** Netting must be explainable and must not treat held or unrelated inventory as available.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Each netting line shows gross demand, eligible supply categories, exclusions, and net requirement.

**AC 2.** Quality-held, blocked, expired, or wrong-owner stock is excluded according to profile.

**AC 3.** Supply quantities are not double counted across categories.

**Exception / edge case:** A receipt or reservation changes while a plan is running; the run retains its snapshot and reports staleness relative to current data.

**Security and audit implications:** Netting configuration changes require approval; plan output cannot directly mutate stock.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Display uses locale-aware units/dates while canonical source values remain intact.

**Verification method:** Golden dataset netting tests including exclusions and duplicate-supply guards.

**Source references:**

ERP-INVENTORY-001

**REQUIREMENT 0315 OF 1120  |  MANUFACTURING, PLANNING, AND QUALITY**

## ERP-MFG-035 — MRP multi-level explosion

**Normative requirement:** The system shall explode multi-level BOM/recipe requirements by selected revision, quantity, yield policy, and effective date, retaining the parent-demand path for each dependent requirement.

**Rationale:** Path-level explosion supports planned purchase and production decisions across levels.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Every dependent requirement has a traversable parent path to independent demand.

**AC 2.** Yield and unit conversions used at each level are stored.

**AC 3.** Circular BOM structures fail the run with a path-specific diagnostic.

**Exception / edge case:** A component is both a top-level demand item and a lower-level component; independent demand and dependent requirement remain separately identifiable.

**Security and audit implications:** Plan output and path visibility obey item/site scope restrictions.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Labels and explanatory text are localized; identifiers, codes, canonical quantities, and timestamps remain locale-neutral.

**Verification method:** Engine test for multi-level, shared-component, cycle, and conversion cases.

**REQUIREMENT 0316 OF 1120  |  MANUFACTURING, PLANNING, AND QUALITY**

## ERP-MFG-036 — MRP lead time and calendar dates

**Normative requirement:** The system shall calculate planned start and due dates using configured item/site lead times, operation calendars, supplier or internal supply calendars, and an explicit date convention.

**Rationale:** Planning dates must disclose assumptions and respect business calendars.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Calculated dates identify each lead-time/calendar source and version.

**AC 2.** Nonworking periods are handled according to selected calendar rules.

**AC 3.** Missing required lead-time data creates an exception rather than a zero-day assumption.

**Exception / edge case:** A due date falls on a time-zone daylight-saving boundary or nonworking day; stored instants and selected business-date convention remain unambiguous.

**Security and audit implications:** Calendar maintenance is permissioned and versioned.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Labels and explanatory text are localized; identifiers, codes, canonical quantities, and timestamps remain locale-neutral.

**Verification method:** Calendar/date boundary tests across time zones and DST transitions.

**REQUIREMENT 0317 OF 1120  |  MANUFACTURING, PLANNING, AND QUALITY**

## ERP-MFG-037 — MRP planned supply recommendations

**Normative requirement:** The system shall generate typed planned production, purchase, transfer, and reschedule recommendations without creating firm orders until an authorized conversion command is accepted.

**Rationale:** Recommendations separate planning proposals from procurement or manufacturing commitments.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Each recommendation has source plan/run, item, quantity, date, site, supply type, and action status.

**AC 2.** Converting a recommendation creates one linked order and is idempotent on retry.

**AC 3.** Rejected or deferred recommendations remain visible with reason.

**Exception / edge case:** An item is make/buy configurable by site; ambiguous sourcing produces a planner exception instead of arbitrary selection.

**Security and audit implications:** Conversion permissions are distinct from planner review; every action is attributed.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Labels and explanatory text are localized; identifiers, codes, canonical quantities, and timestamps remain locale-neutral.

**Verification method:** Conversion API tests for idempotency and source linkage.

**Source references:**

ERP-INVENTORY-001

**REQUIREMENT 0318 OF 1120  |  MANUFACTURING, PLANNING, AND QUALITY**

## ERP-MFG-038 — MRP action messages and exceptions

**Normative requirement:** The system shall create actionable messages for shortages, excesses, delays, cancellations, reschedules, and invalid planning data, with priority and recommended disposition.

**Rationale:** Planners require clear exceptions instead of having to infer problems from aggregate output.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Each message references affected plan line and source facts.

**AC 2.** Message status supports open, acknowledged, resolved, and dismissed with reason.

**AC 3.** Resolution records user, timestamp, and linked corrective action when one exists.

**Exception / edge case:** A shortage is caused by a held lot; the action message links the specific eligibility reason without exposing unauthorized supplier details.

**Security and audit implications:** Message acknowledgement and dismissal are audited; scope follows site and item permissions.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Labels and explanatory text are localized; identifiers, codes, canonical quantities, and timestamps remain locale-neutral.

**Verification method:** Exception lifecycle and permission tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0319 OF 1120  |  MANUFACTURING, PLANNING, AND QUALITY**

## ERP-MFG-039 — MRP planning fences and order modifiers

**Normative requirement:** The system shall apply configurable planning time fences, order modifiers, minimum/maximum quantities, multiples, and rounding rules per item/site profile.

**Rationale:** Planning parameters vary by operation and are made explicit rather than hardcoded.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Run output identifies each applied modifier and resulting quantity.

**AC 2.** Values outside configured ranges are rejected during profile publication.

**AC 3.** A disabled modifier has no effect on the calculated planned quantity.

**Exception / edge case:** A modifier produces supply beyond remaining demand; excess is surfaced with reason and never silently discarded.

**Security and audit implications:** Parameter changes are reviewed, versioned, and audited.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Labels and explanatory text are localized; identifiers, codes, canonical quantities, and timestamps remain locale-neutral.

**Verification method:** Boundary/property tests across minimums, multiples, fences, and maxima.

**REQUIREMENT 0320 OF 1120  |  MANUFACTURING, PLANNING, AND QUALITY**

## ERP-MFG-040 — MRP plan publication and stale-source control

**Normative requirement:** The system shall require planners to review source freshness and material exceptions before publishing a plan for downstream conversion.

**Rationale:** A calculated run can become stale and must not silently drive supply commitments.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Publication records reviewer, snapshot IDs, and exception disposition.

**AC 2.** If configured critical sources have changed beyond tolerance, publication is blocked or requires explicit override.

**AC 3.** Published plan events are idempotent and carry the run ID.

**Exception / edge case:** One source adapter is unreachable; the run is marked incomplete and publication follows a configured block/approval rule.

**Security and audit implications:** Publish, override, and downstream conversion are separately permissioned and audited.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Labels and explanatory text are localized; identifiers, codes, canonical quantities, and timestamps remain locale-neutral.

**Verification method:** Changed-source and upstream-outage publication tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0321 OF 1120  |  MANUFACTURING, PLANNING, AND QUALITY**

## ERP-MFG-041 — Shop-floor operation start and completion

**Normative requirement:** The system shall record operation start, pause, resume, partial completion, and completion against a released order with operator, resource, timestamps, and quantity where applicable.

**Rationale:** Execution events create an attributable operational record and support partial processing.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Start requires a released, dispatchable operation.

**AC 2.** Completion cannot exceed remaining quantity beyond configured tolerance.

**AC 3.** Pause/resume produces separate events and preserves elapsed and reported time.

**Exception / edge case:** Network loss occurs after a scan; client retry with same idempotency key produces one operation event.

**Security and audit implications:** Operators may report only assigned or authorized resources; supervisor corrections are distinct and audited.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Labels and explanatory text are localized; identifiers, codes, canonical quantities, and timestamps remain locale-neutral.

**Verification method:** API/UI state tests including duplicate submissions and partial completions.

**REQUIREMENT 0322 OF 1120  |  MANUFACTURING, PLANNING, AND QUALITY**

## ERP-MFG-042 — Shop-floor material issue and return

**Normative requirement:** The system shall request material issue and return through inventory-owned commands and record the accepted inventory movement reference against the manufacturing order/operation.

**Rationale:** Inventory owns physical stock movements; Manufacturing owns consumption context.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Issue command contains item, quantity, unit, order, operation, and requested lot/serial where controlled.

**AC 2.** Manufacturing status updates only after receiving an accepted movement reference.

**AC 3.** Return quantity links to the originating issue and cannot exceed its remaining returnable amount unless policy allows an adjustment.

**Exception / edge case:** Inventory returns unknown/timeout outcome; Manufacturing retains pending status and reconciles before resubmitting a new movement.

**Security and audit implications:** Issue/return roles are scoped; cost or quantity override requires elevated permission.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Labels and explanatory text are localized; identifiers, codes, canonical quantities, and timestamps remain locale-neutral.

**Verification method:** Contract tests for accepted/rejected/unknown responses and duplicate callbacks.

**Source references:**

ERP-INVENTORY-001

**REQUIREMENT 0323 OF 1120  |  MANUFACTURING, PLANNING, AND QUALITY**

## ERP-MFG-043 — Backflush consumption

**Normative requirement:** The system shall support backflush consumption only when enabled by the item/site/order profile, calculate it from reported output and approved BOM revision, and submit the result to Inventory for posting.

**Rationale:** Backflush can reduce transaction effort but requires controlled calculation and explicit inventory posting.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Backflush output shows calculated components, basis quantity, yield/rounding rule, and revision before commit.

**AC 2.** Posted issue events link to completion event and order operation.

**AC 3.** Actual or configured exceptions exceeding tolerance create a review hold.

**Exception / edge case:** A required lot-controlled material lacks a valid lot allocation; completion does not bypass lot capture.

**Security and audit implications:** Backflush enablement and tolerance changes require approval; override values are audited.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Labels and explanatory text are localized; identifiers, codes, canonical quantities, and timestamps remain locale-neutral.

**Verification method:** Calculation tests for partial output, rounding, missing lot, and retry.

**REQUIREMENT 0324 OF 1120  |  MANUFACTURING, PLANNING, AND QUALITY**

## ERP-MFG-044 — Labor time reporting

**Normative requirement:** The system shall capture labor time entries linked to worker, order, operation, resource where relevant, start/end or duration, time category, and approval state.

**Rationale:** Attributable labor facts support operational analysis and a governed finance/payroll handoff.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Overlapping entries for one worker are flagged under configured overlap policy.

**AC 2.** Submitted duration is recalculated or validated against timestamps and declared time zone.

**AC 3.** Approved entries are immutable except through a linked correction.

**Exception / edge case:** An overnight shift crosses local midnight or DST change; elapsed duration and business-date attribution are both defined and tested.

**Security and audit implications:** Workers report own time; supervisors approve exceptions; payroll/finance exports are separately permissioned.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Labels and explanatory text are localized; identifiers, codes, canonical quantities, and timestamps remain locale-neutral.

**Verification method:** Labor API tests for overlap, DST, correction, and approval.

**REQUIREMENT 0325 OF 1120  |  MANUFACTURING, PLANNING, AND QUALITY**

## ERP-MFG-045 — Machine and production counter reporting

**Normative requirement:** The system shall capture machine states and production counters from authorized manual or integrated sources, retaining raw value, normalized value, source identity, and event time.

**Rationale:** Raw-source preservation enables reconciliation between shop-floor equipment and ERP projections.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Duplicate source event IDs are ignored idempotently.

**AC 2.** Counter reset or rollover is flagged and does not create negative production without configured handling.

**AC 3.** Normalized output links to order/resource and the mapping revision.

**Exception / edge case:** Equipment timestamp is outside allowed clock skew; event is quarantined or accepted with an explicit quality flag.

**Security and audit implications:** Device credentials are scoped to permitted resources; configuration and manual override are audited.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Labels and explanatory text are localized; identifiers, codes, canonical quantities, and timestamps remain locale-neutral.

**Verification method:** Adapter contract test for duplicates, reset, clock skew, and bad mapping.

**REQUIREMENT 0326 OF 1120  |  MANUFACTURING, PLANNING, AND QUALITY**

## ERP-MFG-046 — Downtime and production loss reason

**Normative requirement:** The system shall record downtime, delay, or lost-production intervals with resource, affected order/operation if known, category code, cause, and attribution source.

**Rationale:** Structured loss events support schedule adherence and capacity feedback without presuming a universal taxonomy.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Configured reason codes are validated against effective profile.

**AC 2.** Overlapping intervals for the same exclusive resource are flagged.

**AC 3.** A correction links to the original event and preserves both records.

**Exception / edge case:** Cause is unknown at time of reporting; provisional status and later classification are supported.

**Security and audit implications:** Reason-code administration and retrospective edits require permission and are audited.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Labels and explanatory text are localized; identifiers, codes, canonical quantities, and timestamps remain locale-neutral.

**Verification method:** Interval-overlap, provisional-cause, and correction tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0327 OF 1120  |  MANUFACTURING, PLANNING, AND QUALITY**

## ERP-MFG-047 — WIP quantity and status projection

**Normative requirement:** The system shall maintain a rebuildable WIP projection by order, operation, item, quantity, unit, status, and relevant lot/serial references using accepted execution and inventory events.

**Rationale:** WIP visibility supports operational control while preserving source ownership of movements.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Projection reconciles to accepted output, issue, transfer, scrap, and completion events for a test fixture.

**AC 2.** Every displayed WIP balance includes an as-of watermark and source event versions.

**AC 3.** Projection rebuild produces the same result from an identical event set.

**Exception / edge case:** A source event is delayed or reordered; the view discloses lag and does not overwrite a newer event with stale state.

**Security and audit implications:** WIP query is tenant/site scoped; trace-level details require appropriate permission.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Labels and explanatory text are localized; identifiers, codes, canonical quantities, and timestamps remain locale-neutral.

**Verification method:** Event replay reconciliation and delayed/out-of-order delivery tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0328 OF 1120  |  MANUFACTURING, PLANNING, AND QUALITY**

## ERP-MFG-048 — WIP transfer between operations

**Normative requirement:** The system shall record controlled WIP transfer, queue, and custody changes between operations with source and destination operation, quantity, time, and status.

**Rationale:** Explicit transfer events make work location and in-process quantity visible.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Transferred quantity does not exceed the transferable open quantity.

**AC 2.** Source/destination operations comply with routing precedence or an approved deviation.

**AC 3.** The transfer event appears in order genealogy and WIP projection.

**Exception / edge case:** WIP is split across multiple downstream operations; each transfer conserves quantity or records a reason-coded loss.

**Security and audit implications:** Transfer and routing-deviation rights are separately permissioned.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Labels and explanatory text are localized; identifiers, codes, canonical quantities, and timestamps remain locale-neutral.

**Verification method:** Quantity conservation and route-deviation integration tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0329 OF 1120  |  MANUFACTURING, PLANNING, AND QUALITY**

## ERP-MFG-049 — Production reporting correction

**Normative requirement:** The system shall correct posted production, labor, downtime, and consumption reports through linked reversal or adjustment records rather than silent overwrite.

**Rationale:** Immutable corrections preserve auditability and downstream reconciliation.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Correction references original event and reason.

**AC 2.** Affected WIP, inventory, quality, and costing projections receive compensating events.

**AC 3.** Correction audit records initiator and approver where maker-checker is enabled.

**Exception / edge case:** Correction is requested after financial period close; the configured finance period policy determines whether adjustment is deferred or escalated.

**Security and audit implications:** Correction and approval permissions are separated; sensitive correction exports are audited.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Labels and explanatory text are localized; identifiers, codes, canonical quantities, and timestamps remain locale-neutral.

**Verification method:** End-to-end correction and replay tests.

**Source references:**

ERP-FINANCE-001

**REQUIREMENT 0330 OF 1120  |  MANUFACTURING, PLANNING, AND QUALITY**

## ERP-MFG-050 — Subcontract operation definition

**Normative requirement:** The system shall identify subcontracted routing operations with supplier reference, service item, expected duration, send/return milestones, and applicable quality checks.

**Rationale:** External processing needs explicit routing and supplier context without transferring procurement ownership.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Subcontract operation references a valid procurement supplier and service configuration.

**AC 2.** Route identifies expected dispatch and return events.

**AC 3.** Supplier/service data used is versioned or snapshotted at order release.

**Exception / edge case:** Supplier is blocked or contract data is expired; the operation cannot be newly released without an authorized exception.

**Security and audit implications:** Supplier changes and subcontract release require appropriate procurement/manufacturing permissions.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Labels and explanatory text are localized; identifiers, codes, canonical quantities, and timestamps remain locale-neutral.

**Verification method:** Supplier contract reference and manufacturing/procurement API integration tests.

**Source references:**

ERP-PROCUREMENT-001

**REQUIREMENT 0331 OF 1120  |  MANUFACTURING, PLANNING, AND QUALITY**

## ERP-MFG-051 — Subcontract material custody and reconciliation

**Normative requirement:** The system shall track materials or WIP sent to and returned from a subcontractor by order, item, quantity, lot/serial, and custody status using Inventory-owned transfer/consignment events.

**Rationale:** Custody must remain distinct from on-hand ownership and manufacturing completion.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Outbound and return transactions reference accepted inventory movement IDs.

**AC 2.** Open subcontract quantity reconciles sent quantity to returned, consumed, scrapped, or outstanding amounts.

**AC 3.** Partial returns are supported without closing the remaining balance.

**Exception / edge case:** Supplier reports loss or additional consumption; discrepancy remains open until authorized disposition.

**Security and audit implications:** External portal/service identity is supplier-scoped; custody adjustments require review and are audited.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Labels and explanatory text are localized; identifiers, codes, canonical quantities, and timestamps remain locale-neutral.

**Verification method:** Contract/reconciliation tests for partial, discrepant, and duplicate messages.

**Source references:**

ERP-INVENTORY-001

**REQUIREMENT 0332 OF 1120  |  MANUFACTURING, PLANNING, AND QUALITY**

## ERP-MFG-052 — Subcontract receipt, quality, and completion

**Normative requirement:** The system shall accept subcontract completion only after receipt status and configured quality disposition are available, then reconcile returned quantity to the open order operation.

**Rationale:** External processing cannot bypass inspection or custody reconciliation controls.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A receipt event can be partial and retains supplier evidence reference.

**AC 2.** Quality-required output remains held until disposition is accepted.

**AC 3.** Operation completion quantity cannot exceed accepted returned quantity.

**Exception / edge case:** Return arrives without the expected order reference; it is quarantined for resolution rather than auto-matched by item alone.

**Security and audit implications:** Receipt, quality disposition, and operation completion permissions remain distinguishable.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Labels and explanatory text are localized; identifiers, codes, canonical quantities, and timestamps remain locale-neutral.

**Verification method:** Integrated receipt-quality-operation workflow test.

**REQUIREMENT 0333 OF 1120  |  MANUFACTURING, PLANNING, AND QUALITY**

## ERP-MFG-053 — Maintenance availability interface

**Normative requirement:** The system shall consume versioned maintenance availability events for manufacturing resources and expose planned maintenance requests or downtime referrals through a defined interface without owning asset maintenance records.

**Rationale:** Capacity planning depends on current equipment availability while maintenance remains the asset-system authority.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Imported event contains resource ID, status, interval, source event ID, and source revision.

**AC 2.** Duplicate or out-of-order maintenance messages do not duplicate or regress availability.

**AC 3.** Unmapped asset/resource links produce an integration exception.

**Exception / edge case:** An emergency breakdown is reported locally before the maintenance system confirms it; temporary unavailability is time-bounded and reconciled.

**Security and audit implications:** Only approved service identities may alter resource availability; audit keeps source and normalization values.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Labels and explanatory text are localized; identifiers, codes, canonical quantities, and timestamps remain locale-neutral.

**Verification method:** Interface contract tests for duplicate, stale, and unmapped events.

**Source references:**

ERP-ASSETS-001

**REQUIREMENT 0334 OF 1120  |  MANUFACTURING, PLANNING, AND QUALITY**

## ERP-MFG-054 — Maintenance-to-schedule coordination

**Normative requirement:** The system shall show the effect of maintenance windows on finite schedules and require planner review when a newly received outage intersects released or frozen operations.

**Rationale:** Coordination minimizes hidden schedule violations and makes disruption response traceable.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** The impact list identifies affected operations, resources, and intervals.

**AC 2.** An accepted outage either reschedules work or creates a documented planner exception.

**AC 3.** Resolved maintenance status does not erase prior schedule impact evidence.

**Exception / edge case:** Maintenance events conflict with planned work but the resource is not exclusively reserved; applicable capacity rule determines conflict severity.

**Security and audit implications:** Planner overrides and maintenance interface changes are permissioned and logged.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Labels and explanatory text are localized; identifiers, codes, canonical quantities, and timestamps remain locale-neutral.

**Verification method:** Schedule impact test with open, frozen, and released operations.

**REQUIREMENT 0335 OF 1120  |  MANUFACTURING, PLANNING, AND QUALITY**

## ERP-MFG-055 — Quality plan version and scope

**Normative requirement:** The system shall manage quality plans as approved, versioned definitions scoped by configured item, supplier, process, site, and effective interval.

**Rationale:** Versioned plans identify the checks applicable to a particular receiving or production context.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Each active plan has owner, revision, scope, effective interval, and approval state.

**AC 2.** Inspection creation stores the exact plan revision.

**AC 3.** Overlapping or missing mandatory plan coverage is detected before activation.

**Exception / edge case:** A plan is not applicable to a site or operation; the system reports a coverage gap instead of selecting a nearest match.

**Security and audit implications:** Plan author, approver, inspector, and disposition authority can be separated.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Plan content supports language-specific instructions while check IDs and units remain stable.

**Verification method:** Applicability matrix and approval-separation tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0336 OF 1120  |  MANUFACTURING, PLANNING, AND QUALITY**

## ERP-MFG-056 — Inspection characteristics and methods

**Normative requirement:** The system shall define inspection characteristics with type, unit, method/instruction reference, acceptance rule, evidence requirement, and result precision as configured.

**Rationale:** Typed checks allow repeatable data capture while acceptance rules remain tenant-owned policy.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Characteristic type validates numeric, categorical, Boolean, or attachment result shape.

**AC 2.** Acceptance evaluation records rule version and raw result.

**AC 3.** Missing required characteristic prevents inspection completion.

**Exception / edge case:** An acceptance limit is missing or not effective at inspection time; result is marked unevaluable and disposition is blocked where configured.

**Security and audit implications:** Limit changes require approval and cannot recalculate prior signed results silently.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Labels and explanatory text are localized; identifiers, codes, canonical quantities, and timestamps remain locale-neutral.

**Verification method:** Input validation and rule-evaluation tests at boundaries.

**Source references:**

ERP-INVENTORY-001

**REQUIREMENT 0337 OF 1120  |  MANUFACTURING, PLANNING, AND QUALITY**

## ERP-MFG-057 — Inspection sampling configuration

**Normative requirement:** The system shall support configurable inspection sampling plans with sample size or selection logic, population basis, and revision provenance, without embedding a universal sampling standard.

**Rationale:** Sampling requirements differ by customer, industry, and jurisdiction and must remain explicit policy.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A sample selection records population size, selected identifiers, plan revision, and selection timestamp.

**AC 2.** The engine rejects a plan whose parameters cannot produce a valid sample for the population.

**AC 3.** A configured full-inspection plan selects every unit or records each required result.

**Exception / edge case:** Population changes after selection; the system invalidates or re-evaluates the sample according to configured policy.

**Security and audit implications:** Sampling-plan authoring and result approval are controlled and audited.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Labels and explanatory text are localized; identifiers, codes, canonical quantities, and timestamps remain locale-neutral.

**Verification method:** Sample boundary tests at zero, one, and threshold population sizes.

**REQUIREMENT 0338 OF 1120  |  MANUFACTURING, PLANNING, AND QUALITY**

## ERP-MFG-058 — Inspection result capture and signature

**Normative requirement:** The system shall record inspection result, unit, method, evidence reference, inspector identity, event time, and completion state for each required characteristic.

**Rationale:** Complete context supports review and downstream disposition.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A result cannot be finalized without all required context and checks.

**AC 2.** Finalized results are immutable; correction creates a linked amended result.

**AC 3.** Evidence attachment has access classification and integrity metadata.

**Exception / edge case:** Inspection is recorded offline and later synchronized; original capture time and server receipt time are retained separately.

**Security and audit implications:** Inspectors can record results only within assigned scope; approval/signature evidence is attributable and protected.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Labels and explanatory text are localized; identifiers, codes, canonical quantities, and timestamps remain locale-neutral.

**Verification method:** API tests for completeness, offline sync, and immutable amendments.

**REQUIREMENT 0339 OF 1120  |  MANUFACTURING, PLANNING, AND QUALITY**

## ERP-MFG-059 — Quality hold and disposition authority

**Normative requirement:** The system shall place affected inventory or WIP on a quality hold and accept release, rework, return, scrap, or other configured disposition only from an authorized quality decision.

**Rationale:** Physical availability and manufacturing progress must respect the current quality decision.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A hold is linked to inspection or nonconformance and applies to identified quantity/lot/serial scope.

**AC 2.** Inventory availability reflects the accepted hold/disposition response.

**AC 3.** Only permitted states allow subsequent movement or production use.

**Exception / edge case:** Quality service response is unknown; affected stock remains held until reconciliation confirms disposition.

**Security and audit implications:** Quality disposition is separate from routine receipt, picking, and production-report permissions; decisions are audited.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Labels and explanatory text are localized; identifiers, codes, canonical quantities, and timestamps remain locale-neutral.

**Verification method:** End-to-end hold enforcement tests across inventory and shop-floor operations.

**Source references:**

ERP-INVENTORY-001

**REQUIREMENT 0340 OF 1120  |  MANUFACTURING, PLANNING, AND QUALITY**

## ERP-MFG-060 — Nonconformance record

**Normative requirement:** The system shall create a nonconformance record linked to affected item, lot/serial, order, operation, supplier, inspection, and containment action as applicable.

**Rationale:** A structured record connects defect evidence to impacted work and material.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Nonconformance ID is unique and references at least one affected object and source event.

**AC 2.** Severity, defect code, status, and disposition follow effective tenant configuration.

**AC 3.** Affected quantity is reconciled to held, accepted, reworked, returned, or scrapped quantities.

**Exception / edge case:** Defect source is not yet known; record supports provisional cause and later controlled classification.

**Security and audit implications:** Creation, investigation, and closure roles are separately configurable; sensitive evidence is access-controlled.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Defect taxonomies and narrative fields support translation without changing code identity.

**Verification method:** Lifecycle tests for unknown cause and quantity reconciliation.

**REQUIREMENT 0341 OF 1120  |  MANUFACTURING, PLANNING, AND QUALITY**

## ERP-MFG-061 — Nonconformance containment and review

**Normative requirement:** The system shall track containment scope, owner, due date, affected locations/orders, review decisions, and effectiveness evidence for each nonconformance.

**Rationale:** Containment prevents affected product from being treated as conforming while investigation proceeds.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Containment action has status, responsible role, scope, and evidence.

**AC 2.** Closure is blocked while mandatory containment remains open.

**AC 3.** Review decision records approver, timestamp, and references to affected stock/WIP actions.

**Exception / edge case:** Affected scope expands after initial containment; the system adds linked scope without erasing previous actions.

**Security and audit implications:** Only authorized reviewers may release containment; all scope changes are audited.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Labels and explanatory text are localized; identifiers, codes, canonical quantities, and timestamps remain locale-neutral.

**Verification method:** Workflow test for expanding scope, overdue action, and blocked closure.

**REQUIREMENT 0342 OF 1120  |  MANUFACTURING, PLANNING, AND QUALITY**

## ERP-MFG-062 — Corrective and preventive action workflow

**Normative requirement:** The system shall support configurable CAPA cases linking root-cause analysis, corrective/preventive actions, owners, due dates, evidence, verification, and effectiveness checks.

**Rationale:** CAPA workflows need measurable closure gates but no universal regulatory terminology or mandated timing is assumed.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A CAPA cannot close until configured actions and effectiveness criteria are satisfied.

**AC 2.** Each action records owner, due date, status, and completion evidence.

**AC 3.** The case links to originating nonconformance(s) and subsequent verification outcome.

**Exception / edge case:** Effectiveness check fails; case reopens or creates a linked follow-up according to configured workflow.

**Security and audit implications:** Action completion and case closure approvals can require different roles; changes remain auditable.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Labels and explanatory text are localized; identifiers, codes, canonical quantities, and timestamps remain locale-neutral.

**Verification method:** Workflow acceptance tests for pass, fail, overdue, and reopen paths.

**REQUIREMENT 0343 OF 1120  |  MANUFACTURING, PLANNING, AND QUALITY**

## ERP-MFG-063 — Quality dashboards and evidence retrieval

**Normative requirement:** The system shall provide scoped quality queries for open inspections, holds, nonconformances, CAPA status, and disposition aging using declared freshness and source ownership.

**Rationale:** Operational visibility supports follow-up without turning reports into authoritative write paths.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Each dashboard declares refresh/as-of time and source modules.

**AC 2.** Filters preserve tenant/entity/site scope.

**AC 3.** Evidence download rechecks current authorization and records export where configured.

**Exception / edge case:** A projection is stale or unavailable; the interface indicates freshness and links to authoritative records.

**Security and audit implications:** Quality exports are separately permissioned, tenant-filtered, and audited.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Labels and explanatory text are localized; identifiers, codes, canonical quantities, and timestamps remain locale-neutral.

**Verification method:** Role-scope and stale-projection/export reauthorization tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0344 OF 1120  |  MANUFACTURING, PLANNING, AND QUALITY**

## ERP-MFG-064 — Lot and serial genealogy capture

**Normative requirement:** The system shall link consumed input lots/serials to produced output lots/serials through immutable transformation events associated with order, operation, time, and quantity.

**Rationale:** Transformation links enable forward and backward traceability across production events. \[4]

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Each transformation records input/output identifiers and quantities with units.

**AC 2.** A trace query from an input returns all linked outputs and from an output returns all linked inputs.

**AC 3.** Missing or inconsistent links are reported as trace gaps, not inferred.

**Exception / edge case:** A production output combines multiple source lots or splits one source lot across multiple outputs; links preserve all many-to-many allocations.

**Security and audit implications:** Trace searches are scope-limited; external trace exports are permissioned and logged.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Localized labels do not alter lot/serial IDs; trace reports can render language-specific captions.

**Verification method:** Forward/backward graph tests including split, merge, and missing-link cases.

**Source references:**

4

**REQUIREMENT 0345 OF 1120  |  MANUFACTURING, PLANNING, AND QUALITY**

## ERP-MFG-065 — Traceability profile and identity capture

**Normative requirement:** The system shall apply configurable lot, serial, or other trace-identity capture rules at configured production, issue, transformation, and output events.

**Rationale:** Capture points vary by product and customer; explicit profiles prevent undocumented universal assumptions.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Each required capture event validates identifier format according to the configured profile.

**AC 2.** A controlled item cannot complete the event with missing mandatory identity.

**AC 3.** The event stores raw scanned identifier and normalized key when normalization is configured.

**Exception / edge case:** Identifier is unreadable or duplicated; the operator receives a controlled exception and no substitute ID is silently assigned.

**Security and audit implications:** Profile changes require approved migration/impact analysis; access to trace searches is scoped.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Identifier input supports Unicode/scanner handling where configured while stable IDs remain exact.

**Verification method:** Profile and barcode parsing tests including duplicate and malformed input.

**Source references:**

4

**REQUIREMENT 0346 OF 1120  |  MANUFACTURING, PLANNING, AND QUALITY**

## ERP-MFG-066 — Genealogy query and trace completeness

**Normative requirement:** The system shall provide forward and backward genealogy queries with traversal depth, quantity reconciliation, event timestamp, source revision, and completeness indicators.

**Rationale:** Users must distinguish a complete trace from a partial path before relying on it operationally.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Query output identifies all traversed events and unresolved edges.

**AC 2.** Completeness status changes to incomplete when required links or source acknowledgements are absent.

**AC 3.** Large query results are bounded and support authorized continuation or export.

**Exception / edge case:** Cycles or duplicate events appear in imported genealogy; query terminates safely and highlights data quality defects.

**Security and audit implications:** Sensitive customer/supplier endpoints are minimized by role; trace export is audited.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Query labels and units localize; event keys remain stable.

**Verification method:** Graph tests for cycles, incomplete paths, pagination, and access control.

**Source references:**

4

**REQUIREMENT 0347 OF 1120  |  MANUFACTURING, PLANNING, AND QUALITY**

## ERP-MFG-067 — Scrap and yield-loss reporting

**Normative requirement:** The system shall record scrap quantity, item, lot/serial when applicable, order/operation, reason code, disposition, and whether inventory or WIP movement is required.

**Rationale:** Scrap is a distinct operational outcome and must reconcile with quality, inventory, and costing.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Scrap report records planned versus actual quantity and configured reason code.

**AC 2.** If physical quantity changes, the system sends an Inventory-owned adjustment/disposal command and waits for its reference.

**AC 3.** Scrap quantity is included in order completion reconciliation.

**Exception / edge case:** Scrap is discovered after order closure; a linked adjustment path preserves the original order result.

**Security and audit implications:** Scrap approval thresholds and disposition permissions are configurable; adjustments are audit-linked.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Reason labels localize while codes and canonical quantities remain stable.

**Verification method:** Integration tests across scrap approval, inventory acknowledgement, and closeout.

**Source references:**

ERP-INVENTORY-001

**REQUIREMENT 0348 OF 1120  |  MANUFACTURING, PLANNING, AND QUALITY**

## ERP-MFG-068 — Rework order and return-to-process

**Normative requirement:** The system shall create a linked rework order or rework operation referencing the originating order, defect/nonconformance, affected quantity, route, and required quality reinspection.

**Rationale:** Rework must preserve original genealogy and defect context while creating an executable corrective path.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Rework quantity cannot exceed identified affected quantity without approved adjustment.

**AC 2.** Rework output links to original lot/serial genealogy and the source nonconformance.

**AC 3.** Rework completion invokes the configured reinspection gate before release.

**Exception / edge case:** Rework changes product identity or revision; new output identity is linked to the original through a transformation event.

**Security and audit implications:** Rework approval and final quality release may require distinct roles; actions are audited.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Rework instructions and defect notes may be localized; source trace IDs are not translated.

**Verification method:** End-to-end rework quantity, identity, and inspection tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0349 OF 1120  |  MANUFACTURING, PLANNING, AND QUALITY**

## ERP-MFG-069 — Manufacturing cost handoff

**Normative requirement:** The system shall publish versioned production cost inputs and actuals to Finance, including order, legal entity, item, quantity, material/labor/machine/subcontract/scrap components where configured, cost dimensions, currency, effective time, and source references.

**Rationale:** Manufacturing supplies operational cost facts while Finance owns valuation policy, accounting, and ledger posting.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Handoff totals reconcile to included source events within declared currency precision.

**AC 2.** Payload identifies costing basis and mapping/profile version.

**AC 3.** Finance acknowledgement or rejection is linked to the handoff ID; retry is idempotent.

**Exception / edge case:** Cost event arrives after finance period closure or mapping is missing; it remains in a visible exception queue and is not silently dropped.

**Security and audit implications:** Cost export and mapping changes require permission; sensitive worker-level detail is minimized.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Currency and numbers are canonical; translated descriptions are supplemental only.

**Verification method:** Finance contract tests for balanced totals, rejected mapping, duplicate delivery, and late period.

**Source references:**

ERP-FINANCE-001

**REQUIREMENT 0350 OF 1120  |  MANUFACTURING, PLANNING, AND QUALITY**

## ERP-MFG-070 — Manufacturing close reconciliation and exception controls

**Normative requirement:** The system shall provide an order-level reconciliation of planned, issued, returned, consumed, completed, scrapped, reworked, subcontracted, held, WIP, and cost-handoff quantities/statuses before configurable close or period reporting.

**Rationale:** Reconciliation exposes differences across independently owned modules before they become unexplained operational or financial results.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** For a controlled fixture, each category reconciles to its source event set and displays any variance.

**AC 2.** Every unresolved variance has owner, age, source reference, and disposition status.

**AC 3.** Close policy blocks or records an approved override for each configured critical exception.

**Exception / edge case:** Inventory or finance is unavailable during close; the system records pending acknowledgement and avoids claiming reconciliation succeeded.

**Security and audit implications:** Exception override, reconciliation export, and close approval are permissioned and audited.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Reconciliation reports localized labels and explicit units/currency while preserving canonical IDs.

**Verification method:** Cross-domain end-to-end test with missing, late, and corrected source events.

**Source references:**

ERP-INVENTORY-001

ERP-FINANCE-001

# Human Resources, Workforce, and Payroll

# 06 — Human Resources, Workforce, and Payroll

## Scope and design intent

This chapter specifies the shared HR and payroll core for a multi-tenant commercial ERP serving mid-market and enterprise employers. It covers person and employment records, organizational workforce structure, recruiting handoff, onboarding, time and absence, employee lifecycle, compensation, payroll calculation and controls, employee self-service, and interfaces to finance and external providers. It does not prescribe any country's labor, tax, social-insurance, privacy, benefits, banking, or statutory reporting law as a universal default.

A tenant enables the jurisdictions, worker categories, legal entities, industry extensions, and rule packages it has reviewed. Every such package must declare scope, effective dates, version, authoritative source reference, owner, approval status, and test evidence. Missing or conflicting mandatory configuration blocks finalization instead of silently using a guessed rule. This boundary is essential because employer duties and forms vary even across workers within a country; for example, the IRS publishes US-specific withholding, depositing, reporting, and recordkeeping instructions \[13]. Employment classification, collective agreements, benefits, and industry requirements likewise remain tenant/jurisdiction configuration questions. The product is not legal advice or a claim of statutory compliance.

## Product and architecture baseline

The requested backend baseline is ASP.NET Core on **.NET 11.0**, with PostgreSQL persistence and a lightweight Next.js App Router frontend. Microsoft's official lifecycle page, updated November 10, 2026, lists .NET 11.0.0 released November 10, 2026 as active Standard Term Support, with support through November 14, 2028; it lists .NET 10 as active LTS \[1]. Thus .NET 11 is the latest stable supported .NET release on the requested November 22, 2026 baseline, while .NET 10 remains the longer-support LTS option. The product owner must deliberately choose between latest-release and LTS servicing policy. Reconfirm Microsoft's official lifecycle and latest patch before implementation and each production release; do not ship a preview or stale patch.

Use ASP.NET Core as the authoritative API and workflow boundary. Keep payroll calculations and authorization on the server. Use PostgreSQL constraints for durable row-level invariants and row-level security for defense-in-depth tenant filtering; RLS is default-deny when enabled without a matching policy, but table owners and BYPASSRLS roles can bypass it, so production roles and migrations must be separated and tested \[2] \[3]. Use transactions and uniqueness constraints for atomic approvals and idempotent payroll execution; retry serialization failures only within a bounded policy \[4]. The frontend uses Next.js Server Components for server-side data and secrets and Client Components only for interactive controls \[5]. No browser code connects directly to PostgreSQL.

Microsoft's current ASP.NET Core localization guidance provides localized resources and culture selection \[15]. Next.js supports locale-aware routing and server-loaded translation dictionaries \[6]. Store stable codes and identifiers separately from display strings. Use BCP 47 language tags for language preferences and content metadata \[11], explicit ISO 4217 currency codes \[10], and distinguish date-only facts from local scheduled times and absolute event instants. PostgreSQL documents distinct date/time types and time-zone-aware timestamps \[14]. Localization changes presentation and input parsing, never payroll arithmetic, permissions, identifiers, or effective-date semantics.

## Actors and permission boundaries

- **Employee / worker:** view permitted personal profile, assignments, payslips, leave balances and workflow state; submit allowed profile changes, time, leave, elections, and evidence.
- **Line manager / delegate:** approve scoped team actions and view only fields required for workforce operations. Reporting relationships are effective-dated; restricted health, bank, tax, and full compensation data are not implicitly exposed.
- **HR operations:** maintain person, employment, organization, position, lifecycle, document, and onboarding records within assigned entities or organizational units.
- **Recruiter / talent system:** manage candidate-side data externally or in an optional integrated ATS; only accepted hires cross into the employee record boundary.
- **Time administrator:** configure schedules, time capture, time rules, and approved adjustments within authorized scopes.
- **Payroll processor:** configure pay groups and process previews, exceptions, and calculations; access to bank/tax secrets is narrowly scoped.
- **Payroll approver / treasury releaser:** independently approve payroll and release payment instructions. Initiator and approver are separated where policy requires; payment release is distinct from calculation approval.
- **Benefits administrator:** configure plans and enrollment/provider interfaces without unrestricted access to unrelated HR data.
- **Finance / controller:** receive payroll journals and benefit accounting interfaces; cannot edit employee source facts or recalculate pay unless separately authorized.
- **Tenant administrator / privacy steward / auditor:** configure roles and policy packages, manage privacy/retention, or inspect logs under narrowly separated duties. Platform support receives time-limited, audited access and is not a tenant-wide default principal.

Authorization combines role, tenant, legal entity, organizational scope, person ownership, workflow state, field classification, and action. Access to view does not imply update, approve, export, or execute. Stronger authentication is required by tenant policy for privileged and high-impact operations; NIST SP 800-63B distinguishes assurance levels and calls for phishing-resistant options at AAL2 \[8]. Privacy policy is configuration-bound: GDPR illustrates rights, purpose, data minimization, and retention obligations in one legal framework, but the applicable law and exceptions must be determined for each tenant and jurisdiction \[9].

## Core entities and workflow

Core records are Tenant; LegalEntity; WorkLocation; OrganizationUnit and effective-dated ReportingRelationship; Person; EmploymentRelationship; Position; Assignment; WorkerCategory; JobProfile; CompensationTerm; Schedule and Calendar; TimeEvent and TimeApproval; LeavePolicy, LeaveRequest, and LeaveLedgerEntry; DocumentReference; PayrollGroup and PayrollPeriod; RulePack; EarningDeductionCode; PayrollRun and immutable PayrollResultLine; PaymentInstructionSnapshot; StatutorySubmission; and GeneralLedgerPostingReference. A person can have multiple concurrent or sequential employment relationships and assignments. Person identity is not the same as employment, legal employer, work location, or payroll identity.

The normal lifecycle is authorized requisition/offer handoff → pre-hire person and employment → onboarding → active assignment → time/leave and compensation events → payroll preflight → calculation and reconciliation → independent approval → payment and statutory handoff → finance posting and period close. Termination, leave, rehire, and corrections are explicit effective-dated transitions. Approved payroll snapshots are immutable; correction, void, and retroactivity create linked records rather than changing historical results. Employee-benefit accounting exports provide source measures and references; accounting recognition and measurement remain the accounting engine’s responsibility (IAS 19 describes accounting for employee benefits, including liabilities and expenses) \[12].

## Major decisions and dependencies

**1. Tenant isolation:** shared-schema tenant IDs plus PostgreSQL RLS and application authorization are the baseline. Tenant context must be transaction-local and fail closed. Database owners, migration principals, support identities, and routine application roles must be distinct. If the deployment chooses database/schema-per-tenant instead, it must preserve the same cross-tenant threat tests and audit semantics.

**2. Effective dating:** employment facts, organization, compensation, rules, schedules, and policies carry validity intervals. Record creation time and effective time are separately represented so late corrections do not erase what was known or applied at a prior run.

**3. Payroll jurisdiction packs:** core provides interfaces and calculation primitives; jurisdiction extensions provide reviewed rates, thresholds, caps, filing schemas, forms, calendars, and rule tests. Regulatory content is versioned, deployable, and independently approved. No default rule package is activated solely because a tenant selects a country.

**4. Money and time:** represent currency as code plus exact amount/scale and versioned rounding policy. Do not aggregate unlike currencies without an explicit exchange-rate event. Store date-only hire/effective dates separately from local schedules and absolute event instants; retain named time zone and disambiguation rule for daylight-saving transitions.

**5. External dependencies:** identity provider and MFA; document/object storage; recruiting/ATS; time clocks; banking/payment providers; statutory authorities; benefits providers; general ledger; localization resource pipeline; and tenant-approved tax/labor rule-data supplier. All integrations require versioned contracts, idempotency, retries, reconciliation, secret management, and external acknowledgment tracking.

**6. Employee benefits boundary:** operational enrollment and payroll deductions are not actuarial valuation or financial reporting. Feed finance with traceable events and let the accounting module apply the reporting framework and estimates.

## Cross-module contracts

- **Finance:** approved run → balanced journal lines by legal entity, currency, account, and cost dimensions; reverse or correct with linked compensating records. Finance returns posting reference and rejection detail.
- **Time and attendance:** only approved, attributable, idempotent time and absence inputs are payroll-eligible. A locked period routes late inputs to retro/off-cycle processing.
- **Recruiting:** accepted offer handoff is idempotent; candidates remain outside the employee master until the configured transition. Preserve source IDs and prevent rehire duplicates.
- **Identity and access:** the identity provider supplies authenticated subject and assurance context; People maps it to a tenant-scoped person and permission set. Employment termination and role changes trigger scoped access review/revocation events.
- **Benefits and external payroll services:** exchange minimum data through versioned adapters; reconcile enrollment, deduction, payment, or filing acknowledgments to source records. No external response silently overwrites an approved People record.
- **Audit, privacy, and records:** cross-module operations carry event IDs, tenant IDs, actor/service identity, correlation IDs, timestamps, and policy versions; the privacy and retention service coordinates holds and purge decisions.

## Risks and controls

The highest risks are cross-tenant data leakage; unauthorized profile/bank/tax changes; rule-package errors; duplicate or omitted payment; irreproducible retro calculations; stale manager access; excessive collection or retention; locale-driven numeric/date misinterpretation; and inaccessible employee workflows. Mitigations include RLS plus application scope tests, field-level masking, dual control, rule-pack fixtures, immutable run snapshots, database uniqueness/idempotency, statement-to-run reconciliation, default-deny policy, explicit time/currency semantics, privacy suppression, and WCAG 2.2 AA testing. WCAG 2.2 is a W3C Recommendation with testable success criteria \[7]. Every legal or industry-specific configuration must be validated by tenant counsel or an accountable domain owner before production use.

## Implementation-ready requirements

The following 70 requirements are the normative People-domain baseline. Acceptance criteria are intended to be independently testable. Configuration is required where law, collective agreement, industry, or employer policy varies.

### ERP-PEOPLE-001 — Tenant data isolation

**Shall statement:** The service shall scope every People-domain record, search, report, file, and asynchronous job to an authenticated tenant and enforce tenant isolation in both application authorization and PostgreSQL row-level security. **Rationale:** A cross-tenant disclosure or mutation would expose highly sensitive employment and compensation data. **Acceptance criteria:**

- A request authenticated for tenant A cannot read, update, delete, or infer counts for tenant B records through APIs, exports, search, or background processing.
- Database integration tests show tenant context is set transaction-locally, missing context returns no rows, and application runtime roles do not own protected tables or have BYPASSRLS.

**Exception / edge case:** A support operator or scheduled job without a tenant context is denied rather than treated as a platform-wide administrator. **Security / audit implications:** Use default-deny tenant predicates and test owner/BYPASSRLS bypass paths; log denied cross-tenant attempts without logging personal field values. **Localization implications:** Tenant locale and legal configuration are independent; locale selection never changes tenant scope. **Verification method:** Automated PostgreSQL RLS and API authorization integration tests, including adversarial tenant-id substitution.

### ERP-PEOPLE-002 — Effective-dated organization hierarchy

**Shall statement:** The system shall maintain effective-dated legal-entity, business-unit, department, team, and reporting-line relationships with explicit validity intervals and controlled hierarchy changes. **Rationale:** Historical organization context is required for approvals, workforce reports, and payroll cost attribution. **Acceptance criteria:**

- A unit can be queried as-of any date and returns the hierarchy effective on that date.
- Overlapping effective intervals for the same exclusive parent relationship are rejected; a future-dated transfer leaves the current hierarchy unchanged until its start date.

**Exception / edge case:** A reorganization may split or merge units; historical assignments retain the former unit rather than being rewritten. **Security / audit implications:** Restrict hierarchy edits to delegated administrators; retain before/after values, actor, reason, and effective date in the audit trail. **Localization implications:** Localized unit names are stored as translations while stable IDs and codes remain locale-neutral. **Verification method:** Temporal boundary tests and API/database constraint tests for overlaps and as-of queries.

### ERP-PEOPLE-003 — Legal entities and work locations

**Shall statement:** The system shall represent employing legal entities separately from physical work locations and associate each employment assignment with the applicable entity and location over time. **Rationale:** Payroll, reporting, access, and applicable labor rules may depend on employing entity and work jurisdiction. **Acceptance criteria:**

- An employee can change work location without changing legal employer, and can change legal employer through a separately audited employment event.
- A location record has a country/region code, time zone identifier, address, active period, and optional jurisdiction-extension references.

**Exception / edge case:** Remote work may cause the employee residence, employing entity, and work location to differ; the system preserves each as a separate fact. **Security / audit implications:** Limit legal-entity changes to HR/payroll roles; protect residential and work-address values under separate field permissions. **Localization implications:** Use locale-aware address schemas and region identifiers; retain source-language address text where transliteration is inappropriate. **Verification method:** Domain/API tests for distinct entity-location relationships and jurisdiction mismatch scenarios.

### ERP-PEOPLE-004 — Person identity profile

**Shall statement:** The system shall maintain a person profile independently from one or more employment relationships, with stable internal identity and configurable demographic fields. **Rationale:** Person-level identity should not be duplicated when employment or assignments change. **Acceptance criteria:**

- A person can be linked to multiple employment records in a tenant without duplicating the person identifier.
- Configured required fields are validated by workflow and jurisdiction without making non-configured demographic fields universally mandatory.

**Exception / edge case:** A rehire creates a new employment relationship linked to the existing person after a duplicate check, while a possible match can be flagged for review rather than auto-merged. **Security / audit implications:** Apply field-level access and masking for identity attributes; audit profile merges, sensitive field changes, and exports. **Localization implications:** Names support Unicode, multiple name components, preferred/display names, and scripts without assuming Western first/last-name ordering. **Verification method:** Schema/API tests with Unicode names, duplicate candidates, and profile merge audit assertions.

### ERP-PEOPLE-005 — Employment relationships and assignments

**Shall statement:** The system shall model each employment relationship with effective-dated terms and one or more separately dated positions, work assignments, managers, and costing distributions. **Rationale:** A person may hold multiple jobs or assignments whose terms and approvals differ. **Acceptance criteria:**

- An employee may hold concurrent assignments with distinct FTE, manager, cost center, work location, and validity dates.
- An assignment cannot start outside its employment relationship unless an authorized exception is approved and recorded.

**Exception / edge case:** Concurrent part-time appointments are allowed where tenant policy permits, even if one person has multiple supervisors. **Security / audit implications:** Assignment visibility follows manager scope and entity permissions; salary and personal data are not inherited automatically from reporting-line access. **Localization implications:** Date displays follow user locale, but effective-date storage and comparisons use unambiguous date semantics. **Verification method:** Integration tests for concurrent assignments, scoped visibility, and effective-date invariants.

### ERP-PEOPLE-006 — Worker categories

**Shall statement:** The system shall support tenant-configured worker categories and engagement types, including employee, fixed-term, seasonal, contractor, and other organization-defined categories, without treating any category as a universal legal determination. **Rationale:** Worker classification is jurisdiction- and fact-specific and must not be hard-coded as a global legal conclusion. **Acceptance criteria:**

- A category can require distinct onboarding fields, approval paths, time rules, and downstream integration mappings.
- Reports and APIs expose the configured category code and its effective period, not a fixed legal status inferred by the product.

**Exception / edge case:** A worker classification change may be backdated only through a privileged correction workflow with a reason and impact assessment. **Security / audit implications:** Restrict classification edits and log the prior/new code, actor, reason, and affected periods. **Localization implications:** Category labels can be translated; underlying configured codes remain stable across language changes. **Verification method:** Configuration and regression tests showing policy variations do not change global classification semantics.

### ERP-PEOPLE-007 — Employment lifecycle transitions

**Shall statement:** The system shall enforce an auditable employment lifecycle with configurable states and permitted transitions, including draft, pre-hire, active, leave, suspended, terminated, and rehired states. **Rationale:** Explicit transition rules prevent inconsistent access, pay eligibility, and workforce status. **Acceptance criteria:**

- Each state transition validates required fields, approvals, effective date, and resulting access/payroll flags.
- A termination effective date closes future assignments and triggers configured access and payroll tasks without deleting historical records.

**Exception / edge case:** A rescinded termination or correction is represented as a new approved event that restores the appropriate state; it does not erase the original event. **Security / audit implications:** Separate the authority to approve termination from the authority to execute payroll close; audit all transitions and overrides. **Localization implications:** State labels and employee communications are localized; state codes and event dates are locale-independent. **Verification method:** State-machine unit tests and end-to-end lifecycle tests, including rescinded and future-dated termination.

### ERP-PEOPLE-008 — Position and headcount control

**Shall statement:** The system shall maintain position records with planned FTE, status, reporting unit, grade, and optional budget authorization, and shall control assignment against configured headcount rules. **Rationale:** Position control makes staffing plans and actual workforce commitments reconcilable. **Acceptance criteria:**

- A tenant can configure whether a position permits one incumbent, shared incumbents, or no position assignment.
- An assignment exceeding configured FTE/headcount limits is blocked or routed to an authorized exception approval with the variance recorded.

**Exception / edge case:** A vacant position may remain funded but inactive for hiring; the system shall distinguish vacancy from cancellation. **Security / audit implications:** Limit position-budget overrides; record approver, requested/approved FTE, and reason. **Localization implications:** Position title and organizational labels may be translated without translating stable job/position codes. **Verification method:** Rules-engine tests for single-incumbent, shared-position, vacancy, and exception-approval cases.

### ERP-PEOPLE-009 — Requisition authorization

**Shall statement:** The system shall support controlled requisitions linked to an approved position or explicitly authorized non-position hiring request, with an approval history and hiring status. **Rationale:** Recruiting commitments should be traceable to workforce and budget authority. **Acceptance criteria:**

- A requisition cannot be posted or moved to offer stage until required approvals and budget fields are complete.
- Closing a requisition prevents new offers but preserves candidate and approval history under configured retention.

**Exception / edge case:** Urgent or replacement hiring can use an emergency route only if enabled and followed by a configured retrospective approval. **Security / audit implications:** Limit compensation-range visibility and approval actions by role; log all approval decisions and changes. **Localization implications:** Translate applicant-facing content per locale while retaining the approved internal requisition values and code. **Verification method:** Domain/API integration tests shall execute acceptance criteria 1–2 plus a fixture for the stated exception; assert the persisted outcome, returned status, and relevant audit/security effects.

### ERP-PEOPLE-010 — Recruiting system boundary

**Shall statement:** The People domain shall expose an integration contract for candidate, offer, and hired-person handoff, while keeping applicant tracking workflows optional and separable from the employee master record. **Rationale:** Candidate pipelines are often delivered by specialist systems and should not force duplicate candidate data into employee records. **Acceptance criteria:**

- A signed offer acceptance event can create a pre-hire person/employment record idempotently using an external source key.
- A rejected or withdrawn candidate does not create an active employment or payroll record.

**Exception / edge case:** A returning applicant matching an existing worker is linked for authorized review rather than creating an uncontrolled duplicate person. **Security / audit implications:** Candidate data is restricted to recruiting roles until a documented handoff; log handoff and matching decisions. **Localization implications:** Preserve candidate language preference and localized offer version metadata across the handoff. **Verification method:** Contract tests against mock ATS payloads for duplicates, retries, and rejected-candidate cases.

### ERP-PEOPLE-011 — Onboarding task orchestration
