## ERP-PEOPLE-056 — Historical payroll inquiry

**Normative requirement:** The system shall provide authorized as-of payroll inquiry by worker, assignment, period, and pay code against immutable approved and corrected run snapshots.

**Rationale:** Historical inquiry is needed for employee service, audit, tax, and finance reconciliation.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** An authorized query reproduces the approved result as issued and presents later adjustment runs separately.

**AC 2.** A user outside the worker/entity scope cannot access result lines, bank details, or protected tax inputs through search, API, or export.

**Exception / edge case:** A worker was rehired under a new employment record; inquiry supports both relationships without merging their payroll periods.

**Security and audit implications:** Apply least privilege, masking, query-level audit for sensitive fields, and export controls.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Render historical labels in the selected display language where available while preserving original statement and filing artifacts.

**Verification method:** Payroll calculation and interface tests shall execute acceptance criteria 1–2 plus a fixture for the stated exception; assert the persisted outcome, returned status, and relevant audit/security effects.

## ERP-PEOPLE-057 — Industry extension policy boundary

**Normative requirement:** The system shall expose extension points for industry-specific qualifications, union agreements, fatigue limits, safety credentials, and workforce rules, with package ownership, scope, version, and validation contracts.

**Rationale:** Configured industry behavior must extend common workflows without making one sector’s rules appear universal.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** An extension can add fields, predicates, validation, and approval steps to an identified workflow without modifying core worker identity or payroll result semantics.

**AC 2.** The platform rejects activation of an extension whose declared dependencies or compatibility version are missing.

**Exception / edge case:** An extension package becomes unsupported; existing records remain readable and new affected transactions are blocked or placed into a controlled fallback.

**Security and audit implications:** Extensions execute with least privilege, cannot bypass tenant scoping or audit controls, and require signed/versioned release approval.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Extension-owned labels and help text provide language resources or use a visible tenant-approved fallback language.

## ERP-PEOPLE-058 — Training and credential records

**Normative requirement:** The system shall track training, certifications, licenses, renewal dates, issuing body, evidence reference, and assignment applicability as effective-dated workforce records.

**Rationale:** Credential tracking supports role readiness and regulated-industry requirements without asserting universal qualification law.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A credential can be marked current, expiring, expired, waived, or unverified based on configured date rules and evidence status.

**AC 2.** A configured assignment requirement blocks assignment or creates a designated exception approval when a required credential is expired or missing.

**Exception / edge case:** A credential is valid only in a particular region or employer; its applicability scope is checked before flagging it as current.

**Security and audit implications:** Protect evidence files and personal identifiers; restrict waiver authority and audit expiration overrides.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Credential names, course instructions, and reminders are localized; issuing-body names and original evidence language are retained.

## ERP-PEOPLE-059 — Workforce plan and FTE forecast

**Normative requirement:** The system shall support versioned workforce plans that project positions, FTE, worker category, cost center, and period without changing actual employment or payroll records.

**Rationale:** Planning needs scenario modeling separate from committed headcount and payroll facts.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A forecast scenario has owner, version, planning horizon, assumptions, and actual-versus-plan comparison dimensions.

**AC 2.** Promoting a plan into approved positions or requisitions requires an explicit workflow and creates new operational records linked to the scenario.

**Exception / edge case:** An employee is assigned fractionally to multiple positions; forecast FTE totals follow configured allocation constraints and surface over-allocation.

**Security and audit implications:** Restrict salary assumptions and aggregate small cohorts where configured; audit scenario export and promotion.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Planning periods and monetary assumptions are displayed by locale with explicit currency and time basis.

## ERP-PEOPLE-060 — Labor and cost allocation

**Normative requirement:** The system shall support effective-dated distribution of worked time and compensation across configured cost centers, projects, grants, or other finance dimensions, with validation and reconciliation.

**Rationale:** Operational labor may benefit multiple accounting destinations and must post consistently.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Each allocation set totals 100 percent or an explicitly configured unit total before approval.

**AC 2.** Payroll lines use the allocation effective for the work period and reconcile allocated subtotals to original compensation within configured rounding tolerance.

**Exception / edge case:** A cost object becomes inactive mid-period; the configured fallback or hold-for-review path is applied and recorded.

**Security and audit implications:** Limit cost allocation changes and payroll cost visibility; audit overrides and downstream journal dimensions.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Dimension labels may be localized; percentage precision and currency rounding are explicitly configured and locale-neutral.

## ERP-PEOPLE-061 — People analytics and privacy thresholds

**Normative requirement:** The system shall provide permission-filtered workforce analytics with stable metric definitions, effective-date semantics, and configurable suppression of small identifiable groups.

**Rationale:** Workforce trends are useful, but small or sensitive groups can disclose individual information.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A report defines its population, as-of date, filters, denominator, and metric formula; a test dataset yields the documented result.

**AC 2.** A configured suppression threshold hides or aggregates cells below the threshold in UI, API, and export, including complementary cells that would reveal a suppressed value.

**Exception / edge case:** A senior executive’s narrow filter returns one person; the report widens or suppresses the value rather than exposing a sensitive attribute.

**Security and audit implications:** Enforce row/field permissions before aggregation; audit sensitive report exports and prevent direct identifiers in telemetry.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Report titles and definitions are localized while metric formulas, time periods, and currency basis remain discoverable.

**Verification method:** Authorization and privacy-control integration tests shall execute acceptance criteria 1–2 plus a fixture for the stated exception; assert the persisted outcome, returned status, and relevant audit/security effects.

## ERP-PEOPLE-062 — Bulk data import and export

**Normative requirement:** The system shall provide schema-versioned, tenant-scoped import/export jobs with validation preview, row-level outcomes, idempotency, and protected file handling.

**Rationale:** Bulk operations are operationally necessary but can bypass normal controls if not designed safely.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** An import validates the complete file and produces accepted/rejected row counts plus row-specific error codes before commit.

**AC 2.** A repeated import using the same job key cannot duplicate person, time, or payroll records; exports enforce the requesting user’s field and row scopes.

**Exception / edge case:** A file contains malformed encoding, duplicate natural keys, or mixed tenants; the job fails safely or quarantines invalid rows without partial unreported commits.

**Security and audit implications:** Encrypt uploads/downloads, expire links, scan files, audit job owner and schema version, and exclude secrets from error logs.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Accept Unicode and documented locale-specific input formats; require explicit date, decimal, and currency conventions rather than guessing ambiguous values.

**Verification method:** Contract, workflow, and configuration tests shall execute acceptance criteria 1–2 plus a fixture for the stated exception; assert the persisted outcome, returned status, and relevant audit/security effects.

## ERP-PEOPLE-063 — People-domain API and event contracts

**Normative requirement:** The service shall publish versioned APIs and domain events for worker lifecycle, assignment, time approval, leave, and payroll status using stable identifiers, tenant context, and idempotency semantics.

**Rationale:** Other ERP modules and external providers need reliable contracts without direct access to internal tables.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Contract tests validate required fields, schema version, authorization scope, error codes, and idempotent retry behavior for each published operation.

**AC 2.** Events are emitted only after the source transaction commits and include event ID, tenant ID, effective time, and correlation ID.

**Exception / edge case:** A consumer is offline or receives events out of order; it can replay or deduplicate without changing the source-of-truth record.

**Security and audit implications:** Authenticate clients, minimize personal data in events, redact sensitive payloads, and log subscription and delivery failures.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Event code values and timestamps are locale-neutral; human-readable descriptions are consumer-localized.

**Verification method:** Contract, workflow, and configuration tests shall execute acceptance criteria 1–2 plus a fixture for the stated exception; assert the persisted outcome, returned status, and relevant audit/security effects.

## ERP-PEOPLE-064 — Retention, archival, and purge operations

**Normative requirement:** The system shall support tenant-configured archival, legal hold, anonymization, and purge operations by People-data class, with dry-run counts and evidence of completion.

**Rationale:** Organizations need a controlled lifecycle for employee records while meeting variable retention duties.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A dry run reports candidate count by data class, jurisdiction policy, dependency, and legal hold before any destructive execution.

**AC 2.** A completed purge prevents ordinary API and search retrieval of purged content and produces a non-sensitive run manifest with counts and policy version.

**Exception / edge case:** A record is referenced by an open payroll dispute, court order, or statutory filing; the hold/dependency prevents deletion and identifies the accountable owner.

**Security and audit implications:** Purge authorization is separated from configuration where possible; securely delete file references, audit job access, and protect manifests from exposing identities.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Employee notices and policy summaries are localized; retention dates are calculated from configured legal/event anchors, not display locale.

**Verification method:** Authorization and privacy-control integration tests shall execute acceptance criteria 1–2 plus a fixture for the stated exception; assert the persisted outcome, returned status, and relevant audit/security effects.

**REQUIREMENT 0415 OF 1120  |  HUMAN RESOURCES, WORKFORCE, AND PAYROLL**

## ERP-PEOPLE-065 — Date, time-zone, and calendar semantics

**Normative requirement:** The system shall distinguish date-only employment facts, local wall-clock schedule times, and absolute event instants, and shall persist the relevant named time zone and interpretation.

**Rationale:** PostgreSQL supports separate date/time types and timezone-aware timestamps; conflating date-only facts with instants causes payroll and schedule errors \[14].

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A date-only hire date is unchanged when viewed in another time zone; a clock punch round-trips to the same instant and its original zone.

**AC 2.** Tests across daylight-saving gaps/overlaps and midnight boundaries either apply a configured resolution rule or return an explicit ambiguity error.

**Exception / edge case:** A region changes its time-zone rules; historical instants remain stable and future schedules use the updated rule data after review.

**Security and audit implications:** Audit original device time, normalized instant, zone, and resolution decision for pay-affecting events.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Use locale for display only; accept localized input with explicit parsing and reject ambiguous dates unless the user confirms.

**Verification method:** Time/absence workflow boundary and integration tests shall execute acceptance criteria 1–2 plus a fixture for the stated exception; assert the persisted outcome, returned status, and relevant audit/security effects.

**REQUIREMENT 0416 OF 1120  |  HUMAN RESOURCES, WORKFORCE, AND PAYROLL**

## ERP-PEOPLE-066 — Multilingual content and locale preference

**Normative requirement:** The system shall support tenant-supported language tags, user language preferences, localized interface resources, and per-record translated content with an explicit source-language and fallback policy.

**Rationale:** A commercial ERP must serve multilingual tenants without conflating translation with underlying facts; IETF BCP 47 defines language tags \[11], while ASP.NET Core and Next.js provide documented localization patterns \[15] \[6].

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A user selecting a supported language sees translated interface resources, and the selected language persists across authenticated sessions.

**AC 2.** A missing translation uses the configured fallback and exposes the source language for content that is not translated; unsupported tags are rejected or normalized per registry-aware rules.

**Exception / edge case:** The tenant removes a language that is still referenced by a saved notice; the original content and tag remain intact while new user-facing rendering falls back.

**Security and audit implications:** Avoid localization-dependent authorization or identifiers; audit changes to official templates and language preferences only where they affect controlled output.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Support script, region, right-to-left presentation, Unicode normalization-safe search, and translated validation messages.

**Verification method:** Locale-matrix or accessibility conformance tests shall execute acceptance criteria 1–2 plus a fixture for the stated exception; assert the persisted outcome, returned status, and relevant audit/security effects.

**REQUIREMENT 0417 OF 1120  |  HUMAN RESOURCES, WORKFORCE, AND PAYROLL**

## ERP-PEOPLE-067 — Accessible and responsive People workflows

**Normative requirement:** The Next.js user interface shall provide accessible keyboard-operable, screen-reader-labeled, responsive HR, workforce, and payroll workflows, targeting WCAG 2.2 Level AA unless applicable law or contract requires otherwise \[7].

**Rationale:** Employees and administrators need equitable access to critical employment and pay functions; WCAG 2.2 defines testable success criteria \[7].

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Automated checks and manual keyboard/screen-reader tests cover login, profile update, time entry, leave request, manager approval, and payslip access with no critical blocker.

**AC 2.** At 200 percent zoom and narrow viewport widths, core workflow content and controls remain available without loss of information or forced horizontal scrolling for ordinary text.

**Exception / edge case:** A chart or signature interaction cannot be operated with keyboard alone; an equivalent accessible data/table or alternate confirmation path is provided.

**Security and audit implications:** Accessible authentication avoids revealing protected data on error; ensure focus management and secure timeout warnings for payroll actions.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Test translated layouts including right-to-left and long-string expansion; use locale-appropriate accessible names and document language tags.

**Verification method:** Authorization and privacy-control integration tests shall execute acceptance criteria 1–2 plus a fixture for the stated exception; assert the persisted outcome, returned status, and relevant audit/security effects.

**REQUIREMENT 0418 OF 1120  |  HUMAN RESOURCES, WORKFORCE, AND PAYROLL**

## ERP-PEOPLE-068 — Authentication and privileged actions

**Normative requirement:** The People service shall integrate with the tenant identity provider, support configurable multi-factor and step-up authentication for high-risk operations, and enforce session reauthentication for designated payroll and sensitive-data actions.

**Rationale:** Strong authentication and session controls reduce risk when accessing payroll or personal data; NIST SP 800-63B defines assurance-level and phishing-resistant authentication guidance \[8].

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A configured high-risk action is denied or step-up challenged when the session lacks the required assurance or is expired.

**AC 2.** Credential recovery, authenticator replacement, and privileged role assignment generate notifications and auditable security events.

**Exception / edge case:** An external identity provider is unavailable; the system fails closed for protected actions and never silently downgrades assurance.

**Security and audit implications:** Do not store identity-provider secrets in client code; enforce secure cookies, CSRF protections, session expiry, and risk-based step-up policy.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Authentication screens and recovery instructions are localized without changing assurance policy or bypassing factors.

**Verification method:** Authorization and privacy-control integration tests shall execute acceptance criteria 1–2 plus a fixture for the stated exception; assert the persisted outcome, returned status, and relevant audit/security effects.

**REQUIREMENT 0419 OF 1120  |  HUMAN RESOURCES, WORKFORCE, AND PAYROLL**

## ERP-PEOPLE-069 — Application and database transaction integrity

**Normative requirement:** The service shall perform multi-record HR and payroll state changes atomically, use database constraints for row-level invariants, and handle serialization or uniqueness conflicts with bounded retries and user-visible status.

**Rationale:** PostgreSQL documents row and table constraints and isolation behaviors; transactional design protects concurrent approvals and payroll execution \[3] \[4].

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A forced failure between related writes leaves either all required records committed or none, and a retry does not duplicate business events.

**AC 2.** Concurrent requests to consume the same unique assignment/payroll key produce one valid outcome and a deterministic conflict response.

**Exception / edge case:** A serialization failure or deadlock exhausts the bounded retry policy; the transaction is rolled back and the user receives a safe retryable error.

**Security and audit implications:** Use parameterized queries, tenant-aware constraints, least-privilege database roles, and log transaction IDs without personal payloads.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Error messages and numbers are localized at the API/UI boundary; database comparison and validation semantics remain locale-independent.

**Verification method:** Domain/API integration tests shall execute acceptance criteria 1–2 plus a fixture for the stated exception; assert the persisted outcome, returned status, and relevant audit/security effects.

**REQUIREMENT 0420 OF 1120  |  HUMAN RESOURCES, WORKFORCE, AND PAYROLL**

## ERP-PEOPLE-070 — Lightweight frontend and secure server boundary

**Normative requirement:** The Next.js frontend shall use Server Components for server-only data access and secrets, use Client Components only where interaction requires them, and call the ASP.NET Core service through authenticated contracts rather than direct database access.

**Rationale:** Next.js documents server/client component boundaries and keeping secrets on the server \[5]; a lightweight frontend limits client exposure and payload.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Static analysis/build checks fail if protected API secrets or database connection strings are imported into a client bundle.

**AC 2.** Browser network inspection shows payroll/profile data is returned only for an authorized request and no browser component connects directly to PostgreSQL.

**Exception / edge case:** An interactive filter requires client state; only the minimal approved data and handlers cross the server/client boundary.

**Security and audit implications:** Apply output encoding, CSRF protection for cookie-authenticated mutations, secure headers, and no-store caching for sensitive responses.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Route locale and dictionaries through the documented Next.js localization pattern; cache keys include locale and tenant-safe authorization context.

**Verification method:** Frontend build-boundary and browser-security tests shall execute acceptance criteria 1–2 plus a fixture for the stated exception; assert the persisted outcome, returned status, and relevant audit/security effects.

# Projects, Service Management, and Fixed Assets

# Chapter 07 — Projects, Service Management, and Fixed Assets

## Domain design

### Scope and boundaries

This chapter specifies project delivery and cost control, customer/service operations including field work, and tangible fixed-asset lifecycle records. It covers the shared controls needed to connect those processes in a multi-tenant commercial ERP. Project accounting and planning here consume authoritative accounting, procurement, inventory, HR, customer, and billing services; they do not replace them. Service management covers request-to-resolution and work-order execution, not a universal ITIL implementation or every industry’s regulated maintenance regime. Asset management spans operational identity and book-based asset accounting, not a universal statement of legal capitalization policy.

International accounting is a configurable boundary. IAS 16 describes PPE recognition, initial cost, carrying amount, depreciation, and impairment topics; the ERP therefore models book-specific policy, evidence, and schedules, but tenant finance administrators must select the applicable accounting framework, jurisdiction, elections, and effective policy. It must not infer a tax rule or accounting treatment from locale or asset type alone. IFRS Foundation materials are standards information, not a substitute for locally adopted law or professional interpretation. \[6] Similarly, ISO 55000:2024 supplies asset-management vocabulary, overview, and principles; conformance to that standard is outside the product’s claim unless separately assessed. \[7]

Service extensions are configurable by offering, entitlement, SLA calendar, warranty, work type, maintenance plan, and evidence rule. Industry packs may add specialized approvals, safety permits, calibration, regulated maintenance, public-sector grant tracking, or industry-specific asset classes; those must be versioned extensions with explicit scope and jurisdiction, not global assumptions. Contract interpretation, tax, labor rules, records retention, and signature validity require entity/jurisdiction configuration and customer validation.

### Actors

Core actors are project manager, portfolio manager, project controller, worker/consultant, timesheet approver, service agent, service supervisor, dispatcher, field technician, customer/contact, contract manager, inventory operator, asset custodian, fixed-asset accountant, tax/accounting policy administrator, finance approver, auditor, tenant administrator, and integration service principal. A user may hold several roles, but approvals, posting, master-data administration, and privileged cross-entity access are independently assignable and support maker-checker controls.

### Core entities and source of truth

The project aggregate includes project, legal entity, customer/contract reference, hierarchy/work package, schedule and baseline revisions, budget, resource demand/assignment, timesheet, expense, commitment, actual-cost event, change request, and billing candidate. Approved time and expense are source facts; a posting service creates immutable actuals and links them to general-ledger, payroll, AP, or billing results.

The service aggregate includes service offering/version, account/contact, installed-base asset, entitlement result, case and append-only event stream, SLA clocks, queue/assignment, work order, appointment, parts movement reference, labor/expense, diagnosis, customer communication, warranty/RMA, and charge candidate. The case owns customer communication and SLA state; the work order owns field execution. Both refer to the same installed-base asset identity where applicable.

The fixed-asset aggregate includes asset identity/class, one or more asset books, component hierarchy, acquisition/CIP lineage, effective-dated location/custody history, depreciation profile and schedule, impairment/revaluation, service history link, physical verification, and retirement. The general ledger remains authoritative for posted financial balances. Asset book schedules supply the subledger detail and journal candidates. The ERP should reconcile, not silently overwrite, a mismatch between subledger and ledger.

### Principal workflows

Project initiation establishes entity, customer/contract, currency, manager, plan and access scope. Planning versions scope, schedule, resource demand, and budget. Work execution creates approved time, expenses, procurement commitments, and cost actuals. Change control versions approved scope or funding. Billing candidates are released only after contract evidence and approval. Closure checks open commitments, unbilled work, unresolved changes, and finance gates.

Service intake resolves a service offering and as-of entitlement, establishes response/resolution targets using the correct contract calendar, and routes to a queue. Triage may spawn one or more work orders. Dispatch assigns a qualified technician and appointment. The technician captures parts, labor, diagnostic codes, and completion evidence; approved charge candidates flow to billing. Resolution and closure record customer-visible outcomes. Preventive plans create work orders independently of customer case intake.

Asset acquisition begins as a proposal from procurement or approved project cost. Eligible costs may accumulate in CIP and are settled through an approved allocation into one or more asset records. In-service date and book-specific assumptions drive schedules. Period processing calculates, reviews, and posts depreciation through a versioned ledger contract. Transfer, count, reassessment, impairment/revaluation, maintenance, and retirement are separate effective-dated events. The operational asset register and every accounting book retain distinct histories.

### Permission boundaries and audit

All domain access starts with tenant scope, then applies legal entity, customer/account, region, project, record sensitivity, and action permissions. Read, create, approve, post, export, administer, and retention operations are separate privileges. Integrations use scoped service identities, idempotency keys, and correlation IDs. Row-level database security can provide an additional boundary in a shared-table PostgreSQL deployment, but PostgreSQL documents that table owners, superusers, or BYPASSRLS roles may bypass policies, and that row security does not govern every operation; therefore it is defense in depth, not a replacement for application authorization and test coverage. \[4]

Material decisions append actor, timestamp, tenant, entity, object, decision, reason, source, and correlation data to an audit history. Posted financial events are corrected by reversals or compensating entries, not destructive edits. Audit content and retention are configurable because privacy, tax, labor, customer-contract, and statutory retention requirements vary by deployment. The general security posture should be selected and risk-assessed by the deploying organization; NIST SP 800-53 is a flexible catalog of security and privacy controls, not a universal certification claim for this product. \[10]

### Internationalization and user experience

Tenant default locale, user UI locale, customer communication locale, entity time zone, book calendar, and currency are separate settings. UTF-8/Unicode is required for authored and imported text. Keep machine codes and identifiers stable, preserve user-authored original text, and use translated labels for interface and approved templates. Resolve locale explicitly: user preference for UI, customer/contact preference for outbound communication, and legal-entity or book configuration for accounting output. Format dates, numbers, currencies, units, and addresses at the display boundary; retain canonical values, currencies, instants, and time zones for calculations. Right-to-left layouts, language metadata, localized validation, search behavior, and translated workflow labels require end-to-end tests. W3C authoring guidance recommends UTF-8 and a declared page language; WCAG 2.2 provides testable success criteria and is the recommended web accessibility baseline, subject to the tenant’s applicable conformance obligations. \[8] \[9]

### Platform and architecture decisions

Backend baseline: ASP.NET Core on .NET 11, using the latest supported servicing patch available at build/deployment time. Microsoft’s official policy, last updated 2026-11-10, lists .NET 11 GA/STS, active through 2028-11-14, and .NET 10 LTS, active through the same date. As of 2026-11-22, .NET 11 is the latest stable release, while .NET 10 remains the LTS alternative; the requested baseline selects the latest stable supported release. Reconfirm Microsoft’s policy and patch level when implementation starts and during every release train, because the release cadence is annual and servicing updates are monthly. \[1] \[2]

Database baseline: PostgreSQL 19.0 is listed by the PostgreSQL project as released 2026-11-19 and supported through 2031-11-19; its policy recommends the current minor release for each supported major. At implementation, reconfirm the current supported major/minor, hosting provider compatibility, extensions, and migration path. \[3] Use explicit tenant-scoped keys and referential constraints. If shared-table tenancy uses row-level security, test policies using the actual runtime role and ensure migration/maintenance roles cannot be used by normal requests. \[4]

Frontend baseline: lightweight Next.js with server rendering only where it adds value, keeping domain rules and authorization in ASP.NET Core rather than duplicating them in client components. Next.js documents Node.js server and Docker deployment paths with full framework support; static export has limited feature support. Select server/Docker deployment for authenticated ERP experiences that require runtime capabilities, and pin/reconfirm a supported Next.js and Node.js version when deployment is specified. \[5]

The system is modular, with bounded contexts and versioned APIs/events. A modular monolith is a valid first deployment; the contracts must not assume distributed microservices. Use PostgreSQL transactions for atomic updates to each bounded aggregate, an outbox or equivalent for reliable asynchronous handoffs, optimistic concurrency for user edits, and idempotency for external retries. Document exact ownership of shared references and use stable public IDs rather than cross-module table coupling.

### Dependencies and cross-module contracts

Required upstream references include tenant/legal entity and chart-of-accounts configuration; customer/account/contact and contract master; project/resource and HR identity; procurement/AP commitments and costs; inventory availability and stock movement; time/expense policy; currency-rate service; tax determination; general ledger and fiscal periods; receivables/billing; document storage; identity provider; notification delivery; and, when deployed, lease-accounting, payroll, mobile/offline, and customer-portal services.

Project time, cost, commitment, and billing candidates must carry source IDs, source versions, currency, effective date, entity, work package, and idempotency key where appropriate. Service parts use the inventory service as stock authority. Asset journals use the general ledger as posting authority. Cross-module handoffs acknowledge each source event and return machine-readable rejection reasons. Avoid dual ownership: project actuals do not become the GL; case state does not replace work-order execution state; service maintenance expense does not automatically become asset cost; and the asset register does not replace posted ledger balances.

### Major decisions and risks

Keep the core workflow semantics configurable but not arbitrary: tenant configuration may select allowed states, approvals, calendars, thresholds, tax/accounting books, and extensions, while stable invariants remain enforced by code. Use effective-dated versions for rules so historical outcomes can be reproduced. Configure cross-entity access and billing rather than assume one universal corporate structure. Separate commercial project delivery from generic task/project boards. Separate customer support case management from field-service execution. Separate physical asset custody from book-specific accounting value.

Key risks are tenant data leakage; untraceable manual changes to financial actuals; duplicate postings during retry; stale calculations during concurrent budget, stock, capacity, or depreciation work; time-zone and daylight-saving errors; untranslated customer notifications; inaccessible critical workflows; policy drift between tax/accounting profiles and actual law; customer-data exposure through attachments; and unbounded industry customization. Mitigate with negative authorization tests, immutable posting/reversal, idempotent contracts, time-zone fixtures, translation/RTL and accessibility checks, policy version evidence, scoped document access, and a controlled extension model. The requirements below are the normative, testable baseline.

## Projects, Service Management, and Fixed Assets — requirement cards

**REQUIREMENT 0421 OF 1120  |  PROJECTS, SERVICE MANAGEMENT, AND FIXED ASSETS**

## ERP-ASSETS-001 — Project identity and legal ownership

**Normative requirement:** The system shall assign each project a tenant-scoped immutable identifier and require one owning legal entity, project manager, lifecycle state, and project currency.

**Rationale:** Stable identity and legal ownership are prerequisites for access control, cost collection, reporting, and posting.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Create two tenant projects with the same display code; identifiers remain distinct and tenant-local uniqueness rules are enforced.

**AC 2.** Reject activation without an owner entity, manager, currency, or configured initial state.

**AC 3.** Changing the display code leaves the immutable ID and existing references unchanged.

**Exception / edge case:** A project transfer to another legal entity is a controlled migration, not an edit to already-posted transactions.

**Security and audit implications:** Audit creation, code changes, legal-entity transfer, and status changes; restrict transfers to designated finance administrators.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Display names and descriptions are translatable; identifiers remain locale-neutral and project currency is not inferred from interface locale.

**Verification method:** Automated integration/acceptance tests for the stated scenarios, plus role-based negative tests and audit-record inspection where security or approval is involved.

**REQUIREMENT 0422 OF 1120  |  PROJECTS, SERVICE MANAGEMENT, AND FIXED ASSETS**

## ERP-ASSETS-002 — Project lifecycle state machine

**Normative requirement:** The system shall enforce configurable project states and permitted transitions, with transition guards for approval, start, hold, completion, and closure.

**Rationale:** A controlled lifecycle prevents work and costs from bypassing readiness, review, or close controls.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Attempt every configured valid transition and confirm state, timestamp, actor, and event are recorded.

**AC 2.** Reject a transition when its configured guard is unmet and return the unmet guard codes.

**AC 3.** A closed project rejects new postings while authorized users can view history.

**Exception / edge case:** If an administrator retires a state used by open projects, keep those projects resolvable under the prior state version and block new selection of the retired state.

**Security and audit implications:** State-model administrators may configure transitions; users cannot self-approve a transition requiring their own approval.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** State labels and guard explanations are localized; persisted state keys are stable across locales.

**Verification method:** Automated integration/acceptance tests for the stated scenarios, plus role-based negative tests and audit-record inspection where security or approval is involved.

**REQUIREMENT 0423 OF 1120  |  PROJECTS, SERVICE MANAGEMENT, AND FIXED ASSETS**

## ERP-ASSETS-003 — Project hierarchy and work breakdown

**Normative requirement:** The system shall support tenant-scoped project, phase, and work-package hierarchy with parent-child validation and configurable coding rules.

**Rationale:** A work breakdown structure supplies consistent planning and cost-control dimensions.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Reject a node whose parent belongs to another project or creates a cycle.

**AC 2.** Enforce configured code uniqueness within the project and retain node IDs when labels/codes change.

**AC 3.** Roll-up totals for a parent equal the sum of included child values for a fixed period and currency.

**Exception / edge case:** If a work package has posted actuals, require an authorized reclassification event before moving it to another parent.

**Security and audit implications:** Permission checks apply to the project and inherited nodes; audit hierarchy moves and code changes.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Node names, descriptions, and work-package instructions support localized values; codes are locale-independent.

**Verification method:** Automated integration/acceptance tests for the stated scenarios, plus role-based negative tests and audit-record inspection where security or approval is involved.

**REQUIREMENT 0424 OF 1120  |  PROJECTS, SERVICE MANAGEMENT, AND FIXED ASSETS**

## ERP-ASSETS-004 — Project schedule and dependencies

**Normative requirement:** The system shall store planned start/finish dates, duration, working calendar, and typed predecessor links for scheduled tasks.

**Rationale:** Dependencies and calendars make schedule dates reproducible rather than free-form.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Reject a finish before start and any dependency cycle.

**AC 2.** Recalculate successor dates under configured working days and lag values, excluding configured holidays.

**AC 3.** A calendar revision does not silently rewrite an approved baseline.

**Exception / edge case:** If a predecessor is deleted after successor work has started, preserve the dependency history and require an explicit schedule correction.

**Security and audit implications:** Only schedule editors can change dependency links; record before/after dates and changed links.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Calendars store locale-neutral dates and time zones; calendar names, weekday labels, and holiday descriptions are localizable.

**Verification method:** Automated integration/acceptance tests for the stated scenarios, plus role-based negative tests and audit-record inspection where security or approval is involved.

**REQUIREMENT 0425 OF 1120  |  PROJECTS, SERVICE MANAGEMENT, AND FIXED ASSETS**

## ERP-ASSETS-005 — Versioned schedule and scope baselines

**Normative requirement:** The system shall capture immutable, numbered project baselines for approved scope, dates, and budget, with explicit re-baseline approval.

**Rationale:** Baseline-to-current variance must remain explainable after scope or schedule changes.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Capture a baseline snapshot with version, approver, and effective date.

**AC 2.** Changes after a baseline produce variance without overwriting the snapshot.

**AC 3.** Reject re-baselining without the configured approval and reason.

**Exception / edge case:** If no baseline has been approved, label variance as unbaselined rather than reporting zero variance.

**Security and audit implications:** Baseline approval is segregated from baseline editing; snapshots and approvals are retained in audit history.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Localized labels can vary; baseline IDs, dates, and numeric comparison rules are locale-neutral.

**Verification method:** Automated integration/acceptance tests for the stated scenarios, plus role-based negative tests and audit-record inspection where security or approval is involved.

**REQUIREMENT 0426 OF 1120  |  PROJECTS, SERVICE MANAGEMENT, AND FIXED ASSETS**

## ERP-ASSETS-006 — Budget and cost plan dimensions

**Normative requirement:** The system shall maintain project budget lines by period, cost category, work package, and currency, with configurable control thresholds.

**Rationale:** Budgets require dimensions aligned with how transactions are authorized and analyzed.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Reject a line referencing an inactive category or a work package from another project.

**AC 2.** Calculate budget-to-actual and budget-to-commitment values for matching dimensions.

**AC 3.** At configured thresholds, prevent or route the posting for approval as configured.

**Exception / edge case:** If a budget is revised below already-posted actuals, retain the negative available balance and route it through the configured approval path.

**Security and audit implications:** Budget edits and overrides require assigned roles and reason codes; log threshold overrides.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Localized category labels and formatted amounts use report locale; stored amounts and currency codes remain canonical.

**Verification method:** Automated integration/acceptance tests for the stated scenarios, plus role-based negative tests and audit-record inspection where security or approval is involved.

**REQUIREMENT 0427 OF 1120  |  PROJECTS, SERVICE MANAGEMENT, AND FIXED ASSETS**

## ERP-ASSETS-007 — Resource demand and assignment

**Normative requirement:** The system shall represent role/skill demand and named-person assignments against project work packages and date ranges, subject to capacity rules.

**Rationale:** Resource planning needs a distinction between role demand and committed staff capacity.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Detect overlapping assignments exceeding a configured capacity percentage for a person.

**AC 2.** Allow skill-based role demand before a named person is assigned.

**AC 3.** Report unfilled demand and over-capacity by date interval.

**Exception / edge case:** If a worker becomes inactive during an assignment, retain past allocation and flag future assignment intervals for reassignment.

**Security and audit implications:** Limit access to employee details by HR/project role; changes to named assignments are auditable.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Skill names and role labels support translation; capacity is a normalized percentage, not locale-formatted text.

**Verification method:** Automated integration/acceptance tests for the stated scenarios, plus role-based negative tests and audit-record inspection where security or approval is involved.

**REQUIREMENT 0428 OF 1120  |  PROJECTS, SERVICE MANAGEMENT, AND FIXED ASSETS**

## ERP-ASSETS-008 — Time entry capture

**Normative requirement:** The system shall capture time by worker, work date, project, work package, task code, duration, and billable status using configurable entry precision.

**Rationale:** Time entries feed project cost, utilization, and service billing while retaining their work context.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Reject zero/negative duration, closed periods, inactive projects, and disallowed task codes.

**AC 2.** Round or reject durations according to configured precision and expose the applied rule.

**AC 3.** Submitted entries retain the original entered duration and approved duration separately when adjustment is allowed.

**Exception / edge case:** If a user enters work across midnight or a daylight-saving transition, preserve the entered local interval and calculate elapsed time using the configured zone rules.

**Security and audit implications:** Workers may create their own entries; approval and retroactive edits are separately permissioned and logged.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Date entry, decimal separator, and duration display follow user locale; stored dates use tenant time-zone rules.

**Verification method:** Automated integration/acceptance tests for the stated scenarios, plus role-based negative tests and audit-record inspection where security or approval is involved.

**REQUIREMENT 0429 OF 1120  |  PROJECTS, SERVICE MANAGEMENT, AND FIXED ASSETS**

## ERP-ASSETS-009 — Timesheet submission and approval

**Normative requirement:** The system shall group time entries into period-based timesheets with configurable submit, return, approve, and reject actions.

**Rationale:** Period review establishes accountable approval before time becomes actual labor cost.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Submission freezes submitted lines from author edits until return or authorized correction.

**AC 2.** Approval records approver, timestamp, decision, and included line IDs.

**AC 3.** A user cannot approve their own timesheet when self-approval is disabled.

**Exception / edge case:** If an approver is unavailable after submission, reassign approval through the configured delegation path without changing the submitted line set.

**Security and audit implications:** Enforce approver limits and separation of duties; preserve returned/rejected decision history.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Localized period names and messages do not change the canonical period boundaries or stored dates.

**Verification method:** Automated integration/acceptance tests for the stated scenarios, plus role-based negative tests and audit-record inspection where security or approval is involved.

**REQUIREMENT 0430 OF 1120  |  PROJECTS, SERVICE MANAGEMENT, AND FIXED ASSETS**

## ERP-ASSETS-010 — Expense entry and evidence

**Normative requirement:** The system shall capture project expenses with expense type, date, amount, currency, tax code, reimbursable/billable flags, and supporting-document reference.

**Rationale:** Expense detail supports cost recovery and downstream accounts-payable/reimbursement processing.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Reject missing project/task dimensions, invalid currency, or disallowed expense types.

**AC 2.** An expense above its configured evidence threshold cannot be submitted without an attachment or waiver.

**AC 3.** Display original amount and approved functional-currency amount with exchange-rate date/reference.

**Exception / edge case:** If receipt currency differs from project currency, retain receipt currency and require the configured exchange-rate source/date before approval.

**Security and audit implications:** Sensitive receipts are visible only to submitter, approvers, and authorized finance staff; waiver and edits are audited.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Receipt descriptions and expense labels are localizable; date, number, tax display, and currency formatting follow locale without changing amounts.

**Verification method:** Automated integration/acceptance tests for the stated scenarios, plus role-based negative tests and audit-record inspection where security or approval is involved.

**REQUIREMENT 0431 OF 1120  |  PROJECTS, SERVICE MANAGEMENT, AND FIXED ASSETS**

## ERP-ASSETS-011 — Commitment integration

**Normative requirement:** The system shall associate purchase requisitions, purchase orders, and subcontracts with project cost dimensions and expose remaining commitments.

**Rationale:** Commitment visibility prevents project controls from considering only posted actuals.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A source document posts commitment only once using its source-system ID and version.

**AC 2.** A PO amendment updates its open commitment and retains the former value in history.

**AC 3.** Commitment release on receipt, cancellation, or invoice follows configurable source events and reconciles to the source balance.

**Exception / edge case:** If an upstream PO is cancelled after partial receipt or invoicing, release only the remaining open commitment and retain the consumed portion.

**Security and audit implications:** Only authorized integration principals may write commitments; actor/source and idempotency key are recorded.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Descriptions are localized at display time; commitment amounts preserve source currency and accounting currency separately.

**Verification method:** Automated integration/acceptance tests for the stated scenarios, plus role-based negative tests and audit-record inspection where security or approval is involved.

**REQUIREMENT 0432 OF 1120  |  PROJECTS, SERVICE MANAGEMENT, AND FIXED ASSETS**

## ERP-ASSETS-012 — Actual cost posting and correction

**Normative requirement:** The system shall accept approved project actuals through a controlled posting interface and preserve immutable posted entries with reversal-based correction.

**Rationale:** Immutable actuals provide a reliable audit trail and reconcile to finance and procurement sources.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Posting a source event twice with the same idempotency key produces one actual.

**AC 2.** A posted actual cannot be deleted or overwritten; correction creates a linked reversal and replacement.

**AC 3.** Totals reconcile by source document, account, project, period, and transaction currency.

**Exception / edge case:** If an upstream source sends a correction for a closed accounting period, route it to the configured current-period reversal/adjustment process.

**Security and audit implications:** Restrict posting to approved integration/user roles; log source identifiers, posting outcome, and reversals.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Localized narration may be stored alongside canonical source codes; date/amount rendering is user-locale aware.

**Verification method:** Automated integration/acceptance tests for the stated scenarios, plus role-based negative tests and audit-record inspection where security or approval is involved.

**REQUIREMENT 0433 OF 1120  |  PROJECTS, SERVICE MANAGEMENT, AND FIXED ASSETS**

## ERP-ASSETS-013 — Budget consumption control

**Normative requirement:** The system shall evaluate configured available-budget formulas against actual plus open commitment before accepting controlled transactions.

**Rationale:** Commitment-aware controls can stop overspend before it becomes irreversible.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** For an identical budget dimension and period, available budget equals budget minus actuals minus included commitments.

**AC 2.** Under-limit transaction succeeds; over-limit follows the configured block, warning, or approval route.

**AC 3.** A concurrent pair of transactions cannot both consume the same remaining limit beyond the configured tolerance.

**Exception / edge case:** If the project has no applicable approved budget line, apply the configured no-budget policy and never interpret missing budget as unlimited implicitly.

**Security and audit implications:** Override permission is distinct from normal posting; record calculation inputs and override rationale.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Currency conversions use configured rate types/dates; displayed thresholds follow locale but comparison is decimal-exact.

**Verification method:** Automated integration/acceptance tests for the stated scenarios, plus role-based negative tests and audit-record inspection where security or approval is involved.

**REQUIREMENT 0434 OF 1120  |  PROJECTS, SERVICE MANAGEMENT, AND FIXED ASSETS**

## ERP-ASSETS-014 — Change request governance

**Normative requirement:** The system shall manage project change requests with requested scope, schedule, budget impacts, proposer, reviewer, decision, and effective date.

**Rationale:** Formal change control separates proposed work from approved baseline change.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A request remains non-effective until approved under the assigned workflow.

**AC 2.** Approval writes an effective revision and links affected baseline/work packages.

**AC 3.** Rejection preserves request and reviewer rationale without modifying active plan values.

**Exception / edge case:** If a change request is approved after its requested effective date, preserve both dates and calculate plan impact using the approved effective-date rule.

**Security and audit implications:** Requestors cannot approve their own changes when separation is configured; retain full decision chain.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Request rationale and customer-facing titles accept Unicode and translations; dates and money render by locale.

**Verification method:** Automated integration/acceptance tests for the stated scenarios, plus role-based negative tests and audit-record inspection where security or approval is involved.

**REQUIREMENT 0435 OF 1120  |  PROJECTS, SERVICE MANAGEMENT, AND FIXED ASSETS**

## ERP-ASSETS-015 — Milestone and fixed-fee billing events

**Normative requirement:** The system shall define billable project milestones with contract reference, amount/percentage, evidence, due rule, and invoice eligibility status.

**Rationale:** Milestone evidence provides a controlled trigger for receivables billing.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A milestone cannot become invoice-eligible until configured acceptance evidence and approval are present.

**AC 2.** Generate a billing request at most once per milestone and contract version.

**AC 3.** Contract amount/percentage totals are validated against the configured agreement rule.

**Exception / edge case:** If milestone evidence is revoked after invoice release, retain the released billing event and create a correction workflow instead of deleting it.

**Security and audit implications:** Billing approval and credit/contract changes require separate permissions; audit evidence changes.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Customer description can be localized per customer language; currency and tax labels come from the billing jurisdiction configuration.

**Verification method:** Automated integration/acceptance tests for the stated scenarios, plus role-based negative tests and audit-record inspection where security or approval is involved.

**REQUIREMENT 0436 OF 1120  |  PROJECTS, SERVICE MANAGEMENT, AND FIXED ASSETS**

## ERP-ASSETS-016 — Time-and-material billing preparation

**Normative requirement:** The system shall select approved billable time and expenses using effective-dated rate cards, contract caps, and customer/project billing rules.

**Rationale:** Accurate invoice preparation requires controlled rate selection and traceable source entries.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Rate resolution selects the effective rate by contract, role/task, and service date; missing rate blocks billing.

**AC 2.** A configured cap is applied across the specified contract period and reports the cap balance.

**AC 3.** Every generated charge line links to its source time or expense entry and rate version.

**Exception / edge case:** If multiple rate cards are effective on the same service date, reject ambiguous rate resolution until precedence is explicitly configured.

**Security and audit implications:** Rate-card editing is permissioned and versioned; exclude nonbillable and unapproved source rows.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Invoice description and units support customer language; decimal/date/currency formats follow legal entity/customer profile.

**Verification method:** Automated integration/acceptance tests for the stated scenarios, plus role-based negative tests and audit-record inspection where security or approval is involved.

**REQUIREMENT 0437 OF 1120  |  PROJECTS, SERVICE MANAGEMENT, AND FIXED ASSETS**

## ERP-ASSETS-017 — Revenue recognition handoff

**Normative requirement:** The system shall expose approved project performance and contract-event data to the revenue-recognition interface without embedding jurisdictional accounting policy in project execution.

**Rationale:** Accounting conclusions depend on adopted standards, contract facts, and entity policy.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Export includes contract/project keys, event dates, measure inputs, currency, and lineage to source rows.

**AC 2.** Replaying an exported batch is idempotent and yields the same acknowledged event IDs.

**AC 3.** Unapproved or missing required evidence events are excluded with machine-readable reason codes.

**Exception / edge case:** If an event lacks a required contract measurement input, return it as unprocessable with a reason and do not derive an accounting conclusion.

**Security and audit implications:** Finance may correct mapping configuration; no project user can directly create a posted revenue journal through this interface.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Keep source text and dates intact; accounting policy labels and translated customer performance text remain separate.

**Verification method:** Automated integration/acceptance tests for the stated scenarios, plus role-based negative tests and audit-record inspection where security or approval is involved.

**REQUIREMENT 0438 OF 1120  |  PROJECTS, SERVICE MANAGEMENT, AND FIXED ASSETS**

## ERP-ASSETS-018 — Project intercompany attribution

**Normative requirement:** The system shall support configurable intercompany provider/receiver entities and transfer-price references for cross-entity project work.

**Rationale:** Cross-entity work requires both operational ownership and a financial counterpart.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Reject an intercompany entry if either entity is inactive or not permitted by the configured relationship.

**AC 2.** Provider cost and receiver charge reconcile by shared transaction ID and currency pair.

**AC 3.** A missing transfer-price rule queues the entry as an error rather than silently defaulting to zero.

**Exception / edge case:** If the provider and receiver entities use different calendars or currencies, retain each entity’s basis and reject an incomplete transfer-price conversion.

**Security and audit implications:** Restrict intercompany setup and posting; log both side ledger references and any correction.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Entity names, invoice descriptors, tax presentation, and currency formatting follow each entity’s locale configuration.

**Verification method:** Automated integration/acceptance tests for the stated scenarios, plus role-based negative tests and audit-record inspection where security or approval is involved.

**REQUIREMENT 0439 OF 1120  |  PROJECTS, SERVICE MANAGEMENT, AND FIXED ASSETS**

## ERP-ASSETS-019 — Project completion and closure

**Normative requirement:** The system shall prevent final closure until configurable gates for open commitments, unbilled charges, unresolved changes, and final approvals are satisfied or waived.

**Rationale:** Closure should represent completed commercial and operational obligations.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Each closure attempt returns gate results and source references.

**AC 2.** A waiver requires authorized role, reason, and expiry/effective timestamp.

**AC 3.** Reopening is a distinct audited transition and does not erase closure data.

**Exception / edge case:** If a waiver expires before the closure transaction commits, rerun the gate check and require a current authorization.

**Security and audit implications:** Closure/waiver roles are distinct from ordinary project execution; all gate overrides are attributable.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Gate labels and reasons are translatable; financial close dates use entity calendar, not browser locale.

**Verification method:** Automated integration/acceptance tests for the stated scenarios, plus role-based negative tests and audit-record inspection where security or approval is involved.

**REQUIREMENT 0440 OF 1120  |  PROJECTS, SERVICE MANAGEMENT, AND FIXED ASSETS**

## ERP-ASSETS-020 — Project currency and exchange-rate basis

**Normative requirement:** The system shall retain transaction, project, and legal-entity reporting currency amounts with exchange-rate source/date metadata where conversion is required.

**Rationale:** Currency basis must be transparent for comparison across projects and entities.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** For each converted amount, display source and target currency and the configured rate reference/date.

**AC 2.** Revaluation or rate correction writes a new conversion record without overwriting the source amount.

**AC 3.** Project reports reconcile according to the selected currency basis.

**Exception / edge case:** If a historical exchange rate is later corrected, preserve the original booked conversion and expose any restatement as a separate versioned event.

**Security and audit implications:** Rate-source configuration is finance-admin controlled; log rate overrides and restatements.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Use ISO currency codes in data and locale-specific symbol/precision in display; never infer currency from locale.

**Verification method:** Automated integration/acceptance tests for the stated scenarios, plus role-based negative tests and audit-record inspection where security or approval is involved.

**REQUIREMENT 0441 OF 1120  |  PROJECTS, SERVICE MANAGEMENT, AND FIXED ASSETS**

## ERP-ASSETS-021 — Service catalog and coverage offering

**Normative requirement:** The system shall maintain versioned service offerings with eligible channels, service categories, default priority rules, and effective dates.

**Rationale:** A controlled catalog standardizes service classification and routing.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** New requests resolve to the active offering version on request creation time.

**AC 2.** A retired offering remains visible on historical requests but cannot be selected for new requests.

**AC 3.** Invalid channel/category combinations are rejected by configured validation.

**Exception / edge case:** If an offering is expired when a request arrives, retain the historical offering reference if supplied but route new intake to the configured inactive-offering exception.

**Security and audit implications:** Catalog maintenance is separated from request resolution rights; log effective-dated changes.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Offering names, descriptions, and customer-facing summaries have localized variants with a defined fallback language.

**Verification method:** Automated integration/acceptance tests for the stated scenarios, plus role-based negative tests and audit-record inspection where security or approval is involved.

**REQUIREMENT 0442 OF 1120  |  PROJECTS, SERVICE MANAGEMENT, AND FIXED ASSETS**

## ERP-ASSETS-022 — Customer installed-base asset

**Normative requirement:** The system shall link a serviceable customer-owned or provider-managed asset to customer/account, serial or tag, model, location, and status.

**Rationale:** An installed-base record anchors service history, warranty, entitlement, and installed equipment context.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Enforce configurable serial uniqueness scope and preserve the external manufacturer serial as entered.

**AC 2.** Reject links between an asset and an account the caller cannot access.

**AC 3.** Asset status and location history show effective dates and prior values.

**Exception / edge case:** If a serial is unknown or shared by multiple customer records, allow a provisional unverified identity only under configured policy and prevent entitlement auto-approval.

**Security and audit implications:** Customer data and asset location are restricted by account scope; record serial edits and merges.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Customer-entered names and serials accept Unicode; addresses follow country-specific validation plugins without a global mandatory format.

**Verification method:** Automated integration/acceptance tests for the stated scenarios, plus role-based negative tests and audit-record inspection where security or approval is involved.

**REQUIREMENT 0443 OF 1120  |  PROJECTS, SERVICE MANAGEMENT, AND FIXED ASSETS**

## ERP-ASSETS-023 — Service request intake

**Normative requirement:** The system shall capture inbound service requests with channel, requester, account, offering, summary, description, received timestamp, and severity.

**Rationale:** A complete request record supports triage and later response-time evidence.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Requests cannot be saved without required tenant-configured fields and a valid requester/account link.

**AC 2.** API retries with the same channel request key return the existing request.

**AC 3.** Received timestamp retains UTC instant and originating time-zone offset when supplied.

**Exception / edge case:** If the inbound channel supplies no customer timestamp or a malformed time zone, record receipt time from the server and flag the source-time uncertainty.

**Security and audit implications:** Validate caller access to customer and contact; redact sensitive fields from roles without need-to-know.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Request content supports Unicode and script mixing; detect/store language where provided, without assuming language from country.

**Verification method:** Automated integration/acceptance tests for the stated scenarios, plus role-based negative tests and audit-record inspection where security or approval is involved.

## ERP-ASSETS-024 — Service case lifecycle and resolution

**Normative requirement:** The system shall enforce configurable case states and transition criteria through triage, assigned, in-progress, waiting, resolved, and closed states.

**Rationale:** A case state should reflect operational ownership and customer-visible progress.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Illegal transitions are rejected with transition-specific codes.

**AC 2.** Resolution requires a resolution code and configured closure evidence.

**AC 3.** Reopening creates a linked state event and reactivates applicable timers by configured policy.

**Exception / edge case:** If a case must be reopened after its contract or SLA has expired, preserve the original decision and apply the configured post-expiry clock policy.

**Security and audit implications:** Only authorized roles may resolve or close; store actor, time, previous/new state, and reason.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** State keys are language-neutral; translated labels and resolution-code descriptions are selected per user/customer language.

**Verification method:** Automated integration/acceptance tests for the stated scenarios, plus role-based negative tests and audit-record inspection where security or approval is involved.

## ERP-ASSETS-025 — Entitlement and contract coverage determination

**Normative requirement:** The system shall resolve service entitlement as of request time using effective-dated contract, covered offering/assets, customer, geography, and exclusions.

**Rationale:** Coverage must be explainable based on the agreement in force at intake.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Given overlapping eligible contracts, apply a configured precedence rule and report the selected contract/version.

**AC 2.** Out-of-coverage requests remain serviceable if policy permits, but are flagged and excluded from covered billing.

**AC 3.** Entitlement result stores matched rule inputs and reason code.

**Exception / edge case:** If two active contracts match with equal configured precedence, return an ambiguous-coverage exception rather than choosing arbitrarily.

**Security and audit implications:** Contract terms visible only to service/contract roles; entitlements cannot be altered by request-level users.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Coverage decisions use jurisdiction/customer attributes from configuration; localized explanation text does not alter rule evaluation.

**Verification method:** Automated integration/acceptance tests for the stated scenarios, plus role-based negative tests and audit-record inspection where security or approval is involved.

**REQUIREMENT 0446 OF 1120  |  PROJECTS, SERVICE MANAGEMENT, AND FIXED ASSETS**

## ERP-ASSETS-026 — SLA calendar and target computation

**Normative requirement:** The system shall calculate response and resolution due instants from priority, contract, business calendar, holidays, and time zone.

**Rationale:** SLA measures are only meaningful when target and service hours are explicit.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** For known test calendar intervals, calculate expected due instants including overnight, holiday, and daylight-saving transitions.

**AC 2.** Persist target rule/version and calculation inputs with each SLA instance.

**AC 3.** Changing a calendar affects only requests according to explicit recalculation policy.

**Exception / edge case:** If a local clock change creates an ambiguous or nonexistent appointment time, require an explicit offset or configured disambiguation rule.

**Security and audit implications:** Calendar and SLA target changes are controlled and audited; service users cannot reset elapsed measures.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Calendar locale affects labels only; working intervals use an explicit named time zone and local holiday set.

**Verification method:** Automated integration/acceptance tests for the stated scenarios, plus role-based negative tests and audit-record inspection where security or approval is involved.

## ERP-ASSETS-027 — SLA pause and resume rules

**Normative requirement:** The system shall pause eligible SLA clocks only for configured wait states and record pause start, resume time, reason, and applicable clock.

**Rationale:** Separating customer wait from provider work time enables reproducible SLA results.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Each pause interval is bounded and no two active intervals overlap for the same clock.

**AC 2.** Only configured states/reasons pause each target clock.

**AC 3.** Computed elapsed business time reconciles to recorded intervals within the configured precision.

**Exception / edge case:** If a pause has no matching resume event at closure, end it only under the configured closure rule and expose the open interval for review.

**Security and audit implications:** Pause authority and reason codes are permissioned; changes to historic intervals require correction events and audit.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Localized reason labels are presentation-only; stored reason keys and timestamps remain stable.

**Verification method:** Automated integration/acceptance tests for the stated scenarios, plus role-based negative tests and audit-record inspection where security or approval is involved.

## ERP-ASSETS-028 — Queue routing and skill matching

**Normative requirement:** The system shall route eligible cases using configurable queue, skill, region, offering, and workload rules with explainable rule outcomes.

**Rationale:** Explainable routing accelerates assignment and troubleshooting of misrouted cases.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** For a fixed ruleset and case fixture, return the expected queue and routing rule ID.

**AC 2.** When no eligible queue exists, place the case in a configured exception queue and flag the missing dimension.

**AC 3.** Manual reassignment preserves original queue, actor, time, and reason.

**Exception / edge case:** If workload or skill data is stale, route to the configured fallback queue and mark which routing input was unavailable.

**Security and audit implications:** Routing configuration is admin-only; assignment access respects region, account, and clearance scopes.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Skill/queue labels may be translated; matching uses stable codes and locale-independent case attributes.

**Verification method:** Automated integration/acceptance tests for the stated scenarios, plus role-based negative tests and audit-record inspection where security or approval is involved.

## ERP-ASSETS-029 — Work order creation and linkage

**Normative requirement:** The system shall create work orders from cases or scheduled maintenance and link each to one service context, location, requested work, and execution status.

**Rationale:** A work order represents executable field work, distinct from the customer communication case.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A case can have multiple work orders, but each work order has a unique source link and lifecycle.

**AC 2.** Work orders cannot be completed while mandatory labor, parts, inspection, or completion evidence is missing.

**AC 3.** Work order status changes propagate defined summaries to the linked case without overwriting case history.

**Exception / edge case:** If case conversion is retried, return the previously created work order and do not create another unless multiple-work-order policy explicitly permits it.

**Security and audit implications:** Creation and closure rights are separately granted; preserve origin and cross-module IDs.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Work instructions and completion codes support customer/technician language; canonical status codes stay stable.

**Verification method:** Automated integration/acceptance tests for the stated scenarios, plus role-based negative tests and audit-record inspection where security or approval is involved.

## ERP-ASSETS-030 — Technician dispatch and appointment

**Normative requirement:** The system shall schedule a qualified technician and service window against a work order, respecting shift, skill, travel-zone, and capacity configuration.

**Rationale:** Dispatching balances capability and availability while making customer commitments explicit.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Reject assignment when technician lacks a mandatory skill or is unavailable in the scheduled interval.

**AC 2.** Prevent overlapping assignments beyond configured concurrency/capacity.

**AC 3.** Appointment changes notify the configured recipients and record old/new window.

**Exception / edge case:** If a technician becomes unavailable after customer confirmation, retain the original appointment and require an explicit reschedule notification.

**Security and audit implications:** Dispatchers may see only assigned territories and customer data allowed by role; schedule changes are auditable.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Appointment time is shown in customer and technician time zones with explicit zone labels; dates and weekday text are localized.

## ERP-ASSETS-031 — Service part reservation and issue

**Normative requirement:** The system shall reserve, issue, return, and record consumed parts against a work order and inventory location using source-document references.

**Rationale:** Parts traceability enables service costing and inventory reconciliation.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Reservation cannot exceed available eligible stock under the configured inventory policy.

**AC 2.** Issue and return transactions reconcile to work-order consumption and inventory movement IDs.

**AC 3.** Retrying an inventory event with its idempotency key cannot double-decrement quantity.

**Exception / edge case:** If a reserved lot expires before issue, release or replace it according to inventory policy and record the lot-level exception.

**Security and audit implications:** Only inventory-authorized roles/integrations post stock moves; retain user/source and lot/serial trace.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Part descriptions and units are localized; stock quantities use the item’s configured unit precision.

## ERP-ASSETS-032 — Field labor and expense capture

**Normative requirement:** The system shall record technician labor intervals and reimbursable service expenses against work orders with approval and billable/cost treatment.

**Rationale:** Field work records actual effort for service profitability and customer billing.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Reject invalid overlapping labor intervals for the same technician unless an authorized exception applies.

**AC 2.** Approved labor/expense lines map to configured service cost and charge categories.

**AC 3.** Work-order completion reports missing required labor or required zero-work reason.

**Exception / edge case:** If a technician crosses time zones during a recorded shift, retain the offset for each interval endpoint and avoid silently changing elapsed duration.

**Security and audit implications:** Technicians may submit own lines; approvers cannot silently change source values; adjustments are logged.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Time zones are explicit for start/end; amounts, dates, and units render using locale and legal-entity currency rules.
