## ERP-ASSETS-033 — Diagnosis and resolution taxonomy

**Normative requirement:** The system shall require configurable diagnosis, cause, action, and resolution codes at defined case or work-order transitions.

**Rationale:** Structured resolution data supports recurring-issue analysis and warranty decisions.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Configured transitions reject missing mandatory codes.

**AC 2.** Inactive codes remain on historical records but cannot be newly selected.

**AC 3.** Reports group by stable code across translated labels.

**Exception / edge case:** If a diagnosis code is retired while a work order is open, preserve it on existing history but require an active replacement at final closure if configured.

**Security and audit implications:** Taxonomy editing is restricted; changes are effective-dated and audit logged.

## ERP-ASSETS-034 — Customer-visible versus internal communication

**Normative requirement:** The system shall classify each case note and attachment as customer-visible or internal-only and enforce separate access/rendering paths.

**Rationale:** Internal diagnostics must not leak through customer portals or notifications.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A customer-role API query returns zero internal-only notes and attachments.

**AC 2.** Changing visibility requires an authorized role and creates an audit event.

**AC 3.** Customer exports and notifications include only records classified customer-visible.

**Exception / edge case:** If visibility is changed after a message was sent externally, do not retract history; record the exposure and invoke the configured incident process.

**Security and audit implications:** Apply authorization server-side to all reads, exports, and notification payloads; audit visibility changes.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Customer-visible messages use the customer’s selected language where available; internal notes retain author-entered language metadata.

## ERP-ASSETS-035 — Customer notification preferences and templates

**Normative requirement:** The system shall send configured case notifications using customer contact preferences, event rules, and versioned language-specific templates.

**Rationale:** Consistent localized notifications avoid missed updates and unsupported ad hoc wording.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Each send stores template version, recipient, language, event, delivery result, and correlation ID.

**AC 2.** If no translation exists, use the configured fallback and mark the fallback in message metadata.

**AC 3.** Opt-out and channel preference rules are applied before sending non-mandatory notifications.

**Exception / edge case:** If the contact has opted out or the requested language template is unavailable, suppress non-mandatory delivery or use the configured fallback and retain the delivery decision.

**Security and audit implications:** Prevent unauthorized recipients and template injection; mask sensitive content in logs.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Template selection uses contact language then customer fallback; date, time zone, and decimal output are formatted for recipient locale.

## ERP-ASSETS-036 — Offline field-service synchronization

**Normative requirement:** The system shall support bounded offline capture for configured mobile work-order data and reconcile queued mutations with server versions.

**Rationale:** Field workers may need to operate without continuous connectivity.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** An offline submission receives a stable client-generated ID and uploads at most once under retry.

**AC 2.** Concurrent server edits produce a conflict record with both versions, not silent last-write-wins for controlled fields.

**AC 3.** Expired permissions or tenant context block sync and retain an actionable client error.

**Exception / edge case:** If an offline mutation targets a record whose server version has changed, preserve both versions as a conflict and require an authorized resolution.

**Security and audit implications:** Use short-lived device credentials and server-side reauthorization on sync; audit device and actor IDs.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Offline text is UTF-8; locale preferences and time-zone offsets travel with entries while server canonical values remain normalized.

**Verification method:** Automated integration/acceptance tests for the stated scenarios, plus role-based negative tests and audit-record inspection where security or approval is involved.

## ERP-ASSETS-037 — Escalation and SLA breach action

**Normative requirement:** The system shall evaluate configured escalation conditions and create attributable escalation events when target thresholds are crossed.

**Rationale:** Escalations make service-risk conditions visible to owners before or after breach.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Threshold test fixtures trigger exactly once per configured escalation step.

**AC 2.** Reopened or re-prioritized requests follow configured reset/re-evaluation logic and preserve prior events.

**AC 3.** Failed notification delivery is retried or queued with observable outcome.

**Exception / edge case:** If the target case is closed before a queued escalation runs, apply the configured closed-case rule and retain the evaluation event without reopening silently.

**Security and audit implications:** Only defined roles may resolve escalations or alter priority; preserve source clock and rule version.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Escalation notifications use recipient locale; elapsed-time computations use configured work calendar rather than translated display.

**Verification method:** Automated integration/acceptance tests for the stated scenarios, plus role-based negative tests and audit-record inspection where security or approval is involved.

## ERP-ASSETS-038 — Service billing preparation

**Normative requirement:** The system shall generate charge candidates from approved labor, parts, travel, and contract rules, retaining links to their source events.

**Rationale:** Service revenue needs transparent charge derivation and contract treatment.

**AC 1.** A charge candidate links to one or more source entries and the effective rate/price rule.

**AC 2.** Covered, warranty, no-charge, and billable classifications produce expected charge eligibility.

**AC 3.** Duplicate processing of the same approved work order does not duplicate charge candidates.

## ERP-ASSETS-039 — Customer acceptance and completion evidence

**Normative requirement:** The system shall capture configured completion evidence, including signer identity, method, time, and evidence reference, before work-order closure.

**Rationale:** Customer acceptance or documented exception provides evidence that field work was performed.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Closure is blocked when the configured acceptance rule is unmet.

**AC 2.** Evidence records server time, capture method, and linked work order; uploaded signature/image is checksum-linked.

**AC 3.** An exception path requires reason code and authorized approver.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Consent text and signer name fields support customer language and Unicode; timestamp is retained in UTC with displayed local zone.

## ERP-ASSETS-040 — Preventive maintenance schedule

**Normative requirement:** The system shall generate maintenance work due events from effective-dated calendar, meter threshold, or usage-based plans linked to installed assets.

**Rationale:** Preventive work is the service execution mechanism for planned asset care.

**AC 3.** Plan revision does not rewrite already-created work orders.

## ERP-ASSETS-041 — Asset record identity and classification

**Normative requirement:** The system shall assign an immutable asset ID and require configurable class, owning entity, custodian/location, in-service state, and tracking method.

**Rationale:** A consistent asset master supports lifecycle control and financial books.

**AC 1.** Reject duplicate active tag/serial within configured uniqueness scope.

**AC 2.** Asset identity remains stable across tag, name, and location changes.

**AC 3.** Class defaults are applied only as initial values and are visible in record history.

**Exception / edge case:** If an asset tag is reused after retirement, preserve the old asset identity and require the configured re-tagging/alias workflow.

## ERP-ASSETS-042 — Asset books and accounting basis

**Normative requirement:** The system shall maintain separate effective-dated asset books for configured accounting, tax, regulatory, or management bases without assuming a universal jurisdictional rule.

**Rationale:** Organizations may need materially different carrying and depreciation values across reporting bases.

**AC 2.** A transaction in one book does not mutate another unless an explicit posting rule creates the second-book entry.

**AC 3.** Reports identify book, currency, accounting basis, and effective policy version.

**Exception / edge case:** If an asset is not enabled for a requested book, reject book-specific processing rather than copying values from another book.

## ERP-ASSETS-043 — Capitalization from project or procurement

**Normative requirement:** The system shall create proposed asset additions from approved project or procurement costs using configurable capitalization rules and source-line traceability.

**Rationale:** Capitalization connects investment delivery to the asset register while leaving policy decisions configurable.

**AC 3.** Reprocessing the same source-line IDs does not duplicate an addition.

**Security and audit implications:** Capitalization approval is segregated from source entry; preserve approver and source-document IDs.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Capitalization descriptions support localized text; amount uses source and asset-book currencies with explicit conversion data.

## ERP-ASSETS-044 — Construction in progress and settlement

**Normative requirement:** The system shall accumulate eligible costs in construction-in-progress (CIP) balances and settle them to one or more in-service assets through an approved allocation.

**Rationale:** CIP distinguishes unfinished projects from depreciable assets and preserves capitalization lineage.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Settlement allocations sum exactly to approved CIP amount, with residual policy explicit.

**AC 2.** Settlement records effective in-service date and resulting asset IDs.

**AC 3.** A settled CIP amount cannot be settled again unless first reversed through an authorized event.

**Exception / edge case:** If allocated costs exceed or fall short of the CIP balance, reject settlement unless the configured residual treatment is explicitly approved.

**Security and audit implications:** Settlement requires finance approval and source reconciliation; audit allocation basis and reversal.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Allocation labels are localized; exact amounts and rounding residuals use book precision and deterministic allocation rules.

**Verification method:** Automated integration/acceptance tests for the stated scenarios, plus role-based negative tests and audit-record inspection where security or approval is involved.

**REQUIREMENT 0465 OF 1120  |  PROJECTS, SERVICE MANAGEMENT, AND FIXED ASSETS**

## ERP-ASSETS-045 — Component accounting structure

**Normative requirement:** The system shall support parent assets and separately tracked components with component-specific cost, useful life, depreciation rule, and disposal relationship.

**Rationale:** Material components can have different consumption patterns and replacement timing.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Parent and component book totals reconcile according to configured capitalization/aggregation policy.

**AC 2.** A component replacement can retire the old component without retiring the parent.

**AC 3.** Reject hierarchy cycles and cross-entity parent links.

**Exception / edge case:** If a component is already retired, reject a second retirement unless it is a correction linked to the original event.

**Security and audit implications:** Component creation/disposal is finance-controlled; changes preserve link history.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Component names and descriptions support translation; component IDs and amounts are locale-neutral.

**Verification method:** Automated integration/acceptance tests for the stated scenarios, plus role-based negative tests and audit-record inspection where security or approval is involved.

**REQUIREMENT 0466 OF 1120  |  PROJECTS, SERVICE MANAGEMENT, AND FIXED ASSETS**

## ERP-ASSETS-046 — Depreciation methods and configuration

**Normative requirement:** The system shall provide configurable book-specific depreciation methods, including straight-line, declining-balance, and units-of-production where enabled, with parameters and effective dates.

**Rationale:** Method choice and calculation parameters are accounting-policy decisions, not hard-coded assumptions.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** For published test fixtures, each enabled method produces the documented schedule to the smallest book unit.

**AC 2.** Reject incompatible method parameters, missing units basis, or effective-date gaps.

**AC 3.** Changing a method prospectively preserves posted history and generates a versioned future schedule.

**Exception / edge case:** If a method becomes unavailable in a future-effective policy version, retain existing schedules and block new schedules pending an approved replacement.

**Security and audit implications:** Method configuration is finance-admin controlled and approved; store parameters, calculation version, and overrides.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Method descriptions localize; calculations use fixed decimal precision and book-specific currency rounding, not locale formatting.

**Verification method:** Automated integration/acceptance tests for the stated scenarios, plus role-based negative tests and audit-record inspection where security or approval is involved.

**REQUIREMENT 0467 OF 1120  |  PROJECTS, SERVICE MANAGEMENT, AND FIXED ASSETS**

## ERP-ASSETS-047 — Depreciation schedule calculation

**Normative requirement:** The system shall calculate planned depreciation by asset book and period using cost basis, residual value, in-service date, useful life, conventions, and configured method.

**Rationale:** A reproducible schedule supports forecasting and period-close accounting.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** For fixed fixtures, schedule totals equal depreciable basis within configured rounding treatment.

**AC 2.** Schedule lines include basis inputs, method version, period, and calculated amount.

**AC 3.** The system does not calculate depreciation before configured available-for-use date or after disposal cutoff rule.

**Exception / edge case:** If cost basis is zero or residual value equals/exceeds depreciable basis, produce a zero/exception schedule per policy rather than a negative charge.

**Security and audit implications:** Schedule generation and posting are separately permissioned; log calculation run ID and exceptions.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Periods follow the asset book calendar; display locale affects labels only, not period boundary or computation.

**Verification method:** Automated integration/acceptance tests for the stated scenarios, plus role-based negative tests and audit-record inspection where security or approval is involved.

**REQUIREMENT 0468 OF 1120  |  PROJECTS, SERVICE MANAGEMENT, AND FIXED ASSETS**

## ERP-ASSETS-048 — Depreciation posting and period control

**Normative requirement:** The system shall post depreciation journals through the general-ledger contract with idempotent run IDs and prevent posting to closed periods.

**Rationale:** Financial posting must be controlled and reconcilable to the general ledger.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Retrying a depreciation run ID cannot post duplicate journals.

**AC 2.** A closed-period attempt is rejected with book, period, and close-state reason.

**AC 3.** Posted asset-book depreciation reconciles to journal debit/credit by run and entity.

**Exception / edge case:** If one journal line is rejected downstream, keep the run unposted or in a recoverable partial state; never mark the full run posted.

**Security and audit implications:** Separate schedule, review, and posting roles; journal reference and user/service identity are audited.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Journal description templates are localizable; book-period dates and amounts follow accounting locale without changing values.

**Verification method:** Automated integration/acceptance tests for the stated scenarios, plus role-based negative tests and audit-record inspection where security or approval is involved.

**REQUIREMENT 0469 OF 1120  |  PROJECTS, SERVICE MANAGEMENT, AND FIXED ASSETS**

## ERP-ASSETS-049 — Useful life and residual value review

**Normative requirement:** The system shall support effective-dated reassessment of useful life, residual value, and depreciation method, with reason, approver, and prospective schedule impact.

**Rationale:** Estimates change over time, and revised assumptions must remain traceable.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** An approved reassessment recalculates future schedule from its effective date and preserves posted history.

**AC 2.** Reject an unapproved reassessment or one whose effective date precedes the latest posted period absent adjustment workflow.

**AC 3.** Show prior versus revised assumptions and future-period variance.

**Exception / edge case:** If the effective date falls in a closed period, defer the prospective change or require the configured prior-period adjustment workflow.

**Security and audit implications:** Estimate changes require finance approval and are captured as events, not edits to prior posted periods.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Reason fields support local language; estimates use book currency/precision and period labels.

**Verification method:** Automated integration/acceptance tests for the stated scenarios, plus role-based negative tests and audit-record inspection where security or approval is involved.

**REQUIREMENT 0470 OF 1120  |  PROJECTS, SERVICE MANAGEMENT, AND FIXED ASSETS**

## ERP-ASSETS-050 — Tax depreciation profiles

**Normative requirement:** The system shall support separately configured tax books, classes, conventions, and jurisdiction-specific depreciation parameters without treating a default profile as legal advice.

**Rationale:** Tax depreciation rules vary by jurisdiction, asset class, entity, and date.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Tax-book schedules use the selected effective rule set and show jurisdiction/profile version.

**AC 2.** No tax profile or expired profile results in a validation exception, not silent accounting-book substitution.

**AC 3.** A rule update creates a versioned schedule recalculation preview.

**Exception / edge case:** If the jurisdiction profile is unavailable for a historical tax year, flag the calculation for tax review rather than applying the current profile retroactively.

**Security and audit implications:** Tax profile changes require finance/tax role; preserve version and effective date for filed-period reproducibility.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Jurisdiction, currency, and tax labels derive from entity tax profile; locale display cannot select a different profile.

**Verification method:** Automated integration/acceptance tests for the stated scenarios, plus role-based negative tests and audit-record inspection where security or approval is involved.

**REQUIREMENT 0471 OF 1120  |  PROJECTS, SERVICE MANAGEMENT, AND FIXED ASSETS**

## ERP-ASSETS-051 — Asset transfer and location history

**Normative requirement:** The system shall process effective-dated custody, location, department, and owning-entity transfers as controlled events.

**Rationale:** Transfer history establishes accountability and drives reporting and possible intercompany accounting.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A transfer records from/to values, effective time, actor, and approval where required.

**AC 2.** Reject transfer to inactive or inaccessible location/entity.

**AC 3.** Reports as-of a date return the corresponding historical custodian and location.

**Exception / edge case:** If the transfer crosses entities with different books, create the configured handoff or hold the transfer before changing ownership.

**Security and audit implications:** Transfers to another entity require approval and any configured financial handoff; changes are auditable.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Addresses and location names support local scripts; time zone is explicit for effective timestamps.

**Verification method:** Automated integration/acceptance tests for the stated scenarios, plus role-based negative tests and audit-record inspection where security or approval is involved.

**REQUIREMENT 0472 OF 1120  |  PROJECTS, SERVICE MANAGEMENT, AND FIXED ASSETS**

## ERP-ASSETS-052 — Physical inventory and reconciliation

**Normative requirement:** The system shall support a scoped physical verification campaign comparing expected asset tag/serial/location/custodian with observed data and recording outcomes.

**Rationale:** Physical verification detects missing, moved, or incorrectly recorded assets.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A campaign assigns a defined population and snapshot date and records not-found, found, mismatch, and duplicate outcomes.

**AC 2.** Scanning the same tag twice flags duplicate scan without double-counting the asset.

**AC 3.** Approved reconciliation generates explicit proposed master changes or investigation cases; it does not silently overwrite records.

**Exception / edge case:** If a scanned tag matches multiple active records, open an identity investigation and do not choose a record automatically.

**Security and audit implications:** Campaign access is scoped; reconciliation approvals are distinct from scan entry; record evidence and variance disposition.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Scan input preserves tags/serials; campaign instructions and variance reasons are translatable.

**Verification method:** Automated integration/acceptance tests for the stated scenarios, plus role-based negative tests and audit-record inspection where security or approval is involved.

**REQUIREMENT 0473 OF 1120  |  PROJECTS, SERVICE MANAGEMENT, AND FIXED ASSETS**

## ERP-ASSETS-053 — Impairment and revaluation events

**Normative requirement:** The system shall record book-specific impairment or revaluation events with effective date, basis, approver, and configurable journal impact.

**Rationale:** Measurement treatments differ by accounting basis and entity policy, so event handling must be configurable.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Reject event types disabled for the selected book or missing required valuation evidence.

**AC 2.** Preview shows prior carrying amount, event adjustment, resulting amount, and linked journal candidate.

**AC 3.** Posted event cannot be edited; correction creates linked reversal/replacement.

**Exception / edge case:** If valuation evidence is missing or stale under tenant policy, retain a draft event and block posting.

**Security and audit implications:** Finance approval and valuation evidence are required according to configured policy; log overrides and journal IDs.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Valuation basis descriptions localize; calculations retain currency, precision, and rule version.

**Verification method:** Automated integration/acceptance tests for the stated scenarios, plus role-based negative tests and audit-record inspection where security or approval is involved.

**REQUIREMENT 0474 OF 1120  |  PROJECTS, SERVICE MANAGEMENT, AND FIXED ASSETS**

## ERP-ASSETS-054 — Maintenance history linkage

**Normative requirement:** The system shall link service cases and work orders to an asset ID and expose asset maintenance history without conflating repair cost with asset cost.

**Rationale:** Operational maintenance and capital accounting require traceability but separate classification.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A linked work order appears in the asset’s service timeline with source state and completion date.

**AC 2.** Repair expense remains an expense unless an authorized capitalization event references it.

**AC 3.** Removing an erroneous link creates a dated correction event and preserves the prior link.

**Exception / edge case:** If an asset is merged or retired after a work-order link was created, preserve the original link and resolve to the surviving identity through an auditable alias.

**Security and audit implications:** Asset financial permissions do not automatically grant customer/service details; enforce both record scopes.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Maintenance descriptions use source language with optional translated display labels; asset IDs remain stable.

**Verification method:** Automated integration/acceptance tests for the stated scenarios, plus role-based negative tests and audit-record inspection where security or approval is involved.

**REQUIREMENT 0475 OF 1120  |  PROJECTS, SERVICE MANAGEMENT, AND FIXED ASSETS**

## ERP-ASSETS-055 — Asset disposal and retirement

**Normative requirement:** The system shall process asset retirement with effective date, reason, disposal method, proceeds, approval, and book-specific carrying-value calculation.

**Rationale:** Retirement should end future depreciation and preserve the basis for gain/loss accounting.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Reject retirement date before available-for-use date or before configured period-close boundary without adjustment approval.

**AC 2.** Preview calculates carrying value, proceeds, and gain/loss inputs per book.

**AC 3.** Approved retirement stops future schedules according to book convention and retains asset history.

**Exception / edge case:** If proceeds are unknown at retirement approval, apply only the configured estimate/zero-proceeds path and flag final settlement as pending.

**Security and audit implications:** Approval and posting are distinct; disposal evidence, reason, actor, and journal reference are retained.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Disposal reason and method labels localize; date follows book calendar and amount uses legal-entity currency formatting.

**Verification method:** Automated integration/acceptance tests for the stated scenarios, plus role-based negative tests and audit-record inspection where security or approval is involved.

**REQUIREMENT 0476 OF 1120  |  PROJECTS, SERVICE MANAGEMENT, AND FIXED ASSETS**

## ERP-ASSETS-056 — Disposal proceeds and general-ledger handoff

**Normative requirement:** The system shall send approved disposal proceeds and calculated book values to receivables/cash and general ledger through versioned, idempotent interfaces.

**Rationale:** Asset retirement may require separate proceeds settlement and financial journal workflows.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Each handoff has an external transaction ID and acknowledged status; replay does not duplicate entries.

**AC 2.** Unbalanced or unmapped journal candidates are rejected and remain visible in an exception queue.

**AC 3.** Asset book disposal totals reconcile to posted journal and receipt references.

**Exception / edge case:** If cash proceeds are received after the accounting retirement batch, link the later receipt to the existing disposal without reposting carrying value.

**Security and audit implications:** Only authorized finance integration identities post; store payload hash, correlation ID, and rejection reason.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Narration is localized by entity; account/currency keys are stable codes and amounts exact.

**Verification method:** Automated integration/acceptance tests for the stated scenarios, plus role-based negative tests and audit-record inspection where security or approval is involved.

**REQUIREMENT 0477 OF 1120  |  PROJECTS, SERVICE MANAGEMENT, AND FIXED ASSETS**

## ERP-ASSETS-057 — Lease accounting boundary

**Normative requirement:** The system shall permit a configurable reference or feed for right-of-use assets while delegating lease identification, measurement, and liability accounting to a lease/accounting policy component.

**Rationale:** Lease accounting is distinct from ordinary owned-asset acquisition and varies by adopted framework and contract.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Asset record identifies ownership/lease status and lease contract reference.

**AC 2.** A lease schedule import validates contract, asset, book, effective date, and source version.

**AC 3.** The fixed-asset module does not independently derive lease liability or determine lease term absent an enabled policy integration.

**Exception / edge case:** If imported lease asset data conflicts with the fixed-asset book, quarantine the import and require lease-accounting reconciliation.

**Security and audit implications:** Restrict lease contract terms to finance/legal roles; record source schedule version and accounting approval.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Contract language is retained as entered; jurisdictional policy/configuration is explicit and is not inferred from locale.

**Verification method:** Automated integration/acceptance tests for the stated scenarios, plus role-based negative tests and audit-record inspection where security or approval is involved.

**REQUIREMENT 0478 OF 1120  |  PROJECTS, SERVICE MANAGEMENT, AND FIXED ASSETS**

## ERP-ASSETS-058 — Asset insurance and valuation evidence

**Normative requirement:** The system shall allow configurable insurance policy, insured value, valuation date, provider, and evidence references linked to assets without treating coverage as book value.

**Rationale:** Risk and physical-asset insurance data are useful but are not accounting measurement inputs by default.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Insurance value and carrying value appear as distinct labeled measures.

**AC 2.** Expired policies are flagged using configured notice windows.

**AC 3.** A policy update retains previous effective-dated values and evidence.

**Exception / edge case:** If a policy covers only a subset of components or sites, retain the coverage scope instead of assigning the insured value to the whole parent asset.

**Security and audit implications:** Sensitive policy details are role-scoped; access and updates are audited.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Provider and policy documents support Unicode and local scripts; values display currency and valuation date explicitly.

**Verification method:** Automated integration/acceptance tests for the stated scenarios, plus role-based negative tests and audit-record inspection where security or approval is involved.

**REQUIREMENT 0479 OF 1120  |  PROJECTS, SERVICE MANAGEMENT, AND FIXED ASSETS**

## ERP-ASSETS-059 — Asset register reconciliation

**Normative requirement:** The system shall provide book-by-book reconciliation between asset register balances and general-ledger control accounts for an as-of period.

**Rationale:** Reconciliation detects missing postings, duplicate postings, and mapping errors.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** For matching entity/book/period/accounts, system computes register-minus-ledger variance with drill-down source rows.

**AC 2.** Reconciliation report identifies unposted, rejected, and out-of-balance transactions separately.

**AC 3.** A completed reconciliation stores preparer, reviewer, timestamp, and report snapshot ID.

**Exception / edge case:** If the general-ledger period is not final, label the reconciliation provisional and prevent final sign-off.

**Security and audit implications:** Restrict close/reconciliation sign-off; retain immutable report snapshot and evidence attachments.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Report labels localize; currency basis and accounting period are explicit and consistent across export.

**Verification method:** Automated integration/acceptance tests for the stated scenarios, plus role-based negative tests and audit-record inspection where security or approval is involved.

**REQUIREMENT 0480 OF 1120  |  PROJECTS, SERVICE MANAGEMENT, AND FIXED ASSETS**

## ERP-ASSETS-060 — Tenant isolation across domain records

**Normative requirement:** The system shall scope every project, case, work order, asset, transaction, attachment, and API lookup to an authenticated tenant context.

**Rationale:** A multi-tenant ERP must prevent horizontal access across customer organizations.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Automated tests attempt cross-tenant read, create, update, delete, export, and attachment access and receive denial or not-found.

**AC 2.** Database tenant scope is enforced in application queries and an independently tested persistence control such as row-level security where shared-table tenancy is used.

**AC 3.** Missing tenant context fails closed.

**Exception / edge case:** If the tenant claim is missing, expired, or inconsistent with the requested object, fail closed without disclosing whether a foreign-tenant record exists.

**Security and audit implications:** Use least-privilege database roles; privileged bypass is isolated, monitored, and unavailable to ordinary application requests.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Tenant settings, language, and formatting cannot be selected using a foreign-tenant identifier.

**Verification method:** Automated integration/acceptance tests for the stated scenarios, plus role-based negative tests and audit-record inspection where security or approval is involved.

**REQUIREMENT 0481 OF 1120  |  PROJECTS, SERVICE MANAGEMENT, AND FIXED ASSETS**

## ERP-ASSETS-061 — Role and data-scope authorization

**Normative requirement:** The system shall authorize actions by tenant, legal entity, module role, record scope, and action, with separate permissions for create, approve, post, export, and administer.

**Rationale:** Module-wide roles alone are insufficient for enterprise segregation and least privilege.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A permission matrix test verifies allowed and denied actions for each defined role/scope fixture.

**AC 2.** Approval and posting rights can be assigned independently from data-entry rights.

**AC 3.** Revoked or expired assignment denies the next request without requiring client-side state reset.

**Exception / edge case:** If a user has conflicting roles, apply explicit deny/segregation rules and require privileged resolution rather than assuming the broadest role wins.

**Security and audit implications:** Record authorization decisions for sensitive actions; privileged role grants and scope changes require auditable approval.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Role labels localize but permission keys and policy evaluation remain language-neutral.

**Verification method:** Automated integration/acceptance tests for the stated scenarios, plus role-based negative tests and audit-record inspection where security or approval is involved.

**REQUIREMENT 0482 OF 1120  |  PROJECTS, SERVICE MANAGEMENT, AND FIXED ASSETS**

## ERP-ASSETS-062 — Immutable domain audit events

**Normative requirement:** The system shall emit append-only audit events for material domain changes, approvals, security-relevant reads, and external postings with actor, time, tenant, object, action, and correlation IDs.

**Rationale:** Auditable history supports investigation, reconciliation, and change accountability.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Every tested material mutation creates an event with before/after or change-set reference.

**AC 2.** Ordinary roles cannot update or delete audit events through UI/API.

**AC 3.** Audit export filters by tenant and time range and records the export actor.

**Exception / edge case:** If audit persistence is unavailable, block or durably queue the associated critical mutation according to the configured fail-safe policy; never silently drop its event.

**Security and audit implications:** Protect audit logs from application-user alteration; minimize sensitive payload capture and apply retention configuration.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Audit event labels are translated at presentation; event payload keys, timestamps, and identifiers remain canonical.

**Verification method:** Automated integration/acceptance tests for the stated scenarios, plus role-based negative tests and audit-record inspection where security or approval is involved.

**REQUIREMENT 0483 OF 1120  |  PROJECTS, SERVICE MANAGEMENT, AND FIXED ASSETS**

## ERP-ASSETS-063 — Multilingual text and locale handling

**Normative requirement:** The system shall store domain text in Unicode, distinguish translation from original user-entered content, and resolve UI, tenant, and customer locales using explicit precedence.

**Rationale:** International deployment needs local interfaces without mutating original records or canonical identifiers.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Round-trip test Arabic, CJK, combining marks, emoji, and mixed-script names through API, database, search, and export.

**AC 2.** A missing translation uses the configured fallback and does not substitute translated text for user-authored content.

**AC 3.** Locale precedence is deterministic and visible to the user for UI and outbound documents.

**Exception / edge case:** If a requested locale is unsupported, use the configured fallback and retain the original text and locale tag without transliteration or destructive rewriting.

**Security and audit implications:** Escape user content to prevent injection; restrict translator permissions for approved templates and workflow messages.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Set HTML language and direction metadata; support right-to-left layout and locale-aware collation/formatting while preserving canonical values.

**Verification method:** Automated integration/acceptance tests for the stated scenarios, plus role-based negative tests and audit-record inspection where security or approval is involved.

**REQUIREMENT 0484 OF 1120  |  PROJECTS, SERVICE MANAGEMENT, AND FIXED ASSETS**

## ERP-ASSETS-064 — Accessible domain workflows

**Normative requirement:** The system shall implement project, service, and asset workflows to the organization-selected WCAG 2.2 conformance target, with keyboard operation and programmatic labels for controls and status.

**Rationale:** Accessible interaction is essential for web workflows and can be evaluated against testable criteria.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Automated and manual keyboard tests complete create, approval, dispatch, and asset-posting flows without pointer-only controls.

**AC 2.** Form errors are programmatically associated with fields and announced; state changes are exposed to assistive technology.

**AC 3.** Color is not the sole carrier of status or SLA breach information.

**Exception / edge case:** If a third-party component blocks keyboard or assistive-technology completion of a critical action, disable or replace that path before production release.

**Security and audit implications:** Do not expose inaccessible privileged shortcuts; audit records of approvals remain independent of visual presentation.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Text reflow, language declaration, directionality, and localized accessible names are included in each supported locale test suite.

**Verification method:** Automated integration/acceptance tests for the stated scenarios, plus role-based negative tests and audit-record inspection where security or approval is involved.

**REQUIREMENT 0485 OF 1120  |  PROJECTS, SERVICE MANAGEMENT, AND FIXED ASSETS**

## ERP-ASSETS-065 — Versioned integration contracts and idempotency

**Normative requirement:** The system shall expose versioned APIs/events for project costs, service charges, inventory movements, and asset journals with schema validation and idempotency keys.

**Rationale:** Stable contracts prevent duplicate financial or inventory effects during retries and independent module upgrades.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Invalid schema versions are rejected with documented machine-readable error.

**AC 2.** Same tenant, operation, and idempotency key return the original outcome; reused key with different payload is rejected.

**AC 3.** Contract tests verify correlation, source identifiers, and error/retry semantics for each listed handoff.

**Exception / edge case:** If an idempotency key is replayed with a different payload hash, reject it and return a conflict without applying either new side effect.

**Security and audit implications:** Authenticate service principals, scope them to required endpoints/tenant, and audit integration configuration and message outcomes.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Use stable codes and ISO locale-neutral primitives in payloads; localized descriptions are optional metadata, never routing keys.

**Verification method:** Automated integration/acceptance tests for the stated scenarios, plus role-based negative tests and audit-record inspection where security or approval is involved.

**REQUIREMENT 0486 OF 1120  |  PROJECTS, SERVICE MANAGEMENT, AND FIXED ASSETS**

## ERP-ASSETS-066 — Evidence attachment safety and retention

**Normative requirement:** The system shall store uploaded evidence using tenant-bound references, content-type/size validation, malware scanning, access policy, and configurable retention/disposition.

**Rationale:** Attachments often contain contracts, receipts, signatures, or personal data and need lifecycle controls.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Reject files exceeding configured type/size policy and quarantine malware-positive files.

**AC 2.** Download authorization checks both tenant and linked-record permission.

**AC 3.** Retention action records policy, actor/system job, disposition, and recoverability state.

**Exception / edge case:** If malware scanning is unavailable or times out, quarantine the upload and do not expose it as downloadable evidence.

**Security and audit implications:** Use non-guessable object references and expiring download authorization; log sensitive downloads and administrative access.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Filenames and metadata support Unicode; binary content remains unmodified except approved safe scanning/transformation.

**Verification method:** Automated integration/acceptance tests for the stated scenarios, plus role-based negative tests and audit-record inspection where security or approval is involved.

**REQUIREMENT 0487 OF 1120  |  PROJECTS, SERVICE MANAGEMENT, AND FIXED ASSETS**

## ERP-ASSETS-067 — Configurable workflow and rule versioning

**Normative requirement:** The system shall version tenant-configured statuses, approval paths, calendars, routing, and accounting/service rules, and bind each executed transaction to the active version.

**Rationale:** Configurable extensions need reproducible historical behavior without rewriting prior outcomes.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Publishing a new rule creates immutable version/effective date and does not retroactively alter completed transactions.

**AC 2.** A transaction records the rule version used for routing, approval, SLA, billing, or depreciation where relevant.

**AC 3.** Invalid or overlapping effective versions are rejected at publication.

**Exception / edge case:** If no rule version is effective for the transaction date, reject or route to a configuration exception instead of selecting the nearest version.

**Security and audit implications:** Only configuration administrators can publish; require maker-checker approval for designated high-impact rules and audit all changes.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Rule labels and explanations have translation versions; matching and version keys are stable and locale-independent.

**Verification method:** Automated integration/acceptance tests for the stated scenarios, plus role-based negative tests and audit-record inspection where security or approval is involved.

**REQUIREMENT 0488 OF 1120  |  PROJECTS, SERVICE MANAGEMENT, AND FIXED ASSETS**

## ERP-ASSETS-068 — Bulk import and export controls

**Normative requirement:** The system shall provide validated bulk import/export for approved domain templates with dry-run, row-level errors, scoped permissions, and auditable job status.

**Rationale:** Controlled bulk operations reduce manual work without bypassing business validations.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Dry-run reports accepted/rejected rows without persistent business changes.

**AC 2.** Commit revalidates row-level authorization and domain rules and returns stable row/error IDs.

**AC 3.** Export scopes honor the same permissions as interactive queries and include run ID, filters, and locale/currency basis.

**Exception / edge case:** If a batch contains mixed valid and invalid rows, apply only the explicitly selected transactional mode and report each row outcome without implicit partial commit.

**Security and audit implications:** Apply rate/size limits, protect exported files, and prevent tenant-wide leakage through guessed IDs.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Template column labels may localize, but stable machine field keys and UTF-8 content are preserved.

**Verification method:** Automated integration/acceptance tests for the stated scenarios, plus role-based negative tests and audit-record inspection where security or approval is involved.

**REQUIREMENT 0489 OF 1120  |  PROJECTS, SERVICE MANAGEMENT, AND FIXED ASSETS**

## ERP-ASSETS-069 — Concurrency control for critical transitions

**Normative requirement:** The system shall use optimistic concurrency or equivalent atomic guards for approval, posting, allocation, schedule, and lifecycle transitions.

**Rationale:** Concurrent users must not approve stale values or oversubscribe finite budget, capacity, or stock.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Stale version updates receive a conflict response with current version and no partial side effect.

**AC 2.** Parallel budget, stock, or capacity allocation tests never exceed configured limits.

**AC 3.** A multi-record transition either commits all required records or rolls back all of them.

**Exception / edge case:** If two users submit the same state transition concurrently, commit one transition and return a stale-version conflict for the other.

**Security and audit implications:** Conflict responses reveal only records the caller may access; record rejected attempts for financial/security-sensitive transitions.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Conflict text is localized; version tokens and arithmetic are locale-independent.

**Verification method:** Automated integration/acceptance tests for the stated scenarios, plus role-based negative tests and audit-record inspection where security or approval is involved.

**REQUIREMENT 0490 OF 1120  |  PROJECTS, SERVICE MANAGEMENT, AND FIXED ASSETS**

## ERP-ASSETS-070 — Retention, legal hold, and purge boundary

**Normative requirement:** The system shall apply configurable retention and legal-hold policies to operational records, audit evidence, and attachments, with separate archival and deletion capabilities.

**Rationale:** Retention obligations vary by jurisdiction, contract, and record class and cannot be hard-coded universally.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A held record is excluded from automated purge and records hold reference and release actor/time.

**AC 2.** Expired records are archived or deleted only per configured class policy and workflow.

**AC 3.** Purge test confirms references are handled according to retention policy and cannot orphan financial ledger facts.

**Exception / edge case:** If retention eligibility conflicts with an active legal hold, preserve the record and flag the policy conflict for authorized review.

**Security and audit implications:** Retention-policy changes require authorized approval; log archive, hold, release, and purge actions while minimizing retained personal data.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Policy names and notices localize; retention duration and trigger are explicit configuration values, not inferred from language or country alone.

**Verification method:** Automated integration/acceptance tests for the stated scenarios, plus role-based negative tests and audit-record inspection where security or approval is involved.

# Core Platform, Master Data, Workflow, and Reporting

# 08 — Core platform, master data, workflow, and reporting

**Specification status:** implementation-ready domain chapter. **Product baseline verified for 2026-11-22:** ASP.NET Core on .NET 11.0.0 (GA on 2026-11-10; STS; support ends 2028-11-14) is the latest stable supported .NET listed by Microsoft. Microsoft also lists .NET 10 as supported LTS through the same end date. The baseline intentionally chooses latest stable, .NET 11, and requires current servicing patches; revalidate the lifecycle immediately before implementation freeze and each production release. \[1] The PostgreSQL project currently lists PostgreSQL 19.0 as supported, released 2026-11-19, with upstream support through 2031-11-19. The database baseline is PostgreSQL 19, latest supported minor at the release gate. PostgreSQL 18–15 also remain listed as supported; the exact selected minor and managed-service mapping must be reconfirmed at deployment. \[2] The frontend is a lightweight Next.js App Router application. The official installation guide currently states Node.js 20.9 as the minimum; this specification does not pin a Next.js release number because the version-specific support window and release compatibility must be reconfirmed when the implementation is initialized. Server Components are the default for pages/layouts; client code is limited to interactive boundaries. \[6] \[8]

## Scope and design

This chapter specifies cross-cutting platform services shared by ERP modules: tenant and organization context, identity-to-membership mapping, authorization primitives, governed master-data foundations, configurable workflow execution, report execution/catalog/export, localization, and audit/operations contracts. It does not define transactional domain rules for finance, procurement, HR, manufacturing, tax, or other modules. Industry extensions may add typed records and process-specific behavior through declared contracts; they may not weaken tenant isolation, audit, or platform authorization. Jurisdictional requirements are configuration boundaries, not universal assumptions. The product shall not hard-code a statutory retention period, fiscal year, tax treatment, legal identifier format, approval threshold, required address field, chart of accounts, or industry classification as universal law. A tenant administrator or an approved jurisdiction/industry extension selects sourced, versioned rules and remains responsible for local legal/compliance validation. If legal or regulatory evidence is unavailable or disputed, leave the rule configurable and explicitly unresolved.

### Actors

Actors include tenant users; master-data stewards; workflow authors, publishers, approvers, and task assignees; report authors and consumers; tenant administrators; identity administrators; platform operators; service identities used by integrations; and compliance/investigation users. A person may hold multiple roles, but role combination does not implicitly bypass separation-of-duties policies.

### Core entities

Core entities are Tenant; User identity; TenantMembership; Role and Permission; Organization and LegalEntity; OperatingUnit and Location; FiscalCalendar; TimeZone setting; Currency/Unit reference version; MasterRecord with immutable ID, business code, labels, attributes, lifecycle and effective-dated revisions; WorkflowDefinitionVersion and WorkflowInstance/Task/Decision; ReportDefinitionVersion and ReportRun/Artifact; AuditEvent; RetentionPolicy/LegalHold; ModuleContract; and ExtensionPackage. Tenant-owned records carry tenant scope, and entity scope is represented where appropriate. PostgreSQL unique, primary-key, and foreign-key constraints provide integrity; row-level security can add row filtering but must be verified under the real non-owner/non-BYPASSRLS application role. \[3] \[4]

### Workflows

Provisioning creates a tenant, administrator membership, default locale/time zone, organization shell, and approved configuration through explicit lifecycle transitions. Identity authentication establishes a principal; active tenant membership and operation/resource policy checks then determine access. ASP.NET Core authorization is policy-based and resource-aware: authentication does not itself authorize an endpoint. \[5] Master-data changes follow draft/validate/approve/publish or direct-edit patterns per data type; every type declares lifecycle, uniqueness scope, effective-date behavior, provenance, translations, and merge policy. Workflow authors validate and publish immutable versions; each runtime instance binds to its starting version. State changes are transactional with audit/outbox records, while external notification and integrations are asynchronous, idempotent effects. Reports are catalogued and versioned, scoped and reauthorized at execution/export, and run synchronously only within configured bounds; larger jobs are asynchronous and expiring.

### Permission boundaries

Use least privilege and deny-by-default semantics for tenant membership, resource access, report data, administration, and exports. Separate platform operator elevation from tenant roles. Separate audit read/search from audit retention or infrastructure administration. Master-data stewardship does not imply permission to alter authorization configuration. Workflow assignment does not override transaction-level authority or maker-checker restrictions. Report visibility is enforced server-side, including derived values and cached results. PostgreSQL RLS is defense in depth, not a substitute for application checks: table owners normally bypass RLS, and superusers or BYPASSRLS roles always bypass it. \[3]

### Major decisions

The baseline selects .NET 11 / ASP.NET Core and PostgreSQL 19 based on official primary-source pages available on the specified date. Microsoft says .NET 11 GA was 2026-11-10 and STS ends 2028-11-14; PostgreSQL lists major version 19 supported through 2031-11-19 and recommends the current minor for its major release. \[1] \[2] These are time-sensitive snapshots, not a promise of future support. Reconfirm Microsoft lifecycle, PostgreSQL support/minor, ASP.NET Core target, and managed-provider compatibility before every major release. The frontend is Next.js with server-first rendering and small client components; no specific Next.js version is assumed. \[6] \[8] Use immutable internal identifiers separately from business codes and translated labels. Keep locale, formatting locale, time zone, and content language distinct. Language identifiers follow BCP 47; locale-sensitive dates, numbers, currencies, and plural behavior use a maintained locale-data library such as Unicode CLDR rather than custom per-language formatting. \[7] \[9] \[10] Target WCAG 2.2 AA for complete pages and user journeys. \[11] The platform provides extension points and rules engines but keeps legal/industry decisions out of core defaults. Configured workflow thresholds, fiscal calendars, retention, address requirements, numbering rules, and jurisdiction reference data must have an owner, version, scope, effective date, provenance, and applicable acceptance tests.

### Dependencies and cross-module contracts

Business modules consume stable platform IDs and declared API/event contracts; they must not directly depend on another module’s private tables. Cross-module references declare tenant and legal-entity scope, lifecycle behavior, permission codes, effective-date semantics, and deletion/retirement rules. Module-owned events use a transactional outbox, stable event IDs, tenant context, schema versions, correlation IDs, and idempotent consumer behavior. Common dependencies include external identity providers, time-zone and locale data, email or messaging providers, secrets management, an observability pipeline, and customer-selected industry/jurisdiction extensions.

### Risks and controls

Primary risks are cross-tenant disclosure through direct APIs, RLS bypass by privileged database roles, stale authorization in caches, mass assignment during merge/import, workflow self-approval, report aggregation leakage, unsafe CSV formula execution, locale-dependent parsing errors, daylight-saving schedule drift, schema evolution that breaks modules, and sensitive data copied into logs or exports. Controls include tenant predicates at application and database layers, adversarial isolation tests, scoped roles, immutable audit/outbox events, versioned contracts, typed inputs, bounded queries, reauthorization at download/delivery, Unicode and RTL test fixtures, explicit time-zone policies, retention configuration, and repeated backup/restore and migration rehearsal. Security and privacy controls should be selected and tailored to organizational risk; NIST SP 800-53 is a control catalog rather than a universal legal mandate. \[12]

## Core Platform, Master Data, Workflow, and Reporting — requirement cards

**REQUIREMENT 0491 OF 1120  |  CORE PLATFORM, MASTER DATA, WORKFLOW, AND REPORTING**

## ERP-PLATFORM-001 — Runtime baseline and framework support

**Normative requirement:** The service backend shall target ASP.NET Core on the latest stable, supported .NET release verified at release-baseline approval, with a documented supported runtime and deployment matrix.

**Rationale:** Keeps the platform within vendor support while allowing an explicit revalidation gate for an evolving annual release train.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Build metadata records the target framework and runtime version; CI rejects a target not in the approved matrix.

**AC 2.** The baseline decision record identifies the official Microsoft lifecycle page, verification date, latest stable release, support type, and end-of-support date.

**AC 3.** A deployment smoke test reports the runtime version and fails when it differs from the approved major/minor line.

**Exception / edge case:** If a newer version has only a preview/RC listing or lifecycle evidence is unavailable, retain the currently verified supported release and mark revalidation as a release gate.

**Security and audit implications:** Restrict production runtime images to approved, patched builds; retain signed build provenance and record runtime inventory for incident response.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Runtime selection is independent of user locale; localized diagnostics must not leak secrets or expose untranslated server internals.

**Verification method:** CI policy test, image inspection, and release-record review.

**REQUIREMENT 0492 OF 1120  |  CORE PLATFORM, MASTER DATA, WORKFLOW, AND REPORTING**

## ERP-PLATFORM-002 — Supported runtime patching

**Normative requirement:** The platform shall run the latest vendor-serviced patch of its approved .NET major release and shall provide an owner, cadence, and rollback procedure for runtime updates.

**Rationale:** Vendor support is contingent on remaining current with released patches; controlled patching reduces exposure without arbitrary drift.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A scheduled dependency scan identifies stale runtime images and opens a failing release check when a critical update exceeds the configured remediation window.

**AC 2.** A staging deployment exercises health checks and a smoke suite before production promotion.

**AC 3.** Rollback restores the previous approved image without reverting persisted schema/data changes.

**Exception / edge case:** When a patch is incompatible with an environment, block promotion, document compensating controls, and set an expiry for the exception.

**Security and audit implications:** Patch status and exceptions are auditable; no secrets appear in scan artifacts.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Operator-facing patch alerts use the administrator's selected language and preserve version identifiers verbatim.

**Verification method:** Pipeline policy test, staging deployment test, and audit-log inspection.

**REQUIREMENT 0493 OF 1120  |  CORE PLATFORM, MASTER DATA, WORKFLOW, AND REPORTING**

## ERP-PLATFORM-003 — Database support baseline

**Normative requirement:** The platform shall deploy on a PostgreSQL major version listed as supported by the PostgreSQL project at baseline approval and shall record the selected major/minor versions.

**Rationale:** PostgreSQL major versions have finite support windows and major upgrades can require data-directory migration or pg_upgrade.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Deployment manifest pins the PostgreSQL major version and approved minor range.

**AC 2.** Release check compares deployed major/minor against the recorded approval and refuses unsupported majors.

**AC 3.** Runbook identifies tested major-upgrade path, backup, restore rehearsal, and rollback boundary.

**Exception / edge case:** Managed database services may expose vendor-patched builds; the operator shall record service/version mapping when upstream minor numbers differ.

**Security and audit implications:** Database service accounts are least-privileged; version metadata is retained as part of security asset inventory.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Version checks and database errors are locale-neutral machine signals with translated operator presentation.

**Verification method:** Infrastructure-as-code inspection, support-matrix test, and restore/upgrade rehearsal.

**REQUIREMENT 0494 OF 1120  |  CORE PLATFORM, MASTER DATA, WORKFLOW, AND REPORTING**

## ERP-PLATFORM-004 — Schema migration discipline

**Normative requirement:** Database schema changes shall be delivered as ordered, immutable migrations with explicit compatibility and rollback or forward-fix instructions.

**Rationale:** Auditable, staged schema evolution prevents modules and reporting clients from silently depending on incompatible structures.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** CI applies all migrations to an empty PostgreSQL database and to the prior release fixture.

**AC 2.** Migration ledger records migration ID, checksum, applied timestamp, and deployment identity.

**AC 3.** A migration with a changed checksum or missing predecessor is rejected before execution.

**Exception / edge case:** Destructive changes that cannot be safely reversed require a staged expand/backfill/contract plan and explicit data-recovery procedure.

**Security and audit implications:** Migration execution requires deployment privilege and emits tamper-evident audit events; tenant business data is not included in logs.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Schema identifiers are stable machine names; labels and migration error summaries are localized separately.

**Verification method:** Migration integration tests, checksum-negative test, and migration-ledger review.

**REQUIREMENT 0495 OF 1120  |  CORE PLATFORM, MASTER DATA, WORKFLOW, AND REPORTING**

## ERP-PLATFORM-005 — Versioned public API contract

**Normative requirement:** The platform shall expose a documented, versioned API contract for public and module-to-platform operations, including request/response schemas and error semantics.

**Rationale:** Stable, inspectable contracts allow independently deployed modules and clients to evolve without coupling to internal tables.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** OpenAPI artifact is generated for each released API version and validates against runtime endpoints.

**AC 2.** Breaking schema changes require a new API version or a documented compatibility transition.

**AC 3.** Contract tests verify representative success, validation, authorization, and not-found responses.

**Exception / edge case:** Emergency security fixes may remove an unsafe operation immediately, but the change and client migration impact must be recorded.

**Security and audit implications:** The contract identifies authentication scopes and data classification; error payloads never disclose cross-tenant existence.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Human-readable descriptions and validation messages are translatable; field names and enum wire values remain locale-invariant.

**Verification method:** OpenAPI lint, compatibility checker, and consumer-driven contract tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0496 OF 1120  |  CORE PLATFORM, MASTER DATA, WORKFLOW, AND REPORTING**

## ERP-PLATFORM-006 — Health and readiness endpoints

**Normative requirement:** The service shall expose separate liveness and readiness signals that reflect process health and the ability to serve requests, without disclosing sensitive infrastructure detail.

**Rationale:** Orchestrators need reliable signals that distinguish restart-worthy failure from temporarily unavailable dependencies.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Liveness returns success when the process can make progress, regardless of downstream dependency availability.

**AC 2.** Readiness fails when required database or configuration dependencies are unavailable and recovers when restored.

**AC 3.** Unauthenticated health output contains only status and stable component codes, not connection strings or tenant data.

**Exception / edge case:** Optional integrations may be degraded without making the core service unready when their failure policy is configured as non-blocking.

**Security and audit implications:** Protect detailed diagnostics behind operator authorization and rate limits; health probes must not enumerate tenant records.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Probe payloads use machine codes; dashboards localize descriptions.

**Verification method:** Container probe tests with database/integration outage injection and response inspection.

**REQUIREMENT 0497 OF 1120  |  CORE PLATFORM, MASTER DATA, WORKFLOW, AND REPORTING**

## ERP-PLATFORM-007 — Idempotent command submission

**Normative requirement:** State-changing API commands that may be retried shall support a caller-supplied idempotency key scoped to tenant, operation, and authenticated caller.

**Rationale:** Retries after network timeouts must not create duplicate master records, approvals, or workflow actions.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Repeating the same key and same canonical request within the retention window returns the original result without reapplying side effects.

**AC 2.** Reusing a key with a different request hash returns a conflict and creates no mutation.

**AC 3.** Parallel requests with the same key produce exactly one committed operation.

**Exception / edge case:** After key expiry the operation may be accepted anew; expiry duration is visible in the API contract.

**Security and audit implications:** Keys are not authorization credentials; store a keyed digest where feasible and audit collisions without logging raw secrets.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Canonical request hashing is independent of localized display labels and uses stable wire values.

**Verification method:** API integration tests including concurrent duplicate calls and altered-payload reuse.

**REQUIREMENT 0498 OF 1120  |  CORE PLATFORM, MASTER DATA, WORKFLOW, AND REPORTING**

## ERP-PLATFORM-008 — Transactional boundary ownership

**Normative requirement:** Each platform command shall define its atomic database boundary and shall not report success until all required local changes commit.

**Rationale:** Explicit transaction ownership avoids partial writes across workflow state, master data, and audit records.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A fault injected before commit leaves no partial business-state change.

**AC 2.** A successful command commits its business mutation and required audit/outbox records in the same database transaction.

**AC 3.** The API returns a stable failure code when commit fails and does not return a success identifier.

**Exception / edge case:** External systems cannot join the PostgreSQL transaction; they use an outbox/inbox or compensating workflow rather than pretending to be atomic.

**Security and audit implications:** Transaction errors are correlated to request IDs while parameters and sensitive business values are redacted.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Error messages are localized at presentation; transaction identifiers and timestamps remain machine-readable.

**Verification method:** Database fault-injection tests and transaction/audit consistency assertions.

**REQUIREMENT 0499 OF 1120  |  CORE PLATFORM, MASTER DATA, WORKFLOW, AND REPORTING**

## ERP-PLATFORM-009 — Tenant boundary enforcement

**Normative requirement:** Every tenant-owned record and operation shall be scoped to an immutable tenant identifier, enforced in application authorization and supported by database constraints or row-level policies.

**Rationale:** Tenant separation is a security boundary, not merely a query convention; PostgreSQL RLS is defense in depth and has owner/BYPASSRLS caveats.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Automated tests attempt cross-tenant reads, inserts, updates, deletes, exports, and workflow actions through each data-access path and observe denial or zero rows.

**AC 2.** Tenant ID participates in tenant-owned unique keys and foreign-key relationships where applicable.

**AC 3.** Application database roles are not superusers, table owners, or BYPASSRLS roles; policies are tested under the actual runtime role.

**Exception / edge case:** Platform operators may perform explicitly authorized cross-tenant support actions only through a separately audited, time-limited pathway.

**Security and audit implications:** Tenant context is derived from authenticated membership, never trusted from an unvalidated request field; cross-tenant actions require reason and audit trail.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Tenant locale cannot change tenant scope; locale-specific query/cache keys include tenant ID.

**Verification method:** Cross-tenant penetration tests, PostgreSQL RLS policy tests, and role privilege inspection.

**REQUIREMENT 0500 OF 1120  |  CORE PLATFORM, MASTER DATA, WORKFLOW, AND REPORTING**

## ERP-PLATFORM-010 — Tenant lifecycle

**Normative requirement:** The platform shall implement tenant provisioning, activation, suspension, export, and closure as controlled lifecycle transitions with explicit preconditions and retained evidence.

**Rationale:** Tenant lifecycle operations affect access, retention, billing, and recoverability and must not be modeled as an untracked boolean.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Each lifecycle transition validates permitted prior state and records actor, timestamp, reason, and transition result.

**AC 2.** Suspended tenants cannot authenticate or execute business commands but remain accessible to authorized retention/export workflows.

**AC 3.** Tenant closure cannot complete until configured data export, retention, and deletion obligations are resolved.

**Exception / edge case:** A legal hold, unresolved asynchronous job, or active statutory retention rule may pause closure and clearly return the blocking reason.

**Security and audit implications:** Only platform tenant-administration roles may transition lifecycle state; actions generate immutable audit events.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Lifecycle notification templates support tenant language; identifiers and transition codes remain stable.

**Verification method:** State-machine tests, authorization tests, and closure-blocker integration tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0501 OF 1120  |  CORE PLATFORM, MASTER DATA, WORKFLOW, AND REPORTING**

## ERP-PLATFORM-011 — Tenant configuration isolation

**Normative requirement:** Tenant-specific settings shall be stored and resolved under tenant scope, with defaults, allowed overrides, schema validation, and an auditable effective value.

**Rationale:** Shared deployment supports different organizations without leaking or overwriting configuration across customers.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A tenant can read and update only settings authorized for its scope.

**AC 2.** Invalid setting names, types, or values are rejected against a versioned schema.

**AC 3.** Setting resolution reports whether the effective value comes from platform default, product edition, or tenant override.

**Exception / edge case:** A setting may be locked by platform policy; tenant UI must explain the lock without allowing a shadow override.

**Security and audit implications:** Secrets are stored in a secret manager or encrypted field and are never returned in plaintext after write; changes are audited.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Localized labels/descriptions are separate from stable configuration keys and values.

**Verification method:** Tenant-isolation tests, schema validation tests, and secret-redaction inspection.

**REQUIREMENT 0502 OF 1120  |  CORE PLATFORM, MASTER DATA, WORKFLOW, AND REPORTING**

## ERP-PLATFORM-012 — Organization and legal-entity hierarchy

**Normative requirement:** The platform shall represent tenant organizations, legal entities, operating units, and parent-child relationships as distinct records with effective-dated membership.

**Rationale:** Enterprise deployments need consolidated but separable organizational structures; legal entities must not be conflated with departments or UI groups.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A tenant can create multiple legal entities and operating units with stable IDs and parent links.

**AC 2.** The API rejects cycles in the hierarchy and rejects parent links across tenants.

**AC 3.** Changing a parent preserves prior effective-dated relationships for historical reporting.

**Exception / edge case:** Entity types and legal meaning are configurable by jurisdiction/industry; the core schema does not assert universal legal definitions.

**Security and audit implications:** Legal entity changes require authorized administration and audit before/after values, with sensitive identifiers masked in logs.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Entity names support multiple translations and scripts; registered legal names and transliterations are separately typed values.

**Verification method:** Hierarchy API tests, cycle tests, temporal queries, and audit review.

**REQUIREMENT 0503 OF 1120  |  CORE PLATFORM, MASTER DATA, WORKFLOW, AND REPORTING**

## ERP-PLATFORM-013 — Organizational units and locations

**Normative requirement:** The platform shall maintain typed organizational units and physical/virtual locations with stable identifiers, tenant ownership, and optional parent relationships.

**Rationale:** Modules need a shared location and responsibility vocabulary while businesses retain different structures.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A location record has type, status, owning entity, and optional address reference.

**AC 2.** A transaction cannot reference an inactive or cross-tenant location unless an explicit historical exception is allowed.

**AC 3.** Hierarchy queries return deterministic parent paths and do not recurse through cycles.

**Exception / edge case:** Location address fields and geocoding requirements are country-specific configuration, not universal mandatory fields.

**Security and audit implications:** Access to restricted facility details is permission-controlled and read access is auditable where configured.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Address forms use country-aware validation and locale-sensitive presentation without altering canonical stored values.

**Verification method:** Entity validation tests, hierarchy tests, and address localization test matrix.

**REQUIREMENT 0504 OF 1120  |  CORE PLATFORM, MASTER DATA, WORKFLOW, AND REPORTING**

## ERP-PLATFORM-014 — Fiscal calendar configuration

**Normative requirement:** The platform shall support tenant/entity fiscal calendars with explicit periods, period status, and effective dates without assuming a universal fiscal-year start.

**Rationale:** Workflow deadlines, reports, and downstream modules depend on fiscal periods that vary by organization and jurisdiction.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** An authorized administrator can define a fiscal year start and period boundaries for an entity.

**AC 2.** The platform rejects overlapping periods within the same calendar and prevents closing a period with configured blockers.

**AC 3.** Reports return the calendar ID and period definition used for each fiscal grouping.

**Exception / edge case:** Jurisdiction-specific statutory calendars, special periods, and adjustments are extension/configuration concerns and must be named explicitly.

**Security and audit implications:** Calendar changes are permissioned and audited; closed historical periods cannot be silently rewritten.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Display dates follow user locale while fiscal boundaries are stored as explicit dates and calendar identifiers.

**Verification method:** Boundary tests for leap years, period overlaps, and report grouping; audit assertions.

**REQUIREMENT 0505 OF 1120  |  CORE PLATFORM, MASTER DATA, WORKFLOW, AND REPORTING**

## ERP-PLATFORM-015 — Time-zone configuration

**Normative requirement:** The platform shall store instants in a canonical UTC representation and separately retain the relevant IANA time-zone identifier for local scheduling and display.

**Rationale:** A UTC instant and local business date answer different questions; daylight-saving transitions make fixed offsets unsafe for future schedules.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** An event instant round-trips to UTC and displays in the user's selected zone.

**AC 2.** A scheduled local time records its zone ID and resolves ambiguous/nonexistent DST times using an explicit policy.

**AC 3.** Changing a user's display zone does not alter stored transaction instants or business dates.

**Exception / edge case:** Where local time falls in a DST gap or overlap, the configured reject/earlier/later choice is surfaced rather than guessed.

**Security and audit implications:** Time-zone changes and administrative corrections are audited; no locale string is accepted as a time-zone authorization value.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Dates, calendars, and zone names are locale-formatted; stored identifiers use IANA zone IDs and ISO timestamps.

**Verification method:** Automated tests across DST transitions and UTC/local round-trip checks.

**REQUIREMENT 0506 OF 1120  |  CORE PLATFORM, MASTER DATA, WORKFLOW, AND REPORTING**

## ERP-PLATFORM-016 — Currency and unit reference settings
