**Normative requirement:** The platform shall provide versioned reference settings for currencies and units, while leaving transaction-specific conversion rules and legal reporting requirements to module/jurisdiction configuration.

**Rationale:** Currency display, precision, and unit conversion conventions vary and must not be hard-coded as global legal behavior.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Reference values have stable codes, effective dates, and source/version metadata.

**AC 2.** A configured precision rule is applied consistently to validation and display without silently rounding stored source amounts.

**AC 3.** A deprecated reference value remains resolvable for historical records but cannot be chosen for new records unless permitted.

**Exception / edge case:** Currency redenominations, non-decimal units, and statutory rounding are handled by explicit effective-dated configuration or an industry extension.

**Security and audit implications:** Changes to reference precision or conversion data are restricted and audited; currency values do not grant access.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Formatting uses CLDR locale data; machine API amounts and codes are locale-neutral and never use formatted strings as numeric input.

**Verification method:** Reference-data tests for historical effective dates, decimal parsing, and locale formatting.

**REQUIREMENT 0507 OF 1120  |  CORE PLATFORM, MASTER DATA, WORKFLOW, AND REPORTING**

## ERP-PLATFORM-017 — Configurable business numbering

**Normative requirement:** The platform shall generate configured human-readable identifiers by tenant and document type while retaining an immutable internal primary key.

**Rationale:** Business numbers often require prefixes, sequences, periods, or entity scope and should not become database identity or security tokens.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Concurrent creation under one numbering scope yields unique numbers with no duplicate committed result.

**AC 2.** A sequence format can include configured entity, period, and prefix components and has a documented reset policy.

**AC 3.** Changing the display format does not change previously assigned identifiers.

**Exception / edge case:** Gaps may occur after transaction rollback or reserved number allocation unless a jurisdiction-specific extension requires a different documented control.

**Security and audit implications:** Number assignment is authorized, monitored, and audited; IDs must not be treated as unguessable access tokens.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Prefixes may be localized only if configured; sequence digits and separators must remain unambiguous in exports and integrations.

**Verification method:** Concurrency stress test, rollback test, and numbering configuration tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0508 OF 1120  |  CORE PLATFORM, MASTER DATA, WORKFLOW, AND REPORTING**

## ERP-PLATFORM-018 — Identity-provider integration

**Normative requirement:** The platform shall authenticate human users through a configurable standards-based identity provider and shall separate authentication identity from ERP user and tenant memberships.

**Rationale:** Enterprise customers require federation and identity lifecycle control; a successful login alone does not grant ERP permissions.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A user can sign in through an enabled provider and maps to a stable external subject plus internal user ID.

**AC 2.** Unmapped or disabled external identities cannot access tenant data.

**AC 3.** Provider logout/token-expiry behavior is tested against the configured session policy.

**Exception / edge case:** Break-glass local access, if enabled, is limited to named emergency accounts with an expiry, MFA, and monitored use.

**Security and audit implications:** Provider secrets are protected; authentication events and mapping changes are audited without storing bearer tokens.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** User display names retain Unicode; identity matching uses stable subject identifiers, not locale-dependent name comparison.

**Verification method:** Federation integration tests, unmapped-user denial test, and token/secrets scan.

**REQUIREMENT 0509 OF 1120  |  CORE PLATFORM, MASTER DATA, WORKFLOW, AND REPORTING**

## ERP-PLATFORM-019 — Multi-factor authentication policy boundary

**Normative requirement:** The platform shall support enforcement of multi-factor authentication through the identity provider or an approved authentication component and shall expose the assurance state required by sensitive actions.

**Rationale:** MFA requirements are tenant and risk-policy dependent; the ERP must consume a verifiable assurance signal rather than infer MFA from a login screen.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A protected action configured to require MFA denies a session lacking the required assurance claim.

**AC 2.** The policy can be enabled per tenant or role without changing business data permissions.

**AC 3.** Audit events record whether the configured assurance condition was met, not the user's secret factor.

**Exception / edge case:** Federated providers may use different claim names; mapping to the platform assurance vocabulary is explicitly configured and tested.

**Security and audit implications:** No one-time code, recovery secret, or factor seed is written to application logs; policy change is audited.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Challenge and recovery instructions are localized; assurance identifiers are stable machine values.

**Verification method:** Claim-mapping tests, negative authorization tests, and log-redaction test.

**REQUIREMENT 0510 OF 1120  |  CORE PLATFORM, MASTER DATA, WORKFLOW, AND REPORTING**

## ERP-PLATFORM-020 — Tenant membership lifecycle

**Normative requirement:** The platform shall model user-to-tenant membership with its own status, role assignments, and effective dates independent of global user status.

**Rationale:** One global identity may participate in multiple tenant organizations with different rights and activation state.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A user without active membership cannot access tenant endpoints even with a valid identity-provider session.

**AC 2.** Suspending membership immediately prevents new authorized actions while preserving audit history.

**AC 3.** Membership invitation acceptance binds to the intended identity and expires according to configured policy.

**Exception / edge case:** Removing the user's last membership may leave an identity record for audit or reuse; retention is governed by tenant policy.

**Security and audit implications:** Membership creation, elevation, suspension, and removal are audited; list endpoints do not disclose other tenants' memberships.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Invitation and membership messages use the recipient's selected language, with locale-neutral expiry timestamps in payloads.

**Verification method:** Cross-tenant membership authorization tests and invitation-expiry tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0511 OF 1120  |  CORE PLATFORM, MASTER DATA, WORKFLOW, AND REPORTING**

## ERP-PLATFORM-021 — Role and permission catalog

**Normative requirement:** The platform shall provide a versioned permission catalog and tenant-assignable roles that map to least-privilege actions rather than relying on UI visibility.

**Rationale:** A reusable permission vocabulary supports consistent enforcement across API endpoints, workflows, exports, and administration.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Each protected operation declares a permission code checked by server-side authorization.

**AC 2.** A role assignment can be resolved to effective permission codes and is tenant-scoped.

**AC 3.** Removing a permission from a role denies the corresponding API action even when the UI control is manually invoked.

**Exception / edge case:** Custom tenant roles may combine approved permissions but cannot grant reserved platform-operator capabilities.

**Security and audit implications:** Role changes are audited with actor, target, before/after assignments, and reason; privileged roles require stronger controls.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Permission descriptions are localizable while permission codes remain stable and language-independent.

**Verification method:** Permission-matrix tests, API bypass tests, and role-change audit tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0512 OF 1120  |  CORE PLATFORM, MASTER DATA, WORKFLOW, AND REPORTING**

## ERP-PLATFORM-022 — Resource-level policy checks

**Normative requirement:** The platform shall evaluate authorization against both operation and target resource attributes, including tenant, legal entity, ownership, and status where defined.

**Rationale:** Roles alone cannot safely represent record-level or organization-scope access in an enterprise ERP.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A user authorized for a resource in one entity is denied an equivalent resource in an unauthorized entity.

**AC 2.** Update authorization is checked against both the existing record and proposed new scope attributes.

**AC 3.** Authorization policy tests cover read, create, update, delete, and export operations.

**Exception / edge case:** A delegated cross-entity role may widen scope only through an explicit, effective-dated assignment.

**Security and audit implications:** Use deny-by-default policy for missing scope claims; log policy decision IDs without exposing protected resource fields.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Human-readable denial detail is localized, but policy evaluation uses canonical IDs and codes.

**Verification method:** Policy unit tests and end-to-end negative resource-scope tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0513 OF 1120  |  CORE PLATFORM, MASTER DATA, WORKFLOW, AND REPORTING**

## ERP-PLATFORM-023 — Separation-of-duties controls

**Normative requirement:** The platform shall allow administrators to configure incompatible role or workflow duties and enforce those constraints at assignment or transaction approval time.

**Rationale:** Organizations may require independent creation and approval; one universal duty-conflict matrix cannot be assumed for every industry.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A configured conflicting role pair is rejected or routed for an authorized exception before assignment.

**AC 2.** A configured maker-checker rule prevents the creator from completing the same approval step.

**AC 3.** Exception approval records approver, justification, validity window, and affected control.

**Exception / edge case:** Emergency override requires a documented, time-limited exception and can be disabled per tenant policy.

**Security and audit implications:** Duty-conflict definitions and overrides are privileged configuration and auditable; alert on attempts to self-approve.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Duty names and explanations are translatable; conflict keys are stable configuration identifiers.

**Verification method:** Assignment tests for conflict and exception expiry; workflow self-approval tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0514 OF 1120  |  CORE PLATFORM, MASTER DATA, WORKFLOW, AND REPORTING**

## ERP-PLATFORM-024 — Session revocation and revalidation

**Normative requirement:** The platform shall support revocation or expiry of ERP sessions and re-evaluation of membership and authorization state for sensitive requests.

**Rationale:** Role removal or compromised credentials must take effect before a long-lived browser token silently preserves access.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Revoking a user or membership causes subsequent protected requests to fail within the configured maximum propagation interval.

**AC 2.** Sensitive actions re-check current tenant membership and permission rather than relying solely on a stale client-side role cache.

**AC 3.** Revocation events are correlated with the affected sessions and subsequent denial.

**Exception / edge case:** Read-only cached pages may remain visible until refresh if they contain no newly fetched protected data and the tenant policy permits it.

**Security and audit implications:** Tokens are never logged; revocation is administrative and audited; caches are invalidated by user and tenant scope.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Expired-session and reauthentication prompts are localized without echoing identity secrets.

**Verification method:** Revocation integration test with cached session and permission-change scenarios.

**REQUIREMENT 0515 OF 1120  |  CORE PLATFORM, MASTER DATA, WORKFLOW, AND REPORTING**

## ERP-PLATFORM-025 — Non-human service identities

**Normative requirement:** The platform shall represent integrations and automation as non-human identities with scoped permissions, credential rotation metadata, and an owning administrator.

**Rationale:** Service accounts need narrower access and lifecycle controls than human interactive accounts.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A service identity can be restricted to selected tenants, APIs, and operations.

**AC 2.** Credential expiry or revocation prevents authenticated calls within the configured propagation interval.

**AC 3.** The platform displays last-used time, owner, scopes, and rotation due date for each service identity.

**Exception / edge case:** A vendor integration requiring a shared credential must use a documented compensating boundary and unique client identifier where possible.

**Security and audit implications:** Secrets are stored hashed or in a vault, never shown after creation, and every credential issue/revoke event is audited.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Integration labels may be localized; machine scopes and client identifiers are locale-neutral.

**Verification method:** Service-scope API tests, secret scan, and revocation test.

**REQUIREMENT 0516 OF 1120  |  CORE PLATFORM, MASTER DATA, WORKFLOW, AND REPORTING**

## ERP-PLATFORM-026 — Privileged access elevation

**Normative requirement:** The platform shall gate platform-wide and tenant-wide privileged operations behind a separate elevation workflow with reason, expiry, and immutable audit record.

**Rationale:** Routine support access should not confer persistent broad visibility across tenant information.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** An operator cannot perform an elevated action without an active approved elevation grant.

**AC 2.** Grant expiry automatically removes the elevated capability and subsequent calls are denied.

**AC 3.** Every elevated action records operator, tenant, reason, target, time, and decision.

**Exception / edge case:** Incident response may use emergency elevation only if the emergency path is separately configured and triggers immediate review notification.

**Security and audit implications:** Elevation requires strong authentication, least scope, time bounds, and reviewable audit records; sensitive content is not copied to support logs.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Reason prompts and notifications are localized; immutable IDs and timestamps remain language-neutral.

**Verification method:** Privilege-path negative tests, expiry test, and audit review simulation.

**REQUIREMENT 0517 OF 1120  |  CORE PLATFORM, MASTER DATA, WORKFLOW, AND REPORTING**

## ERP-PLATFORM-027 — Immutable master-data identifiers

**Normative requirement:** Each master-data record shall have an immutable, non-recycled system identifier separate from its editable business code and translated display names.

**Rationale:** Stable references are required for integrations, history, merge lineage, and localization changes.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Changing a business code or translation leaves primary references and foreign keys unchanged.

**AC 2.** Deleted or retired identifiers are never reassigned to a new record.

**AC 3.** API responses distinguish system ID, business code, and localized label.

**Exception / edge case:** Externally assigned IDs are stored as typed aliases with source system and uniqueness scope rather than replacing the internal ID.

**Security and audit implications:** Identifier guessing does not grant access; changes to aliases and codes are audited.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Labels are localized independently; IDs and external references are preserved exactly for round-trip integrations.

**Verification method:** Persistence and API contract tests covering rename and retirement.

**REQUIREMENT 0518 OF 1120  |  CORE PLATFORM, MASTER DATA, WORKFLOW, AND REPORTING**

## ERP-PLATFORM-028 — Tenant-scoped business code uniqueness

**Normative requirement:** The platform shall enforce uniqueness of configured business codes within their declared tenant and object-type scope using database constraints or equivalent atomic validation.

**Rationale:** Application-only duplicate checks race under concurrent entry and can incorrectly impose global uniqueness.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Two concurrent creates with the same normalized code and scope result in exactly one success.

**AC 2.** The same code is permitted in different tenants when configuration allows.

**AC 3.** Uniqueness comparison uses a declared normalization/case rule and the API returns a stable conflict code.

**Exception / edge case:** Historical or imported duplicate codes may be retained under an explicit legacy namespace or exception status.

**Security and audit implications:** Duplicate errors reveal no record details across tenants; code changes are audited.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Normalization is language/Unicode-aware and explicitly configured; labels are not used as uniqueness keys.

**Verification method:** Concurrent database integration tests, collation tests, and cross-tenant duplicate tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0519 OF 1120  |  CORE PLATFORM, MASTER DATA, WORKFLOW, AND REPORTING**

## ERP-PLATFORM-029 — Multilingual master-data labels

**Normative requirement:** Master-data types designated translatable shall store one canonical record with zero or more language-tagged labels and an explicit fallback policy.

**Rationale:** Translated names should not create duplicate business entities or be confused with legally registered names.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A user request for a supported locale returns the exact locale label when present.

**AC 2.** When absent, the configured fallback chain selects one label and reports the fallback locale.

**AC 3.** Translation updates do not alter the master record ID or business code.

**Exception / edge case:** Some fields such as a registered legal name may require source-language fidelity and cannot be replaced by a translated label.

**Security and audit implications:** Translation editing is permissioned and audited; user-supplied strings are output-encoded in UI/export.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Language tags follow BCP 47; labels support Unicode and scripts; fallback behavior is deterministic.

**Verification method:** API tests for exact match/fallback and Unicode round-trip tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0520 OF 1120  |  CORE PLATFORM, MASTER DATA, WORKFLOW, AND REPORTING**

## ERP-PLATFORM-030 — Versioned reference data

**Normative requirement:** The platform shall manage shared code lists and reference datasets with stable code, version, effective date, provenance, and tenant override policy.

**Rationale:** Business modules need consistent statuses and categories without confusing product defaults with government-mandated classifications.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A reference value can be queried as effective for a supplied business date.

**AC 2.** Changes create a new revision or effective-dated record without rewriting past usage.

**AC 3.** Tenant overrides are distinguishable from platform-provided values in API and administration views.

**Exception / edge case:** Jurisdictional tax, company, or industry codes must be sourced and maintained by a separately governed extension; no universal legal list is assumed.

**Security and audit implications:** Only reference-data stewards can publish changes; source and change history are auditable.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Reference descriptions may be localized while codes and version keys remain invariant.

**Verification method:** Temporal reference lookup tests, override isolation tests, and provenance review.

**REQUIREMENT 0521 OF 1120  |  CORE PLATFORM, MASTER DATA, WORKFLOW, AND REPORTING**

## ERP-PLATFORM-031 — Master-data validation rules

**Normative requirement:** The platform shall support versioned validation profiles for master-data types, with field constraints, cross-field rules, and actionable validation errors.

**Rationale:** Organizations and jurisdictions require different mandatory attributes; validation must be configurable rather than hard-coded as global law.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A create/update request is validated against the active profile for its tenant, entity, and effective date.

**AC 2.** Each failed rule returns a stable rule code and field path, with no partial persistence.

**AC 3.** Profile changes are previewable against a representative data set before activation.

**Exception / edge case:** A record already in use may be grandfathered by a profile transition if the administrator records the migration/exception policy.

**Security and audit implications:** Profiles cannot weaken platform security constraints; edits and bypass exceptions are audited.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Rule codes are stable and messages are translatable; validation uses locale-neutral normalized values.

**Verification method:** Profile conformance tests, negative validation tests, and preview dry-run tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0522 OF 1120  |  CORE PLATFORM, MASTER DATA, WORKFLOW, AND REPORTING**

## ERP-PLATFORM-032 — Duplicate detection and merge lineage

**Normative requirement:** The platform shall provide configurable duplicate candidates and a controlled merge operation that preserves source-record lineage and references.

**Rationale:** Consolidating duplicate parties or catalog entries must not erase historical links or silently combine records based on a universal heuristic.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Candidate matching is explainable by configured fields and returns a score/reason set rather than auto-merging by default.

**AC 2.** A merge preserves surviving ID, retired source IDs, actor, timestamp, and selected field provenance.

**AC 3.** All declared foreign-key references are redirected or remain resolvable through the merge map.

**Exception / edge case:** Ambiguous matches, conflicting identifiers, or records subject to legal hold require manual review and may block merge.

**Security and audit implications:** Merge requires a dedicated permission and confirmation; before/after field values and lineage are auditable.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Name matching uses locale-aware search normalization but never discards original script or punctuation from source data.

**Verification method:** Merge integration tests with linked records, conflict fixtures, and audit assertions.

**REQUIREMENT 0523 OF 1120  |  CORE PLATFORM, MASTER DATA, WORKFLOW, AND REPORTING**

## ERP-PLATFORM-033 — Master-record lifecycle states

**Normative requirement:** Each governed master-data type shall define allowed lifecycle states and transitions, including inactive/retired behavior for records referenced by transactions.

**Rationale:** Soft retirement preserves historical integrity while preventing accidental reuse in new transactions.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A record cannot transition to an undefined state or skip a configured required approval.

**AC 2.** Inactive records are excluded from new-entry choices but remain resolvable by historical references.

**AC 3.** Reactivation requires a permitted role and records reason and effective date.

**Exception / edge case:** Hard deletion may be allowed only for unused records or under a specific retention/anonymization rule.

**Security and audit implications:** State transitions and attempted prohibited changes are logged; only authorized stewards can retire/reactivate.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** State labels and transition guidance are localizable; stored state codes are stable.

**Verification method:** Lifecycle state machine tests, historical-reference test, and role tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0524 OF 1120  |  CORE PLATFORM, MASTER DATA, WORKFLOW, AND REPORTING**

## ERP-PLATFORM-034 — Effective-dated master attributes

**Normative requirement:** The platform shall support effective-dated attributes for master data where a value must change over business time, and shall reject unintended overlapping intervals.

**Rationale:** Legal names, assignments, classifications, and reference properties may change without rewriting prior transaction context.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** An as-of query returns the value valid on the supplied date and identifies the applicable revision.

**AC 2.** Overlapping effective intervals are rejected unless the attribute definition explicitly permits overlap.

**AC 3.** Editing a current value preserves the preceding revision and captures actor and reason.

**Exception / edge case:** Corrections may be backdated only by roles permitted by tenant policy and must trigger configured impact review.

**Security and audit implications:** Backdated changes and historical views are audited; access restrictions continue to apply to every revision.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Business dates use configured calendars, not browser locale parsing; translated labels may also be effective-dated if configured.

**Verification method:** Temporal boundary tests, overlap tests, and backdate authorization tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0525 OF 1120  |  CORE PLATFORM, MASTER DATA, WORKFLOW, AND REPORTING**

## ERP-PLATFORM-035 — Master-data relationship integrity

**Normative requirement:** The platform shall validate typed relationships among master records, enforce tenant/entity boundaries, and preserve referential integrity for referenced data.

**Rationale:** Cross-module joins are reliable only when relationships are explicit and references cannot point to missing or out-of-scope entities.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Database foreign keys or equivalent transactional checks reject a reference to a nonexistent target.

**AC 2.** A relationship cannot connect records across tenants unless an approved shared-reference model explicitly permits it.

**AC 3.** Deleting a referenced record is restricted or follows a declared archival action, never an implicit cascade of business history.

**Exception / edge case:** A shared platform dictionary may be linked cross-tenant only as read-only reference data with explicit owner and version.

**Security and audit implications:** Relationship changes are audited and are subject to both source and target permissions.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Relationship labels are localized; keys and relationship types remain stable across languages.

**Verification method:** Constraint tests, cross-tenant relation tests, and delete-behavior tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0526 OF 1120  |  CORE PLATFORM, MASTER DATA, WORKFLOW, AND REPORTING**

## ERP-PLATFORM-036 — Source provenance and change history

**Normative requirement:** The platform shall record provenance for material master-data creation and updates, including source channel, actor/system, timestamp, and changed fields.

**Rationale:** Operators need to explain whether a value came from a user, import, integration, or governed reference-data update.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Every successful governed update emits a history record with before/after values for configured auditable fields.

**AC 2.** Import and API sources are identified by integration/client ID and correlation ID.

**AC 3.** History is queryable by authorized stewards without altering the current record.

**Exception / edge case:** Sensitive or high-volume fields may use masked, hashed, or summarized history according to retention and privacy rules.

**Security and audit implications:** Audit history is append-only for application roles; values classified sensitive are masked to authorized users.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** History field captions and source descriptions are localized; original input is retained without lossy transliteration where policy permits.

**Verification method:** Change-history integration tests and privileged/unprivileged visibility tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0527 OF 1120  |  CORE PLATFORM, MASTER DATA, WORKFLOW, AND REPORTING**

## ERP-PLATFORM-037 — Workflow definition lifecycle

**Normative requirement:** The platform shall support versioned workflow definitions with draft, validated, published, and retired states and explicit activation scope.

**Rationale:** Workflow variation by tenant and process needs governance and reproducible historical execution.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Only a validated version can be published; validation checks missing states, unreachable steps, and unresolved permission references.

**AC 2.** Publishing creates an immutable version identifier and records publisher and time.

**AC 3.** New workflow instances bind to the version active at start and retain it through completion.

**Exception / edge case:** An active version cannot be deleted while instances reference it; retirement stops new starts but preserves running instances.

**Security and audit implications:** Workflow authors, publishers, and executor roles are separate configurable permissions; every publish/retire action is audited.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Workflow labels and instructions support translation per version; transition codes stay locale-neutral.

**Verification method:** Definition validation tests, publication permission tests, and running-instance version tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0528 OF 1120  |  CORE PLATFORM, MASTER DATA, WORKFLOW, AND REPORTING**

## ERP-PLATFORM-038 — Workflow state transition rules

**Normative requirement:** Each workflow instance shall transition only through declared source-to-target edges under a valid actor, command, and precondition.

**Rationale:** Explicit transitions prevent hidden status changes and make process state inspectable by modules and auditors.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** An undeclared state transition returns a stable conflict response and leaves state unchanged.

**AC 2.** A declared transition records prior state, new state, actor, timestamp, and command reference.

**AC 3.** Concurrent transition attempts on one instance result in one valid state change or a documented serial outcome.

**Exception / edge case:** Administrative recovery transitions require a distinct permission, reason, and visible recovery marker.

**Security and audit implications:** State mutation APIs require authorization and optimistic concurrency; attempts and successes are auditable.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** State code is language-neutral; display state and error explanations are translated.

**Verification method:** State machine unit and concurrency tests; audit consistency test.

**REQUIREMENT 0529 OF 1120  |  CORE PLATFORM, MASTER DATA, WORKFLOW, AND REPORTING**

## ERP-PLATFORM-039 — Workflow routing and assignment

**Normative requirement:** The platform shall route workflow tasks using configurable rules over tenant, entity, amount/category attributes, role, and effective-dated organizational assignments.

**Rationale:** Routing differs by organization and process; explicit rule resolution improves explainability and avoids hard-coded approver names.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A test instance with known attributes resolves to the configured queue or assigned user and records matched rule IDs.

**AC 2.** Unmatched routing produces a configured exception queue or fails safely without granting broad access.

**AC 3.** A route is recalculated only at declared points and records old/new assignment when reassigned.

**Exception / edge case:** When a rule resolves to no active eligible user, the task pauses with a visible remediation state rather than auto-approving.

**Security and audit implications:** Routing rules cannot grant access beyond permission policy; assignment changes are logged and auditable.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Rule descriptions and queue labels are localized; matching fields are canonical IDs/codes, not translated text.

**Verification method:** Decision-table tests with matched, unmatched, and inactive-assignee cases.

**REQUIREMENT 0530 OF 1120  |  CORE PLATFORM, MASTER DATA, WORKFLOW, AND REPORTING**

## ERP-PLATFORM-040 — Approval thresholds and authority

**Normative requirement:** The platform shall enforce configurable approval thresholds and authority scopes for workflow actions, with explicit currency/unit basis where numerical thresholds apply.

**Rationale:** Approval limits are organizational controls and vary by tenant, entity, currency, and business process.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A configured boundary value is tested at below, equal-to, and above-threshold amounts.

**AC 2.** Approval checks use the transaction's declared currency and configured conversion source/date when cross-currency comparison is enabled.

**AC 3.** An actor outside the allowed authority scope cannot approve even when assigned to the task.

**Exception / edge case:** Missing or stale exchange-rate configuration blocks or routes the item according to tenant policy; the engine must not infer a conversion.

**Security and audit implications:** Threshold changes require privileged approval and effective dating; decision inputs and rule version are audited.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Amounts use locale-aware entry/display but threshold evaluation uses decimal numeric values and currency codes.

**Verification method:** Boundary-value tests, conversion configuration tests, and authorization tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0531 OF 1120  |  CORE PLATFORM, MASTER DATA, WORKFLOW, AND REPORTING**

## ERP-PLATFORM-041 — Delegation and absence coverage

**Normative requirement:** The platform shall support time-bounded delegation of eligible workflow tasks with explicit delegation scope and preserved original assignee attribution.

**Rationale:** Delegation maintains workflow continuity without obscuring who held original authority or allowing indefinite privilege transfer.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Delegation is active only within its start/end interval and configured workflow/action scope.

**AC 2.** A delegate can act only if they independently satisfy required permissions and any separation-of-duties rule.

**AC 3.** Audit history records delegate actor, delegator, task, action, and delegation grant ID.

**Exception / edge case:** A delegate who is also the task creator or otherwise conflicted is denied and the task remains pending/escalates.

**Security and audit implications:** Delegation creation and cancellation are audited; no delegation grants tenant-wide permissions.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Delegation notifications use recipient locale and display time bounds in the recipient's time zone.

**Verification method:** Time-bound delegation tests, conflict tests, and audit provenance tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0532 OF 1120  |  CORE PLATFORM, MASTER DATA, WORKFLOW, AND REPORTING**

## ERP-PLATFORM-042 — Workflow escalation policy

**Normative requirement:** The platform shall escalate overdue or blocked workflow work according to a configured policy that defines clock source, working calendar, recipient, and next action.

**Rationale:** Enterprise processes use different calendars and time zones; an undocumented elapsed-time rule can miss service targets.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A test task escalates at the configured threshold using the selected calendar and time zone.

**AC 2.** Escalation event records triggering deadline, policy version, recipient, and resulting action.

**AC 3.** Repeated timer delivery does not create duplicate escalation actions.

**Exception / edge case:** Calendar holidays or missing assignee data pause or reroute escalation according to an explicit fallback, never silently discard it.

**Security and audit implications:** Escalation cannot bypass approval authority; recipients are permission-checked and notification metadata is audited.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Deadline display is localized; calculations use explicit calendar/time-zone configuration and UTC instants.

**Verification method:** Clock-controlled integration tests, DST/calendar tests, and idempotency tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0533 OF 1120  |  CORE PLATFORM, MASTER DATA, WORKFLOW, AND REPORTING**

## ERP-PLATFORM-043 — Workflow deadlines and SLA measurement

**Normative requirement:** The platform shall calculate workflow deadlines and elapsed time using an explicit calendar, pause policy, and status-transition history, and expose the calculation basis.

**Rationale:** SLA semantics depend on business days, holidays, pauses, and local time; opaque elapsed counters are not auditable.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** For a defined fixture, the calculated due instant and elapsed duration match the selected working calendar.

**AC 2.** Pause/resume transitions change remaining duration according to the configured pause policy.

**AC 3.** A report includes the policy version and time basis used to calculate each SLA value.

**Exception / edge case:** When no calendar is assigned, the workflow uses a documented tenant default or reports a configuration error.

**Security and audit implications:** SLA data is visible only to authorized users; policy edits and manual deadline overrides are audited.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Durations and dates are formatted by locale, while calculations use unambiguous instants and calendar IDs.

**Verification method:** Deterministic clock tests including pause, holiday, and time-zone boundaries.

**REQUIREMENT 0534 OF 1120  |  CORE PLATFORM, MASTER DATA, WORKFLOW, AND REPORTING**

## ERP-PLATFORM-044 — Return, rejection, and resubmission

**Normative requirement:** The platform shall distinguish rejection, return-for-correction, cancellation, and withdrawal outcomes and require configured reasons for designated outcomes.

**Rationale:** Distinct outcomes carry different downstream meaning and should not collapse into a generic failed state.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Each outcome produces the configured terminal or return state and a stable outcome code.

**AC 2.** A required reason cannot be omitted; resubmission retains a link to the prior version and decision.

**AC 3.** A returned item restarts only the configured approval steps and does not erase prior approvals.

**Exception / edge case:** Sensitive rejection reasons may be visible only to the submitter and designated roles under tenant policy.

**Security and audit implications:** Decision actor, reason, timestamp, and version are audited; unsafe free text is output-encoded and optionally redacted.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Reason templates and status labels are localized; original submitted text is preserved under retention policy.

**Verification method:** Outcome transition tests, reason-required tests, and access-scope tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0535 OF 1120  |  CORE PLATFORM, MASTER DATA, WORKFLOW, AND REPORTING**

## ERP-PLATFORM-045 — Parallel workflow branches

**Normative requirement:** The workflow engine shall support configured parallel branches with explicit join semantics and deterministic handling of branch failure or cancellation.

**Rationale:** Enterprise approval paths may require independent concurrent review and must define whether all, any, or quorum completion is sufficient.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** For each join mode, tests confirm the instance proceeds only when the configured completion condition is satisfied.

**AC 2.** Branch task IDs and outcomes are individually traceable to the parent instance.

**AC 3.** Cancellation of a branch follows declared propagation rules and does not leave an orphan task.

**Exception / edge case:** If a branch remains unresolved after escalation/timeout, the instance follows a configured wait, cancel, or exception path.

**Security and audit implications:** Each branch action is independently permissioned and audited; a branch cannot modify another branch's assignment.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Branch names/descriptions are translatable; join conditions are stable machine configuration.

**Verification method:** Join-mode tests, branch failure tests, and orphan-task consistency checks.

**REQUIREMENT 0536 OF 1120  |  CORE PLATFORM, MASTER DATA, WORKFLOW, AND REPORTING**

## ERP-PLATFORM-046 — Workflow side-effect reliability

**Normative requirement:** Workflow transitions that trigger external notifications or integrations shall commit local state with an outbox record and deliver side effects asynchronously with retry and deduplication.

**Rationale:** A remote service cannot participate in the database transaction; the outbox prevents lost notifications after a committed state change.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A transition commit and its outbox event are atomic in PostgreSQL.

**AC 2.** A simulated dispatcher outage leaves pending events that are delivered after recovery.

**AC 3.** Repeated delivery uses a stable event ID and receiving side-effect handler produces no duplicate business action.

**Exception / edge case:** Permanent downstream failure moves the event to a monitored dead-letter state with replay controls and no rollback of the committed workflow state.

**Security and audit implications:** Outbox payloads are minimized, encrypted in transit, tenant-scoped, and access-controlled; replay actor/reason is audited.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Templates are rendered in recipient locale at delivery time; event schema carries locale preference or locale-neutral content keys.

**Verification method:** Outage/retry/deduplication integration tests and tenant leakage test.

**REQUIREMENT 0537 OF 1120  |  CORE PLATFORM, MASTER DATA, WORKFLOW, AND REPORTING**

## ERP-PLATFORM-047 — Task inbox and actionable work list

**Normative requirement:** The platform shall provide an authorized task inbox showing each user's pending actionable items with status, age/deadline, assignment source, and required next action.

**Rationale:** An inbox is a work queue rather than a generic list; users need clear actionability and current authorization.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Only tasks the current user may view or act on are returned for the selected tenant.

**AC 2.** Counts and rows reconcile to the same query filters and task state at a consistent snapshot.

**AC 3.** Completing or reassigning a task removes or updates it in the next response without requiring a privileged UI path.

**Exception / edge case:** A user may see a read-only delegated or informational task separately from an actionable task when the workflow policy allows it.

**Security and audit implications:** Inbox APIs re-check task-level permission on action; list counts do not leak hidden task volume.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Column labels, deadlines, and status are localized; sort keys and pagination cursors use stable machine values.

**Verification method:** API authorization tests, count/row consistency test, and locale rendering test.

**REQUIREMENT 0538 OF 1120  |  CORE PLATFORM, MASTER DATA, WORKFLOW, AND REPORTING**

## ERP-PLATFORM-048 — Report catalog and ownership

**Normative requirement:** The platform shall maintain a governed report catalog with stable report ID, owner, data scope, parameter schema, version, and sensitivity classification.

**Rationale:** A catalog enables discoverability and responsible ownership while distinguishing approved reporting products from ad hoc queries.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Every executable report has an owner, version, parameter schema, and classification.

**AC 2.** A report cannot be published if required permission and tenant-scope metadata are missing.

**AC 3.** Retirement blocks new executions while preserving references in prior run history.

**Exception / edge case:** Ad hoc/private reports may be supported in a separate namespace and cannot be promoted to shared catalog without review.

**Security and audit implications:** Catalog publication and ownership changes are audited; classification drives export and retention controls.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Report name, descriptions, and parameters support locale-aware labels; report IDs and parameter keys are stable.

**Verification method:** Catalog schema validation, publication negative tests, and permission tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0539 OF 1120  |  CORE PLATFORM, MASTER DATA, WORKFLOW, AND REPORTING**

## ERP-PLATFORM-049 — Tenant-scoped report query execution

**Normative requirement:** Every report query shall apply tenant and authorized organizational scope before aggregation, filtering, or export, with isolation tested against actual runtime credentials.

**Rationale:** A report can leak data through aggregates even when row-level detail screens are secure.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Cross-tenant fixture data never affects totals or row results for a different tenant.

**AC 2.** Changing tenant ID in a client request without valid membership does not change the execution scope.

**AC 3.** Exports and cached report results include tenant scope in their authorization/cache key.

**Exception / edge case:** Platform-level consolidated reporting is restricted to an explicitly granted cross-tenant operator role and is separately logged.

**Security and audit implications:** RLS and application scope checks are tested together; report query builders deny raw unscoped execution to tenant-facing users.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Localized grouping labels do not affect tenant predicates or aggregation inputs.

**Verification method:** Adversarial report tests with sentinel records, database-role inspection, and cache-key tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0540 OF 1120  |  CORE PLATFORM, MASTER DATA, WORKFLOW, AND REPORTING**

## ERP-PLATFORM-050 — Report row and field authorization

**Normative requirement:** The reporting service shall enforce user permissions for report execution and sensitive columns, not merely hide unauthorized fields in the frontend.

**Rationale:** Reports and exports often aggregate sensitive business and personal data beyond ordinary module screens.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A user lacking report permission receives a denial from the API even when calling it directly.

**AC 2.** A user lacking a sensitive-field permission receives neither that field nor derived output classified equivalently.

**AC 3.** Role changes invalidate or re-evaluate cached report authorization before reuse.

**Exception / edge case:** Where a report supports both masked and unmasked variants, the selected variant is visible and recorded in run metadata.

**Security and audit implications:** Sensitive field access and export are auditable; unauthorized values are excluded server-side, not client-masked only.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Column headings and masking indicators are translated while field classification metadata is language-neutral.

**Verification method:** Direct API tests, sensitive-field negative tests, and cache invalidation test.

**REQUIREMENT 0541 OF 1120  |  CORE PLATFORM, MASTER DATA, WORKFLOW, AND REPORTING**

## ERP-PLATFORM-051 — Parameterized and bounded report queries

**Normative requirement:** The reporting service shall accept typed, allow-listed report parameters and enforce configurable execution bounds for row count, time range, and query duration.

**Rationale:** Typed parameters reduce injection risk and bound operational impact from broad analytical queries.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Unknown parameter names and type-invalid values are rejected before database execution.

**AC 2.** Maximum date span, result size, and execution time are enforced with a stable limit-exceeded response.

**AC 3.** Parameter values are passed as database parameters and not concatenated into SQL text.

**Exception / edge case:** Authorized administrators may raise limits within a documented ceiling; the change is audited and does not bypass tenant scope.

**Security and audit implications:** Report parameters are allow-listed and logged in redacted form; cancellation does not reveal SQL or data values.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Date and number inputs parse according to declared locale, then normalize to typed machine values; ambiguous dates are rejected.

**Verification method:** Injection tests, boundary-value tests, query-plan timeout tests, and code review.

**REQUIREMENT 0542 OF 1120  |  CORE PLATFORM, MASTER DATA, WORKFLOW, AND REPORTING**

## ERP-PLATFORM-052 — As-of and snapshot reporting

**Normative requirement:** Reports that claim historical or point-in-time results shall declare their time basis and use effective-dated/business-event data or a documented snapshot mechanism.

**Rationale:** Current master values and current workflow state cannot reliably reconstruct historical reports after data changes.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Every historical report identifies its as-of timestamp/date, time zone, and applicable data/version basis.

**AC 2.** A fixture changed after the selected as-of date returns the prior valid value or prior snapshot result.

**AC 3.** Repeated execution over an immutable snapshot produces identical rows and totals.

**Exception / edge case:** If the source data does not preserve history, the report must be labeled current-state and cannot claim point-in-time accuracy.

**Security and audit implications:** Snapshot creation and access follow tenant retention and authorization policies; report metadata records source dataset version.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Date input and rendering use locale conventions, while the basis stored in metadata is ISO-formatted.

**Verification method:** Historical fixture tests, deterministic rerun tests, and metadata verification.

**REQUIREMENT 0543 OF 1120  |  CORE PLATFORM, MASTER DATA, WORKFLOW, AND REPORTING**

## ERP-PLATFORM-053 — Report export safety and fidelity

**Normative requirement:** The platform shall support approved export formats with explicit locale/encoding, stable column identity, data classification, and server-side reauthorization at export time.

**Rationale:** Downloaded files are easily detached from application controls and may be consumed by spreadsheet software with locale-specific parsing behavior.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Export applies the same row/field permissions and filters as the on-screen report.

**AC 2.** CSV output declares or consistently uses UTF-8 and a documented delimiter/quoting policy; spreadsheet-formula-leading values are safely encoded.

**AC 3.** Export metadata records report version, tenant, actor, locale, time, and filter fingerprint.

**Exception / edge case:** Very large exports are delivered as expiring authenticated downloads or asynchronous jobs rather than unbounded synchronous responses.

**Security and audit implications:** Exports are audited, access-controlled, time-limited, and optionally watermarked; formula injection protections are tested.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Number/date formatting and translations are explicit export options; raw machine export remains available where permitted.

**Verification method:** Export parity tests, Unicode round-trip, formula-injection test, and authorization test.

**REQUIREMENT 0544 OF 1120  |  CORE PLATFORM, MASTER DATA, WORKFLOW, AND REPORTING**

## ERP-PLATFORM-054 — Asynchronous report execution

**Normative requirement:** Reports exceeding configured synchronous limits shall execute asynchronously with durable status, progress, cancellation, expiry, and tenant-scoped result access.

**Rationale:** Long-running queries should not exhaust web request workers or produce untracked files.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A qualifying request returns a job ID and status within the API response budget.

**AC 2.** Job states progress through queued/running/succeeded/failed/cancelled/expired with timestamps and error codes.

**AC 3.** Only the requesting principal or an explicitly authorized delegate in the same tenant can download the result.

**Exception / edge case:** A worker crash requeues only jobs safe to retry and uses idempotency to prevent duplicate result publication.

**Security and audit implications:** Job payloads and artifacts are tenant-scoped, encrypted at rest, and deleted at configured expiry; status access is audited.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Progress and failure text is localized on display; job IDs, state codes, and timestamps are machine-readable.

**Verification method:** Worker crash/retry tests, expiry tests, and cross-tenant download tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0545 OF 1120  |  CORE PLATFORM, MASTER DATA, WORKFLOW, AND REPORTING**

## ERP-PLATFORM-055 — Scheduled report delivery

**Normative requirement:** The platform shall allow authorized users to schedule report runs using an explicit time zone, recurrence rule, recipient authorization, and delivery channel policy.

**Rationale:** Recurring reporting is useful but can disclose data if recipients, membership, or local-time interpretation change.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A schedule stores recurrence, zone ID, report version, parameters, owner, and next-run instant.

**AC 2.** Before delivery, the system revalidates recipient membership, report permission, and data scope.

**AC 3.** A DST overlap/gap follows a configured run-once, skip, earlier, or later policy and records its resolution.

**Exception / edge case:** If the owner is deactivated or recipient authorization is removed, the schedule pauses and alerts an authorized administrator.

**Security and audit implications:** Schedules cannot send tenant data to unapproved external recipients; every run and delivery outcome is auditable.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Email/report content uses recipient locale; recurrence remains explicit and locale-independent in stored rules.

**Verification method:** Scheduled-run simulation, revoked-recipient test, and DST test.

**REQUIREMENT 0546 OF 1120  |  CORE PLATFORM, MASTER DATA, WORKFLOW, AND REPORTING**

## ERP-PLATFORM-056 — Report lineage and reconciliation metadata

**Normative requirement:** Each report execution shall retain a traceable record of report version, parameters, tenant scope, data-as-of basis, row count, execution status, and correlation ID.

**Rationale:** Lineage lets users explain and reconcile numbers without storing unrestricted copies of all underlying data.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Successful and failed runs generate metadata records with required fields and actor identity.

**AC 2.** A total in a report can be traced to the report definition and data basis used for the run.

**AC 3.** Metadata retention follows configured policy and does not store raw sensitive parameter values unless specifically classified.

**Exception / edge case:** For high-volume ad hoc previews, detailed run retention may be shorter than approved scheduled-report retention, subject to policy.

**Security and audit implications:** Only authorized users can inspect run details; correlation IDs are non-secret and audit events are append-only.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Descriptions are localized; timestamps and numeric counters are stable machine fields.

**Verification method:** Run metadata contract tests, reconciliation drill, and field redaction check.

**REQUIREMENT 0547 OF 1120  |  CORE PLATFORM, MASTER DATA, WORKFLOW, AND REPORTING**

## ERP-PLATFORM-057 — User locale and language preferences

**Normative requirement:** The platform shall store separate user interface language, formatting locale, time zone, and optional content language preferences, with tenant-supported allow-lists and deterministic defaults.

**Rationale:** Language, numeric formatting, time zone, and content translation are distinct preferences and should not be inferred from one setting.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A user's preference can be changed and is applied to the next authenticated UI/API presentation response.

**AC 2.** Unsupported preferences are rejected or mapped through the documented fallback without changing tenant configuration.

**AC 3.** Tenant default is used only when a user has no explicit preference.

**Exception / edge case:** A user who selects a language unavailable for a module receives the fallback and a visible indication rather than a blank label.

**Security and audit implications:** Preferences are private profile data; updates are authenticated and audited without logging unrelated profile values.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Language tags are BCP 47; language matching/fallback is deterministic and preserves script/region when relevant.

**Verification method:** Preference API tests, fallback tests, and user profile isolation tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0548 OF 1120  |  CORE PLATFORM, MASTER DATA, WORKFLOW, AND REPORTING**

## ERP-PLATFORM-058 — Locale-aware formatting and parsing

**Normative requirement:** The frontend and API presentation layer shall format dates, numbers, percentages, and currencies using the selected locale while keeping canonical values typed and locale-neutral in storage and transport.

**Rationale:** A formatted amount or date is not a safe interchange representation and differs across locales.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** The same stored decimal and instant render with expected locale-specific separators and ordering for configured locale fixtures.

**AC 2.** Machine APIs accept documented typed formats and reject ambiguous locale-dependent numeric/date strings.

**AC 3.** Changing display locale does not alter stored numeric values, transaction dates, or calculations.

**Exception / edge case:** A tenant-specific legal format or fiscal notation is an explicit presentation profile and cannot silently redefine canonical arithmetic.

**Security and audit implications:** Parsing errors do not log sensitive values; server-side authorization and calculations never rely on client-formatted strings.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** CLDR/approved locale data is used; currency code is displayed where symbols are ambiguous; RTL output is supported.

**Verification method:** Locale matrix tests for en-US, de-DE, ar locale, decimal boundary and API parsing.

**REQUIREMENT 0549 OF 1120  |  CORE PLATFORM, MASTER DATA, WORKFLOW, AND REPORTING**

## ERP-PLATFORM-059 — Unicode text preservation and normalization

**Normative requirement:** Text storage and APIs shall preserve Unicode content without lossy transliteration and shall apply a documented normalization policy only to designated comparison/search keys.

**Rationale:** Names and descriptions may contain multiple scripts, combining marks, and visually similar but distinct characters.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Create/read round trips preserve representative combining-character and non-Latin fixtures.

**AC 2.** Search normalization is isolated from canonical display value and is versioned/tested.

**AC 3.** Inputs exceeding configured code-point/byte limits are rejected with a field-specific validation code.

**Exception / edge case:** Security-sensitive identifiers may restrict script combinations under a tenant policy, but original submitted value and reason for rejection are handled safely.

**Security and audit implications:** Output is contextually encoded to prevent injection; logs and audit views avoid rendering untrusted markup.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Forms support Unicode scripts, IME input, and bidirectional text while preserving original content.

**Verification method:** Unicode round-trip, normalization collision, length-boundary, and output-encoding tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0550 OF 1120  |  CORE PLATFORM, MASTER DATA, WORKFLOW, AND REPORTING**

## ERP-PLATFORM-060 — Translation catalog lifecycle and fallback

**Normative requirement:** The platform shall manage UI translation catalogs with stable message keys, locale-specific translations, completeness status, and an explicit fallback chain.

**Rationale:** Keeping translation keys separate from translated strings permits continuous localization without changing business logic.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A missing translation resolves through a deterministic configured fallback and is observable as missing in localization QA.

**AC 2.** A catalog build rejects duplicate keys, invalid placeholders, and mismatched plural variables.

**AC 3.** Changing UI language updates text without changing persisted business codes or workflow state.

**Exception / edge case:** Critical legal or user-facing content may be configured to block publication when its required locale translation is missing.

**Security and audit implications:** Catalog publishing is restricted and versioned; user-controlled translations are sanitized before rendering.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Pluralization, date/number interpolation, and text expansion are tested per locale; no concatenated sentence fragments are required.

**Verification method:** Catalog lint, locale completeness gate, and UI language-switch test.

**REQUIREMENT 0551 OF 1120  |  CORE PLATFORM, MASTER DATA, WORKFLOW, AND REPORTING**

## ERP-PLATFORM-061 — Right-to-left layout support

**Normative requirement:** The frontend shall support bidirectional text and right-to-left layout through semantic direction handling without reversing numeric or identifier data.

**Rationale:** A multilingual enterprise UI must render Arabic/Hebrew content and mixed-direction values legibly.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** An RTL locale sets document direction and mirrors supported navigation/layout patterns.

**AC 2.** Mixed Arabic/Latin names, account-like identifiers, punctuation, and numbers render in the expected order in supported browsers.

**AC 3.** A visual regression suite covers primary navigation, forms, tables, dialogs, and workflow actions in RTL.

**Exception / edge case:** Specialized third-party widgets that cannot support RTL are excluded or wrapped with a documented accessible alternative.

**Security and audit implications:** Text direction cannot alter authorization decisions or identifiers; avoid embedding sensitive values in direction-control markup.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Language-specific direction is selected by locale metadata; original input remains unchanged.

**Verification method:** RTL visual regression, browser matrix test, and bidirectional string fixtures.

**REQUIREMENT 0552 OF 1120  |  CORE PLATFORM, MASTER DATA, WORKFLOW, AND REPORTING**

## ERP-PLATFORM-062 — Accessible interface baseline

**Normative requirement:** The frontend shall conform to WCAG 2.2 Level AA for complete platform pages and workflows, subject to a documented testing and remediation process.

**Rationale:** ERP work often relies on dense forms and tables; accessible operation enables keyboard and assistive-technology users to complete the same work.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Automated accessibility checks run on representative pages and produce no unresolved critical violations.

**AC 2.** Manual keyboard and screen-reader testing covers login, search, record editing, approval, and report export journeys.

**AC 3.** Accessibility regressions block release or have an approved, time-bounded exception with a conforming alternative where required.

**Exception / edge case:** Complex charts or data grids may require an accessible tabular or downloadable equivalent, but core data/actions must remain available.

**Security and audit implications:** Accessibility test artifacts may include user interaction evidence but must not retain personal data or credentials.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Page and content language are programmatically identified; translated labels and error text are accessible names, not placeholder-only captions.

**Verification method:** WCAG 2.2 AA conformance test plan, automated scans, manual keyboard/screen-reader test.

**REQUIREMENT 0553 OF 1120  |  CORE PLATFORM, MASTER DATA, WORKFLOW, AND REPORTING**

## ERP-PLATFORM-063 — Keyboard operation and focus management

**Normative requirement:** All primary platform actions and workflow state changes shall be operable by keyboard with visible focus, logical focus order, and no keyboard trap.

**Rationale:** ERP navigation and approval actions must not depend on pointer-only interaction.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A tester completes create, edit, approve, reject, filter, and export workflows using keyboard only.

**AC 2.** Focus remains visible and moves to the relevant status or error region after dialog close or validation failure.

**AC 3.** No modal or custom widget prevents escape or provides no documented keyboard exit.

**Exception / edge case:** A specialized canvas visualization may use an alternate accessible data view with equivalent operations.

**Security and audit implications:** Focus indicators must not expose hidden sensitive controls; keyboard shortcuts that perform destructive actions require discoverable confirmation.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Keyboard instructions and shortcut conflicts are localized and adapt to locale-specific key labels.

**Verification method:** Manual keyboard test and automated focus-order assertions.

**REQUIREMENT 0554 OF 1120  |  CORE PLATFORM, MASTER DATA, WORKFLOW, AND REPORTING**

## ERP-PLATFORM-064 — Accessible tables, filters, and validation

**Normative requirement:** Data tables, filters, and forms shall expose semantic headers, labels, status messages, and field-level error associations to assistive technology.

**Rationale:** Core ERP work involves dense tabular data and complex validation; users need relationships and feedback announced programmatically.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Screen readers can identify each data cell's header and each form control's accessible name.

**AC 2.** Validation errors identify the field and are announced without moving focus unpredictably.

**AC 3.** Async save, report progress, and workflow status messages are programmatically exposed.

**Exception / edge case:** A virtualized grid must preserve semantic row/column context for visible data and provide an accessible non-virtualized alternative where necessary.

**Security and audit implications:** Accessible names do not include hidden confidential values; row actions enforce server-side authorization.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Headers, errors, number/date formats, and status announcements are localized and translated accurately.

**Verification method:** Automated accessibility checks plus manual screen-reader tests on grid/form/status cases.

**REQUIREMENT 0555 OF 1120  |  CORE PLATFORM, MASTER DATA, WORKFLOW, AND REPORTING**

## ERP-PLATFORM-065 — Append-only security and business audit events

**Normative requirement:** The platform shall emit append-only audit events for authentication, authorization-sensitive administration, master-data changes, workflow decisions, exports, and privileged access.

**Rationale:** A verifiable event trail supports investigation and governance across domains without relying on mutable application debug logs.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Required event types contain event ID, tenant, actor/system, action, target ID, UTC timestamp, outcome, and correlation ID.

**AC 2.** Application roles cannot update or delete stored audit events through normal APIs or database permissions.

**AC 3.** Tests confirm a denied privileged action and an approved action each create the expected audit record.

**Exception / edge case:** High-volume read events may be sampled or omitted only when policy permits and the audit coverage boundary is documented.

**Security and audit implications:** Audit storage uses restricted write/read roles, integrity monitoring, and secret/PII minimization; no passwords or bearer tokens are recorded.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Event schema is language-neutral; localized event descriptions are presentation-layer transformations of stable codes.

**Verification method:** Event schema tests, role/permission inspection, and tamper/alteration attempt test.

**REQUIREMENT 0556 OF 1120  |  CORE PLATFORM, MASTER DATA, WORKFLOW, AND REPORTING**

## ERP-PLATFORM-066 — Configurable retention and legal hold boundary

**Normative requirement:** The platform shall provide configurable retention policies and legal-hold flags by data category and jurisdiction, with deletion/anonymization jobs that produce completion evidence.

**Rationale:** Retention requirements vary by law, contract, industry, and data category; no universal duration can be assumed.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** An administrator can configure a policy with category, scope, duration/trigger, disposition, and effective date.

**AC 2.** A held record is excluded from automated deletion until hold release by an authorized role.

**AC 3.** A completed disposition job records rule version, affected counts, timestamps, and failures without retaining deleted content.

**Exception / edge case:** Conflicting retention and deletion instructions pause disposition and require legal/compliance configuration review.

**Security and audit implications:** Retention rules and hold actions are privileged and audited; erasure is bounded by backups and downstream copies documented in policy.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Policy labels and notices are localized; retention periods are stored as typed units and dates, not locale-formatted strings.

**Verification method:** Policy simulation, hold exclusion, disposition dry-run, and evidence review.

**REQUIREMENT 0557 OF 1120  |  CORE PLATFORM, MASTER DATA, WORKFLOW, AND REPORTING**

## ERP-PLATFORM-067 — Audit search and access segregation

**Normative requirement:** The platform shall expose audit search to authorized investigators with tenant, time, actor, action, and target filters while separating audit administration from event alteration.

**Rationale:** Investigators need efficient search but should not be able to edit or erase the evidence they inspect.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A role granted audit-read can search permitted tenant records but cannot mutate or purge events.

**AC 2.** Search results honor tenant scope and redact fields according to classification.

**AC 3.** Queries with unsupported filters reject explicitly and paginated searches return stable cursor semantics.

**Exception / edge case:** Cross-tenant incident review requires a separately granted case-specific scope and reason code.

**Security and audit implications:** Every audit query of sensitive event categories is itself logged; read and retention administrator roles are distinct.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Search filters and event descriptions are localized while indexed event attributes remain canonical.

**Verification method:** Role separation tests, cross-tenant query tests, and investigator workflow audit.

**REQUIREMENT 0558 OF 1120  |  CORE PLATFORM, MASTER DATA, WORKFLOW, AND REPORTING**

## ERP-PLATFORM-068 — Privacy-aware diagnostics and redaction

**Normative requirement:** Platform logs, traces, and error responses shall exclude credentials and minimize or redact personal and tenant business data according to a configurable classification policy.

**Rationale:** Observability is essential but diagnostic data can become a secondary store of sensitive information.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Automated tests submit seeded secret/PII values and verify they do not appear in application logs or unprivileged error payloads.

**AC 2.** Every request log includes correlation ID, operation code, outcome, and timing without raw request body by default.

**AC 3.** A privileged diagnostic exception has actor, reason, scope, and expiry recorded.

**Exception / edge case:** Temporary detailed tracing during incident response must be opt-in, time-bounded, and scoped to approved fields/tenants.

**Security and audit implications:** Log access follows least privilege, retention is configured, and deletion/export rules cover log stores where applicable.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Diagnostic summaries are localized only at presentation; canonical log codes and field names are language-neutral.

**Verification method:** Canary-secret log scan, exception response tests, and observability role review.

**REQUIREMENT 0559 OF 1120  |  CORE PLATFORM, MASTER DATA, WORKFLOW, AND REPORTING**

## ERP-PLATFORM-069 — Industry-extension and jurisdiction configuration boundary

**Normative requirement:** The platform shall expose a governed extension/configuration mechanism for industry- and jurisdiction-specific classifications, fields, workflows, validations, and report logic without embedding them as universal core rules.

**Rationale:** Commercial ERP deployments vary; legal obligations and industry semantics must be evidence-based and selected by configuration owners.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** An extension declares owner, version, applicability scope, dependencies, and migration compatibility.

**AC 2.** Enabling/disabling an extension affects only its scoped tenant/entity and cannot rewrite core identifiers.

**AC 3.** A core conformance test suite runs unchanged with no extension and with each supported extension combination.

**Exception / edge case:** Where regulatory interpretation is uncertain or sources conflict, the extension remains disabled pending customer legal/compliance validation.

**Security and audit implications:** Extension publication is signed/reviewed, permissions are scoped, and custom logic cannot bypass tenant authorization or audit emission.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Extension labels, forms, and messages are translatable; jurisdiction codes and version identifiers stay canonical.

**Verification method:** Extension contract tests, scope isolation tests, and configuration review.

**REQUIREMENT 0560 OF 1120  |  CORE PLATFORM, MASTER DATA, WORKFLOW, AND REPORTING**

## ERP-PLATFORM-070 — Module contract registry

**Normative requirement:** The platform shall maintain a registry of module-owned APIs, event schemas, permission codes, master-data dependencies, and compatibility versions as the cross-module integration contract.

**Rationale:** Platform modules should integrate by stable contracts instead of directly coupling to another module's tables or undocumented implementation details.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Every published module contract has owner, version, schema, authorization requirements, and deprecation state.

**AC 2.** CI validates event/API compatibility and fails on unapproved breaking changes.

**AC 3.** A consumer can discover supported contract versions and declared dependency status.

**Exception / edge case:** Emergency removal of a vulnerable contract may precede normal deprecation but requires incident record and consumer notification.

**Security and audit implications:** Registry access is authenticated; contract publication and breaking-change approval are audited; secrets are prohibited in schemas/examples.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Descriptions can be localized, but endpoint names, event types, field keys, and permission codes remain stable.

**Verification method:** Schema registry lint, compatibility CI tests, and consumer integration tests.

# Internationalization, Multilingual UX, and Localization

# Chapter 09 — Internationalization, Multilingual UX, and Localization

## Purpose and scope

This chapter specifies the shared internationalization and localization capability for a commercial, multi-tenant ERP built on ASP.NET Core, PostgreSQL, and a lightweight Next.js frontend. It covers locale context, interface translation, multilingual data, formatting, input, search and sorting, right-to-left presentation, accessible language metadata, localized reports and communications, and release governance. It does not define a universal tax, accounting, labor, address, metrology, privacy, document-language, or statutory-calendar rule. Those rules belong to explicit tenant, jurisdiction, legal-entity, industry-extension, or business-module configuration and must be validated by the responsible domain owner.

**Point-in-time technology baseline.** The Microsoft .NET support page, last updated 2026-11-11, identifies .NET 11 as a supported STS release and .NET 10 as a supported LTS release, both supported until November 2028. Microsoft recommends the latest release for services that can be updated regularly and notes LTS as an option when stability over a longer period is more important \[1]. Accordingly, this chapter targets **.NET 11 / ASP.NET Core 11** as the latest stable supported .NET line on 2026-11-22. The ASP.NET Core 11 release page confirms the .NET 11 release line \[2]. This is a major-version baseline, not a claim about a specific servicing patch: reconfirm the latest supported patch, hosting/runtime support, and exact ASP.NET Core package alignment from official sources at build and production-release time. A deployment choosing .NET 10 LTS is a deliberate support-policy decision, not the latest-release baseline. No specific PostgreSQL or Next.js major version is mandated here; select supported versions at implementation and reconfirm their official release/support status at release.

The design follows BCP 47 language tags \[10], uses UTF-8 storage, and treats locale data as maintained reference data rather than hand-coded assumptions. Unicode CLDR supplies locale-sensitive data and rules for dates, numbers, units, plural categories, and sorting \[15]. ASP.NET Core provides request localization services and configurable culture providers \[3]; the system applies a stable ERP-specific precedence on top. PostgreSQL exposes collation providers and locale-dependent behavior, so database sort semantics are declared and managed rather than assumed to match every user's display locale \[5] \[6]. Next.js supports localized routing and server-side dictionaries through locale route segments \[9]. HTML language and direction are declared separately: W3C guidance recommends lang for the text language and dir for direction, and WCAG 2.2 requires programmatically determinable page language and language of parts \[11] \[12] \[14].

## Actors and permission boundaries

The actors are platform localization administrators, tenant localization administrators, translators, translation reviewers/publishers, tenant business administrators, individual ERP users, workflow approvers, integration clients, support operators, and industry-extension maintainers.
