Platform administrators control platform-owned catalogs and supported runtime capabilities. Tenant localization administrators select tenant-enabled locales, defaults, fallbacks, locale profiles, and tenant glossaries. Translators can draft assigned tenant or platform catalog entries; reviewers approve and publishers activate immutable catalog releases. End users can update their own UI and formatting preferences within tenant policy. Business transaction permissions remain owned by finance, HR, supply chain, CRM, and other modules. Locale permission never implies access to business data. Support access is time-bound, scoped, visible, and audited.

Tenant membership, not a locale route, header, or cookie, determines tenant context. The server validates locale settings against the selected tenant's enabled allowlist. Catalogs, telemetry, preferences, and cache entries are tenant-scoped unless immutable public assets are proven identical. Administrative changes record actor, tenant, previous and new version, timestamp, and reason when policy requires. Sensitive user-entered text is not copied into translation telemetry by default.

## Core entities

The shared model includes TenantLocalePolicy (enabled locale tags, default, fallback chain, policy version), UserLocalePreference (UI language, format locale, time zone, calendar, numbering system), LocaleContext (resolved request/job context), MessageKey and MessageArgumentSchema, TranslationEntry (locale, state, source revision, reviewer), CatalogRelease (immutable release ID/hash), GlossaryTerm, LocaleFormatProfile, CollationProfile, DocumentTemplateLocalePolicy, ImportExportProfile, LocaleAuditEvent, and a localization-quality telemetry event. Locale tag, script direction, formatting culture, time zone, calendar, currency, legal jurisdiction, and legal entity are separate fields. BCP 47 identifies language subtags; it does not establish those other business attributes \[10]. ISO 4217 codes identify currency; they are not inferred from a symbol or user's language \[16].

Store canonical text and business values independently of display strings. Persist multilingual human text in UTF-8; PostgreSQL explicitly warns that SQL_ASCII does not validate non-ASCII data or perform encoding conversion, and documents UTF-8 support \[5]. Store monetary amounts with currency code and the relevant calculation policy. Store date-only values as dates, not instants. Store instants unambiguously and retain a named time zone separately when future civil-time intent matters: PostgreSQL documents that a timestamp with time zone value is normalized to UTC and does not retain the originally stated zone \[7]. Store original user-authored text separately from any normalized/search derivative.

## Core workflows

**Tenant locale setup.** A tenant administrator enables a supported locale, selects the tenant default, declares a fallback chain, configures formatting and direction profiles, and reviews module/extension translation coverage. Changes are versioned, previewed, audited, and isolated from other tenants. Extensions declare namespaced message keys and required locale capabilities before tenant activation.

**User session and language choice.** On sign-in, the API validates tenant membership, resolves UI language from the saved user preference, then tenant default, then product default. Accept-Language can seed a choice for an unset or anonymous flow but cannot overwrite a saved preference. Format locale, time zone, calendar, and numbering system resolve separately. The ASP.NET Core request context is immutable and request-scoped; asynchronous jobs receive serialized context or declare themselves locale-neutral. Next.js validates route locale before loading tenant content. The page declares accurate lang and direction metadata. Next.js's documented pattern supports locale segments and server-side dictionary loading \[9].

**Translation authoring and release.** Stable message keys are exported with module, workflow, placeholder schema, glossary, and source revision context. Translation drafts are validated, reviewed according to role policy, and published as immutable catalog releases. Runtime resolution uses an explicit fallback chain and exposes fallback provenance to authorized diagnostics. Critical or transaction-significant text may prohibit fallback. Missing keys produce minimized structured telemetry. Rollback changes the active catalog pointer, not business data or historical artifact provenance.

**Data entry, search, and rendering.** The UI accepts locale-aware input through declared parsing profiles and rejects ambiguity rather than guessing. The API receives canonical numeric/date values with explicit currency, unit, or time-zone context. Search and sorting use per-field matching policies and named collation/analyzer profiles; tenant and record authorization filters apply before results are returned. PostgreSQL collation behavior is provider- and version-dependent, can be specified per column or expression, and has explicit deterministic/nondeterministic tradeoffs \[6]. A runtime or collation upgrade therefore runs golden behavior tests and an approved index remediation plan.

**Documents, reporting, and notifications.** Each output chooses a recipient, document, entity, or configured statutory language/format policy and records the resulting catalog/template release. Human-readable reports localize captions while preserving canonical values and stable machine fields. Notifications use recipient preference or declared business rule, not country as a language proxy. Jurisdiction/industry extensions govern legal text, tax/calendar behavior, currency rounding, address validation, statutory output language, and required bilingual content. The core system provides typed hooks and enforces policy execution but does not claim universal legal sufficiency.

## Major design decisions

**1.** Use BCP 47 tags for language identifiers and validate them against maintained registries; canonicalize representation without treating tag case as meaningful \[10].

**2.** Model UI language separately from format locale, time zone, calendar, numbering system, currency, script direction, jurisdiction, and entity. Resolution precedence is explicit and testable.

**3.** Use UTF-8 end-to-end for human text. Preserve source text; any normalization, transliteration, tokenization, or accent-insensitive search is a field-level derivative/policy \[5].

**4.** Use maintained CLDR-backed runtime libraries for locale-sensitive formatting and grammatical rules, with pinned runtime/data baselines and upgrade tests \[4] \[15]. Never hand-code universal date, decimal, plural, or unit rules.

**5.** Keep presentation strings out of storage, calculations, API identity, and authorization logic. Use stable codes and typed placeholders.

**6.** Make locale configuration tenant-aware and versioned. Cache by tenant and only those locale dimensions that affect the cached representation.

**7.** Implement RTL with structural HTML direction attributes, semantic inline isolation, and CSS logical properties. Do not simulate direction by reversing strings or merely aligning text right \[12] \[13].

**8.** Release translation catalogs immutably, with role-separated draft/review/publish controls, release provenance, rollback, and configurable critical-text gates.

**9.** Keep the frontend lightweight: use Next.js App Router locale routing and server-side resources where practical; avoid loading every locale bundle to the client \[9].

## Dependencies and cross-module contracts

Identity supplies tenant membership and the authenticated principal before locale preference resolution. Authorization is evaluated independently of locale. The shared localization service supplies message keys, locale resolution, number/date/unit formatting, language/direction metadata, and catalog provenance. Domain modules supply canonical values and stable codes, declare message namespaces and field formatting policy, and own jurisdictional decisions. Finance owns currency calculation/rounding policy and statutory monetary outputs; HR owns employment-language and calendar configuration; supply chain owns item units and localized item descriptions; CRM owns contact language preferences; document management owns template retention and approved versions. Reporting and workflow services carry locale context explicitly or mark a payload locale-neutral. APIs expose stable machine codes and canonical values; localized messages are presentation aids. Import/export connectors declare encoding, delimiter, date/decimal policy, and schema version.

Any event that contains rendered human text carries a locale-context reference and catalog/template release or declares itself machine-only. Cross-module requests never infer tenant identity from a locale. Every consuming module rechecks access using its own policy. All shared schemas are versioned; locale context must not make stable domain identifiers or business amounts locale-dependent.

## Risks and controls

The primary risks are transaction errors from ambiguous numeric/date input; cross-tenant cache leakage; stale or unsupported locale data; incorrect collation ordering after provider upgrades; incomplete or misleading critical translations; RTL punctuation/identifier confusion; personal data leakage in diagnostics; unreviewed jurisdiction-specific assumptions; and inaccessible long-string or screen-reader behavior. Controls include canonical-value APIs, tenant-scoped cache keys, allowlisted locale registries, golden test corpora, provider/version reporting, atomic catalog releases, immutable document provenance, minimization and retention of telemetry, explicit extension boundaries, bilingual/locale-specific workflow review, keyboard and screen-reader tests, and documented rollback. PostgreSQL's locale provider and collation version behavior requires deployment-level controls \[6] \[8]; .NET globalization can vary with ICU and CLDR updates, so the runtime/data baseline is tested \[4] \[15].

## Internationalization, Multilingual UX, and Localization — requirement cards

**REQUIREMENT 0561 OF 1120  |  INTERNATIONALIZATION, MULTILINGUAL UX, AND LOCALIZATION**

## ERP-I18N-001 — Canonical locale identifiers

**Normative requirement:** The platform shall store and exchange language identifiers as validated BCP 47 language tags, preserving recognized language, script, and region subtags and canonicalizing case without treating case as semantically significant.

**Rationale:** A single interoperable tag format avoids ad hoc language/region codes and supports language matching across browser, API, and database boundaries.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Creating a preference with a well-formed tag such as \`zh-Hant-TW` round-trips with all subtags intact.

**AC 2.** A malformed tag is rejected with a field-level validation error and is not saved.

**AC 3.** Tags differing only by subtag letter case resolve to the same supported-locale key.

**Exception / edge case:** A syntactically valid but unsupported private-use or grandfathered tag may be retained as an imported value only when explicitly marked unsupported; it must not silently become a different supported locale.

**Security and audit implications:** Tenant locale administrators may configure only enabled locales; locale tags are configuration data and never grant authorization. Record actor, tenant, prior value, and new value for changes.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Keep language tag separate from formatting locale, script direction, legal jurisdiction, and currency. BCP 47 tags identify language, not all regional business rules.

**Verification method:** Unit-test tag validation/canonicalization against the IANA registry fixtures; API integration-test rejection and round-trip behavior; audit writes to tenant locale policy.

**REQUIREMENT 0562 OF 1120  |  INTERNATIONALIZATION, MULTILINGUAL UX, AND LOCALIZATION**

## ERP-I18N-002 — Tenant-supported locale registry

**Normative requirement:** Each tenant shall have a versioned allowlist of UI and document locales, a default UI locale, and an explicit fallback chain for each enabled locale.

**Rationale:** Tenant-controlled locale availability makes rollout governable and allows language coverage to differ without imposing one global language set.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A tenant administrator can enable and disable a locale without changing another tenant's configuration.

**AC 2.** Every enabled locale resolves to exactly one tenant default and a finite ordered fallback chain.

**AC 3.** Disabling a locale referenced by an active user preference produces a migration preview and does not silently delete the preference.

**Exception / edge case:** The platform's system-administration UI must remain operable in a platform default locale even if a tenant disables all tenant locales.

**Security and audit implications:** Enforce tenant scope on reads/writes and restrict registry changes to tenant localization administrators; log before/after configuration and affected preference count.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Locale allowlists are tenant specific; extensions can declare required locale resources but cannot enable a tenant locale by themselves.

**Verification method:** Integration-test tenant isolation and fallback resolution; test configuration migration preview; audit locale registry version changes.

**REQUIREMENT 0563 OF 1120  |  INTERNATIONALIZATION, MULTILINGUAL UX, AND LOCALIZATION**

## ERP-I18N-003 — Separate language and formatting preferences

**Normative requirement:** The system shall model each user's UI language, formatting locale, time zone, calendar preference, and numbering-system preference as separate settings with defined inheritance and validation.

**Rationale:** Users may need one interface language with another region's date, number, or time conventions; conflating these creates errors in financial and operational work.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A user can select English UI language with a different supported formatting locale and time zone.

**AC 2.** The server resolves each unset user field from tenant defaults and then product defaults in a documented order.

**AC 3.** An unsupported calendar or numbering-system preference is rejected or resolved through an explicit fallback, never ignored silently.

**Exception / edge case:** A workflow requiring a legally configured calendar or entity time zone may override a user display preference for its calculation while leaving the user preference unchanged.

**Security and audit implications:** User may modify personal display settings, but only authorized administrators may change tenant defaults. Avoid logging sensitive profile data beyond preference-change metadata.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Display settings do not change stored monetary values, posted dates, entity domicile, statutory calendar rules, or business-effective dates.

**Verification method:** Test preference precedence in API and UI; test calculation contexts with contrasting user and entity zones; audit user and tenant preference changes.

**REQUIREMENT 0564 OF 1120  |  INTERNATIONALIZATION, MULTILINGUAL UX, AND LOCALIZATION**

## ERP-I18N-004 — Locale resolution precedence

**Normative requirement:** For authenticated ERP requests, the service shall resolve UI language using the explicit user preference first, then the tenant default, then the configured product default; \`Accept-Language` may seed an unset preference only through an explicit user-visible choice.

**Rationale:** Browser headers are hints and may not represent a user's chosen language; stable precedence prevents unexpected screen changes and improves reproducibility.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** With all preferences configured, the resolved UI language equals the stored user choice regardless of the request header.

**AC 2.** For a user with no preference, the resolved value equals the tenant default.

**AC 3.** An \`Accept-Language` value alone never overwrites a saved preference.

**Exception / edge case:** Anonymous sign-in, password-reset, or invitation flows may use weighted \`Accept-Language` matching from the supported allowlist, but offer a visible language switch and use a safe default when no match exists.

**Security and audit implications:** Do not trust headers as identity or tenant selectors. Restrict preference mutation to the authenticated user or authorized admin; audit administrative overrides.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Locale negotiation must be allowlist-bound and distinct from formatting/transaction settings; expose deterministic resolution diagnostics without disclosing another tenant's settings.

**Verification method:** Integration-test precedence with conflicting cookie, header, route, and stored values; verify no cross-tenant preference lookup; inspect audit events for preference updates.

**REQUIREMENT 0565 OF 1120  |  INTERNATIONALIZATION, MULTILINGUAL UX, AND LOCALIZATION**

## ERP-I18N-005 — Persistent user language selection

**Normative requirement:** The user interface shall provide a discoverable language selector that persists the authenticated user's UI-language choice to the user's profile and immediately applies it to subsequent navigation.

**Rationale:** A visible, durable control corrects unreliable browser inference and avoids forcing users to repeat a selection.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Changing language saves the profile preference and refreshes navigation, labels, validation text, and page metadata on the next rendered response.

**AC 2.** The selector displays localized language names and marks the current selection programmatically.

**AC 3.** The selector contains only locales enabled for the current tenant.

**Exception / edge case:** If a user's selected locale is later disabled by tenant policy, the next session falls back using the declared chain and presents a non-blocking explanation with available choices.

**Security and audit implications:** Require authentication to save preferences; prevent profile updates across user/tenant IDs; log change metadata but not unrelated profile fields.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Language names should be self-named where available; selector labels and announcements must be translated, keyboard accessible, and usable in RTL layouts.

**Verification method:** End-to-end test persistence across sign-out/sign-in and tenant switch; verify disabled locales are not selectable; audit profile update actor/time.

**REQUIREMENT 0566 OF 1120  |  INTERNATIONALIZATION, MULTILINGUAL UX, AND LOCALIZATION**

## ERP-I18N-006 — Tenant-switch context isolation

**Normative requirement:** On every tenant switch, the system shall reload the target tenant's locale allowlist, default settings, and user membership-specific preference without carrying the prior tenant's effective context into the new tenant.

**Rationale:** Multi-tenant users may have different permitted languages and defaults in each organization; stale context can cause leakage and confusing behavior.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A user switching between two tenants receives each tenant's own enabled-locale set and resolved default.

**AC 2.** A locale enabled in tenant A but disabled in tenant B is not exposed in tenant B's selector or APIs.

**AC 3.** Cached responses vary by tenant and user locale context or are not shared across those contexts.

**Exception / edge case:** A platform operator explicitly acting under audited support impersonation uses the target tenant's context while retaining a visible support-session indicator.

**Security and audit implications:** Tenant ID must be derived from authenticated membership, not locale-prefixed routes or client-supplied headers. Audit tenant switches and privileged impersonation.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Tenant-specific locale settings must never be inferred from a prior tenant's cookies or cached server context.

**Verification method:** Run cross-tenant isolation tests with shared user identity and deliberately colliding IDs; inspect cache keys and request-context middleware; audit support impersonation.

**REQUIREMENT 0567 OF 1120  |  INTERNATIONALIZATION, MULTILINGUAL UX, AND LOCALIZATION**

## ERP-I18N-007 — Request-scoped culture context

**Normative requirement:** ASP.NET Core shall establish a validated, immutable request-scoped localization context before endpoint formatting or validation, and downstream services shall receive it explicitly rather than mutating process-wide culture state.

**Rationale:** Request-scoped resolution prevents concurrent users in different locales from affecting one another and makes asynchronous operations deterministic.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Parallel requests with distinct cultures produce correct independent formatted values and validation messages.

**AC 2.** A request with an unsupported locale resolves through the configured fallback without changing global process culture.

**AC 3.** Background jobs receive an explicit locale context instead of relying on ambient HTTP request state.

**Exception / edge case:** A system-wide background maintenance job may use invariant formatting if it performs no user-facing rendering; its logs must still include unambiguous machine-readable values.

**Security and audit implications:** Validate locale and tenant before constructing context; isolate tenant and user context in scoped services; audit privileged culture overrides.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Keep UI resources and format culture separately addressable; include the resolved context in diagnostics while minimizing personal data.

**Verification method:** Concurrency integration test with parallel cultures; static analysis or code review verifies no mutable global culture assignment; test job serialization of locale context.

**REQUIREMENT 0568 OF 1120  |  INTERNATIONALIZATION, MULTILINGUAL UX, AND LOCALIZATION**

## ERP-I18N-008 — Locale-aware route handling

**Normative requirement:** The Next.js frontend shall route localized pages through a validated locale segment or an explicitly configured locale domain and shall reject unsupported locale segments before loading tenant data.

**Rationale:** Explicit locale routes support shareable navigation and predictable rendering while preventing arbitrary input from selecting unapproved resources.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Every localized route resolves its locale from the supported registry before server-side data fetch.

**AC 2.** A valid locale route renders the matching translation bundle and correct HTML \`lang` attribute.

**AC 3.** An unsupported route locale returns a controlled not-found or canonical redirect response without fetching tenant records.

**Exception / edge case:** API, webhook, health, and static asset paths that are not localized must remain routable without a locale segment.

**Security and audit implications:** Treat route locale as presentation input only, never as a tenant identity or authorization claim; prevent open redirects during canonical routing.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Use Next.js App Router locale routing and server-side dictionaries as applicable; exclude service endpoints and static assets from locale rewriting.

**Verification method:** Test supported and unsupported route cases, including encoded path attacks; inspect generated server/client route requests for tenant scoping.

**REQUIREMENT 0569 OF 1120  |  INTERNATIONALIZATION, MULTILINGUAL UX, AND LOCALIZATION**

## ERP-I18N-009 — Locale switch preserves task context

**Normative requirement:** The UI language switch shall preserve the current authorized route and safe query state where a corresponding localized route exists, otherwise it shall navigate to the nearest localized parent route and disclose the fallback.

**Rationale:** For ERP tasks, a language switch should not discard unsaved work or send users to an unrelated landing page.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** On a route with a locale-equivalent route, selecting a new language retains the entity/task route and non-sensitive filter state.

**AC 2.** On a route without a localized counterpart, the switch navigates to the configured parent and shows a localized notice.

**AC 3.** The switch never preserves credentials, anti-forgery values, or unapproved sensitive query parameters.

**Exception / edge case:** If a form contains unsaved edits, the switch first invokes the standard unsaved-change confirmation and preserves state only after confirmation.

**Security and audit implications:** Route continuity is subordinate to authorization; re-authorize every destination and strip secrets from query strings and navigation logs.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Localized route maps are content metadata and must not use translated labels as entity keys.

**Verification method:** Browser E2E tests for matching and missing route mappings; test query allowlisting and unsaved form flow; security review of route mapping.

**REQUIREMENT 0570 OF 1120  |  INTERNATIONALIZATION, MULTILINGUAL UX, AND LOCALIZATION**

## ERP-I18N-010 — Language negotiation safety

**Normative requirement:** Unauthenticated locale negotiation shall parse weighted language preferences according to HTTP language matching semantics, match only against the configured public locale allowlist, and use a deterministic fallback.

**Rationale:** Correct matching handles preference weights and partial language ranges without trusting arbitrary user input as a filesystem or resource key.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A test header with multiple ranges and quality weights selects the highest-ranked supported match.

**AC 2.** Malformed, oversized, duplicate, or unsupported ranges cannot produce an exception or arbitrary locale lookup.

**AC 3.** When there is no acceptable supported match, the configured public default is returned.

**Exception / edge case:** If all supported languages are explicitly unacceptable, the endpoint may return the default only if product policy allows it; otherwise it returns a language-choice response without leaking protected content.

**Security and audit implications:** Enforce header-size limits and safe matching; do not use locale negotiation to bypass authentication, tenant routing, or consent boundaries.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Do not treat \`Accept-Language` as definitive for signed-in users; provide a manual choice and preserve separate UI and formatting locales.

**Verification method:** Fuzz-test header parser and maximum size; integration-test fallback and allowlist matching; log rejected header diagnostics without storing full headers by default.

**REQUIREMENT 0571 OF 1120  |  INTERNATIONALIZATION, MULTILINGUAL UX, AND LOCALIZATION**

## ERP-I18N-011 — Stable translation message keys

**Normative requirement:** All user-visible system text shall be referenced by stable, namespaced message keys rather than constructed by concatenating translated fragments or using source-language display strings as identifiers.

**Rationale:** Stable keys allow translators to change wording and reorder sentences without changing business logic or losing translation history.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A localization build fails when an invoked key is missing from the source catalog.

**AC 2.** Replacing a message's English wording without changing its key preserves translation linkage and records a source revision.

**AC 3.** Search for dynamic concatenation in designated localization APIs returns no violations in CI.

**Exception / edge case:** User-authored descriptions, product names, and externally supplied names remain data values and are not forced through static message catalogs.

**Security and audit implications:** Translation keys and catalogs are not access-control policy. Restrict catalog write/publish permissions and keep user-provided text out of executable templates.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Support grammatical reordering and ICU-style placeholders; do not make source-language sentence structure a contract.

**Verification method:** CI lints key references and duplicate keys; code review checks catalog revision and deprecation behavior; audit catalog release publication.

**REQUIREMENT 0572 OF 1120  |  INTERNATIONALIZATION, MULTILINGUAL UX, AND LOCALIZATION**

## ERP-I18N-012 — Catalog versioning and fallback

**Normative requirement:** The localization service shall resolve each message through an immutable catalog release using the ordered locale fallback chain, and it shall expose whether the returned text is exact-locale, fallback-locale, or source text.

**Rationale:** Explicit fallback provenance makes incomplete translations visible and allows consistent rollback across application instances.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A requested translation resolves to the first available catalog in the configured chain.

**AC 2.** The response metadata or telemetry identifies the actual catalog locale and release without changing the displayed message.

**AC 3.** A catalog release can be rolled back to a prior immutable release without modifying stored business records.

**AC 4.** A complete catalog release becomes active through one atomic tenant/locale pointer change, so a request never combines message versions; a failed activation leaves the previous release active.

**Exception / edge case:** For legally controlled output templates, fallback may be prohibited and generation must fail closed until an approved translation exists.

**Security and audit implications:** Only translation publishers may activate tenant catalogs; protect internal release metadata from public API leakage where inappropriate.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Fallback is an explicit product policy, not an automatic assumption for contracts, regulatory labels, or safety text.

**Verification method:** Integration-test chain order, rollback, and no-chain behavior; verify immutable release hashes; audit publication/rollback events.

**REQUIREMENT 0573 OF 1120  |  INTERNATIONALIZATION, MULTILINGUAL UX, AND LOCALIZATION**

## ERP-I18N-013 — Translation workflow states

**Normative requirement:** The translation management workflow shall track each message-locale pair through draft, in-review, approved, and published states, with an authorized role required for each transition.

**Rationale:** Separating draft work from published output prevents unreviewed strings from reaching operational users.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A draft is not served to end users through production APIs.

**AC 2.** Publishing requires an approved entry and records source key, locale, catalog release, reviewer, and timestamp.

**AC 3.** A translator cannot approve their own submission when the tenant's separation-of-duties policy is enabled.

**Exception / edge case:** Emergency hotfix publication may bypass ordinary review only through a named break-glass permission, reason capture, and mandatory post-event review.

**Security and audit implications:** Enforce least privilege and separation of duties per tenant; immutable history records edits and approvals without storing credentials or session secrets.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Review must consider locale grammar, placeholders, tone, and domain terminology, not only literal correctness.

**Verification method:** State-machine unit tests and role-matrix authorization tests; audit trail inspection for normal and break-glass transitions.

**REQUIREMENT 0574 OF 1120  |  INTERNATIONALIZATION, MULTILINGUAL UX, AND LOCALIZATION**

## ERP-I18N-014 — Placeholder contracts

**Normative requirement:** Each translatable message shall declare typed named placeholders, and the catalog validator shall require every locale variant to use the same required placeholder names and compatible types.

**Rationale:** Typed placeholders reduce runtime substitution failures, unsafe content coercion, and grammatical mistakes caused by undocumented variables.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A catalog with a missing, extra-required, or type-incompatible placeholder fails validation before publication.

**AC 2.** Runtime formatting substitutes named values and escapes values for the output context.

**AC 3.** Plural and select branches are validated for all required message arguments.

**Exception / edge case:** A locale may reorder placeholders and may omit an optional placeholder only when the message schema marks it optional and tests prove no information loss.

**Security and audit implications:** Untrusted values remain data, are escaped per rendering context, and must not be executable template fragments; catalog editors cannot access underlying business records.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Placeholder order, plural categories, gender/case agreement and sentence-level variants may differ by locale; avoid string concatenation.

**Verification method:** Unit-test catalog compiler and HTML-escaping behavior with hostile placeholder values; security review of rich-text message rendering.

**REQUIREMENT 0575 OF 1120  |  INTERNATIONALIZATION, MULTILINGUAL UX, AND LOCALIZATION**

## ERP-I18N-015 — Plural, ordinal, and select rules

**Normative requirement:** The message formatter shall use locale data rules for plural categories and declared select branches rather than English-only singular/plural conditionals.

**Rationale:** Languages vary in the number and selection of grammatical quantity categories, so English-centric conditions yield incorrect instructions and labels.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** For each shipped locale, test vectors exercise every plural category used by the message catalog.

**AC 2.** A count of zero follows the configured locale rule or explicit zero branch.

**AC 3.** Missing select values resolve to a declared \`other` or safe fallback branch.

**Exception / edge case:** A message that describes a domain-specific quantity such as a financial balance may intentionally use a non-grammatical category and must document that treatment.

**Security and audit implications:** Formatter input is type-checked and bounded; avoid exposing sensitive count values through telemetry except where explicitly authorized.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Pin/test CLDR-compatible behavior across server and browser runtimes; keep plural logic in catalogs rather than business calculations.

**Verification method:** Automated locale test vectors compare formatter output against pinned CLDR data; test unknown selector values and numeric boundaries.

**REQUIREMENT 0576 OF 1120  |  INTERNATIONALIZATION, MULTILINGUAL UX, AND LOCALIZATION**

## ERP-I18N-016 — Translation context and terminology

**Normative requirement:** Each translatable message shall support translator context metadata containing module, screen/action, audience, character-limit guidance where applicable, and approved domain term references.

**Rationale:** The same source word can have different meanings in finance, inventory, HR, or service workflows; context reduces incorrect translations.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Catalog export includes context metadata without embedding tenant transactional data.

**AC 2.** A configured glossary term is surfaced to a translator and term deviations can be flagged in review.

**AC 3.** Changing context metadata increments the catalog source revision.

**Exception / edge case:** A customer-specific glossary override may be enabled by the tenant but cannot alter platform-owned legal or safety terminology without an approved extension.

**Security and audit implications:** Restrict catalog editing, approval, and publication by tenant and role; escape all interpolated values and retain immutable release provenance for controlled text.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Glossary entries can be locale-specific and may include forbidden synonyms; do not treat translations as legal validation of jurisdictional content.

**Verification method:** Test export redaction of production data; restrict glossary editing and log changes; review approval records for regulated terms.

**REQUIREMENT 0577 OF 1120  |  INTERNATIONALIZATION, MULTILINGUAL UX, AND LOCALIZATION**

## ERP-I18N-017 — Missing translation observability

**Normative requirement:** The runtime shall emit a structured missing-translation event with message key, requested locale, resolved fallback locale, catalog release, tenant pseudonymous identifier, and module, subject to tenant telemetry settings.

**Rationale:** Structured coverage telemetry identifies gaps without exposing translated content or business records.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A missing key produces one structured event with the specified dimensions and a stable event code.

**AC 2.** Repeated misses are rate-limited or aggregated to prevent log floods.

**AC 3.** Tenant telemetry configuration can disable tenant-identifying dimensions while preserving local diagnostics.

**AC 4.** An authorized tenant dashboard can reconcile missing-key, missing-locale, and fallback counts by locale, module, and criticality to the structured events.

**Exception / edge case:** A deliberate source-language-only system constant may be marked non-translatable and excluded from missing-translation reporting.

**Security and audit implications:** Avoid recording full screen text, user input, or customer content in events; restrict tenant-level analytics to authorized roles.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Events must distinguish missing key, missing locale translation, and deliberate fallback so localization managers can act on the right gap.

**Verification method:** Automated test captures telemetry fields and verifies redaction/rate limiting; inspect log access policy and retention.

**REQUIREMENT 0578 OF 1120  |  INTERNATIONALIZATION, MULTILINGUAL UX, AND LOCALIZATION**

## ERP-I18N-018 — Translation quality gates

**Normative requirement:** A catalog release shall not be published until machine validation passes for syntax, key parity, placeholder parity, forbidden empty strings, and configured completion threshold, and designated human review is recorded for critical messages.

**Rationale:** Quality gates catch broken resources and prevent untranslated or structurally invalid strings from entering production.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Release validation rejects malformed resource syntax and a required key absent from the source catalog.

**AC 2.** The configured completion threshold is evaluated per locale and critical-message class.

**AC 3.** Critical authentication, financial, safety, and legal workflow messages have a recorded reviewer approval before publication.

**Exception / edge case:** A tenant may publish a lower-completion draft to a sandbox environment, but the release is marked non-production and is not selected by live sessions.

**Security and audit implications:** Limit who can waive gates; include waived threshold, reason, scope, and expiry in the audit event.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Completion policy can differ by tenant/extension; translation completeness does not establish legal or domain compliance.

**Verification method:** Test build pipeline rejection cases; verify deployment refuses non-production catalog IDs; audit human approvals and release hashes.

**REQUIREMENT 0579 OF 1120  |  INTERNATIONALIZATION, MULTILINGUAL UX, AND LOCALIZATION**

## ERP-I18N-019 — Locale-aware validation messages

**Normative requirement:** API and UI validation shall return stable machine-readable error codes and parameter values, with human-readable messages localized using the resolved UI language.

**Rationale:** Stable codes permit clients and integrations to act consistently while each user sees understandable error text.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** The same invalid payload yields the same error code across locales.

**AC 2.** The rendered validation message changes with the UI locale without changing the validation outcome.

**AC 3.** An API response provides a safe default or source-language message when a translation is unavailable.

**Exception / edge case:** Security-sensitive errors may intentionally use a generic message that does not reveal whether a protected record or account exists.

**Security and audit implications:** Never expose localized messages as authorization signals; preserve safe generic responses and avoid echoing untrusted input without encoding.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Client/server message catalogs may differ in release; API error codes are stable contracts, message locale follows an explicit request context.

**Verification method:** Contract-test error schema across locales; test authorization-sensitive generic responses; lint that API logic branches on codes rather than translated text.

**REQUIREMENT 0580 OF 1120  |  INTERNATIONALIZATION, MULTILINGUAL UX, AND LOCALIZATION**

## ERP-I18N-020 — User-generated localized content

**Normative requirement:** For free-text fields declared language-sensitive, the application shall store the submitted text unchanged as UTF-8 and may store a validated language tag separately, without silently translating or normalizing the user's wording.

**Rationale:** Customer-authored text can have legal and operational significance; preserving original content prevents translation from replacing source evidence.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Read/write round-trip preserves the submitted Unicode scalar sequence for tested scripts.

**AC 2.** A language tag, when supplied, is validated independently from the text value.

**AC 3.** No automatic translation overwrites the source field.

**Exception / edge case:** An optional search-normalized derivative may be created for matching, but it must be separately stored, reproducible, and never used as the authoritative display value.

**Security and audit implications:** Protect user text as sensitive tenant data; escape on output; restrict language metadata changes and retain before/after snapshots where business audit requires.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** A text language tag does not determine jurisdiction, confidentiality, or direction; users may enter mixed-language text.

**Verification method:** Integration-test multilingual round trips, exports, and audit snapshots; inspect derived-field lineage and access controls.

**REQUIREMENT 0581 OF 1120  |  INTERNATIONALIZATION, MULTILINGUAL UX, AND LOCALIZATION**

## ERP-I18N-021 — Culture-based number display

**Normative requirement:** The presentation layer shall format numeric values using the resolved display locale and the value's explicit numeric type, without converting numbers to locale-formatted strings before storage or calculation.

**Rationale:** Decimal separators, digit grouping, and digit shapes differ; separating calculation from presentation avoids corrupt arithmetic.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Equivalent decimal values display with the configured locale's separators and grouping.

**AC 2.** Changing UI or format locale changes rendered text but does not change the stored numeric value or API decimal value.

**AC 3.** Negative values and configured precision render according to the field's display policy.

**Exception / edge case:** Identifiers, account numbers, postal codes, and codes declared non-numeric remain strings and are not reformatted as quantities.

**Security and audit implications:** Do not log formatted sensitive amounts unnecessarily; apply role-based access to financial values independently of localization.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Use locale formatting for display only; define decimal parsing separately and reject ambiguous input rather than guessing.

**Verification method:** Test exact outputs under pinned runtime/CLDR data; verify storage/API contracts use numeric values; inspect logs for locale-specific formatted numbers used in machine calculations.

**REQUIREMENT 0582 OF 1120  |  INTERNATIONALIZATION, MULTILINGUAL UX, AND LOCALIZATION**

## ERP-I18N-022 — Locale-aware numeric input parsing

**Normative requirement:** Numeric input fields shall parse values using the field's configured accepted locale grammar and reject ambiguous or malformed input with a localized correction hint rather than silently reinterpret it.

**Rationale:** Guessing whether punctuation means decimal or grouping can alter prices, quantities, or journal amounts by orders of magnitude.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A valid localized decimal input parses to the expected exact numeric value.

**AC 2.** An ambiguous string such as a mixed-separator value follows an explicit field policy and either parses deterministically or is rejected.

**AC 3.** Rejected input is returned with a localized explanation and a stable validation code.

**Exception / edge case:** Bulk import may accept a declared file-level culture distinct from the user's UI locale; the selected culture must be shown before commit.

**Security and audit implications:** Never infer tenant or jurisdiction from number syntax; avoid returning original sensitive field values in validation telemetry.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Parse under explicit input culture and preserve canonical decimal values; paste behavior and mobile keyboards must be tested for supported locales.

**Verification method:** Fuzz-test grouping/decimal separators and Unicode digit sets; test preview/commit parity; audit import culture override and reject counts.

**REQUIREMENT 0583 OF 1120  |  INTERNATIONALIZATION, MULTILINGUAL UX, AND LOCALIZATION**

## ERP-I18N-023 — Currency identity separate from formatting

**Normative requirement:** Every monetary amount shall be represented with an explicit currency code and numeric amount in the domain model; display formatting shall not determine the transaction currency.

**Rationale:** A symbol such as \`$` is ambiguous across currencies, and a user's region setting must not alter a posted business amount.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** An amount API response exposes a currency code separately from the formatted display string.

**AC 2.** Two currencies sharing a symbol display with an unambiguous code or equivalent context in transaction views.

**AC 3.** Changing the user's locale leaves stored currency code and amount unchanged.

**Exception / edge case:** A currency-free quantity such as a non-monetary valuation estimate may be represented only under a separately declared domain contract and cannot be posted as a monetary transaction.

**Security and audit implications:** Currency access follows financial permissions; tenant-specific currency settings cannot be modified by ordinary users; audit monetary context changes.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Use ISO 4217 code lists with effective dates as a controlled reference-data source; regional display symbol is not a currency identity.

**Verification method:** Contract-test amount DTOs and persistence; test same-symbol currencies; audit currency changes on editable drafts and forbid unapproved changes after posting.

**REQUIREMENT 0584 OF 1120  |  INTERNATIONALIZATION, MULTILINGUAL UX, AND LOCALIZATION**

## ERP-I18N-024 — Currency minor units and rounding policy

**Normative requirement:** Each monetary calculation shall use the transaction's explicit currency precision and a versioned rounding policy configured by the relevant finance/domain module, never a universal two-decimal assumption.

**Rationale:** Currency precision and calculation rules are not universally two decimal places; rounding rules may be jurisdictional, contractual, or product-specific.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A currency precision test fixture drives display and calculation at the configured scale.

**AC 2.** The rounding policy identifier and version are recorded for posted calculations.

**AC 3.** Changing display locale does not change the numeric rounding result.

**Exception / edge case:** A tenant or jurisdiction extension may override default currency precision or rounding only through approved policy configuration; currencies without minor units must be supported where enabled.

**Security and audit implications:** Only finance configuration roles can change calculation rules; preserve policy snapshots with posted records and restrict backdated edits.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Currency metadata is maintained reference data; statutory tax rounding, cash rounding, and accounting precision must be configured per jurisdiction/module.

**Verification method:** Property-test rounding boundaries and currency metadata changes; reconcile posted totals after configuration update; audit rounding-policy activation.

**REQUIREMENT 0585 OF 1120  |  INTERNATIONALIZATION, MULTILINGUAL UX, AND LOCALIZATION**

## ERP-I18N-025 — Date display versus date value

**Normative requirement:** Date-only business fields shall be stored and exchanged as calendar dates without time-zone conversion, while rendering shall use the user's or document's explicitly selected calendar and locale where the workflow permits.

**Rationale:** A due date or birth date is not an instant; converting it through time zones can shift its displayed day.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A date-only value round-trips unchanged across users in different time zones.

**AC 2.** The date is displayed in an explicitly configured calendar/locale format.

**AC 3.** API schemas distinguish date-only values from timestamps.

**Exception / edge case:** A legally fixed Gregorian date may require Gregorian display even when the user's preferred calendar differs; the workflow must label this override.

**Security and audit implications:** Do not rely on client locale to determine statutory date interpretation; permissions for legal date changes are governed by owning module.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Calendar preference affects display only unless a jurisdictional workflow explicitly configures another calendar for domain interpretation.

**Verification method:** Test date-only cross-zone round-trips and alternate calendar display; review API schema and persisted values; audit authorized calendar overrides on documents.

**REQUIREMENT 0586 OF 1120  |  INTERNATIONALIZATION, MULTILINGUAL UX, AND LOCALIZATION**

## ERP-I18N-026 — Instant and time-zone preservation

**Normative requirement:** The system shall store event instants in UTC-capable timestamp types and store the associated IANA time-zone identifier separately whenever future local wall-clock intent or source zone must be preserved.

**Rationale:** A timestamp with time zone alone does not retain the originally stated zone in PostgreSQL; future civil time can shift under political changes to zone rules.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** An event instant with an explicit offset is normalized and round-trips to the same instant.

**AC 2.** A recurring or future local appointment persists both local date/time intent and its named time zone.

**AC 3.** The UI displays the instant in the selected display zone and provides the source zone when relevant.

**Exception / edge case:** A record that represents a fixed-offset device reading may store the offset rather than an IANA region, but it must identify that choice in the schema.

**Security and audit implications:** Time-zone input is validated against an approved identifier set; retain actor/time for scheduling changes and prevent tenant time-zone data leakage.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Do not confuse tenant legal/entity zone, user display zone, and stored UTC instant; resolve ambiguous/nonexistent local times with explicit user choice.

**Verification method:** Integration-test DST gaps/folds and timezone database update scenarios; inspect schema for instant plus zone on future schedules; audit zone edits to committed schedules.

**REQUIREMENT 0587 OF 1120  |  INTERNATIONALIZATION, MULTILINGUAL UX, AND LOCALIZATION**

## ERP-I18N-027 — Date and time input ambiguity

**Normative requirement:** Date/time forms shall expose or infer a single declared input format from the active format locale and reject ambiguous inputs unless the user selects an explicit interpretation.

**Rationale:** Values such as \`03/04/2026` have multiple valid meanings; silent guessing can affect deadlines and payroll.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** The form displays a locale-appropriate format example or structured date picker.

**AC 2.** Ambiguous text is rejected or resolved only under a documented selected format.

**AC 3.** Submitted timestamp input includes an explicit time-zone context when the operation requires an instant.

**Exception / edge case:** An import template may have a documented invariant ISO format regardless of UI locale, with a visible template version and validation report.

**Security and audit implications:** Prevent untrusted format strings from driving server execution; validation errors must not disclose unrelated records.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Date input widgets must support keyboard entry and assistive technology; date labels and examples are localized, while machine interchange remains unambiguous.

**Verification method:** E2E-test locale-specific inputs, DST overlap, and invalid dates; verify import preview uses declared format; audit manual interpretation overrides.

**REQUIREMENT 0588 OF 1120  |  INTERNATIONALIZATION, MULTILINGUAL UX, AND LOCALIZATION**

## ERP-I18N-028 — Localized units and measurement

**Normative requirement:** Quantity presentation shall use a value's explicit unit of measure and a locale-aware formatter; unit conversion shall occur only under a declared conversion rule owned by the relevant industry module.

**Rationale:** Local unit names and display conventions vary, but display localization must not silently change physical quantity or business meaning.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A stored quantity includes a unit code and numeric value.

**AC 2.** Unit labels and number formatting follow the selected locale without changing the canonical value.

**AC 3.** A conversion action identifies the source unit, target unit, and conversion rule/version.

**Exception / edge case:** For temperature and other affine measures, conversion uses the configured dimension-specific formula rather than a generic scale multiplier.

**Security and audit implications:** Unit configuration changes require authorized domain administration; do not accept user-selected units that violate item or process policy.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Unit symbols and names may be translated; conversion policy, tolerances, and legal metrology requirements belong to configurable industry/jurisdiction modules.

**Verification method:** Test unit round-trips, boundary values, and conversions for selected industry extensions; audit conversion-rule version on persisted derived quantities.

**REQUIREMENT 0589 OF 1120  |  INTERNATIONALIZATION, MULTILINGUAL UX, AND LOCALIZATION**

## ERP-I18N-029 — Locale-specific list and address display

**Normative requirement:** The system shall render person and address components according to the selected locale's configured ordering and labels while retaining separate structured fields and a source-preserving free-form address when required.

**Rationale:** Names and addresses do not have one global order, and concatenating them into one format loses searchability and local usability.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A configured locale rendering profile can reorder given/family name and address components without data migration.

**AC 2.** Postal code, region, and locality are rendered only when present and in the configured order.

**AC 3.** A free-form address remains retrievable byte-for-byte after structured display rendering.

**Exception / edge case:** An address-validation or postal-layout rule may be unavailable for a country; the system then preserves entered fields and marks validation as unavailable rather than fabricating a format.

**Security and audit implications:** Apply PII access controls and mask address values in logs; address templates cannot grant rights to view restricted person data.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Country-specific postal rules are extension/reference-data inputs; no single address schema or name-order rule is presumed universal.

**Verification method:** Test address display with missing optional components and non-Latin scripts; verify data import/export fields; audit changes to country-specific profile configuration.

**REQUIREMENT 0590 OF 1120  |  INTERNATIONALIZATION, MULTILINGUAL UX, AND LOCALIZATION**

## ERP-I18N-030 — Rendered value and canonical value separation

**Normative requirement:** The API and persistence layers shall keep canonical machine values separate from localized display strings, and clients shall not submit display-only formatted values as authoritative values without explicit parsing and validation.

**Rationale:** Localized strings are presentation artifacts and cannot be reliably exchanged, indexed, or compared as canonical business values.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A response exposes canonical numeric/date/code fields separately from display text where display text is returned.

**AC 2.** A command containing display-only text without the required canonical field is rejected.

**AC 3.** Locale changes do not alter stored canonical values.

**Exception / edge case:** A report export intended for human viewing may contain formatted values only if it is clearly identified as presentation output and a machine export remains available for the relevant use case.

**Security and audit implications:** Do not accept client display strings as trusted policy inputs; restrict sensitive canonical values independently from display localization.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** This boundary applies consistently to browser forms, APIs, batch files, reports, and integrations.

**Verification method:** Contract-test response schemas and command validation; compare persisted values before and after locale switch; audit parsing overrides in financial entry.

**REQUIREMENT 0591 OF 1120  |  INTERNATIONALIZATION, MULTILINGUAL UX, AND LOCALIZATION**

## ERP-I18N-031 — UTF-8 storage and transport

**Normative requirement:** The application and PostgreSQL deployment shall use UTF-8 as the canonical database and application transport encoding for multilingual human text, rejecting invalid encoding rather than replacing characters silently.

**Rationale:** UTF-8 supports the scripts required by a global ERP and PostgreSQL documents the risks of SQL_ASCII's lack of encoding validation/conversion.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** The production database encoding is verified as UTF8 by deployment health checks.

**AC 2.** Round-trip tests preserve representative Latin, Arabic, Indic, CJK, combining-mark, and supplementary-plane values.

**AC 3.** Invalid byte sequences are rejected at API/import boundaries with a safe validation result.

**Exception / edge case:** Legacy source systems with a different encoding may be imported only through an explicitly declared, tested conversion mapping with a conversion-error report.

**Security and audit implications:** UTF-8 does not identify language or authorize access; use tenant data controls and safe output encoding independently.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** All text fields, API payloads, exports, and logs that preserve human text must use compatible Unicode handling.

**Verification method:** Test DB encoding at startup and CI; test conversion-loss handling for imports; restrict raw file retention and log only counts/error offsets when possible.

**REQUIREMENT 0592 OF 1120  |  INTERNATIONALIZATION, MULTILINGUAL UX, AND LOCALIZATION**

## ERP-I18N-032 — Unicode normalization policy

**Normative requirement:** Text comparison and indexing shall apply a documented normalization strategy appropriate to the field while preserving the original user-entered value for display and audit.

**Rationale:** Canonically equivalent Unicode strings can have different code-point sequences; normalization may aid matching but can affect evidentiary fidelity.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Tests compare precomposed and decomposed forms under the field's declared search policy.

**AC 2.** The authoritative stored text remains unchanged when a normalized search key is generated.

**AC 3.** Normalization version/policy is discoverable for indexed searchable fields.

**Exception / edge case:** Passwords, cryptographic tokens, externally defined identifiers, and other fields with byte-sensitive semantics must not be normalized unless their owning security protocol explicitly requires it.

**Security and audit implications:** Avoid normalization that creates identity collisions or changes access-control principals; protect normalized indexes under the same tenant scope as source data.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Use Unicode-aware policy, not locale-specific lowercasing, as a universal normalization substitute; nondeterministic collation has performance and operation tradeoffs.

**Verification method:** Property-test normalization and collision cases; verify original value retention and audit export; security review byte-sensitive exclusions.

**REQUIREMENT 0593 OF 1120  |  INTERNATIONALIZATION, MULTILINGUAL UX, AND LOCALIZATION**

## ERP-I18N-033 — Search normalization and diacritic behavior

**Normative requirement:** Each user-facing text search shall declare whether matching is exact, case-insensitive, accent-insensitive, transliterated, or tokenized, and shall not apply one global equivalence rule to all fields.

**Rationale:** Search needs vary: names, legal identifiers, and narrative text have different equivalence requirements and false-match risks.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Search API metadata or configuration identifies the matching mode for each searchable field.

**AC 2.** Tests prove exact legal identifiers remain distinct where configured while narrative search supports declared tolerant matching.

**AC 3.** Results are filtered by tenant and record permissions before they are returned.

**Exception / edge case:** Accent-insensitive search may be offered as a user option, but the query must disclose when results use a broadened match and preserve exact-match access for identifiers.

**Security and audit implications:** Search broadening must never bypass row-level authorization or expose existence of restricted records; audit sensitive search access per module policy.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Locale-sensitive search uses configured provider/version and is decoupled from display locale unless the field policy explicitly follows locale.

**Verification method:** Test collisions, Unicode edge cases, and tenant boundary filters; review query plans when changing ICU collation; audit search configuration changes.

**REQUIREMENT 0594 OF 1120  |  INTERNATIONALIZATION, MULTILINGUAL UX, AND LOCALIZATION**

## ERP-I18N-034 — Locale-aware sorting and stable pagination

**Normative requirement:** User-facing alphabetical sorting shall use an explicitly selected collation profile and a stable secondary key so pages do not duplicate or omit rows when primary text values compare equally.

**Rationale:** Natural ordering differs by language and provider; stable tie-breaking protects pagination and predictable ERP lists.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Sort tests include locale-specific order fixtures and strings that compare equal under configured collation.

**AC 2.** Paginated queries include a deterministic unique secondary key.

**AC 3.** Changing collation profile changes order only and does not modify stored text.

**Exception / edge case:** A compliance or machine process may require code-point or identifier order and must declare that order rather than inherit a user locale.

**Security and audit implications:** Sorting does not authorize access; ensure stable sort keys do not expose hidden identifiers in client-visible URLs or logs.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** PostgreSQL provider/version changes can change ordering and invalidate index assumptions; migration plan must include reindex and comparison review where required.

**Verification method:** Test collation-sensitive pagination across page boundaries; include provider version in deployment checks; audit changes to tenant sort profile.

**REQUIREMENT 0595 OF 1120  |  INTERNATIONALIZATION, MULTILINGUAL UX, AND LOCALIZATION**

## ERP-I18N-035 — Search tokenization and language metadata

**Normative requirement:** Full-text search shall select an explicitly configured analyzer per supported language or a documented fallback analyzer and shall preserve source text for display and audit.

**Rationale:** Token boundaries, stemming, and stop words differ by language; a single analyzer reduces recall and precision in multilingual records.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Search configuration maps each enabled analyzer to an approved language identifier and version.

**AC 2.** Queries for supported language fixtures return expected tokens without altering stored source text.

**AC 3.** When text has no language metadata, the fallback analyzer is recorded in query diagnostics.

**Exception / edge case:** Mixed-language text may use a multilingual analyzer or be indexed into more than one language-specific field, but results must not duplicate a record without an explicit reason.

**Security and audit implications:** Analyzer configuration is admin-only; avoid logging complete searched content; search results still obey object-level permissions.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Language tag is optional metadata and may be wrong; analyzer choice must permit graceful fallback and explicit override.

**Verification method:** Integration-test analyzers on mixed-script, short, and untagged input; audit analyzer upgrades and rebuild affected indexes; ensure tenant filters remain mandatory.

**REQUIREMENT 0596 OF 1120  |  INTERNATIONALIZATION, MULTILINGUAL UX, AND LOCALIZATION**

## ERP-I18N-036 — Identifier and code invariance

**Normative requirement:** System identifiers, enum codes, API field names, and integration keys shall be locale-invariant and shall not be translated, case-folded, or reformatted as display text.

**Rationale:** Stable codes allow integrations and audit records to remain consistent across localized interfaces.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** The same identifier is returned in every supported UI locale.

**AC 2.** Localized labels map to a stable code in API requests and responses.

**AC 3.** Changing a locale does not change equality or uniqueness behavior for invariant identifiers.

**Exception / edge case:** A human-readable alias may be localized, but it cannot replace or alter the underlying identifier.

**Security and audit implications:** Security principals must use a dedicated canonicalization policy; block mixed-script/confusable ambiguity where identity risk is assessed.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Translate labels, not wire values, database keys, permission names, or enum members.

**Verification method:** Contract-test stable codes across locales; security-test case and Unicode confusable handling for authentication identifiers; audit alias changes separately.

**REQUIREMENT 0597 OF 1120  |  INTERNATIONALIZATION, MULTILINGUAL UX, AND LOCALIZATION**

## ERP-I18N-037 — Unicode-safe length limits

**Normative requirement:** Text length validation shall count and limit values according to the field's declared unit (grapheme clusters, Unicode scalar values, bytes, or protocol-specific units) and report the same limit consistently across client, API, and database.

**Rationale:** A visible character can comprise multiple code points, and browser code-unit counts can disagree with storage and integration limits.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** For each bounded field, the declared length unit is documented in schema/API metadata.

**AC 2.** Boundary tests include combining sequences and supplementary characters.

**AC 3.** Client and server accept/reject outcomes agree for all tested boundary values.

**Exception / edge case:** A downstream system with a byte limit may impose a stricter connector-specific maximum and must report that limit before submission.

**Security and audit implications:** Length errors must not echo sensitive submitted text; enforce server limits to prevent resource exhaustion regardless of client validation.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Labels and helper text state user-understandable limits; do not confuse grapheme count with encoded byte count.

**Verification method:** Boundary/property tests run across browser and backend; verify DB constraints match declared units; test import error reporting.

**REQUIREMENT 0598 OF 1120  |  INTERNATIONALIZATION, MULTILINGUAL UX, AND LOCALIZATION**

## ERP-I18N-038 — Unicode-safe truncation and export

**Normative requirement:** Any truncation, preview, or fixed-width export shall avoid splitting a grapheme cluster or encoded character and shall mark truncation when the receiver needs to distinguish it from complete content.

**Rationale:** Naive byte/code-unit truncation corrupts multilingual text or creates misleading records and exports.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Preview truncation never emits malformed UTF-8 or partial surrogate pairs.

**AC 2.** Where content is truncated in an export, the export contract identifies truncation or rejects overlength data.

**AC 3.** Round-trip import/export tests preserve characters when the target format permits them.

**Exception / edge case:** If a legacy fixed-width protocol requires byte truncation, it must use an approved connector-specific encoder and report each lossy record for operator review.

**Security and audit implications:** Prevent truncation from hiding security-significant suffixes in identifiers or audit fields; restrict access to exported records.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** UI previews may shorten narrative text visually but must expose the complete value to assistive technology or a detail view.

**Verification method:** Test boundary truncation in all supported scripts and export encodings; security-review delimiters and control-character handling; audit lossy export counts.

**REQUIREMENT 0599 OF 1120  |  INTERNATIONALIZATION, MULTILINGUAL UX, AND LOCALIZATION**

## ERP-I18N-039 — Confusable and mixed-script risk handling

**Normative requirement:** Authentication identifiers and other security-sensitive lookup keys shall use an explicit Unicode confusable/mixed-script risk policy and shall not apply display-locale collation as the identity comparison rule.

**Rationale:** Visually similar characters from distinct scripts can deceive users or create ambiguous identities if compared with locale-dependent text rules.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Identity registration and lookup use the documented canonical comparison key.

**AC 2.** A test corpus of selected confusables triggers the configured review/block behavior.

**AC 3.** The system preserves the original entered identifier and explains rejected or flagged values without exposing another account.

**Exception / edge case:** Business names, free-form descriptions, and multilingual personal names must not be blanket-rejected solely because they mix scripts; risk controls target fields where identity spoofing matters.

**Security and audit implications:** Apply controls narrowly to security principal fields; rate-limit probing and do not disclose matched account identifiers in errors.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Do not use locale sorting equivalence for uniqueness; support legitimate mixed-script person and organization data outside security identifiers.

**Verification method:** Security test identity collision and account enumeration behavior; inspect canonicalization policy and audit flagged/blocked attempts.

**REQUIREMENT 0600 OF 1120  |  INTERNATIONALIZATION, MULTILINGUAL UX, AND LOCALIZATION**

## ERP-I18N-040 — Collation upgrade management

**Normative requirement:** The platform shall record PostgreSQL collation provider and version for locale-sensitive indexes and execute a controlled review/reindex procedure when a provider version mismatch is detected.

**Rationale:** Collation library updates may change ordering; existing indexes can reflect an older sort order and require operational handling.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Deployment health checks surface provider-version mismatch for monitored collations.

**AC 2.** A migration plan identifies affected indexes and blocks promotion until approved remediation completes.

**AC 3.** Post-upgrade regression fixtures compare expected sort and equality behavior.

**Exception / edge case:** An environment using stable code-point ordering may exempt an index from locale-change remediation only when the schema marks that invariant policy.

**Security and audit implications:** Limit collation-management actions to database/platform operators; log operations and avoid exposing database internals to tenant users.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Pin/reference collation behavior for reproducible reports and searches; application formatting locale changes do not automatically change database collation.

**Verification method:** Test mismatch detection and migration runbook in staging; review index integrity after rebuild; audit provider updates and approvals.

**REQUIREMENT 0601 OF 1120  |  INTERNATIONALIZATION, MULTILINGUAL UX, AND LOCALIZATION**

## ERP-I18N-041 — Page language and direction metadata

**Normative requirement:** Every rendered HTML page shall set an accurate BCP 47 \`lang\` value and an explicit base \`dir` value derived from the resolved script/layout direction, independently of language selection.

**Rationale:** Assistive technologies use language metadata, and script identity does not itself set right-to-left direction.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Automated browser inspection confirms \`\<html lang>` matches rendered language.

**AC 2.** RTL pages set \`dir=rtl` on the document root and LTR pages use the documented LTR default or explicit value.

**AC 3.** Switching UI locale updates both metadata attributes on the next render.

**Exception / edge case:** A language can be written in multiple scripts or contain mixed-direction content; direction may be overridden per block without changing document language.

**Security and audit implications:** Correct language metadata can expose selected language but not sensitive data; do not derive security policy from \`lang\` or \`dir` attributes.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Language and direction are independent data fields; direction must follow the actual UI script policy, including script subtags or tenant-specific presentation choices.

**Verification method:** Accessibility scan plus DOM assertions on every locale route; manual screen-reader check for at least one RTL route; review locale-to-direction registry.

**REQUIREMENT 0602 OF 1120  |  INTERNATIONALIZATION, MULTILINGUAL UX, AND LOCALIZATION**

## ERP-I18N-042 — Direction-aware layout styling

**Normative requirement:** The frontend shall use CSS logical properties and direction-aware component layouts for alignment, spacing, borders, and navigation rather than hard-coded left/right assumptions in shared UI components.

**Rationale:** Logical layout maps to inline/block start and end for RTL and future writing modes without duplicating the entire screen.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** The shared design-system lint/test suite rejects newly introduced physical left/right layout declarations in designated components unless allowlisted.

**AC 2.** Representative ERP screens pass visual regression checks in both LTR and RTL modes.

**AC 3.** Keyboard tab order and action order remain logical and consistent across direction changes.

**Exception / edge case:** An embedded third-party component with a fixed physical layout may remain LTR only if it is visually isolated, labeled, and does not disrupt surrounding navigation.

**Security and audit implications:** Prevent RTL mirroring from moving destructive or authorization-sensitive controls into unexpected positions without labels; review for clickjacking-like placement confusion.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Use flex/grid logical flow and icon-specific mirror rules; not every icon or chart should be mirrored.

**Verification method:** Run RTL visual regression and keyboard E2E tests; review allowlist changes; scan CSS bundle for disallowed directional properties.

**REQUIREMENT 0603 OF 1120  |  INTERNATIONALIZATION, MULTILINGUAL UX, AND LOCALIZATION**

## ERP-I18N-043 — Mixed-direction text isolation

**Normative requirement:** User-generated or externally sourced text embedded in a differently directed UI shall be directionally isolated using semantic markup such as \`bdi` or an equivalent safe renderer that determines or declares the run direction.

**Rationale:** Mixed Arabic/Hebrew and Latin product names, codes, URLs, or numbers can reorder adjacent punctuation and values if not isolated.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A test renders opposite-direction names followed by a number and punctuation without spillover into adjacent text.

**AC 2.** Text with unknown direction uses automatic direction detection on the narrow content span.

**AC 3.** Markup is present in rendered DOM for designated dynamic-text components.

**AC 4.** Copying a displayed URL or code from an RTL view yields its original canonical character sequence, and inserted bidi controls cannot reorder adjacent values.

**Exception / edge case:** A fixed-format machine token may be explicitly rendered LTR in an RTL page; the surrounding paragraph direction remains unchanged.

**Security and audit implications:** Escape untrusted text and isolate direction; detect or safely display hidden directional control characters in sensitive identifiers and audit views.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Apply on-screen and printed previews; never reverse source strings in application code to simulate RTL.

**Verification method:** Browser E2E tests with mixed-direction hostile strings and punctuation; verify HTML escaping and no raw bidi override injection.

**REQUIREMENT 0604 OF 1120  |  INTERNATIONALIZATION, MULTILINGUAL UX, AND LOCALIZATION**

## ERP-I18N-044 — RTL form and data-grid behavior

**Normative requirement:** Forms, tables, menus, and grid controls shall support RTL reading order and input behavior while keeping field labels, validation messages, and column-value associations programmatically linked.

**Rationale:** ERP workflows rely on dense forms and tables; mirroring only the page shell leaves data relationships and controls unusable.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** RTL test fixtures show labels and fields in the intended logical sequence.

**AC 2.** Data-grid headers remain associated with the correct data columns after direction change.
