**AC 3.** Validation summary links focus the corresponding invalid control in both LTR and RTL.

**Exception / edge case:** A numeric ledger table may deliberately keep amount columns LTR-aligned for scanability, but its layout and labels must communicate that choice and preserve keyboard order.

**Security and audit implications:** Ensure all actions remain accessible independent of visual direction; do not place security confirmation buttons ambiguously.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Text direction can be mixed per cell; expose \`lang\` and \`dir` as needed and keep screen-reader order logical.

**Verification method:** Automated accessibility checks plus manual keyboard review on RTL forms and grids; visual compare column sort/filter actions.

**REQUIREMENT 0605 OF 1120  |  INTERNATIONALIZATION, MULTILINGUAL UX, AND LOCALIZATION**

## ERP-I18N-045 — Accessible language switching

**Normative requirement:** The language selector shall be operable by keyboard and assistive technology, expose its label and current value in the active UI language, and announce a language change through an accessible status message.

**Rationale:** A language switch that is visually obvious but not programmatically exposed is inaccessible and can leave assistive technology in a stale-language context.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** The selector is reachable and operable without a pointer.

**AC 2.** Accessibility tree exposes a localized name and selected option.

**AC 3.** After selection, the page re-renders with updated \`lang` metadata and a concise live-region confirmation.

**Exception / edge case:** If navigation reloads the page, the selected language remains announced through the new page title/heading and does not require a stale live region.

**Security and audit implications:** Avoid injecting translated text into unsafe live HTML; keep preference write permission constrained to user profile or tenant admin.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Option names should be recognizable across scripts; ensure the control and announcement work with RTL and long translated labels.

**Verification method:** Automated accessibility scan and manual keyboard/screen-reader test for representative locale pairs; check route focus restoration.

**REQUIREMENT 0606 OF 1120  |  INTERNATIONALIZATION, MULTILINGUAL UX, AND LOCALIZATION**

## ERP-I18N-046 — Language of embedded content

**Normative requirement:** When a page contains a substantial passage or control label in a language different from the page default, the rendered markup shall identify that language on the relevant element where the language is known.

**Rationale:** Language metadata enables pronunciation and processing appropriate to each language and supports WCAG language-of-parts conformance.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A multilingual description test marks each known language run with its correct tag.

**AC 2.** Screen-reader testing uses the expected pronunciation engine when available.

**AC 3.** Unknown-language content is not falsely labeled as the page language when the system cannot determine it.

**Exception / edge case:** A multilingual value inside a plain-text attribute that cannot carry nested markup is not falsely segmented; the UI should provide an accessible separate text label where possible.

**Security and audit implications:** Markup metadata is not a trust signal; escaped user content cannot inject \`lang` or alter page structure.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Use validated BCP 47 tags and keep content language separate from user UI language.

**Verification method:** DOM-level automated assertions and assistive-technology testing; review templating components that render mixed-language fields.

**REQUIREMENT 0607 OF 1120  |  INTERNATIONALIZATION, MULTILINGUAL UX, AND LOCALIZATION**

## ERP-I18N-047 — Language-independent icon and action cues

**Normative requirement:** Critical actions and status indicators shall include a localized text label or accessible name and shall not rely solely on directional icon shape, color, or culturally specific imagery.

**Rationale:** Icons may change meaning across cultures and can be ambiguous when mirrored; text labels preserve task safety.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Every icon-only actionable control has a localized accessible name.

**AC 2.** Mirroring does not change the semantic target of back, forward, expand, or destructive-action icons.

**AC 3.** Status meaning remains available in text to assistive technology and not only by color.

**Exception / edge case:** A universally standardized pictogram may supplement a label but cannot replace required accessible naming for critical ERP actions.

**Security and audit implications:** Clear labels reduce accidental destructive actions; permission checks remain server-side regardless of presentation.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Icons should be directionally classified; do not mirror logos, clocks, media controls, or symbols whose semantics are not directional.

**Verification method:** Accessibility-tree tests and RTL visual review; test actions with icons and no visible label; audit exceptions list.

**REQUIREMENT 0608 OF 1120  |  INTERNATIONALIZATION, MULTILINGUAL UX, AND LOCALIZATION**

## ERP-I18N-048 — Localized accessibility announcements

**Normative requirement:** Client-side status, progress, and error announcements shall be generated from localized message resources and update accessible live regions without changing focus unexpectedly.

**Rationale:** Asynchronous ERP operations need accessible status feedback; untranslated announcements are unusable for many users.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A background save announces localized success or failure without moving keyboard focus.

**AC 2.** Live-region text uses the active UI locale and stable message keys.

**AC 3.** Repeated identical progress events are throttled to avoid excessive announcements.

**Exception / edge case:** Security-sensitive failure details may be summarized generically while a separate authorized diagnostic view exposes full technical data.

**Security and audit implications:** Announcements must not expose confidential record values to a shared assistive session; technical diagnostic details remain permission-gated.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Messages must handle RTL punctuation and translated dynamic values; avoid concatenated speech fragments.

**Verification method:** Screen-reader test for save/import flows in at least two locales; unit-test message key availability and event throttling.

**REQUIREMENT 0609 OF 1120  |  INTERNATIONALIZATION, MULTILINGUAL UX, AND LOCALIZATION**

## ERP-I18N-049 — Font coverage and text reflow

**Normative requirement:** The frontend shall provide tested font fallback and responsive reflow for every enabled script, avoiding clipped or overlapping characters in supported screen and document sizes.

**Rationale:** A language can render incorrectly even when translation is correct if fonts lack glyphs or layouts assume short Latin strings.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Visual regression fixtures cover each enabled script family and long-string expansion.

**AC 2.** At supported zoom/reflow test sizes, labels and form controls remain readable without losing function.

**AC 3.** Fallback fonts render combining marks and supplementary characters without missing-glyph boxes in supported browser matrix.

**Exception / edge case:** A tenant-provided font may be used only after licensing, glyph coverage, security, and performance review; missing glyphs fall back to an approved system font.

**Security and audit implications:** Treat uploaded fonts as untrusted assets and validate licensing/source; avoid collecting personal data in visual diagnostics.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Font family is locale/script-aware but not hardwired to a language alone; line height and text expansion require layout slack.

**Verification method:** Run screenshot tests with long translations, CJK, Arabic, and combining-mark samples; test font CSP and asset integrity.

**REQUIREMENT 0610 OF 1120  |  INTERNATIONALIZATION, MULTILINGUAL UX, AND LOCALIZATION**

## ERP-I18N-050 — Localized accessibility conformance

**Normative requirement:** The product shall test localized UI against the adopted WCAG 2.2 conformance target for all supported locale-direction classes and shall block release on critical language metadata or keyboard/accessibility failures.

**Rationale:** Accessibility failures often arise only in translated, expanded, or RTL interfaces; testing only the source language misses them.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** The release report covers at least one route for each enabled script-direction class and includes automated and manual test results.

**AC 2.** Document language and language-of-parts checks pass on localized routes.

**AC 3.** Critical accessibility failures have an owner and block production publication until closed or formally waived under release policy.

**Exception / edge case:** A locale not yet released to production may be excluded from conformance claims but must be clearly marked preview-only and inaccessible routes must not be enabled to end users.

**Security and audit implications:** Accessibility telemetry and recordings must follow privacy rules; release waivers require named accountable approvers and expiry.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Conformance status is per actual supported locale/release; translation completion alone is not evidence of accessibility.

**Verification method:** Review localized accessibility test artifacts; manually verify representative screen-reader and keyboard flows; audit exceptions/waivers.

**REQUIREMENT 0611 OF 1120  |  INTERNATIONALIZATION, MULTILINGUAL UX, AND LOCALIZATION**

## ERP-I18N-051 — Document language, direction, and locale metadata

**Normative requirement:** Generated documents shall declare their content language and direction in the output format where supported and shall use a selected document locale distinct from the requester's UI locale when configured.

**Rationale:** A report recipient may require a different language from the preparer, and metadata affects accessibility and correct rendering.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A generated HTML/PDF document exposes the configured content-language metadata and direction.

**AC 2.** Selecting document language does not change the preparer's profile preference.

**AC 3.** The document output records locale, template version, and generation timestamp in metadata or audit record.

**Exception / edge case:** A machine-only interchange file may omit presentation language metadata only when its schema is locale-neutral and its fields use stable codes.

**Security and audit implications:** Apply document access and retention policy independently of language; ensure metadata does not leak tenant internal IDs to external recipients.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Document language must match actual translated content; mixed-language legal text requires explicit language-part metadata where format supports it.

**Verification method:** Inspect generated artifact metadata for each supported output format; test user/document locale difference; audit document generation context.

**REQUIREMENT 0612 OF 1120  |  INTERNATIONALIZATION, MULTILINGUAL UX, AND LOCALIZATION**

## ERP-I18N-052 — Document template translation coverage

**Normative requirement:** Tenant-published document templates shall declare required locale coverage and identify untranslated segments before generation; critical documents shall fail generation when required approved language content is missing.

**Rationale:** A partially translated invoice, contract, or safety instruction can mislead recipients and may fail customer or jurisdiction requirements.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Template validation reports missing message keys and locale coverage before publication.

**AC 2.** For a template class marked translation-required, generation fails if any mandatory segment lacks an approved translation.

**AC 3.** The generated document stores the exact immutable template/catalog release IDs.

**Exception / edge case:** A tenant may configure a dual-language document template where both languages are intentionally rendered and labeled, rather than selecting a single fallback.

**Security and audit implications:** Restrict template editing/publishing and recipient distribution; preserve evidence of approved text used for business records.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Whether a document must be translated or bilingual is a tenant/jurisdiction/industry policy, not a universal ERP rule.

**Verification method:** Test missing mandatory segment behavior and dual-language output; audit template releases, approval, and generated-document provenance.

**REQUIREMENT 0613 OF 1120  |  INTERNATIONALIZATION, MULTILINGUAL UX, AND LOCALIZATION**

## ERP-I18N-053 — Localized report labels and stable data fields

**Normative requirement:** Reports shall localize headings, filters, legends, and status labels while preserving invariant column identifiers, data values, and formula semantics in machine-readable exports.

**Rationale:** A report must be understandable to users without breaking downstream calculations or reconciliation.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** The same report definition produces localized visible labels and invariant column IDs across two locales.

**AC 2.** CSV/API exports expose canonical field names or schema metadata separate from translated captions.

**AC 3.** Changing locale does not alter selected records, calculation results, or sort/filter logic.

**Exception / edge case:** A human-only PDF may translate captions without exposing canonical field IDs, provided an accompanying machine export or schema is available when integration is in scope.

**Security and audit implications:** Report permissions and row-level filters are applied before localization; exports follow data-loss-prevention and retention controls.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Avoid localized field captions as database keys; define decimal/date export formats explicitly for machine consumers.

**Verification method:** Snapshot-test localized reports; schema-contract-test exports and formulas; audit report locale/template identifiers for regulated usage.

**REQUIREMENT 0614 OF 1120  |  INTERNATIONALIZATION, MULTILINGUAL UX, AND LOCALIZATION**

## ERP-I18N-054 — Email and notification language selection

**Normative requirement:** The communication service shall select message language using an explicit recipient preference or configured business rule, store the selected language and template release, and never infer language solely from a recipient's country.

**Rationale:** Recipients in one country may use different languages, and auditability requires knowing which wording was sent.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A recipient preference overrides the sender's UI language where policy allows.

**AC 2.** Each sent notification records recipient language, template/catalog release, and rendered-content hash or equivalent immutable provenance.

**AC 3.** No preference triggers the configured tenant/entity fallback and is visible to the sender before dispatch where required.

**Exception / edge case:** A mandatory legal notice may require a jurisdiction-approved language or bilingual text that overrides recipient preference under a documented policy.

**Security and audit implications:** Recipient language is personal preference data; restrict it and minimize message-content retention; authorization to send remains a separate permission.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Language policy must be configurable per notification class and channel; do not equate country, nationality, and language.

**Verification method:** Integration-test recipient precedence and fallback; verify send audit entry and access controls; test suppression/retention policies.

**REQUIREMENT 0615 OF 1120  |  INTERNATIONALIZATION, MULTILINGUAL UX, AND LOCALIZATION**

## ERP-I18N-055 — Template variable locale contracts

**Normative requirement:** Each report, document, and notification template shall declare the locale/zone/format policy for every date, number, currency, name, and unit placeholder it renders.

**Rationale:** Template authors must not inherit ambient service locale unpredictably or turn an amount into an ambiguous string.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Template validation fails for an untyped placeholder used in a locale-sensitive formatting context.

**AC 2.** Rendered output matches the declared format policy when request and recipient locales differ.

**AC 3.** Template preview shows the selected locale and formatting context.

**Exception / edge case:** A template may intentionally display both localized and canonical value representations, but each must be labeled and separately typed.

**Security and audit implications:** Template editors receive only authorized sample data; rendering must HTML-escape untrusted variable values and isolate bidi text.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Formatting context should explicitly select UI, tenant/entity, recipient, or statutory locale rather than relying on ambient defaults.

**Verification method:** Unit-test template formatter schema, preview/production parity, and cross-locale values; audit template policy edits.

**REQUIREMENT 0616 OF 1120  |  INTERNATIONALIZATION, MULTILINGUAL UX, AND LOCALIZATION**

## ERP-I18N-056 — Localized workflow task assignment

**Normative requirement:** Workflow tasks shall store a stable task type and canonical state code while rendering task descriptions, action labels, and instructions in the assignee's current UI locale at read time unless the workflow snapshots legally controlled text.

**Rationale:** Dynamic read-time language avoids stale task language after preference changes, while a snapshot preserves controlled wording when required.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Changing an assignee's UI locale changes task labels but not task type, state, or due time.

**AC 2.** A workflow configured for text snapshotting preserves the original rendered language and release provenance.

**AC 3.** Task actions submit stable action codes and produce the same state transition across locales.

**Exception / edge case:** If a task is reassigned to a user with no supported matching locale, it uses the tenant fallback and indicates that fallback without changing workflow state.

**Security and audit implications:** Task assignment and action authorization are independent of language; do not leak task data through locale-specific notification previews.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Workflow extension authors declare translatable labels and whether any displayed text must be immutable once a transaction begins.

**Verification method:** Test task handoff across users/locales and replay state transitions; inspect snapshot provenance and audit trail.

**REQUIREMENT 0617 OF 1120  |  INTERNATIONALIZATION, MULTILINGUAL UX, AND LOCALIZATION**

## ERP-I18N-057 — Localized approval evidence

**Normative requirement:** Approval records shall preserve the approver identity, decision code, timestamp, and the exact language/template release of any material text presented for approval when the text is transaction-significant.

**Rationale:** Auditors need to distinguish stable decision meaning from the language and wording the approver reviewed.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Approval audit record stores canonical decision code and the displayed text release reference for configured workflows.

**AC 2.** A translated label cannot change the underlying approved/rejected decision enum.

**AC 3.** Re-rendering historical approval evidence uses the recorded release or clearly marks an unavailable historical artifact.

**Exception / edge case:** A routine UI label that is not material to the decision need not be copied into every approval event; workflow configuration marks material text fields.

**Security and audit implications:** Approval records are immutable or append-corrected under module policy; restrict access to reviewer identity and confidential evidence.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Legal sufficiency, signature language, and required translations are configured per applicable jurisdiction and document class.

**Verification method:** Integration-test approval across locale changes and catalog upgrades; audit historical evidence retrieval; review retention and tamper protection.

**REQUIREMENT 0618 OF 1120  |  INTERNATIONALIZATION, MULTILINGUAL UX, AND LOCALIZATION**

## ERP-I18N-058 — Cross-module locale context contract

**Normative requirement:** Every module API and asynchronous event that renders or parses human-readable content shall carry an explicit locale-context reference or declare itself locale-neutral, and shall not depend on an undocumented ambient culture.

**Rationale:** Inventory, finance, HR, CRM, and industry extensions must exchange stable machine data without hidden formatting assumptions.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Schema validation rejects a locale-sensitive message event without a valid locale context or locale-neutral declaration.

**AC 2.** An asynchronous consumer produces deterministic output from serialized locale context after restart.

**AC 3.** Module contract tests prove numeric/date canonical payload fields are independent of rendered text.

**Exception / edge case:** A low-level event containing only invariant codes and canonical values may omit locale context and mark itself locale-neutral.

**Security and audit implications:** Tenant identity and authorization claims must travel separately from locale context; reject client-forged tenant or permission data in message payloads.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Use a shared context schema for UI language, format culture, zone, calendar, numbering system, and explicit fallback policy.

**Verification method:** Contract-test event replay and version compatibility across modules; trace missing context; audit schema changes through API governance.

**REQUIREMENT 0619 OF 1120  |  INTERNATIONALIZATION, MULTILINGUAL UX, AND LOCALIZATION**

## ERP-I18N-059 — Localized import/export profile

**Normative requirement:** Each batch import/export profile shall declare its encoding, delimiter, decimal/date conventions, header language, and locale profile version, and shall validate a preview before committing imported business data.

**Rationale:** A CSV's appearance can vary by locale and application; explicit profiles avoid silent column shifts and numeric/date corruption.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Import preview identifies detected or selected profile and shows parsed sample values before commit.

**AC 2.** Unknown encoding, malformed rows, and ambiguous dates are rejected or reported before partial commit according to the configured transaction policy.

**AC 3.** Export metadata identifies profile version and encoding.

**Exception / edge case:** A tenant-defined profile may be updated, but existing scheduled jobs continue to use the pinned version until an authorized migration is approved.

**Security and audit implications:** Import/export permission checks apply to underlying records; protect uploaded files, scan them, and avoid storing them longer than policy requires.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Profiles are per connector and business process; do not infer locale solely from filename, machine locale, or user interface language.

**Verification method:** Test delimiter/encoding/date ambiguity and transactional rollback; audit profile changes, preview, commit, and rejected-row count.

**REQUIREMENT 0620 OF 1120  |  INTERNATIONALIZATION, MULTILINGUAL UX, AND LOCALIZATION**

## ERP-I18N-060 — Industry extension localization contract

**Normative requirement:** An industry extension shall register its message namespaces, required data formats, locale dependencies, and any domain-specific translation or formatting overrides through a versioned extension manifest before it is enabled for a tenant.

**Rationale:** Configurable industry modules may introduce specialized vocabulary and regional conventions that cannot be safely assumed by the core ERP.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** The extension manifest lists all required message keys and locale-dependent assets.

**AC 2.** Extension activation fails when required locale resources or declared formatter capabilities are absent.

**AC 3.** Extension-defined policies are namespaced and cannot overwrite core financial/security messages without an authorized override mechanism.

**Exception / edge case:** An optional extension locale may be disabled if the extension advertises fallback support and no mandatory workflow depends on that locale.

**Security and audit implications:** Extension publishers are trusted principals; verify signatures/provenance of localization bundles and prohibit manifest-based permission escalation.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Jurisdiction- and industry-specific law, document language, units, tax rules, and address formats remain configuration or certified extension boundaries.

**Verification method:** Test activation with complete and incomplete manifests; review namespace collision and privilege boundaries; audit extension policy/version changes.

**REQUIREMENT 0621 OF 1120  |  INTERNATIONALIZATION, MULTILINGUAL UX, AND LOCALIZATION**

## ERP-I18N-061 — Platform and tenant localization permission boundaries

**Normative requirement:** The authorization model shall separate platform locale/catalog administration, tenant locale configuration, translator editing, translator approval, personal preferences, and business transaction permissions.

**Rationale:** Locale administration may alter what users see but must not grant access to transactions or tenant settings beyond its assigned scope.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Role-matrix tests prove a translator can edit permitted catalog entries but cannot read transactional records.

**AC 2.** A tenant administrator cannot modify platform-owned default catalogs or another tenant's locale configuration.

**AC 3.** Personal preference changes cannot modify tenant defaults.

**Exception / edge case:** A small tenant may combine translator and reviewer roles only when its configured policy allows it and the audit trail records the same-person approval exception.

**Security and audit implications:** Keep localization permissions independent from finance/HR/business roles; apply tenant isolation to all localization management APIs.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Locale context is a versioned cross-module contract; canonical machine values and stable codes remain locale invariant while user-facing content follows explicit context.

**Verification method:** Run authorization tests across every role and tenant; review least-privilege grants; inspect privileged-action logs.

**REQUIREMENT 0622 OF 1120  |  INTERNATIONALIZATION, MULTILINGUAL UX, AND LOCALIZATION**

## ERP-I18N-062 — Auditable locale configuration changes

**Normative requirement:** Changes to tenant defaults, enabled locales, fallback chains, formatting profiles, direction mappings, and catalog publication shall create append-only audit events containing actor, tenant, time, old/new version, and reason where policy requires.

**Rationale:** Configuration drift can alter operational displays and document output; a trace is necessary for support and audit.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A change event records the configured fields and immutable version identifiers.

**AC 2.** Unauthorized or failed changes do not create a misleading success audit event.

**AC 3.** Authorized auditors can retrieve events filtered by tenant and date without modifying them.

**Exception / edge case:** A high-volume automated update may be represented by one signed batch event with a manifest of affected configuration objects and a retrievable detailed report.

**Security and audit implications:** Protect audit logs from tenant mutation and cross-tenant reads; minimize values captured to configuration changes rather than unrelated personal data.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Audit should identify locale policy version used to render significant artifacts when required by downstream module policy.

**Verification method:** Integration-test event creation and tamper controls; verify actor attribution under service principals; test authorized retrieval and retention.

**REQUIREMENT 0623 OF 1120  |  INTERNATIONALIZATION, MULTILINGUAL UX, AND LOCALIZATION**

## ERP-I18N-063 — API locale context contract

**Normative requirement:** Public and internal APIs shall define how UI language and format culture are requested, negotiated, returned, and versioned, while keeping canonical data formats invariant and documenting precedence.

**Rationale:** API consumers need predictable localized messages without accidentally coupling business values to their UI locale.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** OpenAPI/schema documentation states supported locale fields and precedence for each localized endpoint.

**AC 2.** API responses use stable canonical numeric/date/code values regardless of localization header.

**AC 3.** Unsupported locale values produce a documented fallback or validation response.

**Exception / edge case:** A machine-to-machine endpoint may ignore UI locale if it returns no human-readable content, and must document itself as locale-neutral.

**Security and audit implications:** Locale headers cannot choose tenant or principal; ensure error messages do not reveal unauthorized record existence and audit administrative locale overrides.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Avoid exposing only localized text to integrations; stable codes and explicit locale context support interoperable clients.

**Verification method:** Schema contract tests with multiple headers and malformed locale values; compatibility tests across API versions; security review of user-controlled locale inputs.

**REQUIREMENT 0624 OF 1120  |  INTERNATIONALIZATION, MULTILINGUAL UX, AND LOCALIZATION**

## ERP-I18N-064 — Cache variation by locale and tenant

**Normative requirement:** Any cache containing localized content or user/tenant-specific locale resolution shall key or vary responses by all effective localization dimensions and tenant identity, or shall cache only locale-neutral data.

**Rationale:** Incorrect cache keys can serve one tenant's or language's content to another user and expose data across boundaries.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Automated cache tests request the same URL under two tenants/locales and receive the correct isolated representations.

**AC 2.** CDN/cache directives vary on locale route/header only where the selected strategy requires it.

**AC 3.** Changing a tenant catalog release invalidates or bypasses stale localized cache entries by release identifier.

**Exception / edge case:** Public immutable static translation assets may be shared across tenants only when the asset is identical, non-sensitive, and keyed by content hash.

**Security and audit implications:** Tenant ID and authorization context must be included in protected-data cache keys; do not cache private localized pages as public assets.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** The cache key includes UI language, format locale only if the cached payload embeds formatted values, zone/calendar where relevant, and catalog version.

**Verification method:** Integration-test cache poisoning and cross-tenant cases; inspect Next.js server/client cache configuration; audit catalog cache invalidation events.

**REQUIREMENT 0625 OF 1120  |  INTERNATIONALIZATION, MULTILINGUAL UX, AND LOCALIZATION**

## ERP-I18N-065 — Locale input validation and resource safety

**Normative requirement:** Locale, calendar, numbering-system, time-zone, and collation inputs shall be validated against bounded allowlists or runtime-supported registries before they are used for resource selection or database operations.

**Rationale:** Unbounded locale strings can cause resource-path traversal, expensive fallback work, invalid format operations, or SQL injection if interpolated as collation names.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Malformed, oversized, and unsupported context values return controlled validation errors.

**AC 2.** Resource lookup uses mapped catalog IDs rather than a client string as a file path.

**AC 3.** Database collation choice is selected from pre-created approved names and never interpolated from raw user input.

**Exception / edge case:** A newly registered locale may be staged in configuration before runtime data is installed, but requests must use safe fallback until activation completes.

**Security and audit implications:** Treat every locale-context field as untrusted input; rate limit negotiation and separate authorization from locale validation.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Runtime registry availability can differ by deployment; health checks identify missing locale data without crashing unrelated tenants.

**Verification method:** Fuzz input validators, test path/SQL injection payloads, and run resource exhaustion tests; review allowlist update process.

**REQUIREMENT 0626 OF 1120  |  INTERNATIONALIZATION, MULTILINGUAL UX, AND LOCALIZATION**

## ERP-I18N-066 — Deterministic localization runtime baseline

**Normative requirement:** The deployment shall pin and report the .NET runtime/ICU, PostgreSQL collation provider/version, Node/Next.js runtime, and locale-data release used for locale-sensitive behavior, with an approved upgrade test process.

**Rationale:** The same locale APIs can yield updated sort and formatting results after runtime or CLDR upgrades, affecting reproducibility and user expectations.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A deployment manifest reports the exact runtime and locale-data dependencies in use.

**AC 2.** A candidate upgrade runs a defined golden corpus of number/date/plural/sort fixtures before production promotion.

**AC 3.** A mismatch in approved baselines blocks release or creates a reviewed change record.

**Exception / edge case:** Security servicing patches may be applied under emergency policy before full locale fixture review, with post-deployment verification and rollback capability.

**Security and audit implications:** Avoid logging personal preference values in build telemetry; limit baseline reporting to software and locale-data versions.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** As of 2026-11-22, Microsoft documents .NET 11 as the latest supported release and .NET 10 as LTS; exact servicing patch and other stack versions must be reconfirmed before release.

**Verification method:** CI verifies manifest and golden fixtures; test controlled runtime upgrade in staging; audit baseline approval and emergency patch events.

**REQUIREMENT 0627 OF 1120  |  INTERNATIONALIZATION, MULTILINGUAL UX, AND LOCALIZATION**

## ERP-I18N-067 — Localization quality telemetry privacy

**Normative requirement:** Product analytics for locale failures, fallback use, and task completion shall use minimized, tenant-configurable telemetry and shall not capture full user-entered text or rendered business documents by default.

**Rationale:** Coverage and usability data are valuable, but collecting full content creates unnecessary confidentiality and privacy exposure.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Telemetry schemas contain only approved event dimensions and exclude raw input/document bodies.

**AC 2.** A tenant can disable or reduce identifiable localization analytics under the product's telemetry controls.

**AC 3.** Access to aggregated cross-tenant analytics is restricted and uses de-identification or aggregation thresholds.

**AC 4.** Expired localization telemetry and draft artifacts are deleted or anonymized under the configured retention policy, with only non-content outcome counts retained.

**Exception / edge case:** A tenant-authorized support diagnostic may temporarily capture a redacted sample only after explicit consent, scope limitation, and expiry.

**Security and audit implications:** Apply data minimization, pseudonymization, role-based access, retention limits, and consent logging to diagnostic telemetry. Apply configured retention and deletion to drafts, preferences, and telemetry; keep historical catalog artifacts only under an approved archive schedule.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Locale, script, and fallback dimensions are useful for quality but should not be treated as sensitive user identity attributes without assessment.

**Verification method:** Schema/privacy tests scan sample events for content fields; test tenant opt-out; review access, retention, and consent expiry.

**REQUIREMENT 0628 OF 1120  |  INTERNATIONALIZATION, MULTILINGUAL UX, AND LOCALIZATION**

## ERP-I18N-068 — Rollback and compatibility of locale releases

**Normative requirement:** Catalog, formatting-profile, and locale-routing releases shall support rollback to the prior compatible version without changing canonical transaction data or invalidating stable API identifiers.

**Rationale:** A translation regression or routing defect must be reversible independently of business data migrations.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A rollback restores previous catalog/routing/profile identifiers for new requests within the declared activation window.

**AC 2.** Existing generated documents retain their recorded original release provenance.

**AC 3.** Rollback does not modify transaction amounts, dates, codes, or user-entered source text.

**Exception / edge case:** A data-schema migration that retires a message key may require a compatibility adapter; rollback must be blocked if the old release can no longer safely interpret the new schema.

**Security and audit implications:** Restrict rollback actions to release operators and tenant scope; retain a tamper-evident activation history.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Schema compatibility and translation release compatibility are validated independently; do not silently render critical legal text from an older unapproved catalog.

**Verification method:** Test activation/rollback under traffic and mixed deployment versions; verify artifact provenance and API compatibility; audit rollback approver and reason.

**REQUIREMENT 0629 OF 1120  |  INTERNATIONALIZATION, MULTILINGUAL UX, AND LOCALIZATION**

## ERP-I18N-069 — Internationalization regression test matrix

**Normative requirement:** CI and release qualification shall execute a declared localization test matrix covering every supported locale group, script direction, representative numeric/date conventions, text expansion, and critical business workflow, with machine-readable results.

**Rationale:** A source-language-only test suite misses locale-specific runtime, layout, and input failures.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** The matrix lists supported locale IDs and maps each to script, direction, formatter fixture, and workflow coverage.

**AC 2.** CI fails when a supported locale has no current test evidence or when a critical fixture regresses.

**AC 3.** The release artifact records test suite version, runtime baseline, and result summary.

**Exception / edge case:** Low-usage locales may use risk-based shared workflow coverage only if each locale still receives basic resource, formatting, direction, and accessibility tests.

**Security and audit implications:** Use synthetic data in localization tests and avoid copying production PII; restrict visibility of test artifacts containing customer translations.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Coverage is based on locale behaviors/classes rather than an arbitrary requirement to run every business workflow in every locale combination.

**Verification method:** Review generated matrix coverage and failure evidence; test deliberate regression detection; audit approved exclusions.

**REQUIREMENT 0630 OF 1120  |  INTERNATIONALIZATION, MULTILINGUAL UX, AND LOCALIZATION**

## ERP-I18N-070 — Release baseline reconfirmation

**Normative requirement:** Before each production release, the platform owner shall reconfirm the latest stable supported .NET and compatible ASP.NET Core servicing level from official Microsoft lifecycle/release sources and record the selected target framework and support rationale.

**Rationale:** The requested reference date is future-dated relative to many deployment plans, and support status and servicing patches change; a documented reconfirmation avoids stale assumptions.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Release evidence links to official Microsoft release/support pages consulted on the release decision date.

**AC 2.** The build target framework and installed runtime are checked against the recorded baseline.

**AC 3.** An unsupported target or missing security servicing level blocks promotion unless a time-bound exception is approved.

**Exception / edge case:** A product may intentionally remain on .NET 10 LTS instead of the latest STS release, but that choice records the support tradeoff and upgrade date; it is not represented as the latest release.

**Security and audit implications:** Only designated platform owners can approve framework exceptions; record risk acceptance, scope, compensating controls, and expiry.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** The chapter's point-in-time baseline is .NET 11 (latest supported on 2026-11-22 per available official documentation); exact patch and future versions are reconfirmed at release.

**Verification method:** Automate target/runtime inventory and verify it in release pipeline; inspect official source snapshot and exception record; test deployment health check.

# ASP.NET Core Backend Architecture and .NET Baseline

# ASP.NET Core backend architecture and current .NET baseline

## Scope and release baseline

This chapter specifies the backend architecture boundary for a multilingual, multi-tenant-capable commercial ERP. The baseline includes ASP.NET Core, EF Core with PostgreSQL, HTTP APIs used by a lightweight Next.js client, tenant isolation, extensibility, and operational safeguards. It does not define accounting, tax, invoicing, records-retention or sector law as universal rules. Those behaviors are explicitly assigned to configured jurisdiction, legal-entity or industry policy packs.

**Release baseline as of 2026-11-22:** Microsoft’s official support policy lists .NET 11, released 2026-11-10, as active STS with 11.0.0 listed as its patch on the policy page updated 2026-11-10. It also lists .NET 10 as active LTS. Therefore, because the requested baseline is the \*latest stable supported* .NET at the stated cutoff, this chapter targets .NET 11 / ASP.NET Core 11, not .NET 10 merely because .NET 10 is LTS. Microsoft distinguishes LTS and STS by support duration, not release quality, and requires the latest released patch to remain supported. Recheck the live Microsoft policy at implementation approval and every patch/release deployment; the listed version is a date-qualified baseline, not a future guarantee. \[1]

## Domain design

### Actors and permission boundaries

Actors are tenant users, tenant administrators, approvers, integration clients, platform operators, support staff, and background workers. Authentication establishes identity; authorization is separately evaluated using endpoint policies, stable permission codes, tenant membership and resource scope. Tenant administrators manage only their tenant. Platform support and deployment identities are distinct from customer-facing identities. Database runtime credentials are restricted to normal application data access; migration identities have separately controlled DDL rights. Cross-tenant operations are exceptional, reason-bearing and auditable. \[4] \[5] \[24]

### Core entities

The backend’s architectural entities include Tenant, TenantMembership, LegalEntity, UserPreference, PermissionAssignment, PolicyPack and its version/effective interval, WorkflowDefinition and version, ExtensionRegistration, business aggregates owned by modules, IdempotencyRecord, OutboxMessage, InboxMessage, AuditEvent, and an immutable concurrency/version token on editable records. Tenant-owned relational records use non-null tenant scope and database constraints for tenant-safe identity/reference relationships. Globally shared reference data is explicitly classified rather than inferred. \[7] \[8] \[11] \[12] \[13]

### Workflows

A request is normalized through trusted proxy handling, parsed into a bounded API contract, authenticated, assigned a validated tenant context and request culture, authorized for operation and resource, validated, and dispatched to a module use case. A business command executes database invariants and required writes transactionally; a concurrency conflict returns a recoverable conflict. When an integration event is needed, its outbox record commits with the business state, then a scoped dispatcher publishes it. Inbound events are verified and deduplicated in an inbox. Large files use bounded asynchronous jobs. Tenant provisioning and schema rollout are controlled lifecycle operations, not side effects of arbitrary user requests. \[2] \[12] \[13] \[20]

### Major architecture decisions

The backend is a modular monolith with explicit module contracts and ownership, avoiding premature distribution of cross-module transactions. ASP.NET Core owns domain operations and the system-of-record API; Next.js remains a thin localized UI/BFF and does not connect directly to PostgreSQL. PostgreSQL is the persistence baseline, but its major version and Npgsql/EF Core compatibility matrix must be selected and tested before production. Single-database discriminator tenancy is an available deployment option, not the only tenancy strategy: separate databases may be required by tenant scale, contractual isolation or residency. EF Core global filters provide safe defaults but are bypassable; optional PostgreSQL RLS provides a further boundary only when roles, pooled connection context and policies are configured correctly. Schema-per-tenant is not assumed to be a generally supported EF Core strategy. \[7] \[8] \[9] \[17]

The product target follows .NET 11 at the requested cutoff. Its STS support horizon is a deliberate release-management trade-off against the concurrently supported .NET 10 LTS line. Do not treat a major target-framework choice as permission to skip monthly servicing. PostgreSQL server version, Next.js package version, identity provider, message broker, hosting platform, data residency, disaster-recovery objectives, locale inventory and tenant deployment model remain release or deployment decisions unless selected by a product ADR. \[1] \[16]

### Dependencies and cross-module contracts

The ASP.NET Core host owns middleware order, authentication, authorization, API versioning, OpenAPI, request culture, error mapping, rate limits, telemetry and health endpoints. Modules expose application contracts, permission metadata, localization resources, migrations and extension capabilities. Shared contracts carry stable IDs, error codes, API/event versions, tenant ID, correlation ID, actor context and (where needed) locale tags. Database contracts own constraints, transaction boundaries and concurrency tokens. The UI consumes stable API identifiers and localized labels; integrations consume language-neutral codes. Outbox/inbox contracts provide durable asynchronous boundaries without claiming exactly-once delivery. Policy-pack contracts carry jurisdiction, owner, version and effective period. \[5] \[11] \[12] \[15] \[21]

### Risks and configuration boundary

The principal risks are tenant-context confusion, query-filter bypass, unsafe cross-tenant support, inconsistent provider/version upgrades, overly broad database roles, duplicated domain logic in Next.js, retries that repeat non-idempotent writes, locale mistaken for jurisdiction, and unreviewed custom extensions. The design mitigates these with default-deny authorization, tenant-bound keys/queries, optional RLS, transactional outbox/inbox, controlled migrations, typed options, stable contracts and testable extension interfaces. No universal fiscal, privacy, retention, invoice, or industry compliance claim is made here: choose jurisdiction-specific policy and retention rules with the responsible product, customer and legal owners. NIST SP 800-53 is a flexible control catalog, not a substitute for determining applicable law or the organization’s risk baseline. \[8] \[9] \[14] \[20] \[24]

### Verification model

Acceptance criteria below are normative and intended to become automated architecture, API, security, persistence, localization and deployment tests. Execute PostgreSQL tests using the same role/grants as the deployed application, not only an owner account. Test at least two tenants concurrently, multiple supported locales, and a cross-tenant denial case. Run the full suite against each declared PostgreSQL compatibility target and supported runtime patch. Treat tenant policy, legal entity, locale and extension matrices as configurable test fixtures.

## ASP.NET Core Backend Architecture and .NET Baseline — requirement cards

**REQUIREMENT 0631 OF 1120  |  ASP.NET CORE BACKEND ARCHITECTURE AND .NET BASELINE**

## ERP-DOTNET-001 — Target the current stable .NET baseline

**Normative requirement:** The backend shall target the latest stable, supported .NET release verified from Microsoft’s lifecycle policy at the release-baseline approval date; for 2026-11-22 this is .NET 11 (ASP.NET Core 11), not a preview build.

**Rationale:** Microsoft lists .NET 11 as released 2026-11-10, active STS, with 11.0.0 as its listed patch on that date. This is the latest stable supported release at the requested cutoff; the shorter STS horizon versus .NET 10 LTS is a conscious product decision.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** CI build metadata reports TargetFramework net11.0 for every production backend project.

**AC 2.** A release gate fails if the selected SDK/runtime is marked preview or out of support by the approved lifecycle manifest.

**AC 3.** The architecture decision record records the verification date, support track, current patch and end-of-support date.

**Exception / edge case:** A vendor may publish a later patch after the cutoff; the deployment pipeline must take the current supported patch rather than freeze 11.0.0.

**Security and audit implications:** Patch releases are mandatory security maintenance; the build must reject preview or end-of-support runtimes. Record the approved runtime image digest.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Runtime globalization data must be available for every enabled language; test framework globalization mode against deployed images.

**Verification method:** Inspect project files, the generated release manifest and a CI negative test using a preview SDK.

**Source references:**

1

**REQUIREMENT 0632 OF 1120  |  ASP.NET CORE BACKEND ARCHITECTURE AND .NET BASELINE**

## ERP-DOTNET-002 — Pin the SDK used to build

**Normative requirement:** The backend repository shall pin an approved .NET SDK feature band and roll-forward behavior in a checked-in global.json, while targeting the selected runtime independently.

**Rationale:** An explicit SDK pin makes local, CI and release builds reproducible without conflating SDK choice with runtime support.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** global.json exists and specifies an approved SDK version and rollForward value.

**AC 2.** CI using the pinned SDK builds and tests all backend projects from a clean checkout.

**AC 3.** A CI job with only an unapproved SDK installed fails with a clear SDK-resolution error.

**Exception / edge case:** Security patching may require an in-band SDK upgrade; change the pin through a reviewed dependency update rather than bypassing it.

**Security and audit implications:** Restrict SDK changes to reviewed commits and retain CI provenance for released binaries.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** SDK pinning does not constrain supported CultureInfo data; locale conformance tests run on the deployed runtime image.

**Verification method:** Run dotnet --version from a clean CI agent and verify a failing test for an incompatible SDK.

**Source references:**

1

**REQUIREMENT 0633 OF 1120  |  ASP.NET CORE BACKEND ARCHITECTURE AND .NET BASELINE**

## ERP-DOTNET-003 — Maintain supported runtime patches

**Normative requirement:** The service shall run only currently supported servicing patches for its chosen .NET major and shall deploy a tested patch update no later than the organization’s vulnerability-remediation SLA.

**Rationale:** Microsoft requires systems to remain current on released patch updates to qualify for support; patching is an operational control, not a one-time version selection.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A scheduled CI job compares the deployed runtime version with the approved Microsoft release manifest.

**AC 2.** A release cannot proceed when its runtime patch is below the current approved patch or outside a documented emergency exception.

**AC 3.** A monthly patch test exercises login, tenant isolation and database write smoke tests before promotion.

**Exception / edge case:** A critical incompatibility can temporarily block rollout; a time-bounded risk exception must identify owner, compensating controls and expiry.

**Security and audit implications:** Track vulnerable runtime components and image digests; retain exception approvals and deployment timestamps.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Run localization smoke tests on every runtime upgrade because globalization behavior depends on runtime data.

**Verification method:** Inspect release automation and simulate a stale runtime manifest in CI.

**Source references:**

1

**REQUIREMENT 0634 OF 1120  |  ASP.NET CORE BACKEND ARCHITECTURE AND .NET BASELINE**

## ERP-DOTNET-004 — Centralize and lock package versions

**Normative requirement:** Backend projects shall centrally pin direct NuGet package versions, including the PostgreSQL EF Core provider, to compatible non-preview versions and shall commit dependency lock files for production restore.

**Rationale:** Independent package versions can drift across the ASP.NET Core, EF Core and Npgsql provider compatibility boundaries.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Directory.Packages.props defines reviewed direct package versions and production projects do not contain floating versions.

**AC 2.** Restore uses locked mode in CI and fails after an uncommitted dependency change.

**AC 3.** A compatibility test restores and migrates a disposable PostgreSQL database using the pinned EF Core/Npgsql pair.

**Exception / edge case:** An upstream zero-day may require emergency override; the change still records tested compatibility and approval.

**Security and audit implications:** Enable dependency vulnerability scanning; prohibit unreviewed package-source overrides and secret-bearing package credentials.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Provider and package selection must not strip Unicode support; run multilingual database round trips on upgrades.

**Verification method:** Inspect package manifests and execute locked restore plus provider integration tests.

**Source references:**

1

7

14

**REQUIREMENT 0635 OF 1120  |  ASP.NET CORE BACKEND ARCHITECTURE AND .NET BASELINE**

## ERP-DOTNET-005 — Produce reproducible and traceable releases

**Normative requirement:** The build pipeline shall produce an immutable release artifact with source revision, SDK/runtime version, dependency inventory and artifact digest.

**Rationale:** Enterprise operators need to know exactly which compiled code and dependencies are deployed and to reproduce or roll back that artifact.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Two clean builds from the same commit produce the same normalized artifact digest, or documented nondeterministic files are excluded from comparison.

**AC 2.** The release manifest contains commit SHA, SDK, target framework, resolved package inventory and container digest.

**AC 3.** The deployed artifact digest matches the signed promotion record.

**Exception / edge case:** A hosted compiler may introduce unavoidable nondeterminism; the pipeline records the difference and still verifies source and artifact provenance.

**Security and audit implications:** Sign artifacts and restrict release promotion; never include secrets, customer data or localized production resources in build logs.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Record locale resource bundle versions in the artifact manifest so translation changes are attributable.

**Verification method:** Rebuild the same commit in isolated agents, compare artifacts and inspect provenance attestations.

**Source references:**

1

24

**REQUIREMENT 0636 OF 1120  |  ASP.NET CORE BACKEND ARCHITECTURE AND .NET BASELINE**

## ERP-DOTNET-006 — Validate configuration at startup

**Normative requirement:** The service shall bind configuration into typed options and fail readiness or startup when required settings are absent, malformed, unsafe or inconsistent.

**Rationale:** Fail-fast configuration prevents serving requests under silently incomplete security, database or tenant-routing settings.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A test with a missing database endpoint prevents host readiness.

**AC 2.** A test with an unsupported default locale or invalid tenant mode fails options validation.

**AC 3.** Production startup rejects development-only placeholders and wildcard CORS origins when credentials are enabled.

**Exception / edge case:** Optional integration configuration may be absent when that integration is disabled; its endpoint must then be unavailable rather than partially active.

**Security and audit implications:** Configuration validation must redact secret values in exceptions and logs; record setting key and failure category only.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Validate configured locale tags against the enabled-locale registry and reject unknown values instead of silently changing accounting culture.

**Verification method:** Run host-start integration tests with valid, missing and malformed option sets.

**Source references:**

4

15

**REQUIREMENT 0637 OF 1120  |  ASP.NET CORE BACKEND ARCHITECTURE AND .NET BASELINE**

## ERP-DOTNET-007 — Enforce dependency-injection lifetime safety

**Normative requirement:** The application shall validate dependency-injection scopes in development and tests and shall not capture request-scoped tenant, user or DbContext services inside singletons.

**Rationale:** A singleton that captures request-scoped context can leak tenant/user state across concurrent requests.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Development and integration hosts enable scope validation and have zero lifetime violations.

**AC 2.** A concurrency test with two tenants proves singleton services return no tenant-specific cached state.

**AC 3.** Hosted services create and dispose an explicit DI scope for each unit of tenant work.

**Exception / edge case:** A process-wide immutable lookup or stateless singleton is permitted after thread-safety review and contains no request-bound data.

**Security and audit implications:** Treat scope violations as potential cross-tenant disclosure; include a regression test for any singleton cache or hosted consumer.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Request culture must be read from a request scope or passed explicitly, never stored as mutable singleton state.

**Verification method:** Run container validation and a parallel tenant isolation test with scope validation enabled.

**Source references:**

3

7

**REQUIREMENT 0638 OF 1120  |  ASP.NET CORE BACKEND ARCHITECTURE AND .NET BASELINE**

## ERP-DOTNET-008 — Organize the backend as a modular monolith

**Normative requirement:** The backend shall deploy as a modular monolith initially, with domain modules separated by explicit application contracts and owned persistence boundaries; module code shall not depend on another module’s internal persistence types.

**Rationale:** A commercial ERP needs consistent business transactions and extension points; bounded modules preserve changeability without premature distributed-system costs.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Architecture tests reject references from a module to another module’s Infrastructure namespace.

**AC 2.** Each module exposes only approved application contracts and owns its EF configurations/migrations.

**AC 3.** A cross-module workflow test verifies orchestration uses the public contract rather than direct table mutation.

**Exception / edge case:** A documented reporting projection may read a shared read model; it may not bypass write ownership or authorization.

**Security and audit implications:** Define a module owner for sensitive data and audit cross-boundary writes through the public use case.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Modules must use shared locale/formatting abstractions while retaining industry-specific terminology resources.

**Verification method:** Run architecture dependency tests and review the module contract inventory.

**Source references:**

4

**REQUIREMENT 0639 OF 1120  |  ASP.NET CORE BACKEND ARCHITECTURE AND .NET BASELINE**

## ERP-DOTNET-009 — Keep Next.js a thin client/BFF

**Normative requirement:** The Next.js frontend shall render and adapt user interaction but shall not become the authoritative ERP domain service or connect directly to PostgreSQL; backend domain mutations shall pass through authenticated ASP.NET Core APIs.

**Rationale:** Next.js documents its BFF capability as an API layer rather than a full backend replacement; a clear authority prevents duplicated rules and database credentials in the frontend.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** The frontend build contains no PostgreSQL driver or production database secret.

**AC 2.** A business mutation invoked through Next.js reaches a versioned ASP.NET Core endpoint and returns its domain outcome.

**AC 3.** Any BFF route has an allow-listed upstream path, validates input and does not forward arbitrary caller headers or credentials.

**Exception / edge case:** A narrowly scoped BFF may transform payloads or manage a session; it must not independently decide ERP posting, approval or tenant ownership.

**Security and audit implications:** Keep bearer/access credentials server-side, prevent open-proxy behavior and apply CSRF protections to cookie-authenticated mutations.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** The route locale may shape UI text, but culture-sensitive calculations and authoritative localized labels are resolved through backend contracts.

**Verification method:** Inspect dependency graph and secrets scan; integration-test an unauthorized and an allowed proxied call.

**Source references:**

17

16

**REQUIREMENT 0640 OF 1120  |  ASP.NET CORE BACKEND ARCHITECTURE AND .NET BASELINE**

## ERP-DOTNET-010 — Order the HTTP middleware pipeline explicitly

**Normative requirement:** The application shall define and test middleware ordering so trusted proxy normalization and exception handling precede routing-dependent authentication, authorization and endpoint execution.

**Rationale:** Middleware executes in sequence; incorrect ordering can bypass security or misinterpret scheme, host, route or error context.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A pipeline integration test confirms a protected endpoint returns 401/403 before its handler executes.

**AC 2.** An injected downstream exception is converted to the configured safe error response by the exception boundary.

**AC 3.** Forwarded-proto is normalized before HTTPS redirection and authentication redirect construction.

**Exception / edge case:** Health probes may use a separately mapped endpoint and policy; they remain subject to the explicit probe exposure rule.

**Security and audit implications:** The middleware order test is a security control; never expose developer exception pages outside local development.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Exception middleware emits the selected request culture’s public message only after stable error classification.

**Verification method:** Use ASP.NET Core TestServer integration tests plus startup source/endpoint metadata checks.

**Source references:**

2

4

19

**REQUIREMENT 0641 OF 1120  |  ASP.NET CORE BACKEND ARCHITECTURE AND .NET BASELINE**

## ERP-DOTNET-011 — Publish and validate an OpenAPI contract

**Normative requirement:** The API shall generate an OpenAPI document from ASP.NET Core endpoint metadata and validate the document as a CI artifact for every supported API version.

**Rationale:** A machine-readable contract lets Next.js, integration partners and localization tooling implement and test against stable request/response shapes.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** CI emits a syntactically valid OpenAPI document for every released version.

**AC 2.** A breaking-change diff against the prior released document fails CI unless an approved version transition is declared.

**AC 3.** The production API document contains no internal hostnames, secret examples or development-only endpoints.

**Exception / edge case:** If the schema itself is access-restricted, an authenticated contract artifact remains available to authorized client teams.

**Security and audit implications:** Do not disclose internal route inventory in an unauthenticated production endpoint; CI artifact access follows code-release permissions.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Document error codes and language-neutral field names; mark which returned text fields are localized.

**Verification method:** Generate the document, validate it with an OpenAPI validator and run a breaking-change comparison.

**Source references:**

## ERP-DOTNET-012 — Version public API contracts compatibly

**Normative requirement:** The backend shall expose an explicit API major version in its route or media contract and shall preserve the documented response semantics for that version until the published deprecation window ends.

**Rationale:** ERP integrations often outlive frontend release cycles; explicit versioning isolates planned breaking changes.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Every public business route has an explicit major API version.

**AC 2.** A contract test verifies an existing version’s required fields and status codes across a release.

**AC 3.** A breaking contract change is rejected unless a new major version and migration notice are present.

**Exception / edge case:** Additive optional fields may be released within a version only if clients are contract-tested to ignore unknown properties.

**Security and audit implications:** Authorization requirements remain enforced identically across all supported API versions; log version use for retirement impact analysis.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Do not encode user-facing translated wording into versioned enum values; use stable machine codes and optional localized display text.

**Verification method:** Run API snapshot tests against the last production contract and a deliberately breaking change.

21

**REQUIREMENT 0643 OF 1120  |  ASP.NET CORE BACKEND ARCHITECTURE AND .NET BASELINE**

## ERP-DOTNET-013 — Return standardized safe error envelopes

**Normative requirement:** The API shall return RFC-compatible Problem Details for unhandled and validation failures, including a stable application error code and correlation identifier while excluding stack traces and secrets.

**Rationale:** Consistent failures simplify client handling, support diagnostics and avoid exposing implementation internals.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Malformed requests produce a 4xx Problem Details JSON response with stable \`type` or extension code.

**AC 2.** Unhandled exceptions produce a 5xx response without stack, SQL, connection string or internal exception text.

**AC 3.** Each response correlation identifier is present in the matching server log event.

**Exception / edge case:** A streaming response that has already started cannot be replaced by a new error envelope; the server shall terminate the stream and log the original failure.

**Security and audit implications:** Sanitize errors against PII and injection; avoid including tenant names or database identifiers in client payloads.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Return a stable code plus a localized human detail selected for the request, with a language-neutral fallback.

**Verification method:** Use API integration tests for validation, exception and already-started-stream behavior.

## ERP-DOTNET-014 — Validate requests at the API boundary

**Normative requirement:** The API shall validate syntactic constraints and required field invariants before invoking application commands, then enforce business invariants again at the domain/application layer.

**Rationale:** Boundary validation gives deterministic feedback while domain checks protect invariants from non-HTTP entry points such as jobs and integrations.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Invalid enum, identifier, range and required-field inputs return 400 with field-level error codes.

**AC 2.** A command invoked from a background worker rejects the same invalid domain transition as the HTTP path.

**AC 3.** The invalid-request test confirms no database write or domain event is emitted.

**Exception / edge case:** A cross-record condition that can change concurrently is enforced transactionally in the database/application operation, not only by a prior validator.

**Security and audit implications:** Validation responses never echo secret or sensitive submitted values; invalid authorization is not disguised as successful mutation.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Validation metadata uses resource keys and parameterized arguments so labels and messages can be localized without changing field identifiers.

**Verification method:** Run API tests, command-handler unit tests and a no-write database assertion for invalid payloads.

## ERP-DOTNET-015 — Bound request and response sizes

**Normative requirement:** The service shall enforce configurable maximum request sizes, upload quotas and bounded response/page sizes per endpoint class before buffering untrusted payloads.

**Rationale:** Unbounded bodies and collections create memory exhaustion and denial-of-service risk, particularly for enterprise bulk operations.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** An oversized JSON request receives 413 before command execution.

**AC 2.** An upload exceeding its configured per-file or per-tenant quota is rejected without retaining a partial final artifact.

**AC 3.** Collection endpoints reject page sizes above the configured maximum and never serialize more than that maximum.

**Exception / edge case:** Approved large import/export flows may stream to bounded temporary storage and use asynchronous processing rather than raising global limits.

**Security and audit implications:** Limits are enforced before expensive parsing, are tenant-aware, and create a rate-limit/quota event without storing body contents.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Localized validation text must report byte/file limits in culture-neutral units or appropriately localized units without changing actual enforcement.

**Verification method:** Use load tests with boundary and over-limit payloads plus storage cleanup verification.

## ERP-DOTNET-016 — Make retried business commands idempotent

**Normative requirement:** For externally retriable create/post commands, the API shall accept an idempotency key scoped to tenant, authenticated client and operation, and persist the completed outcome atomically with the business change.

**Rationale:** Network retries and uncertain commit results can otherwise create duplicate ERP documents or side effects.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Two identical requests with the same key and payload create one business record and return the same outcome.

**AC 2.** Reusing a key with a different normalized payload returns 409 and creates no second effect.

**AC 3.** The uniqueness constraint includes tenant, client and operation and concurrent duplicate requests are serialized.

**Exception / edge case:** Idempotency records expire only under an explicit retention policy; a key outside retention is treated as a new request and the documented expiry is returned to clients.

**Security and audit implications:** Keys are unguessable, not treated as authentication, and stored without unnecessary raw sensitive payload; audit conflicting-key reuse.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Localized display text may differ across retries, but machine outcome code and business resource ID remain stable.

**Verification method:** Run concurrent integration tests with lost-response simulation and verify one committed effect.

## ERP-DOTNET-017 — Paginate all unbounded list APIs

**Normative requirement:** List endpoints shall require or default to bounded pagination and apply deterministic ordering with a unique tie-breaker.

**Rationale:** Bounded queries avoid unbounded memory and latency; stable ordering prevents skipped or duplicated records between pages.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** An omitted page parameter returns no more than the documented default maximum.

**AC 2.** An oversized page size is clamped or rejected consistently and is never passed unbounded to the database.

**AC 3.** Repeated-page tests with duplicate sort values return no duplicates or omissions using the documented cursor/sort key.

**Exception / edge case:** A small fixed reference list may be returned without pagination only if its maximum cardinality is enforced by schema and test.

**Security and audit implications:** Tenant and row-level authorization filters run before pagination; totals or cursors must not disclose inaccessible rows.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Sort by stable stored keys rather than localized display strings unless a locale-specific collation is explicitly part of the contract.

**Verification method:** Run database integration tests with equal sort values, tenant boundaries and page-size edges.

## ERP-DOTNET-018 — Propagate cancellation through asynchronous operations

**Normative requirement:** Every request-bound asynchronous operation shall pass the ASP.NET Core cancellation token through database, file and outbound HTTP calls and shall not convert client cancellation into a successful commit response.

**Rationale:** Cancellation limits wasted work when clients disconnect or host shutdown begins and helps preserve capacity.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A canceled request token reaches repository and outbound-client test doubles.

**AC 2.** A client disconnect during a long query stops database work within the configured cancellation window.

**AC 3.** Cancellation before transaction commit leaves no partial business aggregate or emitted outbox message.

**Exception / edge case:** After a durable commit, cancellation while formatting a response does not roll back the committed fact; the idempotency key permits safe outcome recovery.

**Security and audit implications:** Log cancellation as a distinct event without treating user cancellation as a security failure; avoid logging request bodies.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Cancellation messages are not user-facing translated domain errors; any resulting status follows the documented transport behavior.

**Verification method:** Use cancellation-aware integration tests and a mock handler/database command interceptor.

## ERP-DOTNET-019 — Trust forwarded headers only from configured proxies

**Normative requirement:** The service shall process only the configured forwarded headers, from explicit known proxy addresses or networks, with a bounded forward limit and before scheme/host-dependent middleware.

**Rationale:** Untrusted forwarded headers permit spoofing of client identity, host and HTTPS status.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A request from an untrusted remote address cannot change effective scheme, host or client IP through X-Forwarded headers.

**AC 2.** A request from a configured proxy applies only the documented forwarded fields and number of hops.

**AC 3.** A proxy misconfiguration is visible in structured diagnostics and does not cause wildcard trust.

**Exception / edge case:** A managed ingress with changing addresses requires an authenticated or network-controlled trust mechanism, not acceptance of all sources.

**Security and audit implications:** Use the normalized client IP only after proxy trust for security policies; record original/normalized values under approved retention.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Host/domain-based locale resolution is applied only to a validated host, with unknown hostnames rejected.

**Verification method:** Run reverse-proxy integration tests for trusted, untrusted, multiple-hop and spoofed-host cases.

## ERP-DOTNET-020 — Enforce secure transport and explicit CORS

**Normative requirement:** Public API traffic shall use HTTPS, and browser cross-origin access shall be limited to configured tenant-independent or tenant-approved origins, methods and headers.

**Rationale:** Transport confidentiality and narrow browser origins protect tokens, ERP content and mutation endpoints.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Production HTTP requests are redirected or rejected before business endpoint execution.

**AC 2.** CORS preflight for an unlisted origin receives no allow-origin permission.

**AC 3.** Credentialed CORS configuration rejects wildcard origin and allows only documented methods and headers.

**Exception / edge case:** A private service-to-service endpoint may terminate TLS at a trusted ingress only when the ingress-to-service link is also protected according to deployment policy.

**Security and audit implications:** HSTS is enabled at the public HTTPS boundary; CORS is not considered authentication or tenant authorization.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** CORS does not select a culture; browser language negotiation remains independent from origin policy.

**Verification method:** Run TLS configuration checks and automated allowed/disallowed preflight tests.
