## ERP-DOTNET-021 — Use federated authentication for workforce users

**Normative requirement:** Interactive workforce users shall authenticate through configured OpenID Connect/OAuth 2.0 identity providers using authorization-code flow with PKCE where applicable; the ERP shall not collect the IdP password.

**Rationale:** Federation supports enterprise identity lifecycle, MFA and SSO without making the ERP a password authority.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A valid configured issuer, audience and signature yields an authenticated principal.

**AC 2.** Invalid issuer, expired token, wrong audience and replayed state are rejected.

**AC 3.** A user disabled at the configured identity source cannot start a new ERP session after the configured revocation propagation window.

**Exception / edge case:** A tenant may use a separately approved identity provider; local break-glass access is isolated, time-limited and audited.

**Security and audit implications:** Validate issuer, audience, signature, nonce/state and redirect URI; do not accept identity headers from untrusted callers.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Provider display names may be localized, but stable subject/issuer identifiers remain locale-neutral.

**Verification method:** Run OIDC protocol tests with valid and adversarial tokens and verify account disablement behavior.

## ERP-DOTNET-022 — Require authentication by default

**Normative requirement:** The API shall apply a fallback authorization policy requiring an authenticated principal to every endpoint unless an endpoint is explicitly allow-listed as public.

**Rationale:** Configuring authentication alone does not protect routes; a default-deny endpoint posture prevents newly added routes from being accidentally anonymous.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** An endpoint with no explicit metadata returns 401 for an anonymous request.

**AC 2.** Only the enumerated health/readiness or discovery routes are anonymous, and each has a test asserting no business data is returned.

**AC 3.** A source or endpoint-metadata test fails when a new public route is added without an explicit exception.

**Exception / edge case:** An externally delivered signed webhook may be unauthenticated at the user-session layer only if its signature, timestamp and replay controls are independently verified.

**Security and audit implications:** Anonymous exceptions are code-reviewed and monitored; authenticated endpoints still require authorization.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Authentication failure text uses generic localized wording and does not disclose whether an account exists.

**Verification method:** Execute route enumeration tests and an anonymous endpoint security scan.

## ERP-DOTNET-023 — Authorize actions with named policies and permissions

**Normative requirement:** Every non-public operation shall require a named authorization policy tied to a stable permission or capability rather than relying solely on broad role names.

**Rationale:** Policy-based authorization keeps business actions explicit and allows permission assignment to be configured per tenant.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Each mutating route declares a named policy and its permission requirement.

**AC 2.** A principal lacking the permission receives 403 and the command handler is not invoked.

**AC 3.** Changing an assigned permission takes effect within the documented cache/revocation window.

**Exception / edge case:** A system-level health probe uses a dedicated service identity policy and does not inherit user business permissions.

**Security and audit implications:** Use least privilege; audit permission changes with actor, target user, tenant, before/after values and timestamp.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Permission names and codes remain stable identifiers; translate labels and descriptions in the UI, not claim values.

**Verification method:** Inspect endpoint metadata and run authorization matrix tests for allow/deny cases.

## ERP-DOTNET-024 — Authorize access to each resource

**Normative requirement:** The application shall perform resource-based authorization after loading a resource under the tenant boundary and before exposing or modifying it.

**Rationale:** Endpoint-level permission alone cannot prevent access to another organizational unit, legal entity or record owned by a different user.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** An allowed user can retrieve a resource within assigned scope.

**AC 2.** A user with the same permission but an out-of-scope resource receives 404 or 403 according to the published disclosure policy.

**AC 3.** The authorization handler covers update, delete, attachment download and export paths.

**Exception / edge case:** Resource creation checks the intended target scope before persistence because no persisted resource exists yet.

**Security and audit implications:** Do not rely on opaque identifiers as authorization; log denied resource actions with stable resource type/ID and no sensitive field values.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Resource names in denial messages are localized only after authorization; avoid leaking untranslated display fields on denied requests.

**Verification method:** Run an authorization matrix with same-tenant and cross-scope test principals.

## ERP-DOTNET-025 — Enforce separation of duties on configured approvals

**Normative requirement:** Configurable approval workflows shall support a rule preventing an initiator from approving their own sensitive transaction when the tenant enables that control.

**Rationale:** ERP organizations commonly need maker-checker controls, but exact approval rules vary by industry and jurisdiction and must remain configurable.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** With self-approval disabled, the initiator’s approval attempt is denied and the transaction remains pending.

**AC 2.** An eligible distinct approver can approve and the state transition is recorded once.

**AC 3.** With the tenant rule explicitly configured to permit self-approval for a workflow, that exception is effective and auditable.

**Exception / edge case:** Emergency override requires a separate permission, reason code and audit event; it cannot erase the original initiator or approver identity.

**Security and audit implications:** Record actor, approver, policy version, decision, timestamp and override reason in a tamper-evident audit trail.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Workflow labels and rejection reasons are translated, while state and reason codes are stable machine values.

**Verification method:** Run workflow state-machine tests for self-approval, distinct approval and override scenarios.

## ERP-DOTNET-026 — Authenticate service-to-service callers

**Normative requirement:** Machine clients shall use scoped client credentials, workload identity or mutually authenticated transport approved for the deployment; long-lived shared user passwords shall not be used.

**Rationale:** Integrations need a revocable non-human identity with explicit tenant and operation scope.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 2.** An expired, untrusted or wrong-audience token is rejected.

**AC 3.** Credential rotation can overlap old and new credentials for a bounded interval without making credentials public.

**Exception / edge case:** A legacy partner lacking OAuth support may use a separate adapter with a uniquely issued, revocable credential and compensating network controls.

## ERP-DOTNET-027 — Protect browser sessions and state-changing requests

**Normative requirement:** If the frontend uses cookies for authentication, the application shall use Secure, HttpOnly and appropriate SameSite cookies and require anti-forgery protection for state-changing browser requests.

**Rationale:** Cookie-based sessions are automatically attached by browsers; CSRF defenses are required to prevent cross-site mutations.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Production session cookies include Secure and HttpOnly and the configured SameSite value.

**AC 2.** A cross-site POST without a valid anti-forgery token is rejected before command execution.

**AC 3.** Logout and session expiration invalidate the server-side session or refresh capability within the configured window.

**Exception / edge case:** A bearer-token API call from a non-browser machine client does not use a CSRF token, but still verifies token audience and authorization.

**Security and audit implications:** Do not put access tokens in browser-readable persistent storage unless a reviewed threat model accepts that risk; log session revocation events.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Localized login/logout flows must preserve locale across redirects without accepting unvalidated return URLs.

**Verification method:** Run browser automation for cookie flags, CSRF rejection, logout and open-redirect attempts.

## ERP-DOTNET-028 — Persist a protected shared Data Protection key ring

**Normative requirement:** All ASP.NET Core instances that need to decrypt the same cookies or protected payloads shall share a persisted, access-controlled Data Protection key ring with a stable application name and encryption at rest.

**Rationale:** Ephemeral or per-instance keys break sessions and protected values after restart or load balancing; unencrypted keys raise disclosure risk.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Two application instances with the approved key-ring location can protect and unprotect a test payload.

**AC 2.** Restart and rolling deployment preserve valid session decryption for the configured key lifetime.

**AC 3.** A process without key-store permission fails safely and emits a diagnostic without exposing key material.

**Exception / edge case:** An isolated preview environment uses a distinct application name and key store so it cannot decrypt production cookies.

**Security and audit implications:** Restrict key-store access, encrypt keys with a managed key where supported, and record rotation/permission changes.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Key storage is independent of user culture; cookies must not be bound to a transient locale claim that blocks language preference changes.

**Verification method:** Run cross-instance and restart tests plus a key-store access-denial test.

## ERP-DOTNET-029 — Keep production secrets out of source and logs

**Normative requirement:** Production credentials, signing keys, connection strings and integration tokens shall be supplied at runtime through an approved secret-management mechanism and shall not be committed to source or logged.

**Rationale:** Configuration files, environment and build logs can leak credentials; secret management enables rotation and access control.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Repository secret scanning reports no active credential in tracked files or build artifacts.

**AC 2.** A production boot test retrieves secrets from the approved provider using workload identity.

**AC 3.** A secret rotation test activates the new value without code rebuild and invalidates the retired credential within the defined window.

**Exception / edge case:** Local development may use developer secret storage with synthetic credentials; production secrets are prohibited in developer/test environments.

**Security and audit implications:** Audit secret access/rotation and least-privilege grants; log only secret reference and operation outcome.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Secrets and provider error messages must not be passed into localization resource files or user-visible diagnostics.

## ERP-DOTNET-030 — Partition rate limits by tenant and caller

**Normative requirement:** The service shall enforce configurable request and concurrency limits partitioned by authenticated tenant/client and endpoint class, with an anonymous-source limit for unauthenticated traffic.

**Rationale:** Partitioning prevents one tenant or integration from exhausting shared capacity while protecting login and costly operations.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Exceeding a partition limit returns HTTP 429 with a machine-readable error and Retry-After when known.

**AC 2.** Load generated under tenant A does not consume tenant B’s full independent quota.

**AC 3.** Login, export, search and standard read routes apply separately configurable rate-limit policies.

**Exception / edge case:** Emergency service protection may apply a global limiter when shared infrastructure is saturated, and its activation is visible to operators.

**Security and audit implications:** Do not trust a caller-supplied tenant or raw API key as the limiter partition until identity is verified; bound partition cardinality to prevent memory exhaustion.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** 429 descriptions may be translated but the status, retry metadata and error code remain language-neutral.

**Verification method:** Run concurrent multi-tenant load tests and verify rejection metrics without recording secrets.

## ERP-DOTNET-031 — Resolve tenant only from a trusted identity mapping

**Normative requirement:** For authenticated business requests, the server shall resolve the active tenant from a verified principal membership or approved server-side domain mapping and shall not trust a body/header tenant ID alone.

**Rationale:** A client-controlled tenant identifier is not proof of membership and can create cross-customer data exposure.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A valid user with tenant A membership cannot access tenant B by changing route, body, query or custom header values.

**AC 2.** A tenant domain resolves only after host validation and maps to an active tenant the principal may enter.

**AC 3.** Unknown or suspended tenant resolution is rejected before DbContext construction.

**Exception / edge case:** A user belonging to multiple tenants may select one explicitly, but the selection is checked against current membership and logged.

**Security and audit implications:** Record selected tenant ID in scoped request context only after validation; never infer trust from a hidden form field or Next.js route.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Tenant names shown in selection UI are localized display data and are never used as the immutable tenant key.

## ERP-DOTNET-032 — Make tenant context immutable for each request

**Normative requirement:** The resolved tenant context shall be immutable for the lifetime of a request and shall be explicitly created for each background work item rather than inherited from ambient process state.

**Rationale:** Mutable or ambient tenant state can bleed between requests or be reused by pooled DbContexts and background workers.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Parallel requests for different tenants return only their respective seeded rows under stress.

**AC 2.** Attempting to switch a request tenant after resolution is rejected or creates a fresh explicitly authorized scope.

**AC 3.** Every background execution requires an explicit tenant ID and records it in execution context.

**Exception / edge case:** A global operations task may enumerate tenants only through a privileged scheduler contract that creates one tenant scope per iteration.

**Security and audit implications:** Tenant-context creation is logged as a security-relevant decision; never hold tenant state in static or singleton mutable fields.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Request culture may vary independently of tenant context; switching language must not switch tenant data.

## ERP-DOTNET-033 — Include tenant keys in relational identity boundaries

**Normative requirement:** Every tenant-owned relational row shall carry a non-null tenant identifier, and tenant-scoped alternate keys and foreign-key relationships shall include the tenant identifier where needed to prevent cross-tenant references.

**Rationale:** Database-enforced composite uniqueness and relationships reduce the chance that faulty application filters bind records across tenants.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Schema tests find no tenant-owned table lacking a non-null tenant ID or an approved documented exception.

**AC 2.** Unique business identifiers are unique per tenant using a composite unique constraint or equivalent tenant-scoped index.

**AC 3.** A foreign-key integration test cannot associate a tenant-A child row with a tenant-B parent row.

## ERP-DOTNET-034 — Apply tenant filters to all tenant-owned queries

**Normative requirement:** The data layer shall apply a tenant predicate by default to each tenant-owned EF Core entity and shall require explicit privileged authorization for any query that disables the filter.

**Rationale:** Global filters provide safe default query behavior but are bypassable and therefore are not sufficient alone as the sole authorization mechanism.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 2.** A query using Include/required navigation is tested to ensure filters do not silently omit or expose dependent records.

**AC 3.** Calls to IgnoreQueryFilters are limited to reviewed administrative data-access methods.

**Exception / edge case:** Migrations, backup and global analytics use dedicated paths with explicit cross-tenant authorization and separately tested scopes.

## ERP-DOTNET-035 — Use PostgreSQL row security as optional defense in depth

**Normative requirement:** Where the selected single-database tenancy threat model requires database-enforced row isolation, the deployment shall enable PostgreSQL RLS policies for tenant-owned tables and shall set tenant context transaction-locally for each operation.

**Rationale:** PostgreSQL RLS defaults to deny when enabled without an applicable policy, but table owners and BYPASSRLS roles can bypass it; configuration must account for those exceptions.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Application-role queries with tenant A context cannot select, insert, update or delete tenant B rows.

**AC 2.** A connection reused from the pool cannot retain tenant A context when subsequently serving tenant B.

**AC 3.** The runtime role is neither superuser nor BYPASSRLS and is not the table owner; policy migration tests verify FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY where chosen.

**Exception / edge case:** RLS may be omitted for database-per-tenant deployment or a documented provider limitation; application-level isolation controls remain mandatory.

**Security and audit implications:** Connection context is set transaction-locally and cleared by transaction completion; administrative bypass uses a separate audited role.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** RLS does not depend on locale; database error diagnostics must not expose another tenant’s row values.

**Verification method:** Run PostgreSQL integration tests with the actual runtime role, pooled connections and explicit administrative role.

## ERP-DOTNET-036 — Constrain and audit cross-tenant administration

**Normative requirement:** Cross-tenant support and platform administration shall use a separate permission and explicit reason-bearing operation rather than silently disabling tenant restrictions in ordinary user flows.

**Rationale:** Support staff need controlled diagnostics, but unrestricted impersonation creates a high-impact breach path.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A tenant administrator cannot call a platform-wide query endpoint.

**AC 2.** A platform support action requires privileged authorization plus a reason and records actor, target tenant, resource and time.

**AC 3.** A support session expires after its configured duration and the next request is denied.

**Exception / edge case:** Emergency security response may use a break-glass identity with dual approval or incident reference, then require a post-use review.

**Security and audit implications:** Separate ordinary and support credentials; alert on cross-tenant access and prohibit bulk export through generic support scopes.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Support context uses the target user’s display culture only when needed, without impersonating their immutable subject identity.

## ERP-DOTNET-037 — Provision tenants through versioned lifecycle operations

**Normative requirement:** Tenant creation, suspension, data placement and schema onboarding shall be executed through an idempotent lifecycle workflow that records its stage and schema version.

**Rationale:** Enterprise tenants may use different data placement while requiring repeatable onboarding and recoverable partial provisioning.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Repeating the same provisioning request does not create duplicate tenant, database or baseline rows.

**AC 2.** A failure after each provisioning stage can resume or roll back without exposing an active half-provisioned tenant.

**AC 3.** A suspended tenant cannot authenticate into business APIs or enqueue ordinary tenant jobs.

**Exception / edge case:** Migration maintenance windows may temporarily block writes while read access is retained only if explicitly approved and tested.

**Security and audit implications:** Onboarding credentials are short-lived; database/database-placement records and tenant status changes are audited.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Seed tenant defaults include an explicit default locale and enabled locale set without assuming one country’s legal regime.

**Verification method:** Fault-inject each lifecycle stage and verify idempotent recovery and access denial while suspended.

## ERP-DOTNET-038 — Model jurisdiction and industry rules as configuration boundaries

**Normative requirement:** The platform shall expose jurisdiction-specific, industry-specific and legal-entity policies through versioned configuration or plug-in contracts and shall not hard-code one jurisdiction’s regulatory rule as universal ERP behavior.

**Rationale:** Tax, retention, invoice, accounting and sector obligations vary; the platform baseline cannot invent a universal legal rule.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A tenant can select a configured jurisdiction/industry profile without changing shared backend code.

**AC 2.** A policy configuration records its effective dates, version, owner and provenance.

**AC 3.** An unconfigured or expired mandatory policy blocks the dependent operation with an explicit configuration error rather than guessing a default.

**Exception / edge case:** A tenant’s contractual or statutory policy may require a custom implementation; it must satisfy the same extension contract and security review.

**Security and audit implications:** Policy changes are approved and audited; effective-date changes must not silently rewrite previously posted facts.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Policy labels and explanation text are localized; rule identifiers and stored source/effective dates remain stable.

**Verification method:** Run contract tests with two contrasting tenant policy profiles and a missing/expired policy.

## ERP-DOTNET-039 — Pin the PostgreSQL compatibility matrix

**Normative requirement:** The service shall publish and test an explicit PostgreSQL major-version and Npgsql/EF Core provider compatibility matrix before production deployment.

**Rationale:** The requirement names PostgreSQL but not a major version; \`current` documentation changes, and provider-specific behavior cannot be assumed without a tested matrix.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** CI provisions every PostgreSQL major in the declared support matrix and runs migrations plus persistence integration tests.

**AC 2.** Release metadata identifies the tested PostgreSQL server and Npgsql provider versions.

**AC 3.** A server major outside the supported matrix is rejected by deployment preflight or marked unsupported.

**Exception / edge case:** A managed database service may report a vendor-specific compatible version; it is accepted only after the same acceptance suite passes.

**Security and audit implications:** Use TLS and least-privilege roles per deployment; database version support end dates feed the vulnerability lifecycle process.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Run Unicode, collation, numeric and timezone persistence tests under every declared locale-independent provider target.

## ERP-DOTNET-040 — Scope DbContext per unit of work

**Normative requirement:** The backend shall create a short-lived EF Core DbContext per request or explicit job unit of work and shall not share one context concurrently across requests or threads.

**Rationale:** DbContext is a stateful unit-of-work object; safe lifetimes support concurrency and prevent cross-request state retention.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Concurrent endpoint operations receive distinct DbContext instances.

**AC 2.** A context is disposed after request/job completion, including exception and cancellation paths.

**AC 3.** A test attempting parallel operations on one context is rejected by architecture or code review/test policy.

**Exception / edge case:** A deliberately batched command may use one context for its single serial transaction, but must not capture it beyond that operation.

**Security and audit implications:** Context change tracking can retain sensitive entities; dispose promptly and do not write entity contents into diagnostics.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Culture and tenant values are immutable context inputs for the operation, not mutable global settings.

**Verification method:** Use DI scope tests and an EF interceptor to assert context creation/disposal per work unit.

## ERP-DOTNET-041 — Define atomic transaction boundaries for business commands

**Normative requirement:** Each multi-row business command that must succeed or fail as a unit shall execute all database writes and state transitions in a single PostgreSQL transaction.

**Rationale:** EF Core SaveChanges is transactional for providers that support it, but multi-save operations need an explicit transaction boundary.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A fault injected after the first write leaves no partial aggregate after rollback.

**AC 2.** The transaction includes all same-database rows needed for the command’s invariant.

**AC 3.** Transaction duration remains below its configured maximum under the tested workload.

**Exception / edge case:** External side effects cannot join a PostgreSQL transaction; they must be emitted through the transactional outbox rather than called before commit.

**Security and audit implications:** Audit the command outcome, not transient intermediate state; enforce transaction/lock timeout against resource exhaustion.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Transaction error messages should be translated at the application boundary without using culture to change rollback semantics.

**Verification method:** Run PostgreSQL fault-injection tests around each write and inspect committed state.

## ERP-DOTNET-042 — Use optimistic concurrency for editable records

**Normative requirement:** Mutable business records shall carry a provider-supported concurrency token or equivalent conditional update mechanism and shall return a conflict outcome when the client’s version is stale.

**Rationale:** Concurrent ERP users can overwrite each other’s changes; explicit version checks preserve the user’s opportunity to reconcile.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Two clients reading the same version cannot both silently overwrite the other; the second update receives a defined conflict response.

**AC 2.** The API returns the current version token and requires it on update for configured record types.

**AC 3.** A conflict does not trigger an automatic blind retry of user-entered values.

**Exception / edge case:** A server-owned append-only event can use unique event sequencing instead of row-level edit tokens.

**Security and audit implications:** Audit conflict actor/resource/time and avoid logging full competing payloads that may contain personal data.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Conflict resolution UI labels are localized, but version tokens and conflict codes stay locale-neutral.

**Verification method:** Run two-session PostgreSQL integration tests with an intervening update.

## ERP-DOTNET-043 — Put durable integrity invariants in PostgreSQL constraints

**Normative requirement:** The schema shall enforce primary keys, tenant-scoped uniqueness, referential integrity, non-null requirements and row-local value constraints for invariants that must hold regardless of entry path.

**Rationale:** Database constraints protect data against races and non-HTTP writers; application validation alone cannot guarantee concurrent uniqueness.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Migration tests assert named unique, foreign-key, check and not-null constraints for designated invariants.

**AC 2.** Concurrent attempts to create the same tenant-scoped business identifier yield exactly one success.

**AC 3.** Constraint violations are mapped to stable domain/API errors without returning raw SQL.

**Exception / edge case:** A rule depending on cross-row temporal conditions may need a transaction, exclusion constraint or trigger rather than an invalid cross-row CHECK constraint.

**Security and audit implications:** Name constraints consistently for safe error mapping; database schema changes are reviewed and least-privilege controlled.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Constraint error labels returned to users are translated from stable codes, not raw PostgreSQL messages.

**Verification method:** Inspect PostgreSQL catalogs and run concurrent constraint-violation integration tests.

## ERP-DOTNET-044 — Represent exact quantities with explicit numeric precision

**Normative requirement:** Amounts and measured quantities that require exact decimal semantics shall use PostgreSQL NUMERIC with domain-defined precision/scale and .NET decimal or another explicitly reviewed exact representation, never binary floating point for posted values.

**Rationale:** Financial and inventory values can be corrupted by binary floating-point rounding; precision rules are domain configuration rather than universal legal assumptions.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Model/schema tests verify configured NUMERIC precision and scale for each amount/quantity type.

**AC 2.** Round-trip tests cover zero, maximum, negative/positive boundary and fractional precision values.

**AC 3.** An out-of-range value is rejected before posting and does not silently round beyond the configured policy.

**Exception / edge case:** A scientific measurement with a defined floating-point tolerance may use floating point only outside posted financial quantities and with documented precision semantics.

**Security and audit implications:** Prevent amount tampering by validating server-computed totals and audit configured precision/rounding policy changes.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Formatting is culture-specific only at presentation; persisted numeric value and API decimal serialization remain unambiguous.

**Verification method:** Run EF/PostgreSQL round-trip and boundary tests across configured precision policies.

## ERP-DOTNET-045 — Store instants separately from civil dates and time zones

**Normative requirement:** The backend shall persist event instants in UTC-aware PostgreSQL timestamps and shall represent jurisdictional civil dates, local times and time-zone identifiers as distinct domain values where their meaning is not an instant.

**Rationale:** ERP events, due dates and business calendar dates have different semantics; converting all values through server-local time causes day shifts.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** An instant round-trips to the same UTC instant regardless of server time zone.

**AC 2.** A civil date such as a period close date does not shift when serialized between UTC+14 and UTC-12 clients.

**AC 3.** Ambiguous/nonexistent daylight-saving local times are rejected or resolved by a configured, tested policy.

**Exception / edge case:** Historical jurisdictions may use renamed or changed time-zone rules; retain the selected zone identifier and apply versioned conversion policy where legally required.

**Security and audit implications:** Use UTC timestamps in audit trails and preserve original local-time/zone context when business evidence requires it.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Display timestamps and dates using the user’s selected locale/time zone without changing stored value semantics.

**Verification method:** Run timezone conversion tests for UTC, positive/negative offsets and DST gaps/overlaps.

## ERP-DOTNET-046 — Deploy schema migrations as reviewed release artifacts

**Normative requirement:** Production database migrations shall be built, reviewed and applied by a controlled deployment step using a schema-changing identity distinct from the runtime application identity.

**Rationale:** Runtime credentials should not normally have schema privileges; reviewable migration artifacts reduce unsafe production DDL.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** CI emits ordered SQL or a migration bundle and records the target migration ID.

**AC 2.** A production-like clone applies the artifact from the supported prior schema and passes smoke tests.

**AC 3.** The normal application role cannot create/alter/drop schema objects.

**Exception / edge case:** A small deployment may use a migration bundle instead of reviewed SQL if its rollback, locking and high-availability risks are explicitly accepted.

**Security and audit implications:** Restrict migration artifacts and schema credentials; migration failures produce a deployment event and preserve the previous app version where compatible.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Seed/reference text migration data must preserve Unicode and have a translation-update strategy separate from schema code.

**Rationale:** Raw string interpolation can enable SQL injection and unintended data access.

## ERP-DOTNET-048 — Define soft-delete and retention semantics explicitly

**Normative requirement:** Soft deletion shall be used only for entity types with an approved lifecycle policy; each such entity shall have an explicit deletion marker, actor/time metadata and a governed hard-purge/retention process.

**Rationale:** A universal soft-delete flag can hide data forever, break uniqueness and conflict with jurisdiction-specific erasure or retention obligations.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Only entity types listed in the approved soft-delete registry receive query filters.

**AC 2.** Delete records retain actor, timestamp and reason code when the entity policy requires recoverability.

**AC 3.** The purge process proves it excludes records under legal hold and removes eligible records after the configured retention period.

**Exception / edge case:** Posted or legally evidentiary records may be immutable/reversal-only instead of deletable; applicable rules are configured by jurisdiction and industry.

**Security and audit implications:** Restrict bypasses of soft-delete filters; audit restore, purge, hold and override actions, and minimize personal data in tombstones.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Deletion notice and retention explanations are localized; retention durations and legal bases are tenant/jurisdiction configuration.

## ERP-DOTNET-049 — Write domain changes and outbox events atomically

**Normative requirement:** When a committed business change requires asynchronous publication, the backend shall persist the outbox record in the same PostgreSQL transaction as that change and publish it using a retryable dispatcher.

**Rationale:** A separate post-commit publish can lose events on process failure; atomic outbox makes database state and intent durable together.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A forced crash after database commit but before publish leaves a dispatchable outbox record.

**AC 2.** A rolled-back business transaction leaves no publishable event.

**AC 3.** The dispatcher marks delivery only after broker acknowledgement and retries transient failures without duplicating business state.

**Exception / edge case:** Outbox delivery is at-least-once; consumers must deduplicate by stable event ID rather than assuming exactly-once transport.

**Security and audit implications:** Outbox payloads contain only necessary fields; tenant ID, event ID and actor correlation are protected and retained under policy.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Event names and machine values are locale-neutral; translated display strings are resolved by consumers from resource keys.

**Verification method:** Run crash/fault-injection tests and replay the dispatcher while asserting event identity and tenant scope.

## ERP-DOTNET-061 — Evaluate configurable workflows deterministically

**Normative requirement:** Tenant-configurable workflow definitions shall be versioned, validated before activation and evaluated deterministically against a given record state and policy version.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A workflow definition with missing transition target, unauthorized permission or cycle prohibited by configuration is rejected before activation.

**AC 2.** The same record, workflow version and actor inputs produce the same transition result in a repeat test.

**AC 3.** Activating a new version does not rewrite the workflow version attached to in-flight instances.

**Exception / edge case:** An approved emergency workflow edit may terminate or migrate in-flight instances only through a separate previewed and audited migration operation.

**Security and audit implications:** Workflow editors cannot grant themselves execution permissions; transitions require server-side authorization and record actor/time/version.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Workflow names and instructions are localized independently; transition IDs and stored decisions remain stable.

**Verification method:** Run workflow validator, deterministic replay tests and concurrent transition race tests.

**Source references:**

5

24

**REQUIREMENT 0692 OF 1120  |  ASP.NET CORE BACKEND ARCHITECTURE AND .NET BASELINE**

## ERP-DOTNET-062 — Roll out features with tenant-scoped flags

**Normative requirement:** Feature flags that alter backend behavior shall be evaluated server-side, scoped to approved tenant or deployment cohorts and recorded with their effective configuration version.

**Rationale:** Controlled rollout permits reversible adoption of new modules without exposing features to unauthorized tenants.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A tenant with a disabled flag cannot reach the associated route or background consumer.

**AC 2.** Changing the flag for tenant A does not affect tenant B.

**AC 3.** Flag evaluation is deterministic for the same tenant/configuration version and audit log shows who changed it.

**Exception / edge case:** A global security kill switch may affect all tenants but requires elevated permission, reason and operator alert.

**Security and audit implications:** Flags are not authorization substitutes; sensitive operations still require explicit permission checks.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Feature labels and notices are localized; flag key and cohort identifiers are not translated.

**Verification method:** Run tenant-isolation tests across enabled/disabled cohorts and inspect change audit.

**Source references:**

5

6

24

**REQUIREMENT 0693 OF 1120  |  ASP.NET CORE BACKEND ARCHITECTURE AND .NET BASELINE**

## ERP-DOTNET-063 — Apply timeouts and safe retries to outbound HTTP

**Normative requirement:** Outbound HTTP integrations shall use named HttpClient configurations with explicit timeouts, bounded concurrency and reviewed retry/circuit-breaker policies; non-idempotent methods shall not be retried without deduplication guarantees.

**Rationale:** Resilience prevents one unavailable partner from consuming ERP request capacity, while unsafe retries can duplicate remote actions.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A stalled partner request times out within the configured total deadline and releases capacity.

**AC 2.** A transient read-only call retries only the configured count and observes backoff/jitter limits.

**AC 3.** A non-idempotent POST retry is disabled unless an idempotency contract is tested.

**Exception / edge case:** A partner’s Retry-After may extend delay only within a configured maximum and overall deadline.

**Security and audit implications:** Outbound destinations are allow-listed to prevent SSRF; log integration name/status/duration but not authorization headers or payload secrets.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Partner error mapping is locale-neutral internally and transformed into localized user text at the API boundary.

**Verification method:** Use mock-handler tests for timeouts, status codes, retry count, circuit open and destination validation.

**Source references:**

20

**REQUIREMENT 0694 OF 1120  |  ASP.NET CORE BACKEND ARCHITECTURE AND .NET BASELINE**

## ERP-DOTNET-064 — Deduplicate inbound events and webhooks

**Normative requirement:** Inbound partner events shall be authenticated, timestamp/replay checked and persisted to an inbox with a unique source/event key before asynchronous processing.

**Rationale:** Webhook retries are expected; inbox deduplication avoids duplicate ERP work and replay of captured requests.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** An invalid signature, stale timestamp or disallowed source is rejected without inbox insertion.

**AC 2.** Two concurrent deliveries with the same source/event ID create one inbox record and one domain effect.

**AC 3.** A valid event can be retried from the inbox after transient processing failure without losing its original identity.

**Exception / edge case:** A provider without stable event IDs must use a documented canonical payload hash and bounded deduplication window.

**Security and audit implications:** Verify signatures over the raw canonical bytes, rotate secrets, enforce timestamp skew and audit replay/duplicate outcomes.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Provider locale does not control event interpretation; any text fields remain Unicode and are not used as event identity.

**Verification method:** Run forged, stale, duplicate and concurrent webhook tests plus inbox reprocessing tests.

**Source references:**

4

20

11

**REQUIREMENT 0695 OF 1120  |  ASP.NET CORE BACKEND ARCHITECTURE AND .NET BASELINE**

## ERP-DOTNET-065 — Run background work with explicit tenant scopes

**Normative requirement:** Every tenant-owned background job shall carry a validated tenant ID, actor/system identity, correlation ID and locale only when needed, then create a fresh scoped service provider and DbContext for its execution.

**Rationale:** Jobs execute outside HTTP request scope and can otherwise run with missing or stale tenant context.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A job without tenant context is rejected before touching tenant-owned tables.

**AC 2.** Parallel jobs for tenants A and B observe only their own tenant data.

**AC 3.** The worker records job ID, tenant ID, attempt number, actor type and completion/failure state.

**Exception / edge case:** A platform-wide maintenance job uses a dedicated system scope and enumerates tenant IDs through an authorized scheduler interface.

**Security and audit implications:** Job payloads avoid bearer tokens and unnecessary personal data; authorization is revalidated at execution time for user-delegated jobs.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Locale is explicit for generated user-facing artifacts and is not inherited from whichever request enqueued the job.

**Verification method:** Run worker integration tests with missing context, retries, tenant separation and expired delegated authorization.

**Source references:**

3

7

20

**REQUIREMENT 0696 OF 1120  |  ASP.NET CORE BACKEND ARCHITECTURE AND .NET BASELINE**

## ERP-DOTNET-066 — Handle imports and exports as bounded secure jobs

**Normative requirement:** Large or sensitive imports/exports shall use asynchronous jobs with validated file type/size, malware scanning where applicable, tenant-scoped authorization and expiring private object storage.

**Rationale:** Bulk data movement can exhaust the web process and creates an exfiltration channel if files are public or unbounded.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Oversized, disallowed or malformed files are rejected before import and produce no partial business commit.

**AC 2.** Export objects are private, tenant-scoped and inaccessible after the configured expiry.

**AC 3.** An import report identifies row numbers and stable error codes without storing raw secrets in logs.

**Exception / edge case:** Small text/JSON payloads below configured thresholds may be processed synchronously using a bounded streaming parser.

**Security and audit implications:** Use signed short-lived download access, scan/quarantine untrusted content, audit export requester and row scope, and redact sensitive values in reports.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** CSV/Excel parsing declares an input culture for localized numbers/dates and preserves Unicode; exported display values state their locale.

**Verification method:** Run malicious-file, size-limit, expiry, cross-tenant download and locale-specific import tests.

**Source references:**

23

7

15

**REQUIREMENT 0697 OF 1120  |  ASP.NET CORE BACKEND ARCHITECTURE AND .NET BASELINE**

## ERP-DOTNET-067 — Record security-relevant business audit events

**Normative requirement:** The backend shall write an append-only audit event for designated security and business control changes, recording actor/service, tenant, action, target, UTC time, outcome and correlation ID.

**Rationale:** Auditability supports investigation and governance; NIST’s control catalog identifies audit and accountability as a distinct control family, while exact retention remains organization-specific.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Permission, role, tenant setting, policy, workflow, support access and privileged data export changes produce an audit event.

**AC 2.** Audit events have stable event IDs and cannot be updated/deleted through the normal runtime database role.

**AC 3.** An audit query can filter by tenant, actor and time range under a separate read permission.

**Exception / edge case:** Bulk technical telemetry is not a substitute for a business audit event; non-human system actions identify the service principal.

**Security and audit implications:** Separate audit write/read privileges, protect events from tampering, redact credentials and sensitive values, and configure retention per jurisdiction.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Human-readable summaries may be localized at display time; stored event names, field paths and outcomes use stable codes.

**Verification method:** Run event coverage tests for designated actions and test ordinary-role update/delete denial.

**Source references:**

24

11

5

**REQUIREMENT 0698 OF 1120  |  ASP.NET CORE BACKEND ARCHITECTURE AND .NET BASELINE**

## ERP-DOTNET-068 — Instrument requests with safe traces and metrics

**Normative requirement:** The service shall emit structured logs, distributed trace context and bounded-cardinality metrics for API and job execution while redacting secrets and minimizing personal data.

**Rationale:** Operational signals identify latency, failure and tenant-impact patterns without creating a new disclosure surface or high-cardinality cost.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** An end-to-end request ID links API, EF command and outbound call trace spans.

**AC 2.** Metrics include route template/status/dependency duration but never raw tenant ID, user ID, URL query values or document number as unbounded labels.

**AC 3.** Automated log tests assert that Authorization, cookies, passwords and configured sensitive fields are redacted.

**Exception / edge case:** A tenant support dashboard may show tenant-level aggregates only behind explicit authorization and after cardinality/retention review.

**Security and audit implications:** Protect observability access with least privilege and retention controls; do not make traces publicly queryable.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Operational metric names and structured keys are locale-neutral; localized message text is excluded from metric dimensions.

**Verification method:** Run tracing integration tests and a synthetic-secret redaction test against captured telemetry.

**REQUIREMENT 0699 OF 1120  |  ASP.NET CORE BACKEND ARCHITECTURE AND .NET BASELINE**

## ERP-DOTNET-069 — Expose distinct health and readiness probes

**Normative requirement:** The service shall expose a minimal liveness probe and a readiness probe that checks only dependencies required to serve its declared workload, with non-sensitive output and controlled network access.

**Rationale:** Separating process health from service readiness supports safe restart and traffic routing without leaking dependency details.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Liveness remains healthy when an optional integration is unavailable but the process can continue.

**AC 2.** Readiness returns unhealthy/degraded when PostgreSQL is unavailable or migrations make the schema incompatible.

**AC 3.** Unauthenticated probe output contains only status and no connection string, host, tenant or exception detail.

**Exception / edge case:** A dependency with graceful degradation is excluded from readiness only when the affected feature is clearly disabled or marked degraded.

**Security and audit implications:** Restrict probe network exposure, avoid Host-header trust assumptions, and log state transitions rather than secret diagnostic payloads.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Probe semantics are locale-neutral machine status; any operator dashboard translates display labels separately.

**Verification method:** Run container orchestration probe tests with database up/down, optional dependency failure and unauthorized probe requests.

**Source references:**

22

19

**REQUIREMENT 0700 OF 1120  |  ASP.NET CORE BACKEND ARCHITECTURE AND .NET BASELINE**

## ERP-DOTNET-070 — Prove backup restoration and tenant recovery

**Normative requirement:** The deployment shall define encrypted PostgreSQL backup schedules and perform periodic restore drills that verify integrity, recoverability and tenant-scope controls against documented recovery objectives.

**Rationale:** A backup is useful only if it can be restored; multi-tenant ERP recovery must avoid restoring data into the wrong tenant or environment.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A restore drill completes within the approved RTO/RPO and verifies schema version plus representative row counts/checksums.

**AC 2.** Restored data is isolated from production network and secrets until validation completes.

**AC 3.** For tenant-scoped recovery, a test proves selected-tenant restore/export does not expose another tenant’s records.

**Exception / edge case:** A database-per-tenant deployment may use per-database restore procedures; shared-database recovery may require point-in-time restore plus controlled reconciliation rather than selective row replay.

**Security and audit implications:** Encrypt backups, restrict restore credentials, audit operator and target environment, and apply jurisdiction-specific retention/erasure controls.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Recovery validation includes Unicode text, locale settings and civil-date values without converting tenant jurisdiction or user preferences.

**Verification method:** Run scheduled disaster-recovery drills and retain measured RTO/RPO, restore logs and isolation-test results.

**Source references:**

# PostgreSQL Data Architecture and Operations

# 11. PostgreSQL Data Architecture and Operational Design

**Status date:** 2026-11-22. This chapter specifies relational data architecture and database operations for an internationally deployable, multi-tenant-capable ERP. It is not a jurisdictional compliance determination.

## Platform baseline

The official Microsoft support policy, last updated 2026-11-10, identifies .NET 11.0.0 (released 2026-11-10) as the newest supported release on the requested date, classified STS and active through 2028-11-14. .NET 10 is also supported as LTS through the same date. This specification selects .NET 11 / ASP.NET Core for the requested “latest stable supported” baseline, subject to confirming the current patch and support status again at implementation and each release approval \[1] \[22]. Do not infer releases from an annual schedule.

The official PostgreSQL versioning page lists PostgreSQL 19.0, released 2026-11-19, as supported through 2031-11-19; it recommends staying on the current minor. PostgreSQL 19.0 is therefore the verified major baseline at the requested date; production must use the then-current approved minor and provider-supported patch. Major versions are supported for five years, and major upgrades require a data migration method \[2].

Use ASP.NET Core services as the only transactional database clients. PostgreSQL is the system of record. The lightweight Next.js frontend is a separate browser-facing tier and calls authenticated APIs; it does not connect to PostgreSQL. Next.js documents Node.js and Docker deployment with full feature support, while static export has limited server-dependent capability \[23].

## Scope and design

### Scope

This domain defines PostgreSQL logical and physical design, tenant placement and isolation, schema evolution, transaction integrity, database access, indexing and partitioning, multilingual storage/search, security and audit controls, backup/restore, replication, observability, and lifecycle operations. It establishes architectural interfaces for core ERP modules and configurable industry extensions. It does not prescribe accounting, tax, payroll, privacy, records-retention, or sector-specific rules as universal law. Each variable rule must be provided by a tenant/legal-entity configuration or an approved jurisdiction/industry extension with effective dates and a named owner.

### Actors

- **Tenant administrator/data steward:** configures tenant placement, locale defaults, retention policy, extension schema, and data lifecycle with scoped tenant authority.
- **ERP application service:** ASP.NET Core backend using bounded connection pools and transaction-scoped tenant context.
- **Database platform operator/DBA:** provisions PostgreSQL, roles, backups, replication, upgrades, and monitoring; does not act as routine business user.
- **Migration runner:** separate deployment identity executing approved versioned database changes.
- **Security/audit operator:** reviews grants, privileged access, audit evidence, and security alerts.
- **Integration and analytics consumers:** consume API/outbox/read-model contracts with declared tenant scope and freshness.
- **End user:** accesses the product through Next.js and APIs using assigned role, tenant, language, and time zone.

### Core entities and data boundaries

The minimum platform model comprises Tenant, TenantPlacement, LegalEntity, User/ServicePrincipal, RoleGrant, LocaleProfile, LanguageTag, CurrencyPolicy, CalendarPolicy, ExtensionDefinition, SchemaMigration, DataClassification, RetentionPolicy, AuditEvent, OutboxEvent, Backup/RestorePoint, and operational Job/Batch. Domain modules add stable primary-key entities such as Party, Product, Document, Journal/Posting, InventoryMovement, and their line/relationship tables. Tenant-owned relations carry tenant identity and enforce tenant-consistent foreign keys. Global reference catalogs are explicitly marked and read-only to tenant roles. Localized labels are child rows keyed by entity and BCP 47 tag; canonical keys, amounts, timestamps, and business values are not localized.

Use typed relational columns and constraints for identity, authorization, relationships, money, date/time, status transitions, and frequently queried attributes. JSONB is reserved for bounded, versioned extension or raw integration data. PostgreSQL JSONB has operator-class/index tradeoffs and is not a substitute for typed business invariants \[7]. Schemas define module ownership and privileges; search_path is controlled because writable search-path schemas can subvert object resolution \[4].

### Principal workflows

**1. Provision tenant:** select shared or dedicated placement; apply baseline schema; register tenant and policy configuration; assign roles; verify RLS and health before enabling requests.

**2. Read/write request:** authenticate in API; authorize tenant and action; begin bounded transaction; set tenant context locally; execute parameterized domain logic; commit business rows and outbox atomically; emit audit and trace correlation.

**3. Post or reserve:** validate configuration-effective period/currency/unit rules; enforce relational and concurrency invariants in PostgreSQL; write status, details, audit, and integration event atomically; use bounded whole-transaction retry where safe.

**4. Evolve schema:** produce reviewed migration; test from empty and previous schema; apply expand/backfill/switch/contract with deployment lock; validate data and old/new binary compatibility; record applied version. EF Core migration artifacts may be used, but production application startup is not the migration runner \[21].

**5. Recover/upgrade:** monitor backup and WAL continuity; restore in isolation to a known point; reconcile totals and tenant boundaries; upgrade with rehearsed strategy and explicit cutover/rollback criteria. PostgreSQL documents SQL dump, file-level backup, and continuous archiving as different approaches \[10] \[11].

### Permission boundaries

The browser is untrusted and never receives database credentials. Runtime database roles have no DDL, superuser, or BYPASSRLS rights. Migrations run separately; backups and read-only reporting use separate roles. PostgreSQL RLS is an additional tenant boundary, not the sole one: owners ordinarily bypass policies, and superusers/BYPASSRLS always bypass them; eligible tables therefore require policy coverage and FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY where owner enforcement is intended \[3]. A tenant context must be derived from verified identity or signed job context and set transaction-locally. Cross-tenant operations require a named privileged capability, separate route/role, and audit record.

### Major decisions

- **Tenant topology:** shared logical tenant mode is the default efficiency option; dedicated database/cluster placement is an isolation, scale, residency, or contract option, selected per tenant and provider capability. Cross-tenant global catalogs are explicit.
- **Integrity:** database constraints protect entity relationships and invariant values; services own workflow-level rules. Transactions are short and whole-transaction retries are restricted to idempotent operations.
- **Identifiers:** stable opaque IDs are distinct from display names and configured document sequences. Currency precision, tax/rounding, accounting calendars, and number-sequence law are extension/configuration boundaries.
- **Localization:** store Unicode text and language tags; keep canonical numbers, dates, timestamps, machine keys, and identity invariant across locale. Display sorting and accent/case behavior are explicit field policies; collations may affect equality and index behavior \[8]. W3C describes BCP 47 tags such as fr-CA and zh-Hans \[25].
- **Extensibility:** first-class queried/validated attributes belong in typed extension tables/columns; sparse versioned fields may use JSONB under a schema registry. Core authorization and financial semantics never live only in opaque payloads.
- **Operations:** version migrations are reviewed and deployed independently; indexes and partitions are workload-driven. PostgreSQL partitioned unique constraints must include partition key columns in supported cases, so this is an upfront key-design decision \[9].
- **Recovery:** replication supports availability or data movement but is not a backup. Synchronous and asynchronous modes have different consistency, latency, and data-loss tradeoffs \[12] \[13].

### Dependencies

This design depends on an authoritative identity provider and tenant registry; API authorization; application-level ORM/SQL data-access policy; secrets management; secure network/TLS and managed database capabilities; durable backup/archive storage and encryption keys; deployment orchestration and migration approval; broker/outbox consumers; monitoring/logging/trace systems; localization catalogs and IANA language-tag validation; and tenant-specific legal, financial, and industry policy owners. NIST SP 800-53 is a flexible control catalog, not a claim of compliance; deployments select controls based on their risk and legal obligations \[24].

### Risks and mitigations

- **Cross-tenant disclosure:** composite tenant keys, application authorization, RLS, transaction-local context, negative integration tests, and controlled privileged paths.
- **Incorrect locale assumptions:** canonical typed storage, language-tagged translations, configured collation and calendar behavior, multi-script regression tests, and explicit parsing locale.
- **Migration outage/data drift:** expand-contract, lock/timeouts, measured backfill, reconciliation, restore tests, and rehearsed major upgrades. PostgreSQL major versions may change storage formats and need migration procedures \[2] \[20].
- **Backup mistaken for HA:** distinct backup/PITR and failover objectives, restore drills, and declared RPO/RTO.
- **Uncontrolled extension growth:** schema registry, ownership, validation, indexed workload expectations, limits on DDL, and upgrade compatibility checks.
- **Operational saturation:** bounded pools, connection budgets, autovacuum health, storage/WAL forecasting, timeouts, and alert ownership.
- **Jurisdictional overreach:** retention, erasure, tax, accounting periods, numbering, residency, and industry obligations remain explicit configurations/extensions, not hard-coded universal law.

### Cross-module contracts

- All tenant-owned API commands carry authenticated tenant context; tenant identity is not trusted merely because it appears in request data.
- Entity relationships use stable IDs; module-owned foreign keys and shared references are declared in the schema catalog.
- Financial posting and inventory reservation expose atomic state transitions and durable outbox events.
- Outbox/event consumers receive stable event IDs, canonical amounts/codes, tenant ID, schema version, and language tags only when text is needed.
- Read models declare freshness and authorization propagation; security-sensitive checks use primary/consistency-aware reads.
- Every module declares data classification, retention class, extension ownership, migration dependencies, and localization behavior.
- PostgreSQL errors exposed to API clients are mapped to stable domain codes; SQLSTATE and correlation remain in restricted diagnostics.

## PostgreSQL Data Architecture and Operations — requirement cards

**REQUIREMENT 0701 OF 1120  |  POSTGRESQL DATA ARCHITECTURE AND OPERATIONS**

## ERP-POSTGRES-001 — Pinned supported runtime baseline

**Normative requirement:** The production backend shall target the latest stable, supported .NET release verified at release approval and pin the SDK/runtime patch in its build and deployment manifests.

**Rationale:** An explicitly verified support baseline reduces exposure to unsupported runtimes while avoiding assumptions about future releases.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Release evidence records Microsoft policy URL, verification date, release type, patch, and end-of-support date.

**AC 2.** CI rejects a target framework outside the approved support manifest and reports the required upgrade action.

**Exception / edge case:** If the source has not published a stable release for the target date, the product owner shall select the newest verified supported release and record the reconfirmation gate.

**Security and audit implications:** SBOM and deployment attestation identify runtime versions; patch compliance is reported to security operations.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Runtime choice is not locale-dependent; translated database diagnostics are surfaced by the application, not by changing stored runtime metadata.

**Verification method:** CI policy test plus review of official Microsoft lifecycle policy.

**REQUIREMENT 0702 OF 1120  |  POSTGRESQL DATA ARCHITECTURE AND OPERATIONS**

## ERP-POSTGRES-002 — PostgreSQL supported-major baseline

**Normative requirement:** The database service shall deploy a PostgreSQL major version that is supported by the PostgreSQL Global Development Group and shall remain on its current minor release.

**Rationale:** Community support and minor fixes are necessary for security and corruption fixes.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Deployment inventory identifies major/minor server versions per environment.

**AC 2.** A scheduled compliance check fails when a server is unsupported or behind the approved current minor beyond the defined patch window.

**Exception / edge case:** A managed database provider may lag upstream; deployment approval shall document provider version and compensating timeline rather than claiming unsupported upstream parity.

**Security and audit implications:** DBA and platform security receive version-drift alerts and retain upgrade evidence.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Version metadata and notices use locale-neutral numeric version strings.

**Verification method:** Inventory query/system catalog check, policy test, and release review.

**REQUIREMENT 0703 OF 1120  |  POSTGRESQL DATA ARCHITECTURE AND OPERATIONS**

## ERP-POSTGRES-003 — Date-bound release confirmation

**Normative requirement:** The release process shall revalidate .NET and PostgreSQL support status before every production baseline approval and shall not infer future versions from an annual cadence.

**Rationale:** Official policies change; a date-sensitive baseline must be based on published evidence.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Approval record stores source links, accessed-on date, supported status, and exact version.

**AC 2.** A missing or stale baseline record blocks release sign-off.

**Exception / edge case:** If official documentation does not establish a requested future version, the release baseline shall be marked “reconfirm before approval.”

**Security and audit implications:** Preserve approval and change history; no version claims may be silently edited.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Localized copies of a version notice preserve the canonical version and date.

**Verification method:** Release-gate test and audit of a sample baseline record.

**REQUIREMENT 0704 OF 1120  |  POSTGRESQL DATA ARCHITECTURE AND OPERATIONS**

## ERP-POSTGRES-004 — Tenant data placement strategy

**Normative requirement:** The platform shall support a documented shared-database/shared-schema logical-tenant mode and a separately provisioned database or cluster mode for tenants requiring isolation or residency configuration.

**Rationale:** Tenant isolation, scale, and location needs vary and should not be hard-coded as one universal topology.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Provisioning tests create tenants in both logical and dedicated placement modes.

**AC 2.** Tenant registry resolves each tenant to exactly one active placement and rejects ambiguous routing.

**Exception / edge case:** A tenant may be temporarily dual-written during approved migration only through a controlled migration state with reconciliation.

**Security and audit implications:** Placement changes require privileged approval, audit record, and encrypted transfer.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Tenant locale settings remain tenant-scoped regardless of physical placement.

**Verification method:** Provisioning integration test and routing contract test.

**REQUIREMENT 0705 OF 1120  |  POSTGRESQL DATA ARCHITECTURE AND OPERATIONS**

## ERP-POSTGRES-005 — Tenant-scoped keys

**Normative requirement:** Every tenant-owned operational row in shared tables shall carry a non-null tenant identifier, and tenant-scoped natural uniqueness shall include that identifier.

**Rationale:** Tenant identity in keys prevents accidental cross-tenant associations and collisions.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Schema lint finds tenant_id on all registered tenant-owned tables.

**AC 2.** Database tests prove identical tenant-local codes can coexist while duplicate codes within a tenant fail.

**Exception / edge case:** Global reference data and truly global identities may omit tenant_id only when declared in the data catalog and read-only to tenant roles.

**Security and audit implications:** Cross-tenant queries require a named privileged capability and are audited.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Tenant display names and localized aliases are not used as tenant keys.

**Verification method:** Migration/schema catalog linter and database integration tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0706 OF 1120  |  POSTGRESQL DATA ARCHITECTURE AND OPERATIONS**

## ERP-POSTGRES-006 — Tenant foreign-key integrity

**Normative requirement:** Relationships between tenant-owned records shall enforce tenant equality in PostgreSQL using composite foreign keys or an equivalent database-enforced constraint.

**Rationale:** Application-only relationship checks can be bypassed by jobs, imports, or future code paths.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Inserting a child with a parent ID from a different tenant fails at the database boundary.

**AC 2.** A normal same-tenant parent-child insert and update succeeds.

**Exception / edge case:** For a relationship to a global catalog, the FK shall reference the catalog key and its global scope shall be explicit.

**Security and audit implications:** Constraint violations are logged as safe event metadata without leaking other tenant identifiers.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Localized labels are excluded from referential keys; identifiers remain stable across locale changes.

**Verification method:** SQL integration tests exercising cross-tenant mismatch and valid relationship.

**REQUIREMENT 0707 OF 1120  |  POSTGRESQL DATA ARCHITECTURE AND OPERATIONS**

## ERP-POSTGRES-007 — Tenant isolation enforcement layer

**Normative requirement:** Shared-table tenant isolation shall be enforced both in the application data-access boundary and by PostgreSQL row-level security for eligible tenant-owned tables.

**Rationale:** Defense in depth limits damage from omitted predicates in application queries.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Role-based integration tests show queries under tenant A cannot read or mutate tenant B rows.

**AC 2.** Schema tests enumerate tenant tables and fail when RLS is absent or policy coverage is missing.

**Exception / edge case:** Tables unsuitable for RLS, such as a deliberately global catalog, require a documented exemption and compensating grants.

**Security and audit implications:** RLS is not treated as protection from superusers, BYPASSRLS roles, or owners unless FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY applies; privileged paths are restricted and audited.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Locale changes do not alter tenant policy predicates or the tenant identifier.

**Verification method:** RLS policy tests using non-owner application role and schema coverage test.

**REQUIREMENT 0708 OF 1120  |  POSTGRESQL DATA ARCHITECTURE AND OPERATIONS**

## ERP-POSTGRES-008 — Transaction-local tenant context

**Normative requirement:** The application shall set the authenticated tenant context transaction-locally on every database transaction before accessing tenant data.

**Rationale:** Transaction-local context prevents connection-pool reuse from leaking a prior request’s tenant setting.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A reused physical connection serving sequential tenant A and B transactions returns only each tenant’s data.

**AC 2.** Requests without authenticated tenant context fail closed before tenant-table access.

**Exception / edge case:** Background jobs with explicit tenant scope may set context from a signed job envelope; cross-tenant jobs use a separately authorized route.

**Security and audit implications:** Context source is trusted identity/job metadata, never a client-supplied tenant ID alone; attempted mismatch is audited.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** The tenant’s preferred language is separate from its security context.

**Verification method:** Connection-pool reuse integration test and missing-context denial test.

**REQUIREMENT 0709 OF 1120  |  POSTGRESQL DATA ARCHITECTURE AND OPERATIONS**

## ERP-POSTGRES-009 — Tenant-safe database roles

**Normative requirement:** Database roles shall separate schema ownership/migration, application runtime, read-only reporting, backup, and operations, with runtime roles lacking DDL and superuser privileges.

**Rationale:** Role separation limits blast radius and supports clear operational responsibilities.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Catalog inspection confirms runtime roles have no CREATE/ALTER/DROP schema rights and no SUPERUSER/BYPASSRLS.

**AC 2.** Permission tests confirm read-only reporting role cannot insert, update, or delete operational rows.

**Exception / edge case:** Emergency break-glass access may elevate only through time-bound approval, controlled credential retrieval, and audit capture.

**Security and audit implications:** Role grants and membership changes are auditable; passwords or tokens are never logged.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Human role names/descriptions may be localized in the UI, while database role identifiers remain stable.

**Verification method:** Automated privilege audit against expected-grants manifest.

**REQUIREMENT 0710 OF 1120  |  POSTGRESQL DATA ARCHITECTURE AND OPERATIONS**

## ERP-POSTGRES-010 — Schema namespace safety

**Normative requirement:** Application SQL shall qualify schema object references or use a controlled search_path containing no schema writable by untrusted roles.

**Rationale:** PostgreSQL documents that writable search_path schemas can alter resolution of names and execute attacker-controlled functions.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Runtime search_path is checked at connection initialization and matches an allowlisted value.

**AC 2.** A test role unable to create in application search schemas cannot shadow an application relation or function.

**Exception / edge case:** Temporary schemas may be added for isolated test sessions but shall not be used by production request connections.

**Security and audit implications:** Public CREATE is revoked where not needed; extension installation is owner-controlled.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Localized schema/table names are prohibited; locale-specific content belongs in data rows.

**Verification method:** Catalog grants test and malicious shadow-object integration test.

**REQUIREMENT 0711 OF 1120  |  POSTGRESQL DATA ARCHITECTURE AND OPERATIONS**

## ERP-POSTGRES-011 — Relational constraints for invariants

**Normative requirement:** Business invariants that can be stated as NOT NULL, CHECK, UNIQUE, PRIMARY KEY, or FOREIGN KEY constraints shall be enforced in PostgreSQL as well as validated in the application.

**Rationale:** Database constraints protect integrity across concurrent sessions and integrations.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Schema review maps each approved invariant to a named constraint or records why database enforcement is infeasible.

**AC 2.** Invalid values inserted through direct SQL are rejected for each database-enforceable invariant.

**Exception / edge case:** Cross-row or cross-table business rules that need workflow context remain in a transaction/service and are not misrepresented as a simple CHECK.

**Security and audit implications:** Constraint error responses avoid exposing internal schema details; failed writes are auditable by actor and operation.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Constraints apply to canonical values, not translated display labels.

**Verification method:** DDL inspection and negative integration tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0712 OF 1120  |  POSTGRESQL DATA ARCHITECTURE AND OPERATIONS**

## ERP-POSTGRES-012 — Stable primary identifiers

**Normative requirement:** Each persisted business entity shall have a stable primary key independent of mutable names, localized labels, and user-visible document numbers.

**Rationale:** Stable identifiers preserve links through renaming, translation, and numbering policy changes.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Changing a translated entity label does not change its primary key or dependent foreign keys.

**AC 2.** API and event contracts distinguish immutable entity ID from editable business code.

**Exception / edge case:** A legally prescribed external identifier may be a separate constrained attribute with configurable jurisdiction scope.

**Security and audit implications:** IDs are non-secret references and do not grant access; authorization is checked separately.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** No key is derived from language, locale, or collation-sensitive text.

**Verification method:** Schema/API contract tests with label edits and FK persistence.

**REQUIREMENT 0713 OF 1120  |  POSTGRESQL DATA ARCHITECTURE AND OPERATIONS**

## ERP-POSTGRES-013 — Business document numbering boundary

**Normative requirement:** Document-number sequences shall be configured per tenant, legal entity, document type, and effective period where required, and shall not be treated as database primary keys.

**Rationale:** Numbering, gaps, resets, and legal sequencing rules vary by jurisdiction and document type.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Configuration can express scope, prefix/format, effective dates, and gap policy without altering PKs.

**AC 2.** Two tenants or configured legal entities can issue overlapping display numbers without collision in internal IDs.

**Exception / edge case:** If local law requires no gaps or special cancellation treatment, jurisdiction-specific extension owns and validates that policy; no universal rule is assumed.

**Security and audit implications:** Number allocation and void/reissue decisions create an immutable audit event.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Format tokens may use localized digits only for rendering if policy allows; stored canonical sequence remains numeric/string exact.

**Verification method:** Configuration and concurrency tests, including simultaneous allocation and void path.

**REQUIREMENT 0714 OF 1120  |  POSTGRESQL DATA ARCHITECTURE AND OPERATIONS**

## ERP-POSTGRES-014 — Exact monetary representation

**Normative requirement:** Monetary amounts shall be stored using fixed-precision numeric types with explicit currency code and configured precision/rounding policy, not binary floating point.

**Rationale:** Binary floating point can introduce rounding errors in accounting amounts.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Schema inspection confirms monetary columns use numeric/decimal precision chosen in data dictionary.
