**AC 2.** Round-trip tests preserve exact decimal input for configured currencies and reject unsupported scale at domain boundary.

**Exception / edge case:** Currency minor units, tax rounding, and cash rounding vary; effective-dated currency and jurisdiction configuration decides rules.

**Security and audit implications:** Amounts and changes are access-controlled and financial changes retain before/after audit evidence.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Formatting and decimal/group separators are presentation concerns; localized strings are never parsed as canonical database amounts without locale-aware validation.

**Verification method:** Decimal round-trip/property tests and schema inspection.

**REQUIREMENT 0715 OF 1120  |  POSTGRESQL DATA ARCHITECTURE AND OPERATIONS**

## ERP-POSTGRES-015 — Canonical UTC instants

**Normative requirement:** Event timestamps representing instants shall be stored as timestamptz in UTC semantics; date-only business concepts shall use date and named local-timezone policy where needed.

**Rationale:** Timezone-safe storage prevents ambiguous instants and date shifting across regions.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A timestamp round-trip across two configured zones represents the same instant.

**AC 2.** Date-only fields round-trip without timezone conversion.

**Exception / edge case:** A local appointment in a daylight-saving gap or overlap is rejected or resolved using an explicit configured disambiguation rule.

**Security and audit implications:** Time-zone changes and manual overrides are audit-recorded for controlled business events.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Formatting uses user/tenant locale and time zone; database comparisons operate on instants.

**Verification method:** Boundary tests for UTC conversion and DST gap/overlap cases.

**REQUIREMENT 0716 OF 1120  |  POSTGRESQL DATA ARCHITECTURE AND OPERATIONS**

## ERP-POSTGRES-016 — Tenant and legal-entity calendar configuration

**Normative requirement:** Fiscal calendars, week starts, accounting periods, and business-day calendars shall be data-configured per applicable tenant/legal entity and jurisdiction extension.

**Rationale:** Calendar rules are not universal and affect posting, reporting, and cutoffs.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** At least two test configurations can have different fiscal year starts and holidays.

**AC 2.** A posting date is validated against the active configured period policy.

**Exception / edge case:** If the configured calendar is missing or overlapping, postings fail closed and require an administrator to repair configuration.

**Security and audit implications:** Changing a closed-period configuration requires elevated permission and reason-bearing audit record.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Calendar labels and month names are localized for display while stored dates and period keys remain canonical.

**Verification method:** Configuration contract and cross-calendar posting tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0717 OF 1120  |  POSTGRESQL DATA ARCHITECTURE AND OPERATIONS**

## ERP-POSTGRES-017 — Localized text model

**Normative requirement:** User-facing reference entities shall store canonical identity separately from one-to-many localized labels keyed by valid BCP 47 language tags, with an explicit fallback chain.

**Rationale:** One text column cannot safely represent multiple tenant languages or distinguish content from presentation.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** An entity can have at least two translations without duplicating its business identity.

**AC 2.** Missing requested translation resolves by declared fallback order and is detectable as a missing translation.

**Exception / edge case:** Legally authoritative names may be preserved exactly as supplied and marked with source language rather than overwritten by translation.

**Security and audit implications:** Translation edits follow the same authoring permission and audit controls as the underlying entity.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Language tags are validated against the supported registry policy and preserve script/region where meaningful.

**Verification method:** Database/API tests for valid/invalid tags and fallback behavior.

**REQUIREMENT 0718 OF 1120  |  POSTGRESQL DATA ARCHITECTURE AND OPERATIONS**

## ERP-POSTGRES-018 — Unicode text preservation

**Normative requirement:** Text columns shall preserve Unicode input without lossy transliteration, and input normalization rules shall be explicit per field rather than applied globally.

**Rationale:** International names and descriptions require full character preservation; global normalization can corrupt identifiers or evidence.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Round-trip tests cover Latin combining marks, Arabic, CJK, and supplementary-plane characters.

**AC 2.** Field-specific normalization produces documented behavior and does not alter original legal/evidentiary text.

**Exception / edge case:** Legacy encoding import may require staged conversion and quarantine of undecodable rows.

**Security and audit implications:** Sensitive free-text access is permissioned; normalization/import transformations are audit-traceable.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Store original script; render direction and normalization in UI layers; avoid locale-dependent byte transformations.

**Verification method:** Unicode corpus round-trip test and migration fixture tests.

**REQUIREMENT 0719 OF 1120  |  POSTGRESQL DATA ARCHITECTURE AND OPERATIONS**

## ERP-POSTGRES-019 — Locale-aware sorting and search

**Normative requirement:** Search and ordering shall use explicitly selected collation/search behavior and shall not use collation equality as a universal business identity rule.

**Rationale:** Locale-aware sorting and case/accent-insensitive comparison differ from exact identity and can have index/performance tradeoffs.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Tests show configured collation ordering for representative scripts and a separate exact identifier comparison.

**AC 2.** An index or query plan is validated for every deployed collation-dependent search path.

**Exception / edge case:** If ICU/provider version changes comparison results, collation/index rebuild and revalidation are included in the upgrade plan.

**Security and audit implications:** Search filters must remain tenant-scoped; collation changes are reviewed for duplicate/unique-key implications.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Language/region configuration selects expected sorting behavior; case/accent treatment is specified per search field.

**Verification method:** Collation matrix test and EXPLAIN-based workload test.

**REQUIREMENT 0720 OF 1120  |  POSTGRESQL DATA ARCHITECTURE AND OPERATIONS**

## ERP-POSTGRES-020 — Canonical codes and case policy

**Normative requirement:** Machine codes, enum-like values, and external references shall use a documented canonical representation and explicit case-sensitivity rule independent of UI locale.

**Rationale:** Ambiguous case folding can produce collisions or inconsistent integrations across locales.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Database uniqueness tests confirm the configured case policy for sample identifiers.

**AC 2.** Round-trip API tests preserve code values without locale-sensitive upper/lower conversion.

**Exception / edge case:** A partner system with case-insensitive identifiers is handled by an adapter mapping and not by changing global identifiers.

**Security and audit implications:** Codes are validated and parameterized; sensitive external tokens are not reused as business codes.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Display labels may be translated, but canonical codes are not translated.

**Verification method:** Schema/API contract tests and adversarial casing corpus.

**REQUIREMENT 0721 OF 1120  |  POSTGRESQL DATA ARCHITECTURE AND OPERATIONS**

## ERP-POSTGRES-021 — Locale-independent numeric and date storage

**Normative requirement:** Numbers and dates shall be stored in typed canonical columns and never as locale-formatted text when they participate in arithmetic, ordering, or constraints.

**Rationale:** Persisting formatted strings makes calculations and comparison ambiguous across locales.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Schema scan rejects string-typed fields for declared numeric/date business attributes unless explicitly marked as raw source payload.

**AC 2.** API tests in two locales produce identical persisted canonical values from equivalent inputs.

**Exception / edge case:** Unparsed source documents may retain original string representation alongside a validated normalized value and parse status.

**Security and audit implications:** Import logs redact sensitive input while retaining validation outcome and source record reference.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Parsing uses the supplied user/tenant locale explicitly; export formatting occurs at the presentation boundary.

**Verification method:** Schema dictionary test and locale-switch import test.

**REQUIREMENT 0722 OF 1120  |  POSTGRESQL DATA ARCHITECTURE AND OPERATIONS**

## ERP-POSTGRES-022 — Industry extension boundary

**Normative requirement:** Industry-specific attributes shall be implemented through versioned extension modules, normalized tables for stable queried concepts, or validated JSONB for sparse/versioned attributes, with ownership documented.

**Rationale:** Extensibility must not turn the shared core schema into ungoverned opaque storage.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Each extension field has owner, schema version, validation, and query/index expectations recorded.

**AC 2.** Required reporting attributes are promoted to typed columns or extension tables with tested constraints.

**Exception / edge case:** A configurable tenant field with unknown type or unsupported version is rejected/quarantined instead of silently interpreted.

**Security and audit implications:** Extension authors cannot add database objects in core schemas; tenant data permissions continue to apply.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Localized extension labels/descriptions carry language tags separately from machine keys.

**Verification method:** Extension registry/schema validation test and queryability review.

**REQUIREMENT 0723 OF 1120  |  POSTGRESQL DATA ARCHITECTURE AND OPERATIONS**

## ERP-POSTGRES-023 — JSONB use constraints

**Normative requirement:** JSONB shall be limited to bounded, schema-versioned extension or integration payloads; core relational identity, authorization, financial, and frequently joined attributes shall remain typed relational columns.

**Rationale:** JSONB enables evolving structures but shifts validation and indexing responsibility to applications.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Every JSONB column has a documented JSON schema/version and maximum payload-size validation.

**AC 2.** Fields used for filters, joins, constraints, or aggregates are promoted or have an approved expression/GIN index and workload test.

**Exception / edge case:** Unknown external payload versions are retained only in quarantine/raw ingestion storage until validated.

**Security and audit implications:** Payload fields are classified, redacted from logs, and protected by tenant boundaries; keys cannot override authorization metadata.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Localized values in JSONB must use explicit language-tagged structures; untagged multilingual text is not accepted for translation-bearing content.

**Verification method:** Schema-registry tests, size boundary tests, and EXPLAIN benchmark.

**REQUIREMENT 0724 OF 1120  |  POSTGRESQL DATA ARCHITECTURE AND OPERATIONS**

## ERP-POSTGRES-024 — Domain model schema ownership

**Normative requirement:** Core ERP domains and approved extensions shall have explicit PostgreSQL schema ownership, naming conventions, and dependency directions documented in a schema catalog.

**Rationale:** Explicit ownership reduces accidental coupling and makes privilege and migration review feasible.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Every non-system relation is mapped to one owning module and data steward.

**AC 2.** DDL CI rejects unregistered schemas/tables and cross-module FK not listed in the dependency contract.

**Exception / edge case:** Shared reference tables may be owned by a platform domain with read-only grants to modules.

**Security and audit implications:** Schema ownership is held by non-login owner roles; tenant operators cannot create executable objects.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Schema object names remain language-neutral; translated descriptions reside in catalog metadata.

**Verification method:** Catalog inventory/linter test and architecture review.

**REQUIREMENT 0725 OF 1120  |  POSTGRESQL DATA ARCHITECTURE AND OPERATIONS**

## ERP-POSTGRES-025 — Versioned schema migrations

**Normative requirement:** Database schema changes shall be delivered as versioned, reviewed migration artifacts that are tracked with the application release.

**Rationale:** Versioned migrations enable repeatable environment setup and traceable evolution.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A clean database can be built to the release schema by applying migrations in order.

**AC 2.** The migration history records each applied migration exactly once and detects checksum drift.

**Exception / edge case:** Emergency hotfix DDL requires a follow-up migration that reconciles the declared model to actual state.

**Security and audit implications:** Migration artifact approval records author, reviewer, execution identity, and change ticket.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Migration names and comments are language-neutral; user-facing data migration content uses localized catalogs.

**Verification method:** CI builds empty and prior-version databases and compares expected catalog snapshots.

**REQUIREMENT 0726 OF 1120  |  POSTGRESQL DATA ARCHITECTURE AND OPERATIONS**

## ERP-POSTGRES-026 — Reviewed production migration execution

**Normative requirement:** Production migrations shall execute through a controlled deployment identity using reviewed SQL or a deployment bundle, not automatic schema creation by web application startup.

**Rationale:** Separating migration authority from runtime reduces privilege and startup-race risks.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Runtime startup performs no DDL in production under database audit/log inspection.

**AC 2.** A migration pipeline displays planned operations and records success/failure per environment.

**Exception / edge case:** A reversible migration may be rolled back only where its declared data-loss behavior is acceptable; otherwise use forward repair.

**Security and audit implications:** Production migration credentials are short-lived or vault-managed, isolated from runtime secrets, and audited.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Migration operator UI may be localized; SQL artifacts and IDs remain canonical.

**Verification method:** Deployment pipeline test, credential review, and DB audit inspection.

**REQUIREMENT 0727 OF 1120  |  POSTGRESQL DATA ARCHITECTURE AND OPERATIONS**

## ERP-POSTGRES-027 — Backward-compatible migration phases

**Normative requirement:** Changes to shared tables used by rolling application versions shall follow expand, backfill, switch, and contract phases unless a documented maintenance window makes simultaneous change safe.

**Rationale:** Rolling deployments can run old and new application versions concurrently.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Compatibility tests run previous and next application version against the expanded schema.

**AC 2.** Contract phase is blocked while old binaries or consumers still reference removed structures.

**Exception / edge case:** A small isolated tenant or feature-flag rollout may be used to validate the expanded schema before general rollout.

**Security and audit implications:** Backfills use least-privilege execution and record counts/status without logging row contents.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Data backfills preserve all language variants and do not collapse translations.

**Verification method:** Two-version compatibility integration test and rollout simulation.

**REQUIREMENT 0728 OF 1120  |  POSTGRESQL DATA ARCHITECTURE AND OPERATIONS**

## ERP-POSTGRES-028 — Migration concurrency and locking

**Normative requirement:** Migration execution shall acquire a deployment-level lock and set explicit lock/statement timeouts for production DDL and backfills.

**Rationale:** Concurrent deploys and long locks can block transactions and cause outages.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Two concurrent migration runners result in only one active schema change; the other exits safely.

**AC 2.** A lock-timeout test aborts a blocked migration without leaving an untracked partial state.

**Exception / edge case:** Operations that cannot run transactionally, such as concurrent index builds, use resumable steps and explicit cleanup logic.

**Security and audit implications:** Lock holder and migration action are identifiable in operational audit telemetry.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Lock errors are presented through localized operational tooling but preserve SQLSTATE for diagnosis.

**Verification method:** Concurrent-runner test, lock-injection test, and migration rehearsal.

**REQUIREMENT 0729 OF 1120  |  POSTGRESQL DATA ARCHITECTURE AND OPERATIONS**

## ERP-POSTGRES-029 — Data migration validation

**Normative requirement:** Every migration that transforms existing data shall include precondition, postcondition, reconciliation counts, and a failure/repair strategy.

**Rationale:** Schema success alone does not establish data correctness.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Test fixtures show old-to-new mapping counts match and invalid rows are reported.

**AC 2.** Production migration emits processed, succeeded, quarantined, and failed counts that reconcile to input count.

**Exception / edge case:** Malformed or ambiguous legacy values are quarantined for review rather than coerced silently.

**Security and audit implications:** Logs contain record identifiers and safe error codes, not sensitive full values.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Locale-dependent legacy values are parsed using an explicit source locale per record or batch.

**Verification method:** Fixture test plus production rehearsal and reconciliation assertion.

**REQUIREMENT 0730 OF 1120  |  POSTGRESQL DATA ARCHITECTURE AND OPERATIONS**

## ERP-POSTGRES-030 — Database extension allowlist

**Normative requirement:** Only approved PostgreSQL extensions at approved versions shall be installed, and each extension shall have a documented security, upgrade, and provider-compatibility review.

**Rationale:** Extensions add privileged code and operational dependency beyond application SQL.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Deployment manifest lists installed extension names/versions and fails on unapproved additions.

**AC 2.** Upgrade rehearsal confirms each required extension is available and compatible on target major.

**Exception / edge case:** If managed PostgreSQL does not expose an extension, the feature is disabled or implemented at application layer rather than assuming superuser access.

**Security and audit implications:** Installation rights are restricted to DB owner/operations role; extension versions appear in SBOM/control inventory.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Extension output is normalized to stable codes; locale-sensitive behavior is explicitly configured.

**Verification method:** Catalog query, policy test, and major-upgrade rehearsal.

**REQUIREMENT 0731 OF 1120  |  POSTGRESQL DATA ARCHITECTURE AND OPERATIONS**

## ERP-POSTGRES-031 — Workload-driven index design

**Normative requirement:** Indexes shall be derived from measured query patterns and data distribution, with an owner, purpose, and removal review date for non-constraint indexes.

**Rationale:** Indexes consume storage and write effort and should support actual access paths.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** For each critical query, test data and EXPLAIN output demonstrate the intended index or justified scan.

**AC 2.** Index inventory reports unused/duplicate candidates and size for review, without auto-dropping constraints.

**Exception / edge case:** Low-volume tenant or sequential scan cases may not benefit from an index; retain only with documented rationale.

**Security and audit implications:** Index definitions do not weaken tenant-scoped uniqueness or expose data; index names avoid sensitive labels.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Text search indexes use explicitly configured language dictionaries/collations rather than assuming English.

**Verification method:** EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) workload test and index inventory review.

**REQUIREMENT 0732 OF 1120  |  POSTGRESQL DATA ARCHITECTURE AND OPERATIONS**

## ERP-POSTGRES-032 — Safe production index creation

**Normative requirement:** Large-table production indexes shall use a low-blocking online procedure where supported, and deployment shall verify the resulting index is valid before marking the migration complete.

**Rationale:** A failed concurrent build can leave an invalid index and still consume maintenance overhead.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Migration checks pg_index validity after creation before completing its step.

**AC 2.** Failure-injection test detects invalid indexes and invokes documented drop/rebuild recovery.

**Exception / edge case:** Unique concurrent build may begin enforcing uniqueness before becoming valid; deploy only after duplicate precheck and application conflict handling.

**Security and audit implications:** DDL privileges are limited; operational tooling records index build duration, failures, and cleanup.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Locale-dependent indexes are rebuilt/revalidated after collation provider changes.

**Verification method:** Migration test on populated table, failure injection, and catalog validity assertion.

**REQUIREMENT 0733 OF 1120  |  POSTGRESQL DATA ARCHITECTURE AND OPERATIONS**

## ERP-POSTGRES-033 — Selective partitioning

**Normative requirement:** Partitioning shall be introduced only for tables with measured scale, retention, or maintenance needs and an approved partition key, interval, and lifecycle plan.

**Rationale:** Partitioning adds DDL and maintenance complexity and is not a universal default.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Design record identifies table volume forecast, partition key, boundaries, and query pruning predicates.

**AC 2.** Load test confirms representative time/tenant queries prune partitions as expected.

**Exception / edge case:** When requirements are not met, retain a nonpartitioned table and revisit using measured growth rather than speculative partitioning.

**Security and audit implications:** Partition maintenance role is restricted and cannot attach arbitrary tenant data into core tables.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Partition boundaries use canonical time values; tenant locale does not determine partition slicing.

**Verification method:** Architecture decision record, EXPLAIN test, and partition maintenance rehearsal.

**REQUIREMENT 0734 OF 1120  |  POSTGRESQL DATA ARCHITECTURE AND OPERATIONS**

## ERP-POSTGRES-034 — Partition uniqueness and routing

**Normative requirement:** Partitioned tables shall define unique and primary constraints compatible with PostgreSQL partition-key limitations, including all partition key columns when required.

**Rationale:** Per-partition indexes cannot enforce arbitrary cross-partition uniqueness.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** DDL test rejects a proposed key that omits required partition columns; approved key enforces uniqueness across partitions.

**AC 2.** Application routing and queries include partition predicates for hot paths where the design expects pruning.

**Exception / edge case:** A globally unique identifier may remain unique by generation strategy but shall not be represented as a database-enforced global natural-key constraint if PG cannot enforce it across partitions.

**Security and audit implications:** Tenant scope remains present in partitioned rows and RLS/policies are tested on parent and attached partitions.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Business-local number uniqueness is configured independently of locale and partition boundary.

**Verification method:** DDL acceptance tests and cross-partition duplicate attempt.

**REQUIREMENT 0735 OF 1120  |  POSTGRESQL DATA ARCHITECTURE AND OPERATIONS**

## ERP-POSTGRES-035 — Partition lifecycle automation

**Normative requirement:** Partition maintenance shall create future partitions ahead of expected writes and alert before any row can fail routing due to a missing partition.

**Rationale:** A missing range causes inserts to fail; manual reaction can interrupt ERP posting.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Scheduled test creates the configured future horizon and verifies a row at the horizon boundary routes successfully.

**AC 2.** Alert fires when partition coverage falls below configured days or when a default partition receives rows.

**Exception / edge case:** A controlled default partition may capture unexpected dates only if monitored and drained by an approved process.

**Security and audit implications:** Partition-management credentials cannot read tenant business payloads unless required; changes are audited.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Partition date derivation uses tenant/legal calendar only if the domain explicitly requires it; otherwise UTC event time.

**Verification method:** Time-advance integration test and alert rule test.

**REQUIREMENT 0736 OF 1120  |  POSTGRESQL DATA ARCHITECTURE AND OPERATIONS**

## ERP-POSTGRES-036 — Retention and archival policy boundary

**Normative requirement:** Retention, archival, and deletion shall be configurable by data class, tenant contract, and applicable jurisdiction/industry policy; no universal legal duration shall be hard-coded.

**Rationale:** Retention obligations differ by region, business record, and contract.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Policy registry stores owner, scope, effective dates, trigger, action, and legal/configuration source.

**AC 2.** A dry-run report identifies affected rows/files and counts before purge or archive execution.

**Exception / edge case:** Legal hold blocks purge for matching records and requires explicit release by authorized role.

**Security and audit implications:** Retention actions create audit records while audit retention itself follows a separately governed policy.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Translated labels and language variants are included or purged consistently with the entity retention decision.

**Verification method:** Policy test using conflicting hold/retention cases and dry-run-to-execution reconciliation.

**REQUIREMENT 0737 OF 1120  |  POSTGRESQL DATA ARCHITECTURE AND OPERATIONS**

## ERP-POSTGRES-037 — Archive format and restore linkage

**Normative requirement:** Archived records shall retain tenant/entity keys, schema version, original identifiers, and integrity metadata sufficient for authorized retrieval and reconstruction.

**Rationale:** An archive without relational context and format version is not safely reusable.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Archived sample reconstructs required record fields and source links under the documented reader version.

**AC 2.** Archive validation detects checksum mismatch or unsupported schema version.

**Exception / edge case:** Unavailable external attachments are represented with an explicit unavailable status and reference, never fabricated.

**Security and audit implications:** Archives are encrypted, access-logged, and scoped to tenant/authorized retention operators.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Original text and language tags are preserved; display localization may be rendered by current application without rewriting the archived source.

**Verification method:** Archive round-trip, checksum test, and access audit test.

**REQUIREMENT 0738 OF 1120  |  POSTGRESQL DATA ARCHITECTURE AND OPERATIONS**

## ERP-POSTGRES-038 — Bounded application connections

**Normative requirement:** Application database access shall use a bounded connection pool with explicit acquisition, command, and transaction timeouts.

**Rationale:** Unbounded sessions can exhaust PostgreSQL resources or leave requests stalled.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Load test holds the configured pool maximum and confirms additional work queues or fails within the configured timeout.

**AC 2.** Fault test proves abandoned transactions are canceled/returned rather than held indefinitely.

**Exception / edge case:** Long-running report/export jobs use separate bounded concurrency and do not borrow the interactive pool without policy.

**Security and audit implications:** Connection strings and pool diagnostics redact credentials and tenant PII.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Timeout/error messages are localizable while structured logs retain stable SQLSTATE/error categories.

**Verification method:** Load/fault tests and pool metrics assertion.

**REQUIREMENT 0739 OF 1120  |  POSTGRESQL DATA ARCHITECTURE AND OPERATIONS**

## ERP-POSTGRES-039 — Database connection budget

**Normative requirement:** Service owners shall calculate a per-instance connection budget against PostgreSQL max_connections, reserved slots, replicas, migrations, and operational headroom.

**Rationale:** PostgreSQL resource use grows with configured concurrent connections, so connection growth must be planned.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Capacity manifest formula is testable from replica count, pool maximum, and reserved operator slots.

**AC 2.** Scale-out test shows total possible application connections remain below approved server budget.

**Exception / edge case:** Unexpected autoscaling or failover overlap must trigger admission control rather than consuming emergency DBA slots.

**Security and audit implications:** Connection saturation alarms exclude passwords/connection strings and route to authorized operators.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** No locale dependency; capacity identifiers are stable across regions.

**Verification method:** Capacity calculation check and scale simulation.

**REQUIREMENT 0740 OF 1120  |  POSTGRESQL DATA ARCHITECTURE AND OPERATIONS**

## ERP-POSTGRES-040 — Short transaction boundaries

**Normative requirement:** Database transactions shall cover one cohesive business operation and shall not remain open while waiting for user input, external HTTP calls, or long file processing.

**Rationale:** Long transactions retain locks and old row versions, harming concurrency and vacuum progress.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Code analysis or tracing shows no transaction spans an external network call or user think-time.

**AC 2.** Test injects slow downstream service and confirms DB transaction commits/rolls back before waiting.

**Exception / edge case:** A legitimately long batch uses documented chunking or isolated job execution with progress and cancellation semantics.

**Security and audit implications:** Transaction actor, duration, and outcome are recorded without sensitive payload.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** UI locale and user interaction never define transaction duration.

**Verification method:** Static review plus trace-based integration test.

**REQUIREMENT 0741 OF 1120  |  POSTGRESQL DATA ARCHITECTURE AND OPERATIONS**

## ERP-POSTGRES-041 — Isolation and serialization retry policy

**Normative requirement:** Each business workflow shall declare its isolation/locking strategy, and retryable serialization/deadlock failures shall retry the entire idempotent transaction within a bounded policy.

**Rationale:** PostgreSQL isolation semantics differ; correctness depends on whole-transaction handling, not blind statement retry.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Concurrent test for protected invariant demonstrates no invalid double allocation.

**AC 2.** Injected serialization failure retries from transaction start with a finite attempt cap and jitter.

**Exception / edge case:** Non-idempotent side effects are emitted after commit through an outbox or compensated, not repeated inside retry.

**Security and audit implications:** Retries are audit-correlated without duplicating business events; exhaustion is observable.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Locale formatting is outside retried canonical state transitions.

**Verification method:** Concurrency stress test and failure injection.

**REQUIREMENT 0742 OF 1120  |  POSTGRESQL DATA ARCHITECTURE AND OPERATIONS**

## ERP-POSTGRES-042 — Idempotency for retried commands

**Normative requirement:** Externally retriable create/post commands shall accept a tenant-scoped idempotency key persisted atomically with the business result and request fingerprint.

**Rationale:** Network retries must not duplicate financial or inventory effects.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Repeating the same key and same fingerprint returns the original result and creates one business record.

**AC 2.** Reusing the key with a different fingerprint is rejected and audited.

**Exception / edge case:** Key expiry/retention is configured per integration contract; expiration cannot reopen duplicate risk for posted transactions.

**Security and audit implications:** Keys are non-authorizing, stored securely, and excluded from ordinary logs.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Fingerprint is computed from canonical values, not localized formatting or display strings.

**Verification method:** API-to-database duplicate request test under concurrent submission.

**REQUIREMENT 0743 OF 1120  |  POSTGRESQL DATA ARCHITECTURE AND OPERATIONS**

## ERP-POSTGRES-043 — Atomic posting and ledger invariants

**Normative requirement:** Financial posting shall persist the source transition, balanced journal lines, period reference, and outbox event atomically in one PostgreSQL transaction or equivalent durable commit boundary.

**Rationale:** A partially posted transaction breaks financial reconciliation and downstream consumers.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Injected failure at each write step leaves either all posting rows and event or none.

**AC 2.** Configured balancing invariant rejects a journal whose debits and credits do not balance at the configured currency precision.

**Exception / edge case:** Different ledger bases, currencies, and local reporting rules are explicit configuration/extensions rather than universal assumptions.

**Security and audit implications:** Posting actor, approval reference, reversal link, and before/after status are auditable; posted records are not silently overwritten.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Amounts are canonical; translated account names do not affect journal keys or balance computation.

**Verification method:** Transactional integration test and reconciliation query.

**REQUIREMENT 0744 OF 1120  |  POSTGRESQL DATA ARCHITECTURE AND OPERATIONS**

## ERP-POSTGRES-044 — Inventory concurrency invariants

**Normative requirement:** Inventory quantity updates shall use conditional atomic updates, row locks, or serializable logic to enforce configured availability/reservation rules under concurrent requests.

**Rationale:** Lost updates and overselling can occur when business checks are separated from writes.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Two concurrent reservations against insufficient stock yield no more than the configured available quantity.

**AC 2.** A failed conflict returns a stable domain outcome and does not leave an orphan reservation.

**Exception / edge case:** Backorders, negative stock, and unit-of-measure conversion are configurable by product/location policy.

**Security and audit implications:** Stock adjustments require authorized actor and reason; retries cannot duplicate movement IDs.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Units and decimal separators are normalized before persistence; localized unit labels are presentation only.

**Verification method:** Concurrent integration test with deterministic stock contention.

**REQUIREMENT 0745 OF 1120  |  POSTGRESQL DATA ARCHITECTURE AND OPERATIONS**

## ERP-POSTGRES-045 — Deadlock discipline

**Normative requirement:** Multi-row write workflows shall acquire locks in a deterministic key order and expose bounded deadlock retry behavior for declared retry-safe operations.

**Rationale:** Consistent lock ordering reduces deadlocks; some remain possible and require safe handling.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Stress test of opposite-order requests completes within timeout without persistent deadlock loops.

**AC 2.** Deadlock telemetry captures SQLSTATE 40P01 and workflow correlation ID.

**Exception / edge case:** A business workflow with unavoidable lock ordering differences documents rationale and escalation path.

**Security and audit implications:** Logs do not include full sensitive SQL parameter values; deadlock details are privilege-limited.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** No locale-sensitive ordering of lock keys is permitted.

**Verification method:** Concurrency stress test and structured telemetry assertion.

**REQUIREMENT 0746 OF 1120  |  POSTGRESQL DATA ARCHITECTURE AND OPERATIONS**

## ERP-POSTGRES-046 — Foreign-key delete behavior

**Normative requirement:** Foreign keys shall declare explicit delete/update actions; cascading destructive behavior shall be limited to dependent technical rows and never silently cascade across posted business records.

**Rationale:** Implicit deletion behavior can erase records needed for audit, reconciliation, or downstream links.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Schema review reports every FK action and tests representative delete/restrict behavior.

**AC 2.** Attempting to delete a referenced posted business entity fails or follows an approved reversal/archive workflow.

**Exception / edge case:** Disposable staging rows may cascade if ownership and retention are explicitly documented.

**Security and audit implications:** Destructive actions require permission, reason, and audit trail; referential errors are not bypassed by application flags.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Localized display text deletion does not remove canonical reference entities.

**Verification method:** Catalog FK-action test and deletion workflow integration test.

**REQUIREMENT 0747 OF 1120  |  POSTGRESQL DATA ARCHITECTURE AND OPERATIONS**

## ERP-POSTGRES-047 — Soft-delete semantics

**Normative requirement:** Soft-delete shall be used only for entities whose business lifecycle permits logical deactivation; records requiring immutable history shall use status/reversal events instead of destructive update.

**Rationale:** A single deletion flag is not a substitute for accounting or domain lifecycle semantics.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Entity catalog declares hard-delete, soft-delete, or immutable/reversal policy.

**AC 2.** Queries and unique indexes define whether inactive rows participate in business uniqueness.

**Exception / edge case:** Privacy deletion requirements may mandate anonymization or purge; implement via approved data-class policy and legal hold.

**Security and audit implications:** Delete/deactivate actions are permission-checked and include actor, timestamp, and reason where policy requires.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Translated labels are deactivated consistently; language fallback must not resurrect a deleted entity.

**Verification method:** Domain tests for deactivate/reactivate/duplicate and purge policy.

**REQUIREMENT 0748 OF 1120  |  POSTGRESQL DATA ARCHITECTURE AND OPERATIONS**

## ERP-POSTGRES-048 — Audit event persistence

**Normative requirement:** Material create, update, delete/deactivate, permission, configuration, and posting actions shall append a structured audit event correlated to actor, tenant, entity, operation, and timestamp.

**Rationale:** A durable audit trail supports investigation and accountability.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** For each designated action, the audit event is committed with or durably linked to the business transaction.

**AC 2.** Audit queries can filter by tenant/entity/time and produce the expected event sequence for a test workflow.

**Exception / edge case:** High-volume telemetry that is not business audit may be sampled separately but cannot replace required audit events.

**Security and audit implications:** Audit read/write permissions are segregated; events resist ordinary application-user modification and carry correlation IDs.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Audit labels can be localized at display time; canonical action codes and source values remain language-neutral.

**Verification method:** Workflow audit integration tests, role tests, and event sequence assertion.

**REQUIREMENT 0749 OF 1120  |  POSTGRESQL DATA ARCHITECTURE AND OPERATIONS**

## ERP-POSTGRES-049 — Before/after change capture

**Normative requirement:** Audit events for controlled mutable fields shall identify changed field names and old/new values or approved hashes, with field-level redaction rules.

**Rationale:** An action-only log may be insufficient to explain important master-data and permission changes.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Changing a test-controlled field produces expected old/new values in audit view.

**AC 2.** Sensitive-field policy test confirms secret/credential fields are redacted and cannot be recovered from general audit exports.

**Exception / edge case:** Large JSON/document updates may store a canonical diff or immutable version reference instead of full duplicate payload.

**Security and audit implications:** Audit data is access-restricted, tamper-evident by storage/retention controls, and excluded from ordinary user logs.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Diffs compare canonical text; translation rows identify language tag so translated edits remain distinguishable.

**Verification method:** Audit diff tests across normal and sensitive fields.

**REQUIREMENT 0750 OF 1120  |  POSTGRESQL DATA ARCHITECTURE AND OPERATIONS**

## ERP-POSTGRES-050 — Audit retention configuration

**Normative requirement:** Audit storage and export shall follow configurable retention, residency, and access policies approved for each deployment, with immutable evidence of policy changes.

**Rationale:** Audit duration and location may be governed by customer policy or jurisdiction rather than universal law.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Policy can define retention, archive destination, access role, and effective time.

**AC 2.** Policy test verifies eligible audit partitions/rows are retained or removed only after hold checks.

**Exception / edge case:** Pending investigation or legal hold prevents scheduled expiry until an authorized release is recorded.

**Security and audit implications:** Audit policy administration is separately privileged and generates a meta-audit event.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Localized policy descriptions do not alter machine retention parameters.

**Verification method:** Policy simulator and hold/expiry integration test.

**REQUIREMENT 0751 OF 1120  |  POSTGRESQL DATA ARCHITECTURE AND OPERATIONS**

## ERP-POSTGRES-051 — Sensitive-data catalog

**Normative requirement:** Every persisted field/table shall be assigned a data classification and owner, including whether it contains personal, financial, confidential, or public information.

**Rationale:** Classification drives access, encryption, logging, retention, and export controls.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Schema catalog coverage reaches 100% of application tables/columns or documented table-level inheritance.

**AC 2.** CI blocks addition of a new sensitive field without classification and owner metadata.

**Exception / edge case:** Unknown imported payloads default to restricted classification until triaged.

**Security and audit implications:** Classification maps to permission sets, log redaction, and retention; audit reads are restricted for sensitive classes.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Classification is independent of content language; localized free text receives the same class as the underlying field.

**Verification method:** Catalog completeness check and schema-change CI test.

**REQUIREMENT 0752 OF 1120  |  POSTGRESQL DATA ARCHITECTURE AND OPERATIONS**

## ERP-POSTGRES-052 — Tenant export and erasure workflow

**Normative requirement:** Tenant data export, closure, and deletion shall use a reviewed workflow that enumerates data stores, dependencies, legal holds, and jurisdiction-specific obligations before execution.

**Rationale:** Tenant termination and data-subject requests have different scopes and legal outcomes.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Dry run enumerates tenant-owned rows, attachments, derived data, replicas, and archive status with counts.

**AC 2.** Execution records approval, scope, completion status, and exceptions; no untracked tenant remnants remain in active stores.

**Exception / edge case:** Statutory retention, legal hold, shared reference data, or independently controlled records may prevent full erasure and require documented handling.

**Security and audit implications:** Export is tenant-scoped, encrypted, time-limited, and access-logged; deletion uses least privilege.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Export preserves original scripts and BCP 47 tags; translated text is not substituted for source values.

**Verification method:** End-to-end tenant lifecycle test with held and archived records.

**REQUIREMENT 0753 OF 1120  |  POSTGRESQL DATA ARCHITECTURE AND OPERATIONS**

## ERP-POSTGRES-053 — Transport encryption

**Normative requirement:** All remote application-to-PostgreSQL connections shall use TLS with certificate validation, and plaintext network access shall be disabled or explicitly limited to a private local socket boundary.

**Rationale:** Database credentials and data must not traverse untrusted networks in cleartext.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Connection health check rejects invalid/untrusted certificates and verifies expected server identity.

**AC 2.** Network scan/config inspection finds no externally reachable plaintext PostgreSQL listener.

**Exception / edge case:** Local development may use a private isolated network with synthetic data; production exceptions require documented compensating controls and expiration.

**Security and audit implications:** Certificate rotation and failed validation events are monitored; credentials are not logged.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** No locale effect; operator error messages are localized but retain secure diagnostics.

**Verification method:** TLS handshake test and deployment/network configuration audit.

**REQUIREMENT 0754 OF 1120  |  POSTGRESQL DATA ARCHITECTURE AND OPERATIONS**

## ERP-POSTGRES-054 — Secret lifecycle for DB credentials

**Normative requirement:** Database credentials and certificates shall be delivered from an approved secret manager, rotated under a defined policy, and kept out of source control and client bundles.

**Rationale:** Static credentials in artifacts create long-lived compromise risk.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Repository scanning detects no live connection secret in source, build output, or Next.js public variables.

**AC 2.** Rotation test changes a credential without rebuilding frontend assets and confirms old credential revocation.

**Exception / edge case:** Provider-managed identity may replace passwords where supported; fallback secrets retain equivalent vault/audit controls.

**Security and audit implications:** Secret access is scoped to service identity and logged; break-glass retrieval is time-limited.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Secrets and locale-specific connection settings are never embedded in translation files.

**Verification method:** Secret scan, rotation drill, and deployment manifest inspection.

**REQUIREMENT 0755 OF 1120  |  POSTGRESQL DATA ARCHITECTURE AND OPERATIONS**

## ERP-POSTGRES-055 — Encrypted backup handling

**Normative requirement:** Database backups, WAL archives, exports, and snapshots shall be encrypted in transit and at rest with key ownership and rotation documented per deployment.

**Rationale:** Backup theft can expose the full tenant estate.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Backup storage policy reports encryption status and key identifier for each backup set.

**AC 2.** Restore rehearsal proves approved keys can decrypt a backup while unauthorized identity cannot.

**Exception / edge case:** Customer-managed key loss or rotation incompatibility triggers a controlled stop and recovery process; no key is stored only with the backup.

**Security and audit implications:** Backup access is separated from database runtime access and logged; retention and key deletion follow approved policy.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Encryption is transparent to stored language data; export validation preserves Unicode.

**Verification method:** Storage configuration inspection and restore/decryption authorization test.

**REQUIREMENT 0756 OF 1120  |  POSTGRESQL DATA ARCHITECTURE AND OPERATIONS**

## ERP-POSTGRES-056 — Backup coverage and recovery targets

**Normative requirement:** Each production database shall have an approved backup design matching declared RPO/RTO, with scheduled logical backups and/or base backup plus continuous WAL archiving as appropriate.

**Rationale:** Different backup modes have distinct restoration capabilities; high-availability replication is not itself a backup.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Backup monitor reports last successful backup/WAL archive age against configured objectives.

**AC 2.** A recovery test restores to an approved timestamp or snapshot within the documented RTO measurement.

**Exception / edge case:** A tenant-specific partial restore may need a separate logical-export procedure because physical/PITR recovery can restore a whole cluster/database scope.

**Security and audit implications:** Backup jobs use restricted roles, encrypted destinations, and alert on missing archive sequence.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Restore maps preserve timestamps and translation records; exported filenames are locale-neutral.

**Verification method:** Automated backup validation and timed restore exercise.

**REQUIREMENT 0757 OF 1120  |  POSTGRESQL DATA ARCHITECTURE AND OPERATIONS**

## ERP-POSTGRES-057 — Restore drill and reconciliation

**Normative requirement:** Operations shall perform scheduled restore drills that verify database consistency, tenant boundaries, schema version, and key cross-module reconciliation before declaring recovery successful.

**Rationale:** A backup that has not been restored is unproven.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Drill evidence includes restore point, elapsed time, integrity checks, and exception list.

**AC 2.** Post-restore reconciliation validates critical record counts and financial/inventory control totals against captured expectations.

**Exception / edge case:** If source systems changed after the recovery point, recovery procedure records replay/reconciliation or accepted loss window.

**Security and audit implications:** Restore access is restricted and data is isolated from production routing until approval.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Drill compares canonical stored data; localized report rendering is separately smoke-tested for configured locales.

**Verification method:** Quarterly or policy-scheduled full restore exercise with signed result.

**REQUIREMENT 0758 OF 1120  |  POSTGRESQL DATA ARCHITECTURE AND OPERATIONS**

## ERP-POSTGRES-058 — Failover and durability policy

**Normative requirement:** The database service shall declare primary/standby topology, synchronous/asynchronous commit behavior, failover authority, and data-loss expectation for each environment.

**Rationale:** Replication modes trade latency, availability, and potential loss; “HA” does not mean zero loss by default.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Topology health check records primary and replica roles and replication lag.

**AC 2.** Failover exercise measures data-loss window and recovery time against approved objectives.

**Exception / edge case:** Regional network partition or split-brain risk is handled by one authoritative failover controller and documented fencing.

**Security and audit implications:** Promotion authority is restricted and failover actions are audit-recorded.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Failover notices localize operator messaging without changing ordering/canonical transaction identifiers.

**Verification method:** Game-day failover exercise and topology configuration audit.

**REQUIREMENT 0759 OF 1120  |  POSTGRESQL DATA ARCHITECTURE AND OPERATIONS**

## ERP-POSTGRES-059 — Replica read consistency

**Normative requirement:** Reads routed to asynchronous replicas shall be explicitly marked as potentially stale; read-after-write, posting, and authorization decisions shall use primary or a consistency token/LSN policy.

**Rationale:** Asynchronous replication can lag, so routing all reads to a replica may return stale state.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Test writes a record then issues a consistency-sensitive read and confirms it observes the committed change.

**AC 2.** A stale replica response is either avoided or reports version/lag semantics according to API contract.

**Exception / edge case:** Analytics and noncritical dashboards may accept measured staleness under a declared freshness SLA.

**Security and audit implications:** Authorization and tenant existence decisions never rely solely on lagging replica state.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Locale rendering does not mask stale/missing translation state.

**Verification method:** Replica-lag injection test and routing contract test.

**REQUIREMENT 0760 OF 1120  |  POSTGRESQL DATA ARCHITECTURE AND OPERATIONS**

## ERP-POSTGRES-060 — Logical replication contract

**Normative requirement:** Logical replication shall be used only for documented table/data movement or read models, with explicit publication scope, replica identity, DDL rollout, sequence handling, and conflict ownership.

**Rationale:** Logical replication transmits selected row changes but does not remove the need to manage schema and conflicts.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Publication inventory matches approved table/column list and has a documented owner.

**AC 2.** Initial sync and steady-state tests verify row counts/checksums and monitor apply lag.

**Exception / edge case:** Bidirectional writes to replicated rows are prohibited unless a conflict-resolution design is approved and tested.

**Security and audit implications:** Replication credentials have minimum publication privileges and do not bypass tenant controls for general query access.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Replicated localization rows retain BCP 47 tags and are validated against subscriber schema version.

**Verification method:** Replication rehearsal, privilege audit, and lag monitoring test.

**REQUIREMENT 0761 OF 1120  |  POSTGRESQL DATA ARCHITECTURE AND OPERATIONS**

## ERP-POSTGRES-061 — Analytics isolation

**Normative requirement:** Heavy analytics, search indexing, and exports shall use a bounded read model, replica, or warehouse contract rather than unbounded reporting queries against the transactional primary.

**Rationale:** Isolation protects interactive posting latency and supports separate retention/access rules.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Load test for approved reports does not exceed primary latency/error budget at target concurrency.

**AC 2.** Analytics extract defines freshness, included tenant scope, and deletion/retention propagation behavior.

**Exception / edge case:** An urgent operational report may query primary through a rate-limited approved path and return within a statement timeout.

**Security and audit implications:** Derived stores preserve tenant authorization and classification; exports are access-logged.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Read model retains language tags and source locale metadata rather than pre-translating canonical values.

**Verification method:** Load isolation test and data lineage/access review.

**REQUIREMENT 0762 OF 1120  |  POSTGRESQL DATA ARCHITECTURE AND OPERATIONS**

## ERP-POSTGRES-062 — Transactional outbox contract

**Normative requirement:** Cross-module and external integration events shall be written to a tenant-scoped transactional outbox in the same commit as the source business change.

**Rationale:** The outbox avoids a lost-message gap between database commit and external publish.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Failure after DB commit but before broker publish results in eventual delivery from outbox without duplicate business transition.

**AC 2.** Consumers can deduplicate using stable event ID and idempotent handling.

**Exception / edge case:** Outbox retention or archival may be shortened only after delivery/consumer acknowledgement policy is met.

**Security and audit implications:** Outbox payload contains only authorized minimum data; tenant ID and actor correlation are protected and audited.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Event payload uses canonical codes and language tags for localized text; no localized display string is required for machine processing.

**Verification method:** Crash-injection test and consumer duplicate-delivery test.

**REQUIREMENT 0763 OF 1120  |  POSTGRESQL DATA ARCHITECTURE AND OPERATIONS**

## ERP-POSTGRES-063 — Bulk import staging

**Normative requirement:** Bulk imports shall land in tenant-scoped staging tables or an equivalent isolated batch area, validate schema and row-level errors, and promote accepted data atomically or in resumable chunks.

**Rationale:** Direct bulk writes can bypass business validation and make partial recovery difficult.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Import fixture with valid and invalid rows yields exact accepted/rejected counts and row references.

**AC 2.** Retrying a batch does not duplicate accepted rows because batch and row idempotency keys are enforced.

**Exception / edge case:** Very large batches may commit in chunks only when the import contract declares partial completion and supports restart from a checkpoint.

**Security and audit implications:** Staging access expires or is purged by policy; rejected-row files are encrypted and avoid unnecessary PII copies.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** CSV decimal/date parsing requires declared locale/encoding; original source text is retained where reconciliation needs it.

**Verification method:** Import integration tests for duplicates, malformed Unicode, rollback, and resume.

**REQUIREMENT 0764 OF 1120  |  POSTGRESQL DATA ARCHITECTURE AND OPERATIONS**

## ERP-POSTGRES-064 — Bulk mutation bounds

**Normative requirement:** Bulk updates and deletes shall use bounded batches, deterministic checkpoints, statement timeouts, and progress records for restartable maintenance or migration jobs.

**Rationale:** Unbounded transactions can hold locks, generate excessive WAL, and delay recovery.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Injected process termination resumes from last committed checkpoint without skipped or duplicate rows.

**AC 2.** Batch execution exposes processed/remaining counts and does not exceed approved lock-duration threshold.

**Exception / edge case:** Small table operations may use a single transaction when proven safe and specifically declared.

**Security and audit implications:** Job identity and target tenant/range are recorded; cancellation cannot broaden scope.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Batch order is based on stable IDs/time keys, never localized text order.

**Verification method:** Job interruption/restart test and lock/WAL telemetry check.

**REQUIREMENT 0765 OF 1120  |  POSTGRESQL DATA ARCHITECTURE AND OPERATIONS**

## ERP-POSTGRES-065 — Query telemetry and correlation

**Normative requirement:** Database operations shall expose normalized query latency, errors, connection saturation, deadlocks, replication lag, and transaction duration linked to application trace IDs without sensitive bind values.

**Rationale:** Performance and failure diagnosis require cross-tier observability while protecting data.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Dashboards report p50/p95/p99 query latency and error counts by service/workflow within configured windows.

**AC 2.** Automated test confirms SQL parameters containing seeded secrets do not appear in telemetry.

**Exception / edge case:** Low-volume tenants are aggregated or omitted from shared dashboards where metrics could reveal their activity.

**Security and audit implications:** Telemetry is role-restricted, retention-limited, and redacted; trace IDs do not authorize access.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Error categories are stable language-neutral codes; operator dashboards may translate descriptions.

**Verification method:** Synthetic query/error test and log redaction scan.

**REQUIREMENT 0766 OF 1120  |  POSTGRESQL DATA ARCHITECTURE AND OPERATIONS**

## ERP-POSTGRES-066 — Slow-query review process

**Normative requirement:** Queries exceeding configured duration/volume thresholds shall be captured in normalized form and triaged with EXPLAIN evidence before index or schema changes.

**Rationale:** Planner estimates and measured execution behavior guide safe tuning.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Threshold alert includes query fingerprint, duration distribution, database, and trace sample without raw sensitive literals.

**AC 2.** Tuning ticket includes representative plan, buffer data, before/after metric, and rollback criteria.

**Exception / edge case:** Rare one-off administrative queries may be excluded by approved tag and remain statement-timeout bounded.

**Security and audit implications:** Plan capture respects role grants and does not export row values or credentials.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Search workloads cover target locales and scripts when evaluating plans.

**Verification method:** Synthetic slow-query alert test and EXPLAIN review artifact.

**REQUIREMENT 0767 OF 1120  |  POSTGRESQL DATA ARCHITECTURE AND OPERATIONS**

## ERP-POSTGRES-067 — Vacuum and statistics health

**Normative requirement:** Production PostgreSQL shall retain autovacuum and analyze coverage for every application database and alert on stale statistics, table bloat indicators, or transaction-ID age thresholds.

**Rationale:** Vacuum reclaims reusable space, updates planner stats, and protects against transaction ID wraparound.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Monitoring shows autovacuum/analyze activity and maximum transaction age by database/table.

**AC 2.** A write-heavy test table receives vacuum/analyze and query plan statistics update within configured operational bounds.

**Exception / edge case:** A deliberately long transaction or replication slot may delay cleanup; alert identifies blocking horizon and escalation owner.

**Security and audit implications:** Monitoring roles receive only necessary visibility; operational diagnostics do not include business payload.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** No locale dependency; labels in maintenance alerts may be localized.

**Verification method:** Maintenance dashboard test and long-transaction/wraparound alert simulation.

**REQUIREMENT 0768 OF 1120  |  POSTGRESQL DATA ARCHITECTURE AND OPERATIONS**

## ERP-POSTGRES-068 — Capacity and growth thresholds

**Normative requirement:** Database storage, WAL, table/index growth, connection counts, and backup archive capacity shall have forecasts and actionable alerts based on service-specific thresholds.

**Rationale:** Capacity exhaustion can stop writes or jeopardize recovery.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Forecast report projects threshold crossing based on measured growth window and identifies largest growth contributors.

**AC 2.** Alert tests fire before configured free-space/WAL/archive critical threshold and include operator action.

**Exception / edge case:** Unexpected tenant onboarding or import spike may trigger per-tenant admission controls without delaying unrelated tenants indefinitely.

**Security and audit implications:** Capacity reports aggregate tenant metrics according to access policy and avoid exposing customer names to unauthorized operators.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Capacity thresholds use canonical units; human-readable units are localized only in presentation.

**Verification method:** Load/growth simulation and alert routing test.

**REQUIREMENT 0769 OF 1120  |  POSTGRESQL DATA ARCHITECTURE AND OPERATIONS**

## ERP-POSTGRES-069 — Major-version upgrade rehearsal

**Normative requirement:** PostgreSQL major upgrades shall be rehearsed on production-scale representative data, validate extensions and application behavior, and use a documented cutover/rollback strategy before production execution.

**Rationale:** Major upgrades can change storage format and behavior; dump/restore, pg_upgrade, and replication methods have different constraints.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Rehearsal compares schema, row counts, checksums/control totals, query plans, and application contract tests.

**AC 2.** Cutover plan defines freeze/replication lag threshold, validation gate, rollback decision deadline, and recovery point.

**Exception / edge case:** When rollback after writes is not safe, use forward-fix or restore plan and explicitly state that rollback is not data-loss-free.

**Security and audit implications:** Upgrade operators use privileged change control and preserve logs, test evidence, and version inventory.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Collation/provider changes are included in multilingual sort/search regression tests.

**Verification method:** Full upgrade rehearsal and signed change approval.

**REQUIREMENT 0770 OF 1120  |  POSTGRESQL DATA ARCHITECTURE AND OPERATIONS**

## ERP-POSTGRES-070 — Frontend and API database boundary

**Normative requirement:** The Next.js frontend shall access ERP data only through authenticated ASP.NET Core APIs and shall never connect directly to PostgreSQL or ship database credentials.

**Rationale:** A browser is an untrusted client and cannot enforce database security boundaries.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Production client bundles and network traces contain no PostgreSQL host, user, password, or protocol connection.

**AC 2.** API tests enforce tenant authorization, validation, and stable locale-aware response contracts before database access.

**Exception / edge case:** Static Next.js export may be used only for routes that need no server-side capability; authenticated ERP data routes remain behind the API/runtime boundary.

**Security and audit implications:** API identity maps to narrowly scoped application services; client-supplied tenant IDs are re-authorized.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** The API carries BCP 47 language preferences and formats display output without changing canonical stored values.

**Verification method:** Bundle secret scan, network inspection, and end-to-end authorization/locale test.

# Next.js Frontend Architecture, Performance, and Accessibility

# Chapter 12 — Next.js frontend architecture, performance, and accessibility

## Scope and product baseline

This chapter specifies the lightweight web frontend for a multi-tenant commercial ERP serving mid-market and enterprise organizations. It covers route and component architecture, the browser-to-server boundary, backend integration, performance, multilingual presentation, and accessibility. It does not specify accounting, tax, privacy, records-retention, employment, health, or other jurisdictional/industry rules. Those rules, notices, data retention periods, field validation, and legally required workflows must be supplied through versioned tenant, legal-entity, or industry-extension configuration and authoritative backend contracts; the shared UI must not infer them from language or region alone.

The requested ASP.NET Core baseline is .NET 11, the stable GA release listed by Microsoft's support policy on 2026-11-22. Microsoft records its GA date as November 10, 2026, classifies it as STS, and gives November 14, 2028 as end of support. Use the latest servicing patch available at build and deployment time; the official policy page's release table must be checked again before release because it is updated monthly. The same policy lists .NET 10 as active LTS, so organizations preferring a longer support track may choose it through an explicit platform decision rather than calling it the newest release \[9].

The exact Next.js patch/minor and PostgreSQL server versions are intentionally not asserted here: the consulted official Next.js material documents architecture and practices but does not establish a single latest stable release, and this chapter does not lock a PostgreSQL server release. The implementation owner shall pin compatible stable releases in the build/deployment baseline and reconfirm their support status at procurement and release. Next.js App Router is the selected architecture, using Server Components by default and client islands for interaction \[1] \[2] \[3]. The frontend is not an alternate system of record. ASP.NET Core APIs own business rules, identity/authorization decisions, transaction semantics, audit records, and authoritative tenant boundaries. PostgreSQL is the persistent store; its row-security behavior, including table-owner and privileged-role bypass cases, belongs in backend/database controls and testing, not in frontend assumptions \[10].

The baseline accessibility target is WCAG 2.2 Level AA for application-owned workflows, with manual and automated verification. WCAG conformance is the target, not a claim of certification or a substitute for obligations applicable in a specific market \[11]. The W3C ARIA Authoring Practices Guide informs custom widget behavior; native HTML semantics are preferred when they suffice \[12]. Unicode CLDR-backed locale behavior informs formatting and language adaptation, while formatting never substitutes for a jurisdiction's legal or accounting policy \[13].

## Actors and core entities

The principal actors are: an authenticated employee or operator; a tenant administrator configuring users, language, modules, and extensions; a business approver acting within delegated permissions; a localization or accessibility reviewer; an integration operator diagnosing service failures; and a separately controlled platform support operator. A single identity may belong to multiple tenants, but tenant selection is not itself authorization.

Frontend-relevant entities are Principal, Session, Tenant, TenantMembership, Role/Permission, LocalePreference, TenantConfiguration, ModuleManifest, Route, ViewModel, API Contract, Cache Entry, Workflow Command, Audit/Correlation Reference, Notification, and Translation Catalog. These entities have distinct owners: identity and permissions are resolved by the identity/backend services; tenant configuration and module entitlements by authorized backend administration; route state and transient view state by the frontend; audit evidence by backend services; translation resources by release-governed catalogs or approved tenant configuration.

## Workflows

**1. Sign-in and tenant selection:** authenticate through the configured identity contract, resolve membership server-side, choose an authorized tenant when multiple memberships exist, and load the tenant's enabled modules and locale policy. Sign-in, invitation, and password recovery can use a public layout; they do not receive protected workspace data.

**2. Navigate and retrieve:** resolve the supported locale and tenant context, render the shared workspace shell, and call the server-only data layer or the constrained BFF. Each operation rechecks identity, tenant, resource, and permission. List routes validate filters and use bounded server pagination.

**3. Edit, submit, and approve:** collect accessible, localized input; validate it in the browser for feedback and again in ASP.NET Core as authority; request confirmation when the configured action is consequential; show pending state; accept success only from the server; then refresh/invalidate affected data. Long-running operations transition to a server-owned job state.

**4. Configure or extend:** tenant administrators enable only compatible module manifests and locales. Industry/jurisdiction extensions contribute versioned API and presentation contracts. An absent or stale rule configuration blocks the affected workflow or routes to administration; the shared UI does not invent a legal default.

**5. Recover and diagnose:** present localized, non-sensitive errors with correlation references, while structured details and authoritative audit events stay in access-controlled backend telemetry. Session expiry returns the user safely to the interrupted workflow without replaying a consequential command automatically.

## Permission and trust boundaries

The browser is an untrusted presentation tier. Hiding a menu, disabling a control, filtering a list, or checking a route in a layout is never sufficient authorization. The Next.js server boundary protects credentials and composes UI, but Server Actions and Route Handlers are independently callable entry points and must authenticate, authorize, validate input, and minimize returned fields at the operation/data boundary \[4]. A BFF is a narrow adapter to fixed ASP.NET Core endpoints, not a general-purpose proxy; it forwards only required headers and uses bounded request sizes/timeouts \[6].

The backend resolves tenant membership and permission for every operation. PostgreSQL row security can add defense in depth but is not presumed active by default, and privileged database roles can bypass it; application roles, policies, and ownership must be verified explicitly \[10]. Next.js cache isolation is a separate boundary: any user-, tenant-, permission-, locale-, or configuration-dependent representation must be request-private or keyed and invalidated using all relevant dimensions \[5] \[7]. Audit truth and business state reside in backend services, not local browser state or client telemetry.

## Major architecture decisions

- Use App Router route segments and shared layouts; keep route shells, data composition, and non-interactive UI in Server Components. Restrict use client to the smallest interactive subtree because its imports join the client module graph \[1] \[2] \[3].
- Use a server-only Data Access Layer returning typed minimal view models. Use Server Actions for tightly scoped form mutations only when each action checks authentication, authorization, input, and resource scope. Use Route Handlers for explicit browser-facing BFF contracts or streaming interfaces, not as an extra hop from Server Components \[2] \[4] \[6].
- Make the ASP.NET Core API the business-policy authority. Next.js is a thin view/BFF layer and must not encode accounting, legal, or industry-specific policy as a universal assumption.
- Treat personalized ERP routes as dynamic/private by default until their cache class, key dimensions, freshness window, and invalidation behavior are reviewed. For multi-instance hosting, coordinate cache and tag invalidation or disable shared caching for those paths; deploy consistent artifacts and action-encryption configuration \[5] \[7].
- Use locale-qualified routes or equivalent explicit locale context, a defined precedence for preference resolution, validated catalogs, and lang/direction metadata. User language, tenant defaults, time zone, legal entity, currency, and jurisdiction are separate concepts \[8] \[13].
- Target WCAG 2.2 AA; use Next's route announcements and lint support where applicable, but do not equate automated linting with conformance \[11] \[14]. Forms, tables, dialogs, alerts, and custom widgets need explicit keyboard, focus, naming, and error behavior \[12] \[15].

## Dependencies and cross-module contracts

The frontend depends on: the selected .NET/ASP.NET Core and PostgreSQL deployment baseline; a supported identity provider and session contract; versioned OpenAPI or equivalent APIs; stable permission and error-code vocabularies; tenant membership/configuration and module-entitlement services; a translation/catalog pipeline; supported browser and assistive-technology matrix; approved asset/CDN and telemetry services; and cache/deployment infrastructure that behaves consistently across instances. Independent services and pages should be fetched in parallel; slow panels should stream behind local Suspense boundaries where the workflow permits \[2] \[17].

Cross-module contracts shall standardize route and locale context, tenant identifiers as server-validated context, error envelope and correlation ID, pagination/cursor shape, idempotency and concurrency behavior for mutations, permission codes, DTO/view-model minimization, loading/empty/error states, module manifest version, extension translation namespace, and cache classification/invalidation. List ordering and locale-sensitive search must identify whether the backend or presentation layer owns the semantics. Industry-specific workflow steps and notices remain extension/API configuration. Data grids, form controls, dialogs, status messages, and navigation share design-system accessibility patterns rather than implementing incompatible module-local behavior \[12].

## Risks and controls

The highest-impact risks are cross-tenant disclosure through an unscoped cache or permissive API; authorization bypass through a direct Server Action or guessed identifier; stale workflow state after mutation; client bundle growth and hydration delay; multi-instance version skew; inaccessible data-dense grids/forms; locale-dependent parsing errors; and incorrectly universalized jurisdiction/industry rules. Controls include backend authorization and tenant-isolation tests, cache inventory and adversarial partition tests, production bundle/performance budgets, deployment skew tests, accessible end-to-end scenarios across locales and assistive technologies, and an explicit configuration boundary for varying rules. Next.js itself recommends production-like builds, performance measurement, bounded client components, secure action checks, and accessible fallbacks \[2]. Lazy-loaded tools, optimized local fonts/images, and structured streaming are performance tools, not guarantees; teams verify results in production-like deployment conditions \[16] \[17].

## Normative requirements

The following are 70 distinct requirements.
