Every requirement includes an identifier, normative statement, rationale, objectively testable acceptance criteria, an edge case, security/audit implications, localization implications, and a verification method. The JSON companion contains the same requirement objects as a machine-readable array.

### ERP-NEXTJS-001 — App Router application structure

**Shall.** The frontend shall use the Next.js App Router as the primary route and layout architecture, grouping pages by ERP capability and composing shared tenant, locale, and authenticated-workspace layouts without duplicating application shell code.

**Rationale.** A shared route-segment architecture supports modular ERP areas while enabling layouts, streaming, and gradual capability extensions.

**Acceptance criteria.**

**1.** A route inventory maps every in-scope screen to a named App Router segment and owning capability.

**2.** At least two separate module routes share the same authenticated workspace layout without duplicating its navigation implementation.

**Exception / edge case.** Public sign-in, invitation acceptance, and health or static-resource routes may use separate layouts and must not inherit authenticated workspace data.

**Security and audit.** Layouts may perform early session checks but are not an authorization boundary; sensitive access is rechecked at the data/API boundary. Route ownership and public-route exceptions are reviewed with every route addition.

**Multilingual and localization.** Place locale as a stable route segment or a tenant-approved domain mapping; all protected routes must resolve the same explicit locale context.

**Verification.** Inspect route tree and architecture tests; run route smoke tests for shared and isolated layout cases.

### ERP-NEXTJS-002 — Server Components by default

**Shall.** The frontend shall implement route pages, layouts, data composition, and non-interactive presentation as Server Components unless browser-only state or event handling requires a Client Component.

**Rationale.** Server rendering limits client JavaScript and keeps privileged data access on the server while preserving interactive islands.

**Acceptance criteria.**

**1.** A static-analysis rule rejects unnecessary use client directives in route shells and server data modules.

**2.** A representative record-detail route renders its primary title and summary in server HTML before hydration.

**Exception / edge case.** A component depending on browser APIs, local transient interaction, or a supported client-only vendor SDK may be client-rendered behind a documented boundary.

**Security and audit.** Server rendering does not imply that output is authorized or safe to cache; server data functions must authorize before returning records and redact fields not intended for display.

**Multilingual and localization.** Server-side dictionary loading should avoid shipping complete translation catalogs to the browser when only rendered text is needed.

**Verification.** Review component module graphs and use a production browser trace to confirm representative content exists before hydration.

### ERP-NEXTJS-003 — Narrow client-module boundaries

**Shall.** Each Client Component boundary shall be placed at the smallest practical interactive subtree, and its imported dependency graph shall not include database clients, server credentials, or unrelated module screens.

**Rationale.** The use client boundary includes its imported module graph in the client bundle and can otherwise inflate payloads or expose server-only code.

**Acceptance criteria.**

**1.** Production bundle analysis identifies Client Component entry points and lists each entry's major imported dependencies.

**2.** A build fails if a client entry imports a package marked server-only or a configured secret-bearing module.

**Exception / edge case.** An interaction-heavy canvas or specialized workflow may require a large client island, but must load only on the route where it is used and include an accessible fallback.

**Security and audit.** No secret, database connection string, privileged token, or unredacted server entity may enter client props or JavaScript chunks.

**Multilingual and localization.** Client islands may receive only the localized labels they require; locale changes must update those labels without stale client state.

**Verification.** Run CI dependency-boundary checks and inspect source maps or bundle analyzer output for representative routes.

### ERP-NEXTJS-004 — Typed route and query contracts

**Shall.** The frontend shall define typed contracts for dynamic route parameters and query state, validate all externally supplied route values at runtime, and represent invalid or unsupported values through an explicit not-found or validation outcome.

**Rationale.** URL parameters are untrusted input and ERP list filters and entity identifiers drive sensitive data retrieval.

**Acceptance criteria.**

**1.** Type checking validates all route parameter access without unchecked casts in protected page modules.

**2.** Automated tests for malformed IDs, unknown tabs, and unsupported locales receive a controlled 4xx/not-found result rather than an unhandled exception.

**Exception / edge case.** A saved report may preserve unknown optional filter keys for forward compatibility, but they must be ignored or rejected by an explicit schema version rule.

**Security and audit.** Identifiers and filter values must be authorized on the server; opaque IDs and client-side validation do not prevent IDOR or injection.

**Multilingual and localization.** Locale route parameters are matched against a configured allowlist and must not be used as arbitrary filesystem or import paths.

**Verification.** Run TypeScript build checks and parameter fuzz tests against page and API route contracts.

### ERP-NEXTJS-005 — Route-level error and not-found UI

**Shall.** Each authenticated module route shall provide a localized error boundary and not-found response that disclose no stack trace or sensitive record details and offer a safe recovery action.

**Rationale.** ERP workflows require predictable recovery from backend failures and must not leak implementation or tenant data through error UI.

**Acceptance criteria.**

**1.** A forced module exception renders the module error component with a retry action and generic user-facing message.

**2.** A missing or unauthorized resource does not render a record title, identifier, or payload in the response body or browser console.

**Exception / edge case.** A validation failure may show field-specific safe feedback; a record hidden by authorization may intentionally be represented as not found to avoid existence disclosure.

**Security and audit.** Technical details go only to access-controlled telemetry with correlation IDs; user-visible content excludes stack traces, SQL text, tokens, and cross-tenant identifiers.

**Multilingual and localization.** Error titles, retry labels, and help text use locale dictionaries, while machine-readable error codes remain locale-neutral.

**Verification.** Inject server errors and missing/forbidden records in integration tests; inspect UI text and captured telemetry separately.

### ERP-NEXTJS-006 — Authenticated workspace session handling

**Shall.** The frontend shall establish authenticated server requests from a secure session mechanism and shall not treat a client-visible role, tenant, or user identifier as proof of identity or permission.

**Rationale.** Session state is needed for server-rendered application navigation, but browser state is user-controlled.

**Acceptance criteria.**

**1.** An unauthenticated request to each protected route redirects or returns an authentication response without rendering protected data.

**2.** Tampering with client storage or a submitted user/role value does not change the server-authorized identity.

**Exception / edge case.** A short-lived invitation or password-reset flow may be unauthenticated but is constrained by a server-validated, expiring, single-purpose token.

**Security and audit.** Session establishment, revocation, expiration, and privilege changes are enforced by the identity/backend contract; session identifiers are excluded from telemetry.

**Multilingual and localization.** Login and recovery interfaces localize prompts and errors without changing token semantics or exposing account-enumeration details by locale.

**Verification.** Exercise valid, expired, revoked, and tampered sessions through browser and direct HTTP tests.

### ERP-NEXTJS-007 — Per-operation authorization checks

**Shall.** Every Server Action, Route Handler, server-side mutation, and sensitive record read shall verify the authenticated principal, active tenant, resource scope, and required permission at the operation boundary.

**Rationale.** A route-level or layout-level check does not protect separately callable server functions or resources.

**Acceptance criteria.**

**1.** Tests invoke every mutation endpoint directly without navigating through its page and confirm unauthorized calls are rejected.

**2.** A user with access to one tenant or record cannot read or modify another by substituting its ID in the request.

**Exception / edge case.** System-level support operations may cross tenant scope only through a separately granted, time-bounded privileged capability with an explicit reason.

**Security and audit.** Authorization denials and privileged cross-scope actions are auditable; logs record actor, tenant, action, resource class, decision, and correlation ID, but not secrets.

**Multilingual and localization.** Permission checks use stable permission identifiers, never translated role names or localized UI labels.

**Verification.** Run direct-call authorization matrix tests across roles, tenant IDs, resource IDs, and revocation states.

### ERP-NEXTJS-008 — Server-only data access layer

**Shall.** All privileged data access and policy composition shall be implemented in server-only modules behind a Data Access Layer that returns minimal, typed view models to pages and actions.

**Rationale.** A centralized server-only layer limits accidental client imports and keeps authorization, data shaping, and API evolution consistent.

**Acceptance criteria.**

**1.** A build-time boundary check fails if a client module imports a configured DAL or backend client.

**2.** A page response for a representative entity contains only fields declared in its view-model contract.

**Exception / edge case.** An offline-capable draft may use an explicitly defined local projection, but it must not include fields classified as restricted and must reconcile through authorized APIs.

**Security and audit.** DAL reads and mutations apply authorization before query results are exposed; DTO minimization is reviewed for sensitive fields and PII.

**Multilingual and localization.** The DAL returns stable codes and values; localized presentation is applied by the UI except where backend-owned translated content is explicitly part of the contract.

**Verification.** Use build boundary tests, DTO schema snapshots, and code review of DAL permission checks.

### ERP-NEXTJS-009 — Constrained backend-for-frontend proxy

**Shall.** When Next.js Route Handlers mediate requests to ASP.NET Core, they shall use an allowlisted backend origin and operation map, validate request method, content type, size, and schema, and forward only explicitly approved headers.

**Rationale.** A narrow BFF can adapt browser and backend contracts, but an open proxy risks SSRF, credential forwarding, and input abuse.

**Acceptance criteria.**

**1.** No client-supplied URL, host, or arbitrary path can change the upstream destination.

**2.** Requests exceeding configured body-size limits or with invalid schema are rejected before an upstream call; incoming cookies and authorization headers are not blindly copied.

**Exception / edge case.** Large binary upload/download operations may bypass body buffering through a separately authorized streaming or direct-upload contract.

**Security and audit.** Upstream credentials are server-only, redirects are constrained, timeouts are bounded, and proxy decisions are correlated without logging payload secrets.

**Multilingual and localization.** The BFF forwards an allowlisted locale context or accepts a validated locale field; it must not infer jurisdictional rules solely from browser language.

**Verification.** Pen-test redirect, host, path traversal, header-smuggling, oversized-body, invalid-content-type, and timeout cases.

### ERP-NEXTJS-010 — Explicit tenant context resolution

**Shall.** For each authenticated request, the frontend shall resolve tenant context from a server-validated session or trusted identity claim and bind that context to all subsequent backend calls; a tenant slug from a URL alone shall never establish access.

**Rationale.** Tenant-aware routes support organizations and subsidiaries without making a modifiable URL a data boundary.

**Acceptance criteria.**

**1.** Changing a tenant route segment without corresponding authorized membership yields a denial or safe tenant switch flow.

**2.** Every protected backend request includes the tenant context required by its documented API contract.

**Exception / edge case.** A user with multiple authorized tenants may choose one through a tenant switcher; switching revalidates membership and refreshes tenant-scoped data.

**Security and audit.** Tenant switch events and denied cross-tenant attempts are recorded; tenant identifiers are treated as sensitive and redacted from public error text.

**Multilingual and localization.** Tenant locale defaults and user locale preference remain separate values; selecting a tenant must not silently change language without an explicit product rule.

**Verification.** Automate cross-tenant URL substitution and authorized multi-tenant switch scenarios, then assert downstream request context.

### ERP-NEXTJS-011 — Tenant isolation is enforced server-side

**Shall.** The frontend shall treat tenant filters as usability controls only and require ASP.NET Core and PostgreSQL enforcement to prevent cross-tenant reads and writes independently of client-supplied filters.

**Rationale.** A frontend filter can be removed or forged; PostgreSQL row security has owner and privileged-role bypass conditions that the deployment must account for.

**Acceptance criteria.**

**1.** API contract tests show tenant A cannot retrieve or mutate tenant B records even when the browser submits tenant B identifiers.

**2.** Deployment review confirms application database roles are not superuser, table owner, or BYPASSRLS where row security is relied upon.

**Exception / edge case.** Shared global reference data may be visible to multiple tenants only when its classification and API scope explicitly designate it as non-tenant-owned.

**Security and audit.** The API/database is authoritative for isolation; frontend tests supplement but never substitute backend tenant security tests. Cross-tenant support access is separately audited.

**Multilingual and localization.** Tenant-specific translation and branding resources must be tenant-keyed and authorization-protected; they must not be shared through an unscoped cache.

**Verification.** Execute backend integration tests using separate tenant identities and inspect database roles, policies, and query paths.

### ERP-NEXTJS-012 — Tenant- and user-safe cache keys

**Shall.** Any cache containing user-, tenant-, permission-, locale-, or configuration-dependent output shall either be request-private or use a cache key that includes every dependency affecting authorization and representation.

**Rationale.** Next.js caching can reuse fetched data or rendered output; omission of tenant or identity dimensions can disclose another user's ERP data.

**Acceptance criteria.**

**1.** Automated tests request the same entity path as two tenants and two permission levels and verify no response contains another context's data.

**2.** A cache inventory records owner, key dimensions, lifetime, invalidation trigger, and whether data is sensitive for each application cache.

**Exception / edge case.** Immutable public assets and deliberately global reference data may use shared cache only when they contain no tenant-specific data and authorization does not affect the response.

**Security and audit.** Cache policy is reviewed as a security control; sensitive responses default to no-store or a verified private partition, and cache headers are inspected in production tests.

**Multilingual and localization.** Localized labels/content vary by locale and possibly tenant translation pack; locale and translation-pack revision must be part of any shared cache key.

**Verification.** Use cache poisoning/isolation tests with repeated requests across tenants, roles, locales, and deployment instances.

### ERP-NEXTJS-013 — Correlation-aware audit interaction

**Shall.** The frontend shall propagate a non-secret correlation identifier through requests and surface safe correlation references for failed consequential workflows without claiming that browser telemetry is the authoritative audit record.

**Rationale.** Operations teams need to trace a failed ERP interaction across Next.js, ASP.NET Core, and backend services while audit truth remains server-side.

**Acceptance criteria.**

**1.** Each BFF/API request has a validated or generated correlation ID returned in response metadata.

**2.** An error screen for a failed consequential operation displays the correlation reference and the backend emits its corresponding structured event.

**Exception / edge case.** For client-side offline validation failures with no server request, the UI must not fabricate a backend audit reference.

**Security and audit.** Correlation IDs are non-secret, length-limited, and cannot carry user data; authoritative actor, permission, and before/after audit facts are captured by backend services.

**Multilingual and localization.** The reference label and explanation are translated, while the correlation value and log field names remain invariant.

**Verification.** Trace a successful and rejected transaction from browser network record to backend structured logs using its correlation ID.

### ERP-NEXTJS-014 — Industry extension presentation boundary

**Shall.** The frontend shall load configurable industry extensions through versioned module contracts and feature manifests rather than embedding jurisdiction- or industry-specific rules in the shared ERP shell.

**Rationale.** Commercial ERP deployments vary by sector and jurisdiction; the shared frontend should present configured capabilities without asserting universal compliance logic.

**Acceptance criteria.**

**1.** Each extension declares API contract version, required permission codes, navigation contribution, locale resources, and feature dependencies.

**2.** An extension disabled for a tenant exposes neither its navigation entry nor a direct route capable of returning extension data.

**Exception / edge case.** A platform-wide accessibility, security, or navigation requirement cannot be disabled by an industry extension even if the extension supplies its own controls.

**Security and audit.** Extension manifests are authenticated, reviewed, and least-privilege; runtime module loading is restricted to approved build artifacts rather than tenant-provided executable code.

**Multilingual and localization.** Extensions contribute translation keys for supported locales and declare an explicit fallback; tenant-added labels are escaped and length-bounded.

**Verification.** Test enabled, disabled, incompatible-version, unauthorized, and missing-translation extension configurations.

### ERP-NEXTJS-015 — Supported browser and rendering baseline

**Shall.** The product shall publish and test a supported browser and assistive-technology matrix, and its critical workflows shall not require non-standard browser behavior without a documented fallback.

**Rationale.** Enterprise customers often standardize browser versions and accessible workflows must remain usable across the declared support matrix.

**Acceptance criteria.**

**1.** A versioned support matrix identifies browser families, minimum supported versions, mobile/desktop coverage, and test cadence.

**2.** Sign-in, navigation, record lookup, data entry, approval, and error recovery pass smoke tests on every browser family in that matrix.

**Exception / edge case.** A specialized visualization may require a capability unavailable in an older supported browser if a textual or tabular alternative remains available.

**Security and audit.** Unsupported clients receive a safe compatibility notice and are not allowed to weaken authentication or TLS controls to continue.

**Multilingual and localization.** Matrix tests include at least one right-to-left locale and a non-Latin input locale where browser support permits.

**Verification.** Execute cross-browser CI and release-gate manual checks against the published matrix.

### ERP-NEXTJS-016 — Documented browser-only integration

**Shall.** Browser-only integrations shall be isolated behind client-side adapters that load after the relevant route is requested and expose a server-rendered or static accessible fallback until initialization completes.

**Rationale.** ERP extensions may include charting, scanners, or vendor widgets that depend on browser APIs, but must not break server rendering or block primary workflows.

**Acceptance criteria.**

**1.** A production build succeeds with each supported adapter and no browser global is evaluated during server module initialization.

**2.** With JavaScript disabled or adapter loading failed, users can still read the workflow's essential status and use its documented alternative.

**Exception / edge case.** A WebAuthn or device-dependent capability may be unavailable in a browser; the configured identity policy determines the approved alternate authentication path.

**Security and audit.** Third-party adapters receive only required data, use allowlisted origins, and cannot access privileged credentials or bypass backend authorization.

**Multilingual and localization.** Fallback and initialization messages are localized; extension output must declare its language when it differs from the page language.

**Verification.** Run server build, browser API absence tests, script-blocked checks, and adapter failure injection.

### ERP-NEXTJS-017 — Secret-safe runtime configuration

**Shall.** The frontend shall expose only explicitly public configuration to browser bundles and shall keep backend URLs, signing keys, service tokens, and private deployment metadata in server-only runtime configuration.

**Rationale.** Next.js public environment variables are embedded for client access and cannot safely hold secrets.

**Acceptance criteria.**

**1.** A CI secret scan checks built JavaScript, source maps, and static output for configured canary secret values.

**2.** All variables prefixed for client exposure have a documented non-sensitive purpose and schema validation at startup.

**Exception / edge case.** A public analytics or tenant branding identifier may be browser-visible when its owner classifies it as public and it grants no privileged access.

**Security and audit.** Secret rotation and deployment access are governed outside the client; leaked secret findings trigger credential revocation, incident review, and artifact rebuild.

**Multilingual and localization.** Locale identifiers and public translated labels may be exposed; confidential tenant configuration and unpublished translation assets remain server-scoped.

**Verification.** Inspect build artifacts with secret-canary tests and verify environment-variable allowlists in deployment configuration.

### ERP-NEXTJS-018 — Browser security response headers

**Shall.** The frontend deployment shall apply a security-header policy appropriate to the configured identity flow, including a tested Content Security Policy and framing restrictions, without relying on headers as a replacement for output encoding or authorization.

**Rationale.** ERP screens handle valuable records and frequently combine authenticated content, forms, and operationally sensitive actions.

**Acceptance criteria.**

**1.** Security tests verify Content-Security-Policy, HTTPS transport policy at the edge, and frame embedding policy on protected pages.

**2.** The CSP is exercised against production-like login, server actions, fonts, images, and approved extension assets with no unexplained unsafe wildcard source.

**Exception / edge case.** A customer-configured identity provider or embedded reporting service may require a narrowly scoped origin exception after security approval.

**Security and audit.** Policy exceptions are documented with owner and expiry; CSP violation reports are scrubbed of sensitive query or form values before retention.

**Multilingual and localization.** Security policy must allow configured locale asset origins without allowing arbitrary remote scripts or tenant-supplied executable translation content.

**Verification.** Inspect response headers in deployment tests and run browser CSP reporting in a representative workflow suite.

### ERP-NEXTJS-019 — Stable API and error contracts

**Shall.** The frontend-to-ASP.NET Core contract shall use versioned, typed request and response schemas with stable machine-readable error codes separated from localized display text.

**Rationale.** A typed boundary allows independent frontend and backend releases while supporting user-friendly localization and actionable error handling.

**Acceptance criteria.**

**1.** OpenAPI or equivalent contract artifacts are generated or validated in CI and breaking changes require a versioned compatibility decision.

**2.** Frontend mapping tests cover documented validation, authorization, conflict, not-found, throttling, and server-failure error codes.

**Exception / edge case.** An additive optional response field may be ignored by older frontends; an unknown error code must render a generic safe message rather than fail rendering.

**Security and audit.** Contracts omit server stack details and confidential fields; authentication and tenant constraints are enforced by API operations, not client claims.

**Multilingual and localization.** Backend error codes map to locale dictionaries; server-provided localized text is used only when the contract explicitly designates it as display-safe.

**Verification.** Run schema compatibility checks and consumer-driven contract tests across supported API versions.

### ERP-NEXTJS-020 — Explicit consequential-action confirmation

**Shall.** The frontend shall require a clear confirmation step for configured irreversible or high-impact business actions and shall show the affected entity, action, and consequence before submitting the request.

**Rationale.** ERP users can trigger payments, approvals, posting, release, or deletion operations whose effects may be costly or legally significant depending on tenant configuration.

**Acceptance criteria.**

**1.** For each action classified consequential by the backend contract, the UI displays an explicit confirmation with entity context and cancel option.

**2.** A keyboard-only user can review, confirm, and cancel, and a duplicate click during submission results in no duplicate client request.

**Exception / edge case.** A tenant may configure a bulk workflow to use an authorized step-up or approval protocol instead of per-item dialogs; backend controls remain authoritative.

**Security and audit.** Confirmation is not authorization or transaction signing; backend records actor, decision, and transaction outcome, with idempotency protection where supported.

**Multilingual and localization.** The consequence text and action labels are localized and use tenant-approved terminology; jurisdiction-specific legal warnings are supplied through configured policy content.

**Verification.** Test critical-action confirmation in UI and direct API bypass attempts, including duplicate-submit and canceled-flow cases.

### ERP-NEXTJS-021 — Route-level code splitting

**Shall.** The frontend shall keep module-only client code out of unrelated route bundles through route-level code splitting and shall load optional client features on demand.

**Rationale.** A lightweight shell matters for mid-market and enterprise users who may navigate a broad module catalog but use only a subset in each session.

**Acceptance criteria.**

**1.** Bundle reports show a module's distinctive client dependency is absent from unrelated initial route chunks.

**2.** A route's production initial JavaScript budget is declared and enforced in CI with a documented reviewed exception process.

**Exception / edge case.** A shared runtime dependency may appear in common chunks when the measured total is smaller than duplicating it across module-specific chunks.

**Security and audit.** Chunk splitting is not an access control; disabled modules' endpoints remain protected and private code must not be shipped merely because a route is hidden.

**Multilingual and localization.** Locale dictionaries shall be loaded by locale and route namespace where practical, avoiding a full catalog download for every user.

**Verification.** Build with the bundle analyzer and compare route-chunk manifests against the committed budgets.

### ERP-NEXTJS-022 — Lazy loading of costly interactive tools

**Shall.** Heavy charts, editors, maps, import previews, and other optional interactive tools shall be dynamically imported only when their owning route or user action requires them.

**Rationale.** On-demand loading reduces startup cost for workflows whose users do not need every advanced visualization or editing feature.

**Acceptance criteria.**

**1.** Network tests confirm the optional library chunk is not downloaded before the corresponding view is opened.

**2.** The deferred component provides a localized loading state and a recoverable error state if its chunk fails to load.

**Exception / edge case.** A critical tool required immediately on a dedicated route may load with that route, provided it does not affect the shared ERP shell bundle.

**Security and audit.** Lazy import does not authorize access; the API still checks permissions before returning data, and third-party package versions are pinned and scanned.

**Multilingual and localization.** The fallback label and tool controls must use the active locale and preserve the current locale when the chunk resolves.

**Verification.** Use browser network traces and route tests to verify load timing, localized fallback, and chunk-error recovery.

### ERP-NEXTJS-023 — Server-rendered primary content

**Shall.** For authenticated list and detail routes, the frontend shall server-render the page identity and the primary safe content or an explicit loading/error state before client hydration, unless the route is intentionally client-only for a documented technical reason.

**Rationale.** Server-rendered initial content improves perceived responsiveness and avoids blank shells on large business pages.

**Acceptance criteria.**

**1.** Production HTML for a representative authorized record page contains its localized title and non-sensitive primary summary before hydration.

**2.** An unauthorized request's HTML contains no protected record fields even when the client JavaScript does not execute.

**Exception / edge case.** Highly interactive real-time boards may hydrate client-side data after a server-rendered route heading and accessible skeleton, with the data contract documenting why.

**Security and audit.** Server-generated HTML is subject to the same tenant isolation, no-store, and field-minimization rules as API responses.

**Multilingual and localization.** Initial document language and visible server content must agree with the resolved user locale; client hydration may not flash a different language.

**Verification.** Fetch server HTML without JavaScript for authorized and unauthorized fixtures and compare content and response headers.

### ERP-NEXTJS-024 — Streaming boundaries for slow panels

**Shall.** The frontend shall place Suspense or route loading boundaries around independently slow dashboards and record panels so that ready content can render without waiting for unrelated backend calls.

**Rationale.** A slow optional report widget should not block users from accessing the rest of a working page.

**Acceptance criteria.**

**1.** A test backend delaying one noncritical panel still allows the route heading and an unrelated ready panel to render before that panel resolves.

**2.** Each streamed fallback identifies the pending content and is replaced by content, empty state, or error state when the request finishes.

**Exception / edge case.** A workflow step whose content depends on a preceding authoritative calculation may wait for that calculation, but must show a clear pending state and timeout handling.

**Security and audit.** Each streamed data component independently authorizes its request; responses must not leak partial data before authorization completes.

**Multilingual and localization.** Fallback labels and streamed panel headings use the current locale; layout direction remains stable across streamed replacements.

**Verification.** Use controlled latency and failure injection to assert streaming order, fallback accessibility, and authorized data release.

### ERP-NEXTJS-025 — Parallel independent data retrieval

**Shall.** The frontend server layer shall initiate independent backend reads concurrently and shall preserve explicit dependency sequencing only where business data dependencies require it.

**Rationale.** Avoidable request waterfalls increase time-to-content across dashboards and composite entity pages.

**Acceptance criteria.**

**1.** An instrumented composite route starts independent requests before awaiting any one of them.

**2.** A performance test verifies that two independent configured 300 ms reads complete within a threshold close to their maximum latency rather than their sum, excluding test overhead.

**Exception / edge case.** A follow-up read that requires an identifier or version returned by a prior operation remains sequential and is labeled as a dependency in the data function.

**Security and audit.** Concurrent calls each carry the same validated user and tenant context; cancellation and error handling must not expose partial unauthorized results.

**Multilingual and localization.** Locale/configuration reads may be initiated alongside independent module data, but must resolve before locale-sensitive formatting is rendered.

**Verification.** Use request timing instrumentation and code review to verify independent fetches launch concurrently and dependent operations remain ordered.

### ERP-NEXTJS-026 — Measured web performance telemetry

**Shall.** The frontend shall collect privacy-minimized field performance measurements for agreed Core Web Vitals and route-level interaction timing, segmented by route class and deployment rather than by sensitive record content.

**Rationale.** Laboratory checks alone do not capture performance for actual enterprise network and device conditions.

**Acceptance criteria.**

**1.** Production telemetry records approved metrics with route template, release/build identifier, and coarse device/network dimensions.

**2.** Telemetry payloads contain no names, document contents, tenant secrets, search terms, or raw user identifiers.

**Exception / edge case.** Customers that disable optional analytics may opt out of field telemetry while mandatory operational error metrics remain governed by the service contract.

**Security and audit.** Telemetry has documented retention, access, sampling, and consent/configuration policies; identifiers are pseudonymous and minimized.

**Multilingual and localization.** Metric aggregation does not depend on translated screen labels; locale may be recorded only as a coarse configured tag when approved.

**Verification.** Inspect telemetry schemas and sampled payloads, then compare real-user metric dashboards to release SLO thresholds.

### ERP-NEXTJS-027 — Route performance budgets and regression gate

**Shall.** The frontend shall define route-class performance budgets for transfer size, long tasks, and agreed user-centric timing measures and shall block releases on material regression unless an approved exception is recorded.

**Rationale.** Specific budgets turn lightweight frontend intent into verifiable release criteria.

**Acceptance criteria.**

**1.** CI stores a baseline and threshold for the login, workspace shell, list, detail, and dashboard route classes.

**2.** A deliberate test bundle increase beyond its threshold fails CI and creates a report naming the changed chunks.

**Exception / edge case.** A regulated or data-intensive workflow may need a higher route-specific budget if its owner documents the user benefit and mitigation.

**Security and audit.** Budget exceptions cannot justify removing authentication, CSP, accessibility, or tenant checks to reduce payload or timing.

**Multilingual and localization.** Budget tests include locales with longer text and right-to-left layout to detect wrapping-related layout shifts and extra resource loading.

**Verification.** Run reproducible production builds and CI budget comparison with reviewed, expiring exception records.

### ERP-NEXTJS-028 — Optimized images and font delivery

**Shall.** The frontend shall use responsive image sizing and optimized font delivery for application assets, reserve image dimensions to reduce layout movement, and avoid uncontrolled third-party font requests in protected workflows.

**Rationale.** Images, logos, and multilingual fonts can create avoidable layout shift, network dependency, or privacy exposure.

**Acceptance criteria.**

**1.** Rendered content images include intrinsic dimensions or equivalent layout reservation and have responsive source sizing where appropriate.

**2.** Network tests confirm approved local or explicitly configured font sources and no layout shift beyond the route budget during font/image load.

**Exception / edge case.** Tenant-supplied logos may use a controlled asset service after type, size, and origin validation; missing assets use a stable fallback.

**Security and audit.** Uploaded image and font content is validated and served with safe content types; external requests are allowlisted and assessed for tracking exposure.

**Multilingual and localization.** Font fallback covers required scripts and combining marks; tenant-selected typefaces cannot break readable content or focus indicators.

**Verification.** Run image/font network checks, layout-shift tests, and visual snapshots across supported scripts and tenant branding.

### ERP-NEXTJS-029 — No redundant server-to-self API calls

**Shall.** Server Components shall call their server-only data functions or the backend API directly under the defined security boundary rather than making an additional HTTP request to the application's own Route Handler for the same data.

**Rationale.** Calling a local handler from the server introduces unnecessary latency and another failure surface.

**Acceptance criteria.**

**1.** Static analysis or review identifies no Server Component fetch to a same-application handler for a data function that can be called directly.

**2.** An instrumented page render uses no redundant self-request between the Next.js server and its own BFF endpoint.

**Exception / edge case.** A same-app Route Handler may remain the intended public browser-facing contract when the data request originates in a Client Component or an external client.

**Security and audit.** Direct DAL access still invokes authorization and DTO filtering; performance shortcuts must not bypass the backend permission boundary.

**Multilingual and localization.** Direct data functions must receive the validated locale context explicitly if backend content or formatting depends on locale.

**Verification.** Inspect server network traces and assert direct data function invocation in route integration tests.

### ERP-NEXTJS-030 — Efficient ERP list pagination

**Shall.** Large ERP lists shall use server-backed pagination or cursor-based continuation with bounded page size and shall not load an unbounded record collection into browser memory.

**Rationale.** Enterprise transaction and master-data volumes can be large, and unbounded rendering harms performance and accessibility.

**Acceptance criteria.**

**1.** List requests include a configured maximum page size and the API rejects values above its limit.

**2.** A test dataset exceeding 100,000 rows is navigable without a browser response containing all rows at once.

**Exception / edge case.** A bounded, explicitly small reference list may be fetched completely if its API maximum and measured response size remain within the declared threshold.

**Security and audit.** Every continuation token is bound to authorized tenant/filter context and cannot expand scope by editing client parameters.

**Multilingual and localization.** Page count, row range, and next/previous controls use locale-aware number formatting and translated labels.

**Verification.** Load-test pagination against high-volume fixtures and test tampered cursors and tenant switching.

### ERP-NEXTJS-031 — Safe search and filter query state

**Shall.** List search and filter state shall be encoded using a documented, validated query schema with bounded text and filter counts, and the server shall reauthorize every query against the active tenant and permissions.

**Rationale.** Shareable list URLs support work continuity, but search parameters are untrusted and can expose sensitive values through logs or links.

**Acceptance criteria.**

**1.** Unknown filter fields, overlong search text, and excessive filter counts receive deterministic validation outcomes.

**2.** A bookmarked list URL restores allowed filters for the same authorized scope but returns no unauthorized records after tenant or permission change.

**Exception / edge case.** Sensitive search terms may be kept in transient form state rather than the URL when the configured data classification prohibits them in browser history or referrer logs.

**Security and audit.** Query parameters are escaped, bounded, and excluded or redacted in logs when sensitive; client state never controls tenant access.

**Multilingual and localization.** Search matching and filter captions use locale-aware presentation; stable filter keys and enumerations remain independent of translated labels.

**Verification.** Fuzz query parsing, inspect browser history/referrer behavior, and test restored-state authorization after a role change.

### ERP-NEXTJS-032 — Predictable cache policy by data class

**Shall.** The frontend shall classify fetched content as public immutable, tenant-shared configuration, user-sensitive, or transaction-sensitive and shall define a Next.js cache/revalidation policy for each class before enabling caching.

**Rationale.** Framework caching behavior can reduce latency but business data freshness and confidentiality requirements differ by entity and tenant policy.

**Acceptance criteria.**

**1.** A cache registry names the data class, cache mode, maximum staleness, key dimensions, and owner for each cached backend read.

**2.** Tests confirm transaction-sensitive data is not served from a static shared route cache and configured stale periods are not exceeded.

**Exception / edge case.** A tenant may explicitly accept bounded staleness for low-risk reference data; that does not extend to posted balances, approval state, or other authoritative transactional state unless separately approved.

**Security and audit.** Sensitive data defaults to non-shared caching; cached data class and invalidation policies are included in security and privacy review.

**Multilingual and localization.** Cached presentation content includes locale and translation revision in its key or is localized after fetching locale-neutral data.

**Verification.** Review the cache registry and run stale-data, cross-role, cross-tenant, and cross-locale cache tests.

### ERP-NEXTJS-033 — Mutation-driven cache invalidation

**Shall.** After a successful mutation, the frontend shall invalidate or refresh every affected cached route and data tag through an explicit dependency map, and a failed mutation shall not falsely present stale content as updated.

**Rationale.** ERP users need predictable freshness across record detail, list, dashboards, and related views after changes.

**Acceptance criteria.**

**1.** A mutation dependency test updates a record and verifies the detail route, affected list, and specified summary reflect the new server version.

**2.** A rejected or timed-out mutation leaves the UI in an explicit unresolved/error state and does not show an unconfirmed success message.

**Exception / edge case.** An asynchronous long-running process may return a pending state rather than immediate final data, but the UI must identify the server job and refresh by its authoritative status.

**Security and audit.** Invalidation events are scoped to authorized tenant data; a user cannot trigger cross-tenant revalidation through a caller-selected tag.

**Multilingual and localization.** Invalidation must cover all affected locale variants and tenant translation variants for localized cached records.

**Verification.** Run mutation/revalidation integration tests with multiple application instances and cache-state assertions.

### ERP-NEXTJS-034 — Shared-cache coordination in multi-instance deployment

**Shall.** If Next.js is deployed across multiple instances, the deployment shall coordinate shared cache entries and tag invalidation or explicitly disable shared caching for the relevant data paths.

**Rationale.** Per-instance caches can produce inconsistent data after mutations or revalidation in clustered enterprise deployments.

**Acceptance criteria.**

**1.** A two-instance test performs a mutation on instance A and verifies instance B no longer serves the invalidated result.

**2.** Cache storage has bounded retention and documented behavior for unavailable cache infrastructure.

**Exception / edge case.** A deployment intentionally using no shared cache may use per-instance transient request memoization only when it cannot retain cross-request sensitive data.

**Security and audit.** The shared cache has access controls, encryption and retention appropriate to its data class; cache outages fail safely without widening data access.

**Multilingual and localization.** Shared invalidation reaches all locale keys and locale-specific tenant content; locale-specific entries do not overwrite one another.

**Verification.** Deploy two test instances, inspect cache key/tag propagation, and inject cache-store failure.

### ERP-NEXTJS-035 — Consistent build and rolling deployment behavior

**Shall.** The frontend deployment shall use reproducible artifacts and a deployment identifier or equivalent version-skew control for rolling or multi-instance releases, and all instances serving a deployment shall share the required Server Function encryption configuration.

**Rationale.** Mixed builds can mismatch client assets, Server Function identifiers, or encrypted action closures during enterprise rolling deployments.

**Acceptance criteria.**

**1.** Build metadata identifies an immutable frontend artifact and deployment version used by every instance in a release.

**2.** A rolling-deployment test with an older open browser session either completes safely or performs a controlled reload without invoking an incompatible action.

**Exception / edge case.** A single-instance deployment with atomic replacement may not need a shared multi-instance key, but must still protect secrets and avoid stale static assets.

**Security and audit.** Shared action encryption keys are secret-managed and rotated under a documented procedure; deployment rollback does not expose credentials in logs.

**Multilingual and localization.** Locale resources and route dictionaries ship with the same versioned artifact as the code that references their keys.

**Verification.** Run rolling, rollback, old-tab, and multi-instance action tests using production-like build artifacts.

### ERP-NEXTJS-036 — Bounded bulk-selection and bulk-action UX

**Shall.** Bulk-selection interfaces shall communicate selected-record count, scope, and configured operation limits, and submit stable record identifiers to a backend operation that revalidates authorization and eligibility per record.

**Rationale.** Bulk work is common in ERP and can amplify errors or unauthorized effects across many records.

**Acceptance criteria.**

**1.** The UI prevents selecting more records than the documented client operation limit or presents a supported server-side job workflow.

**2.** Backend results identify per-record success or safe failure without exposing records outside the caller's tenant or scope.

**Exception / edge case.** Very large selections may be represented by a server-issued query snapshot token rather than sending thousands of IDs; the token must expire and preserve the original filters.

**Security and audit.** Bulk actions use idempotency or duplicate protection when supported and produce backend audit events with count and outcome summary.

**Multilingual and localization.** Selection counts, limits, and per-record errors use locale-aware plural forms and do not rely on English plural rules.

**Verification.** Test limit boundaries, stale selections, duplicate submissions, unauthorized mixed-record batches, and per-record response rendering.

### ERP-NEXTJS-037 — Document locale resolution precedence

**Shall.** The frontend shall resolve the UI locale using a documented precedence of explicit user preference, tenant default, supported browser language preference, and configured product fallback, subject to deployment policy.

**Rationale.** A consistent precedence avoids surprising language changes across accounts, tenants, and browsers.

**Acceptance criteria.**

**1.** Automated tests cover conflicting user, tenant, browser, and product-default locale values and assert the documented winner.

**2.** Unsupported or malformed locale input falls back to a configured supported locale without a server error.

**Exception / edge case.** A customer-managed identity provider may supply a locale claim; it is accepted only if explicitly mapped and must not override a user's saved choice contrary to policy.

**Security and audit.** Locale input is allowlisted and cannot select an arbitrary dictionary import or cross-tenant configuration record.

**Multilingual and localization.** Locale represents display language/format conventions and remains distinct from legal entity, tax jurisdiction, accounting calendar, and currency policy.

**Verification.** Run locale precedence tests using cookies, profile preference, tenant settings, Accept-Language, and invalid locale values.

### ERP-NEXTJS-038 — Explicit user language switcher

**Shall.** Authenticated users shall be able to select any locale enabled for their tenant, and the preference shall persist through navigation and authenticated sessions using a server-validated setting.

**Rationale.** Browser negotiation is useful for initial selection, but enterprise users need a stable explicit language choice.

**Acceptance criteria.**

**1.** Changing the language updates the current route to its equivalent localized route where available and persists after sign-out/sign-in according to profile policy.

**2.** A locale unavailable to the tenant is not offered and direct navigation to it follows the configured fallback or not-found behavior.

**Exception / edge case.** When an equivalent localized route does not exist, the language switcher may navigate to the localized module landing page and announce the destination.

**Security and audit.** Preference updates are authenticated and CSRF-protected under the chosen session mechanism; changing language does not change roles or tenant membership.

**Multilingual and localization.** Language display names should be understandable to users in their own language where possible; a switch must not discard unsaved work without warning.

**Verification.** Test persistent preference, disabled locale, route equivalence, unsaved form handling, and multiple tenants with distinct locale availability.

### ERP-NEXTJS-039 — Locale-qualified route and metadata

**Shall.** Localized routes shall expose the resolved locale in their route context, set the document lang attribute, and generate page metadata and navigation links consistent with that locale.

**Rationale.** Explicit locale context supports assistive technology, stable links, and consistent server/client rendering.

**Acceptance criteria.**

**1.** Every rendered page has a valid html lang value matching its primary content language.

**2.** Route links generated by navigation and record workflows preserve the active locale or use an explicitly configured locale-neutral route.

**Exception / edge case.** A page containing a substantial quoted passage or user-authored content in another language must mark that passage separately rather than changing the whole document language.

**Security and audit.** Metadata is generated from trusted route definitions and escaped content; tenant-supplied titles cannot inject markup or reveal restricted records.

**Multilingual and localization.** Localized titles, descriptions, breadcrumb labels, and language direction derive from the same resolved locale resource set.

**Verification.** Inspect rendered DOM and metadata for every locale route and test navigation under client-side and direct-load paths.

### ERP-NEXTJS-040 — Translation-key and catalog governance

**Shall.** User-interface text shall be referenced through namespaced, typed translation keys owned by the application or extension, and translation catalogs shall be schema-validated during CI.

**Rationale.** Centralized catalogs make broad ERP interfaces translatable and prevent scattered hard-coded strings from drifting across modules.

**Acceptance criteria.**

**1.** CI fails on missing required keys, duplicate keys, invalid interpolation variables, or catalog schema mismatch.

**2.** A representative module screen contains no hard-coded user-facing static strings outside approved technical tokens and user-authored data.

**Exception / edge case.** Product names, identifiers, code values, and user-entered content may remain unlocalized when their domain contract explicitly treats them as invariant.

**Security and audit.** Catalogs are trusted application assets; interpolated values are escaped and catalog edits follow review and release provenance controls.

**Multilingual and localization.** Translation workflows include ownership, locale status, reviewer metadata, and explicit fallback behavior rather than silently substituting arbitrary text.

**Verification.** Run catalog validation, static string scanning, and per-locale rendering tests in CI.

### ERP-NEXTJS-041 — Visible and measurable translation fallback

**Shall.** When a translation key is missing, the frontend shall use only a configured fallback locale, report the missing key to controlled localization diagnostics, and avoid rendering raw internal key names to end users.

**Rationale.** Incomplete translation packs are inevitable during rollout, but visible key tokens undermine usability and can reveal implementation structure.

**Acceptance criteria.**

**1.** A test removes one locale key and confirms a valid fallback string is shown without an exception or key identifier.

**2.** Localization diagnostics identify the missing key, locale, route namespace, and release version without recording user-entered values.

**Exception / edge case.** In non-production translator-preview mode, a privileged localization reviewer may see a marked key placeholder, never in normal tenant production sessions.

**Security and audit.** Diagnostics are access-controlled and do not include confidential dynamic data; preview mode requires explicit privilege and is disabled by default.

**Multilingual and localization.** Fallback language is explicitly configured per tenant or product policy and the HTML language reflects the language actually used for the page or marked text.

**Verification.** Inject missing keys in production-mode tests and inspect fallback text, document language, and diagnostic event.

### ERP-NEXTJS-042 — Locale-aware date, number, currency, and unit display

**Shall.** The frontend shall use locale-aware formatting APIs backed by maintained locale data for dates, numeric values, currencies, and units while preserving canonical values for calculations and round-trip edits.

**Rationale.** Localized display conventions vary by language and region; formatting must not alter stored or authoritative transaction values.

**Acceptance criteria.**

**1.** Fixtures render the same canonical decimal, date, and amount correctly for at least three distinct locale conventions, including a locale using non-Latin digits or different separators.

**2.** Editing a formatted amount and submitting it preserves the exact canonical value within the field's declared precision and does not round silently.

**Exception / edge case.** A business document may require a tenant-configured legal or accounting presentation distinct from a user's locale; that presentation must be explicitly identified by the backend policy contract.

**Security and audit.** Locale formatting is presentation-only; server calculations, authorization decisions, audit records, and jurisdictional policy remain authoritative outside the browser.

**Multilingual and localization.** Use locale-specific separators, digit systems, currency placement, grouping, plural/unit rules, and calendar options; do not hard-code a single global format.

**Verification.** Run round-trip locale fixtures through display, edit, validation, and server payload comparison for each supported locale.

### ERP-NEXTJS-043 — Separate user locale, time zone, and business calendar

**Shall.** The frontend shall model display locale, user time zone, tenant or legal-entity time zone, and backend business calendar as distinct settings and shall label times with the relevant zone when ambiguity can affect a workflow.

**Rationale.** Language preference does not determine the time zone or authoritative business date, and conflating them can mislead users across locations.

**Acceptance criteria.**

**1.** A stored UTC instant displays according to the configured viewer zone while an explicitly business-zone date is shown with its zone or policy label.

**2.** Tests around daylight-saving transitions display valid local times and distinguish repeated or skipped local clock times.

**Exception / edge case.** A date-only field such as a document due date may have no time zone; the backend contract identifies it as a calendar date rather than a timestamp.

**Security and audit.** Frontend conversion never rewrites authoritative event timestamps or financial dates; server/audit values preserve their canonical representation.

**Multilingual and localization.** Localized date/time patterns and zone names use locale data while zone selection remains an explicit profile or tenant configuration.

**Verification.** Test timestamp and date-only fixtures across several zones, DST boundaries, and display locales against backend canonical values.

### ERP-NEXTJS-044 — Bidirectional text and layout support

**Shall.** The frontend shall support right-to-left locales using direction-aware layout primitives and Unicode bidirectional isolation for embedded identifiers, dates, amounts, and left-to-right text.

**Rationale.** Mixed-direction ERP data can become unreadable or visually misleading when layouts assume left-to-right flow.

**Acceptance criteria.**

**1.** A right-to-left locale test verifies document direction, navigation placement, form alignment, and reading order while preserving logical DOM order.

**2.** Mixed-language fixtures containing account codes, URLs, negative amounts, and punctuation render without reordering the identifier's semantic sequence.

**Exception / edge case.** A code editor, raw JSON viewer, or externally specified LTR artifact may retain LTR direction inside a labeled isolated region.

**Security and audit.** Bidi controls in user-supplied identifiers are visualized or sanitized according to input policy to reduce spoofing; displayed identity-critical values remain unambiguous.

**Multilingual and localization.** Direction is a locale property independent of translated wording; logical keyboard and screen-reader order remains stable when visual alignment mirrors.

**Verification.** Run DOM, screenshot, keyboard, and assistive-technology checks on mixed-script fixtures in RTL and LTR locales.

### ERP-NEXTJS-045 — Localized form parsing and input guidance

**Shall.** Localized forms shall accept and validate values according to an explicit field input contract, show the expected format and units, and avoid ambiguous parsing based solely on a browser's implicit locale defaults.

**Rationale.** Numeric and date inputs vary across locales, and silent parsing assumptions can change financial or operational values.

**Acceptance criteria.**

**1.** For each locale-sensitive field, tests document accepted input forms and verify valid and invalid examples before submission.

**2.** A value that cannot be unambiguously parsed is rejected with a localized correction message rather than coerced to a different value.

**Exception / edge case.** Native browser date/number controls may use browser locale behavior; their submitted canonical values must be normalized and validated against the explicit backend schema.

**Security and audit.** Client validation is advisory; backend validation is authoritative and logs preserve canonical value and validation outcome according to domain audit policy.

**Multilingual and localization.** Instructions include localized separators, date order, precision, units, and examples; no locale is assumed from IP address alone.

**Verification.** Test parsing and round-trip behavior with locale-specific valid/invalid input, browser locale mismatch, and API tampering.

### ERP-NEXTJS-046 — Locale-sensitive search and sorting contract

**Shall.** The frontend shall use backend-defined search and collation behavior for authoritative ERP results and shall label any client-side sort or search as presentation-only when it cannot reproduce backend semantics.

**Rationale.** Locale-specific collation, diacritics, and case handling differ; client and server ordering must not imply inconsistent business results.

**Acceptance criteria.**

**1.** The API contract identifies whether a search or sort is performed server-side and returns stable sort metadata for paginated results.

**2.** A locale fixture with accented and non-Latin text verifies consistent order across pages without client-side resorting of only the current page.

**Exception / edge case.** A small in-memory option set may be client-filtered if the set is bounded, complete, and the UI indicates that it is a local option filter rather than a global record search.

**Security and audit.** Search endpoints enforce tenant and field-level permissions and rate limits; search terms are not written to broad telemetry by default.

**Multilingual and localization.** Locale and tenant-configured collation are separate parameters; business-specific matching rules are defined by the backend or module contract, not guessed by the shared shell.

**Verification.** Compare API and UI search/sort results across locale fixtures and multiple paginated result pages.

### ERP-NEXTJS-047 — Plural, grammatical, and message interpolation rules

**Shall.** The frontend shall use locale-aware message formatting for counts, quantities, dates, and interpolation rather than concatenating translated fragments using English grammar assumptions.

**Rationale.** Many languages have plural categories and word-order rules not expressible by appending a translated noun to a number.

**Acceptance criteria.**

**1.** A message-catalog test exercises zero, singular, plural, and locale-specific plural categories for supported locales.

**2.** Interpolated values are escaped and preserve declared formatting for user name, entity label, and quantity placeholders.

**Exception / edge case.** A domain code or immutable status label may be displayed verbatim when the data contract requires exact source text, but should be accompanied by a localized explanation where necessary.

**Security and audit.** Message interpolation is output-escaped and must not allow tenant-configured text to inject HTML or executable markup.

**Multilingual and localization.** Translators receive named context and placeholder documentation; grammatical gender or inflection is modeled only where product data supports it.

**Verification.** Run locale message tests against representative count categories and hostile interpolation strings.

### ERP-NEXTJS-048 — Configurable jurisdiction and industry presentation boundary

**Shall.** The shared frontend shall render jurisdictional or industry-specific labels, notices, input constraints, and workflow steps only from versioned tenant or module configuration/API contracts and shall not infer them from UI language or locale alone.

**Rationale.** Legal and industry rules differ; a language or region identifier is insufficient evidence of applicable policy.

**Acceptance criteria.**

**1.** A supported configuration fixture changes a module-specific label or workflow step without changing global translations or hard-coded shared-shell rules.

**2.** If required policy configuration is absent or version-incompatible, the workflow blocks or requests administrator remediation rather than inventing a default legal rule.

**Exception / edge case.** Generic formatting defaults may use locale data for dates and numbers, but legal notices, tax treatment, retention, and filing rules require explicit authoritative configuration.

**Security and audit.** Policy configuration is versioned, access-controlled, attributable, and supplied by the backend or customer governance process; frontend values cannot override server policy.

**Multilingual and localization.** Policy text has an owning jurisdiction/module, effective version, language coverage, and approved fallback; translation does not change legal meaning or scope.

**Verification.** Test configured, missing, stale, and mismatched jurisdiction/industry configurations against server authorization and workflow responses.

### ERP-NEXTJS-049 — Accessibility conformance baseline

**Shall.** The frontend shall target WCAG 2.2 Level AA for all application-owned authenticated workflows and shall maintain a documented exception and remediation process for content or embedded components outside direct control.

**Rationale.** An ERP is a primary work environment and must support users with diverse sensory, motor, cognitive, and assistive-technology needs.

**Acceptance criteria.**

**1.** Every release-critical workflow has automated accessibility checks and manual keyboard/screen-reader review recorded against WCAG 2.2 AA criteria.

**2.** Known exceptions have an owner, impact, workaround, due date, and release approval; no exception silently reduces the product baseline.

**Exception / edge case.** A third-party embedded report that cannot meet the baseline may be isolated with a documented accessible alternative and customer-visible limitation while remediation is pursued.

**Security and audit.** Accessibility telemetry and test evidence are handled without retaining screen-reader output containing confidential business data; accessibility remediation does not weaken access controls.

**Multilingual and localization.** Conformance is tested in supported languages and directions because labels, text length, reading order, and accessible names can change by locale.

**Verification.** Use WCAG mapping, automated scans, manual test scripts, keyboard-only checks, and representative assistive technology.

### ERP-NEXTJS-050 — Descriptive page title and heading hierarchy

**Shall.** Every route shall render a unique, descriptive localized document title and a visible primary heading, with section headings nested in a meaningful hierarchy that identifies module and task context.

**Rationale.** Titles and headings aid route announcements, orientation, navigation, and users managing multiple ERP tabs.

**Acceptance criteria.**

**1.** Automated route tests assert a non-empty unique title and exactly one programmatically identifiable primary page heading for each standard route.

**2.** Heading-level checks find no skipped structural level unless a documented embedded-content boundary explains it.

**Exception / edge case.** A full-screen modal workflow may retain the underlying route title if the modal has its own programmatic title and announced context.

**Security and audit.** Titles and headings must not expose confidential record names on routes where authorization is unresolved or concealment policy applies.

**Multilingual and localization.** Title and heading strings use the active locale; language-specific word order and script are respected rather than concatenated from fragments.

**Verification.** Run route-title/headings assertions and manual screen-reader navigation on representative module routes.

### ERP-NEXTJS-051 — Landmarks and skip navigation

**Shall.** Authenticated layouts shall use semantic header, navigation, main, and complementary landmarks as appropriate and provide a visible-on-focus skip link to the main work region.

**Rationale.** A persistent ERP shell may contain extensive navigation; landmarks and skip links let keyboard and screen-reader users reach the current task efficiently.

**Acceptance criteria.**

**1.** Each workspace route exposes one primary main landmark with a stable accessible name and a reachable skip link that moves focus to it.

**2.** Landmark inspection identifies distinct primary navigation and main content without duplicate ambiguous main landmarks.

**Exception / edge case.** A focused task dialog may temporarily set an appropriate modal context, but must preserve a reliable route back to the underlying workspace.

**Security and audit.** Landmark labels must not include hidden sensitive values; focus movement must not bypass permission-controlled content boundaries.

**Multilingual and localization.** Landmark and skip-link names are localized, while semantic order remains logical in both LTR and RTL layouts.

**Verification.** Navigate using only landmarks and keyboard; inspect accessibility tree and verify skip-link focus target.

### ERP-NEXTJS-052 — Accessible navigation and route announcements

**Shall.** Client-side navigation shall provide a discernible route-change announcement and preserve or deliberately reset keyboard focus according to the navigation context; navigation items shall expose current-page state programmatically.

**Rationale.** Single-page transitions can visually change content without notifying assistive technology users.

**Acceptance criteria.**

**1.** On client route transition, a screen reader receives the new page title or equivalent announcement once, without duplicate announcements.

**2.** The active navigation link exposes aria-current=page or equivalent on the current route and focus remains at a predictable location.

**Exception / edge case.** A background panel refresh that does not change the route shall not announce an entire page transition; only its changed status is announced when relevant.

**Security and audit.** Announcements do not include unredacted backend errors or unauthorized entity names; hidden route metadata is generated only after authorization.

**Multilingual and localization.** Route announcements use the locale actually rendered and do not switch spoken-language context unexpectedly during navigation.

**Verification.** Test navigation with keyboard and screen readers across full route transitions, nested routes, redirects, and locale changes.

### ERP-NEXTJS-053 — Semantic tabular data and accessible data-grid behavior

**Shall.** Static tabular business data shall use semantic table markup with associated headers, and interactive data grids shall implement a documented keyboard pattern, accessible row/column headers, and state announcements.

**Rationale.** ERP users need to correlate large numbers of values; correct table relationships and keyboard navigation are essential to interpreting records.

**Acceptance criteria.**

**1.** A screen reader can identify each data cell's row and column header in representative static tables.

**2.** Interactive grids pass the documented arrow-key, Home/End, selection, and edit-mode tests without trapping focus.

**Exception / edge case.** A responsive narrow-screen view may transform a table into labeled cards only if row/column relationships and all data/actions remain available.

**Security and audit.** Hidden columns and client-only table filtering are not field-level security; restricted fields must not be sent to the browser.

**Multilingual and localization.** Column names, row labels, sort announcements, and numeric/date values are localized; column order may adapt visually in RTL without corrupting semantic associations.

**Verification.** Inspect accessibility tree and test table/grid operation with keyboard and representative screen readers at large data volume.

### ERP-NEXTJS-054 — Complete keyboard operability

**Shall.** All core workflows and controls shall be operable by keyboard without requiring pointer gestures, with a logical focus order and no keyboard trap except while a correctly managed modal dialog is active.

**Rationale.** Keyboard access is necessary for users with motor disabilities and for efficient enterprise data entry.

**Acceptance criteria.**

**1.** A keyboard-only test completes navigation, search, create/edit, save/cancel, approval, and error recovery without a pointer.

**2.** Tab and arrow-key sequences follow a documented pattern for every composite widget and never leave focus in an unreachable state.

**Exception / edge case.** A spatially essential mapping or drawing task may require pointer input, but an equivalent keyboard or non-drag alternative must support the business outcome.

**Security and audit.** Keyboard shortcuts for consequential operations must not bypass confirmation, step-up authentication, or backend permission checks.

**Multilingual and localization.** Keyboard order and shortcut labels are tested for localized labels and RTL layout; shortcuts must avoid conflicts with common input methods where practical.

**Verification.** Perform scripted keyboard-only task tests and automated focus-order checks on supported browsers.

### ERP-NEXTJS-055 — Visible and unobscured keyboard focus

**Shall.** Every keyboard-focusable control shall have a visible focus indicator that meets applicable contrast requirements and remains at least partly visible when sticky navigation, banners, dialogs, or virtualized content are present.

**Rationale.** Visible focus is necessary to identify the active control, particularly on dense forms and tables.

**Acceptance criteria.**

**1.** Computed and visual tests confirm focus indicators are visible against adjacent backgrounds for default, high-contrast, and tenant-brand themes.

**2.** Automated keyboard traversal confirms sticky headers or footers do not completely obscure the focused control.

**Exception / edge case.** A user-agent rendered native control may use its platform focus indicator if it remains visible and is not removed or overridden by application styles.

**Security and audit.** Tenant theming may not suppress focus indicators or produce an ambiguous state on controls that perform privileged actions.

**Multilingual and localization.** Focus visibility must persist when translated labels wrap, controls reorder for RTL, and content expands in a longer-language layout.

**Verification.** Run keyboard focus screenshots and contrast checks across themes, viewport sizes, sticky states, and modal overlays.

### ERP-NEXTJS-056 — Modal dialog focus and escape behavior

**Shall.** Modal dialogs shall expose an accessible name and modal state, move focus into the dialog on open, contain tab navigation while modal, and restore focus to the invoker or a documented successor on close.

**Rationale.** ERP confirmations and editors often use dialogs; unmanaged focus can strand keyboard or screen-reader users.

**Acceptance criteria.**

**1.** Opening a dialog places focus on its documented initial control and screen-reader users receive its title and purpose.

**2.** Tab and Shift+Tab remain within the modal; Escape closes only when the dialog's business policy permits, and closing restores focus predictably.

**Exception / edge case.** A non-dismissible transaction dialog may suppress Escape only when the reason is explained and a visible keyboard-accessible completion or cancel route remains.

**Security and audit.** Dialog state is presentation only; submit/cancel operations recheck authorization and sensitive dialog content is cleared when no longer authorized.

**Multilingual and localization.** Dialog title, action labels, validation, and focus announcements are localized; layout accommodates translated button order and longer text.

**Verification.** Test dialog lifecycle with keyboard, screen reader, nested dialogs where allowed, and rejected/expired-session actions.

### ERP-NEXTJS-057 — Correct accessible patterns for custom widgets

**Shall.** Custom comboboxes, menus, tabs, tree views, and other composite widgets shall follow a W3C ARIA Authoring Practices keyboard and semantics pattern or use native HTML controls when equivalent.

**Rationale.** Adding ARIA roles without expected keyboard behavior can make custom ERP widgets less accessible than native controls.

**Acceptance criteria.**

**1.** Each custom widget has a named pattern, role/state mapping, supported key map, and automated interaction tests.

**2.** The accessibility tree exposes current value, expanded/selected/disabled state, and relationships required by the chosen pattern.

**Exception / edge case.** A vendor component that cannot meet the pattern is prohibited from critical workflows unless an accessible equivalent is provided and approved.

**Security and audit.** Widget visibility and disabled state do not enforce permissions; backend operations must reject unauthorized actions regardless of widget state.

**Multilingual and localization.** Accessible names and type-ahead matching support the active script and locale; key handling must respect input method composition.

**Verification.** Run pattern-specific keyboard scripts, accessibility-tree inspection, and screen-reader testing for each widget type.

### ERP-NEXTJS-058 — Programmatic labels and instructions for controls

**Shall.** Every input and action control shall have a programmatic accessible name, and fields requiring a particular format, unit, or business rule shall expose associated instructions before or during entry.

**Rationale.** A visual placeholder alone does not reliably identify fields or communicate required entry rules to assistive technology users.

**Acceptance criteria.**
