**AC 1.** A test removes one locale key and confirms a valid fallback string is shown without an exception or key identifier.

**AC 2.** Localization diagnostics identify the missing key, locale, route namespace, and release version without recording user-entered values.

**Exception / edge case:** In non-production translator-preview mode, a privileged localization reviewer may see a marked key placeholder, never in normal tenant production sessions.

**Security and audit implications:** Diagnostics are access-controlled and do not include confidential dynamic data; preview mode requires explicit privilege and is disabled by default.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Fallback language is explicitly configured per tenant or product policy and the HTML language reflects the language actually used for the page or marked text.

**Verification method:** Inject missing keys in production-mode tests and inspect fallback text, document language, and diagnostic event.

**REQUIREMENT 0812 OF 1120  |  NEXT.JS FRONTEND ARCHITECTURE, PERFORMANCE, AND ACCESSIBILITY**

## ERP-NEXTJS-042 — Locale-aware date, number, currency, and unit display

**Normative requirement:** The frontend shall use locale-aware formatting APIs backed by maintained locale data for dates, numeric values, currencies, and units while preserving canonical values for calculations and round-trip edits.

**Rationale:** Localized display conventions vary by language and region; formatting must not alter stored or authoritative transaction values.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Fixtures render the same canonical decimal, date, and amount correctly for at least three distinct locale conventions, including a locale using non-Latin digits or different separators.

**AC 2.** Editing a formatted amount and submitting it preserves the exact canonical value within the field's declared precision and does not round silently.

**Exception / edge case:** A business document may require a tenant-configured legal or accounting presentation distinct from a user's locale; that presentation must be explicitly identified by the backend policy contract.

**Security and audit implications:** Locale formatting is presentation-only; server calculations, authorization decisions, audit records, and jurisdictional policy remain authoritative outside the browser.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Use locale-specific separators, digit systems, currency placement, grouping, plural/unit rules, and calendar options; do not hard-code a single global format.

**Verification method:** Run round-trip locale fixtures through display, edit, validation, and server payload comparison for each supported locale.

**REQUIREMENT 0813 OF 1120  |  NEXT.JS FRONTEND ARCHITECTURE, PERFORMANCE, AND ACCESSIBILITY**

## ERP-NEXTJS-043 — Separate user locale, time zone, and business calendar

**Normative requirement:** The frontend shall model display locale, user time zone, tenant or legal-entity time zone, and backend business calendar as distinct settings and shall label times with the relevant zone when ambiguity can affect a workflow.

**Rationale:** Language preference does not determine the time zone or authoritative business date, and conflating them can mislead users across locations.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A stored UTC instant displays according to the configured viewer zone while an explicitly business-zone date is shown with its zone or policy label.

**AC 2.** Tests around daylight-saving transitions display valid local times and distinguish repeated or skipped local clock times.

**Exception / edge case:** A date-only field such as a document due date may have no time zone; the backend contract identifies it as a calendar date rather than a timestamp.

**Security and audit implications:** Frontend conversion never rewrites authoritative event timestamps or financial dates; server/audit values preserve their canonical representation.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Localized date/time patterns and zone names use locale data while zone selection remains an explicit profile or tenant configuration.

**Verification method:** Test timestamp and date-only fixtures across several zones, DST boundaries, and display locales against backend canonical values.

**REQUIREMENT 0814 OF 1120  |  NEXT.JS FRONTEND ARCHITECTURE, PERFORMANCE, AND ACCESSIBILITY**

## ERP-NEXTJS-044 — Bidirectional text and layout support

**Normative requirement:** The frontend shall support right-to-left locales using direction-aware layout primitives and Unicode bidirectional isolation for embedded identifiers, dates, amounts, and left-to-right text.

**Rationale:** Mixed-direction ERP data can become unreadable or visually misleading when layouts assume left-to-right flow.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A right-to-left locale test verifies document direction, navigation placement, form alignment, and reading order while preserving logical DOM order.

**AC 2.** Mixed-language fixtures containing account codes, URLs, negative amounts, and punctuation render without reordering the identifier's semantic sequence.

**Exception / edge case:** A code editor, raw JSON viewer, or externally specified LTR artifact may retain LTR direction inside a labeled isolated region.

**Security and audit implications:** Bidi controls in user-supplied identifiers are visualized or sanitized according to input policy to reduce spoofing; displayed identity-critical values remain unambiguous.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Direction is a locale property independent of translated wording; logical keyboard and screen-reader order remains stable when visual alignment mirrors.

**Verification method:** Run DOM, screenshot, keyboard, and assistive-technology checks on mixed-script fixtures in RTL and LTR locales.

**REQUIREMENT 0815 OF 1120  |  NEXT.JS FRONTEND ARCHITECTURE, PERFORMANCE, AND ACCESSIBILITY**

## ERP-NEXTJS-045 — Localized form parsing and input guidance

**Normative requirement:** Localized forms shall accept and validate values according to an explicit field input contract, show the expected format and units, and avoid ambiguous parsing based solely on a browser's implicit locale defaults.

**Rationale:** Numeric and date inputs vary across locales, and silent parsing assumptions can change financial or operational values.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** For each locale-sensitive field, tests document accepted input forms and verify valid and invalid examples before submission.

**AC 2.** A value that cannot be unambiguously parsed is rejected with a localized correction message rather than coerced to a different value.

**Exception / edge case:** Native browser date/number controls may use browser locale behavior; their submitted canonical values must be normalized and validated against the explicit backend schema.

**Security and audit implications:** Client validation is advisory; backend validation is authoritative and logs preserve canonical value and validation outcome according to domain audit policy.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Instructions include localized separators, date order, precision, units, and examples; no locale is assumed from IP address alone.

**Verification method:** Test parsing and round-trip behavior with locale-specific valid/invalid input, browser locale mismatch, and API tampering.

**REQUIREMENT 0816 OF 1120  |  NEXT.JS FRONTEND ARCHITECTURE, PERFORMANCE, AND ACCESSIBILITY**

## ERP-NEXTJS-046 — Locale-sensitive search and sorting contract

**Normative requirement:** The frontend shall use backend-defined search and collation behavior for authoritative ERP results and shall label any client-side sort or search as presentation-only when it cannot reproduce backend semantics.

**Rationale:** Locale-specific collation, diacritics, and case handling differ; client and server ordering must not imply inconsistent business results.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** The API contract identifies whether a search or sort is performed server-side and returns stable sort metadata for paginated results.

**AC 2.** A locale fixture with accented and non-Latin text verifies consistent order across pages without client-side resorting of only the current page.

**Exception / edge case:** A small in-memory option set may be client-filtered if the set is bounded, complete, and the UI indicates that it is a local option filter rather than a global record search.

**Security and audit implications:** Search endpoints enforce tenant and field-level permissions and rate limits; search terms are not written to broad telemetry by default.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Locale and tenant-configured collation are separate parameters; business-specific matching rules are defined by the backend or module contract, not guessed by the shared shell.

**Verification method:** Compare API and UI search/sort results across locale fixtures and multiple paginated result pages.

**REQUIREMENT 0817 OF 1120  |  NEXT.JS FRONTEND ARCHITECTURE, PERFORMANCE, AND ACCESSIBILITY**

## ERP-NEXTJS-047 — Plural, grammatical, and message interpolation rules

**Normative requirement:** The frontend shall use locale-aware message formatting for counts, quantities, dates, and interpolation rather than concatenating translated fragments using English grammar assumptions.

**Rationale:** Many languages have plural categories and word-order rules not expressible by appending a translated noun to a number.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A message-catalog test exercises zero, singular, plural, and locale-specific plural categories for supported locales.

**AC 2.** Interpolated values are escaped and preserve declared formatting for user name, entity label, and quantity placeholders.

**Exception / edge case:** A domain code or immutable status label may be displayed verbatim when the data contract requires exact source text, but should be accompanied by a localized explanation where necessary.

**Security and audit implications:** Message interpolation is output-escaped and must not allow tenant-configured text to inject HTML or executable markup.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Translators receive named context and placeholder documentation; grammatical gender or inflection is modeled only where product data supports it.

**Verification method:** Run locale message tests against representative count categories and hostile interpolation strings.

**REQUIREMENT 0818 OF 1120  |  NEXT.JS FRONTEND ARCHITECTURE, PERFORMANCE, AND ACCESSIBILITY**

## ERP-NEXTJS-048 — Configurable jurisdiction and industry presentation boundary

**Normative requirement:** The shared frontend shall render jurisdictional or industry-specific labels, notices, input constraints, and workflow steps only from versioned tenant or module configuration/API contracts and shall not infer them from UI language or locale alone.

**Rationale:** Legal and industry rules differ; a language or region identifier is insufficient evidence of applicable policy.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A supported configuration fixture changes a module-specific label or workflow step without changing global translations or hard-coded shared-shell rules.

**AC 2.** If required policy configuration is absent or version-incompatible, the workflow blocks or requests administrator remediation rather than inventing a default legal rule.

**Exception / edge case:** Generic formatting defaults may use locale data for dates and numbers, but legal notices, tax treatment, retention, and filing rules require explicit authoritative configuration.

**Security and audit implications:** Policy configuration is versioned, access-controlled, attributable, and supplied by the backend or customer governance process; frontend values cannot override server policy.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Policy text has an owning jurisdiction/module, effective version, language coverage, and approved fallback; translation does not change legal meaning or scope.

**Verification method:** Test configured, missing, stale, and mismatched jurisdiction/industry configurations against server authorization and workflow responses.

**REQUIREMENT 0819 OF 1120  |  NEXT.JS FRONTEND ARCHITECTURE, PERFORMANCE, AND ACCESSIBILITY**

## ERP-NEXTJS-049 — Accessibility conformance baseline

**Normative requirement:** The frontend shall target WCAG 2.2 Level AA for all application-owned authenticated workflows and shall maintain a documented exception and remediation process for content or embedded components outside direct control.

**Rationale:** An ERP is a primary work environment and must support users with diverse sensory, motor, cognitive, and assistive-technology needs.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Every release-critical workflow has automated accessibility checks and manual keyboard/screen-reader review recorded against WCAG 2.2 AA criteria.

**AC 2.** Known exceptions have an owner, impact, workaround, due date, and release approval; no exception silently reduces the product baseline.

**Exception / edge case:** A third-party embedded report that cannot meet the baseline may be isolated with a documented accessible alternative and customer-visible limitation while remediation is pursued.

**Security and audit implications:** Accessibility telemetry and test evidence are handled without retaining screen-reader output containing confidential business data; accessibility remediation does not weaken access controls.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Conformance is tested in supported languages and directions because labels, text length, reading order, and accessible names can change by locale.

**Verification method:** Use WCAG mapping, automated scans, manual test scripts, keyboard-only checks, and representative assistive technology.

**REQUIREMENT 0820 OF 1120  |  NEXT.JS FRONTEND ARCHITECTURE, PERFORMANCE, AND ACCESSIBILITY**

## ERP-NEXTJS-050 — Descriptive page title and heading hierarchy

**Normative requirement:** Every route shall render a unique, descriptive localized document title and a visible primary heading, with section headings nested in a meaningful hierarchy that identifies module and task context.

**Rationale:** Titles and headings aid route announcements, orientation, navigation, and users managing multiple ERP tabs.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Automated route tests assert a non-empty unique title and exactly one programmatically identifiable primary page heading for each standard route.

**AC 2.** Heading-level checks find no skipped structural level unless a documented embedded-content boundary explains it.

**Exception / edge case:** A full-screen modal workflow may retain the underlying route title if the modal has its own programmatic title and announced context.

**Security and audit implications:** Titles and headings must not expose confidential record names on routes where authorization is unresolved or concealment policy applies.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Title and heading strings use the active locale; language-specific word order and script are respected rather than concatenated from fragments.

**Verification method:** Run route-title/headings assertions and manual screen-reader navigation on representative module routes.

**REQUIREMENT 0821 OF 1120  |  NEXT.JS FRONTEND ARCHITECTURE, PERFORMANCE, AND ACCESSIBILITY**

## ERP-NEXTJS-051 — Landmarks and skip navigation

**Normative requirement:** Authenticated layouts shall use semantic header, navigation, main, and complementary landmarks as appropriate and provide a visible-on-focus skip link to the main work region.

**Rationale:** A persistent ERP shell may contain extensive navigation; landmarks and skip links let keyboard and screen-reader users reach the current task efficiently.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Each workspace route exposes one primary main landmark with a stable accessible name and a reachable skip link that moves focus to it.

**AC 2.** Landmark inspection identifies distinct primary navigation and main content without duplicate ambiguous main landmarks.

**Exception / edge case:** A focused task dialog may temporarily set an appropriate modal context, but must preserve a reliable route back to the underlying workspace.

**Security and audit implications:** Landmark labels must not include hidden sensitive values; focus movement must not bypass permission-controlled content boundaries.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Landmark and skip-link names are localized, while semantic order remains logical in both LTR and RTL layouts.

**Verification method:** Navigate using only landmarks and keyboard; inspect accessibility tree and verify skip-link focus target.

**REQUIREMENT 0822 OF 1120  |  NEXT.JS FRONTEND ARCHITECTURE, PERFORMANCE, AND ACCESSIBILITY**

## ERP-NEXTJS-052 — Accessible navigation and route announcements

**Normative requirement:** Client-side navigation shall provide a discernible route-change announcement and preserve or deliberately reset keyboard focus according to the navigation context; navigation items shall expose current-page state programmatically.

**Rationale:** Single-page transitions can visually change content without notifying assistive technology users.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** On client route transition, a screen reader receives the new page title or equivalent announcement once, without duplicate announcements.

**AC 2.** The active navigation link exposes \`aria-current=page` or equivalent on the current route and focus remains at a predictable location.

**Exception / edge case:** A background panel refresh that does not change the route shall not announce an entire page transition; only its changed status is announced when relevant.

**Security and audit implications:** Announcements do not include unredacted backend errors or unauthorized entity names; hidden route metadata is generated only after authorization.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Route announcements use the locale actually rendered and do not switch spoken-language context unexpectedly during navigation.

**Verification method:** Test navigation with keyboard and screen readers across full route transitions, nested routes, redirects, and locale changes.

**REQUIREMENT 0823 OF 1120  |  NEXT.JS FRONTEND ARCHITECTURE, PERFORMANCE, AND ACCESSIBILITY**

## ERP-NEXTJS-053 — Semantic tabular data and accessible data-grid behavior

**Normative requirement:** Static tabular business data shall use semantic table markup with associated headers, and interactive data grids shall implement a documented keyboard pattern, accessible row/column headers, and state announcements.

**Rationale:** ERP users need to correlate large numbers of values; correct table relationships and keyboard navigation are essential to interpreting records.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A screen reader can identify each data cell's row and column header in representative static tables.

**AC 2.** Interactive grids pass the documented arrow-key, Home/End, selection, and edit-mode tests without trapping focus.

**Exception / edge case:** A responsive narrow-screen view may transform a table into labeled cards only if row/column relationships and all data/actions remain available.

**Security and audit implications:** Hidden columns and client-only table filtering are not field-level security; restricted fields must not be sent to the browser.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Column names, row labels, sort announcements, and numeric/date values are localized; column order may adapt visually in RTL without corrupting semantic associations.

**Verification method:** Inspect accessibility tree and test table/grid operation with keyboard and representative screen readers at large data volume.

**REQUIREMENT 0824 OF 1120  |  NEXT.JS FRONTEND ARCHITECTURE, PERFORMANCE, AND ACCESSIBILITY**

## ERP-NEXTJS-054 — Complete keyboard operability

**Normative requirement:** All core workflows and controls shall be operable by keyboard without requiring pointer gestures, with a logical focus order and no keyboard trap except while a correctly managed modal dialog is active.

**Rationale:** Keyboard access is necessary for users with motor disabilities and for efficient enterprise data entry.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A keyboard-only test completes navigation, search, create/edit, save/cancel, approval, and error recovery without a pointer.

**AC 2.** Tab and arrow-key sequences follow a documented pattern for every composite widget and never leave focus in an unreachable state.

**Exception / edge case:** A spatially essential mapping or drawing task may require pointer input, but an equivalent keyboard or non-drag alternative must support the business outcome.

**Security and audit implications:** Keyboard shortcuts for consequential operations must not bypass confirmation, step-up authentication, or backend permission checks.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Keyboard order and shortcut labels are tested for localized labels and RTL layout; shortcuts must avoid conflicts with common input methods where practical.

**Verification method:** Perform scripted keyboard-only task tests and automated focus-order checks on supported browsers.

**REQUIREMENT 0825 OF 1120  |  NEXT.JS FRONTEND ARCHITECTURE, PERFORMANCE, AND ACCESSIBILITY**

## ERP-NEXTJS-055 — Visible and unobscured keyboard focus

**Normative requirement:** Every keyboard-focusable control shall have a visible focus indicator that meets applicable contrast requirements and remains at least partly visible when sticky navigation, banners, dialogs, or virtualized content are present.

**Rationale:** Visible focus is necessary to identify the active control, particularly on dense forms and tables.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Computed and visual tests confirm focus indicators are visible against adjacent backgrounds for default, high-contrast, and tenant-brand themes.

**AC 2.** Automated keyboard traversal confirms sticky headers or footers do not completely obscure the focused control.

**Exception / edge case:** A user-agent rendered native control may use its platform focus indicator if it remains visible and is not removed or overridden by application styles.

**Security and audit implications:** Tenant theming may not suppress focus indicators or produce an ambiguous state on controls that perform privileged actions.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Focus visibility must persist when translated labels wrap, controls reorder for RTL, and content expands in a longer-language layout.

**Verification method:** Run keyboard focus screenshots and contrast checks across themes, viewport sizes, sticky states, and modal overlays.

**REQUIREMENT 0826 OF 1120  |  NEXT.JS FRONTEND ARCHITECTURE, PERFORMANCE, AND ACCESSIBILITY**

## ERP-NEXTJS-056 — Modal dialog focus and escape behavior

**Normative requirement:** Modal dialogs shall expose an accessible name and modal state, move focus into the dialog on open, contain tab navigation while modal, and restore focus to the invoker or a documented successor on close.

**Rationale:** ERP confirmations and editors often use dialogs; unmanaged focus can strand keyboard or screen-reader users.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Opening a dialog places focus on its documented initial control and screen-reader users receive its title and purpose.

**AC 2.** Tab and Shift+Tab remain within the modal; Escape closes only when the dialog's business policy permits, and closing restores focus predictably.

**Exception / edge case:** A non-dismissible transaction dialog may suppress Escape only when the reason is explained and a visible keyboard-accessible completion or cancel route remains.

**Security and audit implications:** Dialog state is presentation only; submit/cancel operations recheck authorization and sensitive dialog content is cleared when no longer authorized.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Dialog title, action labels, validation, and focus announcements are localized; layout accommodates translated button order and longer text.

**Verification method:** Test dialog lifecycle with keyboard, screen reader, nested dialogs where allowed, and rejected/expired-session actions.

**REQUIREMENT 0827 OF 1120  |  NEXT.JS FRONTEND ARCHITECTURE, PERFORMANCE, AND ACCESSIBILITY**

## ERP-NEXTJS-057 — Correct accessible patterns for custom widgets

**Normative requirement:** Custom comboboxes, menus, tabs, tree views, and other composite widgets shall follow a W3C ARIA Authoring Practices keyboard and semantics pattern or use native HTML controls when equivalent.

**Rationale:** Adding ARIA roles without expected keyboard behavior can make custom ERP widgets less accessible than native controls.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Each custom widget has a named pattern, role/state mapping, supported key map, and automated interaction tests.

**AC 2.** The accessibility tree exposes current value, expanded/selected/disabled state, and relationships required by the chosen pattern.

**Exception / edge case:** A vendor component that cannot meet the pattern is prohibited from critical workflows unless an accessible equivalent is provided and approved.

**Security and audit implications:** Widget visibility and disabled state do not enforce permissions; backend operations must reject unauthorized actions regardless of widget state.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Accessible names and type-ahead matching support the active script and locale; key handling must respect input method composition.

**Verification method:** Run pattern-specific keyboard scripts, accessibility-tree inspection, and screen-reader testing for each widget type.

**REQUIREMENT 0828 OF 1120  |  NEXT.JS FRONTEND ARCHITECTURE, PERFORMANCE, AND ACCESSIBILITY**

## ERP-NEXTJS-058 — Programmatic labels and instructions for controls

**Normative requirement:** Every input and action control shall have a programmatic accessible name, and fields requiring a particular format, unit, or business rule shall expose associated instructions before or during entry.

**Rationale:** A visual placeholder alone does not reliably identify fields or communicate required entry rules to assistive technology users.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Automated accessibility checks report no unlabeled form control in release-critical forms.

**AC 2.** Representative date, amount, identifier, and selection inputs expose their associated instruction and required state in the accessibility tree.

**Exception / edge case:** A compact icon-only toolbar action may use an explicit localized accessible name and tooltip, but its purpose cannot rely on color or icon shape alone.

**Security and audit implications:** Accessible labels and descriptions must not disclose hidden restricted values; input instructions must not reveal security challenge answers or private policies.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Names, descriptions, required markers, and units are translated as complete messages; script and language metadata match the rendered instruction.

**Verification method:** Run form accessibility scans and manually inspect accessible names/descriptions with a screen reader.

**REQUIREMENT 0829 OF 1120  |  NEXT.JS FRONTEND ARCHITECTURE, PERFORMANCE, AND ACCESSIBILITY**

## ERP-NEXTJS-059 — Accessible validation and error recovery

**Normative requirement:** Form validation shall identify invalid fields in text, associate each error with its field, summarize errors after submission, and preserve valid user-entered values when a correctable validation error occurs.

**Rationale:** Clear error identification allows users to correct business data without guessing or re-entering an entire transaction.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Submitting a form with multiple invalid fields presents a localized error summary linking to each invalid control and each control references its own error.

**AC 2.** After server validation returns errors, valid values remain populated and focus moves to the summary or first error according to the documented form pattern.

**Exception / edge case:** A sensitive credential field may be cleared after failure under the authentication policy while other non-sensitive fields are preserved.

**Security and audit implications:** Error content avoids leaking whether protected records or accounts exist; backend validation remains authoritative and logged by stable error code.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Error summaries, field messages, numeric/date guidance, and plural counts are localized; backend codes remain stable for mapping.

**Verification method:** Test client and server validation failures with keyboard/screen reader and compare preserved form data against sensitivity rules.

**REQUIREMENT 0830 OF 1120  |  NEXT.JS FRONTEND ARCHITECTURE, PERFORMANCE, AND ACCESSIBILITY**

## ERP-NEXTJS-060 — Accessible pending, success, and failure announcements

**Normative requirement:** Asynchronous form submissions and background workflow transitions shall expose a perceivable pending state, announce completion or failure through an appropriate live region, and prevent accidental duplicate submission while pending.

**Rationale:** Users need feedback when an action is processing, especially when network latency or server workflows make completion non-immediate.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A screen reader announces pending state and final success/error once for a representative save and approval action.

**AC 2.** The submit control indicates pending status and repeated activation does not create duplicate mutation requests.

**Exception / edge case:** A long-running job may transition to an asynchronous job view with polling or notification; the interface identifies pending versus completed state and provides a cancellation path where supported.

**Security and audit implications:** A displayed success follows authoritative server confirmation; retries use idempotency or reconcile current transaction state before resubmission.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Status messages are localized and use appropriate live-region politeness; dynamic counts use locale-aware plural forms.

**Verification method:** Use delayed and failed test APIs with assistive technology and assert request count, status announcements, and final server state.

**REQUIREMENT 0831 OF 1120  |  NEXT.JS FRONTEND ARCHITECTURE, PERFORMANCE, AND ACCESSIBILITY**

## ERP-NEXTJS-061 — Color contrast and non-color state cues

**Normative requirement:** Text, controls, focus states, status indicators, and meaningful graphical objects shall meet applicable WCAG 2.2 AA contrast requirements and shall not communicate business state through color alone.

**Rationale:** ERP dashboards commonly use color-coded status, and insufficient contrast or color-only cues exclude users with visual impairments.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Automated theme tests verify normal text contrast of at least 4.5:1, large text at least 3:1, and applicable non-text control/graphic contrast at least 3:1.

**AC 2.** Every status color is paired with text, icon, pattern, or another visible distinguishing cue in list, chart, and detail views.

**Exception / edge case:** A decorative or inactive element may be outside a contrast criterion where WCAG permits, but must not convey an actionable state or required information.

**Security and audit implications:** Theme customization cannot conceal warnings, approval state, or access denial; status appearance does not change underlying permission or transaction state.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Contrast and non-color cues are checked after translated text expansion and across all tenant-approved themes, including RTL configurations.

**Verification method:** Run color-contrast automation and manual grayscale/high-contrast inspection across representative pages and configured themes.

**REQUIREMENT 0832 OF 1120  |  NEXT.JS FRONTEND ARCHITECTURE, PERFORMANCE, AND ACCESSIBILITY**

## ERP-NEXTJS-062 — Reflow and zoom for dense ERP pages

**Normative requirement:** Application-owned content shall reflow and remain functional at WCAG 2.2 AA viewport and zoom conditions, with two-dimensional scrolling limited to content that inherently requires it, such as a data table or complex diagram.

**Rationale:** Dense ERP layouts must remain usable when users enlarge text or access the application on narrow screens.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** At 320 CSS pixels wide and 400 percent zoom from a 1280 CSS pixel viewport, ordinary page content has no loss of functionality or horizontal scrolling outside documented exceptions.

**AC 2.** At least one responsive path provides access to every essential row value and action in a wide transactional grid.

**Exception / edge case:** A genuinely two-dimensional financial or operational table may scroll horizontally, but its headers, controls, and row context remain available and announced.

**Security and audit implications:** Responsive transformations must not hide access-denied notices, confirmation text, or security indicators at narrow widths.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Tests include long translated labels and RTL content because text expansion may cause overflow not visible in the default locale.

**Verification method:** Test at required viewport/zoom sizes and inspect wide-table alternative behavior with keyboard and screen reader.

**REQUIREMENT 0833 OF 1120  |  NEXT.JS FRONTEND ARCHITECTURE, PERFORMANCE, AND ACCESSIBILITY**

## ERP-NEXTJS-063 — Minimum pointer target sizing

**Normative requirement:** Pointer-operable controls shall meet WCAG 2.2 AA target-size minimums or a documented criterion exception, with adequate spacing for adjacent high-frequency actions.

**Rationale:** Small controls in dense tables are difficult to activate accurately, particularly on touch devices and for users with motor impairments.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Automated geometry tests confirm in-scope pointer targets are at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels or satisfy an applicable spacing/equivalent-control exception.

**AC 2.** Representative table row actions can be activated on a touch viewport without overlapping neighboring actions.

**Exception / edge case:** Inline text links, user-agent controls, or essential dense data controls may meet a WCAG exception, but an equivalent compliant control must be present when required.

**Security and audit implications:** Larger hit areas must not overlap adjacent privileged actions or cause accidental approval, deletion, or posting without confirmation.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Target geometry remains adequate when labels wrap or action order changes in RTL layouts and localized translations.

**Verification method:** Measure rendered hit boxes and run touch/keyboard action tests on dense list and form screens.

**REQUIREMENT 0834 OF 1120  |  NEXT.JS FRONTEND ARCHITECTURE, PERFORMANCE, AND ACCESSIBILITY**

## ERP-NEXTJS-064 — Alternatives to dragging and pointer-only gestures

**Normative requirement:** Any frontend operation that uses dragging, spatial movement, or a multipoint gesture shall also provide an equivalent single-pointer or keyboard-accessible method unless the movement is essential to the task.

**Rationale:** Dashboard configuration, reorderable lists, and planning boards often use drag interactions that exclude keyboard and touch users.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Every drag-sortable list exposes move-up/down or equivalent accessible actions that produce the same ordering.

**AC 2.** Every drag-based planning action has a tested alternative for setting the same destination or value without dragging.

**Exception / edge case:** A specialized visual planning feature whose value is inherently spatial may document an essential drag exception and provide a separate non-spatial data-entry path for the business outcome.

**Security and audit implications:** Alternative controls invoke the same authorization and audit workflow as pointer interactions; reorder operations validate concurrency and allowed destinations server-side.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Alternative action names and destination cues are localized and remain logical under RTL direction and translated list ordering.

**Verification method:** Complete each drag-capable workflow using keyboard and single-pointer non-drag alternatives and compare resulting server state.

**REQUIREMENT 0835 OF 1120  |  NEXT.JS FRONTEND ARCHITECTURE, PERFORMANCE, AND ACCESSIBILITY**

## ERP-NEXTJS-065 — Reduced motion and animation controls

**Normative requirement:** Non-essential animation shall respect the user's reduced-motion preference and shall not be required to understand changing business state or complete a workflow.

**Rationale:** Motion can cause discomfort or distraction and should not carry information unavailable through text or static state.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** With reduced-motion preference enabled, nonessential transitions are disabled or substantially reduced without removing status information.

**AC 2.** No auto-moving or flashing interface element prevents task completion or lacks an accessible pause/stop mechanism where required.

**Exception / edge case:** A brief animation that communicates a necessary state transition may remain only when it is non-harmful, time-limited, and accompanied by a stable textual state.

**Security and audit implications:** Security prompts and consequential confirmations are not animated in a way that obscures content or delays access to urgent controls.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Localized text and direction changes must not trigger disorienting layout motion; motion preference applies consistently across extension modules.

**Verification method:** Test prefers-reduced-motion and animation behavior in shared shell, charts, dialogs, and extension components.

**REQUIREMENT 0836 OF 1120  |  NEXT.JS FRONTEND ARCHITECTURE, PERFORMANCE, AND ACCESSIBILITY**

## ERP-NEXTJS-066 — Accessible authentication and step-up flows

**Normative requirement:** Authentication, reauthentication, and configured step-up screens shall provide accessible labels, keyboard completion, clear error recovery, and alternatives to cognitive-function tests where the identity provider supports them.

**Rationale:** ERP access controls must protect sensitive actions without making authentication inaccessible to users with disabilities.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Login and step-up flows are operable by keyboard and expose labeled fields, actionable error messages, and password-manager-compatible input semantics where supported.

**AC 2.** An expired or rejected session returns the user to the intended workflow after successful reauthentication without silently replaying a consequential action.

**Exception / edge case:** An external identity provider may own its own accessibility behavior; integration testing documents provider limitations and an approved alternate path where available.

**Security and audit implications:** Accessibility accommodations do not weaken MFA policy, expose recovery secrets, or automatically execute a pending transaction after session renewal.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Authentication prompts and error guidance are localized where controlled by the product; identity-provider locale support and fallback are configured explicitly.

**Verification method:** Test authentication and step-up with keyboard, screen reader, expired sessions, and direct action replay attempts.

**REQUIREMENT 0837 OF 1120  |  NEXT.JS FRONTEND ARCHITECTURE, PERFORMANCE, AND ACCESSIBILITY**

## ERP-NEXTJS-067 — Session timeout warning and recovery

**Normative requirement:** Where a tenant-configured session timeout can interrupt work, the frontend shall provide an accessible warning and a clear extend-or-sign-out choice before expiration when supported by the identity contract, while preserving unsaved drafts only under an approved data policy.

**Rationale:** Long enterprise forms may take time to complete, and surprise expiration can cause data loss or unsafe re-submission.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A test session presents the timeout warning at the configured lead time and announces remaining time without repeatedly interrupting the user.

**AC 2.** After expiration, protected data is cleared or hidden and unsaved input handling follows the configured save/clear policy.

**Exception / edge case:** The identity provider may not disclose exact expiry; the UI then responds safely to an API 401 without displaying an invented countdown.

**Security and audit implications:** Extending a session requires the identity provider's valid renewal and does not bypass revocation; drafts containing sensitive data are not stored in unprotected browser storage.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Warning text uses locale-aware time units and accessible pluralization; the timeout policy itself remains tenant/identity configuration.

**Verification method:** Use short-lived test sessions to verify announcement timing, renewal, expiry, draft clearing, and safe reauthentication.

**REQUIREMENT 0838 OF 1120  |  NEXT.JS FRONTEND ARCHITECTURE, PERFORMANCE, AND ACCESSIBILITY**

## ERP-NEXTJS-068 — Accessible notification center and status messages

**Normative requirement:** In-app notifications, alerts, toasts, and background job updates shall have suitable semantic roles and announcement timing, remain discoverable after initial presentation, and provide a persistent route to actionable details where needed.

**Rationale:** Transient messages may otherwise disappear before users perceive them or may interrupt assistive technology excessively.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** A transient success or failure is announced once and remains discoverable in a notification center or related workflow when it requires later action.

**AC 2.** A background job status update is announced only on meaningful state transitions and exposes a keyboard-accessible detail link.

**Exception / edge case:** A low-priority informational update may be visually available without an assertive announcement; urgent security alerts use the configured accessible alert behavior.

**Security and audit implications:** Notification content is tenant-authorized and excludes confidential payloads; security alerts are delivered only to intended principals and audit references remain non-secret.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Message text, timestamps, priorities, and plural counts are localized; source-provided user content is marked with its language when known.

**Verification method:** Test announcement frequency and notification persistence with screen readers, delayed events, and multiple tenants.

**REQUIREMENT 0839 OF 1120  |  NEXT.JS FRONTEND ARCHITECTURE, PERFORMANCE, AND ACCESSIBILITY**

## ERP-NEXTJS-069 — Text alternatives for meaningful non-text content

**Normative requirement:** Meaningful images, icons, charts, and visual status representations shall have text alternatives or equivalent data content, while purely decorative assets shall be ignored by assistive technology.

**Rationale:** Visual dashboards and icon-driven actions must communicate the same business information to users who cannot perceive the graphic.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** Every non-decorative image and icon action has a localized accessible name or equivalent text alternative.

**AC 2.** Each business chart exposes a concise textual summary and an accessible underlying table or data view for the plotted values.

**Exception / edge case:** A decorative illustration may use an empty alternative only when it carries no status, action, or business meaning.

**Security and audit implications:** Text alternatives do not reveal data omitted from the visual display due to permission policy; chart data is authorized before either representation is rendered.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Alternatives and chart summaries are translated and include units and time periods using the proper locale conventions.

**Verification method:** Inspect accessibility names and compare chart alternative data to the authorized displayed dataset.

**REQUIREMENT 0840 OF 1120  |  NEXT.JS FRONTEND ARCHITECTURE, PERFORMANCE, AND ACCESSIBILITY**

## ERP-NEXTJS-070 — Accessible multi-script and assistive-technology release testing

**Normative requirement:** The frontend release process shall include multilingual accessibility regression tests using representative assistive technologies, scripts, text expansion, and directionality for critical end-to-end ERP workflows.

**Rationale:** Accessibility defects often arise at the intersection of route changes, translations, dynamic data, and component state rather than in isolated static controls.

**Acceptance criteria:**

**AC 1.** The release suite covers at least one LTR Latin locale, one locale with a different date/number convention, and one supported RTL or non-Latin script where configured.

**AC 2.** A documented assistive-technology matrix exercises sign-in, navigation, lookup, data entry, approval, error handling, and session recovery at release cadence.

**Exception / edge case:** A locale not yet enabled for a tenant is excluded from tenant-specific workflow certification but remains covered by product catalog validation before enablement.

**Security and audit implications:** Test fixtures use synthetic data; screenshots, recordings, and accessibility logs must not contain production business records or real credentials.

**Multilingual and localization implications:** Tests verify actual translated content, \`lang` attributes, reading order, bidi behavior, text expansion, and locale-formatted values rather than only checking a locale switch.

**Verification method:** Run CI accessibility automation plus scheduled manual test sessions with keyboard and screen-reader users on the supported browser matrix.

# API, Integration, Eventing, and Data Exchange

# 13. API, Integration, Eventing, and Data Exchange

## Purpose and scope

This chapter specifies the integration boundary of a multi-tenant commercial ERP for mid-market and enterprise deployments. It covers synchronous HTTP APIs, identity and authorization for system clients, tenant-configured connectors, event publication and consumption, webhook delivery, imports and exports, contract evolution, operational recovery, and multilingual exchange. The normative catalogue below contains 70 distinct requirements; the same objects are supplied as a machine-readable JSON array in 13-integration.json.

The chapter does not prescribe a universal accounting, tax, e-invoicing, payroll, privacy, retention, address, or industry rule. Such obligations vary by jurisdiction, legal entity, sector, contract, and effective date. The ERP shall apply versioned configuration profiles approved by the tenant's accountable business/legal owner; when no verified profile exists, the exchange is marked unconfigured instead of guessing. Personal-data obligations and record-retention exceptions are likewise policy inputs, not hard-coded universal legal conclusions.

## Platform and major design decisions

**Backend baseline.** As verified against Microsoft's official .NET support policy updated November 10, 2026, .NET 11 is the newest stable supported release on November 22, 2026; the policy lists .NET 11.0.0 as STS and .NET 10.0.15 as LTS on that page. Microsoft includes ASP.NET Core in the policy's covered technologies. Therefore the release candidate targets ASP.NET Core on .NET 11, with the current servicing patch required at release approval. .NET 11 is STS, not LTS; a deployment choosing a longer support horizon may explicitly choose the supported .NET 10 LTS line instead. The selected release and patch must be reconfirmed from Microsoft's live policy at each production release; no later version or patch is assumed here. \[1]

**Database.** PostgreSQL is the authoritative transactional store for ERP-owned state, integration configuration, inbox/outbox metadata, crosswalks, and job state. The product release manifest will pin an exact supported PostgreSQL major/minor and extensions, and deployment preflight will enforce it. The official documentation's supported-version page is the authority for the release decision; this chapter intentionally does not freeze a guessed future major. Tenant-scoped predicates are mandatory in application access. PostgreSQL row-level security is defense in depth, not a substitute for application authorization; database owners, superusers, and BYPASSRLS roles can bypass policies, so normal runtime identities must not hold those privileges. \[2] \[3]

**Frontend.** Next.js is a lightweight presentation layer for tenant-user interaction, onboarding, consent/configuration screens, job monitoring, and localized diagnostics. ASP.NET Core remains the business API and integration policy enforcement point. Next.js must not become an alternate path for business writes, tenant authorization, scheduled imports, or event processing. Browser sessions should use secure, same-site session handling; long-lived integration credentials and service tokens stay server-side. The exact Next.js release, router, and hosting model are pinned and regression-tested by the frontend release manifest; the official documentation describes both App Router and Pages Router, so this chapter does not assume an unverified future framework version. \[12]

**Contract style.** Public HTTP contracts are versioned and machine-readable in OpenAPI. The format baseline is the published OpenAPI Specification 3.2.1, dated September 10, 2026; the implementation must verify that the chosen ASP.NET Core tooling can emit or validate the selected dialect and must not silently downgrade schema semantics. ASP.NET Core's first-party OpenAPI package supports document generation and build-time output; production exposure of the document is restricted to an explicit approved publication route. \[5] \[13]

**Integration consistency.** Synchronous commands use HTTP semantics, explicit idempotency, and optimistic concurrency. Events are asynchronous notifications of committed business facts, persisted by an outbox in the same database transaction as the business change. Event delivery is at-least-once where the transport cannot guarantee otherwise; stable identity, consumer deduplication, and reconciliation provide exactly-once business effects where needed. PostgreSQL isolation levels have distinct behavior, and stronger isolation can require whole-transaction retries; each business operation must choose the isolation and retry policy based on its invariants. \[6] \[4]

**Event envelope.** Events use CloudEvents-compatible context attributes and a versioned ERP payload schema. source plus id identifies an event; event type and schema identity are stable, locale-neutral keys. Transport-specific headers may carry envelope attributes only through a documented lossless binding. \[8]

**Security baseline.** System-to-system access uses tenant-registered clients, short-lived audience-restricted tokens, least-privilege scopes, and ERP-level resource/field permissions. OAuth authorization-code flows use transaction-specific PKCE S256 where applicable, and token validation checks issuer, audience, signature, lifetime, and tenant/client binding. API protection follows risk-based lifecycle controls and deployment threat modeling. \[9] \[10]

## Actors and trust boundaries

- **Tenant integration administrator:** registers connectors, approves directions and data domains, manages mappings, rotates secret references, controls activation, and authorizes exports within assigned tenant permissions.
- **Tenant business/data owner:** determines system-of-record authority, conflict rules, required reference catalogs, and business acceptance for each data flow.
- **Tenant user or API client:** submits authorized commands, reads permitted resources, starts jobs, or consumes events under a tenant-bound identity.
- **External system/connector:** a separately authenticated source or recipient, represented by an integration registry entry and bounded scopes.
- **Platform operator/support engineer:** has no standing cross-tenant business access; support elevation is just-in-time, time-limited, reason-coded, and audited.
- **Integration worker/event dispatcher:** processes durable jobs and events using service identities restricted to assigned tenants, queues, and data domains.
- **Auditor/privacy/compliance role:** can inspect authorized activity, exchange manifests, retention status, and configured privacy workflows without gaining general write authority.

Trust boundaries are enforced at API ingress, tenant resolution, database execution, job queue, event broker, outbound egress, uploaded-file quarantine, and exported-artifact retrieval. A tenant identifier supplied in a body, URL, or event is not by itself proof of authorization. Each boundary revalidates tenant/client scope and data-domain permissions.

## Core entities

Tenant owns integration setup and data isolation. LegalEntity selects jurisdiction and industry profiles. IntegrationConnection records connector identity, endpoint, direction, scope, data domains, owner, lifecycle state, and responsible administrator. CredentialReference points to secret-store values without exposing them. MappingVersion contains typed source/target field mappings, transformations, validation policy, and effective interval. ExternalIdentity crosswalks a source-system key to an ERP resource. ExchangeJob records import/export state, mapping version, progress, source artifact, and result manifest. ExchangeRecordOutcome identifies accepted, rejected, skipped, or compensated records. EventOutbox stores committed events pending publication; EventInbox stores received identities and consumer outcomes. WebhookSubscription identifies authorized event filters and destination policy. AuditEntry records privileged configuration, access, export, replay, and support actions. ProfileVersion defines jurisdiction-, industry-, or partner-specific schemas and rules without hard-coding them globally.

Entities carrying tenant-owned state include an immutable tenant key. Resource IDs are opaque and locale-neutral. External identifiers, regulatory codes, currency, unit, language, locale, calendar, timezone, and localized display labels remain distinct concepts. A locale or translated label must never alter a canonical code or financial value.

## Principal workflows

**1. Register and activate connector:** administrator selects connector type and legal entity; system validates endpoint, authentication, granted scopes, allowed data domains, direction, mapping, profile version, and ownership policy; a non-posting connection test is run; approval and activation are audited.

**2. Synchronous API mutation:** authenticate client; resolve tenant from identity; enforce scope, ERP role, field policy, and business rules; validate schema and preconditions; apply one transaction; atomically add outbox records; return stable resource version and trace identifier.

**3. Event flow:** dispatcher claims committed outbox records; serializes the versioned envelope; delivers with bounded retry and signature where applicable; consumer validates identity/schema/tenant, deduplicates in its inbox, applies its side effect idempotently, and acknowledges; unrecoverable records enter controlled dead-letter review.

**4. Bulk exchange:** user or client uploads/downloads a bounded artifact; malware/archive checks and schema/profile validation run in isolation; dry run produces a preview; authorized commit follows declared all-or-nothing, per-record, or per-batch semantics; outcomes and hash-bearing manifest are retained under configured policy.

**5. Reconcile and recover:** scheduled or operator-triggered reconciliation compares source/target counts, watermarks, keys, and totals; differences become explicit exceptions; authorized replay, correction, compensation, or closure is recorded and can be tied to the originating request/job/event.

**6. Retire or rotate integration:** disable new work, settle or explicitly cancel in-flight work, rotate/revoke keys, revoke scopes, stop dispatch, apply retention/deletion rules, preserve needed audit evidence, and record closure.

## Permission boundaries and audit

Authorization has independent layers: authenticated client/user; tenant membership; OAuth scope; ERP role and entity scope; record- and field-level permission; workflow state; and export/event data-domain permission. A successful match at one layer does not override another. Tenant context comes from a verified identity or approved support elevation. Database RLS applies defense in depth and normal runtime roles cannot bypass it. Public error responses avoid exposing the existence of another tenant's objects.

Audit events cover credential and permission lifecycle, integration activation/change/disable, mapping/profile change, data export/import, support elevation, access to sensitive payloads, replay, deletion, and reconciliation resolution. Logs and traces are operational telemetry, not a substitute for the protected audit trail. Secrets, bearer tokens, private keys, and unnecessary payload values are excluded or redacted. Audit and artifact retention, legal holds, privacy-request workflows, and regulator reporting are tenant/jurisdiction configuration decisions.

## Dependencies, cross-module contracts, and risks

The API domain depends on identity and access management for issuer/client lifecycle; tenant and legal-entity services for boundary/profile resolution; the ERP domain modules for canonical commands and resource permissions; PostgreSQL for transactional business, outbox/inbox, job, and audit references; secret management for credentials; broker/worker infrastructure for asynchronous delivery; object storage and scanning for files; and observability services for redacted traces and metrics.

**Cross-module contracts:** finance owns posting, period closure, account, tax, currency, and rounding rules; sales/procurement/inventory own their canonical entities and allowed state transitions; HR/payroll owns restricted personal and compensation fields; identity owns principals, client credentials, and role assignment; document management owns artifact retention and download access. Integration adapters may invoke these module contracts but shall not write module tables directly or bypass validations. Event contracts describe committed facts; consumers do not infer hidden state from event order except where the contract explicitly guarantees an aggregate sequence.

Material risks include cross-tenant leakage, duplicate financial commands after timeout, stale or incompatible schemas, bad mapping changes, reference-code drift, duplicate/out-of-order events, webhook SSRF, secrets in logs, spreadsheet formula injection, malicious archives, locale-induced amount/time corruption, partial imports falsely presented as atomic, and retention gaps across copies and backups. The acceptance criteria in the requirement catalogue provide test gates for these failure modes. PostgreSQL serializable/repeatable-read operations can abort on serialization conflict; callers must retry the whole transaction only when the operation is safe and idempotent. \[4] API errors use stable machine codes and RFC 9457 Problem Details; human-readable text can be negotiated independently. \[7]

Language identifiers follow BCP 47. Language choice does not imply locale, currency, calendar, or timezone. API/event identifiers and codes remain invariant; user-facing problem titles, job messages, labels, and documentation may be localized. Date-only business values remain separate from timestamps; timestamp exchange uses explicit zone/offset semantics. \[11] \[6]

## Requirement catalogue

The following catalogue is normative. Every requirement has a unique ERP-INTEGRATION- identifier, an implementation-level shall statement, rationale, objective acceptance criteria, an edge case, security/audit implications, localization implications, and a verification method. The JSON file beside this chapter is the authoritative machine-readable mirror.

### ERP-INTEGRATION-001 — Supported runtime baseline

**Shall:** The integration services shall target ASP.NET Core on the latest stable, supported .NET release available at release approval, and shall be rebuilt on supported servicing patches before production deployment.

**Rationale:** Avoids unsupported frameworks while separating verified baseline facts from future release assumptions.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Build metadata reports the selected target framework and SDK versions; at the 2026-11-22 verification point the approved candidate is .NET 11 STS, with the then-current patch recorded from Microsoft policy.
- Release pipeline fails when the target framework is preview, end-of-support, or has a known available mandatory servicing update not installed.

**Exception / edge case:** A customer-managed runtime may lag only in a documented, time-bounded migration exception; it does not alter the vendor-supported baseline.

**Security / audit:** Record SDK/runtime image digests, patch evidence, SBOM, and exception approver in each release record.

**Multilingual / localization:** Runtime locale defaults shall not determine tenant language, dates, numbers, or currency formatting.

**Verification:** CI policy test against Microsoft lifecycle metadata, build artifact inspection, and deployment image scan.

### ERP-INTEGRATION-002 — PostgreSQL compatibility floor

**Shall:** The service shall run only on PostgreSQL major versions explicitly listed as supported by the product release and shall test migrations against every supported major version.

**Rationale:** PostgreSQL has a defined supported-version window and version-specific behaviors; production compatibility must be deliberate.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Deployment validation rejects database majors absent from the release compatibility manifest.
- CI applies forward and rollback-compatible migrations against every supported major in the matrix.

**Exception / edge case:** A managed database may expose a compatible service version label; the actual server_version_num must still meet the manifest.

**Security / audit:** Database major, minor, extensions, TLS mode, and role grants are captured in infrastructure inventory.

**Multilingual / localization:** Connection/session locale and collation are explicitly configured; locale-sensitive sorting is not assumed identical across versions.

**Verification:** Containerized compatibility matrix, deployment preflight, and migration test report.

### ERP-INTEGRATION-003 — OpenAPI source of truth

**Shall:** Every externally supported HTTP API operation shall be represented by a versioned OpenAPI document generated or validated from the ASP.NET Core service contract.

**Rationale:** A machine-readable contract reduces consumer guesswork and supports generated tests and clients.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- CI validates each published document against the approved OpenAPI specification version and rejects missing operation IDs, request/response schemas, or security declarations.
- A contract-diff job flags breaking changes before merge and stores the diff with the build.

**Exception / edge case:** Internal health probes may be excluded from the public document only when they are separately inventoried and access-restricted.

**Security / audit:** Production contract publishing excludes internal routes and secrets; contract changes are attributable to a reviewed change set.

**Multilingual / localization:** Localized descriptions may be provided as documentation overlays, but operation IDs, property names, and enum wire values remain locale-neutral.

**Verification:** OpenAPI lint, schema validation, generated-client smoke tests, and breaking-change gate.

### ERP-INTEGRATION-004 — Stable resource identifiers

**Shall:** Public integration resources shall use immutable opaque identifiers that are globally unique within the product namespace and shall not expose database keys as contractual identity.

**Rationale:** Stable identifiers allow integrations to survive migrations, tenancy changes, and internal schema evolution.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- API and event contract tests confirm that created resource IDs remain unchanged after rename, merge, and database migration scenarios.
- No public schema contains a sequential internal primary key as its sole resource identifier.

**Exception / edge case:** Human-assigned numbers such as invoice number may be returned as business attributes but can be reused only under a configured legal/entity scope and are not API identity.

**Security / audit:** Opaque IDs reduce enumeration but are never treated as authorization; access checks remain mandatory and reads are auditable.

**Multilingual / localization:** Identifiers are invariant across UI languages and are not transliterated or localized.

**Verification:** Schema inspection, authorization tests using guessed IDs, and migration/rename integration tests.

### ERP-INTEGRATION-005 — Tenant-qualified ownership

**Shall:** Every tenant-owned integration object shall carry an immutable tenant key and every read, write, event, and job shall enforce that tenant boundary from authenticated context rather than caller-supplied body data.

**Rationale:** Tenant identity is a security boundary in shared commercial ERP deployments.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Cross-tenant attempts to read, mutate, subscribe to, export, or poll a job return no protected data and create a security event.
- A payload tenant key that differs from the authenticated tenant is rejected before persistence.

**Exception / edge case:** A platform operator may perform approved cross-tenant support access through a separately authorized, time-limited audited path.

**Security / audit:** Tenant context is recorded in audit logs and database session context; support impersonation has actor and subject attribution.

**Multilingual / localization:** Tenant language and locale are derived only after tenant resolution; tenant-specific content is never used to infer another tenant's locale.

**Verification:** Automated tenant-isolation suite covering every API route, event consumer, export path, and database policy.

### ERP-INTEGRATION-006 — Data ownership contract

**Shall:** Each integration field shall be classified as ERP-owned, externally mastered, shared, or derived, with an explicit write-authority and conflict-resolution rule before synchronization is enabled.

**Rationale:** Explicit ownership prevents silent overwrites and circular synchronization between systems.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- An integration cannot be activated while any mapped mutable field lacks a declared owner and conflict policy.
- A simulated concurrent update from both systems produces the configured winner or a conflict record without silent loss.

**Exception / edge case:** A tenant may configure time-based precedence for a field only if clock source, tie-breaker, and user-visible conflict behavior are specified.

**Security / audit:** Ownership changes require an authorized administrator and produce before/after audit entries.

**Multilingual / localization:** Localized display labels are not synchronization values unless explicitly designated as translatable business content.

**Verification:** Configuration validation and competing-update integration tests.

### ERP-INTEGRATION-007 — Explicit API versioning

**Shall:** The product shall version public API contracts and shall retain a documented compatibility window for each supported major version.

**Rationale:** Consumers need predictable change windows and a defined path away from retired contracts.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Each operation resolves to a declared version and unsupported versions return a documented machine-readable error.
- The published lifecycle registry records release date, deprecation date, end-of-support date, and migration guide URL for every API major.

**Exception / edge case:** Security fixes may be applied to a supported version without waiting for the normal deprecation window, with behavior changes limited to the documented emergency policy.

**Security / audit:** Version retirement decisions and emergency exceptions are logged and communicated to affected integration owners.

**Multilingual / localization:** Version identifiers and deprecation metadata are locale-neutral; explanatory documentation is available in tenant-supported languages where provided.

**Verification:** Lifecycle registry checks, compatibility tests, and simulated deprecated/unsupported-version requests.

### ERP-INTEGRATION-008 — HTTP semantics and status codes

**Shall:** HTTP operations shall use method and status-code semantics consistently, including idempotent behavior for safe retries and distinct outcomes for validation, conflict, authentication, authorization, and throttling.

**Rationale:** Standards-aligned semantics make retries and error handling interoperable.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Contract tests verify GET has no business side effect and repeated PUT/DELETE requests converge to the same intended resource state.
- Known validation, conflict, unauthorized, forbidden, not-found, and rate-limit cases return their specified status classes and headers.

**Exception / edge case:** A POST may be safely retried only where an idempotency token or equivalent deduplication mechanism is active.

**Security / audit:** Responses do not reveal resource existence across tenant or authorization boundaries; anomalous method use is logged.

**Multilingual / localization:** Status codes and machine error identifiers do not vary by language; human-readable text may be negotiated.

**Verification:** HTTP conformance suite and fault-injection retry tests.

### ERP-INTEGRATION-009 — Canonical wire representation

**Shall:** JSON APIs shall use UTF-8, explicit media types, stable property names, and documented null, omission, and numeric precision semantics.

**Rationale:** Unambiguous wire representations prevent client-specific coercion and corrupt financial or multilingual data.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Requests with unsupported media types or invalid UTF-8 are rejected with a documented error before business processing.
- Round-trip tests preserve decimal precision, Unicode code points, explicit nulls, and omitted optional fields according to schema.

**Exception / edge case:** A legacy connector may emit a documented alternate encoding only through a named adapter that converts to UTF-8 at ingress.

**Security / audit:** Payload validation is bounded and raw sensitive payloads are not copied into diagnostic logs.

**Multilingual / localization:** Names and text accept Unicode, including combining marks and non-Latin scripts; no locale-specific normalization may change stored meaning.

**Verification:** Schema tests with Unicode, malformed encoding, null/omission, and high-precision numeric fixtures.

### ERP-INTEGRATION-010 — Traceable request correlation

**Shall:** The API shall create or validate a correlation identifier for every request and propagate it to asynchronous jobs, events, logs, and downstream calls.

**Rationale:** A complete correlation chain is needed to diagnose distributed processing and support auditable operations.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- A request without a correlation identifier receives one, and the response returns it in a documented header.
- A request with a valid identifier produces linked records across API log, job, event, and outbound attempt.

**Exception / edge case:** Malformed, overlong, or control-character correlation values are replaced rather than echoed.

**Security / audit:** Correlation identifiers are not credentials, are length-limited, and are escaped in logs to prevent injection.

**Multilingual / localization:** Correlation metadata is locale-neutral and must not contain user-entered localized labels.

**Verification:** End-to-end trace assertion and log-injection tests.

### ERP-INTEGRATION-011 — OAuth client authentication

**Shall:** External machine clients shall authenticate through tenant-registered OAuth 2.0 clients using short-lived access tokens and supported strong client authentication; public clients shall use authorization code with PKCE where interactive authorization is used.

**Rationale:** Scoped modern client authentication avoids embedded shared credentials and reduces token theft impact.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- A client without valid issuer, audience, expiry, signature, and client identity claims is rejected.
- Authorization-code integration tests require transaction-bound PKCE S256 for public clients and reject downgrade attempts.

**Exception / edge case:** A tenant's identity provider may not support a selected profile; activation remains blocked until an approved alternative profile is configured.

**Security / audit:** Authentication failures and client credential lifecycle actions are logged without logging tokens or secrets.

**Multilingual / localization:** Consent text, login errors, and client setup guidance follow the user's negotiated language; protocol claims stay language-neutral.

**Verification:** OAuth negative tests, token-claim validation tests, and configuration review against current RFC security guidance.

### ERP-INTEGRATION-012 — Least-privilege scopes

**Shall:** Every integration client shall receive only explicitly granted resource and action scopes, and each operation shall enforce both scope and ERP business authorization.

**Rationale:** OAuth scope alone cannot represent ERP entity, record, or workflow permissions.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- A read-only client cannot create, update, approve, post, or delete records in API tests.
- Revoking a scope or ERP role prevents the next request from performing the protected operation.

**Exception / edge case:** A tenant may grant a broad migration scope only with a time limit, dedicated client, and explicit approval workflow.

**Security / audit:** Scope grants, changes, client identity, tenant, and approver are retained in the security audit trail.

**Multilingual / localization:** Role and scope display names are localized but stable keys and authorization decisions are not.

**Verification:** Authorization matrix tests across scope, role, entity, and operation combinations.

### ERP-INTEGRATION-013 — Token audience restriction

**Shall:** The API shall accept access tokens only when their issuer, audience, signature algorithm, expiry, and tenant/client binding match the configured resource server policy.

**Rationale:** Audience and issuer validation prevent token substitution across APIs and tenants.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Tokens with wrong audience, untrusted issuer, expired time, unsupported algorithm, or mismatched tenant are denied.
- Key rotation tests accept overlapping active signing keys only within configured validity intervals.

**Exception / edge case:** Clock skew may be tolerated only within a bounded configured allowance and is covered by monitored authentication telemetry.

**Security / audit:** Rejection reason codes are recorded without sensitive token contents; signing-key configuration changes are audited.

**Multilingual / localization:** Token claims are protocol values and do not use translated role or tenant display names.

**Verification:** Signed-token test vectors for invalid issuer, audience, times, algorithm, key rotation, and tenant binding.

### ERP-INTEGRATION-014 — Tenant-safe database access

**Shall:** Database access shall apply tenant predicates to all tenant-owned reads and writes, and PostgreSQL row-level security shall provide defense in depth where shared tables are used.

**Rationale:** Application filters alone are vulnerable to missed predicates; PostgreSQL RLS can enforce a default-deny boundary.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Tenant tests executed through the production database role cannot select or mutate another tenant's rows, including through joins and background workers.
- The runtime role is neither table owner, superuser, nor BYPASSRLS, and tests confirm RLS is enabled on tenant tables.

**Exception / edge case:** A separately controlled platform migration role may bypass policies only for migrations and is unavailable to normal application processes.

**Security / audit:** RLS policy changes receive security review; elevated database-role use is separately logged and alertable.

**Multilingual / localization:** Database locale/collation must not be used as a tenant boundary or to compare translated identity strings.

**Verification:** Database privilege inspection, RLS catalog assertions, and cross-tenant query penetration tests.

### ERP-INTEGRATION-015 — Field-level data authorization

**Shall:** The API shall enforce field visibility and mutability rules for sensitive and workflow-controlled fields independently of resource-level authorization.

**Rationale:** Many ERP records combine general business data with restricted personal, payroll, banking, tax, and approval data.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Role-matrix tests verify restricted fields are omitted or masked on reads and rejected on unauthorized writes.
- An API request cannot change server-calculated totals, approval status, posted state, or immutable audit fields unless the operation explicitly permits it.

**Exception / edge case:** An authorized export may include restricted fields only when the export permission, purpose, and requested field set are approved.

**Security / audit:** Sensitive-field reads and changes are auditable at a configurable level without replicating the full value into the audit record.

**Multilingual / localization:** Field labels can be localized, but the allow/deny policy binds to canonical field identifiers.

**Verification:** Field-level authorization tests using restricted and workflow-managed attributes.

### ERP-INTEGRATION-016 — Secret vaulting and rotation

**Shall:** Connector credentials, signing keys, webhook secrets, and certificates shall be encrypted in an approved secret store, referenced by identifier, and rotatable without exporting secret material.

**Rationale:** Secrets in configuration files, logs, or operator interfaces create avoidable compromise paths.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Secret values are absent from database configuration tables, source-control scans, logs, and API responses.
- A rotation test activates a new secret, validates successful traffic, expires the previous secret, and records each transition.

**Exception / edge case:** Break-glass recovery may use a sealed, dual-controlled credential with mandatory expiration and incident record.

**Security / audit:** Secret access is limited to the connector runtime identity and produces immutable access audit events.

**Multilingual / localization:** Secret labels and operator guidance can be localized; secret values are never altered by locale transformations.

**Verification:** Secret-store integration test, static secret scan, rotation game day, and API response inspection.

### ERP-INTEGRATION-017 — Tenant-admin connector permissions
